title: Bipartisan Bill Co-Authored by Bilirakis to Combat Illicit Xylazine Unanimously Advances
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congressman Gus Bilirakis (FL-12) today announced that the bipartisan, bicameral Combating Illicit Xylazine Act, legislation he co authored to combat the growing threat of illicit xylazine trafficking while protecting its legitimate veterinary use, was unanimously approved by the House Committee on Energy and Commerce earlier today. The legislation was introduced by Representatives Gus Bilirakis (FL-12), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), August Pfluger (TX-11), Chris Pappas (NH-01), Scott Fitzgerald (WI-05), and Deborah Ross (NC-02). Having now cleared committee, the bill advances to the House Floor for consideration by the full House of Representatives. Companion legislation has been introduced in the Senate by Senators Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV) and Chuck Grassley (R-IA), underscoring the strong bipartisan and bicameral support for addressing this emerging public safety crisis. Xylazine, commonly referred to as "tranq," is a veterinary sedative that has increasingly been mixed with illicit fentanyl and other street drugs, making overdoses more difficult to reverse and contributing to a growing number of overdose deaths nationwide. Criminal organizations have exploited xylazine because it is inexpensive, widely available, and enhances the effects of fentanyl, creating an even more dangerous and deadly drug supply.

The Combating Illicit Xylazine Act would designate illicit xylazine as a Schedule III controlled substance under the Controlled Substances Act while preserving access for veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers who rely on the medication to safely care for animals. The legislation provides law enforcement with additional tools to investigate and prosecute traffickers without disrupting legitimate agricultural and veterinary practices. The legislation has earned the endorsement of 41 state attorneys general, major national law enforcement organizations, and leading veterinary organizations, reflecting the broad consensus that Congress must act to curb the illicit trafficking of xylazine while safeguarding its appropriate medical use.

"Our goal is simple. We want to save lives and ensure law enforcement has the tools they need to hold accountable those who are illegally manufacturing and distributing these deadly substances that are devastating communities across our country," said Congressman Bilirakis. "I am proud that this bipartisan legislation has advanced out of the House Energy and Commerce Committee, bringing us one step closer to addressing this growing threat. Just as importantly, we must ensure that veterinarians who rely on xylazine to provide quality care for animals continue to have access to this important medication. Our legislation strikes the right balance by protecting public health, strengthening public safety, and preserving critical veterinary care."

"The xylazine crisis is only getting worse, and communities across America are paying the price," said Rep. August Pfluger (TX-11)."That's why I am proud to see the Combating Illicit Xylazine Act advance through the House Committee on Energy and Commerce today. Xylazine was never meant for human use, yet traffickers are increasingly mixing it into street drugs to make them more potent and more deadly. This bill takes direct aim at traffickers exploiting this drug for illicit purposes, while preserving its legal use by veterinarians and agricultural producers. I will continue working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle until this critical legislation is signed into law."

"Illicit xylazine is worsening the deadly fentanyl crisis and tearing through communities across our country," said Congressman Panetta. "The bipartisan Combating Illicit Xylazine Act will help us fight back and keep our communities safe by giving law enforcement the tools needed to crack down on traffickers while ensuring that veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers can continue to use the drug safely and responsibly. The overwhelming approval of this bill in the House Energy and Commerce Committee demonstrates the bipartisan consensus around stopping the illicit spread of this dangerous drug. I look forward to working with both my Democratic and Republican colleagues to get this bill across the finish line and save lives."

“This legislation would help law enforcement crack down on illegal drug traffickers by tracking the manufacture of xylazine, a legal animal tranquilizer, which is being mixed with fentanyl, heroin, and other deadly drugs. It’s now passed out of committee and should be swiftly brought to the floor for a vote,” said Rep. Pappas. “As we work to combat the ongoing addiction epidemic, we must ensure our law enforcement has the resources they need to stop drug trafficking.”

“Xylazine, a powerful animal sedative, is increasingly being cut into illicit drugs like fentanyl, boosting the profits of criminal cartels and drug traffickers while fueling the overdose crisis in the United States,” said Rep. Fitzgerald. “I’m pleased the House Committee on Energy and Commerce advanced the Combating Illicit Xylazine Act. This bill will enhance law enforcement’s ability to track xylazine distribution and impose criminal penalties on those who misuse it, while ensuring its availability for necessary veterinary use. I thank my colleagues for their support and look forward to its passage by the full House.”

“Fentanyl overdoses continue to take far too many lives and devastate our communities, in no small part due to the widespread availability of deadly substances like xylazine,” said Rep. Ross. “This bill will save lives by restricting access to this dangerous substance and giving law enforcement the tools they need to crack down on traffickers, while protecting legitimate uses of xylazine by veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers. I am grateful for the bipartisan commitment to addressing this issue and look forward to hopefully passing this legislation with the full support of Congress.”

title: Bonamici, Thompson, Davis, Nunn Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Support Grandfamily, Kinship Caregivers for Children
text:
WASHINGTON, DC [7/21/26] – Today Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR), Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-PA), Danny Davis (D-IL), and Zach Nunn (R-IA) introduced bipartisan legislation to support families in which children do not have parents in the home.

About 2.5 million children across the United States are being raised in grandfamilies, in which grandparents raise children, or kinship families, in which adult relatives or close family friends raise children. Grandfamilies and kinship families play an essential role because they preserve family connections, prevent children from entering foster care, and promote family stability. Without these caregivers, the foster care system would be overwhelmed and cost taxpayers an additional $10.5 billion annually.

The Supporting Grandfamilies Act of 2026 would reauthorize the National Technical Assistance Center on Grandfamilies & Kinship Families to strengthen the nation’s response to and support for these families.

“Living with grandparents or extended family and friends can provide children with the stability they need to thrive when their parents aren’t able to care for them,” said Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici. “We must support these essential caregivers, who often face additional barriers. The bipartisan Supporting Grandfamilies Act will extend support for families and children at a critical time in their lives.”

“Pennsylvania’s grandparents and relatives frequently step in to provide unconditional support to their grandkids and children every day, and often for years on end,” saidRep. Thompson. “As primary caregivers, it’s necessary to provide access to resources that will help them navigate the child welfare system. The Supporting Grandfamilies Act of 2026 provides caregivers who are raising kids and grandkids, with support, ensuring older primary caregivers have the tools needed to support our next generation.”

“My Congressional District historically has the highest percentage of children living with kinship caregivers in the country,” said Rep. Davis. “I am proud to join with Representatives Bonamici, Thompson, and Nunn in leading the Supporting Grandfamilies Act to ensure that the Grandfamilies & Kinship Support Network continues providing the critical and coordinated support to kinship and grandparent caregivers. For these families, connections to extra resources serve as crucial lifelines. Supporting kinship caregivers strengthens families, promotes stability, and helps children thrive.”

"Not every family looks the same. Kelly and I adopted two of our daughters, and across the country, there are 2.5 million kids being raised by grandparents, aunts, uncles, or other relatives — not because of a government mandate, but because family stepped up when the alternative was foster care," said Rep. Nunn. "Those caregivers said yes without hesitation, often with little warning and fewer resources. Our bill reauthorizes the Grandfamilies and Kinship Support Network for another five years to ensure that when a family steps up, they aren’t navigating that journey alone."

The Grandfamilies & Kinship Support Network is the National Technical Assistance Center (TA Center) led by Generations United through a five-year cooperative agreement with the Administration for Community Living at U.S. Department of Health and Human Services. The TA Center brings together national experts and partner organizations to develop evidence-based tools and promote innovative practices that help communities better meet the needs of kinship families and grandfamilies. The Supporting Grandfamilies Act of 2026 guarantees this information work continues by providing funding for the Grandfamilies & Kinship Support Network for another five years.

title: House Passes FDA Modernization Act 3.0, Building on Landmark Reforms Led by Congressman Buchanan
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Vern Buchanan, Vice Chairman of the House Ways and Means Committee and Chairman of the Health Subcommittee, celebrated House passage of the FDA Modernization Act 3.0 by unanimous consent, a bill directing the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to fully implement provisions reducing unnecessary animal testing in drug development and research. Buchanan previously joined Reps. Nanette Barragán (D-Calif.), Buddy Carter (R-Ga.), Troy Carter (D-La.), Rosa DeLauro (D-Conn.) and Diana Harshbarger (R-Tenn.) in introducing the legislation.

Each year in the United States, millions of animals, including an estimated 50,000 dogs, are used in laboratory experiments and testing. This bill require the FDA to fully implement the FDA Modernization Act 2.0, ensuring that safe and effective treatments are developed using advanced, non-animal testing methods. It phases out animal testing through rules that replace archaic animal testing requirements in favor of modern, humane nonclinical testing methods. This gives dogs traditionally used in labs, including the 1,500 beagles recently rescued in Wisconsin, the opportunity to leave research facilities and find caring homes.

“Patients deserve access to the most advanced medical technology available,” said Buchanan. “The FDA Modernization Act 3.0 ensures that drug testing reflects today’s science, bringing promising treatments to families faster without relying on unnecessary animal testing. “As Chairman of the Ways and Means Health Subcommittee and author of the FDA Modernization Act 2.0, I am proud to see this bill build on that work.”

“This bill will transform drug development for the 21st century,” said Carter. “By requiring full implementation of the FDA Modernization Act 3.0, this legislation ensures that developers use innovative, more effective testing methods throughout drug development, rather than relying on outdated and inhumane animal tests. It’s a win for patients, a win for innovation and a win for animal welfare. I’m proud to champion this bipartisan measure to accelerate safer, more humane and more effective medical breakthroughs.”

“Today’s floor vote is another important step toward modernizing how we bring safe and effective drugs to market,” said Harshbarger. “The FDA has the authority to move beyond outdated, cruel testing methods and our bill simply directs the FDA to follow through and update its regulations accordingly. I’m proud to work alongside Congressman Buddy Carter and my colleagues to keep this bipartisan effort moving forward.”

Buchanan, who co-chairs the Animal Protection Caucus in Congress, is a leading advocate for ending animal testing. He previously authored the FDA Modernization Act 2.0, which was signed into law in 2022 and removed an 80-year-old requirement that forced pharmaceutical companies to use animal testing to prove a drug’s safety and efficacy.

title: Case Calls On President To Once Again Extend Jones Act Waiver To Address Severe Risk Of Disruption Of Critical Energy Supplies To Hawaii Resulting From Ongoing Iran War
text:
(Washington, D.C.) – U.S. Representative Ed Case (Hawai‘i-First) asked President Trump to grant another 60-day extension of the current waiver of the Jones Act, citing continued global shipping disruptions, constrained fuel supply chains and rising gasoline and energy costs in Hawai‘i, along with implications for U.S. military readiness in the Indo-Pacific. In April, Case called on the President to grant the initial extension that is set to expire on August 15.

In his latest letter to the President, Case again urged that: “The waiver should be extended now rather than on current expiration because contracts for the acquisition and shipping of fossil fuel products to U.S. ports are signed well in advance of shipping and delivery and failure to provide clarity on that timeframe will seriously disrupt shipping options and prices with wide ranging effects.

“The waiver is operating nationally to mitigate the effects of market disruption on energy availability and pricing nationally. But the need for the waiver is especially acute in Hawai‘i and other noncontiguous jurisdictions which are largely reliant on external fossil fuel-based products for energy, agriculture, transportation, and other key needs, and where the Jones Act, even in a non-disrupted world, imposes unique severe constraints on the delivery of energy supplies and related pricing.”

Case continued: “As I explained before when asking you to extend the waiver earlier this year, Hawai‘i is one of the most isolated parts of our country and depends on shipping for over ninety percent of our goods, including nearly all of our fossil fuel products. Yet the Jones Act severely limits shipping options from the continental U.S. to U.S. Jones Act vessels only, despite the widespread availability of shipping in the international markets. For fossil fuel products specifically, of the thousands of tankers operating globally, only a small fraction are Jones Act-compliant and available for domestic transport, and virtually none are suited for certain bulk commodities such as fertilizer. As a result, even though the United States is a net energy exporter, Hawai‘i typically relies on foreign imports because Jones Act shipping is far more expensive and less dependable that international shipping.”

The Jones Act, a century-old federal maritime law, mandates that all cargo shipped between U.S. ports be transported on U.S.-flagged vessels, excluding most ships operating in global trade that are flagged internationally. With fewer than 100 oceangoing Jones Act vessels nationwide, limited domestic capacity faces no international competition, contributing to higher shipping costs.

The constraints in oil shipping are even more stark: of the nearly 7,500 oil tankers operating worldwide, only 54 are Jones Act-compliant and eligible to move fossil fuel products from the Continent to Hawai‘i, which remains heavily dependent on imported fossil fuel products for energy. As a result, Hawai‘i typically must source most of its essential resources from foreign markets, where shipping is far cheaper.

Case also highlighted to the President the extensive military presence in Hawai‘i, which is largely dependent on the same sources of energy, fuel and other fossil fuel products as the civilian population. He said: “The military in Hawai‘i also depends on this same fuel network. Hawai‘i is the Indo-Pacific home to every service – the Army, Navy, Marines, Air Force and Space Force – along with a significant presence of our nation’s intelligence community.

“It is our nation’s Indo-Pacific headquarters, hosting U.S. Pacific Command, U.S. Pacific Fleet, Pacific Air Forces, U.S. Army Pacific, Marine Corps Forces Pacific, Special Operations Command Pacific, Space Force Indo-Pacific and the National Security Agency Hawai‘i. It also has many key military installations including Joint Base Pearl Harbor-Hickam, Marine Corps Base Hawai‘i, Schofield Barracks, Fort Shafter, the Pacific Missile Range Facility, Pōhakuloa Training Area and various other locations. These installations support key operating forces based in Hawai‘i, including nuclear attack submarines, surface combatants, an Army infantry division, F-22s, MV-22s, C-17s, fuel tankers, Apaches, a Marine Corp regiment and approximately 60,000 Department of Defense (DoD) personnel plus families. Both these services and their active duty and civilian personnel and families are all being impacted by substantially higher fossil fuel-related costs.

“The conditions that justified the initial request, including global tanker dislocation, severely constrained availability of U.S.-flagged vessels and disruptions associated with instability in and around the Strait of Hormuz, continue to affect fuel logistics. These ongoing challenges underscore the importance of maintaining maximum flexibility in maritime transport to ensure both civilian and military fuel needs are met.”

In the current 119th Congress, Case again introduced legislation to reform the Jones Act and open up Hawai‘i - Continent shipping to international competition.

title: Castor Breast Cancer Awareness Bill Passes House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.– Today, U.S. Rep. Kathy Castor (FL-14) celebrated passage of her bipartisan Breast Cancer Education and Awareness Requires Learning Young (EARLY) Act Reauthorization (H.R. 4541) with Reps. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (IA-01), Debbie Dingell (MI-06) and Diana Harshbarger (TN-01).

Breast cancer is the most common cancer diagnosed among women in the United States, where the average risk for developing it sometime in her life is about 1 in 8. More than 316,000 new diagnoses and 42,000 deaths are expected from breast cancer in 2025. And with incidences rising in younger women each year, the earlier it’s caught, the better the chance to survive and overcome this devastating disease.

The key to early detection and treatment starts with education and awareness. This is especially true for younger women and those at greater risk of death from more aggressive forms of breast cancer.

“Too many young women face breast cancer without the knowledge or support they need to catch it early and fight back,” said Rep. Castor. “For more than fifteen years, the EARLY Act has supported young women through outreach and resources that meet them where they are. I’m proud to lead the charge for this bipartisan reauthorization to ensure these critical initiatives that empower women to understand their risks, advocate for their health and get the tools they need to fight the disease continue.”

View Castor’s remarks on the EARLY Act reauthorization here.

The EARLY Act authorizes three programs administered by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), designed to empower young and high-risk women. This includes the Bring Your Brave effort, which amplifies stories of real women to raise awareness of breast cancer in young women between the ages of 18 and 44, and encourages them to understand their risk and the signs and symptoms. It also funds the Young Breast Cancer Survivors Program, which provides grants to non-profit organizations aimed at delivering supportive services and resources to increase patients’ survival and improve their quality of life. And it offers continuing medical education (CME) courses for health care providers about breast cancer.

After fifteen years of successful implementation, it is now time to again reauthorize the EARLY Act to ensure that it continues to reach even more young and higher-risk women across the United States. Reauthorizing the EARLY Act is vital to continuing to save women’s lives.

title: Over 55 members of Congress send letterRep. Smith, Sen. Lee lead bicameral letter to DOJ urging investigation into barbaric deaths of five late-term, preborn babies at D.C. abortion clinic
text:

Rep. Chris Smith, Co-Chair of the Congressional Pro-Life Caucus, said: “The Biden Administration’s deliberate and callous mishandling of the ‘D.C. Five’ case has been a stain on the Department of Justice for over four years now. These five beautiful, innocent babies—who were violently exterminated—deserve justice, accountability, and respect. All those involved and complicit in these children’s barbaric deaths must be held to account, and we are calling upon President Trump’s Department of Justice to ensure that these battered baby victims receive their day in court.”

Sen. Americans cannot tolerate rogue abortion clinics performing gruesome murders and casting helpless victims aside like garbage, especially not in our Nation’s capital. This crime demands attention and prosecution to the fullest extent of the law. I urge the Department of Justice to give this alarming case the full investigation it deserves, and the victims the proper autopsies and burials they are owed.”

In the letter, first obtained by The Daily Wire, the 57 members of Congress explain that the desecrated bodies of these children—one of which bore deep lacerations and injuries consistent with illegal partial-birth abortion procedures—were “recovered by the Metropolitan Police Department in 2022, after they were allegedly aborted in the Washington Surgi-Clinic operated by the late-term abortionist Dr. Cesare Santangelo.”

“For four years, members of Congress have remained alarmed at this clear violation of life and law, but the Biden Administration Department of Justice refused to act,” the Republican lawmakers write.

The letter—dated July 20, 2026—follows an April 2022 letter led by Rep. Smith and Sen. Lee and signed by 67 other members of Congress, which called upon Biden-era Attorney General Merrick Garland to conduct a “comprehensive investigation on the circumstances surrounding the deaths of each preborn baby.”

title: The Daily Wire exclusive article on Smith-led letter to DOJ'EXCLUSIVE: Republican Senators Make Big Demand Of Todd Blanche Ahead Of Confirmation Vote'
text:
By Mary Margaret Olohan

Published July 21, 2026

A group of Republican lawmakers are urging acting Attorney General Todd Blanche to bring long-awaited clarity to the gruesome deaths of five premie-sized babies recovered from a Washington, D.C., abortion clinic in 2022.

Utah Senator Mike Lee and Congressman Chris Smith of New Jersey, along with more than 50 other lawmakers, are calling on Blanche to “comprehensively investigate the circumstances surrounding the deaths of five preborn children” whose remains “were recovered by the Metropolitan Police Department in 2022, after they were allegedly aborted in the Washington Surgi-Clinic operated by the late-term abortionist Dr. Cesare Santangelo.”

“For four years, members of Congress have remained alarmed at this clear violation of life and law, but the Biden Administration Department of Justice refused to act,” the lawmakers write in a letter exclusively obtained by The Daily Wire, noting that their remains are in the possession of the D.C. Medical Examiner and calling on Blanche to find out if the babies “were victims of the crimes of infanticide or partial-birth abortion.”

Blanche, who has been acting attorney general since April, is in the midst of a confirmation battle on Capitol Hill. Blanche faced the Senate Judiciary Committee last week in a two-day hearing where Republican and Democrat lawmakers alike questioned him about the Trump administration’s handling of the Jeffrey Epstein case, among other issues.

Lee and three other signatories of Tuesday’s letter — Senators Chuck Grassley, Ted Cruz, and Josh Hawley — all serve on the Senate Judiciary Committee. Blanche will need their votes to get to a full floor vote, and then for confirmation. As the committee prepares to vote, the signatories are calling Blanche to conduct a “thorough investigation into the death of each child, including autopsies of the infants and the preservation of all collected evidence.”

That is not all, however: they also want the babies to be properly buried.

“We cannot undo the grievous, barbaric acts that killed these children in their most vulnerable stage, but we equally cannot allow such lawlessness and inhumanity to evade our justice system any longer,” the letter reads. “Under President Trump’s and your leadership, we are hopeful that these children will finally receive the justice they deserve.”

Pro-life activists Lauren Handy and Terrisa Bukovinac originally discovered the baby bodies in boxes outside a Foggy Bottom abortion clinic in 2022 shortly before the Supreme Court overturned Roe v. Wade. The Daily Wire has extensively reported on Washington’s lack of interest in how these fully formed babies died.

Advocates and Republican lawmakers have sounded the alarm for years about these babies, warning that they appear to have been brutally and illegally aborted in violation of federal law, but the Biden administration took no steps to properly investigate the matter, instead targeting the women who recovered the bodies.

Doctors estimated to The Daily Wire in 2022 that several of the babies were the victims of late-term abortions — and that at least one baby may have been aborted using illegal partial-birth abortion methods, showing “deep lacerations to the posterior neck which presumably correlates to the method of abortion used to end her life.”

“If this baby girl was alive when the abortionist made these lacerations, then her death directly violated the Partial-Birth Abortion Ban Act of 2003 (18 U.S. Code § 1531), which criminalizes the partial deliverance of a living child for the purpose of performing an overt act that intentionally takes the life of the child,” they wrote.

The lawmakers also point to the estimations of pro-life doctors, noting that one baby boy was estimated to be around 28 to 32 weeks, while another baby looked “like he should have been in the nursery” and was “about the same size as [her] granddaughter when she was born.”

Lee and Smith called on Attorney General Merrick Garland to conduct an investigation into the babies in 2022, as The Daily Wire first reported at the time, but the Justice Department never investigated or responded.

“On the contrary, after two years of inaction, reports indicated that the Department of Justice advised the Chief Medical Examiner to discard the bodies of the infants,” Lee and Smith write in their letter. “Fortunately, members of Congress were able to intervene with the Chief Medical Examiner and urge him to preserve the bodies.”

As recently as April, Republican Reps. Chip Roy (TX) and Andy Biggs (AZ) pushed FBI Director Kash Patel to investigate the babies and their deaths.

title: The Epoch Times article featuring Smith's commentary'US Pledges to Push Back Against Chinese Transnational Repression, Protect Falun Gong'
text:
By Frank Fang & Eva Fu

Published July 21, 2026

WASHINGTON—The U.S. government intends to push back against the Chinese communist regime’s transnational repression on U.S. soil and defend vulnerable groups such as Falun Gong practitioners, the State Department told The Epoch Times.

“We are committed to safeguarding our sovereignty, keeping our communities safe, and defending individuals from the overreach of foreign governments and regimes trying to silence, intimidate, harass, harm, or coerce individuals within our borders,” a State Department spokesperson said on July 21.

“CCP [Chinese Communist Party] repression extends far beyond China’s borders, as Chinese officials or their proxies threaten, harass, and intimidate critics of the CCP overseas, including in the United States.”

Falun Gong, a meditation discipline based on the principles of truthfulness, compassion, and tolerance, quickly spread by word of mouth to reach an estimated 70 million to 100 million practitioners during the 1990s.

The State Department building in Washington on July 27, 2023. Madalina Vasiliu/The Epoch Times

On July 20, Falun Gong practitioners marked 27 years of persecution by the CCP.

“The CCP promoted the Falun Gong movement in the 1990s, but since then has waged a campaign to eradicate the spiritual practice for political reasons, targeting practitioners and their families in China and around the world,” the State Department official said.

New York-based Falun Dafa Information Center, in a recent survey, documented more than 600 cases of transnational repression over a five-year period from 2020.

“The CCP perpetrates acts of transnational repression in the United States and other countries often targeting Chinese diaspora communities, particularly human rights defenders and activists, students, journalists, and dissidents, as well as Hong Kongers, Uyghurs and Tibetans, and followers of certain religious or spiritual groups, including Falun Gong,” the State Department said.

Heightening the concerns of transnational repression is a newly adopted Chinese ethnic unity law, which critics say will allow the Chinese regime to target people in the United States and beyond.

Falun Gong practitioners march during a parade calling for the end of the Chinese Communist Party’s 27 years of ongoing persecution against the spiritual practice, in New York City on July 19, 2026. Larry Dye/The Epoch Times

‘Enemy of Its Own People’

A bipartisan group of lawmakers has joined Falun Gong practitioners in marking the persecution anniversary.

The CCP, fearing that Falun Gong’s popularity threatened the regime’s power, began a brutal campaign to eradicate the practice on July 20, 1999. Untold numbers of practitioners have suffered arbitrary detention, forced labor, torture, and even death by forced organ harvesting.

“The Chinese Communist Party is a direct threat to the American way of life and the enemy of its own people,” Sen. Rick Scott (R-Fla.), who sits on the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, said in a video.

Scott said the legislation he co-introduced in the House last year, the Falun Gong Protection Act, would enable the United States to impose sanctions on individuals responsible for or complicit in China’s state-sanctioned practice of forced organ harvesting.

“We can never stop speaking out and holding the government of communist China accountable for their horrific crimes,” he said.

Sen. Rick Scott (R-Fla.) speaks during a press conference in the U.S. Capitol in Washington on July 11, 2023. Madalina Vasiliu/The Epoch Times

The bill passed the House in May 2025. The Senate version of the legislation, the Falun Gong and Victims of Forced Organ Harvesting Protection Act, advanced out of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee in June.

Rep. Joe Wilson (R-S.C.), who serves on the House Committee on Foreign Affairs, applauded efforts to end the persecution.

“The Chinese Communist Party is terrified of freedom, and their violence against the Falun Gong will not be tolerated,” Wilson said in a statement.

‘Ongong Crime’

The Epoch Times broke the story in 2006 that the CCP was killing prisoners of conscience, primarily Falun Gong practitioners, by harvesting their organs for transplant surgeries.

The allegations have since been confirmed by independent investigators, including Canadian human rights lawyer David Matas, who documented the findings in his book “Bloody Harvest.”

David Matas (R) speaks at a rally after receiving the Friends of Falun Gong Human Rights award jointly with David Kilgour (L) on June 20, 2018 in Washington. Samira Bouaou/The Epoch Times

In 2019, a London-based independent people’s tribunal, known as the China Tribunal, concluded that the Chinese regime had been forcibly harvesting organs from prisoners of conscience for many years, with Falun Gong practitioners as the primary victims.

The tribunal found that medical tests conducted specifically on Falun Gong and Uyghur prisoners were “highly suggestive of methods used to assess organ function.”

Jan Jekielek, senior editor at The Epoch Times, detailed the evidence in his bestselling book “Killed to Order,” published in March. The book explores how the Chinese regime’s industrial practice of forced organ harvesting became an estimated $9 billion industry.

Rep. Sam Graves (R-Mo.), in a letter, called the CCP’s actions against Falun Gong “cruel and unjust.”

“The CCP routinely commits human rights abuses such as murder, organ-harvesting, mass false-imprisonment, and unconscionable torture,” he said, noting that these actions were done to “advance their communist ideology.”

“These genocidal acts are irredeemable and have no place in today’s world.”

Religious freedom is a right that has been “denied to practitioners of Falun Gong in China for far too long,” Rep. Emanuel Cleaver (D-Mo.) said.

“To be arrested, detained, or killed because of your beliefs, peaceful practices, or relationship to spirituality is unacceptable,” he said in a letter. “To stand up for humanity requires standing against persecution.”

Rep. Emanuel Cleaver (D-Mo.) speaks at Uptown Theater in Kansas City, Mo., on Nov. 8, 2016. Whitney Curtis/Getty Images

Four months after the persecution began in 1999, Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.) issued a resolution in 1999 condemning the abuse.

On July 21 this year, Smith said: “In spite of immense pressure and intimidation from a powerful authoritarian regime, the resilient spirit of the Falun Gong has not been broken.”

The persecution is “not a closed chapter of history,” but rather “an ongoing crime—and those responsible should know that they will face justice,” he said in a statement.

He called for the United States to “press for the release of every detained practitioner and sanction the CCP officials responsible for the atrocities committed against the Falun Gong.”

Rep. Chris Smith (R-N.J.), co-chair of the Congressional-Executive Commission on China, during a hearing on Capitol Hill in Washington on May 14, 2026. Madalina Kilroy/The Epoch Times

Transnational Repression

The Falun Dafa Information Center, in its June report, pointed to a 2024 Brooklyn parade where several Falun Gong practitioners were assaulted.

Another incident took place in the Flushing neighborhood, home to New York City’s largest Chinatown, in February. A man dressed mostly in black struck a Falun Gong practitioner in the back of the head, knocking her to the ground.

Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-Fla.) said he was “deeply troubled” by such incidents.

“Any attempt by a foreign government to harass, threaten, or suppress individuals lawfully exercising their constitutional rights on American soil is unacceptable,” he said.

Rep. Gus Bilirakis (R-Fla.) speaks during the International Interfaith Conference, “United in Liberty: The Rise of Spiritual Diplomats,” on Capitol Hill in Washington, on Jan. 22, 2026. Madalina Kilroy/The Epoch Times

Bilirakis, who serves on the House Select Committee on the CCP, sponsored the Transnational Repression Policy Act in 2024. One of the provisions of the legislation calls for the U.S. president to impose property and visa sanctions on foreign actors found responsible for transnational repression.

Applauding Falun Gong practitioners for their courage in the face of the CCP’s campaign, Bilirakis said their commitment to truthfulness, compassion, and tolerance serves as a “powerful reminder that tyranny can never extinguish the human spirit.”

Reps. James Walkinshaw (D-Va.) and Tom Tiffany (R-Wis.) both said the persecution’s anniversary is a reminder of solidarity.

The United States has long supported religious liberty. This solemn day calls to mind the international community’s responsibility to promote accountability for human rights abuses and advance fundamental freedoms, Walkinshaw said.

Falun Gong practitioners participate in a vigil in New York City to mark 27 years of the persecution of Falun Gong by the communist party in China on July 20, 2026. Larry Dye/The Epoch Times

This article was published on July 21, 2026 and can be found online at:

title: Higgins’ Legislation Cracking Down on Toxic Foreign Imports Passes House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Clay Higgins (R-LA) issued a statement after the U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 2715, the Destruction of Hazardous Imports Act.

Congressman Higgins and Congressman Troy Carter (D-LA) introduced the legislation in April 2025. The bill would authorize the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) to destroy imported products that pose significant health risks. Read the bill text here.

The legislation comes amid reports of toxic, radioactive seafood entering U.S. ports, as well as health risks posed by illegal foreign-made vapes, both of which would be subject to destruction under this bill. Currently, the FDA can destroy dangerous imported medicine and medical devices, but not food, which allows foreign vessels turned away at one port to unload their cargo at another. While originally crafted to address seafood imports, H.R. 2715 would close this loophole across the board, preventing hazardous products of all kinds from entering U.S. markets.

“The House is prioritizing the health and safety of the American people by ensuring that predatory foreign actors are not offloading harmful products at our ports,” said Rep. Clay Higgins. “Our bill empowers the FDA to destroy contaminated products, a necessary step to ensure radioactive seafood and counterfeit goods are not reaching American consumers. We are protecting the American people and domestic industry.”

“This legislation will protect Louisiana’s health and support our seafood economy. By granting the FDA the necessary authority to destroy food products that fail to meet our strict health and safety standards, we are closing a dangerous loophole that has allowed contaminated seafood to enter our markets,” said Rep. Troy Carter, Sr. “This bill protects consumers from potential health risks and upholds the integrity of our food supply chain, while supporting Louisiana fishermen and seafood processors.”

“No one should be surprised that foreign exporters choose to ship contaminated food to the U.S. market if the worst that can happen is that the product is returned to them by the FDA,” said Blake Price, Executive Director of the Southern Shrimp Alliance. “This loophole in the law has unintentionally incentivized the flooding of our market with foreign shrimp containing banned antibiotics, harmful pathogens, and, most recently, radioactive substances that undercut hard-working U.S. shrimpers. The American shrimp industry is incredibly grateful for the leadership of Congressmen Clay Higgins and Troy Carter in advancing the Destruction of Hazardous Imports Act, common sense, bipartisan legislation that closes the loophole and gives the FDA authority to destroy goods that pose a significant threat to public health.”

title: Congressman Cleaver Celebrates More than $34 Million for Kansas City Bio Tech Hub, Applauds Additional Investment in Missouri Innovation
text:
(Washington, D.C.) – Today, U.S. Representative Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO), celebrates the U.S. Economic Development Administration’s (EDA) announcement of approximately $34 million in implementation funding for the Kansas City BioSecure Manufacturing Hub (KC Bio) as part of the federal Tech Hubs Program, along with an additional $38 million for Missouri’s Critical Minerals and Materials for Advanced Energy Tech Hub (CM2AE) based in Rolla. Tech Hubs was authorized by the bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act, a key part of President Biden’s Investing in America agenda, which he signed into law in August 2022.

The investments are designed to strengthen America’s global competitiveness by accelerating innovation, expanding advanced manufacturing, strengthening domestic supply chains, and positioning regions like Kansas City as national leaders in critical technologies essential to both economic growth and national security.

“Today’s announcement is a major victory for the region and our nation’s future,” said Congressman Cleaver. “The Kansas City region has long been home to world-class research institutions, pioneering life sciences companies, and an unmatched spirit of collaboration. This investment recognizes what we’ve known for years - that Kansas City is uniquely positioned to lead America in the next generation of biomanufacturing and biotechnology innovation.”

The Kansas City BioSecure Manufacturing Tech Hub, led by BioNexus KC and supported by a broad coalition of public, private, academic, and nonprofit partners, was designated as a federal Tech Hub to strengthen domestic bio manufacturing capacity and accelerate the commercialization of emerging technologies.

Rep. Cleaver has supported efforts to establish Kansas City as a national leader in biosciences and advanced manufacturing sectors, recognizing both the economic opportunity and the national security importance of developing resilient domestic supply chains for critical technologies.

The announcement follows last week’s selection of the University of Missouri-Kansas City to lead a National Science Foundation Innovation Engine, another landmark federal investment that will accelerate research, commercialization, and workforce development across the heartland. Together, the awards reinforce Kansas City’s growing role as a national center for innovation and advanced technology.

“These investments are about much more than today’s dollars,” said Congressman Cleaver. “They are about creating high-paying jobs, strengthening our regional economy, supporting groundbreaking research, and ensuring America, not our global competitors, leads the industries that will define the future.”

In addition to the Kansas City Award, the Critical Minerals and Materials for Advanced Energy Tech Hub will receive approximately $38 million to strengthen domestic production of the materials necessary for advanced energy technologies. The initiative includes partnerships with institutions across Missouri, including the University of Missouri-Kansas City, further expanding the economic and research benefits for the Kansas City region.

Emanuel Cleaver, II is the U.S. Representative for Missouri's Fifth Congressional District, which includes Kansas City, Independence, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Grandview, Sugar Creek, Greenwood, Blue Springs, North Kansas City, Gladstone, and Claycomo. He is a member of the exclusive House Financial Services Committee and Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance.

title: Rep. Michael Cloud to Newsmax: Smithsonian Missing America’s Story
text:
Newsmax Wires | July 21st, 2026

The Smithsonian’s historical displays are “troubling” because of “what’s in there … but also what’s missing,” Rep. Michael Cloud, R-Texas, told Newsmax on Tuesday.

Appearing on “Wake Up America” with co-hosts Sharla McBride and Marc Lotter, Cloud said he expects House lawmakers to press Smithsonian National Museum of American History Director Anthea Hartig over what Republicans say is a growing left-wing bias in the museum’s exhibits.

Cloud, who serves on the House subcommittee holding Tuesday’s hearing, said visitors no longer receive the inspiring account of America’s founding they would expect from the nation’s premier history museum.

“Hopefully, we’ll find out the why behind the what,” Cloud said. “It doesn’t take anything more than the casual observer to walk through the museum and see this isn’t your father’s or your mother’s American History Museum.”

He pointed to exhibits featuring drag performances and what he described as “questionable books for kids,” while arguing that foundational moments in American history receive little attention.

“You would think on the 250th anniversary of America’s history maybe there would be this huge exhibit on the Declaration of Independence — not to be found,” Cloud said.

The White House Domestic Policy Council recently released a report accusing the Smithsonian of promoting an ideologically driven version of American history, allegations museum officials have rejected.

A Smithsonian spokesperson has maintained that the institution has served the public for more than 180 years through “nonpartisan and independent scholarship.”

Cloud, however, said his own visit left him surprised by how difficult it was to find exhibits highlighting some of the nation’s best-known Founding Fathers.

“I went through the museum recently and I just was like, ‘Hey, let me, let me see if I can find anything on John Adams,'” Cloud said. “It was much more difficult than you would think.”

Cloud also said stories about George Washington, Thomas Jefferson, and other iconic figures are overshadowed by exhibits focused on more recent cultural and social issues.

“Where’s that story that unites us?” he asked. “That E pluribus unum, where we say, out of many, became one — this great nation that’s done amazing things for the people who live here.”

Republicans have increasingly scrutinized federally funded cultural institutions, arguing they should celebrate America’s achievements rather than emphasize themes they say divide the country.

Cloud said the Smithsonian should better reflect the nation’s shared heritage, especially as America prepares to commemorate its 250th anniversary.

“The question is, where do the American people go if they can’t go to their own history museum to find out America’s history?” he said.

Cloud also briefly addressed efforts to avoid a government shutdown, saying Republicans are working to pass a continuing resolution while advancing President Donald Trump’s agenda, including the SAVE America Act, and ensuring the military remains fully funded.

title: Congressman Cohen Denounces Heartless Trump-Miller Immigration Policies at Judiciary Committee Markup

“It’s hard to imagine we’re sitting here and having discussions about giving children legal representation when they’re subject to deportation. An (immigration) hearing is supposed to be confrontational, between two sides, adversarial, and a child without representation against an attorney is not a fair process. They do have a right to a hearing; we all understand that, but there needs to be fairness and the fact we’re discussing this is hard to fathom…

“This is coming from Donald Trump. This is what he wants. He wants to deport as many people as possible. That’s the message he gave to the Department of Homeland Security. Stephen Miller gave them head counts and they have to meet their head counts…and they do it sometimes illegally. Sometimes they kill people. They make mistakes and they don’t understand what they’re doing. The President of the United States needs to resign. He’s doing so many unimaginable things to this country, and to justice and to due process…We don’t have it here anymore…

“It’s all about him…a narcissistic grifter. That’s who’s guarding this country…He doesn’t want anyone to have counsel except himself…Roy Cohn told him ‘never admit you’re wrong. Never back down…’ ”

title: Rep. Angie Craig Demands DOJ and SEC Investigate Trump's Insider Trading Subscription Service, “Truth API”

title: Reps. Goldman, Pfluger, Wittman, Panetta, Norcross, Schrier Advance Bipartisan Prior Authorization Transparency Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, the Prior Authorization Accountability Act, led by Reps. Craig Goldman (R-TX-12), August Pfluger (R-TX-11), Rob Wittman (R-VA-01), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19), Donald Norcross (D-NJ-01), and Kim Schrier (D-WA-08) passed out of the House Energy and Commerce Committee. This bill requires all health insurance companies to display claim denial rates.

"For too long, Americans have suffered from surprise medical bills and unexpected denials of health insurance claims. I'm working with my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to increase transparency into the health insurance process so that patients can receive better care," said Congressman Craig Goldman. "I'll keep working to pass smart legislation that actually addresses the core problems in healthcare so patients can have better, more affordable care."

"Insurance is only helpful if you can actually use it when health problems arise," Congressman Donald Norcross (NJ-01) said. "Nobody should get rejected for the care they need, especially if they already paid a ridiculous amount of money for a plan that’s supposed to cover those services in the first place. The transparency requirements of this bill will help families avoid getting the rug pulled out from under them by their insurers, and is one of many necessary changes we must make to America's healthcare system as a whole."

The Prior Authorization Accountability Act would:

Require all health insurance companies to publicly display their claim denial rates

Increase transparency by letting Americans see the number and percentage of claims an insurer rejects before they sign up for a plan

Include data on the percentage of denied claims that are appealed and subsequently overturned, as well as the average time it takes to resolve appeals

Mandate this information to be posted clearly on the insurance company's website and listed in its plan materials

Background:

Every year, millions of Americans sign up for health insurance plans with little to no information about how insurance companies authorize care. As a result, many patients receive unexpected medical bills, experience delayed access to care, and must then navigate a lengthy appeal process to contest any claim denials.

This bill would hold providers accountable while giving potential customers more data to make informed decisions.

Support:

The Prior Authorization Accountability Act is supported by Baylor Scott & White Health, Texas Health Resources, Private Medical Group North Texas, National Psoriasis Foundation, Arthritis Foundation, National Alliance on Mental Illness, and more.

Read the full text of the legislation here.

title: Dingell Leads Bipartisan Effort to Expand ABLE Savings for Americans with Disabilities
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and Derek Schmidt (R-KS-02) introduced the bipartisan ABLE MATCH Act (Making Able a Tool to Combat Hardship), which would help more Americans with disabilities build financial security through Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) savings accounts.

"Financial independence shouldn’t be out of reach for individuals with disabilities,” Congresswoman Dingell said. “By reintroducing the ABLE MATCH Act, we are taking a crucial step toward economic security by matching the hard-earned savings of ABLE account beneficiaries through a refundable tax credit."

The legislation would establish a federal matching contribution for eligible low- and moderate-income individuals who save in ABLE accounts, allowing beneficiaries to receive up to a 100 percent federal match on the first $2,000 they contribute annually, subject to income limits. The federal matching funds would be deposited directly into the beneficiary's ABLE account, helping individuals save for disability-related expenses without jeopardizing eligibility for critical benefits.

title: DOWNING-COSPONSORED FINANCIAL SERVICES BILL PASSES HOUSE
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 6955, the Main Street Capital Access Act, legislation cosponsored by Congressman Troy Downing, to encourage new bank formation and help community lenders better serve families, small businesses, and rural communities across Montana.

The Main Street Capital Access Act reduces regulatory barriers that have made it increasingly difficult to establish and grow community banks. For years, smaller financial institutions have been subjected to many of the same rules designed for the nation’s largest banks. These one-size-fits-all requirements have limited local lending and discouraged the creation of new banks, particularly in rural states like Montana.

“Montana families and small businesses depend on community banks that understand their needs and are invested in the success of their towns,” said Congressman Downing. “Instead, Washington has buried these local lenders in one-size-fits-all rules meant for megabanks. The Main Street Capital Access Act cuts the red tape holding back community lending, makes it easier to establish new banks, and expands access to capital in rural communities. This bill puts Main Street ahead of Washington bureaucracy.”

The legislation also strengthens transparency and accountability in the bank approval process while ensuring regulators remain focused on safety and soundness. By removing unnecessary barriers to entry, the bill will help expand financial services in underserved communities and give more Montanans access to trusted local lenders.

title: Representatives Escobar, Alford Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Cut Red Tape and Accelerate Military Construction
text:
Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) was joined by Congressman Mark Alford (R-MO) in introducing the bipartisan Streamlining Military Infrastructure Act, legislation that would examine how the Department of Defense can expand the use of Intergovernmental Support Agreements to complete minor military construction projects faster and at a lower cost.

“At Fort Bliss and installations across the country, servicemembers should not have to wait years for the facilities and infrastructure they need because of outdated red tape, and taxpayers shouldn’t have to pay millions more in construction costs because of it, either,” said Congresswoman Escobar. “I have been working to reform the outdated military construction process in order to make it less costly and bring more projects to fruition. My legislation lays the groundwork to give installation commanders greater flexibility to use strong local partnerships for minor construction projects. That means faster and more affordable construction, increased partnerships with local governments, and a better quality of life for our servicemembers.”

“Modernizing our military infrastructure doesn’t always require reinventing the wheel; we can make smarter use of the tools we already have. This legislation takes a practical, data-driven approach to see how partnerships with state and local governments can help deliver projects faster, more efficiently, and at a lower cost to taxpayers. I’m proud to co-lead this commonsense first step toward broader reform that puts accountability, efficiency, and mission readiness front and center,” said Congressman Mark Alford

"For years, ADC has advocated for expanding the flexibility and use of Intergovernmental Support Agreements as a proven tool for strengthening military installations and the communities that support them,” said Tom Ford, ADC President. “We applaud Rep. Escobar and Rep Alford for their leadership in advancing this legislation and look forward to working with Congress and the Department of Defense to identify opportunities that improve installation resilience, readiness, and infrastructure delivery."

Intergovernmental Support Agreements, or IGSAs, allow military installations to partner with state and local governments to meet installation needs. The legislation would direct the Department of Defense to assess the feasibility of using these agreements for unspecified minor military construction projects, which can be completed without individual congressional authorization. Expanding this flexibility could help installation commanders reduce unnecessary delays, lower construction costs, and address infrastructure needs that directly affect military readiness and servicemembers’ quality of life.

Specifically, the Streamlining Military Infrastructure Act would:

Require the Assistant Secretaries responsible for installations for the Army, Navy, and Air Force to assess the feasibility of using IGSAs to carry out unspecified minor military construction projects

Examine increasing the maximum project thresholds under IGSA authority from $9 million to $18 million for laboratory revitalization projects and from $4 million to $8 million for projects funded through Operation and Maintenance accounts; and

Require the Department of Defense to identify up to 10 military construction projects that could be eligible to use this expanded authority.

title: Fedorchak’s High-Capacity Grid Act advances out of Energy and Commerce Committee
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, the House Committee on Energy and Commerce advanced Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak's (R-N.D.) High-Capacity Grid Act (H.R. 6633) to the Full House for consideration. The legislation, which passed the Committee with a 49-0 vote, will modernize America’s transmission system by requiring the use of best-available transmission conductors for new interstate transmission lines and rebuilds.

"America's electricity demand is growing at the fastest pace in decades. To meet this demand, we must optimize our existing transmission infrastructure," Fedorchak said. "The High-Capacity Grid Act is a commonsense solution that will help us move more electricity over existing rights-of-way, improve grid reliability, and manage costs for consumers. I'm grateful to my colleagues on the Energy and Commerce Committee for supporting this legislation, and I look forward to securing its passage on the House Floor."

Image

Background on the High-Capacity Grid Act:

Demand for electricity continues to grow as new manufacturing and large energy users come online. Current standards and return on equity methodologies do not incentivize the use of advanced transmission conductors, even when they carry significantly more electricity with lower line losses. This leads to lower capacity lines, more line losses requiring maintenance, and increased costs for American families.

Key aspects of the bill include:

Requiring the use of the highest-capacity, highest-efficiency, and lowest-sag commercially available conductors for new interstate transmission projects and major rebuilds.

Increasing transmission capacity within existing rights-of-way to connect and carry more electricity, reducing the need for additional corridors and new transmission lines.

Improving grid reliability while helping keep electricity affordable for consumers.

Promoting cost-effective utility investments through the deployment of proven, high-performance transmission technologies.

The High-Capacity Grid Act now heads to the full House Floor for consideration.

title: Fitzgerald Banking Reform Bills Included in House-Passed Main Street Capital Access Act
text:
July 21, 2026

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, the U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 6955, the Main Street Capital Access Act, comprehensive legislation to modernize the nation’s banking regulatory framework to strengthen community banks.

This legislation includes three bills introduced by Congressman Scott Fitzgerald (WI-05): the Bank Competition Modernization Act, the Halting Uncertain Methods and Practices in Supervision (HUMPS) Act, and the Merger Agreement Approvals Clarity and Predictability Act. It also includes the Bank Failure Prevention Act, which Congressman Fitzgerald co-led with Congressman Andy Barr (KY-06).

“Community banks are essential to Wisconsin’s families, farmers, and small businesses, but Washington has buried them under red tape and an unpredictable regulatory system for far too long,” said Congressman Scott Fitzgerald. “The Main Street Capital Access Act reins in unelected regulators, increases accountability, and gives community banks the certainty they need to grow, compete, and serve their customers. I am proud that several of my bills are included in this package, and I look forward to working with my Senate colleagues to get these reforms to President Trump’s desk.”

More on Congressman Fitzgerald’s provisions in the legislation:

Bank Competition Modernization Act: Modernizes outdated bank merger review standards. Specifically, the bill creates a $10 billion asset threshold, adjusted for growth in nominal GDP, under which federal banking regulators provide a safe harbor from the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) competition analysis, allowing small community banks to grow and achieve operational efficiencies without the delays associated with the DOJ’s competition review.

Halting Uncertain Methods and Practices in Supervision (HUMPS) Act: Strengthens transparency in how banks are evaluated. Specifically, it directs the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC) to revise the CAMELS rating system by establishing clear, objective standards for each component and updating the formula used to calculate a bank’s overall rating. It also calls for eliminating or reforming the subjective “Management” component, focusing instead on measurable risk governance and internal controls.

Merger Agreement Approvals Clarity and Predictability Act: Addresses political intrusion into the regulatory approval process for bank mergers and acquisitions. Specifically, the bill requires the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct a thorough review of how federal regulators use commitments and conditions when approving mergers of insured depository institutions. It also directs GAO to determine whether regulators rely on extrastatutory considerations, such as policy preferences or non‑statutory goals, when conditioning merger approvals.

Bank Failure Prevention Act: Enhances competition in the U.S. banking system. Specifically, it ensures bank regulators make timely decisions on mergers to bring certainty to bank competition and consumer needs.

title: Fitzpatrick Secures House Passage of Bipartisan EARLY Act Reauthorization
text:
House passage marks a resounding bipartisan victory for women’s health, cancer prevention, and early detection

Washington, DC—Today, Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (R, PA-01), Co-Chair of the House Cancer Caucus, announced House passage of his bipartisan EARLY Act reauthorization—a major victory for women’s health, cancer prevention, and early detection.

The House-passed package renews proven programs that help young and high-risk women understand their breast cancer risk, recognize warning signs, and receive informed care sooner. It also includes the full provisions of Fitzpatrick’s bipartisan SCREENS for Cancer Act, expanding the pathway to breast and cervical cancer screening and diagnostic services for women facing financial, insurance, and other barriers to care.

“America has made extraordinary progress in preventing, detecting, and treating cancer, but that progress only matters if it reaches the people whose lives depend on it,” said Fitzpatrick. “Early detection remains one of the most effective tools we have to improve outcomes and save lives. No woman should miss that opportunity because she lacked the right information, her provider lacked the right resources, or cost and insurance barriers placed care beyond her reach. Closing those gaps has been a top priority of my work as Co-Chair of the House Cancer Caucus.”

“My mother and sister are breast cancer survivors, so this mission is deeply personal to me,” he continued. Their experience is a constant reminder that when women receive the right information and the right care at the right time, lives can change—and lives can be saved. This bipartisan vote is a major step forward for women and families across America. I urge my colleagues in the Senate to act with the same urgency and send this legislation to the President’s desk.”

Breast cancer remains the most common cancer among women. Young women, women of color, and women at elevated risk are too often diagnosed only after the disease has progressed—when treatment options are more limited and outcomes are worse.

Originally enacted in 2010, the Breast Cancer Education and Awareness Requires Learning Young Act supports targeted, CDC-led initiatives designed to reach young and high-risk women before cancer goes undetected.

The House-passed legislation, introduced along with Representatives Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (IA-01), Kathy Castor (FL-14), Debbie Dingell (MI-06), and Diana Harshbarger (TN-01), reauthorizes the EARLY Act through 2031, protecting three core programs:

The Bring Your Brave campaign, which uses the experiences of real women to increase awareness among women ages 18 to 44 about breast cancer risks, symptoms, and early detection;

The Young Breast Cancer Survivors Program, which supports organizations providing assistance and resources to young patients and survivors; and

Continuing medical education for health care providers, strengthening their ability to recognize risk and improve care for younger women at increased risk.

After 15 years of successful implementation, reauthorizing the EARLY Act will ensure these programs can continue reaching women before a diagnosis comes too late—giving patients and providers the knowledge needed to identify risks, recognize warning signs, and act sooner.

The reauthorization also includes Fitzpatrick’s bipartisan SCREENS for Cancer Act, introduced with Congressman Joe Morelle (D, NY-25). The measure reauthorizes and strengthens the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program through 2030.

Since its creation in 1991, the program has served more than 6.4 million people and provided more than 16.5 million breast and cervical cancer screening examinations. Those screenings have helped diagnose nearly 80,000 invasive breast cancers and approximately 5,300 invasive cervical cancers, while identifying hundreds of thousands of precancerous lesions.

The SCREENS for Cancer Act would:

Reauthorize the National Breast and Cervical Cancer Early Detection Program through 2030 with $235 million in annual funding;

Improve access to breast and cervical cancer screening and diagnostic services;

Strengthen patient navigation and appropriate follow-up care;

Support evidence-based strategies proven to increase screening rates in health care settings;

Reduce barriers facing low-income, uninsured, underinsured, geographically isolated, and underserved communities;

Address disparities in breast and cervical cancer incidence and mortality; and

Require a Government Accountability Office study examining program utilization, eligibility, and barriers to screening access.

Together, the EARLY Act and the SCREENS for Cancer Act strengthen the full early-detection pathway—from helping women understand their risks and equipping providers to identify warning signs to ensuring more patients can access screening, diagnosis, and follow-up care.

The EARLY Act reauthorization is supported by more than 20 leading cancer prevention and patient advocacy organizations, including the American Cancer Society Cancer Action Network, Susan G. Komen, Living Beyond Breast Cancer, Sharsheret, the Brem Foundation, and the Prevent Cancer Foundation.

The legislation now advances to the United States Senate for consideration.

title: Foster Introduces Legislation to Crack Down on “Notario” Fraud
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Congressman Bill Foster (D-IL) introduced the Protecting Immigrants from Legal Exploitation Act. The legislation would create penalties for those who provide fraudulent immigration legal services and allow immigrants who are victims of fraud to have their cases reconsidered under certain circumstances. It would also create grant programs to educate immigrants on how to avoid legal service fraud and help qualified nonprofit organizations provide legal services to immigrants.

In many Latin American countries, "notario" or "notario público" refers to state-appointed lawyers. However, in the United States, a notary only has the authority to witness and certify legal documents. This linguistic discrepancy can expose many recent immigrants, particularly those from Latin American countries, to the risk of fraudulent immigration legal services.

“My office, like many other Members of Congress, has seen a large increase in people seeking assistance with their immigration cases in the wake of the Trump Administration’s attacks on immigrant communities,” said Rep. Foster. “Now more than ever, well-meaning immigrants are vulnerable to fraudulent immigration lawyers looking to exploit them for money, possibly leading to their deportation. It's time to stop scammers from targeting vulnerable immigrants who are working to follow the legal immigration process in a time of fear and uncertainty.”

The Protecting Immigrants from Legal Exploitation Act is cosponsored by Reps. Salud Carbajal (D-CA), Judy Chu (D-CA), Gil Cisneros (D-CA), Yvette Clarke (D-NY), Jesús “Chuy” García (D-IL), Hank Johnson (D-GA), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA), Jim McGovern (D-MA), Seth Moulton (D-MA), Jerrold Nadler (D-NY), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), Mike Quigley (D-IL), Jan Schakowsky (D-IL), Paul Tonko (D-NY), Juan Vargas (D-CA), and Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL).

title: RELEASE: Rep. Friedman Statement After Federal Judge Halts Paramount-Warner Bros. Merger
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, July 21, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) releases the following statement after a federal judge’s decision to halt the proposed $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery by Paramount Skydance for two weeks.

On May 7, Friedman led 34 California Members of Congress thanking California Attorney General Rob Bonta for his commitment to a “full and robust review” of the merger and urging him to independently analyze its effects and use his best judgment amid the Trump Administration’s politicization of antitrust enforcement.

“This latest court action reaffirms what I’ve been saying at every step of this deal. We simply cannot trust this Administration to act in the best interests of American workers and consumers. Any merger of this size and scale, with so many local jobs and livelihoods on the line, calls for a rigorous and thorough review. Now, it seems like a judge agrees and wants to give this proposed merger the scrutiny it needs. I’ll continue to follow this case as it makes its way through our legal system,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30).

On-location production in the greater Los Angeles area declined 13.2% for the July through September 2025 period compared to the year prior.

More than 42,000 jobs in Los Angeles County’s motion picture industry were lost from 2022 to 2024.

Paramount is projecting $6 billion in expense cuts over three years if the merger proceeds, with analysts predicting significant job losses.

Decades of entertainment industry consolidation have already reduced output, raised prices, limited consumer choices, and stifled innovation.

Friedman is Hollywood's representative in Congress and has been among the most active voices calling for careful examination of the merger to defend California's entertainment industry. title: Congressman Gabe Evans’ Bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act Passes Energy and Commerce Committee, Heads to House Floor
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Gabe Evans' bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act unanimously passed through the House Energy and Commerce, marking a major step toward protecting American families and small businesses from bearing the costs of powering new data center development. The legislation now advances to the House floor for a vote.

The bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act establishes commonsense standards for states and their Public Utility Commissions (PUCs) to consider when connecting large-load customers—such as data centers and hyperscalers—to the electric grid. The bill helps ensure these companies, rather than everyday ratepayers, are responsible for the costs of new power generation, transmission lines, and other infrastructure needed to meet the immense energy demand they require.

As energy demand continues to grow alongside America's leadership in Artificial Intelligence (AI), the Ratepayer Protection Act provides states with a framework to encourage economic growth while protecting households and small businesses from higher monthly utility rates.

“America must build the energy infrastructure necessary to win the global AI race and outcompete adversaries like Communist China—but hardworking families should never be forced to subsidize that growth through higher electric bills. This bipartisan commonsense legislation ensures the companies creating new demand for electricity pay for the infrastructure they require—not Colorado families, farmers, seniors, and small businesses. I’m proud to see the swift advancement of the Ratepayer Protection Act through committee, and I look forward to its final passage in the House.” –– Congressman Gabe Evans

Background

If enacted, the legislation would establish federal standards for state regulators to use when reviewing proposals for new large-load customers with an electricity demand of 100 megawatts or more. The bill recommends:

Recovering the full incremental cost of grid upgrades from the large-load customer over time through special rate structures or other agreements, ensuring utilities and existing ratepayers are not left paying for infrastructure if a customer later scales back operations or leaves the system.

Requiring financial assurances that large-load customers will pay for the generation, transmission, and other infrastructure necessary to serve their demand, preventing those costs from being shifted onto families and local businesses through higher electricity rates.

The Ratepayer Protection Act builds on the principles of the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, under which major technology companies committed to covering the energy and infrastructure costs associated with new data center development.

The bill now heads to the House floor for consideration.

title: Congressman Gabe Evans’ Stop Pills that Kill Act Clears Committee, Heads to House Floor
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Gabe Evans’ legislation that would crack down on counterfeit prescription pills laced with fentanyl, methamphetamine and other dangerous substances passed through the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

The Stop Pills that Kill Act would implement new penalties and close a sentencing loophole for counterfeit pill production. It would also require the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) to create a comprehensive plan to tackle the influx of deadly pills.

“As a former cop in Colorado, I have seen firsthand how Denver Democrats' soft-on-crime policies have hindered law enforcement's ability to eliminate fentanyl and other counterfeit substances from our communities. The Stop Pills that Kill Act will help equip federal law enforcement with the tools, resources, and education necessary to crack down on the production and distribution of these deadly, illicit drugs across our country. I’m proud to see this legislation advance through committee, and I look forward to its final passage on the House floor.” — Congressman Gabe Evans

Background:

Congressman Evans has made combating fentanyl and the flow of illicit drugs a top legislative priority. Since taking office, he has introduced and supported several bipartisan efforts to address the crisis, including:

Combatting Fentanyl Poisonings Act

No Fentanyl on Social Media Act

HALT Fentanyl Act

Despite overdose deaths decreasing across the country, Colorado continues to see a rise. This is largely due to the sanctuary style and soft-on-crime policies implemented by Denver Democrats like Governor Jared Polis and Denver Mayor Mike Johnston that have made Colorado the second most dangerous state in the nation.

Synthetic opioids (like fentanyl) account for roughly half of all total drug overdoses in Colorado, making them the most commonly involved lethal substance.

The overall CDC drug overdose death rate in Colorado is 25.7 per 100,000 residents — higher than the national average.

Since December 2024, synthetic opioid overdose deaths (SOOD) in Colorado have grown at the third fastest rate in the country at +17%. Meanwhile, the national rate has decreased by -21% during this same period.

title: Garbarino Marks One Year as Chairman of House Committee on Homeland Security
text:

I am proud of what we have accomplished and remain focused on our most important responsibility: keeping Americans safe.”
