The House has also passed 20 bills advanced by the Committee, including Chairman Garbarino’s bipartisan Reimbursable Screening Services Program Extension Act of 2026, which expands and extends a TSA program that provides additional security screening capabilities at airports and major events.

Twenty-five years after September 11, Chairman Garbarino remains focused on the Committee’s most important mission: keeping Americans safe.

title: Rep. Gillen Recognizes the 100th Anniversary of the Long Island Association
text:
A video of the full remarks is available HERE.

WASHINGTON, DC — Yesterday, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04) celebrated the 100th anniversary of the Long Island Association (LIA) on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives. Joined by her Long Island colleagues, Rep. Gillen recognized the LIA’s partnership and work with business and government leaders, helping meet local challenges and support bipartisan solutions for Long Island.

The Long Island Association is the region’s leading non-profit and business organization. Since 1926, the LIA has worked to promote the economic well-being and affordability of Long Island, strengthening connections with lawmakers and advocating for policies that create jobs and stimulate private investment.

Rep. Gillen has consistently advocated for Long Island’s businesses and economic growth, including leading the charge in Congress to eliminate the State and Local Tax Deduction (SALT) cap. She also introduced the bipartisan Advancing Regional Quantum Hubs Act, which would help reinforce Long Island as a national hub for Quantum Computing.

(Remarks as prepared for delivery)

Thank you, M. Speaker.

I rise today to celebrate the 100th anniversary of the Long Island Association.

For a century, it has been an institution at the heart of Long Island’s economy and business community.

Thank you to Chairman Waldman, Acting President Sikes, and the Association’s members for traveling to Washington this week.

It is a privilege to reaffirm our shared commitment to prosperity and opportunity for every Long Islander.

Long Island’s businesses and industries contribute more than $200 billion to the nation’s economy every year.

We are an economic powerhouse, driving innovation and discoveries in national security, medicine, and next-generation technologies.

Giving Long Island’s businesses a strong base with no limits on their success is how we bolster our local economy and way of life.

Core to its mission, the Long Island Association has been a crucial bridge between business and government leaders.

That partnership is foundational to the success of every entrepreneur, industry, and family-owned business that built Long Island.

Our work here in Washington is first and foremost to deliver for our communities through bipartisanship and common sense.

Doing so through pro-business and pro-worker policies gives our region the room to grow and stay competitive.

The Long Island Association’s partnership has been instrumental in helping meet the challenges we face.

I hear them from business owners across my district in Nassau County.

We must make Long Island more affordable to keep attracting world-class talent and give companies the chance to invest in themselves.

That starts with lowering the high costs and taxes our families and businesses pay, including eliminating the SALT cap and undoing harmful tariffs.

It means making housing more affordable and ensuring every young professional and hardworking family has a place to call home.

We must meet our energy needs with an all-of-the-above strategy and guarantee our infrastructure can support a growing economy.

We must cut federal red tape and invest in our industries to fuel greater opportunity across our region.

I’m proud to have worked with the Association and with my Long Island colleagues across the aisle to tackle these challenges head-on.

I remain committed to being a trusted voice in Washington for Long Island’s businesses and workers.

As we celebrate the Long Island Association’s 100 years of excellence, I look forward to our continued partnership.

Congratulations on this historic milestone and the beginning of another remarkable century of service.

title: Reps. Gillen and Malliotakis Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Secure Justice for 9/11 Families and Victims of Iranian State-Sponsored Terrorism
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (D-NY-04) alongside Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY-11) introduced the bipartisan Never Forget the Victims of Terrorism: Joseph D. Mistrulli and Alan Kleinberg USVSST Fund Solvency Act to deliver justice for victims of Iranian-backed terrorism, including families of 9/11 victims. The legislation would provide temporary targeted financing for the U.S. Victims of State-Sponsored Terrorism (USVSST) Fund from the billions of dollars of compensation Iran and other state sponsors of terrorism owe to American victims. More than 20,000 Americans currently hold unpaid judgments from perpetrators of state-sponsored terrorism through the Fund, including Iran.

Reps. Gillen and Malliotakis recently led a bipartisan letter with Rep. Mike Lawler (R-NY-17) to President Trump urging the administration to secure overdue compensation for the victims as part of any negotiation or peace agreement with Iran. They are committed to standing with American victims of terrorism and ensuring they receive the compensation they are owed.

“American victims of Iran’s state-sponsored terrorism have waited far too long for the justice and restitution they are legally owed,” said Rep. Gillen. “The lives of more than 20,000 victims, including families impacted by 9/11, have been forever changed by heinous acts of terror, which is why Congress established the U.S. Victims of State Sponsored Terrorism Fund. This bipartisan legislation ensures that our promises to victims are backed by real action, delivering the long-overdue compensation they deserve while holding Iran accountable for decades of horrific violence against Americans.”

“As New Yorkers, we understand what so many families impacted by state-sponsored terrorism have gone through, particularly as we approach the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks,” said Rep. Malliotakis. “This bipartisan proposal will strengthen the Fund’s solvency and help victims receive what they are owed.”

“We honor Joseph D. Mistrulli and Alan Kleinberg, and every American whose life was stolen by terrorism,” said Angela Mistrulli, Founder, American Victims of State-Sponsored Terrorism United. “Their families deserve justice without delay, and the ‘Never Forget the Victims of Terrorism: Joseph D. Mistrulli and Alan Kleinberg USVSST Fund Solvency Act’ ensures that promise is kept. My family is deeply appreciative of our own Congresswoman Gillen, and of longtime champion and friend Congresswoman Malliotakis, for their unwavering commitment to all American victims of state‑sponsored terrorism. Their leadership continues to give families like ours strength, hope, and a path toward long‑overdue justice. Today, we call upon Congress to bring this bill to the floor immediately for a vote, because justice cannot wait”

The bipartisan Never Forget the Victims of Terrorism: Joseph D. Mistrulli and Alan Kleinberg USVSST Fund Solvency Act would strengthen the fund, which has not kept pace with eligible claims, providing temporary financing and mandatory repayment from future enforcement proceedings. The Government Accountability Office (GAO) found long-term revenue insufficiency in existing statutory sources, providing the need for this legislation.

Established in 2015, the USVSST Fund is a federal program administered by the Department of Justice to provide financial compensation to American victims and families harmed by international terrorism. As Iran refuses to honor billions of dollars in outstanding American judicial judgments, the Fund relies on assets seized from federal enforcement actions and state sponsors to ensure victims receive a measure of justice. 9/11 victims and their family members receive a dedicated 50 percent allocation of all money available for distributions from the USVSST Fund.

title: Goodlander-Backed Bipartisan Bill to Strengthen Alzheimer’s Care Passes the House
text:
Washington, D.C. — Yesterday, the House of Representatives passed the Accelerating Access to Dementia and Alzheimer’s Provider Training (AADAPT) Act, bipartisan legislation cosponsored by Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) to help more primary care providers detect, diagnose, and care for patients with Alzheimer’s disease and other dementias.

With more than 7 million Americans living with Alzheimer’s and millions more caring for loved ones every day, primary care providers are often the first place families turn. In rural and underserved communities, specialists may be hours away.

“Every family facing Alzheimer’s deserves answers, quality care, and real support — no matter their ZIP code,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “Primary care providers are often the first line of defense, but too many lack access to the specialized training they need to detect and manage dementia. I’m proud to support this bipartisan bill to give providers the tools to identify Alzheimer’s earlier and deliver better care closer to home.”

The legislation would reauthorize the federal Technology-enabled Collaborative Learning Program through fiscal year 2031 and add dementia care to the program’s focus areas. The program supports telementoring models such as Project ECHO, which connect frontline providers with specialists to strengthen care in rural and underserved communities.

Goodlander has worked closely alongside New Hampshire Alzheimer’s advocates and brought their priorities to Congress. She is working to strengthen research, expand access to earlier diagnosis and quality care, and ensure caregivers receive the support they need and deserve.

ADDITIONAL BACKGROUND:

After meeting with New Hampshire Alzheimer’s advocates, Goodlander publicly called for advancing the AADAPT and ASAP Acts, emphasizing that early detection and real support for families cannot wait.

Goodlander cosponsored the bipartisan ASAP Act, which would provide Medicare coverage for qualifying blood-based dementia screening tests and help patients obtain earlier diagnoses.

She helped introduce the bipartisan Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act, which would streamline prior authorization in Medicare Advantage so providers can spend more time caring for patients and less time navigating paperwork.

Goodlander cosponsored the bipartisan CONNECT for Health Act, which would permanently expand Medicare telehealth access—an important tool for seniors and families who live far from specialty-care providers.

Her broader rural-health record includes cosponsoring the bipartisan Rural Hospital Stabilization Act, supporting grants to help struggling rural hospitals remain open.

Goodlander also cosponsored the bipartisan Community Paramedicine Act of 2025, which would support community-based paramedicine programs in rural areas.

title: Goodlander Joins House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Democrats to Condemn OMB Rule Politicizing Federal Grantmaking
text:
Washington, D.C. — Last week, Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) joined House Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Takano and Democratic members of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee in submitting a public comment opposing a proposed rule from the Office of Management and Budget that would allow political appointees to make decisions relating to federal grants.

In the comment letter, the Democratic members highlighted the particular risks this rule could have on the veteran community: “Undermining agencies historically shielded from partisan influence risks immeasurable damage. Public trust is particularly critical for the veteran community: how can future generations be expected to serve if the government routinely compromises the care promised to veterans? Stable federal grant administration free from political interference is essential to maintaining that trust.”

Among other things, the proposed rule would:

Allow political appointees, instead of subject-matter experts, to decide which grants to issue;

Allow political appointees to terminate grants at any time if the grants don’t align with their political interests;

Ban funds for research or programs that support “DEI” or “gender ideology,” which will impact research and programs focused on women and minority veterans; and

Damage career development opportunities for researchers, which could make it harder for researchers to discuss their work and for VA to recruit and retain researchers.

This proposed rule was first published in the Federal Register on May 29, 2026, and has received consistent criticism from the scientific community and from numerous stakeholders. All Democratic members of the House Veterans’ Affairs Committee joined the public comment letter to express serious concerns with the proposed rule.

title: RELEASE: At Intelligence Committee Hearing to Review 9/11 Commission Findings Ahead of 25th Anniversary, Gottheimer Warns of AI-Driven Threats

“September 11th was the darkest day in our nation’s history,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “In Jersey, we lost 750 residents that morning, and thousands more since due to 9/11-related illnesses. They were friends, neighbors, and family. Thousands of Jersey and New York law enforcement, firefighters, EMTs, and other heroes answered the call and rushed toward the danger as others ran out.”

As Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on the National Security Agency and Cyber, and as Co-Chair of the House Democratic Commission on AI and the Innovation Economy, Gottheimer emphasized the need to ensure that the Intelligence Community is equipped for the threats of tomorrow while positioning America to win the AI race against China. He also underscored the bipartisan responsibility to ensure such devastating attacks never happen again.

“The attacks on 9/11 took years of planning, training camps, and dozens of people,” Gottheimer continued. “AI is collapsing all of that, letting a small cell or a hostile government move at machine speed. We must defend our grid, water systems, and ports from cyberattack, counter foreign disinformation online, and make sure America — not Beijing — sets the rules for this critical technology.”

The hearing featured testimony from leading national security experts on the current and emerging threats facing the United States and how best to position the Intelligence Community to defend against them.

RELEASE: Reps. Gottheimer and Kean Introduce Resolution to Keep Delaware Water Gap a National Recreation Area, Citing Local Input
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — U.S. Representatives Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) and Tom Kean Jr. (NJ-7) introduced a House resolution opposing the redesignation of the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area as a national park and preserve, pointing to a lack of local support for the change. The resolution was introduced by Representative Kean, whose district includes the Gap.

The push follows years of periodic proposals to convert the Gap’s designation, and comes after extensive outreach to the North Jersey communities that surround it. Gottheimer has said from the beginning that any decision on the Gap’s future needed to be driven by the towns and residents most affected by it.

“As I’ve said from day one, this matter required significant local input because it directly impacts many North Jersey townships, boroughs, and residents,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “I have immense trust in the mayors and local governments of the Fifth District and their ability to represent the views of our shared constituents. Following constructive discussions with local mayors and officials, and solicitation of local input, it does not seem that the proposal to redesignate the Delaware Water Gap as a national park has the necessary local support to move forward.”

“The Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area is an important resource for our region. New Jerseyans have enjoyed fishing, hunting, boating, camping, canoeing, and more there for decades. It is critical that the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area remain a designated Recreation Area so it can continue to be enjoyed by visitors and local residents, rather than threatening its purpose and local outdoor recreation activities by redesignating it a national park,” said Congressman Tom Kean Jr. (NJ-7).

“The Delaware Water Gap Defense Fund has strongly opposed changing its designation to a national park and preserve since 2022,” said Sandy Hull, founder of the Delaware Water Gap Defense Fund. “This resolution reflects cooperative efforts by Congressmen Kean and Gottheimer to maintain the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area as a national recreation area. Support for preserving its current status comes from millions of residents in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, supported by hunting, environmental, recreational, historical, and cultural organizations. As a living legacy of the tragic Tocks Island Dam project, Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area deserves protection, and we thank all who continue to stand up for its history and natural beauty.”

The Delaware Water Gap spans nearly 70,000 acres across New Jersey and Pennsylvania and is currently managed as a National Recreation Area — a designation that supports fishing, hunting, hiking, boating, camping, canoeing, and other activities enjoyed by residents and visitors. It is also home to numerous rare, threatened, and endangered species.

The resolution states that it is the sense of the House of Representatives that the Delaware Water Gap should remain designated as a National Recreation Area, that Congress should continue supporting local access to outdoor recreation, and that no federal funds should be used to pursue redesignating the Gap as a national park and preserve.

Find text of the resolution here.

title: Guthrie, Energy and Commerce Advance Legislation to Protect Ratepayers from Increased Energy Costs Related to Data Center Development
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the House Committee on Energy and Commerce advanced the Ratepayer Protection Act to the full House of Representatives unanimously. Congressman Brett Guthrie (KY-02), Chairman of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce, spoke in support of this legislation, which, if signed into law, would prevent ratepayers from footing the bill for upgrades to any energy generation, transmission, or distribution infrastructure for newly constructed data centers.

Excerpts from Chairman Guthrie’s remarks on the Ratepayer Protection Act from today’s Full Committee Markup as prepared for delivery.

title: Congressman Rogers Votes to Extend Federal Funding Through December,  Preventing a Government Shutdown
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Rep. Harold “Hal” Rogers (KY-05) voted for the Continuing Appropriations Act of 2027 (H.R. 9770), extending federal funding and government operations through December 4, 2026.

The House Appropriations Committee passed all 12 federal funding bills for fiscal year 2027, sending them on to the full House of Representatives, where three of those bills have also been passed by the House. It is the Committee’s fastest completion of the bills since fiscal year 2020.

“This extension simply gives us more time to work with the Senate on federal funding bills ahead of the end of the fiscal year on September 30. We are removing the fear of another looming federal shutdown with the assurance that we have more time, if necessary, to work with the Senate to get these comprehensive funding bills finalized,” said Congressman Rogers, Chairman Emeritus of the House Appropriations Committee. “It ensures all critical programs will continue uninterrupted, including SNAP and WIC benefits, disaster relief, flood insurance, and the like, through December 4, 2026.”

The Congressional Budget Office estimated that the 43-day government shutdown in 2025 cost between $7 billion and $14 billion in lost real Gross Domestic Product.

Supporting this legislation keeps the government open, protects national security and essential services, and preserves the path to completing full-year FY27 appropriations before the end of the year.

The Continuing Appropriations Act passed the House and now moves to the Senate for consideration.

title: Congressman Hamadeh Introduces the Bipartisan BRRRRT Act to Preserve the A-10 Mission and Protect U.S. Warfighters
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ-08) proudly introduced the bipartisan Bolstering Recognition, Resurgence, Retention, and Remembrance of the Thunderbolt (BRRRRT) Act, legislation aimed at preserving the A-10 Thunderbolt II mission. This legislation will ensure that warriors who serve on our front lines have the most lethal close air support until a certified replacement is operational.

The BRRRRT Act, named after the "Brrrrrrrrt," sound the aircraft makes when striking enemy forces while providing close air support (CAS), requires the U.S. Air Force to maintain the aircraft through Fiscal Year 2033.

Congressman Hamadeh is joined by Congressman Don Davis (NC-01) as co-leader, reflecting monumental bipartisan support. Cosponsors include Reps. Richard McCormick (GA-7), Derrick Van Orden (WI-3), Sam Graves (MO-6), and Cory Mills (FL-7).

"The A-10 has repeatedly proven itself on the battlefield, saving American lives and delivering unmatched close air support when our troops need it most," said Congressman Hamadeh. "The BRRRRT Act ensures we do not retire a proven weapons system before a certified replacement exists. This is about common sense, national security, and keeping faith with the men and women who depend on the A-10 in combat."

Background:

The A-10 Thunderbolt II has served as the backbone of the U.S. Air Force's close air support mission for more than four decades, earning a reputation as a trusted platform for protecting American troops on the battlefield.

In April 2026, at the request of President Donald Trump and Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, the Secretary of the Air Force announced that the Air Force will keep the A-10 Thunderbolt II flying through 2030.

According to the military, the Air Force "plans to extend two squadrons of A-10s to 2030, one active-duty squadron at Moody AFB and one reserve squadron at Whiteman AFB."

While the Air Force has committed to maintaining the aircraft through Fiscal Year 2030, current plans risk reducing critical training and maintenance capacity before a certified replacement capability is available.

title: Harshbarger Statement on FY27 Appropriations
text:
Washington, D.C — Congresswoman Diana Harshbarger (R-TN) today released the following statement after voting to pass H.R. 9770, the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027. The vote comes as Senate Democrats yet again threaten to shut down the government ahead of the September 30 fiscal year-end deadline, just weeks before Election Day. This clean, short-term funding measure keeps the government open through December 4, 2026, taking that leverage off the table and sparing the American people from unnecessary uncertainty, disruption, and political brinkmanship:

“After Democrats drove the two longest government shutdowns in American history, they are once again obstructing the constitutional funding process. Senate Democrats are refusing to advance a single FY27 appropriations bill in the upper chamber, and House Democrats have shown today that this isn't only a Senate problem—it's a Democrat problem, top to bottom.

“House Republicans have done the work. Every single appropriations bill is out of committee, three have already passed the Floor, and we're acting weeks ahead of the September 30 deadline to keep the government open. Democrats in both chambers have done nothing but obstruct, because a shutdown right before an election is the only leverage they've got left.

“While Democrats want to hold federal workers, military families, and Americans relying on SNAP and WIC hostage to score political points, House Republicans are taking proactive steps to reject last-minute governing and shutdown politics before the election.

“Tennesseans don't want Washington playing games with a government shutdown, they want us doing our jobs. That's exactly what tonight's vote was about.”

BACKGROUND:

The legislation extends government funding at current levels while the House continues work on full-year fiscal 2027 appropriations. House Republicans have pushed to fund the government through regular order rather than a last-minute, pork-filled omnibus. All 12 FY27 appropriations bills have been reported out of the House Appropriations Committee, and three have passed the House Floor with bipartisan support. The Senate has yet to advance any FY27 appropriations bill due to Democrat-led obstruction.

The stopgap keeps the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP), Special Supplemental Nutrition Program for Women, Infants, and Children (WIC), Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), the National Flood Insurance Program, the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) Disaster Relief Fund, and other essential programs funded without interruption, and includes no partisan add-ons.

Supporting this legislation keeps the government open, protects national security and essential services, and preserves the path to completing full-year FY27 appropriations during the remainder of the 119th Congress.

title: House Passes 2 Huizenga Measures in Bipartisan Bill to Help Main Street, Improve Affordability
text:
Tonight, Congressman Bill Huizenga (R-MI), Vice Chairman of the House Financial Services Committee, released the following statement after the U.S. House of Representatives passed H.R. 6955, the Main Street Capital Access Act. This legislation is designed to strengthen community banks, expand access to credit, and end debanking. Importantly, this bipartisan bill includes two measures authored by Huizenga that strengthen oversight and promote greater competition within the banking system.

"Washington should not be making life more expensive for Americans with needless red tape,” said Congressman Bill Huizenga. “Less competition means fewer financing options, higher borrowing costs, and less investment on Main Street. By cutting through the red tape this bipartisan bill reduces costs and helps community lenders make life more affordable for American families. Lastly, I am glad this legislation includes my provisions to increase accountability and reduce concentration across our financial system.”

Access to affordable credit is critical for families buying a home, farmers investing in their operations, entrepreneurs starting a business, and employers creating jobs. The Main Street Capital Access Act removes unnecessary regulatory burdens on community banks, encourages the formation of new community banks, and allows local lenders to devote more resources to making loans.

Earlier today, Congressman Huizenga spoke on the floor in support of the Main Street Capital Access Act. The video of his remarks is available below.

The Main Street Capital Access Act incorporates two bills authored by Huizenga. The FDIC Board Accountability Act that strengthens governance and accountability at the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, as well as the Enhancing Bank Resolution Participation Act, which broadens participation in failed-bank resolutions to promote competition, protect depositors, and reduce concentration within the banking system. Together, these measures reflect Huizenga's continued work to ensure federal policy supports community financial institutions and the small businesses and families they serve.

The Main Street Capital Access Act passed the House by a vote of 270-155 and now advances to the Senate for consideration.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Ronny Jackson Advances Key National Security Provisions Through the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence
text:
WASHINGTON — Representative Ronny Jackson (TX-13) successfully advanced critical national security policies during the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence’s markup of the Fiscal Year 2027 Intelligence Authorization Act (IAA).

“Meeting the challenges posed by our adversaries requires an intelligence community that is both effective and worthy of the public's trust,” said Rep. Jackson. “This bill provides our intelligence agencies with the authorities and resources they need to address foreign threats while advancing much needed oversight and accountability of America’s intelligence apparatus. The provisions I secured during our markup will strengthen internal investigations procedures at the CIA, help ensure former intelligence officials cannot use their positions to benefit foreign adversaries, and reinforce responsible stewardship of taxpayer dollars.”

Rep. Jackson’s Included Amendments:

Intelligence Community Inspector General (ICIG) CIA Internal Investigative Procedures: Directs the ICIG to conduct an independent review and audit of the CIA’s Counterintelligence, Counterespionage, and Office of Security’s internal investigative activities, strengthening oversight, identifying systemic vulnerabilities, and ensuring these critical functions are carried out effectively and responsibly.

Foreign Adversary Post-Employment Restrictions: Imposes a 10-year post-employment ban on Senate-confirmed Intelligence Community officials from lobbying or representing foreign-adversary-controlled entities before the U.S. government, preventing the transfer of sensitive expertise and denying adversaries, like China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran, access to critical national security knowledge.

Intelligence Community Employee Private Counsel Expenses: Establishes uniform, IC-wide standards for the use of taxpayer funds for private counsel, ending ad hoc, agency-by-agency decisions that create inconsistencies, drive up costs, and increase the risk for conflicts of interest.

title: Jayapal Calls for an Independent Investigation into Toboso Killings
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) is calling for an independent, impartial, and credible investigation into the Philippine Army’s recent killing of 19 people in Toboso, Negros Occidental province. Among those killed were U.S. citizen civilians Kai Sorem, a resident of Seattle, and Lyle Prijoles.

“Ms. Sorem, a 26-year-old resident of Seattle committed to advancing the interests of the most marginalized Filipinos, had traveled to Negros in the Philippines earlier this year to learn about and document the conditions of rural Filipino communities. Mr. Prijoles, a resident of Hayward, California, was a human rights activist and advocate for underserved and rural Filipino communities, including farmworkers,” wrote the Members. “We urge the Government of the Philippines to ensure an independent, impartial, and credible investigation into these killings.”

On April 19, 2026, the 79th Infantry Battalion, 3rd Infantry Division shot and killed 19 people in Barangay Salamanca, Toboso, whom the Army has claimed were all New People’s Army combatants. However, reporting indicates that up to nine of those killed were civilians.

The Philippines’ Commission on Human Rights is currently investigating the incident. Investigations conducted by the commission have been regularly undermined by a lack of cooperation from security forces, including withholding evidence and intimidating witnesses. In this case, the crime scene was maintained by the Philippine Army unit involved in the killings.

The Toboso killings appear to be a part of a larger crackdown by the Philippine government targeting activists and members of progressive civil society organizations (CSOs). Philippine counter-terrorism laws, including the Anti-Terrorism Act and Terrorism Financing Act, are used to prosecute and imprison individuals from CSOs engaged in human rights advocacy, environmental protection, and humanitarian and development work.

The full text of the letter can be read here.

The letter was also signed by Representatives Maxine Dexter, M.D. (OR-03) Jesús G. “Chuy” García (IL-04), James P. McGovern (MA-02), Kweisi Mfume (MD-07), Johnny Olszewski, Jr. (MD-02), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), and Senators Jeffrey A. Merkley (D-OR), Adam B. Schiff (D-CA), and Chris Van Hollen (D-MD).

title: Kaptur Announces $250,000 in Awards for Drug-Free Communities
text:
Washington, DC — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09) announced $250,000 in Drug-Free Communities (DFC) awards for two Northwest Ohio communities. The awards will be given through the US Department of Health and Human Services and administered by the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. EHOVE Career Center’s Future Leaders Program in Sandusky and the Springfield Area Prevention Coalition in Swanton will each receive awards of $125,000 for substance-abuse prevention efforts. These two new awards continue Congresswoman Kaptur’s commitment as a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee to bring Federal dollars home where they are needed most.

“These funds benefit local organizations taking meaningful steps in their communities to prevent substance abuse, a critical issue in our region of Northwest Ohio,” said Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09). “By focusing prevention efforts on youth, we work to reduce the risk of future substance use as they age into adulthood. Encouraging Drug-Free Communities empowers those closest to the problem to take meaningful, lasting action.”

EHOVE Career Center serves both high school students and adults across Erie, Huron, and Ottawa counties who wish to advance their academic and technical skills in preparation for a career or higher education. Their Future Leaders program is a leadership club for high schoolers that encourages students to live drug-free and participate in community service. As part of the program, students take random, confidential drug screenings, reinforcing how small, positive decisions now can lead to success in the future.

Springfield Area Prevention Coalition provides community awareness education on the reduction and prevention of substance abuse. The Coalition serves residents of Swanton, Ohio. It participates in activities like Red Ribbon Week alongside Springfield school systems and community drug take back programs to promote healthy decisions and the benefits of living drug-free.

In 2018, Congresswoman Kaptur secured a $125,000 Drug-Free Communities award for the Erie County Health Department to combat substance abuse concerns. Additionally in 2023 Congresswoman Kaptur delivered a $1.8 Million Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) award to the Erie County Health Department, and in 2024 she delivered a $375,000 SAMHSA award for the Sandusky County Board of Health. Both SAMHSA awards were also aimed at addressing substance abuse prevention.

title: Kean, Gottheimer Introduce Resolution to Protect the Delaware Water Gap
text:
Image

July 21, 2026

(July 21, 2026) WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) and Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05) introduced a bipartisan resolution expressing support for maintaining the designation of the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area.

“The Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area is an important resource for our region,” said Congressman Kean. “New Jerseyans have enjoyed fishing, hunting, boating, camping, canoeing, and more there for decades. It is critical that the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area remain a designated Recreation Area so it can continue to be enjoyed by visitors and local residents, rather than threatening its purpose and local outdoor recreation activities by redesignating it a national park.”

“As I've said from day one, this matter required significant local input because it directly impacts many North Jersey townships, boroughs, and residents,” said Congressman Gottheimer. “I have immense trust in the mayors and local governments of the Fifth District and their ability to represent the views of our shared constituents. Following constructive discussions with local mayors and officials, and solicitation of local input, it does not seem that the proposal to redesignate the Delaware Water Gap as a national park has the necessary local support to move forward.”

“The Delaware Water Gap Defense Fund has strongly opposed changing its designation to a national park and preserve since 2022,” said Sandy Hull, founder of the Delaware Water Gap Defense Fund. “This resolution reflects cooperative efforts by Congressmen Kean and Gottheimer to maintain the Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area as a national recreation area. Support for preserving its current status comes from millions of residents in New Jersey and Pennsylvania, supported by hunting, environmental, recreational, historical, and cultural organizations. As a living legacy of the tragic Tocks Island Dam project, Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area deserves protection, and we thank all who continue to stand up for its history and natural beauty.”

Background:

The Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area is a 70,000-acre national recreation area in New Jersey and Pennsylvania. The area was designated as a recreation area by Congress in 1965 and given to the National Park Service for stewardship in 1975. It remains under the care of the NPS today.

Congressman Kean is a member of the Delaware River Watershed Caucus.

title: Kiggans, House Republicans Deliver Continuing Resolution to Safeguard Americans from Partisan Shutdown
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) voted in favor of the Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027, legislation that will extend government funding at Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26) levels through December 4, 2026 to prevent a lapse in government funding while Congress continues to work through Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) Appropriations.

The clean continuing resolution (CR) ensures critical government functions remain operational, protects national security priorities, and avoids disruptions to essential federal services and benefits millions of Americans rely on every day.

“My Republican colleagues and I have passed three of the full-year Appropriations bills for FY27 on the House Floor. Unfortunately, our colleagues in the Senate have yet to pass one. This threatens another partisan shutdown which would jeopardize timely paychecks for our men and women in uniform as well as our federal workers, and disrupt SNAP benefits for vulnerable Americans,” said Congresswoman Kiggans.

With the September 30th deadline quickly approaching, the Continuing Appropriations Act is a stopgap to ensure the federal government remains open if Congress isn’t able to pass the nine remaining Appropriations bills. While the bill extends FY26 funding levels through December 4th, Congress will continue to work through the FY27 Appropriations process.

Kiggans said, “While a continuing resolution is never my preferred outcome, I am committed to keeping our government open and working for Virginia’s Second District. This bill is a short-term stopgap to avoid a lapse in federal services due to potential partisan gridlock. I’ve supported all three of the FY27 Appropriations bills the House has seen thus far, and I look forward to advancing the nine remaining bills to fully fund our government through 2027.”

Read the bill here.

Background:

Since entering Congress in 2023, Rep. Kiggans has repeatedly voted to keep the government open when partisan bickering threatened a shutdown.

Most recently, the longest shutdown in American history shuttered Transportation Security Administration (TSA), Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA), and U.S. Coast Guard personnel as these agencies faced a funding lapse.

Rep. Kiggans voted to keep the government open. Read her statement at the beginning of the October-November 2025 government shutdown here.

She has supported measures to ensure servicemembers, federal employees, and the millions of Americans who rely on critical government services are not caught in the middle of Washington dysfunction.

In September 2025, Kiggans introduced the Pay Our Troops Act for the third time, which would ensure servicemembers still receive their paychecks in the event of a government shutdown. Read her press release here.

In October 2025, the Congresswoman introduced the Pay Our Public Shipyard Workers Act which would protect the paychecks of the civilian and military workforce during government shutdowns. Read her press release here.

In July 2026, Congresswoman Kiggans voted for the National Security, Department of State, and Related Programs Appropriations Act, 2027. Read her press release here.

In June 2026, Congresswoman Kiggans voted for the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2027. Read her press release here.

title: Krishnamoorthi and McMaster Warn Against Deploying Troops to 2026 Polling Places at House Intelligence Committee Hearing
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, today questioned witnesses during the committee's hearing, "25 Years After 9/11: Confronting the Next Generation of Threats," after President Trump recently refused to rule out deploying the National Guard or ICE to polling places during the 2026 elections. During the hearing, retired Lieutenant General H.R. McMaster reaffirmed that discussing a military role in U.S. elections is "irresponsible" and warned that doing so is "extremely dangerous and damaging" because it threatens to politicize the armed forces.

Krishnamoorthi raised the issue during an exchange with retired Lieutenant General H.R. McMaster, who had previously warned before the 2020 election that discussing the military's role in elections was “irresponsible.”

Congressman Krishnamoorthi: In September 2020, before the November 2020 election, President Trump refused to commit to a peaceful transfer of power, suggesting he could invoke the Insurrection Act to involve the military. In response, you told Meet the Press that it was 'irresponsible' to discuss the military's role in the 2020 election. You said that, right? And now, as we approach the 2026 elections, President Trump again is not ruling out sending the National Guard or ICE to polling places. General, I assume it's again irresponsible to discuss the military's role in the upcoming 2026 election, right?

General H.R. McMaster: Yes. I think it's really important to recognize that our founders, 250 years ago, were most concerned about the military becoming involved in politics, and George Washington set the example during our Revolution. Lately, there has been a tendency to lay out an expectation that the military should be a check on executive authority or should be an arm of the executive authority in activities such as this, which threaten to politicize the military. I think it's extremely dangerous and damaging to that bold line that has to remain in place between our military and partisan politics.

Following the exchange, Krishnamoorthi warned that President Trump's recent comments risk politicizing the military.

“President Trump's willingness to discuss deploying the military to polling places undermines one of the oldest and most important traditions of our democracy. The American people deserve elections decided by voters—not by intimidation. Our armed forces have earned the trust of the American people by remaining above partisan politics, and we should keep it that way,” Congressman Krishnamoorthi said.

Krishnamoorthi also questioned witnesses about the Trump Administration's decision to condition counterterrorism funding on election-related mandates, pressing them on whether redirecting homeland security resources in that way could leave the nation less prepared to confront evolving threats.

He also pressed witnesses on the growing national security implications of artificial intelligence, including the threat that AI-generated deepfakes and other synthetic media could be exploited by foreign adversaries to manipulate public opinion, undermine confidence in democratic institutions, and threaten national security.

title: Krishnamoorthi Secures Provisions on China, Iran, AI, and Prediction Markets While Fighting Politicization of the Intelligence Community
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a senior member of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence, today announced that several of his intelligence oversight priorities were included in the Intelligence Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, which was approved by the House Intelligence Committee.

Among the provisions Krishnamoorthi helped secure are requirements for new intelligence assessments on China's economy and the global consequences of Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, stronger safeguards to prevent intelligence personnel from using nonpublic information to trade on prediction markets, and new oversight of how artificial intelligence is deployed across the Intelligence Community.

"At a time when the United States faces growing threats from China, Iran, and other adversaries, Congress should be focused on strengthening our Intelligence Community, not distracting it with politically motivated investigations," Congressman Krishnamoorthi said. "I'm proud to have secured provisions that will strengthen congressional oversight, improve our understanding of emerging threats, and ensure intelligence resources are used responsibly. Although my amendment to prevent intelligence resources from being diverted to relitigating the 2020 election was rejected, I'll continue fighting to keep our intelligence agencies focused on protecting the American people."

During the markup, Krishnamoorthi also offered an amendment to prohibit National Intelligence Program funds from being used by the FBI to investigate the 2020 election in Fulton County, Georgia. Krishnamoorthi argued that FBI intelligence personnel and resources should instead remain focused on genuine foreign intelligence, counterterrorism, cyber, and other national security threats. The committee rejected the amendment.

title: Landsman Leads Letter to Marco Rubio on Malaysia Hunting Down and Removing Jews

But, it is totally unacceptable that a head of government has publicly declared that his country will hunt down and expel citizens of our close ally based solely on their nationality. It should not be underwritten by the American taxpayer.

“This is also a government that maintains open ties with Hamas. Hamas fighters have even trained on Malaysian soil. The Malaysian government welcomes terrorists while targeting Jews.

title: Congressman Langworthy Introduces Legislation to Modernize Hydropower Permitting, Cut Red Tape, and Strengthen American Energy Production
text:
Washington, D.C.—July 21, 2026… Congressman Nick Langworthy (NY-23) and Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) today introduced the Fair Licensing for Operations of Water Structures (FLOWS) Act, bipartisan legislation to modernize the federal permitting process for hydropower projects by eliminating unnecessary regulatory burdens, streamlining approvals for routine maintenance, and supporting the next generation of American water energy technologies.

Hydropower is America's oldest source of renewable electricity and remains a critical component of the nation's energy portfolio, providing reliable, affordable electricity while supporting grid stability, flood control, and water management. However, outdated federal regulations often require operators to obtain approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) for routine maintenance and other low-risk activities, creating unnecessary delays, increasing costs, and diverting resources from improving reliability and modernizing infrastructure. The FLOWS Act updates that process while preserving FERC's authority over dam safety and environmental protections.

"Hydropower has powered communities across America for generations, but the federal permitting process hasn't kept pace with modern technology or common sense," said Congressman Langworthy. "Too often, operators are forced to navigate unnecessary federal red tape just to perform routine maintenance or replace equipment with identical components. That drives up costs, delays improvements, and makes it harder to keep reliable, affordable power on the grid, while having no real impact on environmental safety. At a time when New Yorkers are being crushed by skyrocketing energy costs, this is bipartisan, common-sense legislation is essential to preserving the future of one of America’s most affordable sources of electricity.”

“The vast majority of Washington State’s energy comes from hydropower, making it essential that we efficiently maintain dams to support our communities,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “Helping our hydropower operators perform routine maintenance, repairs, replacements, and temporary adjustments for our dams will lower energy costs, ensure reliability, and improve public safety. This bill will also support emerging clean energy research as we find new ways to produce energy without emitting greenhouse gases.”

title: Latta's Bills to Combat Rising Synthetic Opioid Deaths Advanced by House Energy and Commerce Committee
text:
Today, the House Energy and Commerce Committee advanced two bills introduced by Congressman Bob Latta (OH-5) to combat the rising synthetic opioid deaths: The Strengthening Tools to Outlaw Poisonous (STOP) Nitazenes Act and Tyler’s Law. Additionally, the Committee also passed Congressman Latta's Nonprescription Drug Innovation Act (H.R.9774) as part of the Lower Costs, More Transparency Act (H.R.9393).

The Strengthening Tools to Outlaw Poisonous (STOP) Nitazenes Act would schedule 2-benzylbenzimidazole opioids, commonly known as nitazenes, as Schedule I controlled substances. Fatal overdoses continue to rise across the United States, and nitazenes, a dangerous class of illicit synthetic opioids, are increasingly contributing to overdose deaths nationwide. Depending on the chemical formulation, some nitazenes can be up to 800 times more potent than morphine and 40 times more potent than fentanyl. Like other illegal street drugs that are often laced with fentanyl, substances may also contain nitazenes without the user’s knowledge.

Tyler's Law requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to complete a study on how frequently hospitals test for fentanyl in patients experiencing an overdose and to use the results of the study to issue guidance to hospitals on implementing fentanyl testing in emergency rules. Congressman Latta is the lead sponsor from the Energy and Commerce Committee and has been working on this legislation since 2023.

The Nonprescription Drug Innovation Act would establish a new “Priority Nonprescription Drug” designation to help expedite the development and review of certain over-the-counter (OTC) medications to give consumers access to manage their own care in a safe and affordable manner.

“Today’s advancement of the STOP Nitazenes Act and Tyler’s Law out of committee is an important step forward in our efforts to save lives and confront the devastating impact of synthetic opioids in communities across the country. These bills will help ensure hospitals and health officials have the tools, data, and authorities they need to respond more effectively to overdoses and keep dangerous substances like nitazenes off our streets. I urge the House floor to take up this legislation immediately,” said Latta.

title: Ranking Member Lofgren's Opening Statement at Full Committee Markup of H.R. 3168, H.R. 8437, H.R. 9326, and H.R. 8981
text:
(Washington, DC) — Today, the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology is holding a Full Committee Markup of H.R. 3168, National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2025; H.R. 8437,Geo POWER Act; H.R. 9326,USA Act; and H.R. 8981, SCALE Biology Act.

Ranking Member Zoe Lofgren's (D-CA) opening statement as prepared for the record is below:

Thank you, Chairman Babin for holding this markup today. It’s a busy day on the Hill so I hope we can move through the bills and amendments quickly.

The first bill on the roster is the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program Reauthorization Act of 2025. Earthquakes are an unfortunate fact of life in California. Earlier this year, researchers at the University of Hawaii reported that the San Jacinto and San Andreas faults, are at their highest stress level in 1000 years. It’s scary to imagine, but we can prepare and minimize loss of life and infrastructure by implementing the best possible building codes, warning-systems, and post-earthquake responses. This Committee has a role in making that possible. The last time we reauthorized the NEHRP program was in the 115th Congress and it expired in 2023. The Senate passed a comprehensive NEHRP reauthorization months ago, which we could have expediently passed into law. The ANS we are considering today adopts most of the language included in the Senate version with some additional improvements. This legislation will go a long way to protecting both life and property in all areas of the country at risk from earthquakes. I support this bill and the amendment made to it and I encourage my colleagues to do the same.

The GEO Power Act continues this committee’s tradition of developing good bipartisan energy legislation aimed at diversifying our clean energy sources and tackling the climate crisis. Yesterday, the House passed the Next Generation Geothermal Research and Development Act in an overwhelming bipartisan vote. Before us today is an important bill that authorizes the next step from what just passed the House - by enabling the scale-up of promising new geothermal technologies into commercially viable solutions. I thank my colleagues, Representatives Begich and Salinas for their leadership on this bill.

Next is the Utilize Standards for All Act. This legislation would address some of the many challenges facing U.S. leadership in international standardization activities. It aims to foster greater US participation in international standards development bodies and to encourage those organizations to conduct their meetings in the United States. While this bill is a good first step, we must remain focused on breaking down the biggest barrier to U.S.-based standards meetings, which is our own government-imposed limitations on visas for foreign technical experts to enter the U.S. for these forums. We also need to ensure we fund these efforts with appropriations. I support my colleague, Representative Webster’s bill, and I hope we can continue to work together to address the full range of challenges to continued U.S. leadership in international standards setting.

The last bill on the roster is Representative McClain-Delaney’s SCALE Biology Act. Several weeks ago, a team of scientists led by Dr. Kate Adamala at the University of Minnesota reported that they had successfully synthesized a cell for the very first time in history. This dazzling feat demonstrates the U.S.’s burgeoning capability in new forms of biotechnology.

The best way to build on this momentous innovation is to elevate our ability to measure the biological inputs that made this possible in the first place, and ensure we can pursue this innovation responsibly, safely, and securely. The SCALE Biology Act does all of this and reinforces U.S. leadership in engineering biology and biomanufacturing. I am very proud of my Democratic colleague’s hard work and commitment to this issue and to the work at NIST.

And with that said, Mr. Chairman, I am excited to get started on today’s markup and yield back the balance of my time.

title: Rep. Anna Paulina Luna Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect Americans from Poisonous Pesticides
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13), joined by co-lead Rep. Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) and original cosponsors Reps. Thomas Massie (KY-04) and Reps. Chellie Pingree (ME-01), today introduced the Americans vs. Poisonous Pesticides Act. This legislation would amend the Federal Insecticide, Fungicide, and Rodenticide Act (FIFRA) to preserve state failure-to-warn claims that are consistent with federal pesticide misbranding standards and prevent manufacturers from using EPA registration or label approval as a complete defense against those claims.

“The Supreme Court’s ruling created a loophole where EPA silence can be used to shield corporate silence,” said Congresswoman Luna. “Families harmed by dangerous products should not lose their right to justice simply because a federal agency failed to require a warning. Our bill protects Americans’ ability to have their claims heard and makes clear that EPA approval is not a license for pesticide manufacturers to conceal serious risks.”

Under the current FIFRA provisions, recent court decisions, including the Supreme Court’s ruling in Monsanto Co. v. Durnell, have allowed EPA approval of a pesticide label to block state failure-to-warn claims even when plaintiffs allege the label omitted serious health or environmental risks. The Americans vs. Poisonous Pesticides Act would ensure that EPA approval alone does not preempt those lawsuits when they are based on the same misbranding standards already established under FIFRA, preserving the ability of farmers, farmworkers, and consumers to hold pesticide manufacturers accountable for inadequate warnings.

“In Monsanto v. Durnell, the Supreme Court ruled that Monsanto/Bayer can’t be sued for omitting a warning even if their herbicides do cause cancer,” said Rep. Thomas Massie (R-KY). “Even if the legal reasoning of the court is sound, it’s a blatant travesty of justice. Congress and the President can fix this, and we absolutely should.”

Under the bill, EPA registration and label approval would remain evidence that a pesticide complies with federal law, but would no longer be conclusive or automatically prevent an individual from pursuing a state-law claim. State claims that enforce the same misbranding standards already established under FIFRA would be allowed to proceed, with a safeguard provision ensuring the bill only adds protections and cannot be used to reduce, restrict, or eliminate any right, lawsuit, or protection already available under state law.

“Glyphosate is dangerous – unlimited exposure can have fatal consequences, but corporate interests are lobbying to keep it on the shelves,” said Rep. Rosa DeLauro (D-CT). “If the EPA will not do its job, Congress must act to protect Americans. The Supreme Court tied the hands of victims – establishing a liability shield and limiting states’ ability to enforce their own safety requirements. Giant corporations do not need a liability shield when their product harms individuals. They need accountability. Americans deserve protection. I am proud to partner with my colleagues in this bipartisan fight to protect the health of Americans, eliminate blanket liability protections, and improve labeling so people know how to handle these products safely.”

The bill would also provide a pathway for a pesticide manufacturer to amend its label when either the company or EPA obtains reliable information indicating that the product may be misbranded. Manufacturers would therefore be permitted to make the necessary change without waiting for prior EPA approval, while EPA would retain the authority to disapprove the amendment or take further action under federal law.

“The Supreme Court handed pesticide manufacturers a roadmap to escape accountability, even when they fail to warn people about serious health risks. That’s wrong. If a company learns its product may be harming people or the environment, it has a responsibility to say so, not hide behind a federal label approved years earlier,” said Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine). “The Americans vs. Poisonous Pesticides Act restores a basic principle: corporations that put profits ahead of people’s health should be held accountable. No one should lose their right to seek justice because a chemical company found a legal loophole.”

Reliable information under the legislation includes a government report, an independent peer-reviewed study, company data, material uncovered through legal discovery, whistleblower disclosures, congressional or other oversight investigations, and pesticide incident reports.

The changes would apply to pending and future civil actions, including cases on remand or appeal, regardless of when the conduct giving rise to the claim occurred. This provision would ensure that Americans whose cases were affected by the Supreme Court’s ruling are not permanently denied their opportunity to seek justice.

title: Mast introduces legislation to keep infant formula safe
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Representative Brian Mast (FL-21) today introduced legislation to establish enforceable federal safety standards for infant formula—giving the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) additional tools to hold manufacturers accountable and giving parents assurance that what they feed their newborns meet a federal standard. The bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act to require the FDA to establish and enforce maximum contaminant levels in infant formula.

“Parents should never have to wonder whether what they are feeding their newborn is safe,” said Congressman Brian Mast. “I’ve always said that if you wouldn’t put it in the bathtub with your kid, it shouldn’t be in our water. That goes for formula, too. The testing shows our formula supply is in good shape, and this bill makes sure it stays that way—putting specific, enforceable limits on the contaminants we don’t want anywhere near our kids, and holding manufacturers accountable for meeting them,” he added.

In April 2026, the FDA reported the largest examination of chemical contaminants in infant formula ever conducted in the United States with more than 120,000 data points from more than 300 formula samples. Thankfully, the results were largely favorable, but complacency cannot be tolerated. By putting enforceable federal standards behind that testing, it gives the FDA the force of law to ensure infant formula continues to meet the highest standards of safety as a habit of routine, not chance.

I’m also requiring the companies who make formulas to test their products first, archive each record, and then publicly report all results. Parents who look for honest data about what they feed their baby should be able to find it, and they should be able to find it easily.

Supporting families with the peace of mind where it counts is what I keep fighting for—our kids’ health isn’t up for debate.

title: MATSUI INTRODUCES NO PASSES FOR POLLUTERS ACT ALONGSIDE NATIONAL ENVIRONMENTAL AND PUBLIC HEALTH COALITION
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07), introduced the No Passes for Polluters Act, legislation to end the president’s unilateral authority to exempt private industrial facilities from key Clean Air Act protections.

Congresswoman Matsui announced the legislation during a press conference joined by Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and Ed Markey (D-MA), Earthjustice Action, and the Health Equity and Environment Action League (HEAL). The event highlighted policy solutions to curb the impacts of climate change and toxic pollution on Americans’ health.

“President Trump has abused the Clean Air Act to let more than 180 industrial facilities off the hook from key toxic pollution requirements,” said Congresswoman Matsui at the press conference. “Clean-air laws should not change based on who occupies the Oval Office, and they should not become something a company can sidestep with a simple call to the White House. The No Passes for Polluters Act will restore accountability and protect the basic federal safeguards every family depends on to breathe clean air.”

The legislation is co-led by Representatives Don Beyer (VA-08), Mike Levin (CA-49), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), and Maxine Dexter (OR-03). The companion bill is led in the Senate by Senators Whitehouse and Schiff (D-CA).

“The Trump administration’s corrupt polluter industry bosses will abuse every loophole available to pollute for free, damn the health consequences for Americans,” said Senator Whitehouse. “Our No Passes for Polluters Act will rein in Trump’s abuse of toxic chemical control exemptions to ensure this process is not used for corrupt giveaways to the fossil fuel industry.”

“President Trump’s EPA is allowing industrial polluters to apply for exemptions to the Clean Air Act’s limits on toxic emissions,” said Senator Schiff. “Trump is the first president to implement such a giveaway to the fossil fuel industry at the expense of our health. Our legislation will stop the administration from giving out free passes to polluters so we can keep our air breathable.”

“The Trump Administration has exploited loopholes to help the dirtiest and most expensive polluters avoid all accountability,” said Congressman Beyer. “Our No Passes for Polluters Act will reinforce Congress' original intent: to guarantee all Americans access to clean and healthy air, not to give free passes to facilities releasing coal waste, toxic metals, and dangerous chemicals and polluting our nation's air."

“During the 2024 election, President Trump promised fossil fuel companies that if they contributed $1 billion to his campaign, he would do whatever they wanted and bend regulations to their will. Big Oil delivered and we’ve seen President Trump keep his promise by rolling back critical environmental protections and scrapping rules that keep our air and water clean,” said Congressman Levin. “The No Passes for Polluters Act would prevent this pay-to-play scheme and block any President from exempting polluters from following the law. I am proud to partner with Reps. Matsui, Beyer, Dexter, and McClellan on this bill that would help ensure no company can further damage our environment and our planet.”

“As a mom to two young kids, I think often of the world we will leave the next generation and the steps we must take to ensure a clean, safe and habitable future for all. Yet the Trump Administration has taken unprecedented steps towards giving facilities a pass to get around the toxic pollution standards set under the Clean Air Act — making it that much easier to pollute with impunity,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “We must act now to prevent the President from unilaterally deciding who gets to play by the rules. The No Passes for Polluters Act would hold the fossil fuel industry accountable and uphold the health and safety of our communities, and I thank Congresswoman Matsui for her leadership on this issue.”

“Our children’s futures are too valuable for us to sit back and hope that polluters choose people over profits. Congress must guarantee they do,” said Congresswoman Dexter. “That’s why I am proud to support legislation to ensure that no president—Donald Trump or anyone who follows—can abuse the Clean Air Act to hand out special favors to polluters. As the first and only lung doctor in Congress, I am committed to enacting environmental laws guided by science, not political favors for corporate polluters.”

Background

In 2025, President Trump began granting unprecedented two-year exemptions from Clean Air Act hazardous air pollution standards to private industrial facilities. To date, more than 180 facilities have received exemptions from safeguards designed to protect nearby communities from toxic emissions.

The Administration’s unprecedented use of this authority left companies unsure how to even request an exemption. According to ProPublica, one company representative emailed the EPA asking, “Hello, I am a gas company looking for an exemption. How do I start?” The Administration ultimately accepted emailed requests before granting sweeping exemptions across multiple industries, a clear effort to shield polluters from following the law and part of a broader pattern that now includes pardons for individuals convicted of environmental crimes.

The No Passes for Polluters Act would end the President’s unilateral authority to exempt private industrial facilities from these Clean Air Act protections and strengthen congressional oversight of the remaining exemption authorities under sections 118(b), 248(e), and 604(f).

The Natural Resources Defense Council, Environmental Defense Fund Action, Earthjustice Action, Sierra Club, and WE ACT for Environmental Justice endorsed the legislation.

“The Trump administration is illegally giving the nation's most hazardous industries a free pass to spew toxic pollution. In a matter of months, the most dangerous facilities in states across the country have been freed to put communities at risk of premature death, respiratory illness, and lifelong harm to children,” said Sam Goodstein, Managing Director of Federal Affairs, NRDC. “These exemptions are part of a broader pattern of sidestepping Congress and federal agencies and shutting communities out of decisions that affect their health. Congress must act to adapt the law to a presidency acting so consistently and fundamentally lawlessly, and the ‘No Passes for Polluters Act’ presents a way to do just that.”

“President Trump’s unlawful free passes to pollute have allowed 180 large industrial polluters around the country to avoid Clean Air Act protections for some of the most dangerous pollutants known to science, including mercury, lead and arsenic – putting the health of millions of Americans at risk,” said Joanna Slaney, Vice President for Political and Government Affairs, Environmental Defense Fund. “No other administration has so brazenly flouted the Clean Air Act. The No Passes for Polluters Act is vital to protect the health of every American from the Trump administration’s unlawful waivers for industrial polluters.”

“Americans deserve a government that works to protect public health and ensure the air we breathe is free from toxic chemicals, not one that gives corporations a free pass to pollute,” said Liz Ruben, Senior Legislative Representative, Earthjustice Action. “We're grateful to Representatives Matsui, Dexter, Levin, McClellan, and Beyer for fighting against this administration’s polluter-friendly policies and standing up for people's right to breathe clean, safe air.”

“The Trump-Zeldin EPA has bent over backward to cater to the needs of fossil fuel companies and corporate polluters, all at the expense of the health of our people and our communities,” said Patrick Drupp, Director of Climate Policy, Sierra Club. “Their polluter-first agenda to skirt the Clean Air Act has made the air we breathe and water we drink less safe, leaving the American people with little to show for it but higher costs and increased risk of asthma, heart and lung disease, and cancer. We thank Representatives Matsui, Beyer, Dexter, Levin, and McClellan for working to rein in this abuse.”

title: Rep. Lucy McBath Announces CobbWorks, Inc. Will Receive $1.5 Million Department of Labor Grant

title: McClain Delaney's Bipartisan SCALE Biology Act Advances Out of House Science, Space, and Technology Committee
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman April McClain Delaney's (D-MD-06) bipartisan Standards and Calibration for American Leadership in Engineering Biology (SCALE Biology) Act advanced this week out of the House Science, Space, and Technology Committee, marking a significant step forward in strengthening U.S. leadership in biotechnology.

The SCALE Biology Act would establish a dedicated biometrology research program at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST). Biometrology—the science of measurement applied to engineering biology—is essential to advancing healthcare, domestic biomanufacturing, agricultural innovation, public health, and national security.

As the bioeconomy continues to grow, researchers, regulators, and industry need a common framework for measuring and evaluating biological systems. The SCALE Biology Act would direct NIST to develop standardized measurements, methodologies, guidelines, and best practices, creating a shared foundation that accelerates innovation and strengthens America's global competitiveness.

"The global race for biotechnology leadership isn't slowing down, and neither can we," said Rep. McClain Delaney. "The United States has the talent and the innovation to lead, including the expert researchers at NIST who call Maryland’s Sixth District home, but we need the standards that allow groundbreaking discoveries to move from the lab to the marketplace. The SCALE Biology Act will help establish those standards and ensure America remains the global leader in biotechnology."

Maryland's Sixth District is home to one of the nation's premier biotechnology ecosystems, including the I-270 Technology Corridor—often referred to as "DNA Valley"—as well as world-renowned federal research institutions such as NIST, NIH, and the National Biodefense and Countermeasures Center, National Interagency Confederation for Biological Research at Fort Detrick. Advancing the SCALE Biology Act reinforces the region's leadership in biotechnology while strengthening America's innovation, competitiveness, health and well-being.

title: McClellan Bill to Increase Data Transparency for Medicare Advantage Supplemental Benefits Advances
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04)’s bill, H.R. 5243, unanimously advanced out of the Energy & Commerce Committee to the House floor for a vote as part of H.R. 9393, the Lower Costs, More Transparency Act of 2026. McClellan’s bill requires Medicare Advantage plan providers to submit enrollee-level data on supplemental benefits to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS). This requirement will increase transparency around supplemental benefits to help seniors choose the best plan for their needs.

“Seniors deserve the most up-to-date and accurate information about the benefits and providers available to them when making health care coverage decisions. Yet a lack of data around Medicare Advantage supplemental benefit plans leads too many people to make decisions that don’t fully meet their needs,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “This lack of transparency also weakens our ability to assess whether these Medicare Advantage plans provide adequate care. My bill will make it easier for seniors to personalize their health care choices and improve their health care outcomes. I thank the Committee for its consideration and advancement of this bill, and I urge my House colleagues to bring it up for a vote as soon as possible.”

Nationally, over half of eligible Medicare beneficiaries are enrolled in Medicare Advantage plans, which can choose to offer benefits not covered under Original Medicare. However, there is no requirement to specifically report on supplemental benefits or their utilization.

McClellan’s bill mandates reporting on data on eligibility for supplemental benefits, the types of benefit categories offered, and utilization of and payments for supplemental benefits. It also requires HHS to publish the data annually with appropriate patient confidentiality safeguards in place.

title: McIver Introduces Bill to Strengthen Small Business Development Centers
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: July 21, 2026

Contact: NJ10Press@mail.house.gov

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) introduced the Small Business Development Centers Improvement Act of 2026. The bill will make sure entrepreneurs and small business owners have access to tools that make starting and strengthening their businesses possible. Specifically, the bill would reauthorize the Small Business Development Center (SBDC) Program at up to $175 million annually through FY2029 while strengthening the program and expanding access to free business counseling and technical assistance.

This legislation is urgently needed as the Trump Administration has once again targeted the SBDC Program for elimination in its FY2027 budget. McIver’s legislation would keep the administration from gutting a program that has, for decades, helped working people, especially low-income, minority, and female entrepreneurs, build businesses, create jobs, and contribute to local economies.

“This bill is about standing up for working people. Small businesses are the bedrock of our communities, and the tools that help them thrive are being threatened by Trump. We need legislation to protect working people, and the small businesses that let them accumulate wealth, from the administration’s constant attacks,” said Rep. McIver. “The SBDC Program is a proven resource and eliminating it will disproportionately harm the most vulnerable entrepreneurs and strip our communities of the establishments that make them special.”

The SBDC Program stands as one of the most effective tools the Small Business Administration (SBA) has to level the playing field for entrepreneurs and small business owners. In New Jersey, the SBDC at Rutgers University is a critical resource for countless businesses, including those in the 10th Congressional District. The Program’s work helping people start businesses, secure capital, and create jobs, is now under threat from an administration that wants to see these resources disappear.

The Small Business Development Centers Improvement Act of 2026 would:

Reauthorize the SBDC Program at up to $175 million annually through FY2029.

Allow SBDCs to use a small portion of their funding to better advertise their services so more entrepreneurs know help is available.

Improve how the SBA measures and reports the program's impact.Reduce unnecessary administrative burdens on SBDCs.

Strengthen privacy protections for small business owners receiving assistance.

Increase transparency and congressional oversight of SBA entrepreneurial development programs.

The legislation builds on bipartisan efforts from previous Congresses to modernize and strengthen the SBDC network while ensuring these critical services remain available to entrepreneurs and small businesses across the country.
