title: Flood Recovery Resources, Updates, and Assistance
text:
Communities across the Hill Country continue recovering from last week’s devastating floods. While we are grateful that the loss of life was far lower than during last year’s flood, two of our fellow Texans were tragically lost, and many communities sustained significant damage to homes, businesses, roads, and other infrastructure.

Damage assessments remain underway, and President Trump has approved a federal emergency declaration to support response efforts across the affected counties. My office remains in close coordination with local, state, and federal officials as our communities begin the work of recovering and rebuilding. Below are resources currently available to affected residents, businesses, and volunteers.

Report Storm Damage to TDEM

If your home or business sustained storm damage, please report it through the Texas Division of Emergency Management’s Individual State of Texas Assessment Tool, or ISTAT.

These reports are vital to helping state and federal officials understand the scope of the damage, deploy resources, and determine eligibility for additional recovery assistance. Completing the survey is not an application for financial assistance.

Please Fill Out the Survey: Here.

Kerr County

Debris Removal and Disaster Recovery

Kerr Together Disaster Recovery Center

98 Coronado Drive

Monday - Friday 8am-5pm

City of Ingram Debris Removal Site

Debris Dumpsters are available for City of Ingram residents this week from 9am to 4pm

Please bring a valid photo ID showing a City of Ingram address or a current utility bill showing an address within the City of Ingram

Volunteer Coordination

TDEM and the Office of the Governor have directed constituents interested in donating or volunteering to RebuildTX.org

Kerr Together is partnering with Global Empowerment Mission to place and coordinate volunteers. To register for volunteer opportunities, please contact Stephanie Hodges shodges@gem.org or call 830-255-7433.

Food and Meal Services

Volunteers with Mercy Chefs are providing food at 610 Methodist Encampment Road, Kerrville.

The Salvation Army is serving meals to support residents, clean-up crews, and first responders affected by recent flooding.

Today, units are serving meals at Ingram Fire Department at 215 TX-39, Ingram, TX, and Calvary Temple Church at 3000 SH 534, Kerrville. There is also another Salvation Army distribution location at 855 Hays Street, Kerrville. Open 10-4 starting tomorrow.

Kendall County

Kendall County residents are encouraged to report damage to the TDEM ISTAT survey so local officials can understand and deploy necessary resources. The link for TDEM ISTAT is here.

Kendall County officials expect to provide additional debris-removal information later this week.

Gillespie County

Property Clean-Up Assistance

Interested in receiving volunteer help with storm debris on your private property? Fill out the TDEM ISTAT survey and/or Contact amorris@fbgtx.org with Fredericksburg/Gillespie Emergency Coordinator Assistance.

Small Business Grants via LiftFund

The LiftFund is deploying small business grants for those impacted by the July 2026 Hill Country floods. Learn more about the Flood Relief Program here.

title: Rep. Salazar Signs Discharge Petition to Advance the American Dream and Promise Act for Dreamers and TPS Recipients
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Rep. María Elvira Salazar (FL-27), a co-lead of the American Dream and Promise Act, signed a discharge petition to bring the bipartisan legislation to the House floor for a vote. The American Dream and Promise Act would create earned pathways to lawful permanent residence for eligible Dreamers and recipients of Temporary Protected Status (TPS).

For years, Dreamers and TPS recipients have lived without a permanent solution from Congress, leaving their futures subject to changing administrations and court rulings. The discharge petition gives the House an opportunity to finally consider legislation that would provide lasting certainty through federal law.

"Dreamers didn't choose how they got here, but they chose what to do once they arrived. They studied, they worked, they served, they built. America is the only home they've ever known. Yet for years, they’ve had to live with a suitcase by the door, waiting for the next court ruling or the next president to decide their future," said Rep. Salazar. "I signed the discharge petition because Congress needs to act. As a co-lead of the American Dream and Promise Act, I am proud to support legislation that gives these young men and women the dignity they have earned: certainty to build their future in the only country they've ever called home.”

Rep. Salazar also emphasized that the American Dream and Promise Act would provide eligible TPS recipients with a long-overdue opportunity to earn permanent legal status after years of living under temporary humanitarian protections.

"Many TPS recipients came to the United States after fleeing failed regimes, violence, or humanitarian disasters in search of freedom and safety. For years, they have carried the responsibility of building a life here without the security of knowing they could keep it. They have worked, raised families, and strengthened our communities. Congress has delayed this conversation for far too long. It's time to let the House vote," Rep. Salazar continued.

The American Dream and Promise Act combines the bipartisan Dream Act and the American Promise Act into a single legislative package. The legislation would:

For eligible Dreamers:

Establish an earned pathway to lawful permanent residence.

Protect eligible applicants from removal while their applications are pending.

Require applicants to have arrived by age 18, meet education and background-check requirements, and complete a higher education, military service, or employment pathway to remove the conditional basis of their permanent residence.

For eligible TPS recipients:

Establish a pathway to lawful permanent residence.

Protect eligible applicants from removal while their applications are pending.

Replace temporary humanitarian protections with permanent legal status established through an act of Congress.

A discharge petition is a procedural mechanism that allows a majority of House Members to bring legislation to the House floor for consideration. Once 218 Members sign the petition, the House must vote on the American Dream and Promise Act.

title: Rep. Andrea Salinas Celebrates the Passage of Two Bipartisan Bills through the House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) celebrated the passage of two of her bills through the House of Representatives with overwhelming bipartisan support. Both of her bills, the Nucleic Acid Screening for Biosecurity Act and the Next-Generation Geothermal Research and Development Act, would strengthen two industries that are critical to Oregon’s future, support American workers, and help the United States remain a global leader in science and energy innovation.

“I am proud that two of my bills have passed the House floor with bipartisan support. My bills will support two industries that are critical to Oregon’s future: geothermal energy and biotechnology,” said Rep. Salinas. “My geothermal bill will help advance the research, testing, and workforce development needed to meet our electricity demand. And my nucleic acid bill will help ensure the safety and reliability of our scientific advancements in biotechnology and health care. Most importantly, both of these bills build on partnerships between government and local industries to create jobs and enhance our energy and biosecurity capabilities, all while delivering benefits for workers, consumers, and communities.”

TheNucleic Acid Screening for Biosecurity Act, co-led by Rep. Rich McCormick (GA-07), would develop technical standards and best practices for nucleic acid screening. The bill authorizes the Director of the National Institute of Standards & Technology (NIST) to carry out programs to support the development of technical standards and best practices related to nucleic acid screening. It would codify nucleic acid screening activities outlined in former President Biden’s Executive Order on the Safe, Secure, and Trustworthy Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence. These reliable standards would help protect the public, give researchers and biotechnology companies greater certainty, and strengthen the United States’ position as a global leader in scientific research.

The Next-Generation Geothermal Research and Development Act, co-led by Rep. Pat Harrigan (NC-10), would improve coordination between the Department of Energy (DOE) and the Department of the Interior to better understand and map geothermal resources across the country, expand testing capabilities at DOE’s Frontier Observatory for Research in Geothermal Energy sites, establish a geothermal Center of Excellence, and authorize $150 million per year through Fiscal Year 2031 to support these activities. These investments would help move promising geothermal technologies toward commercial use, create skilled jobs, and expand access to reliable domestic energy as electricity demand grows.

Both of the bills were passed with overwhelming bipartisan support and now await consideration in the U.S. Senate.

title: Rep. Andrea Salinas’ Statement Following Government Spending Bill Vote
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Andrea Salinas (OR-06) released the following statement regarding her vote against the government spending bill, known as the Continuing Resolution.

title: Rep. Derek Schmidt Joins Bipartisan Effort to Expand ABLE Savings for Americans with Disabilities
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Derek Schmidt (KS-02) today announced he has joined Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-06) as a co-lead of the bipartisan ABLE MATCH (Making Able a Tool to Combat Hardship) Act, legislation to help more Americans with disabilities build financial security through Achieving a Better Life Experience (ABLE) savings accounts.

The legislation would establish a federal matching contribution for eligible low- and moderate-income individuals who save in ABLE accounts, allowing beneficiaries to receive up to a 100 percent federal match on the first $2,000 they contribute annually, subject to income limits. The federal matching funds would be deposited directly into the beneficiary's ABLE account, helping individuals save for disability-related expenses without jeopardizing eligibility for critical benefits.

"ABLE accounts have provided many individuals with disabilities and their families an important tool to save for the future, but too many people still struggle to set aside money because of financial pressures," Congressman Schmidt said. "This bipartisan legislation helps make those savings go further by strengthening and expanding this successful program. Every Kansan deserves the opportunity to build greater financial security.”

"Financial independence shouldn’t be out of reach for individuals with disabilities,” Rep. Dingell said. “By reintroducing the ABLE MATCH Act, we are taking a crucial step toward economic security by matching the hard-earned savings of ABLE account beneficiaries through a refundable tax credit."

"I want to thank Congressman Derek Schmidt and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell for their bipartisan leadership in championing the ABLE MATCH Act,” said Sara Hart Weir, Executive Director for Kansas Council on Developmental Disabilities (KCDD). Kansas has shown that when states make a meaningful investment in ABLE outreach and partner across agencies, families respond. Through our statewide collaboration with the Kansas State Treasurer's Office, we've demonstrated that connecting people to ABLE accounts early and intentionally can transform lives. The ABLE MATCH Act will build on that success by ensuring that low- and moderate-income Kansans with disabilities don't just have access to an ABLE account—they have the financial incentive to start saving and building long-term independence. This legislation has the potential to dramatically scale ABLE participation in Kansas and across the nation."

“Beginning in 2027, the federal government will offer a powerful savings incentive designed to help millions of hard-working Americans save for retirement,” Kansas State Treasurer Steven Johnson said. “For disabled Americans who rely on an ABLE account for building wealth, the incentive funds offered by the Saver’s Match cannot be deposited into an ABLE account. As administrator of the Kansas ABLE Savings Plan, I applaud Congressman Schmidt and Congresswoman Dingell for working to address this savings disparity and giving ABLE account owners access to a powerful wealth-building incentive.”

ABLE accounts allow eligible individuals with disabilities to save money in tax-advantaged accounts to pay for qualified disability-related expenses without losing eligibility for programs such as Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Medicaid.

More than 223,000 ABLE accounts were open nationwide as of September 2025, with an average account balance of approximately $12,863. People with disabilities continue to experience significantly higher rates of poverty and often face substantially higher costs of daily living.

U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-KS) introduced the Senate version of the bill.

The ABLE MATCH Act would apply to taxable years beginning after December 31, 2026. It has been referred to the House Committee on Ways and Means.

title: Congresswoman Schrier Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Support Hydropower Improvements, Lower Energy Costs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (WA-08) and Congressman Nick Langworthy (NY-23) introduced the Fair Licensing for Operations of Water Structures (FLOWS) Act, legislation to streamline the hydropower and marine energy permitting process – bolstering clean energy across the country. Companion legislation was introduced by Senators Lisa Murkowski (R-AK) and Angus King (I-ME) and passed through the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee unanimously.

“The vast majority of Washington State’s energy comes from hydropower, making it essential that we efficiently maintain dams to support our communities,” said Congresswoman Schrier. “Helping our hydropower operators perform routine maintenance, repairs, replacements, and temporary adjustments for our dams will lower energy costs, ensure reliability, and improve public safety. This bill will also support emerging clean energy research as we find new ways to produce energy without emitting greenhouse gases.”

Current federal permitting processes for hydropower projects contain redundancies and inefficiencies that unnecessarily delay project work and increase costs. Under existing requirements, routine maintenance and in-kind replacements at hydropower facilities often require prior approval from the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC), resulting in months-long delays and diluting focus from substantial actions that need it most.

The FLOWS Act aims to chart the course for a reformed hydropower and marine energy permitting process through the following improvements:

Releases hydropower project developers from seeking FERC approval for non-substantial alterations or additions; routine maintenance, repair, or replacement; or seasonal or temporary adjustments in response to circumstances beyond the project’s control.

Requires FERC to conduct a rulemaking with public comment to determine definitions of a ‘‘substantial alteration or addition,’’ ‘‘nonsubstantial alteration or addition,’’ and ‘‘routine maintenance, repair, or replacement.’’

Allows FERC to issue short-term licenses of 10–20 years for hydrokinetic energy projects under five megawatts of installed capacity.

Requires FERC to submit a report to Congress on the effects of these hydrokinetic projects on the environment, economy, and electricity reliability and affordability no later than five years after the bill’s enactment or after the first 50 licensed projects have been operational for one year.

"Hydropower has powered communities across America for generations, but the federal permitting process hasn't kept pace with modern technology or common sense," said Congressman Langworthy. “Too often, operators are forced to navigate unnecessary federal red tape just to perform routine maintenance or replace equipment with identical components. That drives up costs, delays improvements, and makes it harder to keep reliable, affordable power on the grid, while having no real impact on environmental safety. At a time when New Yorkers are being crushed by skyrocketing energy costs, this is bipartisan, common-sense legislation is essential to preserving the future of one of America’s most affordable sources of electricity.”

"Rivers are essential to the health of our communities, wildlife, and economy. As the House considers policies to support hydropower, it is critical that river protection remains a central priority,” said American Rivers’ Hydropower Reform Director Kelly Catlett. “We appreciate Representatives Schrier and Langworthy's thoughtful introduction of the FLOWS Act to build on the important work already underway at FERC, and we look forward to continuing to work with them to strengthen the legislation and ensure it advances both renewable energy and healthy rivers."

“The FLOWS Act is a commonsense, bipartisan solution that reduces red tape for routine maintenance and non-substantial work, allowing hydropower operators to stay focused on what matters most: dam safety, reliability, and keeping power affordable,” said Matthew Allen, Senior Director of Legislative Affairs at the National Hydropower Association. “It also establishes a needed pathway for wave, tidal, and river-current technologies to get into the water more quickly and demonstrate their value to America’s clean energy future. By modernizing outdated processes, this bill will help preserve today’s hydropower fleet while unlocking tomorrow’s innovation. NHA thanks Reps. Langworthy and Schrier for introducing this legislation in the House as well as Senators Lisa Murkowski and Angus King for shepherding the Senate companion bill. NHA looks forward to working with these water power champions to move the bill through Congress as quickly as possible.”

“The FLOWS Act will encourage more investment in existing hydropower supporting reliability, safety, and affordability without triggering unnecessary regulatory processes for non-substantial project modifications or routine maintenance conducted under existing federal licenses. Thank you, Congresswoman Schrier, for advancing this important legislation,” said Kirk Hudson, general manager of Chelan County Public Utility District.

“The University of Washington is proud to be at the cutting edge of research for hydrokinetic technologies that produce clean energy and minimize environmental impact," said Brian Polagye, former Director of the Pacific Marine Energy Center. "With this legislation, new permitting pathways for hydrokinetics can play a crucial role in scaling up prototypes and demonstrating reliability. I thank Representatives Schrier and Langworthy for their work to help meet our state’s growing clean energy demand and lower costs for ratepayers.”

title: Peters Votes Against Irresponsible Short-Term Continuing Resolution
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) voted against a continuing resolution (CR) that would extend government funding at current levels through December 4, 2026. Rep. Peters opposed the bill both on fiscal grounds and because the resolution does not include language to restrict the Administration from directing appropriated funds to Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Border Patrol.

ICE and the Border Patrol currently have about $220 billion in unspent funds—a stockpile larger than the U.S. Marines and FBI combined—and are currently operating without proper guardrails to keep Americans safe. Agents have unjustifiably killed American citizens and people who were not the intended targets of enforcement operations.

"This Republican majority keeps passing continuing resolution after continuing resolution instead of trying to work with Democrats on a bipartisan appropriations process built on the standard 12 individual funding bills,” Rep. Peters said. “I understand the instinct to avoid another shutdown, but this bill wasn't brought to us in good faith. We need a more regular budgeting process that actually cuts wasteful spending, instead of just punting the fight down the road."

During consideration of the bill, Rep. Peters offered an amendment to add guardrails from his Stop Excessive Force in Immigration Act. The amendment would limit the use of military-style equipment, require always-on body cameras, and increase de-escalation training for federal agents. The amendment was not included in the final bill.

"Families in San Diego and across the country are living in fear because of CBP and ICE's poor training and non-existent standards," Rep. Peters continued. "In the past two weeks, we've seen agents kill two people—individuals who were not even the intended targets—while not wearing body cameras and without facing any consequences. Republicans want to borrow more money for these agencies to carry out their reckless immigration agenda, without a single guardrail. That's a non-starter in any spending bill I support."

Background: Rep. Peters has repeatedly spoken out against Congress's habit of funding the government through continuing resolutions rather than passing full budgets on time. As co-chair of the Bipartisan Fiscal Forum with Rep. Bill Huizenga (R-MI), Peters helped reintroduce the Prevent Government Shutdowns Act (PGSA) alongside Budget Committee Chairman Jodey Arrington and a bipartisan group of colleagues. The bill would create an automatic continuing resolution at current spending levels whenever appropriations lapse, along with other incentives to push Congress toward completing appropriations work on time.

title: Rep. Sewell Cosponsors Legislation to Pause AI Data Center Construction Until Federal Guardrails are Established
text:
Washington D.C. — U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) announced today that she has cosponsored the AI Data Center Moratorium Act, legislation to temporarily pause the construction and expansion of large artificial intelligence data centers until Congress establishes comprehensive federal safeguards to protect workers, communities, natural resources, and consumers while ensuring the benefits of AI are broadly shared.

The legislation responds to the rapid nationwide expansion of AI data centers whose enormous demands for water and other public resources are raising concerns in communities across the country, including in Alabama's 7th Congressional District.

Watch Rep. Sewell's video message here.

"Artificial intelligence has the potential to revolutionize health care, strengthen our economy, improve education, and solve some of our nation's greatest challenges," said Rep. Sewell. "I want America to lead the world in AI innovation, and I want Alabama to compete for the industries of the future. But innovation cannot come at the expense of the communities it is meant to serve."

"I have heard from countless residents from across Alabama's 7th Congressional District who are deeply concerned about the impact that large-scale AI data centers could have on their neighborhoods, infrastructure, and quality of life," continued Sewell. "They are asking thoughtful, commonsense questions about water use, energy demands, environmental impacts, and whether local communities will truly benefit from these developments. I share their concerns."

Rep. Sewell emphasized that the legislation is not intended to halt technological progress permanently, but rather to ensure that public policy keeps pace with the rapid advancement of AI.

"I am not anti-AI, and I am certainly not anti-innovation," Sewell continued. "The rate at which these massive data centers are being constructed is simply outpacing our ability to establish meaningful protections for the communities that will host them. Congress has a responsibility to put commonsense federal guardrails in place so that every community—not just a select few—shares in the benefits of this technological revolution."

The AI Data Center Moratorium Act would temporarily pause new AI data center construction and major expansions while Congress develops a comprehensive federal framework addressing environmental impacts, energy and water consumption, labor standards, consumer privacy, community engagement, and equitable economic development.

Rep. Sewell noted that communities across Alabama's 7th Congressional District have increasingly expressed concerns about the unprecedented scale of proposed AI infrastructure and the potential strain on local resources.

"For too long, underserved communities have been asked to shoulder disproportionate environmental and economic burdens while others reap the rewards," Sewell said. "As we build the economy of tomorrow, we must ensure that innovation lifts up every community rather than leaving some to bear the costs. Responsible innovation and community protection are not competing goals—they are complementary ones."

The AI Data Center Moratorium Act is endorsed by a broad coalition of environmental justice, labor, consumer protection, and community advocacy organizations committed to ensuring the responsible development of artificial intelligence infrastructure.

title: Sorensen’s Bipartisan Bill to Lower Prescription Drug Costs Advances Out of House Committee
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Eric Sorensen (IL-17) today celebrated the House Energy and Commerce Committee’s bipartisan approval of his STOP GAMES Act, legislation to lower prescription drug costs by preventing pharmaceutical companies from abusing the Food and Drug Administration’s (FDA) citizen petition process to delay competition from affordable generic drugs.

The bipartisan legislation, led by Congressman Sorensen and Congresswoman Stephanie Bice (OK-05), was approved in today’s full committee markup as part of the Lower Costs, More Transparency Act, a healthcare package aimed at reducing medical expenses and eliminating hidden medication costs. The legislation included several bipartisan, common-sense solutions that will promote competition and lower prescription drug prices for Americans.

This announcement is part of Congressman Sorensen’s broader affordability plan to lower costs for working families and put money back in the pockets of his neighbors. From prescription drugs to everyday expenses, Sorensen is focused on delivering real results that help families keep more of what they earn.

“Too many families are paying more than they should for prescription drugs because big pharmaceutical companies are gaming the system to block lower-cost competition,” said Congressman Sorensen. “The STOP GAMES Act is a bipartisan solution that helps get affordable generic drugs to market faster. This is an important step toward lowering costs for my neighbors and families across the country.”

The STOP GAMES Act cracks down on "sham” citizen petitions, which big pharmaceutical companies file to slow down the FDA approval process for competing generic drugs. While citizen petitions are intended to provide a voice to patients and consumer groups, the process is often co-opted by drug manufacturers to keep prices high.

Sorensen’s legislation allows the FDA to reject a petition if they determine the purpose of the claim is to stop or delay the entry of a new drug to the market. Currently, the agency is forced to investigate every claim.

The House Energy and Commerce Committee oversees healthcare legislation for the House of Representatives.

Now that the bill has cleared the committee, it’s one step closer to advancing to the House floor for a vote.

title: Subramanyam Urges Consideration of New Golden to Mars Route Along Route 606
text:
WASHINGTON, DC– U.S. Representative Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10) released the below statement in support of building the Golden to Mars power line predominantly along Route 606 instead of on school or residential property. Congressman Subramanyam had been informed that this route was not possible because of opposition from the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA). But after intervening by sending a letter to NOAA and meeting with NOAA Administrator Dr. Neil Jacobs, Rep. Subramanyam feels confident NOAA would work with the community to build Golden to Mars along its property.

Congressman Subramanyam issued the following statement:

“We’ve been faced with a false choice: build Golden to Mars power lines on residential property or build them on school property. Both options would be harmful to our community. When I asked whether there was an alternative option along Route 606, I was told that federal agencies like NOAA would oppose building them along their property.

So after sitting down with Administrator Jacobs to make our community’s concerns known and asking for NOAA to explore working with the community, I am confident that the Administrator and his team will explore and even support allowing an alternative Golden to Mars route along their property.

Our community has made its opposition to the current proposals known. So, if we aren't going to underground these lines, I urge the utility company, local and state officials, and the State Corporation Commission to come back to the table and make Route 606 the choice for the Golden to Mars transmission project.

We must consider every option possible, particularly if it can help mitigate harm to our schools and residents. These Golden to Mars deliberations have caused too much pain and the proposed routes will create too much harm to generations of Loudoun residents. We must prioritize giving this option a look instead of endless litigation and fights.”

Last week, Congressman Subramanyam asked NOAA for information about the potential new Golden to Mars route and whether it was ever asked for guidance on Route 606. The 606 route would bring the transmission lines down Old Ox Road and not through neighborhoods.

title: Rep. Sykes Votes Against Funding Bill That Fails to Include ICE and CBP Accountability Reforms

title: Congressman Tim Moore Votes to Extend Government Funding, Prevent Partisan Shutdown
text:

This legislation prevents a September 30, 2026 government shutdown while allowing Congress to continue working on the full-year FY2027 appropriations bills.

"This clean, straightforward continuing resolution keeps the government open, protects our national security, and ensures election-year politics don't jeopardize the funding process," said Congressman Moore. "The House advanced all FY27 appropriations bills through committee and passed three full-year funding bills, but Senate inaction has put that progress at risk. This short-term measure prevents a last-minute funding crisis, protects the critical services Americans rely on, and preserves the path to completing full-year FY27 appropriations without allowing political games to dictate the process."

This legislation keeps the federal government open by continuing funding at current FY26 levels. It also preserves funding authority for disaster response and continues programs such as WIC, SNAP, flood insurance, small-business lending, and assistance for low-income families.

title: Rep. Tokuda Leads Hawaiʻi Delegation Urging President Trump to Approve FEMA Kona Low Recovery Aid
text:
Washington D.C. – U.S. Representative Jill N. Tokuda (HI-02), joined by U.S. Senators Brian Schatz (D-HI) and Mazie Hirono (D-HI) and U.S. Representative Ed Case (HI-01), sent a letter to President Donald J. Trump urging that he support the State of Hawaiʻi’s appeal and reconsideration requests to the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) following the March 2026 Kona low storms.

The delegation is asking the Administration to approve the state’s requests for additional federal disaster assistance to help repair storm-damaged public infrastructure and provide funding for projects that reduce the risk of future flooding and other disasters.

“The appeal for Public Assistance Category G has been updated with additional data, validating more than $20 million in quantifiable damage, including more than $15 million in damage to airport grounds infrastructure and nearly $5 million of damage to parks, trails, cultural facilities, and early warning systems,” the lawmakers wrote in the letter. “This damage includes structural pavement failure of taxiways at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport in Honolulu, the state’s primary gateway for tourists, residents, business travelers, and military service members.”

"Recovering from a disaster of this scale is a long-term commitment, and our priority must be protecting our communities from future vulnerabilities,” said Rep. Tokuda. “This federal assistance is about hardening our infrastructure and making the necessary improvements to prevent the kind of severe disruptions we just witnessed. We must invest in safeguarding our islands so our residents can feel secure and prepared for the future.”

“Hawaiʻi needs additional federal disaster aid to restore critical infrastructure, support ongoing recovery efforts, and help prepare for future disasters. Investing in mitigation and preparedness now can help keep communities safer in the future. Hawaiʻi shouldn't have to face these challenges alone. The people of Hawaiʻi deserve the full support and partnership of the federal government,” said Sen. Schatz.

"As Hawaiʻi communities that were damaged by the Kona Low storms continue to clean up, assess damages, and begin to recover, our federal government has a responsibility to be a continuing partner in helping our state be better protected from future storms,” said Senator Hirono. “This additional federal support will make our state more resilient to the extreme weather events that threaten our state and communities nationwide with increasing frequency.”

“The updated data demonstrating the severe and continuing damage of the Kona Low storms strengthens our request for federal disaster assistance to repair our major international airport,” said Rep. Ed Case. “Our airports are central to an isolated island state, and natural disaster damage to them has wide-ranging ripple effects through our economy and community which FEMA and related federal assistance should assist in addressing.”

title: Trahan Backs Bipartisan Bills to Protect Ratepayers from Data Center Price Hikes
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03) supported the passage of two bipartisan pieces of legislation to protect ratepayers from increased utility costs caused by data centers during a House Energy and Commerce Committee markup. Both bills, the Ratepayer Protection Act and the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act, are now eligible for consideration on the House floor.

“It’s our job to make sure that when data centers are built, they're built on terms that work for the families who live nearby,” Congresswoman Trahan said. “That's what this legislation gets right. It says something simple. If you build the data center, you pay for the data center. The construction costs, the utility costs – those fall on the company, not the family down the street. This bill gives states a strong standard to make sure large load developers foot that bill themselves.”

During the Committee markup, Trahan spoke in favor of both pieces of legislation. Footage of her remarks can be accessed HERE or by clicking the image below. A transcript is embedded below.

Data centers are the fastest-growing source of new electricity demand in the country, and the grid upgrades needed to serve them are not free. Someone has to pay for the new power plants, transmission lines, and substations, and too often that cost gets spread across everyone's monthly bill, leaving families and small businesses to subsidize the energy needs of some of the largest corporations in the world.

To combat this problem, the Ratepayer Protection Act gives state utility regulators clear standards to ensure large-load customers, meaning any new data or information storage facility drawing 100 megawatts or more, cover the full cost of the infrastructure they require. It requires those customers to recover the full incremental cost of grid upgrades over time and to provide financial assurances, so ratepayers stay protected even if a data center scales back or leaves entirely.

Similarly, the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act directs the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission to convene major stakeholders to examine how to shield residents from these rising costs, and it requires FERC to deliver a report with concrete recommendations and best practices so the energy costs tied to AI data centers are not passed on to ordinary consumers.

During her remarks, Trahan pointed out that both bills are important first steps in protecting families from bearing the burden of increased utility costs caused by data centers. She argued that Congress must go further, including by passing a provision in her bipartisan Great American AI Act discussion draft released last month to improve data center efficiency and reduce their environmental footprint.

“Both of these bills are good first steps, Mr. Chairman, but we should also be honest about what they don't do. They don't fully address the water these facilities draw from our communities. They don't answer the concern back home that when the grid is stretched, families worry they'll be deprioritized,” Congresswoman Trahan continued. “People in the district I represent are raising these questions, and they deserve answers. That's exactly why, when Congressman Obernolte and I drafted the Great American AI Act, we included provisions to make data centers more efficient and lessen their environmental footprint. Because the smarter we build these facilities, the less strain they put on the grid, on our water, and on the families who live nearby.”

Both bills passed unanimously and now move to the House floor for consideration by the full House of Representatives.

-----------------------------------

Congresswoman Lori Trahan

Remarks as Delivered

House Energy and Committee Markup

July 21, 2026

Thank you, Mr. Chairman. I too support the Ratepayer Protection Act and look forward to advancing this bipartisan legislation to the House floor today.

Right now, families across our country are afraid to open up their electric bills. The number keeps climbing, and their paycheck isn't keeping pace. They're doing the math at the kitchen table, wondering what they might have to cut next just to keep the lights on.

That fear is real, and too many families have stopped believing that anyone in Washington is listening. They watch prices rise at the pump and at the grocery store. They sit through weeks of brutal heat and run the air conditioning that they can barely afford. And now they read that a data center is coming to their community, and they are told not to worry about what that means for their bills.

Well, to be clear, data centers aren't going away. So it’s our job to make sure that when data centers are built, they're built on terms that work for the families who live nearby.

That's what this legislation gets right. It says something simple. If you build the data center, you pay for the data center. The construction costs, the utility costs – those fall on the company, not the family down the street. This bill gives states a strong standard to make sure large load developers foot that bill themselves. That's a real move toward keeping these costs off our constituents' bills.

I'm also glad H.R. 6529, the Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act, is part of today's markup. It's another effort to make sure surging demand from these massive projects doesn't land on the backs of residential ratepayers.

Both of these bills are good first steps, Mr. Chairman, but we should also be honest about what they don't do. They don't fully address the water these facilities draw from our communities. They don't answer the concern back home that when the grid is stretched, families worry they'll be deprioritized.

People in the district I represent are raising these questions, and they deserve answers. That's exactly why, when Congressman Obernolte and I drafted the Great American AI Act, we included provisions to make data centers more efficient and lessen their environmental footprint. Because the smarter that we build these facilities, the less strain they put on the grid, on our water, and on the families who live nearby.

So, these bills can't be where our work ends. AI is spreading through every corner of our economy, and hardworking Americans cannot be an afterthought while that happens.

I commend the sponsors and Committee staff for their work on this legislation. It really matters. And I look forward to continuing this track record of bipartisan work on AI in the weeks and months ahead.

title: Congressman Valadao Votes to Continue Funding for Critical Programs
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman David Valadao (CA-22) released the following statement after voting in support of a clean, short-term Continuing Resolution (CR) to keep the government funded while the House and Senate continue their work on passing full-year appropriations bills.

“Today, I voted in support of a clean, short-term Continuing Resolution to keep the government running while Congress continues working on full-year funding bills,” said Congressman Valadao. “While a CR isn’t the preferred solution, government shutdowns are unproductive, cost billions, and disrupt the services Americans depend on. As a member of the House Committee on Appropriations, I’m proud we’ve done our job by advancing all twelve Fiscal Year 2027 appropriations bills, and I stand ready to continue negotiations with my Senate colleagues to get full-year funding bills across the finish line.”

The Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027:

Funds the government at current levels through December 4, 2026.

Allows the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) to continue providing food assistance to low-income women, infants, and children for the duration of the CR.

Continues Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) funding for the National Flood Insurance Program and the Disaster Relief Fund.

Authorizes U.S. Forest Service (USFS) and the U.S. Department of the Interior (DOI) to obligate funding for critical wildfire suppression efforts.

Provides the Small Business Association (SBA) with the authority to continue small business support programs.

Extends authorization of the Livestock Mandatory Reporting Program

Background:

The House and Senate each must pass 12 full-year appropriations bills before September 30th or a Continuing Resolution (CR) to buy more time to find agreement between the House, Senate, and White House on various funding levels to keep the government open. The House Appropriations Committee passed all 12 bills out of Committee and passed 3 off the House Floor. Congress now has until December 4, 2026 to find agreement on full-year appropriations bills for Fiscal Year 2027.

title: Congressman Van Drew Demands Accountability After New Jersey Confirms Thousands of Non-Citizens Were Registered to Vote
text:
Washington, DC -Today, Congressman Van Drew issued the following statement after Governor Mikie Sherrill announced that approximately 6,600 non-citizens were identified on New Jersey's voter rolls, with nearly 400 having cast ballots.

"This is exactly why so many New Jerseyans have lost confidence in our election system," said Congressman Van Drew. "For years, we have warned that our voter rolls needed to be cleaned up, only to be dismissed and called conspiracy theorists. Now, the state's own findings confirm that thousands of non-citizens were registered to vote and hundreds cast ballots.

"I will be demanding accountability for how this happened, who allowed it to happen, and which safeguards failed. We have had extremely close elections in New Jersey, and God knows how many other ineligible voters may still be on the rolls or how many ballots have been cast without ever being identified. It is unacceptable. New Jersey should end automatic voter registration at the Motor Vehicle Commission (MVC), clean up its voter rolls, and require proof of citizenship to register to vote. These are basic safeguards that should already be in place."

title: Walberg Votes to Prevent Another Democrat Shutdown
text:
Today, Congressman Tim Walberg (MI-05) voted in favor of, and the House passed H.R. 9770, the Continuing Appropriations Act of 2027, by a vote of 220-205. The legislation would continue federal funding through December 4, 2026, while Congress completes work on the full-year fiscal year 2027 appropriations bills.

"Last year, congressional Democrats triggered the longest full government shutdown in American history, disrupting air travel, critical services, and nutrition assistance," said Rep. Walberg. "Their obstruction left servicemembers, air traffic controllers, TSA personnel, federal law enforcement officers, and other federal employees unsure of when they would receive their next paycheck and Michigan families wondering how they would put food on the table. This clean continuing resolution ensures that another costly government shutdown does not befall the American people while Congress continues to complete the appropriations process in regular order."

Background

A 43-day government shutdown began on October 1, 2025, following a lapse in federal appropriations. While House Republicans voted on September 19, 2025, for a bipartisan government funding deal, Democrats in the Senate voted 15 times against it to keep the government closed, forcing the longest full government shutdown in U.S. history that cost taxpayers $15 billion per week.

Beginning on February 14, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security also experienced a historic 75-day funding lapse, jeopardizing our homeland security and placing undue financial insecurity on employees of one of our nation’s largest federal agencies.

title: Walberg's Legislation to Combat Invasive Species Examined by Subcommittee
text:
Today, the House Committee on Natural Resources' Subcommittee on Water, Wildlife and Fisheries held a legislative hearing and examined the Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) Control and Prevention Act, introduced by Representatives Tim Walberg (R-MI) and Sarah Elfreth (D-MD). The bipartisan legislation would modernize federal AIS authorities to better prevent, control, and eradicate aquatic invasive species.

Congressman Walberg, a member of the House Natural Resources Committee, had the opportunity to ask Dr. Marc Gaden, the Executive Secretary of the Great Lakes Fishery Commission, about how the legislation would bridge gaps in the federal government's current approach to preventing and managing aquatic invasive species.

"As Michiganders, we know the long-term health of our fisheries is critical to our fishing industry, economy, and way of life," said Rep. Walberg. "I was glad to see the subcommittee consider my legislation, the bipartisan AIS Control and Prevention Act, to streamline coordination and prioritize prevention and rapid response. The Great Lakes are a national treasure, and we must continue to be good stewards of their waters and wildlife."

Background

Aquatic invasive species, including zebra mussels, invasive Asian carp, and sea lamprey, impose billions of dollars in costs annually, damaging fisheries, aquatic habitat, hydropower, irrigation, drinking water, and other water infrastructure nationwide. They also pose a significant threat to the ecological and economic health of the Great Lakes region by outcompeting native fish populations, degrading water quality, and endangering the economies and communities that depend on a healthy ecosystem.

The Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) Control and Prevention Act would:

Support state-led, coordinated invasive species management

Protect fisheries, boating access, water infrastructure, and outdoor recreation economies

Improve coordination across existing federal, state, and regional AIS programs

Prioritize prevention and rapid response to reduce long-term, costly management

The Aquatic Invasive Species (AIS) Control and Prevention Act is supported by a number of organizations representing recreational anglers, boaters, and the industries they support.

title: Wasserman Schultz Calls on FIU to Rescind Punishment of Student ICE Protest
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25) called on Florida International University (FIU) to rescind its disciplinary actions against students who engaged in silent protest against the university’s voluntary collaboration with ICE enforcement on campus.

In March, seven students engaged in a silent protest at a school event. Recently, the students were told they had to record videos about FIU policies that they allegedly violated or have a hold placed on their accounts, preventing them from signing up for classes or receiving a diploma.

“This push to muzzle silent protest is a gross violation of our Constitution, FIU's own rules and sets a dangerous precedent,” said Wasserman Schultz. “I'm hopeful that by rescinding these forced-confession punishments FIU can restore its reputation for rigorous speech and debate.”

Read the full letter here or below:

Dear President Nuñez,

The recent penalization imposed by Florida International University’s (FIU) administration upon seven of its students for their silent protest staged at a campus event in March of this year is a grave violation of First Amendment free-speech protections. FIU’s actions set up a dangerous precedent and will have a chilling effect on students’ ability to freely express themselves and their ideas—a bedrock tenet of our free and democratic society, as enshrined in our Constitution, particularly in a university environment.

FIU’s own regulations, as defined in FIU-110 Expressive Activities in Outdoor Areas on Campus, protect students’ First Amendment activities, including “assemblies, demonstrations, exercises of free speech, protests, parades, marches, and picketing protected under the First Amendment to the United States Constitution and Article 1 of the Florida Constitution.” FIU regulations permit such activities so long as they are lawful and do not “[…] materially and substantially disrupt the normal operations of the University or materially and substantially infringe upon the rights of others.”

FIU has maintained that the seven students violated a university ban on expressive activities indoors. However, students’ First Amendment rights on campus have been upheld at the federal level at least since the Supreme Court precedent set in 1969 by the Tinker v. Des Moines Independent Community School District decision. The majority ruled in Tinker that neither students nor teachers “shed their constitutional rights to freedom of speech or expression at the schoolhouse gate.”

University regulations plainly serve to prevent disruption of the learning environment. It is disingenuous to suggest that the seven students standing up to display the message on their shirts is “materially and substantially” disruptive to normal university operations.

Per public reporting, the punishment levied against students includes forcing them to record a two-minute video explaining university expectations around indoor and outdoor areas, which they could be compelled to re-record if it does not meet FIU Office of Student Conduct and Academic Integrity standards. This punishment itself violates students’ First Amendment rights, given that no governing body can force individuals to support certain expressions— often referred to as the compelled speech doctrine— as upheld by West Virginia State Board of Education v. Barnette.

FIU’s violation of constitutionally guaranteed free-speech rights for students is thus twofold. Responding to the violation of a protected First Amendment expression with a further violation is an unacceptable form of disciplinary action. The university’s actions send a clear message to students that free expression will be silenced if it is convenient for the university, and that they must fall in line or suffer the consequences.

This presents a clear disincentive for students to voice controversial, unpopular or divisive opinions, which is both a right and an important part of the education process. As part of the State University System of Florida, FIU adopted its Statement of Free Expression “to support and encourage full and open discourse and the robust exchange of ideas and perspectives on our respective campuses.” Punishing students in the aforementioned manner for silent protest is in direct violation of this statement, as well as FIU’s publicly stated values of “freedom of thought and expression.”

As a public university supported by federal funding and entrusted with advancing the education of our students, FIU has a responsibility to uphold students’ First Amendment rights. I strongly urge FIU to rescind its disciplinary actions against these students and fully restore First Amendment speech protections for its student body.

Sincerely,

Debbie Wasserman Schultz

Member of Congress

title: Wasserman Schultz Leads Latino-Jewish Caucus, Argentina Caucus in Marking Anniversary of AMIA Jewish Center Bombing, Demanding Accountability
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25), co-chair of the Congressional Latino-Jewish Caucus, was joined by fellow co-chairs, Reps. Mario Díaz-Balart (FL-26), and Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Chair of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Western Hemisphere Rep. Maria Salazar (FL-27), and co-chairs of the Argentina Caucus, Reps. Darren Soto (FL-09) and Michael Rulli (OH-06) in sponsoring a resolution to commemorate the 32nd anniversary of the 1994 bombing of the AMIA Jewish Community Center in Buenos Aires and demanding justice and accountability for those responsible for the attack.

“More than three decades after the tragic AMIA Jewish Center bombing, and there’s still no justice for the 85 victims, the hundreds of injured, and countless people who were traumatized by this Iran-backed Hezbollah attack,” said Wasserman Schultz. “With antisemitism skyrocketing around the world, this gruesome attack on Argentina’s thriving Jewish community cannot go unanswered. I’m proud to honor the victims of this attack and keep up the vital pursuit of justice for their loved ones.”

“With this resolution, we honor the 85 innocent people who lost their lives and the more than 300 who were injured in the bombing of the Asociación Mutual Israelita Argentina (AMIA). This heinous act of terror, carried out by Iran and its proxy Hezbollah, remains the deadliest antisemitic terrorist attack in Argentina’s history and serves as a painful reminder of the consequences of extremism,” said Diaz-Balart. “This past May, I visited the AMIA memorial in Buenos Aires, where I paid my respects to the victims and reflected on the enduring impact of this tragedy. We must never forget the victims, and we must continue to condemn the alarming rise of antisemitism and hold accountable those who commit terrorism.”

“The AMIA attack is a painful reminder of the dangers of antisemitism,” said Soto. “Today and every day, we keep the memories of those we lost alive by continuing to reject the extremism that leads to these violent acts of terror.”

“As Co-Chair of the Congressional Argentina Caucus, I strongly support this resolution condemning the 1994 AMIA bombing and demanding full accountability from Iran and Hezbollah,” said Rulli. “After 32 years, the victims’ families deserve justice. The United States stands with Argentina and the Jewish community in their fight against terror and impunity.”

“As we mark the 32nd anniversary of the AMIA bombing, we stand in solidarity with Argentina's Jewish community as we remember the 85 people who were killed and the many others who were injured,” said Dina Siegel Vann, Director, The Arthur and Rochelle Belfer Institute for Latino and Latin American Affairs, AJC. “Thank you to Representatives Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), Mario Díaz-Balart (R-FL), Adriano Espaillat (D-NY), Maria Salazar (R-FL), Darren Soto (D-FL), and Michael Rulli (R-OH) for championing this resolution, honoring the victims, and demanding accountability for the Iranian regime and Hezbollah terrorists responsible for this vicious attack.”

First established in 2011 with support from the American Jewish Committee, the bipartisan Congressional Latino-Jewish Caucus has cemented stronger bonds based on Latino and Jewish communities’ shared histories as immigrants and minorities. It has also been vocal in responding to the growing wave of antisemitism across the globe in the U.S. The 25-member Caucus is now led by Reps. Wasserman Schultz, Díaz-Balart, and Espaillat. In 2024, Rep. Wasserman Schultz joined a Congressional delegation to Buenos Aires to participate in the formal 30th anniversary commemoration of the AMIA attack.

title: Rep. Weber’s Pipeline Safety Authorization Act of 2026 Advances Out of the House Energy and Commerce Committee
text:
Read Congressman Weber's opening statement as prepared for delivery:

"Mr. Chairman, I have an amendment in the nature of a substitute at the desk.

"It is Amendment in the Nature of a Substitute (AINS) H.R. 9338_01.

"This Amendment in the Nature of a Substitute before us today reflects important updates made since the Energy Subcommittee markup last month. These changes fulfill the commitments we made during that markup to keep working across the aisle toward a strong bipartisan final product.

"We listened, we kept our word, and we tightened the language to protect the First Amendment rights of lawful protesters while holding those accountable who knowingly and willfully damage pipeline equipment or disrupt operations by manipulating a valve.

"Throughout this process, we have worked closely with stakeholders across the industry and within the government to develop and refine this legislation. The result is a stronger bill that gives the Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) the resources and direction necessary to continue safeguarding more than 3 million miles of pipeline infrastructure across these great United States.

"The bill strengthens civil penalties for pipeline safety violations, promotes best practices across state damage prevention programs, and establishes a voluntary information-sharing system so lessons learned from accidents and near misses can help prevent the next one.

"It also supports communities working to repair and replace aging natural gas distribution systems, sets deadlines for updated carbon dioxide pipeline safety standards, and requires PHMSA to lay out a plan for completing overdue pipeline safety rulemakings.

"Americans deserve nothing less than our continued effort to move the needle closer and closer to 100 percent safety, and this legislation helps us do exactly that.

"Our nation’s pipeline infrastructure operates 24 hours a day, seven days a week to safely deliver the reliable and affordable energy that powers American homes, businesses, and industries while supporting our allies around the world.

"Few regions in the country can rival the pipeline infrastructure along the Texas Gulf Coast. Every day, that infrastructure helps produce, refine, process, and export the energy that powers America and supports our allies abroad.

"In Texas’ 14th Congressional District, we produce and move more energy than just about any other district in the United States. Few places better illustrate the important role pipeline infrastructure plays in our everyday lives.

"Whether that energy originates in the Permian Basin or comes from our neighbors to the north in Alberta, Canada, producing it is only half the battle. American energy dominance depends on our ability to deliver that energy safely and reliably to the people, businesses, and industries that depend on it every day.

"This bill reflects what dedicated members of this body and their staff can accomplish when they come together at the table to make America better. I thank them for their hard work, and I urge every member of this committee to support H.R. 9338 and help move this strong bipartisan bill one step closer to the House floor.

"I yield back the balance of my time."

title: ICYMI: Rep. Weber Pens Op-Ed Highlighting the Need for Honest, Reliable Packaging Claims
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - In a new op-ed in 535 News, Congressman Randy Weber (TX-14) made the case for passing the bipartisan PACK Act to bring greater clarity and consistency to packaging claims nationwide. Rep. Weber detailed how conflicting state labeling requirements create confusion for families and higher costs for businesses, emphasizing the need for honest, reliable packaging claims that keep consumers informed.

In case you missed it…

It Shouldn’t Take a Lawyer to Know What Belongs in the Recycling Bin

535 News

Congressman Randy Weber

July 21, 2026

Picture a mother standing in her kitchen, holding an empty container over two bins. Its label says recyclable, but her recycling program says it does not belong in the blue bin. She searches for instructions and still cannot tell where it should go.

She wants to do the right thing. She should not need a law degree to figure it out.

That moment plays out across America. Recycling symbols can mean one thing in Texas and another in California. Even packaging made from recyclable material may be rejected because of its shape, size, color, or the equipment available locally.

The result is confusion, higher costs, and more material in landfills.

California is making the problem even worse.

California’s S.B. 343, dubbed the “Truth in Recycling“, prohibits the use of the “chasing arrows” symbol or any other recyclability claim unless the product meets specific criteria determined solely by California.

California may govern itself, but its laws should not dictate how businesses operate nationwide. While there is an injunction against S.B. 343 for the moment, the issue remains that states are trying to create standards for what is labeled as recyclable (and compostable and reusable), when the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) long had jurisdiction over claims on packages.

Companies cannot realistically create a different label for every state’s definitions and standards. When California imposes its own standard, businesses may be forced to apply it nationwide. In effect, California’s elected officials get to play Congress, writing rules for Americans who never voted for them.

Fortunately, Congress already has the bipartisan solution in the palm of its hand. I like to call it the PACK Act, short for the Packaging and Claims Knowledge Act.

Within the PACK Act, companies remain free to decide whether to label their packaging recyclable, compostable, or reusable. But once a company decides to make one of those claims, it has to prove it.

Every claim would first be verified by an accredited independent third-party certifier. When local access is limited, recyclable labels would have to say so. Compostable and reusable claims would have to live up to their promises too.

To make sure those protections are applied consistently across the country, the FTC would enforce the law and issue compliance guidance with input from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and technical experts. That would create one clear national framework, so a label that follows the rules in Texas is not forced to meet a different standard every time it crosses a state line.

At the end of the day, a mother standing over her recycling bin will have honest information about whether a package belongs there. Businesses that choose to make these claims will have certainty too, without being forced to spend more navigating a different standard in every state.

That kind of clarity and consistency is why the PACK Act has earned overwhelming support across the American marketplace. Families and businesses alike are ready for one honest, reliable national packaging standard.

This week, the PACK Act gets its day before the House Energy and Commerce Committee’s Subcommittee on Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade during a hearing on “Legislative Proposals to Strengthen Consumer Protection in a Changing Marketplace.”

In a town where bipartisan agreement is hard to come by, the PACK Act has brought both sides to the table. This hearing will show why the issue has cut through the Washington noise and why it is time to get it fixed.

If Congress fails to seize this moment, packaging-claim rules like California’s could become the de facto national standard. Businesses will spend more navigating regulations and less on hiring workers or improving products. Small manufacturers may pull products from certain markets, while consumers pay more and understand less.

Families stretching their grocery budgets should not foot the bill for California’s regulatory agenda. Main Street businesses should not need Sacramento’s permission to sell nationwide. Without congressional action, the confusion will deepen, and the most restrictive state will continue setting policy for everyone else.

The PACK Act keeps consumers informed, businesses competitive, and the words on a package worth trusting. Congress must take this bipartisan bill across the finish line and send it to President Trump’s desk.

We are the United States of America, not the United States of California. One state does not get to write the rules for the other 49.

title: Wied Introduces 10-Year Ban on Members of Congress Becoming Lobbyists or Federal Contractors
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Tony Wied (R-WI) introduced legislation today to address an issue that has plagued the DC swamp for far too long: career politicians using their connections and insider knowledge to enrich themselves as lobbyists and federal contractors after leaving office.

The Safeguarding Ethics and Restoring Voter Expectations (SERVE) Act establishes a mandatory ten-year cooling-off period prohibiting any individual who serves as a Member of Congress during the 119th Congress or any succeeding Congress from lobbying or engaging in compensated federal contracting activities.

“Public service is supposed to be about the people we represent, not a steppingstone to personal gain,” said Congressman Wied. “Yet too often, we see former Members of Congress leverage their time in Washington to position themselves for lucrative lobbying or federal contracting opportunities immediately after leaving office. This self-serving cycle is exactly why the American people have lost faith in Washington, and I don't blame them. Until we end this revolving door, career politicians will continue to abuse the system to enrich themselves and further erode trust in our government.”

Background: For decades, Americans have watched as former Members of Congress have walked out of the Capitol and immediately cashed in on their time in office, turning public trust into private profit. This revolving-door culture erodes confidence in Congress and fuels the perception that decisions made here are shaped by future job prospects rather than the interests of our constituents. Currently, Senators are prohibited from lobbying for 2 years after leaving office, and Representatives are prohibited from lobbying for 1 year. There are no restrictions prohibiting former Members of Congress from serving as federal contractors.

The SERVE Act addresses this conflict of interest by:

Establishing a mandatory ten-year cooling-off period for any individual who serves as a Member of Congress during the 119th Congress or any Congress thereafter.

Prohibiting former Members from:

Lobbying Congress or federal agencies.

Engaging in compensated federal contracting activities for ten years after leaving office.

This legislation institutes practical, commonsense reforms that put constituents first and will help rebuild faith in Congress.

title: Sen. Banks and Sen. Warren Introduce Resolution Calling for FTC Investigation into Fire Truck Manufacturing Industry
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) introduced a bipartisan resolution directing the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to investigate potential anticompetitive practices in the fire truck manufacturing industry. The resolution calls on the FTC to examine allegations of price fixing, price gouging, serial acquisitions, monopolization, and other potential violations of federal antitrust laws that have driven up costs and delayed the delivery of critical firefighting equipment.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “When anticompetitive practices leave firefighters without the equipment they need to save lives, it becomes more than just an economic issue. This is about public safety and I’m proud to join this bipartisan investigation as we fight to put the safety and security of the American people first.”

Mayor Sue Finkam, Carmel, Indiana: “Public safety is measured in minutes, not years. The faster our first responders reach someone in need, the better the outcome. Delays in getting the equipment they need put lives and property at risk. I’m grateful to Senator Banks and Warren for leading this bipartisan effort to help communities put lifesaving equipment into service faster.”

The resolution follows concerns raised by firefighters, local officials, and municipalities in Indiana, Massachusetts, Vermont, Virginia and across the country about skyrocketing fire truck prices and growing delivery backlogs. As the resolution notes, just three manufacturers control between 70 to 80 percent of the U.S. fire truck market. Since 2013, the cost of a pumper truck has nearly doubled—from approximately $500,000 to nearly $1 million—while ladder truck prices have climbed from roughly $900,000 to nearly $2 million. Meanwhile, delivery times have increased from one to two years to as long as four and a half years.

The resolution directs the FTC to submit a report to Congress within one year detailing:

The extent of anticompetitive practices and potential violations of federal antitrust laws in the fire truck manufacturing industry, including price-fixing, price-gouging, serial acquisitions, and monopolization.

The impact of these practices on firefighters, fire departments, municipalities, states, and small businesses.

Recommendations for legislative or other actions to restore competition and protect public safety.

The resolution also requires the FTC to notify Congress if companies fail to cooperate with its investigation.

title: Bennet, Colleagues Announce Legislation to Hold Purchasers of Russian Oil Accountable
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, joined a bipartisan group of over 60 colleagues led by Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) and Darline Graham (R-S.C.) to introduce legislation negotiated with the late Senator Lindsey Graham (R-S.C.) and the White House to hold major purchasers of Russian oil and gas accountable for supporting Russia’s war in Ukraine. Bennet has supported a version of this legislation for over a year.

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 would impose sanctions on Vladimir Putin’s inner circle and his enablers across Russian industry and financial institutions, the Russian shadow fleet, and firms providing certain goods and services to Russia’s defense industrial base. The legislation also authorizes the President to impose tariffs on goods from countries that buy the majority of Russian oil and gas, or help Russia evade sanctions. The negotiated text narrows that authority to the five largest importers of Russian crude oil and gas and major sanctions evaders.

“For over four years, the Ukrainian people have shown us what it looks like to fight and die for democracy, for their country, and for the West. Their courage in the face of Vladimir Putin’s war offers the greatest example of how to fight back against authoritarian aggression. Amid Putin’s intransigence at the negotiating table and daily attacks on civilians across Ukraine, Congress must make Russia pay a further price,” said Bennet. “This bill will impose greater pressure on Putin to end his unprovoked war, especially as Ukraine makes progress on the battlefield and as the Russian economy struggles under the weight of U.S. and allied measures. Only by demonstrating our firm resolve can the United States and our allies support Ukraine’s pursuit of a just and durable end to this war and successfully defend the principle of a Europe whole, free, and at peace. Backing Ukraine today will be our best deterrence against authoritarian ambitions tomorrow.”

Over 60 senators support the bill, including Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.); Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Co-Chair of the Senate Ukraine Caucus; Jim Risch (R-Idaho) and Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), the Chairman and Ranking Member of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee; and Roger Wicker (R-Miss.) and Jack Reed (D-R.I.), the Chairman and Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee.

Bennet has staunchly supported the Ukrainian people since Putin launched his unprovoked full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022.

He leads legislation in both the Senate committee-passed defense and intelligence bills to bolster drone and intelligence cooperation with Ukraine. Bennet also co-sponsors the bipartisan SHADOW Fleets Act to target a collection of older, reflagged oil tankers that Russia uses to circumvent existing U.S. sanctions on Russian oil and energy revenue and the bipartisan DROP Act, legislation requiring targeted sanctions on firms and individuals dealing in Russian oil. Additionally, in May 2026, Bennet led 14 Senate colleagues to urge Secretary of the Treasury Scott Bessent to fully resume sanctions on Russian oil and use every available tool to cut into Russia’s war windfall profits.

Earlier this year, Bennet wrote an op-ed in EURACTIV – a leading European outlet – urging the United States and like-minded allies to form a coalition to cooperatively and immediately use Russian sovereign assets on Ukraine’s behalf. In December 2025, Bennet led a bipartisan letter to Belgian Ambassador to the U.S. Frédéric Bernard expressing support for European Commission efforts to leverage Russian sovereign assets to finance a loan for Ukraine. Bennet co-sponsors bipartisan legislation to repurpose frozen Russian sovereign assets held in the United States to support Ukraine. The legislation would build on the Rebuilding Economic Prosperity and Opportunity (REPO) for Ukrainians Act, which Bennet co-sponsored and which President Joe Biden signed into law in April 2024.

Bennet played a leading role in securing the April 2024 passage of the national security supplemental package, which included $60.84 billion in emergency support for Ukraine, including by objecting and holding must-pass measures through 2023 and 2024.
