title: Murphy Demands Answers from Hegseth on Objectives for Iran War & Taxpayer Dollars Spent on Trump's Luxury Jet
text:
WASHINGTON–U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), a member of the Senate Appropriations Committee, on Tuesday questioned Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth about President Trump’s objectives in his disastrous war with Iran during a hearing on the administration’s request for nearly $70 billion in supplemental funding to enable more of their devastating military missteps abroad. Murphy also pushed Hegseth to provide the American people with answers about how much taxpayer money has been spent to retrofit a luxury jet that Qatar gifted to Trump. Murphy pressed Hegseth not to permit Trump’s corrupt plans to take the taxpayer-funded plane with him for personal use once he leaves office.

“The American people either didn't want this war or were deeply skeptical of this war because they have seen this country make the same mistake over and over again in wars in the Middle East, and that is to create either unrealistic or open-ended objectives,” Murphy said.

Pointing to contradictions in Hegseth’s testimony, Murphy demanded answers on whether the Trump administration has abandoned its stated objective to destroy Iran’s military capabilities: “You said in March that the United States was ‘on plan to defeat, destroy, and disable all of Iran's meaningful military capabilities at a pace that the world has never seen before.’ Obviously, as we've discussed here today, that objective has not been achieved and is not going to be achieved. Iran is adept, more adept than even at the start of the war, at hiding their capabilities or repairing after damage we have done. There's an open report that when it comes to their missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz, 30 of 33 are still operational. But I've also heard you say in this hearing that the objectives now seem to be more limited than they were at the outset of the war. That this is about reopening the Strait and this is about dismantling [Iran’s] nuclear capability. So, my question is pretty simple: Is it correct that it is no longer a war objective to destroy all of their military capacities?

As the Pentagon requests an additional $67 billion in funding, Murphy described the continued lack of transparency from the administration about what American taxpayers have already been charged to retrofit the luxury jet that Qatar gifted to Trump: “Reports suggest that maybe as much as $1 billion in your base funding - an extraordinary amount of money - has been used for an upgrade, and the plane is back in the shop for a second upgrade. As far as I can tell, never before has an administration not made public the amount of money for an upgrade or a construction contract on a presidential airplane. Obviously, we don't need or want to disclose the details of that upgrade. But never before have you withheld from Congress and the public the total amount of money.”

Murphy pushed Hegseth to disclose the cost to taxpayers and commit that Trump won’t take the plane with him when he leaves office: “The only thing more insulting to the taxpayers than spending money on a jet they don't need, would be for the president to take it with him, to take it out of our military inventory, when he leaves office.”

Hegseth: “See, the Air Force has done an incredible job making that a capable jet. But its capabilities and investment are classified and shouldn't be talked about.”

Murphy: “That’s not what I’m asking. Will you disclose the amount of money publicly?”

Hegseth: “I would imagine, as part of the regular budget process, that's something that we would look at.”

Murphy: “And will you commit that the president will not take…”

Hegseth: “But you have to look at the classification level of certain things that are not devolved for reasons of national security.”

Murphy: “Will you commit that the president will not take this jet with him out of federal inventory when he leaves office?”

Hegseth: “That's not a decision for necessarily me to make. And ultimately, we're grateful to have it in the fleet for the Air Force to protect the president of the United States.”

Murphy: “That's a deeply unsatisfactory answer to the American public.”

A full transcript of Murphy’s remarks is available below.

Murphy: Thank you all for being here today, Secretary Hegseth. The American people either didn't want this war or were deeply skeptical of this war because they have seen this country make the same mistake over and over again in wars in the Middle East, and that is to create either unrealistic or open-ended objectives. You said in March that the United States was “on plan to defeat, destroy, and disable all of Iran's meaningful military capabilities at a pace that the world has never seen before.” Obviously, as we've discussed here today, that objective has not been achieved and is not going to be achieved. Iran is adept, more adept than even at the start of the war, at hiding their capabilities or repairing after damage we have done. There's an open report that when it comes to their missile sites along the Strait of Hormuz, 30 of 33 are still operational.

Hegseth: I wouldn't believe all the open reports, Senator.

Murphy: But I've also heard you say in this hearing that the objectives now seem to be more limited than they were at the outset of the war. That this is about reopening the Strait and this is about dismantling [Iran’s] nuclear capability. And the president, of course, has said himself that he thinks Iran has a right to a missile program.

So, my question is pretty simple: Is it correct that it is no longer a war objective to destroy all of their military capacities? This is what the president has said. Have our goals been simplified to reopening the Strait and to getting into a negotiation over a nuclear program. Now, I don't think you have a realistic plan to do either of those things, but I think it's important for us to know what we're funding. Are the objectives much more limited today than they were when you made that statement in March?

Hegseth: So, I think the objectives have been consistent and clear from the beginning. And I would compare it to North Korea, where a conventional buildup was used to hide a nuclear capability that eventually evolved to a point where it couldn't be contested. And what Iran continued to do, even after Midnight Hammer, was try to build that conventional capability to dare anyone to stop them from pursuing nuclear weapons.

So, getting after their conventional capabilities, missile launchers, defense industrial base, their navy was all part of it. Ensuring they can't blackmail us into pursuing a nuclear capability, laser-focused on Iran will never have a nuclear capability – that's the promise the president has made, and that he will keep.

Murphy: Is it still a war objective, either through military action or through a diplomatic agreement to destroy and disable all of Iran's meaningful military capacities, including their missile program?

Hegseth: As far as all: when we talked about that from the podium at the outset of this, we were talking about their defense industrial base. And if you look at the metrics of their ability to make more, that it's been overwhelmingly destroyed. Not everything, but overwhelmingly. Now, do they have missiles in underground bunkers because they're a terror state? Sure, they do, and we've acknowledged that from the beginning. But their capacity is less today than it's ever been…

Murphy: They obviously, they obviously have significant capacity to effectively disrupt the entirety of the Middle East and oil flows out of the Middle East, and that's not going to change.

Let me ask you one more question. This is a request for supplemental funding because you don't have the funding in your base budget to do what you need to do, which makes questions about the base budget relevant.

There's been a lot of attention, Mr. Secretary, on the modernization of a luxury jet that was gifted to the president by the government of Qatar. Reports suggest that maybe as much as $1 billion in your base funding - an extraordinary amount of money - has been used for an upgrade, and the plane is back in the shop for a second upgrade.

As far as I can tell, never before has an administration not made public the amount of money for an upgrade or a construction contract on a presidential airplane. Obviously, we don't need or want to disclose the details of that upgrade. But never before have you withheld from Congress and the public the total amount of money.

I think there are two really important questions here. One, will you make public the amount of money that you are spending to upgrade this plane? And two, can you commit to this Congress and this committee that the president isn't going to take this plane with him when he leaves office? The only thing more insulting to the taxpayers than spending money on a jet they don't need, would be for the president to take it with him, to take it out of our military inventory, when he leaves office.

Hegseth: See, the Air Force has done an incredible job making that a capable jet. But its capabilities and investment are classified and shouldn't be talked about.

Murphy: That’s not what I’m asking. Will you disclose the amount of money publicly?

Hegseth: I would imagine, as part of the regular budget process, that's something that we would look at.

Murphy: And will you commit that the president will not take -

Hegseth: But you have to look at the classification level of certain things that are not devolved for reasons of national security.

Murphy: Will you commit that the president will not take this jet with him out of federal inventory when he leaves office?

Hegseth: That's not a decision for necessarily me to make. And ultimately, we're grateful to have it in the fleet for the Air Force to protect the president of the United States.

Murphy: That's a deeply unsatisfactory answer to the American public.

title: Sen. Murray Opening Remarks at Hearing with Sec. Hegseth on Trump’s $88 Billion Supplemental Request
text:
Murray: “My Democratic colleagues and I will do absolutely everything to ensure that we do take care of our servicemembers and keep our country safe… But my colleagues and I cannot and will not support rubberstamping a request to bankroll this war and whatever other misadventures Trump wants to get us into next.”

Murray: “President Trump has—by any objective measure—failed to achieve his goals. Our country is no safer or better off than before the war. In fact, we are considerably less safe.”

Murray: “Instead of bankrolling the president’s war or sending ICE $70 billion, my colleagues on the other side of the aisle could work with us to quadruple our investments to cure cancer, or help families afford child care, or help them afford to cool their homes.”

***WATCH: Senator Murray’s full opening remarks***

Washington, D.C. — Today—at a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing on President Trump’s supplemental funding request for the Iran war and more Pentagon funding—U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, delivered the following opening remarks.

Senator Murray’s remarks, as delivered, are below:

[ON SENATOR GRAHAM’S PASSING]

“First, I want to also acknowledge the loss of one of our colleagues on this dais. Like so many, I was very shocked and saddened to learn of Senator Graham’s passing. We disagreed on many issues, but there was no denying the energy that Lindsey brought to this job—and whenever we could find common ground, we managed to get something done. So I just wanted to express my heart goes out to his family, friends, and loved ones.

[TRUMP’S ILLEGAL WAR]

“Now, I want to start with a few facts.

“143 days ago, President Trump started a war of his own choosing with Iran.

“He did not consult Congress. He did not get authorization from Congress.

“He did not build a coalition of allies.

“He did not make a case to the American people. Nor did he ever win their support. Two-thirds of Americans oppose the war.

[TRAGIC CASUALTIES]

“And the president’s decision had catastrophic costs.

“Seventeen American servicemembers have now died.

“That includes three who tragically lost their lives over the last few days. And another is still missing.

“Several hundred more have been injured—including nearly 100 who have been hurt in just the last few weeks.

“We owe all of them and their families a debt of gratitude we can never repay.

“Thousands of civilians have also been killed.

[STAGGERING FINANCIAL COSTS OF THE WAR]

“The administration will tell the public—or Congress—the true financial costs of the war but we know it is very well into the tens of billions of dollars.

“Tax dollars we could’ve spent helping people afford health care—or building new housing—have now been lit on fire by a president who blundered us into a disastrous war.

“And the costs to families’ bank accounts are staggering.

“Economic growth has slowed to a crawl. Inflation has shot up about 50% since this war began.

“On average, gas cost just under three dollars on February 28. Today, it’s over four dollars and ticking back up with the Strait closed again. Americans have now paid more than $70 billion more on gas since the war began. That is $550 more per household.

“Fertilizer costs skyrocketed in the middle of spring planting, crushing farmers operating on extremely thin margins, and costing families more on just about everything they buy at the grocery store.

[COMPLETE LACK OF A PLAN OR CLEAR OBJECTIVES]

“The costs of this war have been astronomical. And what has it been for? What has actually been achieved?

“We hear a different rationale for this war every few days. It was about preempting ‘imminent threats,’ which we now know did not exist. It was about regime change, then liberating the Iranian people. It was about destroying Iran’s nuclear program and its navy. And at one point, it was about taking out its ballistic missiles until, that is, the president decided that actually ‘it’s a little bit unfair for them not to have some.’ Trump has even suggested the war is about taking Iran’s oil to ‘make a fortune.’

“And now, the United States’ primary strategic objective seems to actually just be reopening the Strait of Hormuz, which, of course, was fully open—toll-free—before the war began.

[FAILURE TO ACHIEVE STATED GOALS]

“President Trump has—by any objective measure—failed to achieve his goals. Our country is no safer or better off than before the war. In fact, we are considerably less safe.

“Our stockpiles have been depleted—and it’ll take years of production to fully replenish them—no matter how much money is thrown at the problem.

“Our global force posture is much weaker as assets have been moved to the Middle East.

“And we are now much farther away from a long-term solution to halt Iran’s nuclear program than we were before Trump ripped up the deal that President Obama negotiated, which secured actual, measurable commitments and progress—without ever starting a costly war.

“In fact, there are new reports that Iran may have moved nuclear assets into a mountain bunker—which raises concerns about whether Iran might restart its program.

[THE PRESIDENT’S FLIPPANT APPROACH TO DEADLY WAR]

“It used to be a pretty somber and serious thing—a president taking America to war and costing lives and taxpayer dollars, but this president has been downright flippant.

“The people I represent worry Trump thinks this is all a game and has sent men and women into harm’s way without any sort of plan, and now that he’s driven the car into the ditch, he wants taxpayers to bail him out.

“As the daughter of a World War II veteran and a Purple Heart recipient, the way this White House has blissfully operated with no plan for success is disrespectful to our men and women in uniform.

“These are patriots who are highly trained and have sacrificed tremendously to keep us safe. They shouldn’t be forced to put on a show for the president’s birthday parade, or do the job of Border Patrol agents, or risk their lives in a disastrous war that the president clearly failed to think through.

“And as a U.S. Senator, this administration’s refusal to explain what it is doing or how this war is protecting Americans, its refusal to seek authorization from Congress, and its expectation that Americans will now just pay for it all without any explanation or transparency, is disrespectful, and it’s insulting to the people back home that all of us represent.

[TRUMP’S ASK FOR MORE MONEY TO BANKROLL THE WAR]

“So, here we are. Five months later. The Strait is closed. The ceasefire hasn’t just disintegrated—this war is now spiraling out of control again.

“The president is threatening escalation and war crimes, and suggesting this could be another forever war.

“He has told us over 40 times now that a deal is near, and the war will be over soon. But now, he’s asking for $70 billion dollars more—and for us to just trust him it’ll work out fine.

“Look, I’ve been very clear, my Democratic colleagues and I will do absolutely everything to ensure that we do take care of our servicemembers and keep our country safe.

“Chairman Caine, I hope you know that every Democrat on this Committee deeply respects the sacrifices that you and our servicemembers and their families are making. Everyone who signed up to serve our country deserves to be more than an afterthought in a war that the president decided to launch, despite all the blinking red warnings.

“But my colleagues and I cannot and will not support rubberstamping a request to bankroll this war and whatever other misadventures Trump wants to get us into next.

“The American people want to see a quick and strategic end to this war, not $70 billion of their tax dollars sent to keep it going.

[INCOHERENT SUPPLEMENTAL REQUEST FOR PENTAGON]

“And I want to make a few important points:

“First, the president’s request is not even primarily a request to cover costs of the Iran war. This request is chock-full of asks to fund unrelated DOD priorities, which should be considered through our annual appropriations process, not in an emergency supplemental. And that includes almost a billion dollars for SOUTHCOM, nearly a billion dollars to keep deploying the National Guard here in D.C., and more than a billion dollars for the southern border.

“Secondly, President Trump is making this request as the Pentagon has a record-breaking $1 trillion total budget for FY26, including over $75 billion it has in unspent money from Republicans’ Big Ugly Bill. I understand you may have mismanaged your budget, Secretary Hegseth, but you have to do your due diligence to fix the cash flow problems that you’ve caused—before asking taxpayers for more.

“Third, the president is now asking all of us to approve tens of billions of dollars in new funding for the war while his administration still has yet to share actual cost estimates, essential information to justify the request, and a plan for where on Earth this conflict goes next.

“This administration is either hiding the truth from Congress and the American people or if you take at face value what they’ve said in the few briefings we’ve had, they have no idea what is going on and no plan to right the ship. Neither of which is acceptable.

[REQUEST FOR ASSISTANCE TO FARMERS WHACKED BY TRUMP’S POLICIES]

“Now, Trump is also asking Congress for over $10 billion to help struggling American farmers who have been crushed first by the tariffs, and then by this war, which has shot fertilizer and diesel costs through the roof.

“I’m digging into that request—but let me be clear: as we’re looking at what farmers might need to weather Trump’s storm, we must also help families put food on the table. And to do that, we should delay and ultimately reverse—Republicans’ deep cuts to SNAP, which have already kicked at least one million kids off of food assistance.

[REQUEST FOR STATE DEPT. FUNDING TRUMP REFUSES TO SPEND]

“Finally, Trump has also requested—and I had to read this one twice to believe—$1.3 billion dollars in new funding for the State Department for global health and humanitarian needs at the very same time his administration is withholding more than twice that amount in funding that has already been signed into law and is available for the same purposes.

“He is also asking for authorities to make U.S. taxpayers dollars subsidize the Venezuelan oil industry and to finance the establishment of private investment funds like the one he just handed over to one of his ballroom donors.

“Unfortunately, Secretary Rubio is not here with us today to explain those requests, to talk about how this war forced one of the largest evacuations of our diplomatic posts ever, or to explain whether, as National Security Advisor, he still thinks this war is the ‘right decision’ and whether he still ‘believe[s] in it strongly.’

[WHAT CONGRESS SHOULD BE FUNDING INSTEAD]

“So this is really a request to make taxpayers pay for the president’s reckless decisions from the Iran war to his trade wars, to his global health cuts—all while doing nothing to help families back home who are suffering because of those decisions. And that—that—is what we should be focused on: helping people.

“Because as Senator Padilla and others on both sides of the aisle will tell us shortly, there are urgent domestic needs we should be addressing instead of sending more money for Trump to drop bombs overseas. Priorities like disaster relief for our communities that have been ravaged by the unthinkable—or taking action to lower families’ costs.

“You know what’s a crisis right now? The fact that there are families I hear from back home who are working full-time and still being forced to decide whether to skip meals so they can finally buy their kids a new pair of shoes.

“You know what’s a crisis? The fact that hospitals are shutting down and kids are going hungry because of Republican cuts.

“Instead of bankrolling the president’s war or sending ICE $70 billion, my colleagues on the other side of the aisle could work with us to quadruple our investments to cure cancer, or help families afford child care, or help them afford to cool their homes.

“These are policy choices. And Republican leadership has chosen to focus on funding war and ICE endlessly without a single cent for our American families.

“So let me close with this: this president says we can’t afford health care. We can’t afford child care. We can’t afford housing. But somehow—we can always afford another war. No price tag on that.

“Families in Washington state are skipping doctor’s visits so they can afford groceries—and Trump wants Congress to cut him a blank check for a war no one supports.

“The American people entrust us to spend their taxpayer dollars strategically and thoughtfully. This is a huge responsibility.

“So let me be clear: I’m ready to work with my colleagues in a bipartisan way as always to address the needs of our nation and the American people, but I hope we can have real conversations about why there seems to always be money for Trump’s wars but never money for the families back home who are desperate for a little relief.

“So, I look forward to today’s discussion.”

###

title: Senator Murray Grills Hegseth on State of Iran War, Refuses to Write Trump a Blank Check to Fund Iran War
text:
***WATCH and READ: Senator Murray’s opening remarks***

***WATCH: Senator Murray’s full questioning***

Washington, D.C. — Today—at a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing on President Trump’s supplemental funding request for the Iran war, more Pentagon funding, and other requests—U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, grilled Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins on the disastrous and costly failure that is the Iran war and on why the president is seeking more funding to keep it going—particularly as the Pentagon sits on unspent funds—instead of working with Congress to help families with skyrocketing costs.

“My Democratic colleagues and I will do absolutely everything to ensure that we do take care of our servicemembers and keep our country safe,” Senator Murray said in opening remarks. “But my colleagues and I cannot and will not support rubberstamping a request to bankroll this war and whatever other misadventures Trump wants to get us into next. The American people want to see a quick and strategic end to this war, not $70 billion of their tax dollars sent to keep it going.”

“Instead of bankrolling the president’s war or sending ICE $70 billion, my colleagues on the other side of the aisle could work with us to quadruple our investments to cure cancer, or help families afford child care, or help them afford to cool their homes,” continued Murray. “These are policy choices.”

President Trump has requested $87.6 billion in supplemental funding he wants Congress to quickly approve in addition to the staggering $1.5 trillion defense budget he has already requested for fiscal year 2027. His supplemental request includes asks for:

$67.1 billion in new funding for the Department of Defense, even as DOD has a historic $1 trillion combined budget for FY26 and sits on roughly $75 billion in unspent funding provided in Republicans’ “Big Beautiful Bill.” The request includes:

$18+ billion in munitions that have already been requested in the president’s FY27 budget request.

$800 million to continue funding the National Guard’s deployment in D.C.

$1+ billion for the Army to patrol the southern border.

$900 million for SOUTHCOM to support this administration’s illegal boat strikes in the Caribbean.

Operational and management funding to cover unexpected costs associated with the Iran war, which the Pentagon has existing flexibilities to shift funds around to cover.

$1.7 billion to cover costs associated with recruiting more servicemembers than DOD needs and than was contemplated by the FY26 budget. DOD has already submitted a request to reprogram existing funding to cover these costs.

$11.1 billion for the U.S. Department of Agriculture, which includes:

$10 billion to make economic relief payments to farmers ravaged by Trump’s tariffs and rising input costs fueled by the Iran war.

$1.1 billion for ad hoc disaster assistance that would only benefit farmers in Florida.

$9.4 billion for a variety of other requests, including:

$3.3 billion for the State Department. Of that amount, $1.3 billion is requested for Ebola response and humanitarian assistance—all while the administration withholds more than twice that amount in already-enacted funding available for the same purposes.

[TRUMP’S INCOHERENT PENTAGON REQUEST]

Senator Murray began by pressing Secretary Hegseth on how the Pentagon’s request is not merely a request to cover costs associated with President Trump’s disastrous war, but an effort to secure tens of billions of dollars more for unrelated Pentagon priorities that are not needed on an emergency basis and should be considered in the annual appropriations process.

MURRAY: Secretary Hegseth, your department received $150 billion last year in the Republicans’ “Big Beautiful Bill.” And it also received a record $839 billion for fiscal year 2026 – more money than you asked for last year. Combined, that is a $1 trillion budget for the year—and as I already mentioned, your department has yet to spend half of the reconciliation funds.

Despite that, you are here today asking for tens of billions of dollars more for things that you’ve already asked for in your FY27 request or that have nothing to do with Iran.

This administration has tried to sell this as an emergency request, but it may be better understood as an attempt to skirt the normal appropriations process.

Here are just a few of the things requested in this “Iran” supplemental: $800 million for the National Guard to patrol DC even longer. Over $1 billion for the Army to patrol the southern border, which is DHS’s job. $900 million to support the administration’s illegal boat strikes in the Caribbean. Over $18 billion for munitions, which you have already requested in your FY27 budget request. And $1.7 billion to pay for your decision to recruit more people than the services need, which was not contemplated by the FY26 funding bill Congress recently passed. Now, you have already submitted a reprogramming request on this that our subcommittee is considering now, which really underscores the point I made in my opening remarks that the problem is not a lack of money, but poor planning.

So, I’ll be blunt: the truth is your request does not make a lot of sense.

So, let me ask you a simple question: Why exactly are billions of dollars more for the National Guard and this administration’s illegal strikes in the Caribbean urgently needed for the Iran war?

HEGSETH: Well, Senator, I wouldn’t—of course—agree with your characterization, but why this kind of spending is needed is because of the gross negligence and neglect of the Biden administration inside our department. [Biden] ran it like a bureaucracy, abandoned our strength posture around the world, so we’re having to reestablish deterrence.

You mentioned the end strength numbers, and I will acknowledge that we are ahead of schedule on end strength in recruiting, 8,000 in the Navy, 6,000 in the Army, 4,000 in the Air Force. Because under President Trump, there’s been record and historic over 30-year recruiting records inside our department since he won the election. Because the American people didn’t want to sign up for what Joe Biden was providing our military, and they want to sign up for what President Trump is doing in his leadership, and so those are good problems to have that we need to fund, and a reflection of momentum. And this budget will allow us to continue the kind of momentum that gets us ahead.

MURRAY: My point is that a lot of this request does not feel like an emergency. Let me move on.

[HEGSETH’S CONTRADICTORY STATEMENTS ON THE WAR]

Senator Murray then grilled Secretary Hegseth on a few of the many contradictory statements he has made about what the U.S. has achieved in the war.

MURRAY: Secretary Hegseth, like most Americans, I have had a lot of trouble following this administration’s contradictory statements about the war.

On April 8, you said, and I quote, “Their missile program is functionally destroyed, launchers, production facilities and existing stockpiles depleted and decimated and almost completely ineffective.”

Mr. Secretary, Iran has been firing at U.S. military bases in the region and at ships for the last week. How is it possible if their capabilities were “functionally destroyed” three months earlier, as you claimed for them to be doing this now?

HEGSETH: Senator, Iran is at the weakest point militarily it has ever been in in the past decade. Certainly, maybe in 47 years, as they’d gathered effectively a terror army, and that terror army was built to try to create conventional capabilities to defend against a pursuit of nuclear weapons, which meant thousands of ballistic missiles, many of which we have destroyed, others of which they have put inside facilities and hidden in underground facilities—that’s what terror regimes would do. So, I acknowledge they still have capabilities, no doubt, but the amount of damage that we’ve done to them over the course of these series of operations has put them in the worst place they’ve ever been.

MURRAY: Let me move on. On May 5, you claimed that “Iran doesn’t control the Strait,” and you said that there was a “powerful red, white, and blue dome over the Strait.”

If that was true, how did Iran shrink ship traffic in the Strait to a trickle again last week?

HEGSETH: We pushed almost, I believe, between 400 and 500 million barrels of oil under the nose of Iran over the course of Project Freedom, which went underground, which I acknowledged after we did so. Covertly, because it was more effective to do so quietly than to do so publicly. So, we’ve been in control of moving traffic through there for quite some time. Will they retain the ability to recklessly shoot at commercial shipping? And that’s what happened. We had a ceasefire, and then they shot at commercial shipping recklessly—

MURRAY: Well, you also said at that same press conference—and I’m going to quote you—you urged Iran to, “let innocent ships pass freely. These international waters belong to all nations, not to Iran to tax, toll, or control.”

Last week, President Trump said that the U.S. would charge a 20 percent toll to each ship to pass through the Strait. So, based on your opposition to tolls, did you talk the President out of that idea or did someone else?

HEGSETH: Iran’s not charging tolls, and they’re shooting at ships right now.

MURRAY: But Trump said that he wanted to charge a 20 percent toll.

HEGSETH: We have a blockade right now of all Iranian ships, Iranian ports, and it’s effective.

MURRAY: My time is up.

###

title: Padilla, Schumer Launch New Anti-Corruption Initiative to Expose Trump’s Self-Dealing, Stop Presidential Profiteering
text:
New Senate Democratic working group to expose the cost of corruption for American families, develop legislation to stop Presidential profiteering

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) joined Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) in launching a new Senate Democratic anti-corruption initiative to expose how President Trump’s rampant self-dealing is costing American families and to develop legislation that would prevent future presidents from using public office for personal profit.

The initiative includes a new Senate Democratic anti-corruption working group and the release of a report, “The Cost of Corruption: How Trump Turns Power Into Profit At Americans’ Expense.” The working group will expose the Trump Administration’s abuses, identify the financial harm inflicted on taxpayers and working families, and develop reforms to stop future presidents from exploiting the power of the White House for their own enrichment.

“In this Administration, corruption flows from the top down,” said Senator Padilla. “From sweetheart deals with the DOJ to stock purchases ahead of mega-million government contracts and payments for pardons, the pattern is clear: the grift is coming directly from the Oval Office. Meanwhile, MAGA Republicans have made it harder than ever for families to make ends meet by driving up the cost of gas, groceries, and healthcare. We’ll keep exposing their corruption — and keep fighting to hold them accountable.”

“Trump is without question the most corrupt president in American history,” said Leader Schumer. “Trump has betrayed the American people by using our highest office not for the good of country, but to pad his own bank account, at the expense of working families. Senate Democrats are launching this effort to expose the corruption, show Americans exactly what it is costing them, and build the reforms needed to stop any president from using public office for personal profit. The presidency belongs to the American people. It is not Donald Trump’s business to sell.”

On the campaign trail, President Trump promised to “end government corruption and to take our country back from the special interests.” But his presidency has done the opposite: using the presidency to advance his own financial interests, reward wealthy donors and corporate allies, and direct taxpayer resources toward vanity projects and political favors. Early in 2025, he fired a long-serving Democratic commissioner from the Federal Election Commission, the bipartisan anti-corruption watchdog agency founded after the Watergate scandals and has left the agency sidelined without a quorum for over a year.

The new report details how Trump has used public power to benefit himself, his family, his friends, and his supporters—and how ordinary Americans have paid the price. The report documents the Administration’s efforts to:

Weaken the agency charged with protecting consumers from financial abuse

Undermine wages, workplace protections, and workers’ bargaining power

Cut food assistance and other basic support to finance tax breaks for the wealthy

Waste taxpayer money on Trump’s vanity projects

Reward corporations, donors, and political allies with favorable government treatment

Create opportunities for foreign governments and private interests to curry favor with the President through his family’s businesses and financial ventures

In addition to Padilla and Schumer, the Senate Democratic anti-corruption working group will be comprised of Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), and Andy Kim (D-N.J.).

As Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Rules and Administration with jurisdiction over the Federal Election Commission, Senator Padilla is a leader in the fight against corruption and for campaign finance reform. He is a lead cosponsor of Senator Jeanne Shaheen’s (D-N.H.) constitutional amendment to overturn the Supreme Court’s misguided and destructive Citizens United v. FEC decision, which removed campaign finance restrictions and enabled organizations to spend unlimited money to influence elections. Last year, Senator Padilla denounced the illegal firing of FEC Chair Ellen Weintraub and led 10 Democratic Senators to demand President Trump rescind his attempt to fire her. Last month, Padilla joined several Democratic colleagues on the floor to mark the anniversary of the Citizens United decision and call to take back our democracy from the unlimited influence of billionaire donors.

The full report is available here.

###

title: WATCH: Padilla Blasts Trump Administration for Leaving Disaster Survivors Behind
text:
WATCH: Padilla: “Disasters do not distinguish between red states and blue states – and when it comes to disaster aid, neither should Congress”

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) testified at a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing to raise concerns over President Trump’s recent supplemental funding request that did not include disaster aid funding for communities to rebuild and recover following catastrophic natural disasters across the country.

In his remarks, Padilla recognized the lasting impact of last year’s Eaton and Palisades fires, highlighting the damage caused by the fires and the need for long-term funding to recover and rebuild. He emphasized that during the fires, neighboring states provided firefighting support, yet the Trump Administration has blocked further funding for disaster aid.

“Walking around the Palisades and the Altadena communities during the fires and after the fires, you couldn’t help but be moved by the scale of the devastation,” said Senator Padilla. “Congress has historically come together on a bipartisan basis to provide aid and long-term recovery funding to help communities recover and rebuild… But instead of following that historical practice, this Administration has left California waiting for more than a year and a half.”

Padilla further slammed the Trump Administration’s politicization of and efforts to limit disaster aid funding and instead prioritize Trump’s unauthorized war in Iran that has increased costs for American families.

“Californians in Altadena and the Palisades have now waited more than 18 months. Yet, long-term recovery funding is still absent from even the Administration’s request,” continued Senator Padilla. “Instead, it asks taxpayers to spend hundreds of billions of dollars more on a war that Congress has never authorized. A war that’s raising gas prices, worsening supply chains, and making our country less safe. And for which 17 servicemembers have already paid the ultimate sacrifice, with many more seriously injured.”

Padilla urged the Senate Appropriations Committee to quickly address the need for bipartisan disaster relief without strings attached so that communities can recover and rebuild. He expressed concern over recent wildfires and encouraged his colleagues increase funding for resources to respond to the growing threats of natural disasters across the country.

“I want to be crystal clear: no disaster-impacted community, regardless of where it is located, should ever be held hostage or treated as a bargaining chip for other political priorities,” Senator Padilla continued. “Disasters do not distinguish between red states and blue states. And when it comes to disaster aid, neither should Congress.”

Senator Padilla has fought relentlessly to secure and protect access to desperately needed disaster relief aid for families in California.

Yesterday, Padilla, along with Senators Thom Tillis (R-N.C.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), and John Curtis (R-Utah) urged Congressional leaders to include long-term disaster recovery funding in any supplemental appropriations package moving forward.

In January, on the one-year anniversary of the devastating Eaton and Palisades fires, Padilla and Schiff and the Chairs of the Republican and Democratic Congressional Delegations — Representatives Ken Calvert (R-Calif.-41) and Zoe Lofgren (D-Calif.-18) — led the entire bipartisan California Congressional delegation in urging Trump to provide overdue federal disaster relief funding and resources to help Los Angeles County communities rebuild and recover.

In the immediate aftermath of the Los Angeles fires, Padilla and Schiff led 47 bipartisan members of the California Congressional delegation in successfully urging President Biden to grant Governor Newsom’s request for a major disaster declaration to expedite timely relief to Los Angeles County residents impacted by these disasters.

Video of Padilla’s testimony is available here.

Transcript of Padilla’s remarks is available below:

Thank you, Madam Chair, Vice Chair Murray, members of the committee. Appreciate the opportunity to testify on behalf of the people of California, and especially the survivors of last year’s devastating fires in Los Angeles County. And I want to acknowledge that some of them are here in the audience today, advocating for relief, and I’m proud to work alongside them.

As many of you recall, 18 months ago, 60,000 acres across Southern California burned. That’s roughly three and a half times the size of Manhattan. Over 16,000 homes, businesses, schools, and other structures were destroyed. And most devastatingly, 31 Californians lost their lives. To respond, more than 7,500 firefighters worked literally round the clock for more than three weeks to extinguish the fires. And those firefighters weren’t just from California. Many came from our neighboring states of Oregon, Washington, Arizona, some as far away as Utah, Texas, and Montana. Colleagues, because as Americans, that’s what we do. We help each other. We don’t condition our response based on who a community voted for in the last election. When Americans need help, we help.

Now, walking around the Palisades and the Altadena communities during the fires and after the fires, you couldn’t help but be moved by the scale of the devastation. The images of nothing standing but a chimney amongst a pile of ash. Cars literally melted into the streets where the drivers where they had been parked. In the wake of disasters like this, Congress has historically come together on a bipartisan basis to provide aid and long-term recovery funding to help communities recover and rebuild, regardless of whether the disaster was in a state represented by Republicans or Democrats. But instead of following that historical practice, this Administration has left California waiting for more than a year and a half, while asking Congress to fund hundreds of billion dollars for other purposes.

I want to be crystal clear: no disaster-impacted community, regardless of where it is located, should ever be held hostage or treated as a bargaining chip for other political priorities. Californians in Altadena and the Palisades have now waited more than 18 months. Yet, long-term recovery funding is still absent from even the Administration’s request. Instead, it asks taxpayers to spend hundreds of billions of dollars more on a war that Congress has never authorized. A war that’s raising gas prices, worsening supply chains, and making our country less safe. And for which 17 servicemembers have already paid the ultimate sacrifice, with many more seriously injured. Now we know this committee can address disaster relief without tying it to a laundry list of unrelated priorities because it’s done so many times before. Including as recently as December 2024, when the committee, on a bipartisan basis, passed more than 100 billion dollars of relief. There’s no reason we can’t do it again.

Congress, we must, excuse me Colleagues, we must reject the premise that it is okay to keep survivors waiting for help, because the president, any president, decides they need something else from Congress to get it. To that end, I do want to thank my colleagues, Senators Tillis, Schiff, and Curtis, for joining me in sending a bipartisan letter to the committee just yesterday, supporting long-term disaster recovery funding, Madam Chair, I’d like to enter this letter into the record at this time.

And I’ll be wrapping up soon here. I also want to reiterate what I said earlier. We know the next disaster is coming. Anyone who stepped outside of Washington this last weekend, or across at least a dozen states, saw and breathed the very impacts of wildfires. And it may be Canada now, but it’s going to be one of our states next. As of last week, the federal government has already spent over 3.3 billion dollars in wildfire suppression this fiscal year. Even though the peak of fire season is August and September, that’s still ahead of us. That should concern the committee.

We cannot allow wildfire suppression funding to run out before the end of the fiscal year. So in addition to the long-term disaster recovery funding, I urge the committee to examine the need for emergency suppression funds as well. And I would note that the Fire Fix, which has provided a steady resource for fighting wildfires, will expire in Fiscal Year 2027. Congress needs to extend and increase that funding to ensure firefighters have all the resources they need to respond to the ever-growing threat of wildfires.

I’ll close by reiterating what I said at the outset: disasters do not distinguish between red states and blue states. And when it comes to disaster aid, neither should Congress. So, thank you again for holding this hearing and allowing me to be a voice for my constituents and for disaster survivors across the country. I look forward to working with this committee to ensure that everyone has the resources and support that they need to recover and rebuild, regardless of which state they call home. Thank you very much.

###

title: Reed & Whitehouse Push to Get Graham’s Bipartisan Russia Sanctions Bill to Trump’s Desk
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – When Russian President Vladimir Putin ordered the invasion of Ukraine in February of 2022, he envisioned a quick and easy military operation. Nearly four and half years later, the conflict has turned into a military, economic, and human disaster for Russia. But the Russian war machine continues to be fueled by high oil and gas prices.

In an effort to put pressure on Putin to end the war, U.S. Senators Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) are teaming up with U.S. Senators Darline Graham (R-SC), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Ted Budd (R-NC) and 56 of their Senate colleagues in introducing the bipartisan Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 (S.5025). The legislation aims to hold major purchasers of Russian oil and natural gas accountable for economically supporting Russia’s war in Ukraine. The bill would sanction key sectors of Russia’s war economy, including its shadow fleet -- which is used to export oil despite sanctions -- and penalize countries like China who’ve helped fund the Russian invasion.

A version of the bipartisan bill had been stalled by the Trump Administration for over a year. The day before former Senator Lindsey Graham (R-SC) unexpectedly passed away on July 11, after returning from Ukraine, he and a group of bipartisan lawmakers announced that the Trump Administration agreed to support the bipartisan measure to impose new U.S. sanctions on Russia.

“Until the very day he passed, Lindsey remained focused on passing the Russia sanctions bill. Passing this legislation would honor my brother’s steadfast commitment to our national security and it would provide President Trump with additional leverage to bring this war to an end. I look forward to working with my colleagues to pass this legislation and send it to President Trump’s desk,” said Senator Darline Graham.

“Ukraine is at a critical crossroads — and we must meet this pivotal moment with a powerful sanctions bill. As Ukraine turns the tide on the battlefield, our Russia sanctions bill would be historically impactful in stopping Russia’s murderous slaughter,” said Senator Richard Blumenthal. “When Senator Graham and I last spoke, he was absolutely exultant, calling from Kyiv with news that President Trump would support this bill to impose scorching tariffs and sanctions on purchasers of Russian oil and stop them from fueling Putin’s war machine. Now is the time to push Russia toward peace. Ukraine is gaining net territory and reaching deep into Russia with its drones and missiles. Sanctions provide a path toward peace. Our bill is the product of lengthy, detailed, difficult bipartisan work, and now has broad bipartisan support. Passing this legislation right now would be a fitting tribute to Senator Graham’s fierce support for Ukraine’s freedom.”

“The time to increase pressure on Moscow is now. Our overwhelmingly bipartisan sanctions package has the power to cripple Putin’s revenue streams by targeting the energy exports that bankroll Russia’s unjust war machine. Our colleague and friend, Senator Lindsey Graham, worked tirelessly to stand up to Russian aggression, and now we have the opportunity to honor his leadership and cement his legacy,” said Senator Ted Budd.

“This measure is a tribute to Senator Graham’s tenacious, bipartisan work in support of Ukraine, and a necessary step to deprive Putin’s war machine of financial resources for its illegal invasion,” said Senator Jack Reed, the Ranking Member of the Senate Armed Services Committee.

“Today’s bill continues the work of the late Senator Graham, my dear friend and one of Ukraine’s most relentless advocates in the Senate,” said Senator Whitehouse, a member of the Finance Committee. “This forceful, bipartisan measure will disrupt the Kremlin’s massive oil and gas economy, up the financial stakes, and help achieve victory for Ukraine.”

With sixty cosponsors, the bipartisan bill has already established a filibuster-proof majority. It is now up to Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-SD) to schedule a vote on the bill.

The legislation is also cosponsored by U.S. Senators John Thune (R-SD), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Katie Britt (R-AL), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Roger Wicker (R-MS), Jim Risch (R-ID), Chris Coons (D-DE), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), Michael Bennet (D-CO) Tom Cotton (R-AR), Tim Scott (R-SC), Angus King (I-ME), John Barrasso (R-WY), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Susan Collins (R-ME), Mitch McConnell (R-KY), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Thom Tillis (R-NC), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Joni Ernst (R-IA), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Pete Ricketts (R-NE), Brian Schatz (D-HI), John Cornyn (R-TX), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Tim Sheehy (R-MT), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), John Curtis (R-UT), John Fetterman (D-PA), Dan Sullivan (R-AK), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Gary Peters (D-MI), James Lankford (R-OK), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Marsha Blackburn (R-TN), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), John Boozman (R-AR), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Kevin Cramer (R-ND), Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), Jon Husted (R-OH), John Hoeven (R-ND), Deb Fischer (R-NE), Jim Justice (R-WV), Mike Rounds (R-SD), Ted Cruz (R-TX), John Kennedy (R-LA), Cynthia Lummis (R-WY), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Rick Scott (R-FL), Jerry Moran (R-KS), Tommy Tuberville (R-AL), Dave McCormick (R-PA), Alan Armstrong (R-OK), and Steve Daines (R-MT).

BACKGROUND

The Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026 would impose primary and secondary sanctions against Russia and actors supporting Russia’s war in Ukraine. The sanctions target Russian officials, oligarchs, their family members, foreign persons, Russian banks and financial institutions, and the Russian Shadow Fleet.

The legislation also directs the President to impose up to 100 percent tariffs on imported goods from countries that buy the majority of Russian oil and gas and enable Russian sanctions evasion. The new text limits these tariffs to the five largest importers of Russian crude oil and gas. It also contains a waiver, consistent with other mandatory sanctions bills, allowing the President to waive sanctions, restrictions, or duties upon a justification and certification to Congress that the waiver is in the national interest of the United States.

The bill also includes an exception for countries importing less than 15 percent of Russia's natural gas exports and taking significant steps to reduce those imports.

title: Reed Questions Hegseth on DOD Iran War & Notes That DOD Has Plenty of Money but Lacks Right Priorities, Strategy, & Civilian Leadership
text:
*** WATCH: Video of Sen. Reed at Appropriations Committee hearing ***

WASHINGTON, DC – Noting that President Trump rushed the nation into an unauthorized war with Iran; failed to plan for the most obvious contingencies; and has yet to achieve any of the objectives used as a pre-text for war, U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI), a member of the Appropriations Committee who opposed the war from the outset, today questioned Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth at a Senate Appropriations Committee hearing on President Trump’s $67.1 billion supplemental funding request for the Iran war, which continues to increase prices on all Americans.

As President Trump intensifies the conflict with Iran, his Administration is seeking more taxpayer dollars to fund the war: $67.1 billion in extra military spending this year. That number includes over $18 billion in munitions that have already been requested in the president’s FY27 budget request; an extra $1 billion for the Army to patrol the southern border; and another $800 million to continue funding the National Guard’s deployment in Washington, DC. President Trump’s supplemental request also comes at a time when DOD sits on roughly $75 billion in unspent funding provided in Republicans’ party-line “One Big Beautiful Bill.”

At the outset of the hearing, Reed noted that while the supplemental request seeks billions of dollars for ad hoc disaster assistance that would only benefit farmers in the Midwest and Florida, President Trump is unfairly denying over $19 million in emergency declaration assistance to Rhode Island for the historic blizzard the state experienced earlier this year.

During the hearing, Senator Reed pressed Secretary Hegseth about the failure to plan for the obvious contingency that Iran would try to effectively shut down the Strait of Hormuz.

SEN. REED: Secretary Hegseth: On February 28th, when you initiated this war without authorization from Congress, the Strait of Hormuz was open and providing vital fuel supplies for the whole world. Now they're closed effectively, impacting globally the price of oil and the economies of the whole world. But the Department of Defense has been planning for potential operations against Iran for many, many years. And one of their obvious assumptions was that the Strait of Hormuz could be closed. Were you unaware of that?

SEC. HEGSETH: Senator, you are correct. Nobody plans more and looks at more contingencies than our department, and so, of course, undertaking a historic effort like this, at this scope and scale, of course, the Strait of Hormuz was front and center in every single aspect of that. Hence why one of our key objectives to begin with was to sink the entirety of Iran's Navy, which its conventional Navy was sunk. Now, you can't get rid of every single fast boat in every single machine gun and a fast boat, or every single coastal cruise missile. So we acknowledge that if the state decided to become a terror state shooting at commercial shipping, that would be an ongoing and contested part of the battle, to include their willingness to mine international waters.

REED: So you were completely aware of that the Strait of Hormuz could be closed. And obviously, sinking their ships has not affected their ability to effectively close the Strait. Did you...

HEGSETH: We had U.S. boats that surrendered to Iranian ships under the Biden administration. So, their Navy was effective in...

REED: Listen, we're talking about the war you started. Not a situation in which oil was flowing freely. There was no conflict. We weren’t losing personnel as a result of Iranian action. So, your fallback to the Biden administration is just a very, very obvious excuse for what I think is, probably, as you describe so often, gross negligence. You did not fully inform the President that you would be in a situation where the Strait of Hormuz could be effectively closed, oil prices could surge, and, effectively, the Iranians could maintain their ability to strike back as they are right now. They just killed some of our servicemembers last weekend.

HEGSETH: This battlefield, and all the dynamics of it, of which the Chairman and I are responsible for ensuring the President understands every branch and sequel of what could happen, and we did. So the fact that those contingencies all were part of the possibility, and we understood that, is all the more reason why President Trump deserves the kind of praise he should get for undertaking this effort, having the courage to ensure that crazy Islamists can't have a nuclear weapon to hold us at issue, and he's been willing to stay here to do that, regardless of the challenge... It should be. So these should be...

REED: Excuse me. He should be praised for starting a war without authority, creating a situation in which the world economy is suffering tremendously? Where we have to have extra money for our farmers? And we have no outcome, at least no realistic outcome in sight yet. Let me switch to General Caine. General Caine, these airstrikes have not yet deterred and defeated the Iranians. Do you think airstrikes alone will do that?

GEN. CAINE: Sir, I think academically, as you look across the totality of history, air power's got limits, and we always have to be mindful of those. I think where America's area of exclusivity is, is when we bring the totality of the diplomatic, informational, economic, and pair that with the military and there's a lot of that work going on, sir.

REED: Well, the military, the next step would be escalation by ground combat. Do you anticipate that escalation?

CAINE: Sir, I think it'd be unhelpful for me to opine on hypotheticals. What I can tell you is we always develop an unbelievable amount of options and the associated risks, and then my main job is to always ensure that leaders understand those options and the risks.

REED: Now, if you employ ground troops to seize objectives, which I would assume would be the first stage. Are you prepared for an extended guerrilla war, which would likely happen in that area?

CAINE: Sir, with all due respect, I think it'd be unhelpful for me to opine on hypothetical situations, on whatever decisions the president may or may not take in the future.

REED: Have you advised the President that ground combat would be very expensive in the lives of our soldiers, sailors, marines, airmen, and also could probably to an extended unconventional war in that area? I don't see the Iranian sort of throwing their hands up and saying, you know, ‘welcome to Iran.’

CAINE: [Laughter] Senator, I always advised the president on a range of military options, and all of the risks that are contained within that. But I have to keep my military advice to the president, private, sir.

REED: Well, thank you.

After the hearing, Senator Reed stated:

“DOD has plenty of money. It lacks the right priorities and sensible civilian leadership. There is no reason for Congress to approve $67.1 billion when this Administration continues to mislead about the actual cost of this war.

“I opposed this war from the start because it was clear where things were headed with Trump and Hegseth in charge. Their actions are driving up prices, costing U.S. servicemember lives, and depleting important weapon stockpiles. Unfortunately, President Trump and Secretary Hegseth are only now just realizing that military supremacy without a coherent strategy and robust diplomatic engagement does not translate to automatic victory. The Trump Administration doesn’t seem to have a firm grasp on Iran’s political and strategic thinking.

“Given that President Trump has no coherent endgame and has not achieved the stated objectives he used as a pretext for war, Americans are right to be skeptical of simply throwing more money and military weapons at the problem and expecting a different result.

“Nearly five months into a high-cost, low-return war that has failed to make America more secure, President Trump should not be asking for more money without first seeking authorization from Congress and the American people.”

title: Ricketts Announces Support for Reforming Birthright Citizenship
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE) announced his support for reforming birthright citizenship:

“Birthright citizenship was included in the U.S. Constitution to reconcile an incredible error in America. It was added to ensure those freed from slavery were granted American citizenship. This made our nation better.

Today, birthright citizenship is being exploited by bad actors and our adversaries. We are one of the only nations that lacks commonsense guardrails on birthright citizenship. This incentivizes illegal immigration and promotes birth tourism. Illegal immigrants and non-citizens are crossing our borders and having children, who are then given American citizenship automatically. Our current policy also allows bad actors to game the system with birth tourism. Unrestrained birthright citizenship hands Communist China an opportunity to infiltrate our country. We must reform the system.

I am proud to be an American. I understand why others want to be a citizen of our great nation. But becoming an American is a privilege, not a right. It is about more than being born on our soil. It’s about committing to our nation’s promise and holding to our values of freedom and democracy. I support reforming birthright citizenship in America.”

title: VIDEO: Ricketts on Combatting ATM Fraud and Scams in Nebraska
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE) discussed his work to combat crypto ATM fraud in Nebraska. Ricketts highlighted successes at the State of Nebraska Department of Banking and discouraged overreliance on the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB).

“As Governor of Nebraska, I had a Department of Banking, and if any of our consumers in Nebraska came and approached us with a problem, no matter how big the bank was, we would investigate to make sure that that consumer got the resolution they needed from whatever problem they had,” Ricketts said. “Take the example of crypto kiosk ATM scams. The state of Nebraska and twenty-eight other states have passed laws to protect consumers on this and combat them. In Nebraska, from September 2025 to June 2026, the Nebraska Department of Banking returned $325,000 back to consumers in our state stemming from crypto ATM fraud and scams. It wasn’t the CFPB that did that — it was the State of Nebraska Department of Banking. In the CLARITY Act, I worked to ensure that the bill preserves the authority of states to enforce laws such as these crypto ATM laws, laws that have helped protect consumers.”

title: Risch, Crapo, Simpson Celebrate Idaho Nuclear Tech Hub Designation
text:
WASHINGTON-U.S. Senators Jim Risch and Mike Crapo and U.S. Representative Mike Simpson (all R-Idaho) celebrated the U.S. Economic Development Administration’s (EDA) announcement awarding approximately $31 million to the Intermountain-West Nuclear Energy Corridor (INEC) Tech Hub, a regional initiative led by the Idaho Advanced Energy Consortium (IAEC) of more than 45 organizations across Idaho and Wyoming.

The INEC Tech Hub aims to leverage the region’s existing nuclear ecosystem to accelerate the deployment and commercialization of advanced nuclear reactors, strengthen domestic nuclear supply chains, and enhance U.S. energy security. IAEC estimates the Tech Hub will create more than 900 high-paying jobs and generate $190 million in regional economic impact over five years.

“The future of American nuclear energy is being developed in Idaho,” said Risch. “Today’s investment by the U.S. Department of Commerce in the Intermountain-West Nuclear Energy Consortium Tech Hub capitalizes on Idaho’s deep nuclear history and will expand opportunities for the West to maintain this strong reputation.”

“This $31 million award is a significant investment in Idaho’s future and further establishes our state as a national leader in advanced nuclear energy,” said Crapo. “The INEC Tech Hub, led by the Idaho Advanced Energy Consortium, will build on Idaho’s unmatched expertise and innovation in small modular reactors and reinforce our nation’s technological leadership while reducing reliance on foreign adversaries for critical energy capabilities. I congratulate the many public and private partners whose collaboration has helped make this achievement possible.”

“I’m thrilled to celebrate the Department of Commerce’s $31 million investment in the INEC Tech Hub,” said Simpson. “After my Idaho colleagues and I expressed our strong support for this application, it is exciting to see this investment become a reality. This funding will strengthen American nuclear energy while reinforcing Idaho’s leadership in nuclear innovation. Today’s announcement is an important step toward advancing American energy dominance and strengthening our energy security.”

“What we’re building here is bigger than any one organization, any one company, or any one community,” said Hope Morrow, IAEC Vice President and Workforce and Economic Development Manager at INL. “The INEC Tech Hub is what American innovation looks like when everyone brings their best — and the people of the Intermountain West are going to see the benefits in jobs, opportunity, and long-term energy security.”

“The demand for nuclear energy is on the rise, and the Trump Administration is providing the energy industry with the resources it needs to meet that demand, including more nuclear reactors,” said U.S. Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick. “This award will position Idaho and Wyoming as global leaders in advanced small modular reactors and leverage the region’s existing nuclear manufacturing capabilities to accelerate reactor deployment, speed commercialization of next-generation reactors, and enhance U.S. energy security.”

The $31 million investment will:

Support advanced nuclear fuel fabrication, testing, and transportation;

Train workers for careers in nuclear construction, manufacturing, fuel fabrication, and operations; and

Help firms develop and strengthen the nuclear supply chain.

Background:

The Regional Technology and Innovation Hub (Tech Hubs) Program aims to strengthen America’s economic competitiveness and national security by investing in regions making significant advancements in critical technologies. The Fiscal Year 2025 National Defense Authorization Act included $220 million in funding for Tech Hubs, including the INEC.

title: Rosen to Oppose Trump TSA Administrator Nominee Following Failure to Directly Answer Questions on Cooperation with ICE
text:
Last Week, Senator Rosen Pledged Not To Vote To Confirm David Cummins As TSA Administrator Unless Her Questions On TSA’s Cooperation With ICE Were Answered

WASHINGTON, DC – Ahead of a confirmation vote, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) is announcing she will vote against the nomination of David Cummins to be the next Administrator of the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) for his inability to answer her questions regarding TSA cooperation with ICE. Last week, Senator Rosen submitted a number of questions regarding what he would do as TSA Administrator when it came to cooperating with ICE at airports. Mr. Cummins failed to give any meaningful response or insight; instead, claiming he is “not privy to this information” even when the questions were about how he would address ICE operations at airports if confirmed.

“As ICE continues to run rampant and without accountability or oversight, I’m extremely concerned that they are carrying out misguided operations at airports that are increasing fear in communities and hurting our tourism industry. As the person nominated to run the federal agency in charge of security at our nation’s airports, I asked David Cummins directly about the recent conduct of ICE agents at Harry Reid International Airport and asked him to commit to preventing such abuses in the future,” said Senator Rosen. “Unfortunately, the disappointing responses Mr. Cummins provided were unserious and did not even attempt to answer my questions about how he would act if confirmed to the role. As a result, I will vote against David Cummins’ nomination to be TSA Administrator.”

Rosen’s actions come in the immediate aftermath of an incident at Harry Reid International Airport in Las Vegas where masked, plain-clothed ICE officers — without any identification and seemingly with the support of TSA — attempted to violently arrest an elderly man before running off following public intervention. It was later reported that the man had no outstanding warrants.

Senator Rosen is a member of the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, which has jurisdiction over TSA. She has been adamant about the need for commonsense guardrails for ICE agents. Senator Rosen criticized Trump’s decision to reverse the suspension of ICE traffic stops following two separate ICE killings during enforcement operations. In June, Senator Rosen voted against the ultra-partisan Republican budget, which gave ICE more funding without any guardrails or accountability mechanisms.
