title: Reps. García, Bonamici, Omar and Correa Introduce the Right to Learn Act
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — Today, Representative Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), alongside Representatives Ilhan Omar (MN-05), Lou Correa (CA-46), and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) introduced the Right to Learn Act, legislation designed to provide resources and support for students, families, and school communities impacted by immigration enforcement actions.

The Right to Learn Act will establish a federal grant program to help schools maintain safe, stable, and trauma-informed learning environments when immigration enforcement actions disrupt school communities.

By establishing a federal grant program, this legislation will:

Support students’ well-being and learning stability

Equip educational and school staffs

Strengthen school-community partnerships

Protect students’ privacy and access to education

“When immigration enforcement actions disrupt a school community, students, educators, and families all feel the impact. No child should have to learn in fear, and no school should face these challenges without support. The Right to Learn Act will provide schools with the resources they need and send a clear message: every child belongs in the classroom, not living in fear,” said Congressman García.

“Minnesota kids continue to live with the fear and trauma that Operation Metro Surge unleashed,” said Congresswoman Omar. “Our schools should always be a safe space for our kids, regardless of their immigration status. I'm proud to join my colleagues in leading this legislation to ensure our public schools can access the resources they need to provide students with a safe, stable learning environment.”

“President Trump promised to go after the worst of the worst, instead during his tenure we’ve seen immigration enforcement at elementary schools, places of learning and refuge for our children,” said Congressman Correa. “This critical legislation will make sure our students have a safe learning environment where they can thrive and become our leaders of tomorrow.”

“For decades, public schools have been a safe space for students to learn and grow regardless of their immigration status. With those protections and immigrants now under threat, we must take action to keep children safe so they can continue to learn. I'm grateful to lead this legislation with several of my colleagues to keep schools safe, welcoming, and responsive,” said Congresswoman Bonamici.

“The Right to Learn Act is about acknowledging the pain that the Trump administration’s cruel and illegal immigration operations have inflicted on America’s students—and doing something about it. This bill makes additional resources available to schools to meet the needs of kids and families who have been caught up in the federal dragnet. We have a moral obligation to commit resources to help repair the damage done by the administration’s crass and careless actions. The AFT strongly supports this legislation and will continue to mobilize and demand that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement stop terrorizing our schools and neighborhoods,” said Randi Weingarten, President of The American Federation of Teachers.

“We know teachers in classrooms across our country are doing everything they can, teaching kids who are afraid that their parents are not going to be home when they come from school. There is no learning when a kid has to live like that,” said Keri Rodriguez, founding President of the National Parents Union. “We are seeing an increase in chronic absenteeism because schools don’t feel like a safe place. We need to do everything we can to support the people who are trying to get our children through this traumatic moment.”

Cosponsors of this legislation include Representatives: Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-00), Robert Garcia (CA-42), Frederica S. Wilson (FL-24), Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Jasmine Crockett (TX-30), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), Angie Craig (MN-02), Summer Lee (PA-12), Dwight Evans (PA-03), Adelita S. Grijalva (AZ-07), and Adriano Espaillat (NY-13).

Endorsing organizations include: Mano a Mano Family Resource Center, Instituto del Progreso Latino, Telpochcalli Community Education Project, Enlace Chicago, the Forum for Youth Investment, Southwest Organizing Project, Brighton Park Neighborhood Council, Southwest Organizing Project, Center for Law and Social Policy, Gads Hill Center, Latino Policy Forum, Leyden Community High School District 212, Casa Michoacan I Fedecmi, Institutional Solutions, Los Angeles Unified School District, The National Parents Union, National Education Association, Coalition on Human Needs, Young Center for Immigrant Children's Rights, Latino Community Center, and Alternatives.

title: Rep. Cisneros Champions Legislation to Stop Private Equity From Blocking Access To Childcare
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Gil Cisneros (CA-31) joined Congressman Josh Riley (NY-19) to introduce the Protecting Childcare from Private Equity Act alongside Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35), Congresswoman April McClain Delaney (MD-06), Congressman Suhas Subramanyam (VA-10), and Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07). This legislation implements significant guardrails to protect access to local affordable childcare options and stop private equity from implementing harmful changes that restrict providers.

Private equity currently controls 8 of the 10 largest for-profit childcare chains in America. Corporate accountability of these chains falls concerningly short. Supervision is critical to ensure American families can continue to access affordable childcare options without being priced out. This bill strengthens oversight to ensure private firms responsibly run childcare providers and do not indiscriminately raise prices for our hardworking families.

“Taking care of our children is investing in their future. I’m proud to champion childcare that strengthens our communities and lifts the burden of care off parents’ shoulders,” said Congressman Cisneros. “As a father, I will always support essential guardrails that protect access to childcare. I am proud to co-lead the Protecting Childcare from Private Equity Act with Rep. Riley to prevent private firms from harming access to childcare. This legislation is a critical step towards corporate transparency and accountability. No private equity firm should restrict families' access to the quality care they rely on.”

“Wall Street investors don’t care about the bills hitting our kitchen tables or the number of preschool slots open to Upstate New York families - all they care about is profit for their shareholders. We can’t let them swoop into our communities, buy up daycares, and squeeze families for every dollar they can get,” said Congressman Riley. “This is about creating guardrails to stop predatory investors from pricing out families, and making sure every parent has access to local, high-quality childcare they can actually afford.”

Full text of the bill can be found here.

Rep. Cisneros is a Navy Veteran and the former Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness. title: Congressman Cleaver Introduces CHARTS Act to Modernize and Improve Long-Term Care for Seniors
text:
(Washington, D.C.) – Today, U.S. Representative Emanuel Cleaver, II (D-MO), introduced the Connecting Health and Records Technology for Seniors (CHARTS) Act, legislation to help long-term and post-acute care providers modernize patient record systems, improve care coordination, and ensure America’s seniors receive safer, more connected healthcare.

When Congress passed the HITECH Act of 2009, hospitals and physician practices received federal incentives to adopt electronic health records (EHRs). Long-term care providers, including skilled nursing facilities, nursing homes, rehabilitation centers, and home health agencies, were largely left out. As a result, many facilities caring for older Americans continue to rely on outdated systems that make it more difficult to share patient information, coordinate care between providers, and participate in today’s increasingly data-driven healthcare system.

The legislation comes as the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid services continues its transition toward value-based care models, where providers are increasingly expected to coordinate care across multiple settings. Yet many long-term care providers remain unable to fully participate because implementing electronic health record systems can cost between $100,000 and $250,000 – a significant financial hurdle for many facilities.

“Healthcare doesn’t stop when a patient leaves the hospital, and neither should access to their medical records,” said Congressman Cleaver. “Too many seniors experience fragmented care simply because the providers caring for them don’t have the tools to communicate effectively with one another. Whether someone is transitioning from a hospital to a rehabilitation facility, a nursing home, or receiving care at home, their health information should move with them. The CHARTS Act is a commonsense investment that will improve care, reduce unnecessary costs, and give healthcare professionals more time to focus on what matters most: their patients.”

“ADVION thanks Congressman Emanuel Cleaver for introducing this important legislation, which will help ensure skilled nursing facilities and home health agencies have the resources needed to implement and fully leverage electronic health records. As the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) continues to advance data standards and expectations for real-time information exchange, providers must be equipped to share critical patient data seamlessly with care teams, payers, families, and CMS. Many nursing facilities and home health agencies have faced financial and operational barriers to adopting or optimizing EHR technology. This grant program represents a meaningful step toward closing that gap—supporting providers in delivering more coordinated, data-driven, and high-quality care to the patients and residents they serve,” said Genice Hornberger, RN, President of the Board of Directors of ADVION, an organization advocating for high-quality, cost-effective care for America’s seniors and our most vulnerable citizens.

The CHARTS Act would establish a competitive pilot grant program through the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to help long-term and post-acute care providers purchase and implement electronic health record systems.

Specifically, the CHARTS Act would:

Authorize $5 million annually in FY2027 and FY2028 for competitive grants to eligible providers

Award grants of up to $500,000 to help providers purchase and implement electronic health record systems

Improve communication and real-time information sharing between hospitals, nursing facilities, home health agencies, physicians, and other healthcare providers

Support better care coordination, reduce duplicative services, strengthen medication management, and improve clinical decision-making

Require HHS to report back to Congress on how the program improves patient outcomes and recommend whether the initiative should be expanded

Full text of the bill here.

Emanuel Cleaver, II is the U.S. Representative for Missouri's Fifth Congressional District, which includes Kansas City, Independence, Lee's Summit, Raytown, Grandview, Sugar Creek, Greenwood, Blue Springs, North Kansas City, Gladstone, and Claycomo. He is a member of the exclusive House Financial Services Committee and Ranking Member of the House Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance.

title: CORREA, VAN DREW INTRODUCE BILL TO PROTECT BENEFITS FOR FAMILIES OF PUBLIC SAFETY OFFICERS
text:
Bill Addresses Technicality That Denies Grieving Families of Benefits Their Loved Ones Earned

WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Representatives Lou Correa (D-CA) and Jefferson Van Drew (R-NJ) introduced the bipartisan Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Enhancement Act, which would improve the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits (PSOB) Program by making it easier for families of public safety officers who suffer from fatal heart attacks or strokes in the line of duty to receive benefits from the program.

"Firefighters and officers put their bodies on the line every single shift, and sometimes that toll shows up hours or days later, not the same afternoon. A 24-hour cutoff doesn't match how a heart attack or stroke actually works. This bill just brings the rule in line with reality, so families aren't punished for paperwork technicalities while they're grieving," said Congressman Lou Correa.

The need for the legislation was brought forth by the family of Stephen Wilson, a California Fire Apparatus Engineer. When Mr. Wilson died, his wife, Annette Wilson, filed for death benefits through the PSOB Program with all the required paperwork. The claim was denied anyway. The government stated the record didn't show his death was "a direct and proximate result of a line of duty injury" under the PSOB Act's rules because he did not see a doctor within 24 hours of leaving work.

"My husband spent his career running toward danger to keep our community safe. He died because of that work, and yet his own claim was denied because of a technicality," said Annette Wilson, wife of Stephen Wilson. "No family should have to fight this hard for benefits their loved one earned. This bill means people do not have to go through what I did."

“When our first responders answer the call, they are willing to put everything on the line for complete strangers,” said Congressman Van Drew. “If the stress of that job costs them their life, their loved ones should not have to battle the government for the support they deserve. This is a common-sense fix, and I am proud to work with Congressman Correa to get it done.”

"The Public Safety Officers' Benefits Enhancement Act represents a critical step toward ensuring that the families of fallen firefighters and other first responders receive the support they deserve. Too often, survivors face unnecessary barriers when seeking benefits after a line-of-duty heart attack or stroke. By extending the eligibility window and creating a fairer presumption that recognizes the realities of emergency service, this legislation strengthens the Public Safety Officers' Benefits Program and honors the sacrifices made by our nation's first responders. The National Fallen Firefighters Foundation is proud to support this important legislation," said Victor Stagnaro, Chief Executive Officer of the National Fallen Firefighters Foundation.

"Our nation's public safety officers deserve the assurance that if they make the ultimate sacrifice, their families will be treated fairly and receive the benefits they deserve," said Mathew Silverman, Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association (FLEOA) National President. "The Public Safety Officers' Benefits Enhancement Act is a commonsense, bipartisan measure that better reflects the realities of line-of-duty service and removes unnecessary barriers for surviving families to receive much needed benefits and FLEOA strongly supports its passage."

“Unless there is evidence to the contrary, it should be presumed that a police officer’s line-of-duty fatal heart attack or stroke was job related. Requiring police families to offer definitive proof, especially when it’s known that cardiovascular disease and strokes are leading causes of illness and mortality, places undue hardship on grieving survivors. It also dishonors the memories of our heroes who sacrifice greatly to protect and serve. The National Police Association is grateful to Reps. J. Luis Correa and Jefferson Van Drew for introducing the Public Safety Officers’ Benefits Enhancement Act, a bill that will help ensure law enforcement families are spared from having to navigate these unnecessary bureaucratic hurdles,” said Paula Fitzsimmons, Legislative Director, National Police Association

"When a peace officer makes the ultimate sacrifice, their family shouldn't have to fight a second battle just to receive the support they were promised. This legislation honors that sacrifice by removing unnecessary obstacles from the claims process, ensuring survivors can access the benefits they deserve when they need them most.” said Brian R. Marvel, President, Peace Officers Research Association of California.

This bill is cosponsored by U.S. Representatives Mike Thompson (D-CA), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), Don Bacon (R-NE), Mark Alford (R-MO), Thomas Kean (R-NJ), Adam Gray (D-CA), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Jared Golden (D-ME), and Marie Gluesenkamp Perez (D-WA).

This bill is endorsed by the Blue Dog Coalition, National Association of Police Organizations, Federal Law Enforcement Officers Association, National Police Association, National Fallen Firefighters Foundation, International Association of Fire Fighters, Major County Sheriffs of America, Peace Officers Research Association of California, and National Narcotic Officers' Associations' Coalition.

View bill text here.

Background

The PSOB Program provides death and education benefits to survivors of fallen law enforcement officers, firefighters, and other first responders, and disability benefits to officers catastrophically injured in the line of duty.

The program provides benefits to survivors when first responders suffer from fatal heart attacks or strokes in the line of duty, but current law requires that the heart attack or stroke begin within 24 hours of nonroutine physical activity and requires the survivors to prove that the line of duty action directly resulted in the heart attack or stroke—which leads to claims being excluded where additional risk factors may have been at play.

This bill modifies the PSOB program by:

Extending the time period for heart attacks and strokes to be covered from 24 to 72 hours.

Changing the presumption so that qualifying events are covered unless medical evidence says it was unrelated to service—instead of placing the burden of proof on the survivors to show it was directly caused by the activity.

title: Republican Leaders Mangle Bipartisan Defense Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congress Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, issued the following statement after the House passed the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act. To watch Courtney’s floor speech urging against partisan poison amendments, click here. title: Rep. Angie Craig Introduces Comprehensive Regulatory Framework for Hemp
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Representative and Ranking Member of the House Agriculture Committee Angie Craig (D-MN-02) introduced legislation alongside Rep. Andy Barr (R-KY-06) to create a comprehensive regulatory framework for hemp and hemp-derived THC products, ensuring hemp remains safe and available for Minnesota’s farmers, processors, brewers, retailers and consumers.

Rep. Craig’s Lawful Hemp Protection Act comes after House Republicans effectively repealed a 2018 law that allowed Minnesota and other states to legally produce hemp and sell hemp-derived products, such as hemp beverages and textiles. Since 2018, the hemp industry has grown into a roughly $300 million a year industry and provided a new income stream for local farmers, brewers and small businesses. As of 2023, the Minnesota hemp industry supported over 3,400 jobs. The state is home to 132 licensed grow operations, 96 processors and over 2,000 retailers. If Congress does not act by November 12, 2026, Minnesota’s legal hemp industry will effectively be shut down.

“Minnesota became the model for responsible hemp regulation when it established a regulatory framework that complied with federal law and enabled local farmers and businesses to thrive,” said Rep. Craig. “My commonsense legislation will give regulatory clarity to Minnesota farmers, brewers and small business owners and provide an alternative to short-sighted federal policies that threaten Minnesota jobs and consumer choice. I am proud to have worked with Rep. Barr on a solution that protects our farmers and small businesses while also keeping our kids and communities safe.”

“Kentucky farmers helped build America’s hemp industry and they deserve certainty,” said Rep. Andy Barr. “The Lawful Hemp Protection Act protects Kentucky agriculture, safeguards consumers, and establishes a commonsense regulatory framework that allows this important industry to continue to grow while ensuring products are safe and kept out of the hands of children. Kentucky has demonstrated that hemp can be successfully regulated while supporting farmers and protecting consumers. This legislation builds on that success by creating a national framework that rewards responsible producers, eliminates bad actors and ensures consumers have confidence in the products they purchase.”

“We are dangerously close to one of Minnesota’s most promising small business industries being shut down,” said Bob Galligan, director of government and industry relations for the Minnesota Craft Brewers Guild. “Minnesotans proved that responsible regulation can lift businesses, strengthen economies and protect consumers. We now need Congress to do its job. We’re grateful for Rep. Craig for her continuous support and for now forging a path that reflects what our state has already shown: prohibition doesn’t work, but thoughtful, practical regulation does.”

“The entire Minnesota hemp industry thanks both Reps. Angie Craig and Andy Barr for their leadership in bringing sensible regulation to this industry that is so important to so many,” said Kyle Markinovich, the founder and CEO of Northern Diversified Solutions in Burnsville, MN. “The farmers, brands, distributors, retailers, patients, and consumers are so grateful this amazing success story will continue to grow and thrive. As Minnesotans, we are particularly grateful to Rep. Craig who continues to serve hemp farmers and businesses so well in the Congress.”

“Reps. Andy Barr and Angie Craig deserve tremendous credit for stepping forward with a serious, science-based and bipartisan solution at exactly the moment the hemp industry needs it most,” said Jonathan Miller, general counsel of the U.S. Hemp Roundtable. “Their leadership on the Lawful Hemp Protection Act reflects a clear-eyed recognition that prohibition is the wrong path, and that American farmers, small businesses, manufacturers, retailers and consumers deserve a workable federal framework built on responsible regulation. We are grateful for their willingness to engage stakeholders across the industry throughout the drafting process, and we look forward to continuing to work with them and their colleagues in Congress to advance a long-term federal solution.”

title: NDAA Passes House; Rep. Crank Secures Critical Investments for El Paso County
text:

This bill is a clear signal that the Department of War is doubling down on its long-term commitment to Colorado Springs, creating jobs, supporting our local economy, and reinforcing our community's role as the heart of America's space enterprise.”

title: Rep. Crank Introduces Resolution to Restore Integrity and Protect Congressional Staff
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, Representative Jeff Crank (CO-05) introduced. H.Res. 1443, a resolution to strengthen the House of Representatives’ ethics rules by prohibiting Members of the U.S. House of Representatives from engaging in sexual relationships with any House employee, unless the relationship is first disclosed to the House Ethics Committee.

The current Code of Official Conduct only prohibits Members from having a relationship with staff directly under their supervision, but does not apply to relationships between Members and other House employees. There is an imbalance of power between members of Congress and staff, and this resolution will establish additional guardrails to protect congressional staff from an abuse of that power.

“I firmly believe that Members of Congress should be held to the highest standard,” said Rep. Crank. “We must recognize that as elected officials, we can have unbalanced influence over House employees, regardless of who they work for. The personal conduct of some of my colleagues has undermined public trust in this institution, and the legislative process, and we must do better.”

Background:

The resolution would ensure that all Member-employee relationships are subject to appropriate ethical review and that the House maintains the highest standards of accountability and public trust.

title: Rep. Crank Votes to Ban Lawmakers from Using their Positions to Benefit off of Insider Trading
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, Representative Jeff Crank (CO-05) voted in favor of H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act.

The Stop Insider Trading Act ensures that lawmakers cannot use their positions to profit off of insider trading. It bans Members, their spouses, and their dependent children from purchasing securities issued by a publicly traded company. It also requires Members to file a public notice at least 7 days in advance for any intended stock sale with the Clerk of the House of Representatives.

"For years, Members of Congress have gotten rich off insider information—that's plain wrong," said Rep. Crank. "To be clear: I don't own any individual, publicly traded stock, and as long as I represent the people of Colorado's Fifth Congressional District, I will never buy any. The Stop Insider Trading Act will work to restore integrity to Congress by banning stock trading by Members of Congress."

Background:

Violators will be assessed a fine equal to $2,000 or 10% of the value of the transaction, whichever is greater, and any net gain from a transaction.

Exceptions include:

Widely held investment fund, diversified and publicly traded;

Employment compensation received by Member, their spouse, or dependent child;

Investments held in a trust as long as the covered individual has no authority over a trustee of the trust;

Financial interest in a small business concern.

title: Dingell, Moolenaar Joint Statement on Senate Commerce Committee Passage of the Connected Vehicle Security Act
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06) and John Moolenaar (R-MI-02), Chairman of the Select Committee on China, released the following statement after the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation passed the Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026.

“The Connected Vehicles Security Act is crucial to protect American jobs, national security, and the future of American manufacturing. Chinese automakers use slave labor, massive government subsidies, and unfair trade practices, and their vehicles are a national security risk with equipment that transmits data to China. These companies have already decimated European competitors in their home markets, causing layoffs and production cuts, and we will not let them do the same thing in the United States. Thank you to our colleagues on the Senate Commerce Committee for rejecting weak amendments and passing a strong bill that keeps China out of our market. This will protect American workers, manufacturers, supply chains, and our national security,” said Representatives Dingell and Moolenaar.

The bipartisan legislation would prohibit the importation, manufacture, and sale of connected vehicles, software, and hardware linked to China. Chairman John Moolenaar (R-MI) of the Select Committee on China and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (D-MI) led the bill’s introduction in the House, and the Senate version is led by Senator Bernie Moreno (R-OH).

The bill would:

Prohibit the importation, manufacture, sale, or introduction into U.S. commerce of connected vehicles originating from or controlled by a covered foreign adversary country.

Prohibit connected vehicle software and hardware linked to covered foreign adversaries.

Cover China, Russia, North Korea, and Iran.

Allow for phased-in adoption of prohibitions so auto companies can adjust their manufacturing and supply chains with minimal disruption.

title: Congressman Don Davis Votes for House Passage of Eastern North Carolina Defense Priorities in FY 2027 NDAA
text:
July 22, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Don Davis (NC-01), Vice Ranking Member of the House Armed Services Committee, sponsored 31 provisions that have advanced through House passage of H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2027. He joined his colleagues in voting for the fourth consecutive year to pass the annual defense bill in the House, with a bipartisan margin of 216–212. The package includes a range of priorities championed by Congressman Davis to strengthen military readiness, support servicemembers and military families, and reinforce the strategic importance of eastern North Carolina's defense infrastructure.

The provisions would bolster key military installations that anchor eastern North Carolina’s defense economy, including Seymour Johnson Air Force Base and Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point, while supporting the communities that play a vital role in the nation's defense. The legislation advances investments in military construction, workforce development, quality-of-life improvements, and national security capabilities to help ensure eastern North Carolina remains at the forefront of military readiness.

“By investing in our military installations, strengthening American manufacturing, and modernizing our military, this legislation helps ensure our servicemembers remain ready to meet evolving global security challenges. These investments will create opportunities for eastern North Carolina, support military families, and strengthen our nation's ability to confront emerging threats and protect the American people,” said Congressman Don Davis.

The House’s passage of H.R. 8800 means that 31 provisions, including those below championed by Congressman Davis, will advance in the legislative process to the Senate:

Improving Aircraft Mission Readiness at Cherry Point: Supports the artificial intelligence (AI) pilot program initiated through the 2nd Marine Aircraft Wing (MAW) based in Havelock, NC, to address perennial challenges in asset availability, starting with the MV-22B Osprey platform.

F-35 Lightning II Sustainment: Establishes multi-year procurement authority for the fighter platform, further stabilizing spare parts availability, enhancing fleet readiness, and reducing life cycle costs. Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point currently hosts F-35 squadrons.

F-35 Aircraft Sustainment Center Authorization at Cherry Point: Authorizes $89 million for additional investments in the Fleet Readiness Center (FRC) East facility.

Standing Up to Drug Cartels: Requires a report on the urgent threat posed by and combat tactics to counter fiber optic-guided and first-person-view unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) employed by Transnational Criminal Organizations (TCOs).

Enhancing Preparedness for Biological Threats to the Warfighter: Requires the Department of Defense to brief Congress on plans to ensure a stable, secure, and sustainable stockpile of anthrax countermeasures in the event of a biological attack on the homeland.

Improving Biodefense Capabilities: Requires a briefing on the best strategies to further develop effective countermeasures to address the threat that biological agents pose to the warfighter, and the public-private partnerships underway to further such research.

Supporting American-made Textiles: Builds on a provision in the Fiscal Year 2026 NDAA by reiterating the value of the Berry Amendment to the domestic textile industrial base in North Carolina and across America, and requiring a briefing on efforts to strengthen compliance with the Berry Amendment and Buy American requirements for textile and apparel items.

Supporting American-made Drone Hardware: Requires the Secretary of Defense to report on opportunities to accelerate development and acquisition of low-cost, platform-agnostic autonomy modules for small unmanned aerial systems (sUAS).

Advancing American-made Battery Technology: Requires the Secretary of the Army to report on resilient tactical power and battery safety systems to highlight the critical role of battery separators in stabilizing the battery supply chain and ensuring its security.

Expansion of Artificial Intelligence-Enabled Logistics and Supply Chain Optimization: Directs the Air Force to deploy AI-enabled maintenance data cleansing and correction tools across Air Education and Training Command to improve the quality and usability of maintenance and logistics data.

AI-Enabled Logistics Supply Chain Funding: Authorizes $22 million for a pilot program to deploy AI-enabled technology to predict future aircraft maintenance challenges.

Keeping Troops Safe: Builds on a provision in the Fiscal Year 2026 NDAA to study counter-drone infiltrations on American military bases and supports the $10 million authorization in FY 2026 for base security technology at three Air Force bases.

Tobacco Harm Reduction: Allows the Department of Defense to establish a pilot program for servicemembers who smoke by providing them with smokeless tobacco alternatives, including nicotine patches and gum.

Traumatic Brain Injury (TBI) Research Funding Increase: Provides an additional $5 million for the Physics-based Neutralizations of Threats to Human Tissues and Organs Research (PANTHER) program through the Office of Naval Research to address TBIs suffered by servicemembers.

Health Data for Troops: Establishes a pilot program to provide servicemembers, prior to separation, with a secure, approved mobile Personal Health Record, giving veterans immediate and permanent access to their information and the ability to securely share records with the Department of Veterans Affairs, private providers, or legal representatives.

Promoting American Battery Production: Supports securing the domestic critical mineral and battery supply chain to prevent influence from the People's Republic of China.

Assessing Name, Image, and Likeness for Service Academy Athletes: Establishes a Military Service Academy Panel to review the impacts of NCAA rules on compensation of athletes, as well as the transfer portal for athletes on the military service academies.

Promoting Military Public Health: Directs the Department of Defense to report on influenza policy changes announced in April 2026, including how the changes compare to the Department’s longstanding prior policies and their impact on force readiness.

Addressing Affordability in the Force: Directs a report on the leading cost-of-living and financial literacy challenges servicemembers and their families are facing to enhance their quality of life.

Slowing Military Equipment Aging: Provides $5.5 million through the Army National Guard’s Controlled Humidity Preservation (CHP) program to utilize specialized technology to prevent moisture-induced corrosion on vehicles, electronics, and weapons.

Suicide Prevention: Requires reporting on emerging virtual reality technology that provides real-time mental health training for servicemembers so they are prepared to assist fellow troops suffering from acute or chronic suicidal ideation.

Simplifying Military Personnel Data: Requires a report on the imperative to shift from siloed legacy data management systems to a single, human capital management platform, therefore enhancing operational success in contested environments.

Saluting Our Canines: Requires a report on best practices to enhance military working dog wellness and long-term sustainability.

Congressman Don Davis is a 1994 U.S. Air Force Academy graduate, a member of its Board of Visitors, and a U.S. Air Force veteran. He serves as the Vice Ranking Member of the U.S. House Armed Services Committee, where he serves on the Readiness and Tactical Air and Land Forces subcommittees.

title: Reps. Dunn, Carter, and Craig Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Access to Mental Health Care for Children
text:
Today, Congressman Neal Dunn (FL-02), Congressman Troy Carter (LA-02), and Congresswoman Angie Craig (MN-02) introduced the Improving Coordination and Access to Resources Equitably for Youth Act (Improving CARE for Youth Act). This bipartisan legislation increases access to mental health services for children enrolled in Medicaid.

Under current Medicaid policy, health care providers generally may only bill for one service per patient per day. As a result, when a child visits a primary care physician and is identified as needing behavioral or mental health services, practices with an integrated mental health provider often cannot bill for both the primary care visit and the same-day mental health service. This outdated billing restriction discourages same-day treatment, forcing many children to schedule a separate appointment and delaying access to critical care.

"Our nation is facing a growing youth mental health crisis, and we should be removing barriers to care, not creating them," said Rep. Dunn. "As a physician, I know that early intervention can make a profound difference in a child's long-term health and well-being. Protecting the future of the youth in our country is too important to be hindered by a Medicaid billing restriction. The Improving CARE for Youth Act ensures children can receive the care they need when they need it.”

“This is a common-sense, no-cost fix that removes a bureaucratic barrier standing between patients and the integrated care model that providers already want to deliver. When a doctor identifies a need for behavioral health support, that patient shouldn't have to wait — they should be able to see a provider down the hall, right then and there,” said Rep. Carter. “The Improving CARE for Youth Act allows Medicaid to reimburse for behavioral health and primary care services delivered on the same day, at the same visit. This is lifesaving care for patients when they need it most.”

“We are facing a mental health crisis in our country, and we've got to make sure young people have access to the mental health care they need when they need it,” said Rep. Craig. “I’m proud to reintroduce this bipartisan bill alongside my colleagues that will remove barriers to mental health care for children on Medicaid and ensure a better future for our kids and grandkids."

title: Elfreth Votes No on Annual Defense Authorization Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03), a member of the House Armed Services Committee, voted against the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) on the House floor. “As a member of the House Armed Services Committee, I have a great appreciation for the tireless bipartisan effort that goes into crafting the National Defense Authorization Act and the impact it has on our men and women in uniform. I have spent much of my first term in Congress finding avenues in this bill to strengthen installation readiness, lower costs for servicemembers, support our military families, advance health care and medical research, invest in the shipbuilding industry, modernize our cybersecurity, and so much more,” said Congresswoman Elfreth. “Despite the advancements we secured in this legislation, we cannot ignore the larger context of this bill and this moment. I could not vote to authorize $1.15 trillion for the Department of Defense as this Administration wages an unjustified, unconstitutional war with Iran with no end in sight. I could not vote in support of the hateful culture wars that House Republicans inserted into this traditionally bipartisan legislation. I could not vote on a bill that places virtually no checks on an Administration and Department of Defense that continues to put our servicemembers in harm's way and spends untold and unchecked billions of taxpayer dollars. That is why I once again voted no on this year's defense authorization bill.”

Elfreth worked with colleagues on both sides of the aisle to strengthen the legislation in support of our servicemembers. In all, 23 of Elfreth’s provisions were included in the base text of the NDAA, and Elfreth successfully introduced 20 provisions as amendments, including two floor amendments to study reserve child care programs and to develop a domestic critical mineral workforce. title: Congresswoman Escobar Introduces Legislation to Strengthen Military Child Care and Expand Employment Opportunities for Military Spouses
text:
Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) introduced the Military Spouse Employment and Child Care Readiness Act, legislation that would direct the Department of Defense to identify ways to strengthen the military child care workforce while creating meaningful employment opportunities for military spouses.

“Supporting our servicemembers means supporting their families,” said Congresswoman Escobar. “Military spouses often sacrifice their own careers, stability, and opportunities every time they answer the call and have to start over in a new community. The Military Spouse Employment and Child Care Readiness Act provides a crucial first step toward removing unnecessary barriers to employment for military spouses, strengthening military child care, and ensuring military families have the support they need to thrive."

Military families frequently relocate wherever the mission requires, often requiring spouses to rebuild their careers and navigate new licensing, certifications, or other requirements. At the same time, staffing shortages at military child development centers can limit the number of children who receive care. Together, these challenges prevent military spouses from entering the workforce, strain family finances, and make it more difficult for active-duty servicemembers to balance the demands of their service with the basic needs of their families.

By examining barriers and opportunities, the Military Spouse Employment and Child Care Readiness Act would pave the way for Department of Defense-supported career pathways that can follow military spouses between installations and expand the network of qualified child care providers serving military communities. It endorsed by the Military Family Advisory Network.

Specifically, the legislation would direct the Department of Defense to:

Determine the percentage of military child development center employees who are military spouses or spouses of retired or separated servicemembers

Assess the feasibility of making child care licenses and certifications more portable for military spouses

Examine vacancy rates at military child development centers and identify the primary causes of staffing shortages

Determine how many additional children could receive care if military child development centers were fully staffed

Assess whether military spouses living in on-post housing could provide home-based child care

Recommend incentives to attract and retain military spouses in the military child care workforce.

title: TRANSCRIPT: Congresswoman Escobar Opposes Additional Funding for War in Iran, Speaks on House Floor

title: Congresswoman Escobar Statement on National Defense Authorization Act
text:
Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) released the following statement:

"The National Defense Authorization Act is one of the most important bills Congress considers each year, and, as a former member of the House Armed Services Committee (HASC), I have tremendous respect for the bipartisan work HASC has done for decades to support our national security and our servicemembers. The United States faces real threats, and we need to make sure our military has the resources, training, and support it's needs. But supporting our national defense also means being responsible with taxpayer dollars and having a clear strategy for how we keep our country safe.

"Congress should not be authorizing massive levels of defense spending while the President launches our country into another conflict without a clear strategy, a defined objective, or a meaningful debate with Congress about the use of military force. We cannot give a blank check to an administration that is recklessly expanding our involvement in another war while Republicans continue to cut critical domestic programs and pass tax breaks for the wealthy here at home.

"Additionally, Republicans ensured several provisions were included in the bill that are red lines for me. Policies that attack LGBTQ+ servicemembers and their families, make firearms more accessible on base, exacerbate voter suppression, expand U.S. military support for Israel by deepening defense technology cooperation and integrating defense supply chains, and more.

"I am proud of the provisions I was able to secure in this bill, including three of my bills: the Streamlining Military Infrastructure Act, JROTC POWER Act, and Military Spouse Employment and Child Care Readiness Act. But those important provisions do not outweigh my concerns about the bill’s overall spending levels, the Administration’s war of choice with Iran, and the process surrounding its passage. title: Rep. Estes Votes to Pass National Defense Authorization Act, Securing Key Authorization for 184th Wing at McConnell AFB
text:
U.S. Representative Ron Estes (KS-04) released the following statement after voting in favor of the House passage of H.R. 8800, the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA):

“Providing for a strong national defense and ensuring our service members have the tools they need to protect our homeland is one of Congress’s most critical constitutional duties.

This year’s NDAA delivers on rebuilding the arsenal of freedom, including provisions to bolster readiness, strengthen quality of life and military families, restore lethality, reinvigorate our defense industrial base, and reinforce American military deterrence. The bill directly supports the crucial role that Kansas airmen and soldiers play in protecting our nation.

It is especially significant that this legislation includes a $10 million authorization for the Point Defense Battle Lab (PDBL) mission. The 184th Wing at McConnell Air Force Base is the only National Guard Wing supporting this mission, and the 184th Wing is uniquely positioned to leverage Kansas’s world-class aviation expertise, workforce, and research institutions like Wichita State University’s National Institute for Aviation Research (NIAR).

Advancing our Counter-small Unmanned Aircraft Systems (C-sUAS) capabilities and hardening our military installations is an urgent operational necessity in today’s evolving threat landscape. While the NDAA is an authorization bill rather than a funding bill, securing this authorization is an important step toward equipping the 184th Wing with the infrastructure and equipment needed to execute this critical national security mission,” Rep. Ron Estes said.

Point Defense Battle Lab Background:

Along with the 319th Reconnaissance Wing out of Grand Forks Air Force Base, the Point Defense Battle Lab (PDBL) initiative focuses on validating tactics, techniques, and procedures for countering a wide range of airborne threats. Ultimately, the PDBL aims to safeguard installations and protect critical Department of War assets. The 184th Wing at McConnell Air Force Base in Wichita was designated by Air Combat Command (ACC) to support the Air Force’s PBDL mission, the only National Guard Wing supporting this mission.

Representative Estes previously advocated for the selection of the 184th Wing to be designated as a partner unit for the PDBL mission, as it presents a unique opportunity for the DoW to leverage south central Kansas’s expertise, industry, and capabilities.

title: PASSED BY THE HOUSE: Ezell Votes to Strengthen America's Military
text:

title: Rep. Fallon's Ensuring Federal Purchasing Efficiency Act Passes the House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, the House passed the Ensuring Federal Purchasing Efficiency Act introduced by Rep. Pat Fallon (TX-04). This bill requires the Federal Acquisition Regulatory Council to adjust certain acquisition-related dollar thresholds for inflation every three years instead of every five years.

“Our House majority promised the American people that we would work to make the federal government more streamlined and efficient,” commented Rep. title: Feenstra Applauds House Passage of Bill to Ban Members of Congress from Purchasing Individual Stocks
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra (R-Hull) applauded the House passage of the Stop Insider Trading Act, legislation he helped introduce earlier this year.

The bill prohibits Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing individual stocks in publicly traded companies while serving in office. It also requires Members to provide at least seven days' public notice before selling any individual stocks, helping to prevent Members of Congress from profiting from insider information.

“I have always believed that serving as a Member of Congress should be about service to the people, and should never be a profession where personal wealth can be made at the expense of our constituents,” said Rep. Feenstra. “Our constituents put faith in us to act as public servants, and this measure is an important step forward to restore that trust. I am proud to have helped lead this legislation and pleased to see it move to the Senate for consideration.”

title: VIDEO: N.M. Delegation Joins Pueblo Governors to Push for Permanent Protections for Chaco Canyon
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Representatives Teresa Leger Fernández (D-N.M.), Melanie Stansbury (D-N.M.), and Gabe Vasquez (D-N.M.) and U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) and Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) joined the All Pueblo Council of Governors (APCG) at a press conference to call for permanent protection of Chaco Canyon.

Located in northwestern New Mexico, the Greater Chaco landscape is a region of great cultural, spiritual, and historical significance to many Pueblos and Tribes and contains living sacred sites. Chaco was listed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1987 and is one of only 24 such sites in the United States.

Last week, the Trump administration announced a proposal to fully revoke a 20-year mineral withdrawal that has protected public lands surrounding the Chaco Culture National Historic Park, and only allowed 14 days for public comment. The N.M. Delegation released a statement strongly condemning the Trump administration’s actions.

This week, Heinrich, Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, led a N.M. Delegation letter urging U.S. Department of the Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to extend the public comment period to 90-days and conduct genuine Tribal consultation and extensive public engagement before revoking protections for the Chaco region. Most importantly, the Delegation urged Secretary Burgum to withdraw this proposal and leave Public Land Order No. 7923 in place. The Delegation also, once again, invited Secretary Burgum to visit Chaco before taking any action that would put this irreplaceable cultural landmark at risk.

VIDEO: The N.M. Delegation joins the All Pueblo Council of Governors to call for permanent protection of the Chaco Canyon Cultural Protection Zone, July 22, 2026.

“There is not a single molecule of gas worth sacrificing a landscape that holds more than 4,700 archaeological sites, the prayers and history of generations, and the living culture of Chaco Canyon,” said Leger Fernández, Ranking Member of the House Indian and Insular Affairs Subcommittee. “Secretary Burgum lied when he promised meaningful, in-person tribal consultation before any decision was made. Our Chaco Cultural Heritage Area Protection Act will permanently protect Chaco. In the meantime, we will use every tool at our disposal to stop the bulldozers from tearing up living history.”

“Chaco Canyon is not for sale! As one the most sacred places on the planet — the Greater Chaco Landscape has been a sacred landscape for Pueblo and Diné people since time immemorial,” said Stansbury. “The Trump Administration's plan to open these sacred places to oil and gas drilling is a direct attack to Tribal Sovereignty and New Mexico's history, cultures, and living traditions. I am proud to stand today and every day with the entire New Mexico delegation, the All Pueblo Council of Governors, Tribal leaders, advocates, and communities across our state to protect this irreplaceable landscape for generations to come. We ask the American people to stand with us — and please submit a public comment and help save Chaco Canyon.”

“Chaco is central to New Mexico’s identity — a living cultural landscape, a sacred place and an irreplaceable unit of our national public lands. The Administration’s attempt to revoke the protections of this landscape, built through years of consultation and community engagement, with just 14 days of public comment is disingenuous and disrespectful,” said Vasquez. “Secretary Burgum must withdraw this proposal and come to New Mexico to hear directly from Pueblo leaders. He has an open invitation to come to Chaco and meet with Pueblo leaders. We can support responsible energy development without sacrificing places like Chaco that, once damaged, will be lost forever.”

“Chaco Canyon is not for sale. New Mexico has an important role to play producing energy for the nation. We're the second largest producer of oil in the country, we produce far more electrons than we consume, and we have never had to sacrifice our most sacred places to do that — and we should not do that going forward,” said Heinrich. “Chaco Canyon is not just a place on a map. It is not a museum. It is not about what happened 1,000 years ago. It is about the future. It is about these governors and their communities, their identity, and their relationship to this sacred place that they use now. This is about our state's ability to stand up for what is right and moral. Our New Mexico Delegation stands arm in arm and shoulder to shoulder with these Tribal governors and their communities in standing up to protect this place. And we will fight that fight until we win.”

“Chaco Canyon is more than a place on a map — it is thousands of years of culture, history, and the enduring spirit of the Pueblo peoples. Protecting Chaco is our sacred responsibility. Once Chaco is damaged, it cannot be undone. That’s why we are standing together to make our voices heard,” said Luján. “I am deeply grateful for the Pueblo leaders whose leadership and tireless advocacy are at the heart of the fight to protect Chaco Canyon. Now is your turn to make your voice heard. Submit your comment today to tell the Trump administration to keep its hands off Chaco.”

The New Mexico Congressional Delegation has worked tirelessly to permanently protect Chaco Canyon.

Last week, the N.M. Delegation released a statement in response to the news that the Trump administration is proposing to fully revoke a 20-year mineral withdrawal that has protected public lands surrounding the Chaco Culture National Historic Park, and only allowing 14 days for public comment.

In April, the N.M. Delegation submitted a comment letter to the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) urging the Trump administration to reverse course on its decision to initiate the process to undo a 20-year mineral withdrawal that has kept public lands in the Chaco Canyon Cultural Protection Zone off-limits to new oil and gas leasing. Earlier that month, the N.M. Delegation sent statements in opposition to the Trump administration only granting seven days to submit scoping comments.

Last November, Heinrich, Luján, and Stansbury hosted a press conference with Pueblo leaders on the actions needed to permanently protect the landscape.

Last September, the N.M. Delegation hosted a press conference in front of the U.S. Capitol with 20 Governors and leaders from the Santa Ana, Picuris, Cochiti, Zia, Tesuque, Acoma, Santo Domingo, and Laguna Pueblos to demand the Trump administration permanently protect Chaco Canyon, and to invite U.S. Department of the Interior Secretary Doug Burgum to visit the Greater Chaco landscape before deciding its fate. Watch the video of the full press conference here.

In June 2025, the N.M. Delegation sent a letter initially inviting Secretary Burgum to visit Chaco Canyon and engage directly with Tribal leaders and local communities to hear about the profound cultural and spiritual significance of this sacred landscape. Secretary Burgum issued the directive to begin revoking the Chaco protections without experiencing it firsthand. Following Secretary Burgum’s directive, the N.M. Delegation sent a letter urging the Trump administration to reverse course on its decision to initiate the process to fully revoke Chaco Canyon’s protections.

title: Figures Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Establish Tuskegee Airmen Memorial in Washington, DC
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Shomari C. Figures (AL-02) introduced the Tuskegee Airmen Memorial Act, a bill to create a memorial in Washington, DC, to commemorate the service, sacrifice, and enduring legacy of the Tuskegee Airmen.

“The Tuskegee Airmen are among the most heroic and consequential soldiers that our nation has ever had,” said Congressman Figures. “While facing horrific discrimination at home, these men risked their lives to defend rights and freedoms abroad. Their courage, skill, and unwavering dedication not only contributed to the Allied victory but also helped pave the way for the desegregation of the U.S. military. Their contributions to our country deserve to be memorialized in our nation’s capital, and I'm proud to introduce this bipartisan bill to make that a reality.”

"The introduction of this authorizing legislation in Congress is a vital milestone in our ongoing mission to preserve and honor the legacy of our nation’s pioneering heroes,” said Ms. Angela Holmes, 1st Vice President for Tuskegee Airmen, Inc. "We extend our deepest gratitude to Representative Shomari Figures and our congressional partners for championing this effort. As we see the final generation of our original members passing, establishing a permanent landmark in Washington, D.C., ensures that their monumental contributions to military integration, excellence, and civil rights will never be forgotten by future generations.”

Congressman Figures’ bill would authorize Tuskegee Airmen, Incorporated to establish a memorial on federal land in the District of Columbia. This is a key, necessary first step towards making this well-deserved memorial a reality. Tuskegee Airmen, Incorporated is a national nonprofit founded to preserve the history and achievements of the original Tuskegee Airmen and engage with youth to inspire future careers in aviation, aerospace and STEM.

The memorial will serve as an educational resource, designed to teach future generations about one of the greatest, most well-decorated fighting forces in our nation’s history, and to highlight the important roles that Black military pilots and support personnel played in World War II.

This bill is cosponsored by the entire Alabama House Congressional Delegation, Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), Sanford Bishop (GA-02), and Emilia Sykes (OH-13).

title: Finstad Votes to Keep Government Funded, Protect Full-Year Appropriations Process with Clean Continuing Resolution
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) released a statement following today’s passage of H.R. 9770, Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027, legislation that extends government funding at current levels with a continuing resolution (CR) through December 4, 2026:

“The House Committee on Appropriations has successfully advanced all twelve funding bills out of committee, working hard to responsibly fund the government and restore long overdue regular order to our appropriations process. I was proud to vote yes on this clean CR, which prevents another government shutdown like the record-long funding halt that we experienced last year due to the Democrats’ political games. By continuing federal funding through December 4th, this legislation prevents another costly shutdown, ensures constituents can continue to rely on essential government services, and gives Congress time to finalize full-year appropriations bills.”

title: Congressmen Flood (R-NE) and Sorensen (D-IL) Launch Caucus Focused on Weather Industry
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congressman Mike Flood (R-NE) and Congressman Eric Sorensen (D-IL), launched the Weather Enterprise Caucus for the 119th Congress. This bipartisan caucus aims to educate Members of Congress about all things weather forecasting and research — focusing on the economic, societal, and national security value of the United States Weather Enterprise.

“Our nation’s ability to sustain and improve the accuracy of weather forecasts has a direct impact on communities and businesses across the country,” said Congressman Flood. “From hailstorms and wildfires in Nebraska to hurricanes and flooding in Florida, every community benefits from a stronger, more resilient Weather Enterprise. I am glad to help launch the first Weather Enterprise Caucus in congressional history and look forward to the opportunities this will create to strengthen the Weather Enterprise through greater investment and innovation. I thank Congressman Sorensen for joining me as co-chair of this important effort.”

“When severe weather strikes, every second matters,” said Congressman Eric Sorensen. “Accurate forecasts and timely warnings save lives, protect our communities, and help our nation prepare for the challenges ahead. The Weather Enterprise Caucus was created to make sure Congress continues to recognize the importance of weather science, innovation, and the work being done every day to keep Americans safe."

Photos of the caucus launch can be found by clicking here.

Guest speakers at the caucus launch included:

Congressman Mike Flood (R-NE)

Congressman Eric Sorensen (D-IL)

Taylor Jordan, NOAA Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Environmental Observation and Prediction

Ken Graham, Director, NOAA’s National Weather Service

Doug Hilderbrand, Executive Director, American Weather Enterprise Association

Amanda Staudt, Executive Director, American Meteorological Society

The Weather Enterprise Caucus is a bipartisan group of Members of Congress dedicated to advancing the 'Weather Enterprise’ — the industries surrounding weather forecasting, research, weatherization efforts, and related sectors. The caucus's founding co-chairs both have backgrounds in the broadcast industry.

By educating their congressional colleagues and advocating for policies that strengthen the broader Weather Enterprise, the caucus seeks to encourage investment, innovation, and continued support for this crucial sector.

title: Fong Secures Three Amendments in House-passed National Defense Legislation
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, the House of Representatives passed the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), legislation that strengthens America's national defense, invests in our military installations, and delivers for the men and women who serve this nation. Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) voted in support of the bill and successfully secured three amendments directly benefiting the defense community of California’s 20th Congressional District.

"From a historic pay raise for our service members to investing in advanced defense technology while cutting nearly $30 billion in wasteful programs, this bill ensures America remains the strongest, most capable military force in the world,” said Congressman Fong. “I secured three critical amendments that honors those we lost at Edwards Air Force Base (AFB), ensures those at Edwards AFB have the healthcare resources they need, and expands our nation's aerospace testing capabilities by exploring a potential supersonic corridor connecting the airspace supporting NAWS China Lake, Edwards AFB, and Fort Irwin to Point Mugu’s Sea Range. Importantly, this bill also advances critical facility projects at NAS Lemoore and the Air Force Research Laboratory (AFRL) Rocket Lab at Edwards AFB. Our community is the backbone of American defense and aerospace innovation, and I will always fight to make sure it has the resources it needs."

"These amendments provide critical support for Kern County’s aerospace and defense sector, honoring those lost in a tragic incident, advancing efforts to address healthcare access, and enhancing our flight test capabilities,” said Justin Salters, California lead at the Griffiss Institute. “We appreciate Rep. Fong’s continued leadership and commitment to accelerating innovation in Kern County and supporting our base communities.”

“Establishing a connection between the R-2508 Airspace and the Naval Air Warfare Center Weapons Division Point Mugu Sea Test Range would establish one of the nation’s most capable, integrated, and urgently required supersonic test corridors,” said Stephen Farmer, Executive Director of China Lake Alliance. “This corridor would enable government and industry to conduct more intricate, efficient, and realistic testing. The development, testing, and delivery of longer-range, supersonic weapons are essential to counter our most formidable foreign threats. The absence of this corridor is hindering the timely acquisition of this crucial capability that is urgently needed by our military. Furthermore, this corridor would expand opportunities for innovation within California’s aerospace and defense ecosystem.”

The FY2027 NDAA includes three amendments authored by Congressman Fong:

Amendment 136: Honoring the Edwards AFB B-52 Crash Victims

Honors the eight heroes lost in the tragic B-52 crash at Edwards AFB last month. Directs the Department of War to brief Congress on the crash.

Last month, Rep. Fong led a moment of silence on the House floor to honor those who lost their lives in the plane crash at Edwards AFB. You can find more information here.

Amendment 137: Medical and Safety Resources Study at Edwards AFB

Directs a comprehensive study of medical and safety resources at Edwards AFB to ensure the workforce, including military servicemembers, DOW civilians, and contractors, have what is needed to operate safely and effectively.

Amendment 135: R-2508 Complex and Point Mugu Sea Range Airspace Study

Directs a study of supersonic airspace connectivity between the R-2508 Airspace Complex and the Point Mugu Sea Range. Together, these ranges encompass over 56,000 square miles of world-class testing capacity. Better integration between them would expand test capabilities for both military and commercial aerospace, keeping America at the cutting edge of defense innovation. The R-2508 Airspace is home to Edwards AFB, NAWS China Lake, Fort Irwin, and is adjacent to the Mojave Air and Space Port.

Additionally, the FY2027 NDAA advances two significant military construction projects that strengthens the mission of NAS Lemoore and the AFRL Rocket Lab at Edwards AFB:

NAS Lemoore: $155,939,000 for the Strike Fighter Center of Excellence Pacific

Secures additional authorization to build the Strike Fighter Center of Excellence at NAS Lemoore, providing cutting-edge training facilities for Navy personnel to safely handle and load ordinance on Strike Fighter aircraft. This builds on $55,542,000, which was included in the FY26 NDAA for this facility.

Edwards AFB: $4,500,000 to Construct Vehicle Search Area at the AFRL Rocket Lab, Edwards Air Force Base

Secures authorization to construct a dedicated Vehicle Search Area at the AFRL Rocket Lab Gate Entry Control Point (ECP) at Edwards AFB. This project will strengthen installation security, improve access control, and support the base’s critical research and development mission.

Overall, the FY2027 NDAA delivers for servicemembers, veterans, and national security across the board, including:

Historic Pay Raise for Servicemembers

Provides a 5-7% pay raise for all servicemembers, supporting quality of life improvements, along with improved housing, education, and access to childcare.

Revitalizing the Defense Industrial Base

Expands U.S. production capacity, unleashes private sector investment, opens the door to new and innovative defense entrants, reduces needless regulations, and creates thousands of skilled jobs for Americans.

Restoring Lethal Capabilities

Rebuilds depleted stockpiles by expediting the production and acquisition of munitions and key warfighting capabilities, and accelerates new technologies including quantum computing, hypersonics, and autonomous systems.

Peace through Strength

Invests to maintain a strong U.S. posture, strengthens nuclear deterrence, expands missile defense, and targets resources to counter adversaries.

Implements President Trump's Agenda

Advances over 65 of President Trump's Executive Orders and Legislative Proposals, fully authorizing his top defense priorities.

Eliminating Waste, Fraud, and Abuse

Cuts nearly $30 billion in wasteful programs, stands up a new task force to eliminate fraudulent payments, and requires a full and clean DOW audit within 24 months.

The NDAA passed 216-212 with bipartisan support. The bill now advances to the Senate for consideration.

###

title: Rep. Foushee Votes Against Wasteful Budget Resolution Which Lays Groundwork for Republican Reconciliation Package
text:
WASHINGTON, DC (July 22, 2026) — Today, Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) voted against H.Con.Res.113, a Republican Budget Resolution which attempts to begin the Reconciliation process.

“While over 8 million Americans have already lost health insurance coverage and over 4 million Americans have lost their SNAP access due to Republicans’ funding cuts, Congress is voting on whether we should ship tens of billions in taxpayer dollars abroad for unwanted war. This is completely out-of-touch and is not what the American people sent us to Washington to accomplish,” said Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04). “In this third round of reconciliation, Republicans are lying and saying we don’t have enough money for our military while separately trying to pass a $1.1 trillion defense budget. I voted no because the people of North Carolina’s Fourth District are not looking for more funding for war, they want a federal government that actively responds to the rising cost of education, healthcare, housing, and everyday expenses.”

The reconciliation process begins with a congressional budget resolution. The resolution directs committees to change spending by specific amounts, with the Budget Committee putting together each committee’s bill needed to achieve the target spending limit in one larger reconciliation package like the so-called "One Big Beautiful Bill" that passed in 2025. In this case, H.Con.Res.113 allocates over $70 billion in supplemental funding for defense and intelligence operations over the next 10 years.

Congresswoman Foushee is a supporter of the Block the Bombs Act, the Iran War Powers Resolution, the Cuba War Powers Resolution, and the Venezuela War Powers Resolution.

Congresswoman Foushee has voted in favor of every War Powers Resolution brought to the House floor during the 119th Congress. In May, Congresswoman Foushee introduced her own Iran War Powers Resolution.

title: Franklin Supports Clean Continuing Resolution To Prevent Government Shutdown
text:
Congressman Scott Franklin issued the following statement after House passage of H.R. 9770, the Continuing Appropriations Act:

“For too long, Congress has relied on last-minute negotiations and massive omnibus spending bills instead of doing the work the Constitution requires. As a member of the House Appropriations Committee, I’ve been committed to restoring regular order by considering each of the twelve annual funding bills individually, debating them openly and moving them through the legislative process.

“This continuing resolution keeps the government open through December 4th while preserving the progress we’ve made on the FY27 appropriations process. It maintains funding for our military, disaster response and other essential government services while giving Congress additional time to complete negotiations on each of the twelve annual funding bills.

“Government shutdowns disrupt the services Americans rely on and create real consequences for families, federal employees, service members and local communities. This legislation removes the immediate threat of a shutdown, but it is only a short-term solution. The goal is to complete the appropriations process through regular order and replace this continuing resolution with full-year funding bills.

“The House Appropriations Committee has advanced all twelve FY27 funding bills, and the House has passed three of those measures on the floor. I urge the Senate to build on that progress so Congress can finish the job, move beyond temporary funding measures and provide the certainty and responsible oversight taxpayers deserve.”

title: Franklin Statement On House Passage Of The FY27 National Defense Authorization Act
text:

"Our military cannot maintain its edge if we fail to invest in the people, equipment and industrial capacity that make mission success possible. The FY27 National Defense Authorization Act strengthens that foundation by rebuilding our defense industrial base, expanding domestic production and ensuring America can produce the ships, munitions and emerging technologies needed to deter our adversaries and meet the threats of today and tomorrow.

"As a retired Naval Aviator, I know military readiness isn't measured by what we say. It's measured by whether our service members have the training, equipment and support they need to accomplish the mission. This legislation invests in next-generation capabilities, strengthens our nuclear deterrent and missile defenses and helps ensure our armed forces remain prepared to deter adversaries like the Chinese Communist Party.

Strong oversight helps ensure defense dollars are focused where they belong: equipping our service members, strengthening readiness and maintaining America's military advantage.

"Meeting tomorrow's threats requires making the right investments today. The FY27 NDAA strengthens our military, supports our service members and ensures America is prepared to deter China, outpace our adversaries and preserve our military advantage."
