title: Congressman Gabe Evans Votes to Strengthen America's Military, Support Service Members, and Restore Deterrence
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Gabe Evans, a veteran of the Global War on Terror and former Black Hawk helicopter pilot, voted to pass the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), legislation that strengthens America's military, invests in service members and their families, modernizes our defense capabilities, and ensures the United States remains prepared to confront growing threats from adversaries like Communist China.

“As an Army veteran who has completed a combat deployment in the Middle East, I know firsthand that peace is achieved through strength. Our service members deserve the best training, equipment, and support possible to accomplish their mission and return home safely. I'm especially proud that the House also adopted two of my amendments—one to help ensure our National Guard and Reserve service members finally receive equal special incentive pay for the same skills and qualifications as their active-duty counterparts, and another to strengthen military aviation by supporting critical upgrades for our rotary wing helicopter fleet.

This year's National Defense Authorization Act invests in military readiness, strengthens our defense industrial base, modernizes the force for future conflicts, and continues rebuilding the world's strongest fighting force. At a time when adversaries like Communist China, the Iranian Regime, and transnational criminal organizations are growing more aggressive, Congress has a responsibility to ensure America remains prepared to deter conflict and defend our national security.” — Congressman Gabe Evans

Congressman Evans introduced two amendments based on his experience serving in the Colorado Army National Guard — both of which passed the House and were included in the final bill. As a Black Hawk helicopter pilot, he flew missions overseas and responded to dangerous wildfires here in Colorado. During his service, he saw firsthand that National Guard members are held to the same high standards as Active-Duty service members but don't always receive the same incentive pay. That's why one of his amendments helps ensure Guardsmen and Reservists are paid fairly when they meet the same qualifications. His second amendment invests in upgrades that will make military helicopters safer, stronger, and more capable so pilots have the equipment they need to complete their missions and return home safely.

Drawing on his own military experience, Congressman Evans worked to ensure this year's NDAA not only strengthens America's national defense, but also supports the men and women who wear the uniform. He knows firsthand that giving our service members the right tools and resources are essential to maintaining the strongest military in the world.

The Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act will:

Strengthen America's military readiness by investing in advanced weapons systems, hypersonic capabilities, missile defense, autonomous systems, and next-generation technologies.

Increase pay for America's service members while supporting military families through expanded counseling resources, childcare assistance, and quality-of-life improvements.

Accelerate defense innovation by expanding investments in emerging technologies, artificial intelligence, cybersecurity, and strengthening America's defense industrial base.

Counter growing threats from Communist China by strengthening supply chain resilience, protecting critical infrastructure, expanding Indo-Pacific deterrence, and reducing reliance on foreign adversaries.

Enhance border and counter-drug operations by increasing support for National Guard counter-drug programs and strengthening efforts to combat transnational criminal organizations.

Modernize the Department of Defense by improving acquisition processes, increasing transparency, strengthening financial accountability, and delivering capabilities to the warfighter faster.

Restore merit and military readiness by ensuring defense resources remain focused on warfighting, mission accomplishment, and the needs of America's service members.

The Fiscal Year 2027 NDAA reflects Congress' commitment to ensuring the United States military remains the strongest, most capable fighting force in the world while providing service members with the resources, equipment, and support they need to defend our nation.

title: Evans' Bipartisan FIRE Act Gains Momentum as Senate Introduces Companion Legislation
text:
WASHINGTON —Today, Congressman Gabe Evans joined Rep. Adam Gray in welcoming the introduction of bipartisan companion legislation in the U.S. Senate that builds on the commonsense reforms included in the Fire Improvement and Reforming Exceptional Events (FIRE) Act, which passed the House of Representatives earlier this year with bipartisan support.

Led by Senators John Curtis (R-Utah) and Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), the bipartisan Wildfire Emissions Prevention Act (WEPA) incorporates key provisions championed by Congressman Evans and Congressman Adam Gray to make it easier for states to use prescribed fires to prevent catastrophic wildfires while ensuring communities are not unfairly penalized under the Clean Air Act for proactive wildfire mitigation efforts. The Senate legislation would also provide greater regulatory certainty for states, protect ecosystems and wildlife habitat, and help communities better prepare for future wildfire seasons.

“Representative Gabe Evans and Representative Adam Gray welcome the announcement of the Senate compromise on FIRE/WEPA. This legislation builds on our bipartisan solution to codify prescribed fires in the exceptional events process to prevent wildfires, creating regulatory certainty for communities, protecting jobs and the economy, and allowing states to take proactive steps to improve their air quality instead of being punished for emissions beyond their control. We thank our Senate colleagues for their work on this issue, urge them to pass this critical package swiftly, and look forward to its consideration in the House. When it comes to wildfires, Congress cannot afford to wait. We must act now.”

Background

In April, the House of Representatives passed Congressman Evans' bipartisan FIRE Act, legislation to modernize the Clean Air Act by ensuring states are not penalized for emissions caused by wildfires and prescribed burns while encouraging proactive forest management and reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens.

The newly introduced Senate companion bill builds on those same principles by making it easier for states and communities to use prescribed fire to reduce catastrophic wildfire risk, providing certainty that states will not be penalized for taking action to prevent wildfires, promoting the efficient use of state air quality resources, and making forests and communities safer, healthier, and cleaner.

title: Rep. Garamendi, House Democrats Demand the Trump Administration Abandon Illegal Plans to Dismantle Civil Rights and Special Education Offices
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman John Garamendi (CA-08) joined eighty-five House Democrats calling on the Department of Education to immediately abandon its plan to transfer the Office of Special Education and Rehabilitative Services (OSERS) to the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) and the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) to the Department of Justice (DOJ).

In their letter, the Members argue that the Trump Administration’s plan to dismantle OCR and OSERS through Interagency Agreements (IAAs) is unlawful because Congress established both offices and only Congress has the authority to eliminate them or alter their responsibilities.

“The law is clear: Congress created OCR and OSERS and Congress alone can eliminate them. The use of Interagency Agreements to accomplish your ‘final mission’ – to eliminate the Department in all but name – is counter to the will of Congress and rests on questionable legal ground. Even Congressional Republicans have expressed reservations and attempted to keep money appropriated to the Department within the Department, rather than being outsourced through IAAs…,” wrote the Members.

Beyond legal concerns, the Members warned that transferring OCR and OSERS functions would weaken services for students, families, and individuals with disabilities because DOJ and HHS are ill-equipped to carry out the offices’ core functions.

“The movement of OCR and OSERS also disrespects the very people who rely on those services. Specifically, these moves effectively segregates special education from the rest of the education system, moving it to an agency that has indicated it intends to treat disabilities as a health issue to be remedied, against the wishes of groups that advocate on behalf of disabled children and their families. Such action is particularly concerning given the inaccurate and harmful comments from the HHS Secretary regarding children diagnosed with autism. Comments such as these will leave those relying on special education services fearful about whether their rights will be upheld and their needs met. Regarding OCR, given the sensitive nature of many of the cases it handles, victims may be hesitant to seek support knowing the investigation will be run by the nation’s primary law enforcement agency. Such delays may cause cases of discrimination to fester and worsen while sending the wrong message to vulnerable communities,” concluded the Members.

In February 2026, the Government Accountability Office (GAO) reported that ED paid OCR investigators up to $38 million not to work.

In April 2026, the Senate HELP Committee released a report that in 2025, OCR reached zero resolution agreements involving sexual harassment, sexual violence, seclusion or restraint, racial harassment, or discriminatory school discipline — despite more than 2,700 pending cases.

title: Rep. Garamendi Statement on Trump-Saudi Arabia Nuclear Deal
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman John Garamendi (CA-08), co-chair of the bicameral Nuclear Weapons and Arms Control Working Group and a senior member of the House Armed Services Committee, issued the following statement in response to the Trump administration announcing a Saudi Arabia that would open the door to providing the Kingdom with the most sensitive nuclear technologies, including the enrichment of uranium, without requiring the most stringent safeguards against the development of nuclear weapons.

“The last thing the world needs is more nuclear weapons. and yet, today’s deal takes us one step closer to creating a terrifying world of further nuclear proliferation and an arm’s race in the Middle East.

“In November, I urged that any civilian nuclear cooperation agreement with Saudi Arabia include the “Gold Standard”—the strongest nuclear nonproliferation safeguards available, including a clear commitment to forgo uranium enrichment and plutonium reprocessing on Saudi soil. Those provisions help ensure that civilian nuclear programs cannot be diverted toward the development of nuclear weapons.

“The Administration chose not to make those safeguards a requirement for a deal, leaving open the possibility that Saudi Arabia could build a nuclear weapons program.

“This is a consequential mistake. We need less nuclear weapons, not more.”

title: Top Democrat on House Armed Services Readiness, Rep. Garamendi, Statement Votes NO on NDAA

“There is no world in which I can justify spending $1.15 trillion on defense so that President Trump can continue to recklessly start wars around the globe. Yet President Trump and Republicans are prepared to spend your tax dollars on the military while cutting your health care and driving up energy and gas costs.

“To make matters even worse, Republicans hijacked this process by adding provisions that would restrict access to the ballot for millions of Americans.

I have always fought and will continue to fight to make this bill as good as it can be.

“But the irresponsible price tag and lack of any meaningful administration oversight made my decision clear. This Administration is waging an illegal war of choice in Iran, deploying the military to our city streets, bombing boats in the Caribbean, diverting military resources to Trump’s vanity project, and dramatically increasing spending on nuclear weapons.

Congress should not support blank checks, politicized defense policy, or remain silent when it has a constitutional duty to provide oversight. For these reasons, and many more, I cannot in good conscience support this bill.”

title: Gluesenkamp Perez Returns Home to Speak to Machinist Apprentices, Visit with Truck Manufacturing Workers and Tour a Box Manufacturing Company
text:
SOUTHWEST WASHINGTON — Earlier this month, Rep. Marie Gluesenkamp Perez came home to Southwest Washington to visit a number of trades workers and local businesses. This work period included a stop to Northwest Paper box to talk about the role paper plays in our region, a tour of Summit Truck to learn about supporting U.S. manufacturing, and a visit to a machinists apprentice program to talk about supporting students involved in trades work.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez started the District Work Period with a tour of Summit Body Trucking in Ridgefield, a manufacturing facility that builds truck bodies. There, she was able to speak to skilled trades workers about the operational landscape of a major manufacturing facility, and what it takes to keep jobs local.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez joins workers on a tour of Summit Body Trucking

“We can’t have a strong local economy without a reliable, efficient way to get goods from A to B. Places like Summit Body aren’t just supporting local jobs, they’re building an economy where we have agency and self-reliance.” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “Thank you to the skilled tradesmen who welcomed me in to see their process and discuss what it takes to keep our local goods on the road.”

Later in the week, Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez was invited to Northwest Paper Box Manufacturers in Camas to discuss timber products and how to continue supporting the pulp and paper industry. At this second generation family business, she spoke with workers about the vital need for a strong diversified timber industry in Southwest Washington. The Congresswoman has spent much of her time in congress as a fighter for the natural resource economy, including paper mills across Southwest Washington. In 2025, she introduced the Jobs in the Woods Act aimed at investing in education for a new generation of skilled labor.

Rep Gluesenkamp Perez speaks at Northwest Paper Box about the critical role paper mills play in the timber economy.

To round out the district work period, the Congresswoman stopped in to visit the Machinist Institute in Vancouver to learn more about their apprenticeship program. Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez has been a champion for trades education and apprenticeship programs. She has fought for AP credits for shop class and introduced legislation to allow the use of 529 funds for students in trades education.

Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez joins machinist apprentices learning lathe skills.

“It takes a lot of grit and determination to wake up every day and make a living with your hands. We need robust education programs to make sure that the next generation of machinists, welders and fabricators are right here, building things worth having in our community.” Said Rep. Gluesenkamp Perez, “I’m so proud to support the people doing the work of teaching our students that they can build durable, fulfilling careers in the trades.”

title: Golden votes against GOP’s reconciliation framework
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) voted today against Republicans’ partisan reconciliation framework.

“While we don’t know the details of the Republicans’ reconciliation plan yet, I've watched the GOP run this play before and I’m not expecting it to add up to anything good for Maine,” Golden said. “I’ll keep an open mind and will assess whatever they pull together on the merits. But I’m not going to grease the skids for the majority to write a partisan bill behind closed doors.”

The vote passed the House in a party-line 216-214vote.

Background:

Reconciliation is a budgetary maneuver that allows the majority party to amend the current budget and bypass the 60-vote threshold for passage in the Senate.

The resolution before the House today begins the process with a framework that outlines $95 billion in new spending to be drafted by the committees on Agriculture, Armed Services, Intelligence, and House Administration. Their proposals will then be lumped together into one bill to be laid before the full House of Representatives.

###

title: Golden votes to extend government funding through December 4
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) voted in favor of a Continuing Resolution (CR) to keep the government funded until December 4, preventing a risk of government shutdown on October 1.

The CR contains no major changes to federal policies, programs or current spending levels. The bill passed the House Tuesday night in a 220-205 vote.

“It is unusual to pass a CR this far ahead of a funding deadline, but the reality is the House and Senate are far away from a deal to keep government funded and, with an election coming up, the risk of political gamesmanship is high,” Golden said. “This CR will give us space to continue negotiating an appropriations deal while removing the incentive for either party to hold the government hostage in an attempt to score electoral points.”

Golden has a long history of voting to avoid government shutdowns because of the harm they cause. This past winter, a lapse in appropriations triggered the longest shutdown in the nation’s history. As a result, millions of federal workers missed paychecks, travelers experienced long delays, food assistance benefits for needy families were disrupted and core public health and food safety programs were paused.

A government shutdown in October would affect the more than 11,000 federal employees in Maine and could force Acadia National Park to close.

The CR now heads to the Senate for consideration.

###

title: House passes defense authorization bill with Golden’s pro-shipbuilding provisions
text:
WASHINGTON — The U.S. House of Representatives on Wednesday passed the 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), including provisions won by Congressman Jared Golden (ME-02) to protect American shipbuilding from offshoring and to fund an additional destroyer to be built in Maine at Bath Iron Works (BIW).

The 2027 NDAA authorizes $1.15 trillion in spending for the Department of Defense and other national security priorities. Golden — a member of the House Armed Services Committee, which drafted the bill — voted in favor of the legislation, which passed the House in a bipartisan 216-212 vote.

“This bill is a win for America’s shipbuilders, including the thousands of workers at Bath Iron Works for whom it will provide job security so they can keep building the world-class destroyers that are the workhorse of America’s surface fleet,” Golden said. “By blocking the Pentagon’s plan to move shipbuilding overseas, we have proven that Congress will act to protect American industry, jobs, innovation and our national security.”

Golden fought successfully in committee to attach two critical provisions to the final 2027 NDAA:

Language to block the U.S. Navy’s offshoring plan: In May, the Navy issued a shipbuilding plan that included a proposal to allow American ships, or parts of ships, to be built in overseas yards using foreign labor. Golden pushed back and won language to specify that no funds authorized under the 2027 NDAA may be obligated to enter into a contract for the procurement of a battle force ship to be built in a foreign yard.

Language to authorize additional funds to ensure construction of a DDG-51 destroyer at BIW: In previous years, the pentagon has requested authorization to build multiple DDG-51 destroyers, creating demand for ships at both Ingalls Shipbuilding in Mississippi and Bath Iron Works. This year, the president’s budget proposal included only one ship, which was expected to be built at Ingalls. General Dynamics, BIW’s parent company, told HASC that this would have resulted in layoffs in Bath. Ultimately, Golden successfully won inclusion of $1 billion for a second ship, expected to be built in Bath. His language also allowed for incremental funding, which will keep shipbuilders working at BIW.

In addition to the shipbuilding provisions, Golden also lauded several elements of the 2027 NDAA that will improve quality of life for America’s service members.

The most immediate individual benefits are a pay raise of 5 to 7 percent for all troops, improved cost-of-living adjustments for troops stationed in high-cost areas, increased paid leave allowances, fertility coverage and junior-reserve dental coverage.

title: Congressman Gonzalez Hits the Ground Running for CCAD
text:
Contact: Alexis Torres

Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman Vicente Gonzalez (TX-34) voted in favor of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27), which authorizes $1.14 trillion in discretionary funding for our national defense and an up to 7% pay raise for all military personnel. The bill also includes language and amendments the Congressman authored to strengthen military operations at installations like the Corpus Christi Army Depot (CCAD) and to safeguard the domestic South Texas shrimping industry. It now heads to the Senate for a vote.

“Every year, Congress is responsible for funding our nation’s defense priorities to keep Americans safe and our military strong. I worked in a bipartisan manner to raise military pay and expand access to housing, childcare, and healthcare for our service members and their families in South Texas and around the world, including at the Naval Air Stations in Kingsville and Corpus Christi. Also included in this bill is language and amendments I authored to protect Corpus Christi Army Depot’s military competitiveness and the thousands of hardworking South Texans it employs. Together, we will ensure that the economy continues to thrive and our region remains a critical part of our national security.”

The base text of the House-passed FY27 NDAA includes language secured by Congressman Gonzalez that build on his efforts to protect jobs and increase a declining workload at CCAD. These provisions include:

Allowing depots like CCAD to promptly write off debt associated with government directed mission changes (Sec. 1862, page 23).

Directing the Department of Defense (DoD) to increase transparency into the way that depot-level maintenance and repair work is divided between military installations and private companies (Sec. 1861, page 1340).

Requiring the Secretary of Defense to submit a report to Congress within 60 days on the status of funds set aside for the completion and modernization of a Powertrain Facility at CCAD. This facility will provide the Army with adequate space to maintain a wide range of helicopters and related parts.

Prohibiting the DoD from procurement or commissary sales of seafood originating or processed in China (co-sponsored with Congressman Troy Carter of Louisiana).

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Calls for Government-Wide Review of IDEMIA’s Role in TSA, CBP, FBI, and DOD Identity Systems
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Wednesday, July 22, 2026, Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) sent a letter to the U.S. General Services Administration (GSA) Administrator Edward C. Forst and the U.S. Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russell Vought requesting a comprehensive, government-wide audit of every federal contract involving IDEMIA, the technology contractor whose software failure resulted in approximately 6,600 noncitizens being added to New Jersey’s voter rolls.

The text of the letter can be found here.

The error, which New Jersey officials identified on July 21, 2026, stemmed from a malfunction at the state’s Motor Vehicle Commission that mistakenly registered noncitizens to vote when they applied for driver’s licenses and identification cards between June 2023 and June 2024, during the previous State Administration.

Gottheimer’s letter emphasizes that the problem extends far beyond New Jersey. IDEMIA holds a sweeping portfolio of federal identity and security contracts, including:

TSA’s Universal Enrollment Services provider for PreCheck and other screening programs.

Border Patrol’s (CBP) biometric entry-exit mission.

FBI’s fingerprint submission system.

Driver’s license provider in 36 states.

Department of Defense’s identity operations.

This is also not the first time IDEMIA has faced backlash from its technology. IDEMIA was embroiled in a scandal in South Africa, where the airport company terminated its contract in August 2024, amid a government investigation, and the company faced a multimillion-rand damages claim arising from that procurement.

“This incident raises serious concerns about the reliability of IDEMIA’s software, the company’s quality control practices, and the federal government’s reliance on a single contractor to manage highly sensitive identity and biometric systems,” Gottheimer wrote.

“A single vendor is thus embedded, simultaneously, in how the government screens travelers, secures ports and hazardous-materials handlers, processes travelers at the border, runs criminal background checks, issues civilian identity credentials, and supports military and intelligence identity operations,” the letter states.

###

title: GRAY INTRODUCES BIPARTISAN BILL TO SPEED UP CENTRAL VALLEY INFRASTRUCTURE PROJECTS
text:
Today, Congressman Adam Gray (CA-13) and Congressman David Rouzer (NC-07) introduced the Certainty and Uniform Reviews for Reliable Energy and Transmission (CURRENT) Act, bipartisan legislation to modernize the federal permitting process, cut through unnecessary government red tape, and provide greater certainty for infrastructure projects while maintaining key provisions of the Clean Water Act.

"For too long, the State of California has used the Section 401 process under the Clean Water Act to hold up critical permits in the Central Valley," said Congressman Adam Gray (CA-13). "Every delay creates more uncertainty for our farmers, water districts, and local economy by making a path to reliable water deliveries through collaborative voluntary agreements harder to secure. The CURRENT Act ensures that California and other states can't use the permitting process to impose impractical and costly requirements on energy projects. We can protect clean water while giving our communities the certainty they need."

"Long term regulatory certainty is key to providing the confidence needed to grow businesses, create jobs, and strengthen our economy. This legislation builds on the important work of the PERMIT Act by further strengthening the Section 401 permitting process through clear and efficient procedures — ensuring environmental reviews remain focused on protecting water quality, not obstructing critical infrastructure projects,” said Congressman David Rouzer (NC-07).

Under current law, Section 401 of the Clean Water Act requires applicants seeking certain federal permits or licenses to obtain a water quality certification from states, tribes, or authorized agencies. Over time, the certification process has become increasingly unpredictable, resulting in permitting delays, litigation, and uncertainty for critical infrastructure projects.

The CURRENT Act reforms Section 401 to provide greater certainty, transparency, and consistency in the federal permitting process for energy, hydropower, transmission, carbon dioxide infrastructure, and other federally licensed projects.

Specifically, this bill limits a states’ ability to mandate conditions outside of what would impact the federal water quality standard. The legislation establishes firm timelines, increasing transparency, and streamlines judicial review.

“Merced Irrigation District is pleased to support this common-sense legislation. MID’s relicensing of the Merced River Hydroelectric Project includes a 401-water quality control certification. Our operations benefit the entire state and nation, including providing vital flood control, clean energy and electric grid support – as well as recreation. Crucially, MID’s operations provide water supply to the 5th largest agricultural economy in the nation. We are happy to evaluate the actual effects of the water discharge from the hydroelectric project. However, we do not believe that numerous other issues outside our operations should become entangled in what should be a straight-forward analysis of water quality,” said the Merced Irrigation District.

"TID was built on the belief that water and power delivered reliably and affordably are the foundation of a thriving Central Valley — and that a healthy Tuolumne River is part of that foundation. When regulatory processes expand beyond their core statutory purpose, it creates uncertainty that can put that balance at risk — for our communities and the environment alike. We welcome Congressman Gray's efforts to refocus the Clean Water Act on its core water quality mission and look forward to working with partners at every level to get this right,” said Brad Koehn, Turlock Irrigation District General Manager.

“California has stretched Section 401 beyond what Congress intended, using it to regulate issues unrelated to water quality. This has complicated the federal licensing process, created regulatory uncertainty, and imposed avoidable costs on our ratepayers. We appreciate and support Congressman Gray's efforts to realign Section 401 with its original purpose while preserving essential water quality protections,” said Jimi Netniss, Modesto Irrigation District General Manager.

"America's affordability crisis and the ‘race for AI’ both come down to the same bottleneck: our inability to build the infrastructure this country needs, fast enough. Section 401 of the Clean Water Act was intended to protect water quality — not serve as an open-ended tool to delay or block the infrastructure our country depends on. That is why we are encouraged to see Representatives Gray and Rouzer introduce the bipartisan CURRENT Act, to bring more certainty, clearer timelines, and consistent standards to the broken permitting process. We appreciate their bipartisan leadership and look forward to working with them and Members of both parties to see meaningful Section 401 reform in a bold, comprehensive permitting reform package — one that finally lets America build the energy future it needs," said Chad Zamarin, Williams President and CEO.

"The CURRENT Act will help return the Clean Water Act to its intended purpose: protecting water quality. For too long, hydropower producers have been forced to pay for wish-list items under Sec. 401 water quality certifications that have nothing to do with the reliable power they provide. The bill provides greater clarity and certainty in the water quality certification process, and in turn will streamline the hydropower licensing process to meet growing electricity demand and help keep power bills lower for consumers. This bipartisan legislation proves that Congress can find common ground on our most challenging permitting reform issues. NHA thanks Representatives Adam Gray and David Rouzer for advancing this bill, and we urge Congress to pass it swiftly," said Matthew Allen, NHA’s Senior Director of Legislative Affairs.

Read the full text of the bill here.

title: Rep. Grijalva Statement After Federal Court Hears Tohono O'odham Nation's Challenge to Border Wall Construction
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the following statement after a federal district court in Washington, D.C. heard the Tohono O'odham Nation's lawsuit challenging the Department of Homeland Security's plan to construct a second border wall through the Nation's reservation.

"It is against the law for DHS to unilaterally alter the boundaries of a sovereign Tribal Nation, yet that is exactly what they are trying to do—usurping authority that only Congress has. We have already seen the devastating consequences of when this administration ignores Tribal governments with the destruction of the Las Playas Intaglio. Now, other sacred sites, such as Quitobaquito Springs, are under threat. This is not just temporary damage to land – it is irreparable destruction of a sacred place tied to the O’odham people’s history, identity, and spiritual practices.”

“This administration is willing to violate Tribal sovereignty, threaten culturally and environmentally significant lands, and waste billions of taxpayer dollars on another useless border wall that does nothing to make our communities safer. If DHS is serious about border security, they should invest in staffing and modernizing our ports of entry – not bulldozing sacred Tribal lands and building another unnecessary wall despite Tribal opposition."

In May, Rep. Grijalva questioned Department of the Interior Secretary Doug Burgum about the destruction of the Las Playas Intaglio site during a House Natural Resources Committee hearing. She also asked him for assurances that Quitobaquito Springs would not be touched. This site was negatively impacted during the construction of the first border wall.

title: Guthrie Votes in Favor of House FY 2027 National Defense Authorization Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Brett Guthrie (KY-02) issued the following statement following the House passage of H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act, FY2027 (NDAA). This legislation would authorize $1.15 trillion in discretionary defense spending, matching President Trump’s presidential budget request. At its core, this NDAA focuses on reinvigorating America’s defense industrial base to ensure our troops can continue to keep our country safe.

“As a graduate of West Point and former officer in the U.S. Army, I am proud to support this year’s NDAA, which ensures America’s heroes have the tools and support necessary to carry out their mission,” said Congressman Guthrie. “This legislation unleashes America’s private defense manufacturing capabilities and invests in much-needed quality of life improvements for our servicemembers. This bill is a win for our military and national security, plain and simple.”

Background:

H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act, FY2027:

Authorizes $1.15 trillion in total defense discretionary spending, including:

$258 billion for procurement of new equipment

$219 billion for research, development, test, & evaluation

$247 billion for military personnel & health

$338 billion for operation & maintenance

$28 billion for military construction & military family housing

$41 towards defense nuclear programs

Provides a 5% to 7% pay raise to all servicemembers.

Directs targeted resources to strengthen nuclear deterrence, expand missile defense, and counter threats from our adversaries such as China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

Makes statutory reforms to expand domestic defense manufacturing and reinvigorate our defense industrial base.

Authorizes almost $1 billion to counter drug trafficking and grants the National Guard the authority to procure equipment for counter-narcotics and drug interdiction operations.

A topline summary of H.R. 8800, provided by the House Armed Services Committee, can be found HERE.

title: Congressman Rogers Supports Rebuilding America’s Arsenal of Freedom with U.S. Production

title: Congressman Hamadeh Urges Senate to Pass the Save America Act Following Continuous House Action
text:
Washington, D.C.— Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ-08) is urging the U.S. Senate to finally pass the Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) America Act after the House advanced it by attaching its key provisions to both the NDAA and Budget Resolutions.

As part of the House Budget Resolution and consideration of H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, the House adopted a special rule directing that the text of the SAVE America Act be added to the legislation at engrossment, ensuring that it’s pushed to the Senate alongside one of Congress's most important legislative packages. The action comes after the House's continued commitment to protecting election integrity after previously passing the SAVE America Act in February 2026.

The SAVE America Act requires voters to present valid ID when voting in federal elections, verifying proof of citizenship. The vast majority of Americans support voter ID laws, with 97 percent of Republicans, 84 percent of Independents, and 53 percent of Democrats in support, according to Gallup polling.

Congressman Hamadeh applauds Speaker Mike Johnson for his leadership in utilizing all available legislative avenues to prioritize election integrity and ensure the voices of American voters remain protected.

“Election integrity is essential to protecting the voice of the American people and preserving our Constitutional Republic. Our elections should be decided by only American citizens with every lawful ballot protected,” said Congressman Abraham J. Hamadeh. “I am proud to support the SAVE America Act. The Senate must stop delaying action and join the House in defending the integrity of our elections and protecting the sacred right of American citizens to vote.”

Arizona continues to be at the center of the national conversation on election administration, making election integrity a priority for many families across Arizona's Eighth Congressional District. Congressman Hamadeh believes every eligible American citizen deserves confidence that federal elections are conducted fairly, transparently, and in accordance with the law.

Background:

The Safeguard American Voter Eligibility (SAVE) America Act was introduced by Congressman Chip Roy (R- TX) and requires proof of US citizenship for registration to vote in federal elections. The legislation passed the House on February 11, 2026.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Introduces SAFE Rural Act to Strengthen Flood Resilience in Rural Communities
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) introduced the Sustainable and Flood Resilient Engineering for Rural Areas (SAFE Rural) Act, bipartisan legislation to expand access to FEMA flood resilience funding for rural communities and remove barriers that too often prevent small towns from preparing before disaster strikes. Congressman Eric Sorensen (IL-17) joined Harrigan as the bill's original co-lead.

"Communities across western North Carolina know better than anyone that rebuilding after a flood is always harder and more expensive than preparing beforehand. The problem is that too many rural communities never get the chance to prepare because they don't have the staff or resources to navigate Washington's grant process. The SAFE Rural Act changes that by making it easier for small towns to access the funding they need to strengthen critical infrastructure before the next disaster hits. That's a smarter use of taxpayer dollars, and it's how we build more resilient communities for the long haul," said Congressman Harrigan.

“Rural communities are often the first to feel the impacts of severe weather and flooding, but they don’t always have the resources to prepare,” said Congressman Eric Sorensen. “The SAFE Rural Act helps level the playing field by making sure small towns and rural areas have the tools and funding they need to protect their families, infrastructure, and communities before disaster strikes.”

The SAFE Rural Act has earned the support of leading organizations representing engineers, floodplain managers, and resilience experts:

“Small, rural and under-resourced communities often lack the funding and capacity to build resilience before disaster strikes, and BRIC's competitive grant model too often leaves them behind. AFCA applauds Congressman Harrigan and Congressman Sorensen for their introduction of the SAFE Rural Act. This bipartisan proposal would empower states to steer proactive resilience investment where it's needed most with fewer bureaucratic hurdles, and deliver dedicated funding for rural and under-resourced communities,” said Julie Seger, Federal Advocacy & Policy Director at AFCA.

"Rural, Tribal, and U.S. territorial communities are often among the most vulnerable to severe flooding and its devastating impacts. By expanding access to hazard mitigation funding, encouraging the use of modern engineering practices and helping underserved communities overcome barriers to project delivery, the SAFE Rural Act will help these communities to better protect their residents, critical infrastructure systems, and local economies while reducing the long-term costs of disaster recovery,” said Marsha Anderson Bomar, President of the American Society of Civil Engineers.

"The Association of State Floodplain Managers (ASFPM) is proud to support the SAFE Rural Act in addressing one of the shortcomings of existing pre-disaster hazard mitigation programs - equal opportunity for rural areas and Tribal nations. By using proven approaches to provide technical assistance and funding to these communities and avoiding known pitfalls in existing programs, the SAFE Rural Act allows funding to be flexibly used for locally identified and prioritized flood hazard mitigation efforts. We' ve long known that the benefits of hazard mitigation actions far exceed their costs. By directing a small part of the Disaster Relief Fund towards hazard mitigation, the SAFE Rural Act compels responsible stewardship of these taxpayer dollars by enabling long-term community flood resilience,” said Chad Berginnis, Executive Director of ASFPM.

“The National Association of Flood & Stormwater Management Agencies (NAFSMA) strongly supports the Sustainable and Flood Resilient Engineering for Rural Areas Act (SAFE Rural Act) and urges Congress to pass it without delay. Rural communities, Tribal lands, and U.S. territories often face the greatest flood risks and the least capacity to access federal mitigation funding. The SAFE Rural Act fixes this by establishing a dedicated, formula-based funding stream within the BRIC program, capitalized by a 2 percent set-aside from the FEMA Disaster Relief Fund. It streamlines applications for small projects, waives cost-share requirements for economically distressed communities, and builds state and local capacity through the Community Assistance Program. Every dollar invested in pre-disaster resilience saves many more in post-disaster recovery. This legislation reflects that reality, and NAFSMA is proud to support it,” said Sunny Simpkins, Executive Director of NAFSMA.

The SAFE Rural Act establishes a dedicated rural flood resilience fund within FEMA's Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC) program to provide formula-based funding for eligible rural communities, Tribal governments, and U.S. territories. The legislation streamlines applications for smaller projects, expands technical assistance, and helps communities invest in flood mitigation projects before disasters occur, reducing long-term recovery costs while strengthening critical infrastructure.

The SAFE Rural Act has been referred to the House Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure for consideration.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Votes to Ban Congressional Stock Trading
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10), an original cosponsor of the Stop Insider Trading Act, voted in favor of H.R. 7008, legislation to prohibit Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing individual stocks while serving in office and strengthen transparency requirements for stock sales.

"Congress shouldn't be playing the stock market while writing the laws, which is why I haven't touched individual stocks since coming to Congress and why Americans expect better from Washington," said Congressman Harrigan. "If we're asking the American people to trust us with the power to write the rules, they should never have to wonder whether those same rules are being used for personal financial gain."

The Stop Insider Trading Act prohibits Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing individual stocks while in office, while continuing to allow diversified investment funds, blind trusts, and certain other exempt investments. The legislation also requires advance public disclosure before covered individuals sell individual stocks and establishes meaningful penalties for violations.

Congressman Harrigan has consistently supported stronger ethics standards in Congress and has not traded individual stocks since taking office. As an original cosponsor of the Stop Insider Trading Act, he believes restoring public trust requires holding Members of Congress to the same standard Americans expect from anyone entrusted with public office.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Votes for FY27 NDAA, Secures Five Key Wins to Strengthen Military Readiness
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) voted in favor of the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), legislation that strengthens America's military while including five provisions authored by Harrigan to improve military readiness, secure critical defense supply chains, and modernize the Armed Forces.

"The world isn't getting any safer, and our military can't afford to prepare for yesterday's fight. This year's NDAA strengthens the industrial base that underpins our national defense, invests in the technologies that will shape the next generation of warfare, and delivers meaningful improvements for our servicemembers and their families. I'm especially proud that it includes several provisions I fought for to help the Department of Defense move faster, operate smarter, and stay ahead of our adversaries," said Congressman Harrigan.

Among the provisions secured by Congressman Harrigan are:

Military Right to Repair, bipartisan legislation ensuring the Department of Defense has access to the technical data needed to maintain and repair mission-critical equipment without being dependent on contractor monopolies.

Deployable Nuclear Power for INDOPACOM, directing the Department of Defense to deploy a transportable nuclear microreactor in the Indo-Pacific by 2030 to provide reliable power for expeditionary operations.

Ban on Chinese-Manufactured Optical Fiber, prohibiting the Department of Defense and its contractors from procuring or using optical fiber produced or controlled by entities under the jurisdiction of the People's Republic of China.

Repair by Replacement Reform, strengthening the Department of Defense's ability to sustain equipment in the field by improving how replacement parts are procured and maintained.

6.8mm NATO Standardization, directing the Department of Defense to pursue NATO standardization of next-generation 6.8x51mm ammunition to improve interoperability and logistics among allied forces.

Beyond Congressman Harrigan's provisions, the FY27 NDAA rebuilds America's defense industrial base by expanding domestic manufacturing capacity, restoring critical stockpiles, strengthening shipyards, and supporting the defense workforce. It also strengthens nuclear deterrence and missile defense, accelerates the development of emerging technologies such as hypersonics, quantum computing, and autonomous systems, provides a 5 to 7 percent pay raise for servicemembers, improves military housing and childcare, and advances reforms to eliminate waste and improve Pentagon accountability.

The FY27 NDAA now moves to the Senate, where differences between the House and Senate versions will be reconciled before final consideration by Congress.

title: Hern Applauds Passage of FY27 National Defense Authorization Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Kevin Hern (OK-01) today voted in support of the Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). The FY27 NDAA strengthens America’s national defense by revitalizing the defense industrial base, improving quality of life for servicemembers and their families, and investing in the production and acquisition of key capabilities needed to protect the United States and our allies around the world.

“Under the weak leadership of the Biden administration, our military suffered as supply chains weakened, recruitment declined, critical programs stalled, and our adversaries grew emboldened,” said Rep. Hern. “But with President Trump as Commander-in-Chief, readiness and lethality have been restored in our Armed Forces. The FY27 NDAA delivers a well-earned pay raise for servicemembers, strengthens the United States’ defense industrial base, and provides our troops with the resources, equipment, and support they need to defend our interests at home and abroad. The only way to secure peace is through strength, and this legislation ensures our military remains the most capable fighting force in the world.”

title: Comisionado Residente anuncia que la Cámara autoriza $33.5 millones para sistema de agua en Fort Buchanan.
text:
WASHINGTON DC - El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández, anunció hoy la aprobación en la Cámara de Representantes de la Ley de Autorización de Defensa Nacional para el año fiscal 2027, que incluye varias disposiciones relacionadas con instalaciones militares y personal de las Fuerzas Armadas en Puerto Rico. La medida pasa ahora al Senado para su consideración.

“Estas inversiones fortalecen la infraestructura crítica de nuestras instalaciones militares y su capacidad para continuar operando durante una emergencia. El nuevo sistema de tratamiento de agua en Fort Buchanan atiende una necesidad concreta de seguridad y resiliencia”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

La medida autoriza $33.5 millones para construir un sistema de tratamiento de agua de emergencia en Fort Buchanan. El proyecto busca permitir que la instalación pueda tratar y mantener un suministro de agua durante interrupciones del servicio, desastres naturales u otras emergencias, fortaleciendo la continuidad de sus operaciones.

También la medida extiende la autorización de un proyecto previamente aprobado de microred eléctrica y generación de energía de respaldo en Fort Buchanan. Esta extensión evita que la autorización expire mientras se completan los procesos necesarios para desarrollar la obra. Además, mantiene vigente la autorización para proyectos previamente aprobados en el Campamento Santiago de la Guardia Nacional de Puerto Rico, incluyendo infraestructura para mantenimiento de aeronaves y otras mejoras de apoyo operacional.

La medida también incluye disposiciones nacionales que aplican a Puerto Rico, entre ellas protecciones relacionadas con planes suplementarios de salud para militares y esfuerzos para facilitar que médicos de combate y otro personal de salud militar puedan utilizar su experiencia y credenciales al ingresar a la fuerza laboral civil.

title: Comisionado Residente: Hay Dinero para la Guerra pero no para Bajar el Costo de Vida
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — El Comisionado Residente de Puerto Rico, Pablo José Hernández advirtió que la nueva resolución presupuestaria impulsada por la mayoría republicana en la Cámara de Representantes podría resultar en recortes significativos a programas federales de los que dependen miles de familias, municipios y organizaciones en Puerto Rico.

“Hoy el Congreso no votó para bajar la compra, mejorar el acceso a servicios médicos ni acelerar la reconstrucción de Puerto Rico. Votó para abrir la puerta a decenas de miles de millones de dólares en nuevos gastos, mientras las necesidades más urgentes de nuestra gente siguen esperando”, expresó el Comisionado Residente.

La resolución autoriza al Comité de Servicios Armados a preparar hasta $60,000 millones en nuevos gastos y al Comité de Agricultura hasta $12,000 millones. La votación no aprobó todavía esos fondos, sino que permitió que ambos comités comiencen a redactar legislación que podría avanzar posteriormente mediante el proceso de reconciliación.

Para Puerto Rico, esto significa que el Congreso podría destinar miles de millones de dólares adicionales a operaciones militares y a atender los efectos de las políticas arancelarias del presidente Donald Trump, sin garantizar nuevos recursos para combatir el alto costo de vida, fortalecer el sistema de salud o acelerar la reconstrucción.

En total, el próximo paquete podría aumentar el déficit federal hasta en $95,000 millones durante los próximos diez años. También incluye instrucciones para aumentar los gastos de los comités de Inteligencia y Administración de la Cámara.

La resolución presupuestaria no se convierte en ley ni requiere la firma del presidente. Su aprobación establece las instrucciones para que los comités comiencen a redactar el próximo paquete de reconciliación. El comisionado residente continuará evaluando las propuestas específicas a medida que sean presentadas y fiscalizando cualquier impacto sobre Puerto Rico.

title: RELEASE: HOUSE PASSES HILL'S MAIN STREET CAPITAL ACCESS ACT
text:
The U.S. House of Representatives yesterday passed H.R. 6955, Rep. French Hill's (AR-02) Main Street Capital Access Act, by a vote of 270-155-1. As Chairman of the House Financial Services Committee, Rep. Hill led the effort to pass the bill alongside Financial Institutions Subcommittee Chairman Andy Barr (KY-06). The bipartisan bill revitalizes local bank formation and ensures community lenders can focus on serving families, small businesses, and local economies, making life more affordable for Americans and empowering Main Street.

Rep. Hill said, “As a former community banker in central Arkansas, I know how important our Main Street banks are to our local economy. From growing cities like Conway to our smallest rural towns, community banks drive economic growth. Whether a young couple wants to open a coffee shop in downtown Little Rock, a local manufacturer is looking to expand in Jacksonville, or a farmer in White County needs a loan for a new combine, it's our local banks that step up.

“Yet for decades, Washington has forced these local banks to operate under rules written for the nation's largest institutions, stifling local lending, accelerating industry consolidation, and making big banks even bigger. This bill fixes that. It right-sizes regulations for our community banks, freeing them up to lend so entrepreneurs can invest, businesses can grow, and families can build wealth. It will spur new bank formation, increase competition, remove barriers to lending, and benefit communities from coast to coast."

title: RELEASE: HILL VOTES TO STRENGTHEN AMERICA'S MILITARY READINESS
text:
Today, Rep. French Hill (AR-02) voted for H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2027, which passed the House by a vote of 216-212. The bipartisan bill supports our military personnel and families, strengthens our national defense, modernizes our military capabilities, and includes four amendments introduced by or cosponsored by Rep. Hill, three of which will directly benefit the Arkansas National Guard.

Rep. Hill said, “It is critical that Beijing, Moscow, and Tehran have no doubt about the lethality of the United States military or our ability to project power anywhere in the world. This NDAA advances peace through strength by restocking critical munitions, strengthening defense supply chains, and accelerating weapons production. It also raises pay for the men and women who wear the uniform and invests in the technologies that will define tomorrow's battlefield. It redirects billions from lower-priority spending to our warfighting mission and eliminates distractions that have nothing to do with winning wars. This bill ensures our military has what it needs to deter our adversaries and defend American interests around the globe.

“I am also proud that several of my priorities were included in this year’s NDAA to support our Guardsmen in central Arkansas.”

Background:

H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, authorizes $1.15 trillion in national defense discretionary spending. The bill revitalizes the defense industrial base, revives the organic industrial base, provides the certainty industry needs to expand capacity, and grows and develops the defense industrial workforce. It advances small business participation in the defense industrial base, secures our supply chains, furthers acquisition reform, and improves collaboration on data rights. The legislation also raises pay for all servicemembers by 5 to 7 percent and improves housing, education, and childcare access for military families.

title: Hinson Votes to Ban Congressional Stock Trading & Implement Voter ID
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Ashley Hinson (IA-02) voted in support of two commonsense reforms to strengthen Americans' confidence in our federal government: requiring photo ID to vote in federal elections and banning Members of Congress from publicly trading individual stocks.

"Iowans expect their elected officials to serve the people, not themselves, and they deserve elections they can trust. If you need an ID to board a plane and buy a six pack, you should need an ID to vote – this is a commonsense election integrity policy that the vast majority of Americans support.

"Additionally, Members of Congress should not use insider information to trade stocks. I voluntarily sold my publicly traded individual stocks shortly after taking office and believe every Member of Congress should be held to that same standard. Voter ID and ensuring Members of Congress aren’t trading public stocks are commonsense reforms that restore confidence in our institutions. There’s still way more work to do to clean up Washington, but this is an important step in the right direction to restore integrity to public service and our nation’s elections.” — Congresswoman Ashley Hinson

Background:

The Voter ID Act requires voters to present a photo ID when voting in federal elections, while ensuring eligible voters can still cast a provisional ballot if they forget their ID.

The Stop Insider Trading Act prohibits Members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing publicly traded stocks. It also increases transparency by requiring advance public notice before covered stock sales and establishes penalties for violations.

Hinson does not trade stocks. She and her husband sold their publicly traded individual stocks shortly after she began serving in Congress.

title: Hoyer Statement on FY2027 National Defense Authorization Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement after the House passed the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2027:

“Hardworking civilian federal employees at the Defense Department are no less deserving of an annual raise than their compatriots in uniform. Oftentimes, civilian and military personnel work side by side doing similar work at the Pentagon and on bases across the world, yet this National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) gives military personnel as much as a 7% raise while leaving civilian employees behind. That disparity is wrong, and it’s why I did not support this bill, which balloons the defense budget by over 28% and will cost more than a trillion dollars but cannot find enough funds to ensure parity in raises between civilian and military personnel. The Trump Administration should be ashamed of itself for proposing this pay disparity, and I urge the Senate to address it and insist on parity. All those who serve ought to receive our gratitude and respect.”

title: Hudson Votes for Fort Bragg Wins in Annual Defense Bill, Secures Over $140 Million for North Carolina
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Richard Hudson (NC-09) voted to pass the Fiscal Year 2027 (FY 27) National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), which delivers significant new funding and protections for Fort Bragg and defense projects across North Carolina. Hudson delivered more than $140 million through the bill, ranking near the top of all House members in total authorizations awarded, while helping secure additional investments for Fort Bragg.

"As Fort Bragg’s Congressman, making sure our soldiers and their families have the resources they need is a top priority," said Rep. Hudson. "Through this year's NDAA, I was able to deliver critical funding for facility maintenance upgrades, promote statewide innovation, and enhance the safety and wellbeing of my soldiers and their families at Fort Bragg. I urge my colleagues in the Senate to take up this legislation quickly and look forward to the President signing this bill into law."

The $140.4 million in project authorizations Hudson secured includes:

$65,000,000 for a Special Operations Forces Ammunition Supply Point at Fort Bragg

$6,400,000 for a Special Operations Forces Battalion Operations Facility at Fort Bragg

$69,000,000 for an Aircraft Maintenance Hangar Addition and Alteration for the North Carolina National Guard

The FY27 NDAA also includes the following priorities that Congressman Hudson helped secure for Fort Bragg and North Carolina:

$50,000,000 for Special Operations Forces Operational Training Facility at Fort Bragg

$31,000,000 for Aircraft Maintenance Hangar at Fort Bragg

$10,500,000 for Microgrid and Backup Power Reauthorization at Fort Bragg

$2,500,000 for defense innovation in North Carolina

Language to protect the identities of special operators and other personnel involved in critical military activities by making the unauthorized disclosure of their identities subject to prison time and fines

Language to support military construction and facilities maintenance at Fort Bragg

Language to support North Carolina companies working in the defense space

The FY27 NDAA authorizes $1.15 trillion in national defense discretionary spending to revitalize our defense industrial base, strengthen American deterrence, and support our service members. This legislation presents a conservative approach to national security, explicitly focusing on policy changes and the authorization of funds that will enhance military lethality, restore fiscal discipline, and support President Trump’s "Peace through Strength” agenda. By securing supply chains, expanding domestic manufacturing, developing our skilled technical workforce, and reducing procurement costs, the FY27 NDAA is focused on “Rebuilding the Arsenal of Freedom” to restore the American defense industrial base to global preeminence.

title: 70+ House Democrats Demand NPS Address Multimillion-Dollar Grant Backlog Delaying Trail Maintenance, Wildfire Prevention, and Critical Projects
text:
Washington, D.C. – House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-CA) and Congressman Don Beyer (D-VA) led 70 House Democrats in demanding that the National Park Service (NPS) immediately address its reported backlog of 1,400 grant approvals, which has delayed more than $360 million in funding for critical projects that keep national parks safe and accessible to the American public.

In a letter addressed to NPS Acting Director Jessica Bowron, the lawmakers warned that the grant approval bottleneck is delaying routine but essential work, including trail maintenance, wildfire mitigation, and other projects during peak visitation and wildfire risk season.

The Members pointed to a new grant process that requires two political appointees to manually review every grant and agreement over $50,000. Members stressed this review process has resulted in more than $360 million in delayed NPS funding. The Members also noted this process bears similarities to review processes that were rolled back at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) after findings they violated federal court orders.

“These delays are unacceptable. Nonprofit programs to clear trails have been delayed at the critical start of peak visitation season, while prescribed burns and other wildfire control programs are at risk of the same fate during peak wildfire risk season,” wrote the Members. “Choosing to make such grants contingent on review by unqualified political appointees puts the safety of the American people at risk, whether they choose to visit our national parks or simply live near them.”

The letter is signed by Representatives Becca Balint (D-VT), Nanette Barragán (D-CA), Wesley Bell (D-MO), Julia Brownley (D-CA), Salud Carbajal (D-CA), Andre Carson (D-IN), Ed Case (D-HI), Joaquin Castro (D-TX), Judy Chu (D-CA), Steve Cohen (D-TN), Herb Conaway (D-NJ), Jim Costa (D-CA), Angie Craig (D-MN), Jasmine Crockett (D-TX), Madeleine Dean (D-PA), Diana DeGette (D-CO), Mark DeSaulnier (D-CA), Sarah Elfreth (D-MD), Laura Friedman (D-CA), John Garamendi (D-CA), Robert Garcia (D-CA), Jesus “Chuy” Garcia (D-IL), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX), Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ), Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ), Pablo Hernández (D-PR), Steven Horsford (D-NV), Sara Jacobs (D-CA), Hank Johnson (D-GA), Julie Johnson (D-TX), Robin Kelly (D-IL), Ro Khanna (D-CA), Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), Ted Lieu (D-CA), Zoe Lofgren (D-CA), Stephen Lynch (D-MA), Seth Magaziner (D-RI), April McClain Delaney (D-MD), Jennifer McClellan (D-VA), Betty McCollum (D-MN), Dave Min (D-CA), Kelly Morrison (D-MN), Jared Moskowitz (D-FL), Seth Moulton (D-MA), Joe Neguse (D-CO), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), Frank Pallone (D-NJ), Nancy Pelosi (D-CA), Scott Peters (D-CA), Mike Quigley (D-IL), Raul Ruiz (D-CA), Mary Gay Scanlon (D-PA), Jan Schakowsky (D-IL), Kim Schrier (D-WA), Bobby Scott (D-VA), Lateefah Simon (D-CA), Melanie Stansbury (D-NM), Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA), Mark Takano (D-CA), Mike Thompson (D-CA), Dina Titus (D-NV), Rashida Tlaib (D-MI), Jill Tokuda (D-HI), Paul Tonko (D-NY), Juan Vargas (D-CA), Gabe Vasquez (D-NM), Nydia Velázquez (D-NY), Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL), Bonnie Watson Coleman (D-NJ), George Whitesides (D-CA).

Full text of the letter follows below, and a signed copy is available here.

***

Dear Acting Director Bowron:

We write to request that National Park Service (NPS) immediately adjust its grant review process to address a reported 1,400 active grant approval backlog. According to public reports, NPS currently requires all grants and cooperative agreements valued at $50,000 or above to be manually reviewed by two political appointees. Those appointees serve at the department level and are not solely tasked with ensuring timely review of NPS grants and agreements, creating a severe bottleneck that has left more than $360 million in NPS funding behind schedule.

These delays are unacceptable. Nonprofit programs to clear trails have been delayed at the critical start of peak visitation season, while prescribed burns and other wildfire control programs are at risk of the same fate during peak wildfire risk season. Ensuring that those and similarly routine programs are funded during critical times of the year should be part of the regular operation of the National Park System. Choosing to make such grants contingent on review by unqualified political appointees puts the safety of the American people at risk, whether they choose to visit our national parks or simply live near them.

During the first Trump administration, the Government Accountability Office investigated DOI’s grants review process that was also run through an unqualified political appointee. They found that the appointee, an old football friend of then-Secretary of the Interior, Ryan Zinke, centralized grants review for all bureaus at DOI. He “closely scrutinized applications focused on certain topics, such as endangered species and climate change, rather than considering the merit of individual grant applications or program policy factors, such as leveraging resources between similar programs.” When he rejected grants, he kept his decisions off the books, hiding the truth from the American people and suggesting willful malfeasance.

The NPS decision bears striking similarities to other manual review processes that have been rolled back at the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA). Last year, DHS instituted a manual grant review process that – similar to the reported NPS process – required additional review above a value threshold. That process delayed more than 1,000 FEMA contracts, grants, and disaster assistance awards. The delays came amid historic flooding in Texas and in the heart of the Atlantic hurricane season. After repeated findings that the process violated federal court orders, the DHS approval system was rolled back earlier this year.

We urge you to do the same at NPS, while also providing a full accounting of the current NPS grant and cooperative agreement backlog. It is a core responsibility of NPS to ensure that routine, lifesaving programs are funded on time and in full, while offering full transparency on the status of any delayed approvals. We request an update on NPS’ plans for its grant review process, as well as a full list of all grants and cooperative agreements in the approval backlog, no later than July 28, 2026.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Ronny Jackson Speaks on the House Floor in Support of FY27 NDAA
text:
WASHINGTON — Yesterday, Representative Ronny Jackson (TX-13) spoke on the floor of the U.S. House of Representatives in support of the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027.

Click here or above to watch Rep. Jackson’s full remarks.

Rep. Ronny Jackson’s remarks as prepared:

I rise today in support of H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027.

I would like to begin by thanking Chairman Rogers for his leadership in bringing the NDAA to the Floor for the 66th consecutive year.

As Chairman of the Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee, I am especially proud that this bill provides our Special Operations Forces, the Defense Intelligence Enterprise, and the security cooperation enterprise with the tools and resources needed to execute the Department’s National Defense Strategy and counter an ever-changing threat landscape.

Crucially, this bill provides an approximately $1.3 billion increase in funding for U.S. Special Operations Command to address critical needs within its programs. This bill also invests in a wide range of intelligence capabilities and disciplines, including my provision to develop a periodic ISR strategy to make better threat-informed decisions.

We continue to ask more of our Special Operations Forces, uniform and civilian intelligence professionals, and security cooperation personnel, and this year’s NDAA ensures they are equipped with the capabilities necessary to maintain their operational edge over any adversary.

I’d also like to highlight that this bill advances critical reforms to revitalize our Defense Industrial Base, restore lethality, and deliver on President Trump’s “Peace Through Strength” agenda. I was proud to lead efforts to support test and training space for unmanned aerial systems, incorporate foreign military sales demand into domestic industrial base assessments, and to officially restore the name of the Department of War.

Finally, I want to recognize the tremendous work of the professional staff from the ISO Subcommittee and my personal office staff to develop this bill.

Mr. Speaker, I urge my colleagues to support H.R. 8800, and with that, I yield back.

title: Jayapal, Dingell, CPC Members Host Universal Healthcare Shadow Hearing
text:
Full video of the hearing can be watched HERE.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — The Congressional Progressive Caucus (CPC) today hosted a shadow hearing on Medicare for All, led by Chair Emerita Congresswoman Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) and Congresswoman Debbie Dingell (MI-06), the lead sponsors of the Medicare for All Act of 2025. During the hearing, CPC Members and witnesses discussed the transformative change that Medicare for All would bring to the U.S. healthcare system.

“We do not suffer from scarcity in this country; we suffer from greed — the greed of Big Insurance corporations that rake in billions while denying care, and the greed of Big Pharma that jacks up prices, leaving people with impossible choices,” said Jayapal. “Medicare for All is the path to fix the broken healthcare system that has let corporate interests determine who lives and dies. The reality is that Medicare for All is the only solution that guarantees care for everyone in the U.S., brings down costs for working families, and generates savings for the country. I thank everyone who came out for this hearing today to continue building the momentum for this necessary legislation.”

“Healthcare is a human right, not a privilege reserved for those who can afford it. Millions of American families still face impossible choices between filling a prescription and putting food on the table, or being forced into financial ruin over an unexpected medical diagnosis. I am proud to continue this fight alongside Congresswoman Jayapal,” said Congresswoman Dingell.

“Passing Medicare for All is one of the top priorities of the Progressive Caucus,” said Congressional Progressive Caucus Chair Greg Casar (TX-35). “It is the best way to make sure no American ever has to check their bank account before going to the doctor. I am grateful to Rep. Jayapal and Rep. Dingell for leading this fight and for convening today’s important hearing.”

“As a long-practicing gynecologic oncologist, I’ve seen how broken our health care system truly is—and how Republican cuts have made this ongoing crisis even worse. Returning to the pre-Trump status quo will not solve our deep-rooted problems, and neither will reforms that enrich corporate profiteers in return for a sliver of what my patients truly need. Only Medicare for All would cut out profit-hungry investors, eliminate dangerous conflicts of interest, and empower me and my colleagues to provide high-quality, trustworthy care for every single person living in the U.S,” said Dr. Diljeet Singh, President, Physicians for a National Health Program.

“As bedside nurses, we see every day how Americans are suffering needlessly from a for-profit health care system,” said Jamie Brown, RN and NNU President. “The failure to pass visionary policies that center care and health for working people, in order to favor billionaire and corporate profit, is a stain on our country’s morality. Elected officials can do what is both necessary and popular and deliver to their constituents a guaranteed health care system with Medicare for All.”

“As today’s hearing showed, now is the time to fight for Medicare for All. Americans are struggling every day to get the care they need and Republicans in Congress and the White House are making it worse through draconian cuts to the Affordable Care Act and Medicaid. Medicare for All would finally guarantee that everyone in the U.S. can get the care they need when they need it. We call on all members of Congress to join Reps. Jayapal and Dingell and the rapidly growing movement fighting for the passage of Medicare for All,” said Eagan Kemp, Health Care Policy Advocate, Public Citizen.

“I came to DC from Chicago to testify in Congress because I’m furious that in the richest country in the history of the world, we have to constantly fight the system for dignified health care that we all deserve. Meanwhile, giant corporations like UnitedHealth Care play life and death games and get rich off our suffering. I’m furious that every day members of the community and people across the country are forced to choose between paying for medicine or buying food,” said Chela Garcia, member-leader and volunteer organizer, the People’s Lobby Education Institute & People’s Action Institute. “Medicare for All is not a radical dream — it is a moral baseline.”

Medicare for All would expand the Medicare program to provide comprehensive health care to every American with no premiums, no co-payments, and no deductibles. It would also expand Medicare to include dental, hearing, and vision care, and it would give every American the freedom to choose their doctors without interference from insurance companies. The Congressional Budget Office has estimated that Medicare for All would save the American healthcare system $650 billion a year. Researchers at Yale University have also estimated that the legislation would save 68,000 lives a year.

The hearing was also attended by Representatives Alma S. Adams (NC-12), Donald Beyer (VA-08), Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Judy Chu (CA-28), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), Jesús “Chuy” García (IL-04), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Grace Meng (NY-06), Emily Randall (WA-06), Melanie Stansbury (NM-01), Mark Takano (CA-39), and Rashida Tlaib (MI-12).
