title: Magaziner Secures Wins for Rhode Island in Annual Defense Bill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Seth Magaziner (RI-02) applauded the House passage of several key priorities he helped secure in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) to strengthen Rhode Island’s submarine industry and workforce and to support mental health programs for servicemembers transitioning to veteran status.

"I am proud to have secured key provisions in this year's defense bill that strengthen Rhode Island's submarine industry and workforce, support our maritime security, and improve support for veterans transitioning to civilian life," said Magaziner.

Magaziner secured passage of his amendment reaffirming Congress's commitment to the AUKUS security partnership between the United States, Australia, and the United Kingdom, which supports deterrence in the Indo-Pacific by helping Australia acquire submarines built and maintained with U.S. and U.K. support, and calls for greater investment in the United States' submarine industrial base to support the partnership. Rep. Magaziner also co-sponsored a bipartisan amendment that was adopted, led by Rep. Joe Courtney (CT-02), increasing the sale of Virginia-class submarines to Australia from two to three. Rhode Island workers manufacture Virginia-class submarines at Quonset Point.

Magaziner also partnered with Rep. Zach Nunn (IA-03) to pass their bipartisan amendment requiring a study of methods to better provide mental health resources to servicemembers during the first year after leaving the military. The study will identify opportunities to strengthen suicide prevention programs for transitioning servicemembers and veterans.

This effort builds on the bipartisan Daniel J. Harvey and Adam Lambert Improving Servicemember Transition to Reduce Veteran Suicide Act, introduced by Magaziner and Nunn. The legislation is named in part for Johnston native Lance Cpl. Daniel J. Harvey Jr., who tragically died by suicide within a year of leaving the Marine Corps.

Although Magaziner successfully secured House passage of these priorities benefiting Rhode Island's defense industry and veterans, he ultimately voted against final House-passage of the NDAA because of partisan anti-LGBTQ and voter suppression measures that were included.

title: Malliotakis Applauds Ways & Means Committee Passage of Her Bill to Stop Foreign Influence in American Elections
text:
(WASHINGTON, DC) — Congresswoman Nicole Malliotakis (NY-11) is celebrating the passage of her legislation,H.R. 9771, the Stopping Foreign Influence in Elections Act of 2026, out of the House Ways and Means Committee. This legislation would establish safeguards to ensure foreign nationals cannot contribute to tax-exempt organizations that ultimately use those funds to influence American elections by ensuring foreign nationals cannot simply route foreign money to a 501(c)(4), either directly or indirectly through a charitable 501(c)(3), that then makes unlimited contributions to political committees, including Super PACs.

The Stopping Foreign Influence in Elections Act prohibits larger tax-exempt organizations from making contributions to political committees for two years after receiving a gift or contribution from a foreign national. The restriction applies to organizations with at least $200,000 in annual gross receipts or $500,000 in assets. The legislation also establishes escalating penalties for tax-exempt organizations that violate this prohibition by accepting contributions from foreign nationals and then donating to political committees. After a third violation, the organization's tax-exempt status is suspended for a two-year period beginning on the date the prohibited contribution is made.

For example, Swiss billionaire Hansjörg Wyss has reportedly used his U.S.-based tax-exempt organizations to contribute to other organizations that then directed significant sums into the political process. Mr. Wyss operates both a 501(c)(3) organization, the Wyss Foundation, and a 501(c)(4) organization, the Berger Action Fund. According to reporting by The New York Times, cited in a House Ways and Means Committee report, the Berger Action Fund contributed more than $135 million to the Sixteen Thirty Fund over a four-year period. In 2020 alone, the Sixteen Thirty Fund contributed $63 million to Super PACs supporting President Biden and other Democrats.

“I am pleased that my legislation, the Stopping Foreign Influence in Elections Act, passed out of the Ways and Means Committee, and I thank Chairman Smith for his support for this important bill. Foreign nationals should not be able to use tax-exempt organizations as a vehicle to influence American elections. Our elections should be decided by American voters—not by foreign billionaires who can move money through a network of nonprofit organizations and political groups to influence our democratic process,” said Rep. Nicole Malliotakis. “This legislation is a critical step toward preventing foreign money from entering our political process through nonprofit organizations and restoring Americans’ confidence in our elections.”

“Americans ought to be able to have confidence that foreign nationals are not funding political parties and candidates in our elections,” said Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith. “Representative Malliotakis has offered a straightforward solution that will keep tax-exempt organizations in this country from becoming money laundering schemes for political influence coming in from abroad. Thanks to her leadership, Congress can close a loophole in our tax laws to make sure that wealthy foreign donors are not having any say in our political discourse.”

title: Congressman Harris Applauds House Passage of Budget Reconciliation 3.0 Framework
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) issued the following statement in response to the House passage of H. Con. Res. 113, a resolution that begins the budget reconciliation 3.0 process.

“Since the beginning of this Congress, House Republicans have been united in getting our country back on track and delivering on the mandate entrusted to us by the American people,” said Congressman Harris. “Without a single Democrat vote, we have used the budget reconciliation process to pass the largest tax cut in American history and fund the law enforcement agencies tasked with securing our border.

“By passing this third budget resolution, we are taking the first step toward ensuring the brave men and women who defend our nation have the tools, resources, and support they need to carry out their missions and keep the American people safe. We are also advancing commonsense measures to restore confidence in our elections and provide assistance to the farmers and producers who sustain our nation’s food supply.

“The Senate should now build on the work of the House without delay so we can advance these critical priorities and seize the opportunity of our Republican majority to make our nation stronger, safer, and more prosperous.”

BACKGROUND:

H. Con. Res. 113 unlocks the budget reconciliation process, allowing Congress to advance legislation with a simple majority vote in the Senate and avoid the 60-vote threshold.

The resolution contains budgetary instructions totaling up to $95 billion across four House committees.

It instructs the House Armed Services Committee to develop legislation providing up to $60 billion for military operations, readiness, service member pay, and critical munitions investments. It also instructs the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence to develop legislation providing up to $13 billion for intelligence-related activities that protect the nation.

The resolution instructs the Committee on House Administration to develop legislation providing up to $10 billion to advance election integrity measures included in the SAVE America Act.

It also instructs the House Committee on Agriculture, on which Congressman Harris serves, to develop legislation providing up to $12 billion in economic assistance for American farmers and food producers and help ensure the nation’s food supply remains secure and affordable.

During consideration of H. Con. Res. 113, 211 House Democrats voted against moving forward with the framework to strengthen our national defense, secure our elections, and support American farmers.

title: Congressman Harris Applauds House Passage of FY27 National Defense Authorization Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Mark Harris (NC-08) applauded House passage of H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, the annual legislation that sets national defense policy and authorizes funding for the United States military.

“The first and foremost responsibility of the federal government is to provide for the common defense and protect the American people,” said Congressman Harris. “At a time of growing threats from China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and terrorist organizations around the world, America must have the military strength and industrial capacity necessary to deter our adversaries and defend our interests at home and abroad.

“This legislation rebuilds America’s arsenal by strengthening domestic manufacturing, securing critical supply chains, replenishing our munitions stockpiles, and investing in the capabilities our warfighters need to carry out their missions. It also supports our service members and their families through increased military pay and important investments in housing, education, and childcare.

“For decades, the National Defense Authorization Act has reflected a bipartisan commitment to putting our national security first. Today’s vote reflects the unfortunate political reality that 205 House Democrats opposed the annual defense legislation necessary to maintain America’s military readiness and protect our nation.”

BACKGROUND:

H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027, authorizes $1.15 trillion for national defense priorities to strengthen America’s military, revitalize the defense industrial base, support service members and their families, and advance President Trump’s Peace Through Strength agenda.

The FY27 NDAA focuses on rebuilding America’s Arsenal of Freedom by expanding domestic defense production, strengthening critical supply chains, reducing barriers for small businesses and innovative companies, and creating new opportunities for America’s skilled technical workforce.

The legislation authorizes multiyear procurement for critical weapons systems, accelerates the production and acquisition of munitions, and invests in the ships, aircraft, combat vehicles, missile defenses, autonomous systems, hypersonic weapons, and other capabilities American warfighters need to deter and defeat emerging threats.

The bill supports service members and military families by authorizing a 5% to 7% pay increase, investing more than $1.8 billion in military barracks and family housing, expanding access to on-base childcare, and increasing the Family Separation Allowance for deployed service members.

The FY27 NDAA strengthens American deterrence against China, Russia, Iran, North Korea, and terrorist organizations while supporting key allies and partners around the world. It also continues military support for law enforcement operations along the southern and maritime borders.

The legislation cuts nearly $30 billion in wasteful spending, including funding for inefficient and underperforming programs, while advancing reforms intended to reduce fraudulent payments and move the Department of War toward a full and clean audit.

Under the rule governing consideration of H.R. 8800, the text of the House-passed SAVE America Act will be added to the legislation before it is transmitted to the Senate. The SAVE America Act requires proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections and establishes voter identification requirements for federal elections.

H.R. 8800 passed the House by a vote of 216-212.

title: Rep. McBride, Senators Coons, Blunt Rochester Celebrate Nearly $1 Million Investment in Affordable Housing for Kent and Sussex Counties
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, U.S. Representative Sarah McBride and U.S. Senators Chris Coons and Lisa Blunt Rochester (all D-Del.) celebrated a $940,000 U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Rural Development grant for Milford Housing Development Corporation. The funding, awarded through the USDA Rural Development’s 523 Mutual Self-Help Housing Technical Assistance Grant program, will support the construction of two dozen new, energy-efficient homes for low-income families in rural communities throughout Sussex and Kent Counties. Over a two-year period, the grant will help Milford Housing Development Corporation continue its self-help housing program and expand access to affordable homeownership in rural Delaware.

“Every Delaware family deserves access to a safe, stable, and affordable place to call home,” said U.S. Representative Sarah McBride. “This grant will help Milford Housing Development Corporation build 24 energy-efficient homes, continuing their work to make homeownership more attainable for working families in Kent and Sussex counties. I am proud to join Senators Coons and Blunt Rochester in celebrating this investment to expand affordable housing opportunities in rural Delaware, and I look forward to continuing to work together to bring down housing costs across our state.”

“Affordable housing is about more than building homes, it’s about creating opportunity. Thanks to this $940,000 investment, the Milford Housing Development Corporation will help more Delaware families realize the dream of homeownership in our rural communities,” said U.S. Senator Chris Coons. “I’m grateful for USDA’s continued partnership in creating safe, decent, affordable housing that strengthens neighborhoods, lowers energy costs, and builds a brighter future for the next generation.”

“Good homes are the foundation of strong communities — because without a roof over your head, the promise of good-paying jobs and high-quality education are out of reach,” said U.S. Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester. “That is why I’m so excited for communities in Kent and Sussex Counties, who will be receiving two dozen new energy-efficient homes through this grant. Alongside Senator Coons and Representative McBride, I am committed to making housing more attainable and expanding opportunity for all Delawareans.”

“We are incredibly grateful to continue our long-standing partnership with USDA Rural Development in expanding access to affordable homeownership opportunities” said David Moore President/CEO Milford Housing Development Corporation. “Through the Self-Help Housing Program, individuals and families who might otherwise be unable to achieve homeownership invest their own "sweat equity" by working together to build not only their own homes, but also those of their neighbors. This unique approach fosters a strong sense of community while making homeownership attainable and affordable. Along the way, participants gain valuable construction experience, financial education, and the confidence needed to become successful, informed homeowners, creating lasting benefits for themselves, their families, and their communities”.

This $940,000 investment represents an ongoing effort by Coons, Blunt Rochester, and McBride to secure more federal investment to address the cost-of-living crisis and to expand access to affordable housing opportunities, especially in rural and low-income areas across Delaware. Recently, the congressional delegation voted to pass the bipartisan 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act in their respective chambers – the first comprehensive housing affordability bill to pass Congress in three decades. The congressional delegation will continue working to secure resources that increase housing supply, strengthen rural communities, and help more families achieve the stability of homeownership.

title: Reps. McBride, Hill Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Expand Employment Opportunities for People with Disabilities
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Ahead of the 36th anniversary of the landmark Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), U.S. Representatives Sarah McBride (D-Del.) and French Hill (R-Ark.) introduced the bipartisan Disabled Access Credit Modernization Act, legislation to help small businesses — in Delaware and across the country — hire people with disabilities, expanding access to employment, the dignity of work, and that opportunity to fully participate in our economy.

“Every Delawarean deserves the opportunity to work and build a career with dignity, including people with disabilities,” said Rep. McBride. “By equipping small businesses with the support they need to provide reasonable accommodations, this bipartisan legislation will empower more Delawareans with disabilities to enter and thrive in the workforce. Thirty-six years after the ADA became law, we have an opportunity to build on its legacy by ensuring all Delawareans can fully participate in our economy and our communities. I’m glad to be partnering with Rep. Hill on this important legislation.”

Under the ADA, employers with 15 or more employees are required to provide “reasonable accommodations” to employees with disabilities. However, the cost of providing workplace accommodations — while essential to ADA compliance — is not explicitly covered under the Disabled Access Credit (DAC) in its current form.

The Disabled Access Credit Modernization Act would address this oversight by adding "reasonable accommodations" as a qualifying expenditure under the DAC. By expanding eligible expenses, the legislation would help small businesses provide the accommodations employees need while expanding access to employment opportunities for people with disabilities.

“When the ADA was passed, accessibility was largely limited to physical access, like ramps, elevators, and bathrooms,” said Rep. Hill. “Today, as more disabled Americans look to join the workforce, it means screen readers, adaptive software, and modified equipment that let people thrive in a modern workplace. This practical bill simply brings the spirit of the original law into the modern era. It gives employers a real incentive to provide the accommodations that matter today and gives more disabled Americans a genuine path into the workforce. I am pleased to work with Representative McBride on this commonsense solution."

In Delaware, small businesses make up 98% of the state’s total businesses and are the backbone of the First State’s economy. However, providing workplace accommodations comes with added costs, and many small businesses currently lack the resources to pay additional expenses. At a time when small business owners are already navigating workforce shortages and the impact of the administration’s tariff policies, this legislation would help make providing “reasonable accommodations” more affordable for small businesses while expanding employment opportunities for workers with disabilities.

McBride and Hill’s legislation is endorsed by a broad coalition, including The Arc, American Network of Community Options and Resources (ANCOR), Autism Speaks, CEO Commission for Disability Employment, Chimes International, Easterseals National, Melwood Inc., National Down Syndrome Society, SourceAmerica, Community Legal Aid Society of Delaware, Delaware Developmental Disabilities Council, Easterseals Delaware, and the University of Delaware Center for Disability Studies.

"People with disabilities represent one of our nation's most underutilized talent pools, but for too long outdated policies have stood in the way of opportunity. That is why Melwood is proud to support the Disabled Access Credit Modernization Act, which offers a meaningful step toward removing barriers to employment and creating more inclusive workplaces that benefit all of us. By helping small businesses provide reasonable accommodations, this legislation opens more pathways to economic independence for people with disabilities who are ready to work, contribute, and strengthen our nation's workforce," said Larysa Kautz, President & CEO of Melwood.

“ANCOR is grateful to Representatives McBride and Hill for their leadership in expanding the Disabled Access Credit (DAC), which supports small businesses to employ people with disabilities. By increasing the eligible expenses covered by this important tax credit, more small businesses will have the resources they need to make their workplaces accessible and meet the needs of today’s workforce. Especially on the eve of the 36th anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act becoming law, ANCOR is proud to support this important legislation that seeks to ensure the promise of community inclusion is a reality for workers with disabilities,” said Barbara Merrill, ANCOR’s chief executive officer.

“Reasonable accommodations are more than an accessibility tool; they are a talent strategy. They unlock the full potential of the talent employers hire by ensuring employees have the resources they need to perform at their highest potential. The Disabled Access Credit Modernization Act helps small businesses invest in that talent, strengthening businesses, expanding employment opportunities, and growing our economy,” said Rob Snow, Executive Director of the CEO Commission for Disability Employment.

“Too many people with disabilities who are ready and eager to work still face unnecessary barriers getting or keeping a job if they need reasonable accommodations for their disability, such as modified workplace rules, special technology, interpretation, or other supports. While making accessibility changes like these can greatly benefit both employers and workers, the upfront cost can be challenging for small businesses operating on tight margins to stay afloat. Modifying the Disabled Access Credit to include reasonable accommodations would be a significant extension of the benefits of the program for businesses and workers alike, helping employers attract and retain talented employees and expanding employment opportunities for people with disabilities. In addition to helping to pay for necessary accommodations, giving businesses the flexibility to go beyond the minimum requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act is a practical, commonsense way to support successful outcomes for employers and workers and strengthen our economy by ensuring that workers with disabilities are fully included in the workforce. We thank Representative McBride for introducing this important legislation and for her leadership in advancing policies that promote equal opportunity for people with disabilities,” said Marissa Band, Esq., Project Director of Disability Rights Delaware of Community Legal Aid Society, Inc.

“At Easterseals, we believe meaningful employment is key to independence, dignity, and community inclusion for people with disabilities. Small businesses have long been valued partners in creating employment opportunities, and this legislation will give them additional support to hire and accommodate even more talented individuals with disabilities. By expanding tax incentives for workplace accommodations, this bill removes barriers for employers while advancing a more inclusive workforce. We proudly support its passage," said Ken Sklenar, President/CEO of Easterseals Delaware & Maryland’s Eastern Shore.

“People with disabilities have the right to work, contribute, and succeed. Accessibility and reasonable accommodations are not expenses; they are investments in people, businesses, and stronger communities. The Disabled Access Credit Modernization Act recognizes that by helping small businesses offset the cost of accommodations, it will remove barriers to employment, expand opportunity, and strengthen our workforce. The Delaware Developmental Disabilities Council Thanks Representative McBride for introducing this important legislation and for her continued leadership in advancing policies that promote equal opportunity, economic inclusion, and a workforce where everyone has the chance to thrive,” said Maitri Campbell, Chair of Delaware Developmental Disabilities Council Policy and Law Committee.

“Good workers don’t come with a uniform set of needs. Rep. McBride’s bill, the Disabled Access Credit Modernization Act, expands the disability access credit for small businesses and makes it possible for them to provide accommodations—a modified telephone, alternate access to a computer, or a tablet that converts speech into text—that result in an employee who thrives and returns long-lasting benefits to the business,” said Dr. Beth Mineo, Director for the University of Delaware’s Center for Disabilities Studies.

“Autistic people can and want to work, yet too many face employment barriers that don’t reflect their skills, talents or desire to contribute. The Disabled Access Credit Modernization Act would help small businesses provide reasonable accommodations that can make workplaces more accessible and inclusive for employees with autism, while also helping employers meet their workforce needs. We are grateful to Representatives Sarah McBride and French Hill for championing this bipartisan legislation and moving us closer to the promise of the ADA: equal opportunity for all,” said Keith Wargo, President and CEO of Autism Speaks.

The full text of the bill can be found here.

title: VIDEO RELEASE: Rep. McBride Presses U.N. Ambassador on Trump's Broken Promise to End the War in Ukraine
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Today, U.S. Representative Sarah McBride (D-Del.), a member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, questioned U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz about President Trump's repeated promise to end Russia's unjustified war in Ukraine on day one, highlighting how the administration has failed to deliver and pressing him on U.S. votes at the United Nations.

Rep. McBride's full exchange with Ambassador Waltz can be found here. Key excerpts are below.

On Trump’s Broken Promise to End the War in Ukraine:

Rep. McBride: “We are well over four years into a war Vladimir Putin started by invading Ukraine. And during the course of the 2024 election, the president promised at least 53 times to end the war on or before day one. On January 20th, 2025 as the sun set and the president pardoned more than a thousand January 6th insurrectionists, when the sun set, the president failed to deliver on his promise that he would end the war between Russia and Ukraine. Ambassador Waltz, why did the president fail to deliver on his promise to end the war?

Ambassador Waltz: “The president is doing everything he can to end the war. To date, neither Vladimir Putin with Russia or President Zelensky has seen fit to enter into the final deal. However, the president has put significant pressure – this administration – by sanctioning Lukoil, by sanctioning Rosneft, and is doing everything he can to stop the killing.”

Rep. McBride: “So I guess we're in agreement 538 days into the administration that the president has not delivered on his promise that he made at least 53 times during the course of the campaign to end the war on day one.”

Ambassador Waltz: “The president has found, despite incredible efforts from him and his team, to be a very frustrating effort…”

Rep. McBride: “Well, maybe he shouldn't have made those grandiose promises.”

On U.S. Votes at the United Nations on Ukraine:

Rep. McBride: “…On February 24th, a month after the president failed to deliver on that promise, U.S. representatives at the United Nations voted no on a resolution advancing a comprehensive, just, and lasting peace in Ukraine. Earlier today, Representative Titus brought up this vote, and you incorrectly stated that the U.S. abstained from voting on the February 2025 resolution. That's not true. The U.S. voted no alongside Russia, Belarus, and North Korea. Really, really great company. Would you like to correct the record that the U.S. indeed voted no?”

Ambassador Waltz: “I understood and perhaps I misunderstood her to be talking about a General Assembly resolution just this past summer where the United States abstained.”

Rep. McBride: “My understanding, the words that she specifically used…was referring to the February 2025 resolution, which the U.S. did indeed vote no on. Then on February 18, 2026, over a year after President Trump failed to deliver on his promise to end the war on day one, U.S. representation at the U.N. under your leadership refused to vote on a resolution expressing support for lasting peace in Ukraine. Ambassador, I'm curious why the United States is scared to call out and stand up to Vladimir Putin at the United Nations?”

Ambassador Waltz: “The United States, under this administration, has put more pressure on Russia to come to the table. Their economy is reflective of that, and this administration sanctioned their top two oil producers and the dark fleet, not the last administration.”

Rep. McBride: “Well, they're now getting more money because of the Strait of Hormuz, but that's neither here nor there. Why did the United States vote no and refuse to vote to denounce Vladimir Putin's illegal war in Ukraine?”

Ambassador Waltz: “I'll have to come back to record that prior vote was obviously before my time, so I'll have to look at the wording and the resolution…”

Rep. McBride: “Apparently, the only other countries that objected to any of the specific language in that resolution, at least in February 2025, were Belarus, North Korea, and Russia. So not very good company…”

Ambassador Waltz: “My memory is we were shifting to a more neutral mediator position. As we try to end this war unlike the ill-defined victory so-called of the last one…”

Rep. McBride: “A strategy that did not work, has not worked…”

Ambassador Waltz: “Has worked a lot better than the last administration's.”

Rep. McBride: “Well, I don't think that that's true.”

Ambassador Waltz: “They’re at least in the room talking which is the art of diplomacy.”

Rep. McBride: “There was a photo op in Alaska that the president gave Vladimir Putin, and I think these votes…no votes, only send a message to Vladimir Putin that we are not there.”

###

title: McCaul Applauds House Passage of FY27 NDAA, Inclusion of Provisions He Championed
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Michael McCaul (R-Texas) — chairman emeritus of the House Homeland Security and Foreign Affairs Committees — released the following statement after voting for the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA).

“Providing for our national defense is a fundamental duty of Congress — one that has never been more vital as America’s adversaries seek to undermine global stability. I proudly voted for this year’s NDAA to support our brave servicemembers and their families, equip our warfighters with the tools they need to win, and deter our adversaries’ aggression around the world.” -Rep. McCaul

McCaul championed several of the provisions in this year’s NDAA, including a provision he led with Rep. Morgan Luttrell (R-Texas) to expand access to neuroplastogen treatments like ibogaine for our nation's veterans.

"Our servicemembers and special operators risk everything to defend our freedoms, and far too many return home with deep wounds — both seen and unseen. Mounting evidence suggests that, where traditional medicine has failed, ibogaine can offer a durable path to recovery for these heroes. Our nation's veterans answered the call for us, and I'm proud to help deliver for them.” -Rep. McCaul

Click here to watch McCauls House floor speech, urging his colleagues to support the provision.

McCaul also joined Rep. Jodey Arrington (R-Texas) in securing a provision to establish a pilot program providing anonymous counseling for Special Operations Forces.

"Our special operators face unimaginable danger and trauma. They should not be penalized for seeking the help they need to continue doing their high-risk jobs successfully. I’m proud to support this provision to help increase their access to mental health resources as they continue to fight and risk their lives for this nation.” -Rep. McCaul

Additionally, he helped secure two provisions to strengthen the AUKUS partnership:

A provision he led with Bill Huizenga (R-Mich.) enabling the U.S., U.K., and Australia to share long-range missile and drone technology more freely.

A provision he led with Joe Courtney (D-Conn.) and others to allow the U.S. to transfer an additional Virginia-class submarine to Australia, bringing the total number of submarines allowed under the AUKUS agreement to three.

“The Chinese Communist Party is working at lightning speed to advance its military apparatus — and it does not play fair. We must empower the United States and its allies to meet that generational challenge head-on by removing burdensome red tape that slows down the transfer of critical military technologies. This important provision will strengthen crucial partnerships like the AUKUS defense pact and deter the CCP’s malign activity in the Indo-Pacific and beyond.” -Rep. McCaul

McCaul also successfully included his provision to accelerate the development and testing of unmanned systems and platforms to counter them.

title: McCaul Discusses Iran Conflict at Hearing with Ambassador Waltz
text:
WASHINGTON – At today's House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing, Congressman Michael McCaul (R-Texas) — chairman emeritus of the committee — discussed the need to unleash the full power of the U.S. military in Iran and asked U.S. Ambassador to the United Nations Mike Waltz about the role the UN is playing in the conflict.

Image

Click to watch

Full Exchange:

McCaul: Thank you, Mr. Chairman and Ambassador Waltz. It's great to see you again. It's great to see a friend and a former colleague in this position. And let me just say, I think you're doing an outstanding job.

Reforming the United Nations is quite a daunting task. Ambassador Bartos, you mentioned your wife questioning your sanity in taking on the job, but I commend you for it.

I want to follow up with Iran. You know, since 1979, a dark veil of terror has reigned over the Middle East. This, in my judgment, was a reckoning that was eventually going to happen. It was unavoidable with this regime, as long as the regime is in power. I commend this president for being the first president to take on this regime and Iran on its path to a nuclear bomb.

Negotiating in the past hasn't worked.

I have to be honest with you, ambassador. I'm not sanguine about the current negotiations. I understand we have to give that a chance and give peace a chance. We have to try to negotiate, but I do think that as Reagan said, peace through strength [is crucial, and] as the Powell Doctrine [states:] either you go all in to win, or you get the hell out of there.

Right now, they're reconstituting their centrifuges in underground storage facilities. Then their launch pads are still striking.

It is my sincere hope, and it's not your responsibility, but that the president unleashes our Department of War on Iran. I know that's what is happening now to take out the launchpads, to take out the IRGC, to let Mossad and Israel do its job because I think as long as this regime's in power, we're going to continue to have this problem.

And Russia providing targeting information is absolutely unacceptable from my point of view, and I think from the United States' point of view.

I'm really pleased to see the White House join with Lindsey Graham. As I went to Ukraine, his last wishes were [for] his Russian sanctions bill to pass.

I will be introducing that in the [House of Representatives] ... I want to thank the White House for its work there because nothing will end that war sooner than passing that sanctions bill. It's a path to peace, not a path to war.

My question to you [is regarding] the Straits of Hormuz. We're a net gain [energy] producer. We don't really even have to rely on this. We are doing this to the benefit of our European allies.

... I applaud the president as well for getting the Gulf States involved to help finance this operation because it's in their best interest to open up these straits. I think it's a very doable thing if we unleash our military and allow them to do what they do best.

Sir, and you know the military better than I do; they're fully capable of accomplishing this mission. I know that's not the hat you wear today, but I'd like for you to comment on the overall status of the straits. ... I think the Gulf States are stepping up. What role, if any, is the United Nations and Security Council playing in this?

Waltz: Well, thank you. And just to set the table for the answer, I want to answer that very specifically, you're absolutely right. Iran has been at war with the United States since 1979. [Iran has] killed thousands of my fellow servicemen in Iraq, in Lebanon, in the Gulf, literally all over the world, in addition to its plots here in the United States to kill the president of the United States and members of his cabinet.

Yet, Iran is in the worst place, is in the weakest place it has been through a combination of both military and diplomacy in its war against the United States. In Lebanon, you have the Lebanese government — you had the president here yesterday and today — you have Lebanon negotiating with Israel for the first time. You have the Assad regime gone and probably the most hope in Syria that we've seen in a generation. You just had the Iraqi president here in Texas, signing deals with American oil and gas companies.

And the Iranian regime is literally cratering economically, militarily, and at war, frankly, with its own people in addition to the region.

To your point on the Straits of Hormuz, Secretary Bessent just said yesterday, China, the main buyer of Iranian illegal oil, has cut its purchases by half and nobody else wants to buy it. The blockade is absolutely working. And then on the UN, look, we've had Iran absolutely diplomatically isolated.

We may not pay a lot of attention to what happens in the UN Security Council here in our media, but I can tell you around the rest of the world, they are glued to every word. It's the only forum Iran really has on the global stage. And 140 countries have sided with us and condemned their attacks on civilian shipping, the mines that they're putting in international waterways, and their violations of international law across the board. Keeping them diplomatically isolated is my job.

And as the ranking member mentioned, we also have sanctions authority. The snapback sanctions that were lifted under the JCPOA are now back in place, and the rest of the world has joined us in that economic isolation.

title: McCaul Urges Colleagues To Support NDAA Amendment Increasing Veterans' Access to Ibogaine
text:
Amendment is led by former Navy SEAL Morgan Luttrell (R-Texas), with whom McCaul has worked extensively to champion this issue

WASHINGTON – Today, House Foreign Affairs Committee Chairman Emeritus Michael McCaul (R-Texas) took to the House floor to urge his colleagues to pass an NDAA amendment he has championed alongside its author, Morgan Luttrell (R-Texas), to increase veterans' access to neuroplastogen treatments like ibogaine.

Image

Click to watch

Full Remarks:

Thank you, Mr. Speaker, and thank you, Mr. Chairman, for your great work on this National Defense Authorization Bill. As always, you've delivered.

Mr. Speaker, every day our nation loses 17 veterans to suicide. These are men and women who survived combat, but then lost to a quiet and longer war against the invisible wounds that they carried with them.

Since the disastrous withdrawal from Afghanistan, many of them are asking, "Was it worth it?" Well, we're providing a solution to that problem here today.

And I want to thank my colleague, Mr. Luttrell, for his service as a Navy SEAL, and also for introducing this amendment to increase veterans' access to ibogaine.

I know personally how much this means to our nation's heroes, because I've talked to them — the Special Operators Association, to people, veterans across this nation who are clamoring for a solution to their problem. And we have one.

They should not have to travel to Mexico to receive this treatment. Countless vets have told me that they were going to give this one shot before they committed suicide. They went down, they experienced ibogaine, and they came back cured.

Stanford University did a study on 30 veterans with TBI and PTSD ... [in which] MRI brain scans [demonstrated] that this medicine actually regenerated brain tissue and helped them get over their addiction to opioids and resolve their PTSD and TBI.

This needs to be available in the United States of America now, in clinical trials to our veterans. My home state of Texas passed legislation to provide clinical trials to veterans for ibogaine.

I want to thank my former Governor Rick Perry and Mr. Bryan Hubbard, [CEO of] Americans for Ibogaine, for leading this effort. I want to thank Morgan Luttrell and Marcus, his brother — ... we all know his Lone Survivor story. Ibogaine saved their lives. And we've heard the testimony from them about the effectiveness of this medicine.

It is time, Mr. Speaker, to make this medicine available to our veterans here in the United States, at our VA clinics across the nation. And this amendment — and I want to thank the chairman for supporting it — will take us to that point where we can now save their lives, where they don't have to worry about suicide, they don't have to be on 30 medications, for God's sake, to treat their addiction, to treat their PTSD, when we know we have a medicine that works. The evidence is there, the data is there, the Stanford study is there, to save their lives.

So I urge my colleagues to vote for this measure. Again, I want to thank all my colleagues, including the chairman, Morgan Luttrell. I want to thank the Energy and Commerce Committee for their work to bring all this to the floor, not only today, but in the future, with future legislation.

And I want to thank the heroes, those who have served this country in harm's way, those who have put their lives at risk, who are suffering from these diseases today. We owe it to them to pass this legislation. And with that, Mr. Speaker, I yield back.

title: McClellan Statement on House Passage of the FY27 National Defense Authorization Act
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) issued the following statement on House passage of H.R. 8800, the National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27 NDAA):

“The NDAA has traditionally passed on a bipartisan basis to bolster our national security, international diplomacy and global leadership. These goals, however, cannot come at the expense of the essential domestic services used by millions across our country. While I support military modernization and quality of life improvements for our servicemembers and their families, I cannot support a bill that massively expands our military’s budget as millions of Americans lose their access to health care, food assistance and other vital programs.

“As America faces a cost-of-living crisis across the board and our constituents find it increasingly difficult to afford day-to-day life, this bill authorizes $1.15 trillion in discretionary spending for the Department of Defense, National Nuclear Security Agency and other programs. This comes at a time when people face impossible decisions between putting food on the table, paying for their rent or mortgage, keeping their health insurance and more. Republicans’ attempt to increase military funding by more than $250 billion compared to the previous fiscal year also comes amidst a war of choice in Iran that seemingly has no clear goal or exit strategy. As the American people pay the price at the gas pump and beyond and our servicemembers are asked to make the ultimate sacrifice, a vote to funnel more money into a war that has cost at least 17 U.S. servicemembers’ lives and billions of dollars would only rubberstamp the President’s agenda to keep us in a forever war with no end in sight.

“All of this would be bad enough on its own. But House Republicans have further tainted the NDAA with poison pills that play more into culture wars and partisan games than investment in our military and those who serve. They pushed for Section 219 to expand and merge American and Israeli defense capabilities, a provision that undermines our sovereignty and lacks any form of oversight. They continued their assault on the LGBTQ+ community by targeting trans servicemembers. And they attached the NDAA to the SAVE America Act, a modern-day poll tax that only makes it harder for people to vote.

“Virginia is home to multiple military installations and thousands of servicemembers, all of whom work to make our nation safer and more secure. I have always fought for and will continue to support policies to improve their quality of life — but we can and must do more to protect those already left vulnerable by Republicans’ devastating cuts. I urge the Senate to curb the excesses of House Republicans and the Trump Administration and will continue to fight for the people they continually neglect.”

title: Congressman McCormick Helps Pass FY27 NDAA, Secures Key Georgia Priorities
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Rich McCormick (GA-07) voted in favor of the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 (H.R. 8800), passing it out of the House of Representatives this afternoon in a XXX-XXX vote.

The annual defense bill authorizes funding, policies, and priorities to strengthen America’s military, support servicemembers and their families, and ensure the United States remains prepared to deter and defeat emerging threats. The package strengthens America’s military by rebuilding the defense industrial base, restoring military readiness, supporting emerging technologies, improving servicemembers’ quality of life, cutting nearly $30 billion in Pentagon waste, and providing a 5–7 percent pay raise for servicemembers.

“Passing the NDAA reaffirms America’s firm commitment to peace through strength," said Congressman McCormick. “As a Marine and physician, I know our military’s greatest advantage is the strength of the men and women who wear the uniform, backed by the strongest defense industrial base in the world. This bill rebuilds America’s military by investing in readiness, modernizing our defense manufacturing base, improving quality of life for our servicemembers, and ensuring we can outpace adversaries like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea. I’m especially proud that several priorities I fought for were included to strengthen Georgia’s defense industry, improve the health and readiness of our warfighters, and support our national security.”

The FY27 NDAA authorizes $1.15 trillion for America’s national defense and includes many provisions championed by Congressman McCormick, including:

Establishment of a site-neutral payments policy for TRICARE in order to reduce growth in military healthcare spending without limiting patients’ access to care providers.

Funding authorizations and legislative language supporting Georgia National Guard’s top procurement priorities, the University of North Georgia’s participation in the Senior Military College Cyber Institute program, and the defense industrial base in Georgia’s 7th District and across our state.

Codification of military human performance programs by directing the Marine Corps, Navy, Army, Air Force, and Space Force to develop comprehensive strategies that enhance the health, well-being, and readiness of servicemembers.

A stronger military medicine supply chain through new measures to reduce reliance on prescription drugs sourced from foreign adversaries and encourage the procurement of American-made pharmaceuticals.

title: McIver Attends Hearing Rife with Republican Lies About Delaney Hall
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman LaMonica McIver (NJ-10) attended a hearing held by the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Oversight, titled "False Narratives Surrounding Conditions at the Delaney Hall ICE Detention Center." The hearing was chaired by Republican extremist Rep. Jeff Van Drew (NJ-02). Delaney Hall sits in the heart of McIver’s district and is the center of the federal case the Trump Department of Justice (DOJ) is bringing against her for conducting legally authorized oversight.

Claims from Van Drew and Republicans that Democrats like McIver are pushing a false narrative about the facility completely ignore firsthand accounts from lawmakers, advocates, and detainees who describe unsafe conditions, rotten food, and brutality from guards at the facility.

“If Jeff Van Drew’s lips are moving, he’s lying. Delaney Hall is in my district; I have visited many times, often in response to reports of neglect and abuse. What I have seen there is cruel and inhumane. It’s disgusting that Van Drew was trying to paper over the facts in his hearing,” said McIver. “Everything about Delaney makes it obvious: for the Trump administration, the cruelty is the point. They are holding high schoolers, pregnant women, and sick folks in conditions so brutal that even detainees with legal status elect to self-deport simply to escape the suffering. The lies in today’s hearing from Republicans with no firsthand knowledge were as outrageous as they were offensive—just a clown car of Trump loyalists putting political allegiance over the lives and dignity of human beings."

The first ICE detention center opened in Trump’s second term, Delaney Hall’s corporate owners lacked municipal permits and refused inspections. In December of 2025, a detainee died in ICE custody after being held at Delaney for less than 24 hours, calling into question the conditions in the facility. In recent months, detainees went on a hunger strike to protest conditions they described as torture. Denial of basic medical care, unsafe drinking water, violence, rotten food, and indefinite detention without due process were all reported by detainees at Delaney Hall. Earlier this year, McIver was able to facilitate the release of a high schooler who was unjustly detained at the facility.

Consistently a flashpoint for controversy, Delaney Hall is at the center of the Trump administration’s baseless case against McIver, stemming from an oversight visit she conducted in May, 2025. The oversight visit, which should have been routine, was escalated by ICE, leading to the Trump administration bringing federal charges against McIver. She now faces up to 17 years in prison. The case is ongoing.

title: House Foreign Affairs Ranking Member Meeks Delivers Opening Remarks at Committee Hearing with Ambassador Waltz
text:
Washington, DC -- Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, today delivered the following opening remarks, as prepared, at a full committee hearing entitled "United Nations Accountability and Reform: Advancing an America First Foreign Policy Through Strategic Diplomacy and Burden Sharing.”

Members heard testimony from Mike Waltz, Representative of the United States to the United Nations, and Jeff Bartos, Representative of the United States to the United Nations for UN Management and Reform.

"Thank you, Chairman Mast, for calling this hearing. Welcome, Ambassador Waltz and Ambassador Bartos.

"In the eight decades since the United Nations’ formation, the United States has benefitted greatly from the multilateral world order it helped create and led. Of course, the United Nations has never been perfect. It is a complex institution, often slow-moving and imperfect. Congress has often demanded that it pursue reforms so the UN can better deliver on its mandate to promote international peace, security, and human rights.

"That’s because leaders from both parties have understood a fundamental truth: American security and prosperity are strongest when we shape the international system – not when we abandon it.

"The UN is not simply a forum for speeches. It is where sanctions are negotiated, peacekeeping missions are authorized, and pandemic responses are coordinated. It’s where refugees get help, international law is made, and coalitions are built to meet the shared challenges of our time. No nation, not even the United States, can solve these problems alone.

"American leadership at the UN has always been about ensuring those debates and decisions serve the American people. That is why I am deeply concerned by this administration’s 'burn it down' approach. Rather than strengthen America’s leadership within the UN system, this administration has surrendered it.

"Since January 2025 the Trump administration has withdrawn the U.S. from 69 UN agencies or entities, including the very UN body responsible for protecting children from sexual violence in war. It has pulled the U.S. out of UNESCO, withdrawn from the Human Rights Council, and abandoned the World Health Organization—even during an active Ebola outbreak, when it refused to let Americans exposed to the virus come home.

"This is not reform. This is retreat.

"And it has failed to pay our UN dues—funds Congress already appropriated—forcing severe budget cuts across UN entities, even ones the administration claims to champion.

"We hear the argument that this is tough love, necessary to drive UN reforms. But you cannot reform an institution by starving it. You can only weaken it, and hand the advantage to those who wish us harm. And the administration’s approach is also confounding our allies and accelerating our decline on the world stage.

"Mr. Waltz, you are leading this American retreat. Under your tenure, China is now paying to keep the lights on at the UN headquarters in New York, using our own austerity to cast itself as the responsible steward of the very system we built. The PRC has even offered to host UN bodies in Beijing and Hong Kong.

"Under your ambassadorship, the U.S. is siding with Russia and other adversaries on key votes, opposing UN resolutions on human rights, women, children, and refugees -- not on principle, but over culture war objections to a single word: 'gender.'

"And, Ambassador Waltz, you have called Trump the 'peace president,' yet this administration has gutted UN peacekeeping and replaced experienced negotiators with real estate developers. You have been a defender of President Trump’s war-of-choice in Iran, a war that has cost the lives of 18 U.S. servicemembers and achieved none of our core objectives. This includes one of my constituents, Sgt. Angel Rampersad from Ozone Park, who was killed this past Friday. You’ve done so with indifference to the costs this war has imposed on American families, or its upending of the global economy and our bilateral relationships.

"I cannot imagine a worse time to cede U.S. influence at the U.N than during a war Trump started with Iran—and still cannot end. The threats Iran poses can only be addressed diplomatically, multilaterally, with our allies and partners. Instead, this administration treats our friends like enemies—absurd new tariffs against Canada being the latest example. Countries around the world are asking—if this is how the U.S. acts toward its closest friends, how will it treat us? That doesn’t make them yield to our demands—it drives them to look elsewhere for leadership, and China is happy to provide it.

"The administration casts its foreign policies as putting 'America First.' In reality, it is America alone, a foreign policy of chaos and corruption that puts Americans last.

"Let me be frank: Ambassador Waltz, you moved into this job at the UN after a debacle in which you and other senior administration officials texted classified war plans to a journalist. 16 months later, nothing has changed. The incompetence continues—and it is Americans who keep paying the price.

"I welcome the witnesses’ testimony on the matters before us today. Thank you."

###

title: House Foreign Affairs Ranking Member Meeks Delivers Remarks During Floor Debate on Iran War Powers Resolution
text:
Washington, DC – Representative Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, today delivered the following remarks on the floor, as prepared, during debate on H.Con.Res.89, the War Powers Resolution that directs the President to remove U.S. Armed Forces from hostilities against Iran.

"Before I get into my primary remarks, I want to take a moment to recognize Sergeant Angel Rampersad from Ozone Park in my district, who was killed on July 17 in Jordan. My thoughts and prayers are with her family and loved ones and all those families of the service members lost in this war.

"M. Speaker, I rise today in strong support of Rep. Jayapal’s Iran War Powers Resolution.

"Let me be clear: This body has already spoken. The War Powers Resolution passed with bipartisan support in the House and the Senate. The Trump administration was required to end its hostilities against Iran. It has not.

"A dual-chamber concurrent resolution has never been struck down by the courts, certainly not in the war powers context. Any claim otherwise is simply wrong.

"I will also be introducing legislation that would require the speaker to bring suit against the administration, to force it to abide by Congress’ vote on the War Powers Resolution.

"But we are here because the administration broke the law. Three more U.S. servicemembers having made the ultimate sacrifice for an illegal, unauthorized war that the American people don’t want. This administration has never sought an Authorization for Use of Military Force from Congress. And most Republicans in this chamber continue to enable it.

"As I have said before on this floor: this war has achieved none of our core objectives, and more bombing will not change the reality on the ground. with respect to Iran's nuclear program, its hardline regime, its closure of the Strait of Hormuz, or any of its malign practices.

"Addressing those threats requires diplomacy not more war, and diplomacy must be led by seasoned diplomats and nonproliferation experts, not real estate developers.

"We need our European allies, our Gulf partners, and yes, even our adversaries back at the table. Because bombing without strategy isn’t a foreign policy, it’s a tantrum by a president who cannot clean up the mess he’s made.

"Make no mistake: the president's tantrum is why gas is back over $4 a gallon, and it will keep climbing now that the Houthis have threatened their own blockade of the Red Sea.

"That tantrum is why American troops are under fire. It's why our munitions stockpiles are being drained. And it's why we are teetering on the edge of the forever war we warned this would become.

"To my Republican colleagues, this war is indefensible and deep down many of you know it. Uphold your oath. Uphold the Constitution. Stand with us and make clear, once again, that this president cannot wage war without our consent.

"And if you still believe this war should continue, fine. Then vote in support of this measure and demand the administration come to Congress and follow the Constitution, as the law requires. I yield back."

title: Chairman Meuser Releases Staff Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee Report on Fraud and Scams, Holds Fireside Chat with Chairman Hill
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Dan Meuser (PA-09), Chairman of the House Financial Services Subcommittee on Oversight and Investigations, released a final staff report on financial fraud and scams facing the American public. The report, entitled Fighting Back: A Policy Framework for Combating the Rise of Financial Fraud & Scams, represents the culmination of an exhaustive investigation into the growing threat of financial fraud, convening roundtables with banks, social media firms, telecom companies, the DOJ, FBI, Attorneys General, the Fed, and other federal agencies to discuss the scope of the problem and identify policy solutions to address scams.

The report outlines the findings of this yearlong investigation, identifies the biggest threats to consumers, highlights emerging strategies and technologies fraudsters are using, and provides recommendations to strengthen protections by improving coordination between law enforcement, regulators, and the private sector.

“Financial fraud and scams affect everyone. From veterans and small businesses to seniors and young people, everyone is vulnerable to financial fraud and scams,” said Subcommittee Chair Meuser. “As Chair of the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee, I’ve made it a top priority to address the threat of financial fraud and scams and provide the public the tools they need to secure their finances. However, as schemes become more elaborate and are increasingly perpetrated by transnational criminal organizations, our committee and other stakeholders must remain vigilant and address threats as they evolve. Over the past several months, I have convened roundtables with stakeholders, including banks, social media firms, telecom companies, the DOJ, FBI, Attorneys General, the Fed, State Department, FTC, and FCC to identify problems and determine solutions. This report highlights the need for an all-of-ecosystem approach to include a coordinated government response. I want to thank Chairman Hill for letting the Oversight & Investigations Subcommittee spearhead this Committee-wide initiative and look forward to advocating for implementation of the report’s recommendations.”

“Financial fraud is one of the fastest-growing threats facing Americans, costing consumers and financial institutions billions of dollars each year,” said Financial Services Committee Chairman Hill. “As fraudsters become more sophisticated, we must ensure law enforcement, regulators, and financial institutions have the tools they need to stay ahead of these evolving threats. I thank Subcommittee Chairman Meuser for his leadership on this issue and his work to develop a framework that strengthens fraud prevention, improves coordination among law enforcement, regulators, and the private sector, and better protects Americans’ hard-earned money.”

Following the release of the report, Chairman Meuser and Financial Services Committee Chairman French Hill (AR-02) held a Fireside chat detailing the Subcommittee’s findings and recommendations for combating the rise of financial fraud and scams. The fireside chat was moderated by Leigh Ann Caldwell of Puck News. Watch the fireside chat here.

Background:

The Scale of the Threat

Financial fraud is now the largest category of property crime in America by dollar value. In 2025, Americans reported nearly $15.9 billion in losses to fraud and scams — and because most victims never come forward, the true cost is estimated at roughly $196 billion. An estimated 15 million Americans were scammed last year alone, a 24% increase over 2024. The harm reaches every generation: losses among seniors have quadrupled since 2020, from $600 million to $2.4 billion, with the average senior victim losing roughly $83,000 — yet younger Americans are twice as likely to be scammed as the elderly.

A Year-Long Investigation

This report is the culmination of a year-long inquiry led by the Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee. The Committee convened four hearings across its subcommittees and three roundtables — bringing industry, law enforcement, and financial regulators to the same table — to examine how modern scams operate and what it will take to stop them. The same priorities surfaced again and again: stronger consumer education, deliberate friction to slow suspicious transactions, greater cross-industry data sharing, more aggressive prosecution, and a coordinated, cross-agency response.

A Whole-of-Ecosystem Response

The report documents a fight now underway on every front. Across the private sector, banks, payment networks, social media platforms, and telecom carriers are deploying new detection tools, filtering billions of scam calls and texts, dismantling fraudulent networks, and expanding financial-literacy campaigns. Federal regulators like Secretary Bessent, Vice Chair Bowman, Chairman Ferguson of the FTC, and Chairman Carr of the FCC are answering with sanctions and financial monitoring, reforms to modernize outdated payment rules, oversea call screening, and simpler ways for victims to report. In coordination with international partners, U.S. authorities have disrupted overseas scam compounds and secured arrests abroad.

The Trump Administration has mobilized the federal government behind the effort. A series of executive orders has moved to close information silos, screen federal payments for fraud, modernize outdated payment systems, and directly target the transnational criminal organizations behind these schemes. Vice President J.D. Vance chairs the Task Force to Eliminate Fraud, a whole-of-government initiative to root out fraud across federal benefit programs. And the Department of Justice’s Scam Center Strike Force, led by U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro, has carried the fight overseas — dismantling Southeast Asian scam operations and recovering more than $800 million in stolen funds for victims.

Yet despite this progress, the threat keeps growing — the central reason the report calls for a unified, all-of-ecosystem strategy that brings these efforts together.

title: Meuser Advocates for Increasing Access to Capital for Main Street Businesses
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Yesterday, Congressman Dan Meuser (PA-09) spoke on the House floor ahead of passage of H.R. 6955, the Main Street Capital Access Act, legislation that would reduce regulations on community banks to make it easier for these institutions to lend to families and small businesses. The legislation would encourage the creation of new banks by tailoring regulations based on a bank’s size and risk profile to help community banks remain competitive.

The Main Street Capital Access Act, led by House Financial Services Committee Chairman French Hill (AR-02) and Financial Institutions Subcommittee Chairman Andy Barr (KY-06),addresses concerns that current regulations place disproportionate burdens on community banks and credit unions. Despite significant differences in the size of smaller financial institutions, many are still beholden to the same regulations as large financial institutions. This bill seeks to establish a more tailored regulatory framework for community banks and credit unions while preserving the strength of banking sector regulations, rather than relying on a one-size-fits-all approach. By establishing new standards designed for community banks, this legislation will allow smaller operations to compete with the country’s largest financial institutions, improving competition in the financial sector.

“Twenty years ago, community banks financed the majority of America’s home loans. Today, it is less than a third. This bill helps reverse that trend; it lowers capital hurdles so new community banks can form and tailors bank regulations so small and mid-size banks are regulated fairly,” said Congressman Meuser. “These changes will allow community banks and credit unions to extend more mortgages, be more competitive with their small business loans, and improve access to capital for all Americans. This is a housing bill, a small business bill, an affordability bill, and an access to capital bill. This legislation supports community banks and protects Main Streets across the country.”

"As a former community banker, I've seen firsthand how community banks drive Main Street's growth,” said Financial Services Committee Chairman French Hill. “For decades, Washington has forced these institutions to operate under rules built for the largest, most systemically important banks, stifling local lending and accelerating industry consolidation. This bill fixes that. It spurs the formation of new banks, restores common-sense tailoring to bank regulation, and removes barriers that have limited lending in communities across the country. Expanding access to capital means entrepreneurs can invest, businesses can grow, and families can build wealth. I want to thank Subcommittee Chairman Andy Barr for his partnership on this bill, and I look forward to the Senate taking up this important legislation.”

"Community banks are at the heart of Kentucky's economy. They finance our small businesses, stand by our farmers, and help hardworking families buy homes, start businesses, and build a better future,” said Congressman Barr. “House Republicans are delivering on our commitment to strengthen Main Street by cutting red tape, expanding access to capital, and creating an environment where community banks can thrive. I'm grateful to Chairman French Hill for his leadership, and I'm proud the House is advancing this legislation to support the local financial institutions that keep our communities strong."

The Main Street Capital Access Act will establish a three-year phase-in period for capital requirements, allowing new banks time to grow before meeting full regulatory standards. It will also require regulators to provide clear guidelines for new banks, increasing transparency in the chartering and supervisory process.

This legislation will streamline reporting requirements for community and regional banks, reduce compliance costs, allow banks more flexibility to focus on lending, and standardize the bank examination process by promoting more consistent supervisory standards.

The Main Street Capital Access Act passed the House of Representatives by a bipartisan vote of 270 – 155.

title: House Passes the Stop Insider Trading Act

title: Main Street Capital Access Act Passes House with Rep. Kennedy’s support
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – The House passed the Main Street Capital Access (“Main Street”) Act by a vote of 270-155-1. This legislation is co-sponsored by Congressman Mike Kennedy (UT-03), and led by House Committee on Financial Services Chairman French Hill (AR-02) and Subcommittee on Financial Institutions Chair Andy Barr (KY-06).

Rep. Kennedy signed on early as a co-sponsor of the package because of its focus on strengthening community banks: the institutions that power small businesses, farms, and local economies across Utah's 3rd district and throughout the country. The Main Street Act will revitalize local bank formation and ensure that community lenders can focus on serving families and Main Street businesses, helping make life more affordable for Americans.

“The backbone of a free and strong economy is the local business owner,” said Congressman Mike Kennedy. “Supporting Main Street institutions is one of the most effective ways to lower costs and secure long-term stability for American families. I appreciate Chairman Hill for his dedicated leadership on this issue, and am honored to join him in this fight for affordability and economic opportunity.”

"As a former community banker, I've seen firsthand how community banks drive Main Street's growth,” said Chairman French Hill (AR-02). “For decades, Washington has forced these institutions to operate under rules built for the largest, most systemically important banks, stifling local lending and accelerating industry consolidation. This bill fixes that. It spurs the formation of new banks, restores common-sense tailoring to bank regulation, and removes barriers that have limited lending in communities across the country. Expanding access to capital means entrepreneurs can invest, businesses can grow, and families can build wealth. I want to thank Subcommittee Chairman Andy Barr for his partnership on this bill, and I look forward to the Senate taking up this important legislation.”

“Community banks are the backbone of Kentucky’s economy,” said Financial Institutions Subcommittee Chairman Andy Barr (KY-06). “They help our small businesses grow, support our farmers, and give hardworking families a chance to achieve the American Dream. House Republicans are keeping our promise to make that dream more attainable by advancing a regulatory framework that expands access to capital, promotes economic growth, and strengthens Main Street. I’m grateful to Chairman French Hill for his leadership, and I’m proud the House is passing this package to support community banks and the Americans they serve.”

“America cannot succeed if Main Street doesn’t, and for too long, unnecessary barriers have made it harder for small businesses to receive the support they need to thrive,” said Speaker Mike Johnson (LA-04). “The Main Street Capital Access Act offers commonsense solutions by helping local lenders better serve local businesses and the communities that rely on them. I commend Chairman Hill and Rep. Barr for their leadership on this issue and look forward to this important legislation supporting communities across the nation..”

“When community banks thrive, American workers on Main Street thrive. House Republicans are modernizing outdated regulations that have placed costly and unnecessary burdens on community banks and credit unions,” said Majority Leader Scalise (LA-01). “The Main Street Capital Access Act will make it easier for local lenders to serve families and small businesses, and strengthen the communities they serve. I thank Chairman French Hill, Andy Barr, and the entire House Financial Services Committee for advancing this commonsense legislation.”

“It’s time to bring commonsense back to banking, and the Main Street Capital Access Act does just that,” said Majority Whip Tom Emmer (MN-06). “This legislation will right-size federal bank regulations that currently treat local and mid-sized banks the same as the largest banks in the country. By cutting unnecessary red tape and expanding access to funding, we are going to keep community banks strong. We’re also pleased to see the Keeping Deposits Local Act included in this final bill. I want to thank Chairman French Hill and Congressman Andy Barr for their work on this legislation and helping keep community banks competitive.”

“The Main Street Capital Access Act cuts unnecessary red tape, promotes competition, and ensures smaller lenders can spend more time serving their customers instead of satisfying bureaucrats,” said House Republican Conference Chairwoman Lisa McClain (MI-09). “That's exactly the kind of commonsense reform Republicans are fighting for to strengthen Main Street and keep the American Dream within reach.”
