title: Representative Derek Tran Raises Alarm on Human Rights Abuses in Vietnam
text:
Washington, D.C. – In a letter to the Socialist Republic of Vietnam’s Ambassador to the United States, Ambassador Nguyen Quoc Dzung, U.S. Representative Derek Tran (CA-45) once again expressed grave concern about the Vietnamese government’s consistent violation of human rights. Credible evidence has shown that the Vietnamese government has engaged in arbitrary killings, torture, arrests, restrictions on free expression, including arresting journalists, restrictions on religious freedom, and restrictions on workers’ freedom of association.

Read the full letter HERE.

“I urge the Vietnamese government to honor its commitments under international law, not merely in word but in practice. I also strongly encourage open and candid discussions on human rights, which is essential to foster greater stability and progress. U.S.-Vietnam bilateral relationships will be stronger, more reliable, and more productive when the Vietnamese government fully respects the rights and dignities of its own citizens,” wrote Representative Tran.

As the son of Vietnamese refugees and the first Vietnamese American elected to represent the world’s largest Vietnamese diaspora in Congress, Representative Tran is committed to holding the Vietnamese government accountable for human rights abuses. In an April 2026 letter to General Secretary Tô Lâm, Representative Tran demanded to visit prisoners of conscience imprisoned by the Socialist Republic of Vietnam to monitor their well-being. Tran introduced a congressional resolution to formally mark April 30, 2026 as the 51st anniversary of Black April. In April 2025, Congressman Tran held a roundtable with Vietnamese human rights activists and former prisoners of conscience to uplift their firsthand accounts of the oppression they faced at the hands of the Vietnamese government. Tran, a vocal advocate for advancing human rights in Vietnam, co-led H.R. 3122, the bipartisan Vietnam Human Rights Act, to hold Vietnamese communist officials accountable for human rights abuses and establish human rights and fair-trade priorities for U.S.-Vietnam relations. Representative Tran serves as the official sponsor of Le Huu Minh Tuan, a Vietnamese journalist who was wrongfully imprisoned by the communist government, through the Tom Lantos Human Rights Commission’s Defending Freedoms Project and continues to fight for the release of prisoners of conscience around the world.

title: Another Momnibus Bill, Underwood’s Bipartisan NIH IMPROVE Act, Passes House
text:
WASHINGTON – This week, Rep. Lauren Underwood’s bipartisan NIH IMPROVE Act to ensure consistent funding for research on disparities in maternal care and mortality passed the House with unanimous support. The legislation is co-led by Rep. Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA).

The NIH IMPROVE Act is part of the Momnibus, a comprehensive package of 14 pieces of legislation designed to address every clinical and nonclinical driver of our nation’s maternal health crisis.

“80% of maternal deaths are preventable—and the NIH IMPROVE Initiative is a key tool to stop them. I am so pleased that this critical legislation for moms and families has passed the House. The Momnibus continues to make incredible progress, and this leap puts us one step closer to seeing the entire package signed into law,” said Rep. Underwood. “Since 2019, IMPROVE has invested more than $200 million in life-saving research that will help end our nation’s maternal health crisis, which disproportionately impacts Black moms. This bipartisan legislation will advance maternal health research by permanently authorizing funding for this initiative and make sure NIH can continue this critical work.”

In early 2019, Co-Chairs Adams and Underwood met with then-Director Francis Collins of the National Institutes of Health (NIH) to urge the agency to do more to prioritize research that will help solve our maternal health crisis. In response, NIH launched the Implementing a Maternal Health and Pregnancy Outcomes Vision for Everyone (IMPROVE) Initiative later that year. Since then, Rep. Underwood has increased funding for the program five-fold through the appropriations process. For more information and a complete list of awards, click here.

The IMPROVE Initiative supports research to reduce preventable causes of maternal deaths, understand and reduce disparities, and improve health care for women before, during, and after pregnancy. It includes a special emphasis on health disparities and populations that are disproportionately affected, such as racial and ethnic minorities, very young women and women of advanced maternal age, and people with disabilities.

However, this critical research program lacks a sustained funding source, threatening research outcomes and conclusions. The NIH IMPROVE Act would authorize $63.4 million annually for six years to carry out the IMPROVE Initiative and support research on potential causes of maternal mortality and severe morbidity. This funding would be used to target disparities associated with maternal mortality and severe morbidity, reduce preventable causes of maternal deaths, and build an evidence base for improved care and outcomes in underserved maternal care deserts.

title: Congressman Valadao Votes to Strengthen Our Nation’s Defense Capabilities
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman David Valadao (CA-22) released the following statement after voting in support of the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). The NDAA authorizes funding for all discretionary military programs and activities, including personnel, operations, maintenance, procurement, research, and development.

“At a time of growing threats around the world, it’s more important than ever that we provide our servicemembers with the resources they need to keep our country safe,” said Congressman Valadao. “I was proud to support the bipartisan FY27 National Defense Authorization Act because it delivers on our commitment to our men and women in uniform and their families. This bill provides a well-deserved pay raise for our troops, improves military housing, expands access to education, childcare, and healthcare, and strengthens our military readiness by investing in advanced technologies and rebuilding our defense industrial base. Our servicemembers volunteer to defend our freedoms every day, and Congress has a responsibility to ensure they have the support they need to succeed.”

The Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act:

Provides servicemembers with a 5-7% pay raise.

Improves housing, education, and access to childcare for military families.

Expands access to healthcare for servicemembers and their families.

Enhances America’s nuclear deterrent and new nuclear power technologies.

Prioritizes investment in the forces and capabilities needed to counter foreign adversaries like China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea.

Rebuilds depleted stockpiles by providing the authorities and resources required to expedite the production and acquisition of munitions and key warfighting capabilities

title: Rep. Van Epps Secures Major Legislative Victories in FY27 NDAA
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. - Rep. Matt Van Epps (TN-07) released the following statement after four of his amendments were included in the House’s version of the Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA).

HONOR Gold Star Families Act Amendment

Rep. Van Epps stated, “I am proud that core provisions of my HONOR Gold Star Families Act made it into the FY27 NDAA. For the first time in nearly two decades, this legislation updates the military death gratuity by increasing the benefit for survivors from $100,000 to $165,000 and indexing future payments to inflation through a cost-of-living adjustment. This legislation will provide greater financial support to the families of fallen servicemembers who have sacrificed so much.”

Read more here.

Fort Campbell Water and Wastewater Infrastructure Amendment

Rep. Van Epps said, “The fact of the matter is that aging water and wastewater infrastructure has become a growing concern for readiness and quality of life. Much of Fort Campbell’s utility system is more than 60 years old and requires significant maintenance and modernization to reduce the risk of service disruptions. Should a major disruption occur, it could affect everything from mission execution to the health of military families,” he continued.

He said, “Fort Campbell isn’t the only aging base. According to a 2024 CBO report, the four services have $50 billion in deferred maintenance on their bases, with the Army and Navy making up 70 percent of the backlog. Yet, despite the scale of the challenge, the Department of War (DOW) lacks a comprehensive assessment that identifies and prioritizes the military's most critical aging utility systems. That’s why I am introducing this amendment today.

My amendment directs the DOW to evaluate the condition, costs, and operational impacts of these systems across all military installations. Once that is done, the Department of War will rank the highest-risk projects and provide recommendations for prioritizing future investments.”

“This data-driven roadmap for modernization will ensure installations like Fort Campbell receive appropriate attention before infrastructure failures degrade military readiness,” he concluded.

Read more about this amendment here and here.

Report on Defense Prototype Transition to Program of Record Amendment

Rep. Van Epps said, “My amendment to accelerate the delivery of advanced technologies to our warfighters was also included in the NDAA. Too often, groundbreaking research and development from institutions like Vanderbilt University in my district or Tennessee’s Oak Ridge National Lab take far too long to reach the battlefield. It doesn’t help to have the best scientists, engineers, and innovators in the world, only to have their breakthrough discoveries stifled by bureaucracy. My amendment directs the DOW to identify and address the barriers that prevent successful prototype projects from transitioning into procurement and production. My hope is to get the best tools we have into our warfighters' hands faster. I hope this amendment will help do just that.”

Read more about this amendment here.

Defense Contractor Maximum Production Plan Requirement Amendment

Rep. Van Epps stated, “This amendment will help ensure our nation can meet the demands of any future conflict. Recent events in Ukraine and Iran have shown how quickly modern conflicts consume artillery rounds, precision-guided munitions, air defense interceptors, and other critical systems. That is why I introduced an amendment requiring major defense contractors to outline how they would rapidly increase production capacity during a national emergency or major conflict. I am confident that this amendment will identify problematic bottlenecks, whether it be aging infrastructure or workforce shortages, that could keep us from being the most lethal fighting force on the planet.”

title: Rep. Gabe Vasquez Statement Against Insider Trading Loopholes for Members of Congress and the Republican Attack on American Citizens’ Right to Vote
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On July 22, 2026, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) released the following statement on H.R. 7008, a MAGA-led bill that would allow members of Congress to keep the stocks they own and continue to profit off of their positions of power. The bill — which received bipartisan opposition — aims to impose excessive and unworkable voter identification requirements just weeks before the 2026 general election, sowing chaos and exposing voters to privacy risks by requiring them to mail photocopies of their personally identifiable information (such as a driver’s license or Social Security information) if they wish to exercise their right to vote by mail.

“I support banning members of Congress from trading all stocks and profiting off their positions of power, and I support commonsense voter ID requirements to keep our elections secure. Unfortunately, this MAGA-led bill, H.R. 7008, does neither,” said Vasquez. “Under this bill, rich members of Congress are permitted to keep their existing stocks, buy new ones, and continue using their power to get richer through insider trading. I support the Restore Trust in Congress Act and the TRUST in Congress Act, comprehensive bills that truly tackle the corruption problem in D.C. rather than this partisan show-vote that does nothing to actually hold politicians accountable. ”

The loopholes baked into H.R. 7008 allow members of Congress to continue to use their power to amass wealth. Under the bill:

Members would be able to keep stocks they currently own.

Members would be permitted to buy new privately traded stocks.

Members could continue to profit off of financial vehicles like cryptocurrency.

It also does not impose any anti-corruption restrictions on the executive branch.

New voting requirements and concerns under H.R. 7008 include:

A new photo ID requirement for individuals voting in-person in federal elections, eroding voting rights for American citizens who do not have driver’s licenses or passports, as well as those who rely on Tribal IDs that lack expiration dates and photos

New privacy concerns, as Americans who want to exercise their right to vote by mail must now comply with one of three options: 1) mailing a photocopy of their driver’s license or passport alongside their ballot, 2) mailing their Social Security information and a signed affidavit alongside their ballot, or 3) mailing a notarized attestation alongside their ballot — all of which impose new red tape and put personally-identifiable information at risk

“The Native American Rights Fund opposes imposing new voting requirements shortly before an election, especially while Native Americans nationwide still lack equal voter services. This bill is flawed in several ways, including its arbitrary requirement that Tribal IDs include expiration dates,” said the Native American Rights Fund. “Obviously, Native American Tribal membership does not expire, so Tribal IDs often do not include expiration dates. Instead of creating new barriers for Native voters, we urge Congress to address the urgent need for basic voting services in Indian Country.”

“Congress should pass a clean bill to ban insider trading—not use it as a vehicle to add a national voter ID mandate. These are separate issues that deserve separate votes. Tell your Representative to vote NO on this package and demand a clean insider trading bill,” said Keaton Sunchild, Federal Director of Government and Political Relations of Western Native Voice.

Rep. Vasquez supports reasonable, nationwide standards for voter ID that don’t sacrifice American rights and privacy, such as the Freedom to Vote Act. He is a cosponsor of the Restore Trust in Congress Act and the TRUST in Congress Act — two comprehensive, bipartisan bills to crack down on corruption and insider trading by D.C. politicians.

title: Rep. Vasquez Introduces CHILE Act to Support New Mexico’s Specialty Crop Farmers
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On July 22, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) introduced the CHILE Act, a bill to deliver much-needed federal funding to New Mexico’s specialty crop farmers who produce staples like red and green chile, onions, tomatoes, and more. Specifically, the bill would provide $5 billion in direct assistance to specialty crop producers, require the Department of Agriculture to use the Specialty Crop Emergency Assistance Framework when providing direct assistance to specialty crop growers, and clarify that specialty crops include New Mexico’s fruits and vegetables, tree nuts, dried fruits, and nursery crops.

Currently, USDA does not have a disaster assistance plan for specialty crop farmers. This bill would create a dedicated program and protect our farmers from increasingly common extreme weather events and economic instability.

“There’s nothing more New Mexican than our chile, but unfortunately the farmers who grow these beloved crops have been through a lot in recent years, from extreme weather to tariffs to economic turmoil. That’s exactly why I introduced the CHILE Act,” said Vasquez. “This bill would provide $5 billion in much-needed federal funding to our specialty crop growers and create disaster relief programs so they have the stability they need to stay on the land they love and grow the chiles, onions, and tomatoes that New Mexicans love to eat every day.”

This legislation is supported by the New Mexico Chile Association and Western Growers Association.

"The New Mexico Farm & Livestock Bureau appreciates the continued efforts of our congressional delegation and federal leaders to engage with the needs of New Mexico agriculture. We welcome the introduction of the CHILE Act of 2026 as an important conversation about strengthening support for specialty crop producers," said Josh Wood, Coordinator of Government Affairs for the New Mexico Farm & Livestock Bureau. "New Mexico’s chile industry plays a vital role in our state’s economy and agricultural heritage, and we look forward to working with policymakers to ensure producers have access to practical, effective tools that help them navigate future challenges."

This legislation builds on Rep. Vasquez’s long record of fighting for farmers and delivering real wins for New Mexico agriculture:

Rep. Vasquez secured several bipartisan winsin the process of passing this year’s Farm Bill through the House, including preventing the imposition of new red tape that would hinder growers’ access to the Specialty Crop Block Grant program.

Rep. Vasquez has held the USDA accountable countless times, including introducing his Honor Farmer Contracts Act, which ensures the USDA pays farmers what they’re owed.

He’s taken concerns directly from New Mexico’s farmers and ranchers to Washington and turned them into action through his Agriculture Advisory Group.

In January, Rep. Vasquez introduced the Farm and Family Relief Act to help farmers recover from chaos caused by the Administration’s reckless tariff policy.

title: Rep. Vasquez Votes to Expand Access to Capital for New Mexico Small Businesses and Strengthen Community Banks
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – On July 21, 2026, U.S. Representative Gabe Vasquez (NM-02) voted in favor of the Main Street Capital Access Act, bipartisan legislation to strengthen community banks, expand access to credit for small businesses in places like New Mexico, and support economic growth in overlooked rural communities.

“Small businesses are the heart of our economy in New Mexico, but too many entrepreneurs in small and rural communities are overlooked by Wall Street and struggle to get the financing they need to grow,” said Rep. Vasquez. “Community banks understand our communities because they live and work alongside the families and businesses they serve. They know our local small business owners personally, and they know what makes for a smart investment in communities like ours. This legislation gives local banks the tools to better compete with Wall Street institutions and megabanks while helping more small businesses, farmers, and families access the capital they need to succeed and grow our state’s economy.”

The Main Street Capital Access Act updates federal banking regulations for community banks, easing unnecessary burdens on smaller financial institutions while maintaining oversight of the banking system. The legislation also includes provisions to prevent the nation's largest banks from gaining an unfair advantage through acquisitions of failing institutions.

Specific measures in the bill include, among others:

Tailors banking regulations to the class and categories of each bank, reducing unnecessary red tape for smaller community banks so they can spend more time lending to local families and businesses instead of complying with one-size-fits-all rules.

Reduces unnecessary barriers for new and rural community banks by gradually phasing in capital requirements and adjusting the Community Bank Leverage Ratio (CBLR), allowing smaller banks to make more loans and invest in the communities they serve.

Creates a more balanced bank rating process, helping well-managed community banks to continue supporting local customers and businesses.

Directs the Federal Reserve to review its discount window — a critical tool used to support liquidity of financial institutions — to identify ways to better support community banks during times of financial stress.

Community banks play a critical role across New Mexico, particularly in rural communities where they often serve as the primary source of financing for local businesses, agricultural producers, and first-time homebuyers. By expanding lending capacity and modernizing outdated regulations, the bill is designed to increase investment in Main Street businesses and local economies.

Rep. Vasquez has consistently supported policies that strengthen small businesses, expand economic opportunity, and ensure rural communities have the resources they need to thrive:

Introduced the Honor and Hire Veteran Act, which would increase tax credits for businesses that hire veterans.

Boosted federal funding for small businesses by securing $500,000 to help upgrade 200 local businesses’ storefronts and surrounding infrastructure in the South Valley — improving safety, helping advertising efforts, and creating better spaces for customers, investors, and workers alike.

Introduced the Economic Opportunity for Border Communities Act, which would direct the Department of Commerce to develop a national strategy for strengthening economies along the U.S.-Mexico Border. This bill is supported by the Bipartisan Southwest Caucus and Border Industrial Association.

title: Vindman-Led Bill to Protect Americans and Combat Deadly Nitazenes Passes Out of Committee
text:
In August 2025, Vindman Introduced the First-Ever Bill in Congress to Combat the Alarming Rise of Nitazenes

WASHINGTON, D.C. – A bipartisan bill led by U.S. Representatives Eugene Vindman (D-Va.-07) and Bob Latta (R-Ohio-05) to crack down on deadly synthetic opioids and keep communities safe yesterday advanced out of the House Energy and Commerce Committee.

“Nitazenes are the next fentanyl — stronger, deadlier, and already threatening communities across the country. I’m proud to see my bipartisan bill advance out of committee, bringing us one step closer to giving law enforcement the tools they need to crack down on these dangerous synthetic opioids. But there’s more work to do,” said Vindman. “I’ll keep fighting to get this legislation across the finish line because every family deserves to be protected from this growing threat.”

The Strengthening Tools to Outlaw Poisonous (STOP) Nitazenes Act would permanently classify 2-benzylbenzimidazole opioids, commonly known as nitazenes, as Schedule I controlled substances. As overdose deaths continue to claim lives across the country, nitazenes have emerged as an increasingly dangerous threat. These illicit synthetic opioids are significantly more potent than fentanyl and are contributing to a growing number of fatal overdoses nationwide.

The legislation would also give law enforcement the resources needed to interdict and eliminate nitazenes. The DEA added nitazenes to its 2025 National Drug Threat assessment, further emphasizing the need for legislation to combat this drug.

BACKGROUND

In August 2025, Vindman introduced the first-ever bill in Congress to combat the nitazene crisis. The Nitazene Control Act of 2026 would close loopholes that traffickers exploit by making slight chemical changes to evade enforcement.

Later that month, Vindman toured the Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) Clandestine Lab & Training Facility in Quantico, Virginia. During his visit, agents emphasized the urgent need for Congress to take action against deadly nitazenes.

Vindman has also long been engaged in the fight against the fentanyl epidemic — backing the HALT Fentanyl Act, the FEND Off Fentanyl Act, and increased federal resources for law enforcement and treatment programs to address the opioid crisis. He has also introduced legislation to block the spread of fentanyl at the southern border and study the sale of illicit opioids to young people online.

title: After Dangerous Air Quality Blankets D.C. Region, Walkinshaw, Fitzpatrick, Tonko, Beyer, & Norton Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Improve Air in Federal Buildings
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Following a weekend of dangerously poor air quality across the Washington region, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11), joined by Representatives Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Paul Tonko (NY-20), Don Beyer (VA-08), and Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC) introduced the bipartisan Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act to identify and address air quality and ventilation problems across federal buildings.

Recently, wildfire smoke pushed the region into Code Purple conditions, meaning the air was considered very unhealthy for everyone.

“Last week’s dangerous air quality was a stark reminder that clean indoor air is essential to protecting public health,” said Congressman Walkinshaw. “Federal employees should never have to risk their health by showing up to work, yet General Services Administration’s own watchdog has identified persistent ventilation problems in federal buildings. Our bipartisan bill will uncover these deficiencies and require agencies to develop concrete plans to fix them.”

“The federal government should lead by example when it comes to protecting the health and safety of its workforce,” said Congressman Fitzpatrick. “The men and women who serve the American people should never be placed at risk by preventable failures in the buildings where they work. This bipartisan bill will identify those failures, demand corrective action, and ensure our federal facilities meet the standard our public servants deserve.”

“In recent weeks, communities across the Northeast have experienced the public health harms that stem from unsafe air quality,” said Congressman Paul Tonko. “We know that poor air quality can lead to negative health impacts in both the short and long term. But for too many Americans, poor ventilation and filtration in our buildings mean that even spending time indoors does not offer adequate protection. Our government must do more to address indoor air quality, and we can start by improving ventilation and filtration in federal facilities across the nation. That’s why I’m proud to support the Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act, a bipartisan bill that will help our government lead by example and ensure that our hardworking federal employees have a safe, healthy environment in which to work on behalf of the American people.”

"Federal employees should never have to wonder whether the air in their own workplace is safe to breathe," Norton said. "I'm proud to join Congressman Walkinshaw and this bipartisan coalition in cosponsoring the Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act. GAO's review will finally give us the data we need to hold GSA and federal agencies accountable for the ventilation problems their own watchdog has already flagged. This is a commonsense, bipartisan step, and I urge my colleagues on both sides of the aisle to support it.”

“Too many of our federal buildings have aging ventilation and systems that may no longer meet modern standards. We know that indoor air quality impacts the health and productivity of our workforce and as outside threats like wildfire smoke and other climate-driven impacts become more common and further threaten indoor air quality, we have a responsibility to protect the health and well-being of the public servants who keep our government running,” said Rep. Don Beyer. “Our bill would provide the comprehensive information needed to identify deficiencies in air quality and ventilation standards, guide necessary improvements, and help ensure our federal workforce can breathe clean, healthy air in the workplace.”

“We are proud to endorse the bipartisan Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act, innovative and long overdue legislation introduced by Rep. James Walkinshaw (D-VA) and three longtime champions for safe and healthy indoor air quality, Reps. Paul Tonko (D-NY), Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA), and Don Beyer (D-VA). While many public officials are speaking out now due to the hazardous smoke covering many states in our nation, these four Members of Congress have advocated for assessing HVAC deficiencies and remediating indoor air quality dangers for many years at the local, state and federal levels, especially in schools, military facilities and all types of public buildings. Our firms are the leaders in the installation of IAQ mechanical systems in existing buildings and facilities and in new public facility construction projects. These highly skilled construction corporations and their skilled workforce know well that countless thousands of public employees and the millions of our citizens who visit public buildings nationwide will benefit from such a valuable federal effort. The Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act is a vital legislative effort to assess the federal building portfolio and then move quickly to better protect the health and well-being of America’s public employees,” said Stan Kolbe, Executive Director for Government and Political Affairs, Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors’ National Association (SMACNA).

“Over the last couple weeks, as hazardous air covered huge parts of the country, Americans have been reminded just how critical it is to make sure our buildings have clean, healthy air indoors,” said the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART). “That’s why it’s so important for Congress to get behind the Federal Facilities Indoor Air Quality Assessment Act. This bill would implement a comprehensive review of indoor air quality conditions across all federal buildings, protecting the safety of millions of people and putting SMART members to work ensuring indoor air quality in those buildings. This legislation just makes sense — for SMART sheet metal workers, government employees and Americans nationwide. We thank Rep. Walkinshaw for introducing this act, and we urge every pro-worker member of Congress to add their support.”

“Federal employees deserve workplaces that are safe, healthy, and equipped to support their well-being. Too many federal workers spend their days in buildings with aging infrastructure and ventilation systems that may not provide the indoor air quality they need to do their jobs safely and effectively,” said Everett Kelly, National President, American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE). “We commend Representative Walkinshaw for introducing this important legislation directing the Government Accountability Office to evaluate indoor air quality across federal buildings. This commonsense step will help identify where improvements are needed, strengthen workplace health and safety, and ensure the federal government is making informed investments in the facilities where public servants work every day. AFGE is proud to support this effort to protect the health of the federal workforce.”

“Ensuring that federal buildings provide healthy indoor environments is essential to protecting occupant health and supporting productivity," said Sarah E. Maston, P.E., BCxP, LEED AP BD+C, President,American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE). "A comprehensive review of indoor air quality across the federal building portfolio will provide valuable information about how these facilities perform against nationally recognized indoor air quality standards and where improvements may be needed. This legislation demonstrates a commitment to improving the spaces where millions of federal employees and visitors live, work, and conduct business.”

The legislation directs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to conduct a comprehensive review of indoor air quality, ventilation, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning system performance across federal buildings and facilities. The review would examine:

Whether federal buildings meet applicable air quality, ventilation, and HVAC standards;

How agencies monitor, test, and document indoor air quality;

The frequency and causes of air quality deficiencies;

Whether agencies effectively identify and correct indoor air hazards; and

The qualifications and certifications of workers performing HVAC installation, maintenance, and remediation.

GAO would report its findings and recommendations to Congress within 12 months. Agencies found to have material indoor air quality deficiencies would then have six months to submit corrective action plans.

The bill is endorsed by the International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers (SMART), the Sheet Metal and Air Conditioning Contractors’ National Association (SMACNA), the American Society of Heating, Refrigerating and Air-Conditioning Engineers (ASHRAE), and the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE).

title: Walkinshaw, Lee Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Protect Families & First Responders from Swatting Attacks
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congressman James R. Walkinshaw (VA-11) and Congresswoman Laurel Lee (FL-15) introduced the Swatting Registry Best Practices Act, bipartisan legislation to help State, Tribal, territorial, and local governments reduce the risk of deadly swatting incidents through voluntary, privacy-protective tools and stronger emergency response protocols.

Swatting is a serious public safety threat. Former FBI Special Agent Kevin Kolbye estimated that swatting incidents increased from approximately 400 cases in 2011 to more than 1,000 in 2019. However, inconsistent reporting and classification across law enforcement agencies make it difficult to determine the full scope of the problem.

Swatting is the deliberate act of making a false report of a violent emergency—such as an active shooter, hostage situation, bomb threat, or murder—to trigger an armed law enforcement response to an unsuspecting person’s home or workplace. These hoaxes put innocent families and first responders at risk, divert emergency resources from real crises, and can quickly turn deadly. According to NBC News, law enforcement agencies have estimated that a swatting incident can cost several thousand dollars and potentially $10,000 or more, even before follow-up expenses such as investigations, property repairs, and counseling.

"Swatting weaponizes our emergency response system against innocent people," said Congressman Walkinshaw. "A single false call can send heavily armed officers to a family's front door, putting lives at risk in a matter of minutes. My bill gives communities practical tools to help prevent these dangerous hoaxes while protecting privacy and civil liberties."

“Swatting is a dangerous crime that puts innocent families, law enforcement officers, and entire communities at unnecessary risk,” said Congresswoman Lee. “When emergency responders are dispatched to a fabricated crisis, critical resources are diverted from people facing real emergencies, and a split-second decision can have tragic consequences. The Swatting Registry Best Practices Act provides law enforcement with voluntary, commonsense guidance to help identify potential swatting incidents while protecting privacy and civil liberties. I am proud to join Congressman Walkinshaw in advancing this bipartisan legislation to better protect both the public and the first responders who put their lives on the line every day.”

The Swatting Registry Best Practices Act directs the Department of Justice, in consultation with the Department of Homeland Security, to develop national best practices for jurisdictions that choose to establish voluntary swatting registries or integrate swatting verification into existing 911 and dispatch operations. The bill also authorizes technical assistance for agencies seeking to implement these practices.

title: Watson Coleman Votes to Reject Sham Stock Trading Bill
text:
Today, Congresswoman Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) voted to reject a Speaker Johnson-endorsed measure that purported to ban members of Congress from trading stocks but in fact failed to address insider trading.

The so-called “Stop Insider Trading Act,” which has been promoted as a ban on stock trading by members of Congress, fails to actually end the ownership or sale of stock by members.

The American people deserve to be confident that their members of Congress do not trade stocks held in industries they oversee nor profit from insider information on upcoming legislation or regulations of those industries.

The bill, H.R. 7008, which has been endorsed by Speaker of the House Mike Johnson and President Trump, allows members of Congress to keep the stocks they already hold and sell them when it is most financially advantageous. The bill also allows Members and their families to purchase certain securities and privately traded stocks.

In addition, H.R. 7008 includes an unrelated strict voter ID provision that requires a very narrow set of acceptable photo ID to cast a ballot and would functionally gut mail voting. The bill also does nothing to address the well reported insider trading by President Trump and his family or other members of the Administration.

“This piece of legislation does nothing to assure Americans that members of Congress are putting the interests of their constituents above their own financial self-interests,” said Watson Coleman. “I will not play political games with the confidence of the public in their representatives so that Republicans can spend the August recess lying to their constituents. Sadly, this bogus legislation is what we’ve come to expect from the most corrupt, self-dealing President in my lifetime and his enablers in Congress.”

Congresswoman Watson Coleman does not currently own or trade any stock.

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Senator Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.) and Congresswoman Nanette Barragán (D-Calif.-44) introduced three bills that will close historical gaps in dental coverage across the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP), Medicaid, and Medicare. These bills will ensure that children, low-income adults, and seniors can access necessary dental care without facing the barriers of caps and optional benefits.

The Ensuring Kids Have Access to Medically Necessary Dental Care Act strengthens CHIP by banning annual and lifetime dollar limits in children’s dental benefits and requiring wraparound coverage where it is currently optional.

The Medicaid Dental Benefit Act of 2026 makes adult dental care a mandatory Medicaid benefit rather than a state-by-state option with full federal funding for the first three years.

The Medicare Dental Benefit Act of 2026 would add routine, basic, major, and emergency dental coverage to Medicare Part B, reducing the disparities that leave half of all Medicare beneficiaries without dental coverage today.

18 years ago, a young Marylander named Deamonte Driver died of complications from a tooth infection because his family was kicked off Medicaid and could not afford the care they needed. He was only 12 years old. Senator Cardin worked tirelessly throughout his career to ensure that no child should ever suffer Deamonte’s fate, and Senator Alsobrooks is continuing to carry on that legacy.

“No one. No child, adult, or senior should have to choose between affording groceries or being able to have access to dental treatment. I am so proud to be introducing three bills to address this issue and to finally ensure quality, affordable access to dental care for Marylanders – and all Americans. In Maryland, we know all too well that access to dental care is literally a matter of life and death. In 2007, we lost 12-year-old Deamonte Driver because of a toothache. That should have never happened. And while Republicans seem hellbent on kicking as many people off their health insurance as possible, we will fight to expand coverage and to ensure that every American, every child in particular, has access to the care they need,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

“Dental health is an often-overlooked part of your overall health, particularly for those from underserved and vulnerable communities who lack comprehensive health insurance coverage and cannot afford to pay for these routine services out-of-pocket. That is why Senator Alsobrooks and I are reintroducing my bills to strengthen dental benefits so we can make dental care more affordable and prevent health conditions before they become more expensive and deadly,” said Congresswoman Barragán.

“Dental care and coverage is key to overall health, employment, and economic stability. There is widespread concern about rising health care costs, including for oral care access and affordability — and especially among low-income families and seniors on fixed incomes. The Medicaid Dental Benefit Act and Medicare Dental Benefit Act would close the oral health gap for those on key public programs: guaranteeing comprehensive dental coverage for adults on Medicaid, and adding dental care to Medicare Part B. We applaud Representative Barragán and Senator Alsobrooks for their leadership in reimagining what affordable, accessible oral health care can look like for all,” said Anthony Wright, Executive Director of Families USA

“Everyone deserves access to comprehensive dental care,” said Melissa Burroughs, Senior Director of Public Policy at CareQuest Institute for Oral Health. “We’re proud to support this legislation that addresses existing gaps in oral health coverage for seniors, children, low-income families, and people with disabilities. Oral health is essential to overall health, and ensuring people have access to this critical form of care will support healthier communities, reduce health care costs, and advance health equity across the country.”

“Oral health is health care, yet far too many people still struggle to get the dental care they need because of gaps in coverage and affordability. Community Catalyst is proud to stand with partners supporting legislation that strengthens and expands oral health coverage in Medicaid, Medicare, and the Children’s Health Insurance Program (CHIP). These bills would help ensure adults can access comprehensive dental services, bring needed dental coverage to Medicare beneficiaries, and strengthen protections so children can receive the care they need without unnecessary coverage limits. Together, these proposals represent an important step toward treating oral health as an essential part of health care,” said Shaina Goodman, Vice President for Policy & Government Affairs, Community Catalyst

The Medicaid Dental Benefit Act has been endorsed by: American Dental Association, Academy of General Dentistry, American Academy of Oral & Maxillofacial Pathology, American Academy of Orofacial Pain, American Academy of Periodontology, American Association for Dental, Oral, and Craniofacial Research, American Association of Public Health Dentistry, American Dental Education Association, American Student Dental Association, National Network for Oral Health Access, Society of American Indian Dentists, ASTDD Foundation, Inc., American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry, and National Dental Association.

The Medicare Dental Benefit Act has been endorsed by: Community Catalyst, Families USA, CareQuest Institute for Oral Health, Center for Medicare Advocacy, and Justice in Aging.

The Ensuring Kids Have Access to Medically Necessary Dental Care Act has been endorsed by: American Dental Association, Academy of General Dentistry, American Academy of Oral & Maxillofacial Pathology, American Academy of Orofacial Pain, American Academy of Periodontology, American Association for Dental, Oral, and Craniofacial Research, American Association of Endodontists, American Association of Public Health Dentistry, American Dental Education Association, American Student Dental Association, National Network for Oral Health Access, Society of American Indian Dentists, ASTDD Foundation, Inc., American Academy of Pediatric Dentistry, National Dental Association, and American Association of Oral and Maxillofacial Surgeons.

title: ALSOBROOKS, CRAMER INTRODUCE LEGISLATION TO EASE FEDERAL PERMITTING PROCESS FOR TRANSIT
text:
July 22, 2026

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee, and Kevin Cramer (R-N.D.) Chairman of the EPW Transportation and Infrastructure Subcommittee, introduced the Modal Parity in Permitting Act, legislation that would allow transit and passenger rail project sponsors to acquire ‘real property interest’ and parity during the federal permitting process.

Congresswoman Dina Titus (D-Nev.-01) and Congressman Rob Bresnahan (R-Pa.-08) introduced this bipartisan legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Currently, Federal Transit Administration (FTA) funds may only be used for acquisition of rights-of-way such as rail assignments, guideways, and associated easements, before a National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review is completed. This limits transit agencies’ ability to secure other property needed for projects like station sites, maintenance facilities, and parking areas. This bill would expand eligibility by allowing FTA funds to be used for a wider range of real property interests, giving transit agencies more flexibility to acquire land and facilities needed to move projects forward.

“I am proud to partner with Senator Cramer in introducing the Modal Parity in Permitting Act. This bipartisan bill will allow transit and passenger rail projects to have the same flexibility as highway projects when it comes to securing the property they need while their environmental reviews move forward. It just makes sense, let’s get this done,” said Senator Alsobrooks.

“Every time we cut red tape and get the federal government out of the way, infrastructure projects move faster and more efficiently,” said Senator Cramer. “The Modal Parity in Permitting Act removes unnecessary permitting hurdles, allowing local agencies to spend less time navigating bureaucracy and more time delivering transportation improvements for their communities. It’s a simple change with a significant impact.”

“Providing transit and passenger rail projects with greater flexibility to secure property needed for future investments, while maintaining important environmental protections, means agencies like the Maryland Department of Transportation can better manage project timelines, costs and risks,” said Maryland Transportation Secretary Katie Thomson. “We value Senator Alsobrooks’ leadership in advancing solutions that help our state deliver meaningful transportation projects.”

“Many folks in Southern Nevada depend on bus services to get around our community,” said Congresswoman Titus. “Another emerging critical mode of transportation in our region is passenger rail. When high-speed rail comes to Southern Nevada, it will support tourism, improve air quality, and ease traffic congestion. The Modal Parity in Permitting Act will help ensure that the permitting process that allows these services to be built in our community is in line with the process for highway projects.”

“We applaud Sen. Alsobrooks and Sen. Cramer for introducing the Modal Parity in Permitting Act. Public transit and passenger rail projects deserve the same permitting opportunities as highway projects. By allowing FTA and FRA projects to acquire property before completion of the NEPA review—just as highway projects can—this bipartisan legislation will help advance critical public transportation investments more efficiently. We urge Congress to pass this commonsense bill without delay,” said American Public Transportation Association (APTA) President and CEO, Paul P. Skoutelas.

title: Baldwin Pushes Bipartisan Bill to Ban Chinese Vehicles, Protect American Workers Through Senate Committee
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) successfully passed a bipartisan bill to protect American workers and families from the growing threat of Chinese-made vehicles through the Senate Commerce Committee. The Baldwin-backed Connected Vehicle Security Act prevents Americans’ data from being collected on American roads and sent back to Beijing by cutting off the supply of vehicles, software, and critical hardware originating from China or Chinese companies at every point in the chain, from the manufacturing process, to import, to sale.

“Chinese connected vehicles pose a serious threat to American jobs and Americans’ safety,” said Senator Baldwin. “I am proud to have worked with my Democratic and Republican colleagues to take a step forward in our fight to prevent China from collecting our data and help keep Wisconsin workers and families safe.”

Specifically, the Connected Vehicle Security Act:

Bans foreign adversary vehicles by prohibiting the importation, manufacture, sale, and resale of connected vehicles, software, and hardware linked to China or other foreign adversaries, including those from joint ventures or entities under their control;

Empowers the Department of Commerce to identify and block high-risk vehicle technologies, components, and transactions that threaten U.S. economic or national security;

Establishes enforcement mechanisms to ensure prohibited technologies are kept out of the U.S. market; and

Phases implementation with vehicle and software restrictions taking effect in 2027, and hardware restrictions in 2030, giving the U.S. industry time to secure a domestic supply, in line with the Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) Connected Vehicles rule.

The bill is led by Senators Bernie Moreno (R-OH) and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI).

title: Baldwin’s Bipartisan Bill to Cap Insulin Costs at $35 Per Month for Millions Advances in the Senate
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) voted for and helped advance legislation to cap the out-of-pocket cost of insulin at $35 per month out of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee. The Improving Needed Safeguards for Users of Lifesaving Insulin Now (INSULIN) Act, legislation Senator Baldwin cosponsors, now heads to the Senate floor for consideration by the full Senate.

“Wisconsin families are feeling the weight of rising costs across the board – and for the half a million Wisconsinites with diabetes, the cost of insulin is one more thing stretching their budgets,” said Senator Baldwin. “There is no reason these big drug companies should be able to continue to charge so much for a medicine that has been around for more than 100 years and remains basically unchanged. Our bipartisan legislation to finally stop this price gouging, tackle the root causes of high insulin costs, and cut prescription drug costs is now one step closer to becoming law of the land.”

A report from the American Diabetes Association shows the cost of diabetes in America, including the cost of insulin, continues to skyrocket for patients and the federal government. More than 40 million Americans live with diabetes, including over 526,000 Wisconsinites. The disease is one of the leading causes of death in the United States, claiming over 100,000 lives in 2021. It is also the most expensive chronic condition in the nation, costing Americans a combined total of $412.9 billion per year. The rising cost of insulin presents a barrier to care for a growing number of Americans living with diabetes; 1 in 4 individuals report reducing insulin use due to cost.

The INSULIN Act would directly address the root problems in the insulin market that cause high list prices, while simultaneously extending vital patient protections, fostering competition, and broadening access to needed insulin products. Senator Baldwin also offered a bipartisan amendment to ensure that provisions creating a pilot program to get $35 per month insulin to uninsured patients and establishing a resource center to help patients access affordable insulin remained in the bill, which was adopted. When the legislation gained enough support from both parties to surpass the filibuster and pass on the Senate floor, Senator Baldwin called on Republican Leader John Thune to bring the legislation up for a vote.

Senator Baldwin has long advocated for holding big drug companies accountable and expanding access to affordable health care for Wisconsinites. In 2022, she helped pass the Inflation Reduction Act, which for the first time allows Medicare to negotiate lower drug prices and caps the cost of insulin at $35-a-month for Medicare recipients. The INSULIN Act builds on that momentum to cap out-of-pocket costs for all Americans who rely on insulin.

title: Barrasso Questions FERC Commissioners on Wyoming’s Seminoe Pumped Storage Project
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) questioned Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) commissioners about electricity markets and the Seminoe Pumped Storage Project, a proposed hydropower project located in central Wyoming.

Barrasso specifically urged the commissioners to take into account the State of Wyoming’s concerns about how the Seminoe project could impact one of the most legendary trout fisheries in Wyoming, and other local wildlife.

All five FERC commissioners testified during today’s Senate Energy and Natural Resources oversight hearing.

On Seminoe Pumped Storage Project State Input:

“What I want to talk about is the Seminoe Pumped Storage Project — which is in the State of Wyoming.

“On June 12, FERC staff issued their recommended Final Environmental Impact Statement for the Seminoe Pumped Storage Project.

“This is a private project, and it would create water pumped storage infrastructure above Seminoe Reservoir — which is in Central Wyoming.

“Functionally, the project works as a battery with about a capacity of efficiency of about 70%.

“It uses power to pump water into storage, and then it sells power at a profit when the grid needs electricity.

“Wyoming constituents that I’ve heard from have concerns.

“They worry that the project harms the only disease-free Big Horn Sheep herd in the state, and critical Mule Deer, Pronghorn, and Sage Grouse habitat.

“They also worry that it harms one of the most legendary trout fisheries in Wyoming and the world. It’s known as ‘The Miracle Mile.’

“But it’s over 5 miles; it’s a stretch of the North Platte River between the Seminoe Reservoir and the Pathfinder Reservoir.

“This is an area that must be protected.

“The project received its water quality permit from the state — their concerns about wildlife that haven’t yet been resolved in the recommended Environmental Impact Statement.

“The State submitted comments on the project, which I have here and would, Mr. Chairman, like to enter into the hearing record without objection.

“It’s critically important that Wyoming’s concerns are thoughtfully and carefully considered in this process.

“So, Madam Chairman, I would ask others and you to commit to taking a renewed look at the State’s comments and consider their incorporation into your final decision?”

Follow-up:

“Thank you. Anyone else want to weigh in on this?”

On Electricity Market Governance:

“Western electricity markets — they are evolving rapidly, as you all know.

“This comes from the implementation of new day-ahead markets.

“It comes from the new Regional Organization for Western Energy, and Southwest Power Pool’s expansion to the west.

“The goal is unified and coordinated electricity transmission.

“While participation in this new model can be a good thing, states like Wyoming need a meaningful voice in governance.

“Wyoming is the number one electricity exporter in the western interconnection.

“We have the highest net exports of energy per capita.

“That makes Wyoming the backbone of the grid.

“So, what steps are FERC planning to take to ensure meaningful state participation as the Extended Day Ahead Market and Western Energy Imbalance Markets evolve?”

Follow-up:

“Great. Anyone else want to respond on that?”

###

title: Barrasso Questions US Trade Rep on Wyoming Soda Ash, Beef, Sheep and Chemical Manufacturing
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) questioned United States Trade Representative Jamieson Greer on how trade barriers impact Wyoming’s soda ash exports, beef, chemical manufacturing, and sheep industry.

Greer testified during today’s Senate Committee on Finance hearing on the President’s 2026 Trade Agenda.

On Soda Ash Exports:

“I want to talk about soda ash exports.

“As you know, Wyoming’s Green River Basin is home to the world’s largest deposits of naturally occurring trona – the mineral that’s refined into soda ash.

“It’s Wyoming’s top export – supports thousands of jobs across the state.

“And, the industry is facing a serious challenge.

“That’s because earlier this year, producers in India petitioned their government to restrict imports of American soda ash.

“The result could be a hard limit on how much American soda ash can enter their market, regardless of the price, regardless of the demand.

“And, our soda ash producers can compete with anyone in the world on a level playing field.

“What we’re worrying about is what’s happening in India – making sure we never get the level playing field.

“How are you working to ensure fair market access for American producers like soda ash in India?”

On Wyoming Beef:

“Wyoming Beef. Our ranchers produce the highest-quality beef in the world.

“Beef is Wyoming’s top agricultural export – nearly $150 million shipped around the world each year.

“For far too long, our ranchers faced barriers that kept them out of foreign markets that they have every right to compete in.

“Through the Administration’s trade agenda, we are seeing some real change – but we believe there is more work to be done.

“There’s still too many markets that are able to hide behind unscientific and discriminatory restrictions that put our ranchers at a disadvantage.

“So, as you continue negotiating new trade agreements, what more can be done to open markets for American beef and ensure that Wyoming ranchers can compete on equal footing?”

On Wyoming Chemical Manufacturing:

“I appreciate the job you’re doing highlighting American manufacturing job gains and wage growth.

“You did it in your testimony today. So, congratulations on your success there.

“You know, in Wyoming, chemical manufacturing is driving much of our progress.

“Wyoming sends over a billion dollars in chemical products across the world each year.

“Our producers are positioned to reach even more markets.

“So, trade deals like the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) have included commitments to reduce barriers in specific industries like chemical manufacturing.

“Progress has been limited.

“So, how are you pushing trading partners to follow through on industry-specific commitments and open their markets to our manufacturers across the board?”

On Wyoming Sheep Industry:

“Let me finish with this question on the Wyoming sheep industry.

“The sheep industry has been part of our ranching heritage for longer than we’ve actually been a state.

“And, earlier this year, I raised concerns with your office about surging lamb imports and the strains that they’re putting on Wyoming’s sheep industry.

“Family-owned operations that have sustained rural communities in Wyoming for generations are now fighting to survive.

“So, I want to thank you for directing the International Trade Commission to investigate whether these imports are harming our domestic industry.

“And, our producers deserve, I believe, a fair chance to compete in their own market.

“So, can you speak to how this investigation is expected to unfold? And, what you expect going forward?”

###

title: Bennet, Blunt Rochester Reintroduce Bill to Connect Workers with Higher Wages
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet and Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.) reintroduced the Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act to expand funding for evidence-based and innovative workforce development programs to ensure that workers have the skills needed to compete in a 21st-century economy.

“I hear from veterans and single parents in Colorado who want to provide for themselves and their families but do not have the skills to earn a living wage,” said Bennet. “They want to build sustainable careers that pay living wages, we have the programs to train them, and Colorado’s economy needs the skills and talent they can provide. The last piece of the puzzle is to invest in the workforce training programs that are proven to create economic mobility for workers of every background.”

“As we address a changing economy and the widespread adoption of AI, we must ensure pathways to good jobs are available,” said Blunt Rochester. “I’m proud to co-lead the Better Jobs Through Evidence and Innovation Act to meet the moment by both investing in what works when it comes to workforce training, and supporting the development of promising new strategies to prepare our future workforce.”

Programs that upskill workers support long-term economic mobility for individuals, including those without a college degree. These programs are ready and able to serve workers and employers, but remain severely underfunded. The Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act would establish the Workforce Development Innovation Fund in the U.S. Department of Labor to test and scale proven innovative strategies to improve employment outcomes for American workers.

The Workforce Development Innovation Fund would make three tiers of funding available to evidence-based employment and training programs that generate demonstrated, long-term economic improvements for jobseekers and employers, and produce high-quality evaluations of their effects.

“America Forward applauds Senators Michael Bennet and Lisa Blunt Rochester for championing the Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act, which would invest in evidence-based workforce development programs delivering real, long-term economic mobility for workers and employers in a rapidly-changing economy,” said Deborah Smolover, Executive Director of America Forward. “As the pace of change in our labor market accelerates, this legislation ensures that the high-impact organizations driving economic mobility, many of which are members of the America Forward Coalition, have the support they need to grow and meet the evolving needs of workers and communities nationwide.”

“Too many Americans are completing workforce programs only to find themselves without a job or a path to higher earnings, and that’s simply not good enough,” said David Medina, co-founder and COO of Results for America. “The Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act would address this challenge by finding, funding and implementing workforce programs with proven track records of success, while continuing to build the evidence base for the next generation of solutions. We applaud Sens. Bennet and Blunt Rochester for their leadership in ensuring that workforce investments deliver real, measurable and lasting results for jobseekers and their families.”

“Senator Bennet’s Better Jobs Through Evidence and Innovation Act represents exactly the approach our workforce development system urgently needs,” said Roger Low, CEO & Founder of the Colorado Equitable Economic Mobility Initiative. “By creating a tiered evidence fund, the legislation directs limited federal upskilling and reskilling dollars toward the two priorities that matter most: building strong evidence of effectiveness across promising training and credentialing pathways, and scaling the approaches that work.”

“There are training programs across the country with a proven record of moving people into quality careers — and they could achieve so much more with additional investment. Senator Bennet’s Better Jobs through Evidence and Innovation Act would channel federal support to the models that work,” said Plinio Ayala, CEO of Per Scholas. “For organizations like Per Scholas, that means reaching more learners, connecting employers with the skilled talent they need, and opening durable, demand-driven pathways to economic mobility.”

title: VIDEO: Blackburn Blasts Democrats’ War on ICE Following NYC Incendiary Device Attack
text:

title: Blumenthal Introduces Bill Strengthening Social Security
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) introduced the Social Security 2100 Act, legislation to increase Social Security benefits and make the critical system financially stable throughout the 21st Century. As our nation’s bedrock social insurance program, Social Security is the most important source of retirement income for 4 out of 5 seniors and provides vital protections for disabled workers and families who have lost a breadwinner. U.S. Representative John Larson (D-CT) has introduced the bill in the U.S. House of Representatives.

“Social Security is a promise that must be kept. The Trump Administration’s threats to Social Security and skyrocketing costs require common sense steps to expand benefits and ensure financial stability,” said Blumenthal. “Bolstering Social Security guarantees all Americans a standard of living and protects the American dream.”

“Thanks to Trump policies, automatic benefit cuts are closer than ever—and Connecticut seniors will be hit the hardest if Congress fails to act. Republicans in Congress want to raise the retirement age and have stood by as ‘DOGE’ cut staff and tried to slash services at the Social Security Administration. Benefit cuts are not the answer—we need to make the wealthy pay their fair share. Social Security 2100 will protect Americans’ hard-earned benefits from cuts and enhance the program to keep pace with rising costs, by finally making the wealthy pay their fair share. I’m thrilled to team up with Senator Blumenthal on this important issue, as we build a growing coalition with the courage to stand up and act on Social Security,” said Larson.

The Social Security 2100 Act is cosponsored in the Senate by U.S. Senators Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Tammy Duckworth (D-IL).

The legislation would increase benefits for current and new beneficiaries by eliminating the Social Security tax cap and by adding a tax on investment income for taxpayers making over $400,000. Additionally, the bill would utilize an improved cost-of-living adjustment to more accurately take into account true costs incurred by seniors and implement a stronger minimum benefit, so an individual who works their whole life will not retire into poverty.

The bill also includes provisions to fight back against the Trump Administration’s attacks on the Social Security Administration (SSA), including undoing staffing cuts made by the Trump Administration, blocking any future efforts by the Administration to close Social Security field offices, and preventing DOGE and political appointees from accessing sensitive data systems at SSA.

title: Blumenthal Joins 13 Senate Colleagues in Investigation into Trump Administration Efforts to Abandon Offshore Wind Projects
text:
[Hartford, CT] — Today, U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal joined 13 of his Senate colleagues in launching an investigation into the Trump Administration’s efforts to kill offshore wind energy projects and seeking answers from four offshore wind companies about the lease buyout agreements.

“These buyouts have been announced amid a larger effort by the Trump Administration to stall wind and solar projects – the energy sources that are cheap, clean, and fastest to bring online – across the country,” the Senators wrote. “At a time when gas prices have spiked by an average of more than $1 dollar per gallon due to the President’s war in Iran and electricity prices are rising nearly twice as fast as inflation, clean energy offers a critical opportunity to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels and relieve costs for people across the country. Dismantling the burgeoning offshore wind industry now and creating broader uncertainty for investment in cheap, clean energy will have consequences for decades to come.”

The Trump Administration has agreed to pay the four companies more than $2.7 billion in taxpayer funding to abandon projects that could have delivered energy to millions of homes and created tens of thousands of jobs up and down the East and West Coasts.

“These projects were poised not only to advance U.S. leadership in clean energy technology and generation capacity, but also to unlock hundreds of millions of dollars in federal and state investment in research and development, port upgrades, workforce development, and community benefit agreements,” the Senators continued. “The two Invenergy projects in the Gulf of Maine were expected to help power more than 2 million homes and support over 18,000 jobs. The Leading Light Wind project in the New York Bight was projected to generate more than $3.7 billion in economic development benefits and over 7,000 jobs. The Golden State Wind project off California’s Central Coast would have powered 1.1 million homes, created more than 8,000 jobs, and delivered a $30 million commitment to workforce development and supply chain initiatives.”

The Senators called on the companies to turn over internal communications and posed a series of questions: whether the Administration had raised legitimate national security concerns, whether the companies had struck a deal with the Department of the Interior involving a pledge to invest in fossil fuel projects, and whether any conditions were attached to the payouts.

The letters, led by Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), and U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Angus King (I-Maine), and Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) were also signed by U.S. Senators Chris Coons (D-Del.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.).

Read the full text of the letters here and below.

Dear [TotalEnergies, Ocean Winds, Duke Energy, Invenergy]:

We write to express deep concern with your company’s voluntary termination of [nine] leases to develop offshore wind energy in the United States. Over the last few months, President Trump’s Administration has agreed to pay companies, including [TotalEnergies, Ocean Winds, Duke Energy, Invenergy], a total of more than $2.7 billion in taxpayer dollars to abandon projects that could have delivered energy to communities spanning from California to North Carolina to Maine. We are concerned that these decisions will harm grid reliability, job opportunities, and economic development in states across the country, and we request your response to several inquiries.

Since March, 2026, the Department of the Interior (DOI) and the Department of Justice (DOJ) have announced agreements to terminate eight leases for offshore wind projects, including TotalEnergies’ leases for Attentive Energy in the New York Bight and Carolina Long Bay; Ocean Winds’ leases for Bluepoint Wind in the New York Bight and Golden State Wind off Morro Bay in California; and Invenergy’s leases in the New York Bight, Gulf of Maine, Morro Bay in California’s Central Coast, and Duke Energy’s lease in the Carolina Long Bay. The Trump Administration agreed to reimburse companies for their leases in exchange for investments in oil, gas, and geothermal projects that, in large part, will be hundreds of miles away from the states that were planning for these offshore wind projects. In total, the Trump Administration’s agreements could result in the loss of more than 15 GW of planned, fixed-price clean energy, which would have helped meet increasing energy demand in regions such as New England and the Mid-Atlantic that are already facing supply constraints.

These projects were poised not only to advance U.S. leadership in clean energy technology and generation capacity, but also to unlock hundreds of millions of dollars in federal and state investment in research and development, port upgrades, workforce development, and community benefit agreements. The two Invenergy projects in the Gulf of Maine were expected to help power more than 2 million homes and support over 18,000 jobs. The Leading Light Wind project in the New York Bight was projected to generate more than $3.7 billion in economic development benefits and over 7,000 jobs. The Golden State Wind project off California’s Central Coast would have powered 1.1 million homes, created more than 8,000 jobs, and delivered a $30 million commitment to workforce development and supply chain initiatives.

Several states have already begun making substantial investments to prepare for offshore wind projects to move forward, including over $100 million in investments by California to modernize ports and support planning. By accepting DOI’s buyout deals, you are stranding these investments, undermining job expectations, and disrupting the yearslong process of electricity capacity planning by states and utilities.

These buyouts have been announced amid a larger effort by the Trump Administration to stall wind and solar projects – the energy sources that are cheap, clean, and fastest to bring online – across the country. In December 2025, the Administration paused the construction of five largescale offshore wind projects, claiming “national security risks.” Secretary Burgum issued a directive requiring his personal review and approval of every wind and solar energy project on public lands, holding up at least 57GW as identified in court documents. The Department of Defense is holding up all new wind projects on private land, a total of more than 30 GW of onshore wind capacity. At a time when gas prices have spiked by an average of more than $1 dollar per gallon due to the President’s war in Iran and electricity prices are rising nearly twice as fast as inflation, clean energy offers a critical opportunity to reduce our dependence on fossil fuels and relieve costs for people across the country. Dismantling the burgeoning offshore wind industry now and creating broader uncertainty for investment in cheap, clean energy will have consequences for decades to come.

There is no law that entitles leaseholders to refunds for voluntarily surrendering a lease, and lease cancellations must be executed according to the law. The Trump Administration has asserted that these payments can be made from the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Judgment Fund—a position that may not be permissible under statute and that is the subject of ongoing litigation brought by the attorneys general of New York, New Jersey, Connecticut, Maine, Massachusetts, Rhode Island, and Vermont. These buyouts risk setting a dangerous precedent that could encourage further misuse of public funds to terminate clean energy projects in certain states in favor of fossil fuel investments that benefit other states.

In light of these questions and concerns, and to better understand the legal basis for the lease buyout agreements between your company and DOI, we request the following information by August 7, 2026.

Please state when initial conversations began between your company and the Administration regarding initiating a lease buyout agreement.

Please state if anyone in the Trump Administration communicated to your company, whether verbal or written, that it would suspend your offshore wind projects if the project moved forward. If communication occurred, please provide responses to the following:

Did your company consider the threat of suspension a viable threat?

Did your company communicate directly that it would file suit for a breach of contract if the Trump Administration suspended your company’s project(s)? Please provide all supporting documentation and communications.

Please state what national security issues, if any, the Trump Administration raised or identified with your company with respect to the terminated leases.

Please state if your company or any representative of DOI or the Trump Administration provided notice to the states affected by the lease terminations. If not, why not?

Please state whether DOI held a hearing related to the planned termination of your company’s leases. If so, please describe.

Please state which projects your company has agreed to reinvest in and the settled payments amount. In responding to this question, please provide the following information:

The location of these projects.

If specific projects have not been identified, how and when will those investments be chosen?

If the specific projects have been identified, was your company already planning in investing in those projects prior to the settlement, or is the investment contingent on receiving funds from DOI?

If your company accepted an agreement with DOI in exchange for a pledge to invest in fossil fuel projects, describe the nature of the pledge and note whether any aspects of the pledge are legally binding.

Please state whether your company currently has other clean energy projects that are pending review by DOI, the Department of Defense, or any other federal government agency. In responding to this question, please provide the following information:

The name and type of project(s) affected and the location.

The total generation capacity at risk by ongoing delays.

The total amount of investment at risk by ongoing delays.

The total number of jobs supported by the projects that are stalled.

Please provide all correspondence with DOI, including with the Bureau of Ocean Energy Management (BOEM) and any email correspondence, papers, books, records, and documents in your possession or under your control relating to these agreements.

We look forward to your prompt response with the information requested above.

Sincerely,
