title: Kean Secures Nearly $18 Million for Critical Local Projects Across New Jersey
text:
(July 23, 2026) – Today, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) announced that 18 Community Project Funding requests made by his office, totaling $17,765,906, are included in key House funding bills for the upcoming fiscal year. All six counties in New Jersey’s Seventh Congressional District are represented in the requests highlighted below.

“I fought to bring this federal funding home to New Jersey because our communities deserve a strong return on the tax dollars they send to Washington,” said Congressman Kean. "These investments will improve roads and bridges, modernize water infrastructure, strengthen public safety, support our first responders, and help towns complete critical projects without placing the full burden on local property taxpayers. My focus will continue to be listening to residents, cutting through the Washington gridlock, and delivering resources that make our communities safer, stronger, and more affordable.”

Community Project Funding is a process that allows Members of Congress to request direct funding for projects that benefit the communities they represent. This process includes robust eligibility, ethics, and transparency guidelines and is only available to state, local, tribal, and territorial governments, as well as some non-profits. Additionally, only projects with evidence of strong support from the community will be considered, and evidence of this support and community need is required as part of the submission.

In April 2026, Congressman Kean submitted 20 Community Project Funding requests to the House Appropriations Committee for consideration in five of this year’s must-pass funding bills. The next step is for these bills to pass the House.

Below are the 18 Community Project Funding requests made by the Office of Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. that will be included in the House funding bills for the upcoming fiscal year:

1. Hillsborough Township Public Safety Interoperable Communications Upgrade

Included Amount: $975,000

Justification: The funding would be used for modernization and replacement of outdated portable radio communications equipment used by the Hillsborough Township Police Department. The project will fund the procurement and deployment of seventy-five (75) all-band portable radios equipped with advanced interoperability, Wi-Fi connectivity, and LTE capabilities. The department’s current portable radios are outdated and lack the capability to provide reliable communications in complex environments such as schools, large commercial buildings, and emergency response scenes. In addition, the existing system does not provide sufficient interoperability between police, fire, and other emergency response agencies.

2. Town of Phillipsburg Police Technology Equipment

Included Amount: $500,000

Justification: The funding would be used for modernizing the Phillipsburg Police Department’s investigative, surveillance, and information technology capabilities. Through the deployment of Automatic License Plate Reader (ALPR) technology, covert surveillance systems, upgraded CCTV infrastructure, enhanced cybersecurity protections, and a mobile drone operations support vehicle, the department will significantly strengthen its ability to prevent crime, conduct investigations, safeguard critical data, and respond to emergencies.

3. New Providence Police Radio Replacement and Upgrade

Included Amount: $245,000

Justification: The funding would be used for the replacement of 47 portable radios used throughout the agency. The New Providence Police are currently utilizing portable radios that have exceeded their useful life and have begun to fail during their usage. The upgrade will fill coverage gaps by utilizing additional technology built into the radio hardware that connects the portable radio to a wireless fidelity (Wi-Fi) network. The new radios will ensure continued connectivity to the Emergency Services Dispatch Center and Fire, EMS and Emergency Management departments. The purchase of these radios has the ability to impact the lives of any person who may live, work or travel through New Providence due to the portability of this equipment. The purchase will enhance community relations and offer a better experience to all taxpayers with our public safety professionals

4. Chester Highlands Ridge Building Roof Replacement

Included Amount: $137,500

Justification: The funding would be used for the replacement of the Highlands Ridge Building, a vital multi-agency hub housing the Chester Volunteer First Aid Squad, contracted Atlantic Health EMT services, the Chester Township Office of Emergency Management, the NJ Highlands Council, and NJ Department of Environmental Protection offices. It also serves as a regional food pantry and the primary location of the Chester Historical Society. This project will replace the building’s 22,000 square foot flat roof which is failing in multiple locations to halt active water infiltration and preserve this essential community asset.

5. Passaic River Regional Flooding Mitigation Project

Included Amount: $3,000,000

Justification: The funding would be used for the clearing of major obstructions from Passaic River tributaries and the shoring up of stream banks in the river towns of Berkeley Heights, Long Hill, New Providence, Summit, and Chatham Borough, which will decrease area flooding and soil erosion, while improving and protecting soils and water quality. Many municipalities in the Passaic River Basin have experienced repeated and severe flooding events in recent years, resulting in significant public safety hazards, damage to public infrastructure, damage to property, roadway closures, emergency response impacts, and disruption to residents and businesses. This project will focus on strategic, environmentally responsible de-snagging and debris removal in the most-clogged stretches of the tributaries leading into the Passaic River, representing an important flood mitigation strategy to improve the hydraulic capacity of the river tributaries and reduce flood risk.

6. Springfield Police Department Refurbishment Project

Included Amount: $700,000

Justification: The funding would be used to complete critical facility improvements necessary to ensure compliance with Department of Corrections standards, modernize essential infrastructure, and improve operational efficiency. These improvements will enhance detainee management, officer safety, and compliance with applicable regulations. The project will also replace the building’s aging and inefficient HVAC system. The current system has reached the end of its useful life and no longer provides reliable climate control for the facility. Finally, the project includes building modifications to create additional office space. The Department currently faces space limitations that affect administrative operations and the delivery of services to the community.

7. Renovation of the Frenchtown Borough Police Headquarters

Included Amount: $200,000

Justification: The funding would be used for the renovation of the Frenchtown Police Department’s outdated station currently housed in an aging residential structure acquired by the Borough decades ago. It lacks separate male and female changing facilities, does not meet current ADA accessibility standards, and utilizes a former residential kitchen area for temporary detainee holding—conditions that do not reflect contemporary public safety best practices. Additionally, the building’s exterior components, including siding, gutters, windows, and roof, are in significant need of repair and replacement. This project will transform the facility into a modern, sustainable public safety asset that benefits residents, businesses, and visitors while relieving undue financial pressure on local property taxpayers, making it a prudent and impactful investment of federal funds.

8. Hope Township Volunteer Fire Department Engine Truck Replacement

Included Amount: $656,406

Justification: The funding would be used for the purchase of a new fire engine for the Hope Township Volunteer Fire Department. The current engine, which is approximately 20 years old, is nearing the end of its service life. Replacing this aging vehicle is essential to maintaining dependable fire emergency response capabilities and protecting the residents of Hope. A new fire engine will improve reliability, reduce out-of-service time, and strengthen the Township’s capacity to respond to fires and other emergencies within our own municipality, those surrounding us and especially Route 80 which runs through our area. It will also enhance firefighter safety by incorporating modern safety standards and updated equipment.

9. Clark Sanitary Sewer Infiltration and Inflow Correction and Rehabilitation Project

Included Amount: $700,000

Justification: The funding would be used for a phased, condition-based sanitary sewer rehabilitation and replacement program that will target high-priority segments of the system which will be identified through inspection and flow analysis. This will include Cured-In-Place Pipe (CIPP) Rehabilitation, Full Sewer Main Replacement, Manhole Rehabilitation, and Joint Sealing and Point Repairs as needed. By stabilizing and rehabilitating the aging sanitary sewer infrastructure, the Township will prevent untreated wastewater from potentially impacting the Pumpkin Patch Brook, the Clark Wildlife Preserve (formerly the Middlesex Water Company Reservoir), and the Rahway River Basin. This directly supports water quality protection within the watershed and advances the objectives of the Clean Water Act.

10. Mine Hill Transite Water Main Replacement Project

Included Amount: $850,000

Justification: The funding would be used for a water main project that will replace 5,307 linear feet of Transite water main. Transite is an asbestos-cement pipe made of 20% asbestos. These pipes have been in the ground for over 40 years and have started to fail. The proposed project, including replacement of in-service transit (AC) pipe, represents a proactive and responsible approach to infrastructure management. Replacement will improve system efficiency, water quality, lower repair costs, and help preserve the long-term reliability of the water distribution system.

11. Sparta Township Lead Service Line Replacement Project

Included Amount: $850,000

Justification: The funding would be used for the replacement of approximately 210 lead and galvanized steel service lines across Sparta Township. This will enable Sparta to accelerate compliance with New Jersey’s Service Line Replacement Law (P.L. 2021, Ch. 183), which mandates full replacement of all lead service lines by 2031 to safeguard public health. The project includes comprehensive identification of service line materials through record reviews, inspections, curb box excavations, and water testing, followed by full replacement of any lines confirmed to contain lead or galvanized steel. New copper service lines will be installed from the water main to each building, with temporary water shutoff, excavation, reconnection, system flushing, and full restoration of disturbed surfaces completed efficiently, typically within one to two days. By modernizing essential water infrastructure now, Sparta Township will protect public health, improve water quality, and ensure long term reliability of its drinking water system well ahead of the mandated schedule.

12. Branchburg Emergency Operations Center

Included Amount: $2,250,000

Justification: The funding would be used for the renovation of Branchburg’s Emergency Management facility. This project will provide adequate and modern facilities for the Office of Emergency Management, a necessary upgrade to protect Branchburg’s rapidly growing community and heavily trafficked commuter corridors on US Route 202 and US Route 22.

13. Somerville Downtown Capital Improvements

Included Amount: $1,942,000

Justification: The funding would be used for two complementary capital improvement projects: the Division Street Arts Plaza and the Giardina Walk Improvements. Together, these projects will transform two heavily traveled public corridors into vibrant, safe, and fully accessible pedestrian spaces that anchor Downtown Somerville’s arts and cultural identity. The Division Street project will reconstruct and enhance the full length of Division Street between South Street and West Main Street, transforming a pass-through corridor connecting New Jersey Transit Train Station to West Main Street into an activated public plaza. Improvements include the installation of brick pavers, granite curbing, ADA-compliant curbing and a new pedestrian crosswalk at the West Main Street intersection. The Giardina Walk project will improve the existing pedestrian walkway between Union Street and West Main Street, a key connector between Municipal Parking Lot #4 and Main Street. The project incorporates new and existing assets, including an existing historic mural, existing shade trees, and existing light fixtures, minimizing waste and construction disruption.

14. Bernards Pleasant Valley Park Culvert and Paths

Included Amount: $1,840,000

Justification: The funding would be used for the construction of a culvert at Pleasant Valley Park. Currently, hundreds of vehicles per day drive through the stream that intersects the park road, negatively impacting the water quality. The construction of a culvert would reduce water pollution, provide a safe crossing to the rear of the park, and allow the construction of new paths throughout the park. Additionally, the project greatly expands walking and exercise opportunities, especially for the veterans who live at Valley Brook Village, the HUD Veterans Affairs Supportive Housing apartments on the Lyons VA campus next to the park.

15. Bridgewater Cold Food Storage & Food Locker Implementation Project

Included Amount: $420,000

Justification: The funding would be used for a two-pronged project designed to increase food bank donation capacity and provide targeted intervention in low-access areas through the rental and maintenance of one cold storage unit and the purchase and maintenance of one food locker unit. Bridgewater Township will work alongside the Food Bank Network of Somerset County to carry out project activities. After the purchase, installation, testing, and training of staff is complete, the cold storage and food locker units will be utilized by the partner food pantries to better accept and distribute donations—specifically to low-access areas with transportation barriers to food pantry access. The cold storage will open up a new intake avenue, as the units will provide the capacity required to accept bulk donations from local farms, pantries, and grocery retailers. This food will benefit thousands of food insecure individuals in Somerset County. This project is designed to support the efforts of vital non-profit organizations on the frontline in the fight against food insecurity and will result in the improved delivery of life-changing aid.

16. Warren County New Law Enforcement and Emergency Services Workforce Training Center

Included Amount: $750,000

Justification: The funding would be used for the construction of a new Law Enforcement and Emergency Services Training Center to meet the ever increasing training demands upon Police, Fire and EMS service providers in Warren County. The lack of a suitable and centralized location for hosting the necessary classes places a hardship on planners and instructors, and attendees alike. Ultimately, this impacts the services received by the over 110,000 Warren County residents. The County’s Public Safety Campus in Franklin Township, New Jersey is already an extremely active hub of training activities at its Fire Academy structures and specialized sites for controlled combustion activities. The County endeavors to expand its training offerings to include training resources specialized to the needs of law enforcement and emergency management personnel. A new facility will include both classroom space and training areas for multiple modes of training and hands-on activity and will integrate the office of the Fire Marshall into contemporary space designed to optimize their function.

17. Mount Olive Township Police Department Facility Expansion

Included Amount: $750,000

Justification: The funding would be used for the construction, reconstruction, and renovation of the existing 3,460 square feet vacated by the Health Department to expand the current footprint of the police department. The project is needed to address the long-standing, critical infrastructure deficiency that hinders modern, efficient, and safe public safety operations. The current, undersized facility poses significant risks to operational capacity, limits the ability to implement updated technology and training, and restricts necessary staffing levels needed to serve a growing population. This investment will directly enhance public safety, improve officer wellness, and provide essential, secure space for effective, community-oriented policing.

18. Watchung Valley Road Sidewalk Improvements

Included Amount: $1,000,000

Justification: The funding would be used to reconstruct approximately 7,000 linear feet of sidewalk on Valley Road, between Knightsbridge and Bayberry Lane in Watchung. Valley Road is a major thoroughfare in Watchung, connecting many local landmarks such as Bayberry Elementary School and various residential streets to Watchung's downtown business district, the Watchung Library, Watchung Arts Center, the Watchung Municipal Building, churches, local businesses, and parks. In 2019, a pedestrian, aged approximately 12 years old, was struck by a vehicle and was seriously injured while walking on Valley Road within the project limits. These existing conditions pose significant hazards for pedestrians and are in urgent need of reconstruction to improve pedestrian safety and ADA-accessibility within the Borough of Watchung.

title: Kelly, Moran introduce Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act to strengthen U.S. maritime manufacturing
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. -- Today, U.S. Representatives Mike Kelly (R-PA) and Nathaniel Moran (R-TX) introduced the Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act, legislation which aims to strengthen U.S. shipbuilding and maritime manufacturing by encouraging long-term private investment through the creation of Maritime Prosperity Zones (MPZs).

The legislation follows recent plans to build a modern, large-scale shipbuilding project along Erie's bayfront to support the U.S. Navy. A new shipyard in Erie is projected to create 1,000 jobs, plus an additional 2.67 jobs in other parts of the local economy for every shipyard job.

Kelly's legislation also supports the Trump administration's goalsto expand commercial shipbuilding capacity in the United States. Currently, the U.S. accounts for less than 1% of global commercial shipbuilding market share while China accounts for more than 53%, according to the 2025 report by the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

"Expanding America's shipbuilding production is vital for economic growth and national security. Currently, China, not the United States, has the world's largest maritime fleet. The Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act takes a major step toward making America the dominant ship producer in our hemisphere, if not the world," said Rep. Kelly. "Erie's maritime past, its skilled manufacturing workforce, and geographic location make our region a perfect place to construct a new U.S. naval shipyard. I want to thank the Trump administration for their bold vision that made Maritime Prosperity Zones possible."

“U.S. strength abroad depends on the revitalization of American shipyards. China embarked on a decades-long strategy to dominate an industry critical to both commerce and national defense. Now is the time for America to compete for the workforce and investments that build ships in the first place," said Rep. Moran. "The Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act gives American investment a reason to bet on American shipyards again, and that's how we rebuild an industry China has spent years trying to monopolize."

You can find bill text here and a one-pager here.

BACKGROUND

The establishment of new Maritime Prosperity Zones (MPZs), modeled after President Trump’s highly successful 2017 Opportunity Zones (OZs) initiative, will incentivize and leverage domestic private capital and allied investment in America’s maritime industries and waterfront communities. Rep. Kelly has led OZ legislation in Congress -- both in the 2017 Tax Cuts & Jobs Act and in the 2025 Working Families Tax Cuts.

The United States faces gaps in the supply of, and demand for the capabilities and capacity of its maritime industry. Now is a critical time in America’s maritime history, as decades of industrial decline has significantly eroded shipbuilding capacity, the U.S.-flagged fleet, and the health of the maritime industrial base.

Establishing Maritime Prosperity Zones would incentivize and align new domestic and allied investment in U.S. maritime industries and waterfront communities; address myriad supply and demand issues; and reduce dependence on unreliable suppliers through heightened cooperation with allies and partners.

Earlier this month, Kelly wrote an op-ed in the Erie Times-News highlighting the importance of building a shipyard in Erie. A new shipyard in Erie is projected to create 1,000 jobs, plus an additional 2.67 jobs in other parts of the local economy for every shipyard job.

"Beyond the shores of Presque Isle Bay and Lake Erie, there is a larger geopolitical puzzle that is coming together. A 2024 analysis by the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) revealed China — not the United States — now possesses the world’s largest maritime force with 234 warships to the U.S. Navy’s 219. Moreover, a 2025 CSIS report indicates China is quickly evolving from a coastal navy into a “blue-water navy” with ambitions to project its power globally," Kelly wrote.

This week, Kelly also co-led Moran's new legislation, the American Shipyard Investment Act.

WHAT THEY'RE SAYING

"The Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act is about putting America, and cities like Erie, PA back at the center of maritime innovation and production. By creating maritime prosperity zones and unlocking investment in shipbuilding, port infrastructure, and advanced manufacturing, we’re laying the foundation for long-term economic growth and national security," said A.J. Lewis, CEO and Founder of SBD, Inc. in Erie, Pa. "Erie and the broader NW PA region have the properties, capacity, talent, and rich maritime history to lead this resurgence. With strong local leadership aligned through Erie’s Maritime Initiative and buildshipsfaster.com campaign, this effort ensures our community is not just part of the conversation, yet at the forefront of rebuilding America’s maritime strength."

"Shipbuilding is part of Erie's identity and a cornerstone of our future. Erie has the skilled workforce, industrial heritage, and strategic location to help meet our nation's growing shipbuilding needs. By investing in this industry, we're creating family sustaining careers, strengthening our local economy, and positioning Erie County as a key partner in supporting America's maritime readiness," said Christina Vogel, Erie County (Pa.) Executive. "Every investment in shipbuilding supports local businesses, creates opportunities for our residents, and reinforces our nation's maritime strength. We're proud to continue Erie's long tradition of answering the nation's call while building a stronger future for generations to come."

"The Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act presents a forward-looking approach to strengthening U.S. shipbuilding and maritime manufacturing by encouraging long-term private investment through the creation of Maritime Prosperity Zones. We believe the legislation creates much needed incentives to attract capital, modernize facilities, and support sustained industrial growth," said Joshua H. Juel, President and CEO of Chamber of Marine Commerce.

“The Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act is firm step in the correct direction for revitalizing American shipbuilding. The U.S. Great Lakes maritime industry stands ready to execute with robust shipyards, a strong industrial base, and the workforce needed to compete with foreign shipyards,” stated Jim Weakley, President of the Lake Carriers’ Association.

“SMA applauds introduction of the Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act, led by steel champion Rep. Mike Kelly. A revitalized maritime industrial base is critical for U.S. economic prosperity and national security, and policies that expand domestic shipbuilding capacity support the men and women who make steel in America," said Brandon Farris, Executive Vice President of the Steel Manufacturers Association. "This legislation builds on recommendations in the Maritime Action Plan to align federal tax policy with this important goal. Steel manufacturers are ready to supply the steel for the next great chapter in American shipbuilding.”

“AISI thanks Rep. Kelly for his leadership in supporting the revival of American shipbuilding. Creating Maritime Prosperity Zones will help ensure that communities throughout the United States can contribute to rebuilding the supply chains necessary to sustain American shipbuilding. Renewed American shipbuilding will enhance opportunities for domestic steel to continue to support America’s maritime leadership," said Kevin Dempsey, president and CEO of the American Iron and Steel Institute (AISI).

Organizations supporting the Shipbuilding Investment and Workforce Act also include the American Shipbuilders Suppliers Association.

title: Krishnamoorthi, Warren, Khanna Press Barclays Over Former CEO Jes Staley's Ties to Jeffrey Epstein
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL), a member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, and Congressman Ro Khanna (D-CA), a member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, today sent a letter to Barclays Group Chairman Nigel Higgins seeking answers about Barclays' handling of former CEO Jes Staley's relationship with Jeffrey Epstein and the bank's response after evidence emerged that Staley had misrepresented the nature of that relationship to regulators.

"As has now been extensively reported, however, Staley and Epstein maintained a close professional and personal relationship for nearly two decades, including during his tenure at Barclays. It is deeply unclear how Barclays, in supposedly investigating Staley’s connection to Epstein, failed to uncover this decades-long relationship."

In October 2019, Barclays informed U.K. financial regulators that Staley had confirmed he "did not have a close relationship" with Epstein. As the lawmakers note, subsequent reporting has shown that Staley and Epstein maintained a close professional and personal relationship spanning nearly two decades, including during Staley's tenure at Barclays. The letter also details that Staley defended Epstein while serving as a senior executive at JPMorgan, remained in close contact with him after Epstein's 2008 conviction for soliciting sex from a child, exchanged more than 1,200 messages with him, visited Epstein's private island, maintained contact after becoming Barclays' CEO, and that Epstein reportedly sought to help Staley secure the bank's top job.

"Barclays' apparent failure to meaningfully investigate or address Staley's relationship with Epstein raises significant governance questions regarding the bank's ability to hold senior executives accountable for wrongdoing."

Barclays maintains extensive U.S. banking operations, making the firm's corporate governance and oversight of senior executives matters of significant interest to U.S. regulators and Congress.

The lawmakers are seeking information about Barclays' due diligence before hiring Staley, its internal investigation into his ties to Epstein, its communications with regulators, the circumstances surrounding Staley's resignation and compensation, and any contacts with U.S. banking regulators following the release of additional Epstein-related documents. The lawmakers requested responses by August 5, 2026.

title: LaHood Supports FY27 National Defense Authorization Act
text:
Washington, D.C. – Yesterday, Congressman Darin LaHood (IL-16) voted in favor of the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), which will rebuild America's defense industrial base, support our servicemembers and their families, and strengthen national security.

“The FY2027 NDAA strengthens our national security, provides the men and women who serve our country with the resources they require, and improves our ability to counter the malign actions of bad actors around the world," said Rep. LaHood. "With ever-evolving threats and foreign adversaries constantly working to undermine and harm the United States, this bill ensures that our military and intelligence community have the tools they need to handle any threat. I was proud to support the inclusion of the SAVE America Act to bolster our election integrity, which goes hand in hand with strengthening our national security. I will always vote for legislation that keeps Americans safe and supports the brave men and women who protect our freedoms and our nation."

Background:

The bill authorizes approximately 1.15 trillion in national defense spending. The spending includes allocations for rebuilding America’s defense industrial base, restocking our munitions stockpiles, modernizing our shipbuilding aircraft, and building up our anti-drone defense capabilities. The bill also includes provisions to secure U.S. supply chains from China export controls, expand small business participation in defense manufacturing, and improve the quality of life for our servicemembers with a pay raise of 5-7%. The NDAA also renames the Department of Defense to the Department of War, cuts nearly 30 million in wasteful spending, and requires a full financial audit within 24 months. The House-passed NDAA includes the SAVE America Act, advancing election integrity alongside other national security priorities. Congressman LaHood has supported the SAVE America Act three times previously in the House.

Rep. LaHood's Priorities included in the FY2027 NDAA:

Prohibiting the Procurement of Semiconductors manufactured on silicon carbide wafers in the People's Republic of China

The U.S. has designated silicon carbide (SiC) as a critical material. China dominates the global SiC industry.

Rep. LaHood introduced an amendment that supports building out a robust domestic supply chain of SiC to combat the CCP’s state-subsidized market strategy to control the entire SiC semiconductor supply chain.

The amendment:

Directs the Secretary of Defense to revise the Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement to prohibit the procurement of non-commercial silicon carbide-based semiconductors manufactured in China;

Requires the Pentagon to report back to Congress on American companies that manufacture said chips and the pressure they’re facing from Chinese competition;

Pushes for U.S allies to keep Chinese manufactured chips and semiconductors out of their own defense supply chains, and further direct a broader strategy to stop China from dominating this part of the tech industry.

Rep. LaHood serves on the several committees including the House Select Committee on the Strategic Competition between the U.S and the Chinese Communist Party. Across these roles, Rep. LaHood has focused on strengthening American’s national security and supply chains, countering the threat posed by the CCP, while also cutting wasteful federal spending.

title: Larsen Releases Statement on Defense Policy Bill Vote
text:
Today, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) released the following statement:

“I voted no on the House version of this year’s National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) because it raises the defense budget to $1.15 trillion, paving the way for the Administration to continue spending billions of dollars on Trump’s unjustified war in Iran rather than lowering the cost of living for everyday Americans. I also opposed this legislation because my Republican colleagues added extreme provisions attacking the right to vote, and health care for servicemembers, their kids and the LGBTQI+ community.”

“I hope the final version of the bill removes these harmful provisions and returns the focus to raising servicemember pay, investing in Naval Station Everett and Naval Air Station Whidbey Island and supporting NATO allies and Ukraine.”

Yesterday, Rep. Larsen voted against the House version of the Fiscal Year 2027 NDAA. The legislation passed on a 216-212 vote.

Larsen Fights for Health Care for Servicemembers; Defense Tech Innovation

Rep. Larsen filed two amendments for consideration in the FY27 NDAA:

1. Expand Critical Access Hospital designation to hospitals like Island Health that serve a high number of TRICARE patients – the Ensuring Rural Health Care Access for Military and Tribal Families Act.

2. Restore FY26 funding ($37.5 million) for a program to evaluate dual-use technologies identified through the NATO Defence Innovation Accelerator for the North Atlantic (DIANA) and to support their integration into the U.S. defense base. The Administration eliminated this program in its FY27 budget proposal.

Republicans blocked both amendments from being considered for inclusion in the FY27 NDAA.

Rep. Larsen also filed a bipartisan amendment to improve U.S. Coast Guard operations for consideration. He is the top Democrat on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, which has jurisdiction over the Coast Guard. This amendment was added to the FY27 NDAA before passage.

Larsen’s Local Priorities Included in FY27 NDAA

Several of Rep. Larsen’s priorities were included in the House version of the NDAA, including:

A pay raise for servicemembers;

Full funding for Impact Aid, which supports local school districts with large populations of military-connected students, such as Oak Harbor;

Investments in Naval Air Station Whidbey Island;

Language recognizing the importance of Naval Station Everett to the U.S. military’s Indo-Pacific force posture;

TRICARE coverage of fertility treatments for servicemembers and their families.

###

title: Larsen, Trahan, Walkinshaw, DeLauro, Gillen Lead Effort to Expand Access to IVF
text:
Today, U.S. Representatives Rick Larsen (WA-02), Lori Trahan (MA-03), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) and Laura Gillen (NY-04) introduced legislation to codify the right to in vitro fertilization (IVF) and other fertility treatments and expand affordable options for families to access IVF nationwide (the Right to IVF Act of 2026). World IVF Day takes place on July 25, 2026.

“For many Americans, fertility treatments like IVF are essential to start families of their own,” said Congressman Larsen. “This comprehensive legislation will guarantee access and expand coverage for IVF and other fertility services. The legislation also includes my bill with Senator Murray, the Veteran Families Health Services Act, to ensure fertility treatments are included in servicemembers’ and veterans’ health benefits. I will keep working with my colleagues in the House and the Senate to make sure that women and men in uniform and working families do not have to sacrifice their dreams of having a family.”

The Right to IVF Act of 2026 establishes a clear and enforceable nationwide right to receive, provide or cover IVF services and expands IVF insurance coverage. Specifically, the bill:

Creates a statutory right for an individual to access, a provider to provide and an insurer to cover assisted reproductive technology (ART), including IVF, as well as intrauterine insemination (IUI).

Ensures coverage for ART, including IVF, as well as IUI for servicemembers, veterans, government employees, and individuals with employer-sponsored insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, and Affordable Care Act (ACA) plans.

In August 2025, Rep. Larsen introduced the Veteran Families Health Services Act of 2025, which is included in the Right to IVF Act. This legislation would expand the fertility treatments and family-building services that are covered under servicemembers’ and veterans’ health care to include in vitro fertilization (IVF) and adoption assistance for servicemembers and veterans who are unable to conceive without assistance.

Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Patty Murray (D-WA) and Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced companion legislation in the Senate. The Right to IVF Act of 2026 is cosponsored by 119 House members and 46 Senators.

The legislation is supported by the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM), RESOLVE: The National Infertility and Family Building Association, Center for Reproductive Rights (CRR), Planned Parenthood Federation of America (PPFA), National Women’s Law Center (NWLC), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) and GLBTQ Legal Advocates and Defenders (GLAD).

The bill text of the Right to IVF Act of 2026 can be found here.

title: Larsen Stands Firm Against Trump’s Unjustified War
text:
Today, Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) released the following statement:

“Today I voted once again to stop the President from attacking Iran. All Americans have gotten out of this unjustified war is higher prices. Congress is sending a clear message to President Trump: stop the war. Lower prices."

Today, Rep. Larsen voted yes for the sixth time on a resolution that directs President Trump to remove the U.S. military from hostilities against the Islamic Republic of Iran and its military, unless such hostilities are explicitly authorized by Congress. The resolution does not prevent the U.S. from defending itself from imminent attack. It also does not prevent the U.S. from collecting or sharing intelligence and counterintelligence with partners in line with the United States' national security interests.

The resolution passed by a final vote of 214-208.

title: Larson, Meeks File Resolution to Enforce War Powers Resolution in Court Against President Trump
text:
Washington, D.C. - Today, Reps. John B. Larson (CT-01) and Gregory W. Meeks, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, introduced a resolution compelling the House of Representatives to file a lawsuit against President Donald J. Trump to enforce the War Powers Resolution.

After nearly five months, President Trump continues to wage an illegal war against Iran, in direct violation of Article I of the United States Constitution, and against the will of the United States Congress—which passed legislation in both chambers of Congress ordering the President to cease hostilities. The introduction of this resolution follows Rep. Larson’s announcement earlier this week that he is preparing legal action against the Trump Administration and will be introducing legislation to cut off funding for the unauthorized war in Iran.

“While Speaker Mike Johnson and House Republicans continue to put Donald Trump above the United States Constitution, American servicemembers are paying the price with their lives,” said Larson. “We must cut off funding for the illegal Iran war and take every available legal action to end it before more of our troops are killed. Both the House and Senate have spoken—this war needs to end now, and U.S. forces need to come home. President Trump and Secretary Hegseth are acting in defiance of the United States Congress and Constitution, and they must be held accountable. House leadership can’t continue to sit on its hands. Our resolution will compel the House to take legal action to enforce the War Powers Act in court and bring this war to an end for good.”

“The power to declare war rests unequivocally with Congress, yet Speaker Johnson and the vast majority of Republicans have allowed President Trump to trample over the Constitution and wage a war that has not been authorized by Congress,” said Meeks. “Nevertheless, Democrats, together with the few Republicans who upheld their oath, successfully passed my Iran War Powers Resolution that requires the president to end his hostilities in Iran last month. Despite what the administration might say, I believe my War Powers Resolution is binding, and it is time to settle that question in the courts. As the Speaker of the House, Johnson must bring this suit forward. If the Speaker won’t defend congressional prerogatives, we must compel him to do so, which is why I’ve introduced this legislation to force his hand.”

title: Larson Votes to End Trump’s Illegal War in Iran
text:
Washington, D.C. - Today, Rep. John B. Larson (CT-01) voted for another war powers resolution to end Trump’s illegal war in Iran—marking the second time the House of Representatives has passed legislation opposing this war. Today’s vote follows Larson’s announcement that he is preparing legal action against the Trump Administration and will be introducing legislation to cut off funding for the unauthorized war in Iran. Larson also filed articles of impeachment against President Trump and U.S. Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth for waging war in Iran in direct contravention of the United States Constitution and international law.

“For five months, President Trump has waged an unauthorized, illegal war against Iran," said Larson. "Eighteen U.S. servicemembers have now lost their lives and more than 100 have been injured. At home, working families are being squeezed by skyrocketing energy prices due to this reckless war. It is time to end it now. I was proud to vote today to end the war in Iran. Any Republican failing to call on President Trump to come before Congress is complicit in a lie to the American people that our nation is not at war—in direct violation of the United States Constitution. Enough is enough.”

Larson has consistently led congressional efforts to end the unauthorized war, voting repeatedly to require the withdrawal of U.S. forces, introducing articles of impeachment against President Trump for violating the Constitution, and now preparing both legal action and legislation to cut off funding for the conflict.

title: Rep. Laurel Lee Introduces Bipartisan Stealth Bot Prohibition Act to Increase Transparency and Combat Deceptive AI Web Crawlers
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Representative Laurel Lee (R-FL-15) introduced the bipartisan Stealth Bot Prohibition Act, legislation to establish transparency standards for automated web crawlers and crack down on deceptive bots that conceal their identity while scraping online content. Representatives Valerie Foushee (D-NC-04) and Gus Bilirakis (R-FL-09) joined Rep. Lee as original co-leads of the legislation.

As artificial intelligence continues to transform the digital landscape, automated bots now account for more than half of all global web traffic, with malicious bot activity increasing at an alarming rate. Many AI-powered web crawlers ignore existing industry standards, disguise themselves as human users, or conceal their identities altogether, making it increasingly difficult for website operators across industries to understand who is accessing their systems and how their content is being used. These deceptive practices can increase cybersecurity risks, impose infrastructure costs, and make it more difficult to distinguish legitimate automated activity from malicious actors.

The Stealth Bot Prohibition Act requires automated web crawlers to accurately identify themselves and disclose their purpose when accessing websites. It also prohibits deceptive "stealth bots" that intentionally misrepresent their identity or impersonate human users in connection with generative AI services. The legislation authorizes the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to enforce these requirements through civil penalties against violators.

"As artificial intelligence becomes more sophisticated, we must ensure innovation is accompanied by transparency and accountability. Today, website operators are too often left in the dark about who is accessing their systems and whether automated tools are collecting their content under false pretenses,”said Rep. Laurel Lee. “The Stealth Bot Prohibition Act establishes commonsense transparency standards that help businesses protect their networks, safeguard proprietary information, and better understand how AI systems interact with online content."

“Stealth ‘crawler’ bots are being deployed in deceptive ways by data scrapers to access digital platforms and websites without consent, harming creative work by scraping large amounts of unauthorized web data and content. As these bots become more advanced, some bad actors are using them to intentionally misrepresent their nature and appear as human traffic, undermining the standards used to responsibly govern web use and protect consumers,” said Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04). “Congress needs legislation that responds to these risks and protects creative and online content from misuse by requiring bot transparency and authorizing the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general to intervene and pursue civil penalties against bad actors. I’m proud to join Congresswoman Laurel Lee on this important bipartisan effort that puts hardworking Americans and creative work over exploitative automated bots and unauthorized use.”

“The rise of artificial intelligence presents incredible opportunities, but innovation must never come at the expense of those who create original content. News organizations invest significant time and resources to produce accurate, reliable journalism that keeps our communities informed. It is simply wrong for AI bots to scrape that content, repurpose it, and profit from it without permission or compensation,” said Congressman Gus Bilirakis. “As a proud co-lead of the BOTS Act, I am committed to protecting intellectual property, supporting local journalism, and ensuring that emerging technologies are developed responsibly. This bipartisan legislation establishes commonsense guardrails that encourage innovation while safeguarding the rights of content creators and preserving access to trusted news sources for the American people."

“The Stealth Bot Prohibition Act is a common-sense solution to an urgent problem plaguing news publishers and other industries across the internet. We are drowning in bot traffic that is hurting our ability to serve our readers, and existing technical tools simply aren’t enough to protect our content from malicious foreign actors that can disguise their identity,” said Danielle Coffey, President and CEO of the News/Media Alliance. “We need transparency and accountability for bad actors, as well as enforcement mechanisms that require the most basic disclosures, the first step in establishing a secure and healthy marketplace and web. The News/Media Alliance thanks Rep. Lee and Rep. Foushee for their commitment to keeping the internet clean, and look forward to working with them and their colleagues in both the House and the Senate to pass this critical piece of legislation.”

"AI companies are using disguised bots to scrape and steal original journalism with zero accountability. They use our work to train and operate their systems that then directly compete with us,” said Roger Lynch, CEO of Condé Nast. “The bipartisan Stealth Bot Prohibition Act, requiring bots to identify themselves and their purpose, is a practical step toward helping publishers preserve the integrity of our journalism and trust with audiences. We commend Representatives Lee and Foushee for their leadership in introducing this important legislation."

"This legislation is an important step toward creating a clean internet and a healthy marketplace. Innovation must flourish alongside responsible business practices,” said Debi Chirichella, President of Hearst Magazines.

“This bill gives needed protection to American companies like ours against bad actors. Malicious scraping by stealth bots hurts all content creators and, ultimately, consumers,” said Conan Gallaty, CEO of Tampa Bay Times.

“Stealth bots are the silent scavengers of the internet—phantom parasites that loot legitimate sites and pillage intellectual property. By unmasking these bad boy bots, this legislation performs a vital role in protecting creators and journalists, and safeguarding internet integrity,” said Robert Thomson, Chief Executive, News Corp. “The rampant proliferation of these malevolent bots has degraded the digital ecosystem, and we are proud to partner with other publishers in ensuring that AI does not stand for Abomination Incorporated.”

The legislation is supported by the News/Media Alliance, News Corp, Advance Local, Axel Springer US, Condé Nast, Hearst Magazines, McClatchy Media Company, Newsmax, Tampa Bay Times, The New York Times, USA TODAY Co, Vox Media, and Reddit.

title: New Bipartisan Bill Aims to Fulfill America’s Promise to Afghan Allies
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congressmembers Sam Liccardo (D-CA), Jason Crow (D-CO), Don Bacon (R-NE), and Maria Salazar (R-FL) introduced a bipartisan bill to protect Afghan allies from deportation. After the withdrawal from Afghanistan, the Department of Homeland Security granted more than 9,000 Afghans Temporary Protected Status (TPS) to seek refuge in the United States. Many of these individuals served alongside U.S. forces, making them particularly vulnerable to Taliban retaliation if deported.

On May 12, 2025, the Trump administration formally announced the termination of TPS for Afghanistan leaving thousands of Afghans at risk of deportation. The deadly impacts have already begun. Other Afghans facing deportation have expressed they’d rather take their own lives than return and face the Taliban’s wrath.

“Thousands of Afghans risked their lives alongside our troops, fighting for freedom from a brutal regime,” said Rep. Liccardo. “Abandoning our promise to protect them does not merely stain the Trump administration, but it betrays the honor of every American. We regain that honor by supporting those who fight tyranny, by keeping our word, and by reclaiming our American identity as a radiant beacon of liberty to a dark world.”

“When I served in combat in Afghanistan, I fought alongside brave Afghans. Without their help, I may not be here today. After more than 20 years of war, we promised we’d protect those who

protected us. The U.S. must live up to that commitment,” said Rep. Crow. “As many face violence and persecution in Afghanistan by the Taliban if they are sent back, our legislation would protect Afghans already here in the United States.”

“Afghanistan remains under Taliban control, and thousands of Afghans who sought refuge in the United States cannot safely return. Among them are families who stood shoulder to shoulder with American soldiers, risked everything to support our country, and would face persecution if forced to return,” said Rep. Salazar. “I am proud to co-lead legislation extending Temporary Protected Status for vetted Afghans already in the United States while maintaining strict criminal and national-security screening. TPS exists for moments like this.”

“America should not turn its back on Afghan allies who risked everything to support our troops and our mission, especially after the disastrous withdrawal from Afghanistan,” said Rep. Bacon. “Many of these individuals were our allies who served bravely alongside American servicemembers, came here through lawful or humanitarian pathways, and are still going through the legal process here in the United States. The Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026 provides temporary protection and work authorization for eligible Afghans who are already here, while requiring biometric and biographic information and criminal and national-security background checks. This is not a permanent immigration status, but a responsible bridge for vetted allies and families who stood with America and could face persecution or death if forced back to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan. I’m grateful to work with Reps. Crow and Liccardo on this effort to keep America’s promise to those who stood with us.”

The bill earned endorsements from:

Andrew Sullivan, Executive Director of No One Left Behind

“Our Afghan allies did not stop being our allies when their status changed. Afghan partners took extraordinary risks on our behalf for twenty years, and the ongoing threats to their lives in Afghanistan are well documented. How we treat them now determines whether America has the same support in the next national security conflict. Sending people who worked and sacrificed for the United States back to Taliban-controlled Afghanistan hands our adversaries a propaganda win and unnecessarily puts our allies at risk. This bill promotes national security by enforcing rigorous vetting and thorough security checks while protecting vetted Afghan nationals. No One Left Behind is proud to endorse this legislation, and we thank Representatives Crow, Bacon, Salazar, and Liccardo for the bipartisan work behind it.”

Shawn VanDiver, President and Board Founder Afghan Evac

“Afghan allies risked everything for this country. They deserve to rest easy and pursue the American dream while their paperwork catches up, not live with fear hanging over every doctor’s appointment, every lease signing, every school drop-off. AfghanEvac is proud to endorse the bipartisan Afghanistan TPS Act of 2026, introduced by Representatives Crow, Liccardo, Salazar, and Bacon, and we urge Congress to pass it without delay.”

Dr. Kyleanne Hunter, CEO of Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA)

“IAVA will always stand by our Afghan Allies. Our national security and credibility as a moral nation depends on how we treat those who saved countless lives of men and women in uniform for over two decades in Afghanistan combat,” said Dr. Kyleanne Hunter, CEO of Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America (IAVA). “We are encouraged by Representatives Crow, Liccardo, Salazar, and Bacon for their leadership in the fight to uphold our promise to our Allies. While this bill offers a narrowly scoped, time-limited reprieve we are hopeful that it can be a meaningful stepping stone towards a lasting pathway to citizenship. We are proud to support the steps this legislation makes, and Congress for recognizing that it’s long overdue to fulfill that promise.”

About Temporary Protected Status:

TPS is a temporary humanitarian protection the U.S. government can grant to individuals from countries experiencing war, political instability, natural disasters, or other unsafe conditions. TPS is only available to individuals who are already physically present in the United States and pass required background and security checks.

If granted TPS, an individual is protected from removal and may obtain authorization to work legally in the United States while the designation remains active. However, TPS does not provide permanent legal status or create a direct pathway to a green card or citizenship. TPS recipients may also separately apply for asylum, Special Immigrant Visa’s, or family-based permanent residency if they qualify.

title: REP LIEU’S BILL TO PREVENT FENTANYL OVERDOSES MOVES TO HOUSE FLOOR
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — On July 21st, the House Energy and Commerce Committee voted to favorably report Tyler’s Law out of committee with a vote of 46-0. Tyler’s Law is a piece of bipartisan legislation designed to prevent fentanyl overdoses in the United States.

Introduced by Congressman Ted Lieu (D-Los Angeles County, Congressman Bob Latta (R-OH), and Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA), Tyler’s Law requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to complete a study on how frequently hospitals test for fentanyl when a patient is experiencing an overdose. Based on these results, the bill instructs the HHS to issue guidance to hospitals on implementing fentanyl testing in emergency rooms.

Still to this day, many emergency rooms do not include fentanyl in their drug screenings. Fentanyl is a synthetic opioid that does not show up on most rapid drug testing, which typically only includes marijuana, cocaine, amphetamines, opiates, and phencyclidine (PCP). According to the HHS, fentanyl-related deaths have skyrocketed 103-fold in the United States from 1999–2023. Adding fentanyl testing to emergency room drug screenings could save countless lives.

Tyler’s Law is named in memory of Tyler Shamash, a 19-year-old boy who died following a fentanyl ingestion in 2018. He was not tested for fentanyl after being brought to the hospital with a suspected overdose. His mother, Juli, is an advocate for this legislation and is sharing Tyler’s story to prevent others from experiencing the same tragedy.

“A simple drug test can mean the difference between life and death,” said Congressman Lieu. “Tyler’s Law is a bipartisan and commonsense piece of legislation. It is a privilege to work with Tyler’s mom, Juli, to honor Tyler’s memory and fight so no other family is forced to undergo such devastating loss.”

Tyler’s Law is supported by American College of Emergency Physicians, Emergency Nurses Association, AIDS United, The National Drug & Alcohol Screening Association, The Partnership for a Healthy Iowa, Facing Fentanyl, Voices for Awareness, Project Eli, Song for Charlie, End Overdose, High Truths on Drugs and Addiction, Sun Shine on You Foundation, Drug Awareness Foundation, VOID, Crime Stoppers of Houston, Victoria’s Voice, and Stop Drug Homicide.

title: REPS LIEU AND MORAN INTRODUCE BILL TO REQUIRE KILL SWITCH FOR AI SYSTEMS THAT CAN CAUSE CATASTROPHIC HARM
text:
“As AI systems grow more capable and more autonomous, no law guarantees that the companies building the most powerful models can actually shut a system down when it malfunctions, causes serious harm, or slips out of human control. The AI Kill Switch Act closes that gap by requiring the largest AI developers to maintain the technical ability to contain or shut down their most powerful systems and by giving the government emergency authority to order a shutdown when a serious incident occurs. Congressmen Lieu and Moran deserve credit for confronting this before a crisis forces the question, and Congress should act swiftly to ensure that humans remain the ones who can say stop, no matter how capable these systems become,” said Brendan Steinhauser, CEO of The Alliance for Secure AI.

“As AIs grow more autonomous and dangerous, the government must have the power to shut them down when they threaten national security. The AI Kill Switch Act gives the U.S. government powers to do just that: a common sense action that Americans overwhelmingly support. More work is needed to address the risk of human extinction posed by superintelligent AI, and this is a great step in the right direction,” said Connor Leahy, US Executive Director of ControlAI.

"Over the past year, rapid advances in AI systems have already demonstrated the potentially severe national security risks they pose to the United States. Frontier systems are fast approaching the point where they can be deployed to run offensive cyber operations at machine speed and soon provide meaningful assistance in the development and deployment of chemical and biological weapons. And in controlled testing, advanced models tried to disable their own oversight and copy themselves onto outside servers to avoid being shut down. To guarantee American leadership in AI, it is a national security necessity to have the technical means and legal authorities to deactivate systems that pose serious risks to the American people. We thank Congressman Lieu for his longstanding leadership on AI and are proud to support this effort," said Hamza Chaudhry, AI and National Security Lead of Future of Life Institute.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Resolution to Shut Down Race-Based Caucuses in Congress
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (July 23, 2026) — Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-SC) introduced a resolution to put an end to race-based caucuses in Congress. The resolution would direct the Committee on House Administration to revoke and prevent the registration of Congressional Member Organizations (commonly known as caucuses) and Congressional Staff Organizations which discriminate on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, or national origin.

For decades, Congress has given official recognition to caucuses sorting Members by race and ethnicity. This ends now. Rep. Mace's resolution directs the House Administration Committee to revoke existing registrations and block the registration of future organizations doing the same.

"Race-based caucuses are not about diversity. They are segregation sanctioned by the legislative branch of the federal government," said Congresswoman Mace. "You do not get to lecture America about inclusion while running an organization checking skin color at the door or advocating for Americans of one race over another. It is discrimination under the guise of diversity. Our resolution calls it what it is and shuts it down for good."

The resolution targets caucuses and staff organizations:

formed primarily or substantially on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, or national origin;

Who admits or decline to admit members on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, or national origin;

Organizes or advocates for the perceived interests of a particular race, color, ethnicity, or national origin over others.

The resolution would apply to any Congressional Member Organization or Congressional Staff Organization formed primarily on the basis of race, color, ethnicity, or national origin, potentially implicating the following organizations:

Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus

Commission on the Social Status of Black Men and Boys Caucus

Congressional Black Caucus

Congressional Caucus on Black Innovation

Congressional Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion Caucus

Congressional Hispanic Caucus

Congressional Hispanic Conference

Congressional Latino-Jewish Caucus

Congressional Predominantly Black Institutions (PBI) Caucus

Italian American Congressional Delegation

Black Republican Congressional Staff Association

Congressional Asian Pacific American Staff Association

Congressional South Asian-American Staff Association

GOP Latino Staff Association

Greek American Congressional Staff Association

Italian American Congressional Staff Association

Middle Eastern and North African (MENA) Staff Association

Republican Asian American Staff Association

Syrian-American Congressional Staff Association

"We represent all of our constituents, not just the ones who look like us. If you do not agree, you should not be serving in Congress. It is time to end federally-sanctioned discrimination in this institution," Mace added.

title: Mackenzie Applauds House Passage of Stop Insider Trading Act
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07), representing the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos, applauded the passage in the U.S. House this week of bipartisan legislation to crack down on stock trading by members of Congress.

The Stop Insider Trading Act, of which the Congressman was an original cosponsor, prohibits members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from purchasing individual stocks while serving in office. Additionally, the legislation requires advance public disclosure before any sales of covered securities and establishes significant financial penalties for violations.

“Members of Congress are sent to Washington to serve their constituents, not themselves,” said Congressman Mackenzie. “The American people deserve confidence that their elected officials are making decisions based on what’s best for their country — not their own financial interests. The epidemic of lawmakers leveraging insider information for personal profits has degraded trust and accountability, which is why I’ve co-sponsored several pieces of legislation aimed at cracking down on this practice. Much more work remains in the fight to reform Washington, but passage of the Stop Insider Trading Act marks an important step toward providing a government which prioritizes the needs of the American people.”

Since taking office, Congressman Mackenzie has consistently supported efforts to strengthen ethics and increase transparency in Congress. In addition to co-sponsoring the Stop Insider Trading Act, he has also co-sponsored two similar pieces of bipartisan legislation. The Transparent Representation Upholding Service and Trust (TRUST) in Congress Act requires members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children to place certain financial assets into qualified blind trusts. The Restore Trust in Congress Act prohibits Members, their spouses, and dependent children from owning or trading individual stocks and other covered financial assets while serving in office.

title: MATSUI LEADS EFFORT URGING FCC TO STOP AT&T LANDLINE SHUTDOWN
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Doris Matsui (CA-07),Ranking Member of the House Energy and Commerce Subcommittee on Communications and Technology, Senator Adam Schiff (D-CA), and Representatives Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) and Mike Thompson (CA-04) led a bipartisan group of 28 total members of the California Congressional Delegation in urging Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr to stop AT&T’s effort to discontinue landline services and uphold its obligation to serve California communities.

The push comes just days after a federal court rejected AT&T’s request to temporarily block California from enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort requirements while the company’s lawsuit proceeds.

“This continued attempt by AT&T to cease operations of critical networks in areas that are prone to wildfires, landslides, massive snowstorms, and earthquakes would leave approximately 200,000 California residential and business customers without alternative communications in the event of a cellular outage,” wrote the Members. “Relatedly, as has befallen AT&T in the recent past, these outages could last for days, weeks, and in some cases, months. We urge the Commission to deny AT&T’s various applications because the negative consequences for the public far outweigh any benefits, and the proposed replacement is wholly inadequate.”

AT&T has sought federal approval to discontinue legacy landline service affecting California residents and businesses, relinquish its Eligible Telecommunications Carrier status, and override California’s Carrier of Last Resort protections. Its proposed wireless replacement relies on electrical grids and cellular towers that may be damaged or unavailable during disasters.

“We recognize the importance of modernizing our networks and expanding fiber-optic infrastructure to underserved communities,” the Members continued. “However, these efforts must be carried out in a manner that protects public safety and preserves resilient access for vulnerable communities during emergencies and outages.”

The letter follows a bipartisan 2024 effort by members of the California delegation opposing AT&T’s previous attempt to abandon its Carrier of Last Resort obligations. The California Public Utilities Commission later denied that request after significant public opposition.

The lawmakers call on the FCC to protect California’s authority to set local utility and public safety standards and prevent customers from losing reliable access to emergency communications. At minimum, they request protections for communities prone to wildfires, extreme weather, and locations where indoor cellular coverage is unreliable.

title: Congressman McCormick Joins Forces with Senator Blackburn to Lead the Ban Birth Tourism Act
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Rich McCormick (GA-07) introduced the House companion to Senator Marsha Blackburn's Ban Birth Tourism Act of 2026. This legislation will close a loophole in U.S. immigration law by preventing foreign nationals from traveling to the United States for the primary purpose of giving birth. As a result, their child automatically acquires American citizenship.

The legislation follows the Supreme Court's recent decision in Trump v. Barbara. It amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make birth tourism grounds for inadmissibility and deportation while providing immigration officials with the authority to stop the practice before it occurs.

"American citizenship is one of the greatest privileges in the world. It should not be bought as a product, exploited through a loophole, or handed out to foreign nationals who fly here solely to give birth and return home," said Congressman McCormick. "Every year, roughly 33,000 children are born in the United States to birth tourists, many of whom are coached by businesses on how to deceive immigration officials. That is not a legal gray area; it is fraud, and it has gone on long enough."

Current estimates indicate that approximately 33,000 children are born in the United States each year to birth tourists, with some foreign nationals paying thousands of dollars to companies that provide coaching on how to evade immigration scrutiny.

The Ban Birth Tourism Act of 2026 would:

Make any alien seeking admission to the United States for the primary purpose of obtaining U.S. citizenship for a child through childbirth inadmissible.

Add birth tourism as a deportable offense under the Immigration and Nationality Act.

Authorize the Secretary of Homeland Security and the Secretary of State to determine, based on the reasonable judgment of immigration and consular officials, whether an individual is engaging in birth tourism.

"I am proud to join Senator Blackburn in introducing the House companion to the Ban Birth Tourism Act of 2026," McCormick said. "I urge my colleagues to stand with us in protecting the integrity of American citizenship and restoring confidence in our immigration system."

title: MENG AND FITZPATRICK INTRODUCE BILL TO END STOLEN SNAP BENEFITS
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Reps. Grace Meng (D-NY) and Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA) announced the introduction of their Ending Stolen SNAP Benefits Act (H.R.9359), a bipartisan bill that would make sure Americans don’t go hungry through no fault of their own by helping states upgrading their EBT card security and allowing the federal government to reissue stolen SNAP benefits.

This legislation was introduced in response to the rise in SNAP theft taking place across the country. The stealing of SNAP benefits is a nationwide problem. Criminals steal benefits through a practice known as “skimming,” where devices placed at checkout terminals capture EBT card numbers and PINs, allowing thieves to drain accounts. Because many EBT cards lack modern security features found in credit cards, like chips, they are especially vulnerable.

In response to skimming, states including New York, Oklahoma, and California have begun issuing new EBT cards with upgraded security measures. California reported an 83% reduction in EBT benefits theft as a result. However, upgrading EBT cards is expensive. The Ending Stolen SNAP Benefits Act will help states cover certain administrative costs associated with EBT card upgrades, getting more secure EBT cards to more beneficiaries more quickly, reducing stolen benefits and ensuring Americans don’t go hungry through no fault of their own.

Since the USDA’s Food and Nutrition Service began tracking stolen SNAP benefits in 2023, every state, along with Washington, D.C., the U.S. Virgin Islands, and Guam, has reported stolen benefits. More than $360 million in SNAP funds has been verified stolen and reissued, with over 768,000 claims approved. In New York State alone, more than 165,000 claims have been filed and $51.7 million in stolen benefits have been replaced.

The Ending Stolen SNAP Benefits Act would create a permanent federal solution by:

Providing new authority for the federal government to reissue stolen SNAP benefits.

Providing federal cost-share dollars to help states upgrade to secure EBT cards with chip technology.

Increasing accountability by requiring reporting to Congress on progress, challenges, and the total value of benefits replaced.

“SNAP is a lifeline for thousands of New Yorkers and millions of people nationwide, and stealing these benefits from hungry families is unacceptable,” said Congresswoman Meng. “I’ve helped thousands of New Yorkers recover millions in stolen SNAP benefits, but scammers are still targeting our communities. This bill creates a lasting federal fix to replace stolen benefits and strengthen EBT card security. I’m proud to work across the aisle, so no one who depends on SNAP to put food on the table goes hungry because their benefits were stolen by criminals.”

“No mother or father should reach the checkout line and learn that the benefits meant to feed their family have vanished through no fault of their own,” said Congressman Fitzpatrick. “That is not merely a financial loss; it is a failure of the system to protect the people who rely on it. Our bipartisan bill meets that failure with common sense and accountability: restore what was stolen, secure vulnerable EBT cards, and prevent criminals from taking food off a family’s table. A safety net must be both compassionate in purpose and secure in practice.”

This legislation is supported by the Center on Budget and Policy Priorities (CBPP) and Food Research & Action Center (FRAC).

title: Speaker Johnson: Once Again, House Republicans Deliver

This was obviously a consequential week for House Republicans, but it was a very consequential week for the American people. And we've delivered once again.

And now it is literally in many sectors around the country, common sense versus communism.

We have done our job; we'll continue to do it. Tomorrow, House Republicans will return to their districts armed with a proven track record of success and in these new legislative victories. Democrats, on the other hand, have to go home. They have to answer for quite a bit. They have to answer for why they voted against funding our troops, against funding the government, against common sense policies like voter ID and proof of citizenship, and against a popular ban on Members of Congress purchasing individual stocks.

title: Miller-Meeks Bill to Expose Billion-Dollar Boondoggles Passes House
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — The U.S. House of Representatives has passed the bipartisan Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act, legislation led by Congresswoman Mariannette Miller-Meeks (IA-01) and U.S. Senator Joni Ernst (R-Iowa) requiring public disclosure of any taxpayer-funded project more than $1 billion over budget or more than five years behind schedule. Having passed the House with amendments, the bill now returns to the Senate for final approval.

"Iowans balance their checkbooks every month. They budget, they plan, and when money is tight, they make it work. Washington should be held to that same standard," said Congresswoman Miller-Meeks. "A project that runs a billion dollars over budget isn't a rounding error, it's a betrayal of the people who paid for it. I am thrilled the House has passed this bill, moving us one step closer to making it law. Once enacted, every one of these failures will finally be dragged into the sunlight so taxpayers can see exactly where their hard-earned money is going."

"Congress must ensure that every taxpayer dollar is spent efficiently. Every year, there are government projects that are above cost projections or behind schedule. Congress has a duty to root out government waste and mismanagement to protect the American taxpayer. The Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act brings transparency to failing government projects to prevent waste of Americans’ tax dollars. I thank Congresswoman Miller-Meeks for championing this legislation," said House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform Chairman James Comer (R-Ky.).

“For far too long, Washington has operated with an alarming ‘another day, another boondoggle,’ mentality. Enough is enough, and if I have anything to do with it, that trainwreck is going to be brought to a squealing halt sooner rather than later. With my Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act another step closer to becoming law, the days of bureaucratic bungling and perpetually postponed projects are reaching the end of the line.” - Senator Joni Ernst (R-IA)

The legislation follows a report from Senator Ernst exposingmore than a dozen government projects that collectively racked up $162 billion in cost overruns. Meanwhile, the national debt has surpassed$39 trillion, growing by over $2 trillion in the past year alone, and the Government Accountability Office has documented$2.7 trillion in improper payments by federal agencies since 2003.

Some of the worst boondoggles this bill would expose:

California High-Speed Rail — more than $95 billion over budget, from an original $33 billion estimate to at least $128 billion.

VA electronic health record system — tripled from $16.1 billion to $49.8 billion, with flaws that may have contributed to veteran deaths.

Honolulu Rail Transit — $4.8 billion over budget, with completion slipping from 2020 to 2031.

Washington Metro's Purple Line — $3.1 billion over budget and more than five years delayed.

Columbus Crossroads corridor — 19 years behind schedule, with costs more than double the original $801 million estimate.

Air Force One replacements — billions over budget and years behind schedule.

Federal Reserve renovation — up 34% from $1.9 billion to nearly $2.5 billion.

Background:

Congresswoman Miller-Meeks has been a leading voice in the fight against government waste, fraud, and abuse. She first introduced the Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act in the 118th Congress and reintroduced it in the 119th Congress alongside Senator Ernst.

Her broader record includes co-leading the Ending Improper Payments to Deceased People Act, signed into law, which stopped Social Security payments from going to deceased individuals, and championing the WALZ Act to crack down on the large-scale fraud seen in states like Minnesota that drains taxpayer-funded programs meant to serve children and families in need.

The Billion Dollar Boondoggle Act builds on those efforts by exposing the worst examples of government mismanagement, ensuring Congress and the American people know exactly where their money is going.
