title: Rep. Sewell Recognizes Cancer Survivor and Iron Strong Award Recipient Yolanda Jackson
text:
Washington D.C. — Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) spoke on the House Floor to honor three-time cancer survivor Yolanda Jackson. On Friday, July 24, the O'Neal Comprehensive Cancer Center at the University of Alabama at Birmingham will honor Ms. Jackson with their Iron Strong Survivor Award for overcoming her courageous battle with cancer.

Watch it on YouTube here.

Rep. Sewell: Mister Speaker, I rise today to honor a dear friend, an extraordinary woman of faith, and a living testament to courage and resilience—Ms. Yolanda Jackson.

This week, the O'Neal Comprehensive Center for Cancer at the University of Alabama at Birmingham will present Yolanda with its Iron Strong Award for her courageous battle with breast cancer. I cannot think of anyone more deserving of this recognition.

I have known Yolanda for more than twenty years. We became fast friends as neighbors in 2005 after we moved into the same apartment complex in Birmingham, Alabama. But our connection actually began years earlier. While working as a human resources consultant for the City of Selma in the early nineties, Yolanda became known to my mother, Nancy Gardner Sewell—Selma’s first Black City Councilwoman—and she adored Yolanda. It was a wonderful reminder of how small and how special our Alabama family can be.

Over the past two decades, we've celebrated life's blessings together, and we've stood beside one another through some of life's toughest moments. Yolanda has been there for me, just as I try to be there for her, and I am extraordinarily grateful for her friendship. My life is richer because she is in it.

Not long ago, after moving to Birmingham in 2005, Yolanda was diagnosed with breast cancer. She would go on to face two more cancer diagnoses, in 2022 and again in 2024.

Three cancer diagnoses. Three difficult battles. Three remarkable victories.

Throughout every step of that journey, Yolanda received exceptional care from the physicians, nurses, and staff at the O'Neal Comprehensive Cancer Center at UAB. Her final testimony was in October 2025. Her treatment was a success, and today I am grateful to say that she remains in remission.

When you ask Yolanda where she finds her strength, her answer is simple: her faith.

She believes that even at our hardest moments, God is at work. That through suffering, He walks beside us, gives us strength to endure, and uses our trials to shape our character, deepen our faith, and make us into the people He wants us to be.

Yolanda has lived that belief every day of her life.

She encourages everyone facing cancer to hold on to hope, to stay positive, never stop fighting. She believes we all need someone to love and something to look forward to and something to live for.

For Yolanda, that purpose shines brightest through her beautiful family. In 2019, she welcomed and adopted two precious twin boys, Ayden and Jayden, into her life. And last year, she opened her heart again by adopting their younger brother, Kyrie. Those three boys are truly blessed to have such a loving, faithful, and determined mom.

Today, we celebrate Yolanda. We also celebrate the extraordinary work of the O'Neal Comprehensive Cancer Center at UAB. Their groundbreaking research, innovative treatments, and compassionate care have transformed countless lives, and Yolanda's story is a powerful testament to their mission.

Today, we celebrate an Iron Strong survivor, my dear friend, Yolanda Jackson. More than that, we celebrate an Iron Strong woman—a faithful servant, a devoted mother, loyal friend, and an inspiration to everyone blessed enough to know her.

Congratulations, Yolanda, on this well-deserved honor. Your courage, your faith, and your unwavering hope inspire everyone who has been privileged to know you.

I ask my colleagues of the United States House of Representatives to join me in congratulating Ms. Yolanda Jackson and wishing her beautiful family many years of continued health, happiness, and God's abundant blessings.

Thank you, and I yield back the balance of my time. We love you, Yolanda.

title: Shreve Leads Indiana Delegation Resolution Supporting Freedom 250 Grand Prix
text:
WASHINGTON — Congressman Jefferson Shreve (IN-06) today introduced a resolution expressing support for the Freedom 250 Grand Prix, the first INDYCAR race ever held in the nation’s capital. Scheduled for Aug. 21-23, 2026, the event will bring one of Indiana’s signature traditions to Washington as part of America's 250th anniversary.

Each Memorial Day weekend, hundreds of thousands of fans from around the world attend the Indianapolis 500, the world’s largest single-day sporting event. This August, that Hoosier tradition comes to Washington, where INDYCAR drivers will race past some of the nation’s most recognizable landmarks on a street course surrounding the National Mall.

The resolution is cosponsored by every Indiana Republican in the U.S. House of Representatives, underscoring the delegation’s unified support for showcasing Indiana’s motorsports heritage during America’s 250th anniversary. Congressman Richard Hudson (NC-09), chairman of the Congressional Motorsports Caucus and the National Republican Congressional Committee, also joined as a cosponsor.

“Racing is Indiana’s gift to American sport,” said Rep. Jefferson Shreve (IN-06). “For the first time, INDYCAR will race through the streets of our nation’s capital during America’s 250th anniversary. Few sports better showcase American innovation, precision and determination. It’s fitting that an Indiana tradition will help celebrate this milestone in our nation’s history.”

“Motorsports represent the best of American grit, innovation, and our people’s competitive spirit. The industry also drives about $69.2 billion in economic impact, supports more than 318,000 jobs, and generates roughly $8.2 billion in tax revenue each year.” said Rep. Richard Hudson (NC-09). “As a lifelong racing fan, I can’t think of a better way to celebrate America’s 250th birthday than bringing racing to our nation’s capital for the first time.”

“There's no better way to celebrate America's 250th birthday than with the roar of INDYCAR engines racing past our most iconic monuments. I'm excited for the nation to see the same passion for racing that has defined Indiana for generations on full display in Washington,” said Rep. Rudy Yakym (IN-02).

“Having the Freedom 250 Grand Prix in Washington, D.C. to celebrate our country’s history is a true showing of a uniquely Hoosier tradition on the national stage,” said Rep. Marlin Stutzman (IN-03). “The nation will watch in awe as these incredible machines weave their way between the monuments and museums that highlight American historical triumphs. Thanks to President Trump for making this amazing spectacle possible.”

"The Indianapolis 500 is a staple of American culture and history. Every year, the best racers in the world circle the Brickyard at breathtaking speeds. Now, the Hoosier State will bring this iconic event to our nation’s capital with the Freedom 250 Grand Prix,” said Rep. Jim Baird (IN-04). “This momentous event is about becoming better, faster, and more resilient, much like our great nation. I’m ready to celebrate America's 250th at the racetrack in Washington and look forward to great chapters still to come."

“As we celebrate America’s 250th anniversary, we are proud to showcase Indiana’s racing heritage - a testament to the innovation and spirit of freedom that define our Republic,” said Rep. Victoria Spartz (IN-05).

“Washington, D.C. and its visitors will finally get a first-hand experience of what Hoosiers have been celebrating for over 100 years, an INDYCAR racing extravaganza!”said Rep. Mark Messmer (IN-08). “I applaud President Trump and the America250 organizers for bringing the Freedom 250 Grand Prix to the local streets of our nation’s capital! Indiana is proud to share this beloved pastime with all Americans!”

"The Freedom 250 Grand Prix is a fitting tribute to Indiana’s proud legacy as the home of American motorsports. For generations, INDYCAR racing has showcased the innovation, grit, determination, and excellence that define our state and our nation,” said Rep. Erin Houchin (IN-09). “As we commemorate America’s 250th birthday, the Freedom 250 Grand Prix honors that legacy while celebrating an exciting racing tradition that continues to inspire Americans and the world today."

title: Smucker Fiscal Sponsorship Transparency Act Advances Through Ways and Means Committee
text:
WASHINGTON— Legislation introduced by Rep. Lloyd Smucker (PA-11), a senior member of the Committee on Ways and Means, was approved during today’s committee markup.

The Fiscal Sponsorship Transparency Act was approved by a vote of 23-15.

Rep. Smucker’s legislation cracks down on bad actors who exploit charitable organizations to collect tax-deductible donations without public accountability.

Fiscal sponsorship is a longstanding practice that allows established charities to accept tax-deductible donations on behalf of projects or organizations that have not yet obtained their own tax-exempt status. While most fiscal sponsorship arrangements serve legitimate charitable purposes, there are currently no uniform public reporting requirements for these arrangements, making it difficult to identify abuse.

That lack of transparency has already been exploited. One recent example involved Samidoun, an organization sanctioned by the U.S. Department of the Treasury for supporting the Popular Front for the Liberation of Palestine (PFLP), a designated foreign terrorist organization. Samidoun was able to receive charitable donations through a fiscal sponsorship arrangement while operating under the umbrella of a U.S. tax-exempt organization.

The Fiscal Sponsorship Transparency Act would shine a light on these agreements by requiring public disclosure of fiscal sponsorship arrangements, preventing abusive conduit arrangements, and establishing penalties for organizations that improperly funnel charitable donations to non-exempt entities.

“Fiscal sponsorship arrangements play an important role in America’s charitable sector, and the vast majority are operated responsibly and in good faith. Congress should strengthen public confidence in these arrangements by ensuring greater transparency and accountability whenever taxpayers provide generous tax benefits for charitable giving. Tax-exempt status is a public trust, and taxpayers deserve confidence that charitable dollars are being administered consistent with charitable purposes,” said Rep. Lloyd Smucker.

“This bill protects legitimate charities by promoting transparency, reinforcing responsible stewardship, and ensuring that bad actors cannot undermine public confidence in the non-profit sector,” Smucker continued.

“The fact that tax-exempt organizations can funnel massive sums of money to an untold number of other entities, without disclosing the recipients, creates significant blind spots in our oversight efforts,” said Ways and Means Committee Chairman Jason Smith (MO-08). “Thanks to Representative Smucker’s leadership, we have an opportunity to inject much-needed accountability and transparency into the financial relationships that exist between sponsoring organizations and their projects. I appreciate his advocacy on behalf of American taxpayers as we work to go after bad actors that are hiding behind tax-exempt status.”

title: House Passes Steil's Congressional Stock Trading Ban
text:
(July 22, 2026) Washington, D.C. – Congressman Bryan Steil (WI-01) issued the following statement after the House of Representatives passed H.R. 7008, the Stop Insider Trading Act.

“The Stop Insider Trading Act is a major step forward for ethics reform on Capitol Hill. It ensures no lawmaker can profit off of insider information,” said Steil. “I urge my Senate colleagues to quickly take it up and send it to President Trump’s desk.”

The Stop Insider Trading Act bill prohibits Members of Congress, spouses, and dependent children from purchasing publicly traded stocks. The bill also requires public notice 7 days before a lawmaker, spouse, or dependent child may sell a stock. Finally, the bill institutes strict penalties for any violation.

Watch Chairman Steil’s closing remarks on the House Floor in support of the bill here.

Background:

In January 2026, Chairman Steil introduced the Stop Insider Trading Act.

The legislation:

Bans Members, their spouses, and their dependent children from purchasing a security issued by a publicly traded company.

Requires Members of Congress to file a public notice at least 7 days, but no more than 14 days, in advance for each intended sale with the Clerk of the House of Representatives or Secretary of the Senate.

Penalties for a violation:

Requires the respective ethics committees to issue a fee equal to $2,000 or 10% of the value of the covered investment, whichever is greater.

Also requires forfeiture of any realized profit from a sale.

The Stop Insider Trading Act passed the House on a bipartisan vote of 232-198.

title: Rep. Steube Recognized by National Taxpayers Union for Protecting Taxpayers from Government Bailout

WASHINGTON, D.C. —U.S. Representative Greg Steube (R-Fla.) was named the National Taxpayers Union’s (NTU) Taxpayer Defender of the Month for his leadership in protecting American taxpayers from being forced to bail out fiscally irresponsible state and local governments. title: REP. STUTZMAN INTRODUCES NO LENIENCY FOR FENTANYL DEALERS ACT
text:
WASHINGTON, DC - Today, Congressman Marlin Stutzman (IN-03) introduced the No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act, the House companion to Senator John Kennedy’s (R-LA) Fairness in Fentanyl Sentencing Act. The legislation significantly lowers the quantity thresholds of fentanyl and fentanyl analogues required to trigger federal mandatory minimum prison sentences and strengthens enforcement tools to combat trafficking. It also updates sentencing guidelines and enhances drug interdiction efforts, particularly through the mail system.

Breitbart first covered this legislation in an exclusive article by Jasmyn Jordan.

Image

Along with being co-led by Senator Kennedy in the Senate, this legislation is also cosponsored by Fentanyl Prevention Caucus Co-Chairman Congressman Ken Calvert (CA-41), Congressman Clay Fuller (GA-14), Congressman Don Bacon (NE-02), Congressman Rob Bresnahan (PA-08), Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz (TX-15), and Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02).

The members said the following:

“Hundreds of thousands of Americans die every year from fentanyl poisoning. I am proud to take up the No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act with Senator Kennedy so those peddling this lethal substance are punished with sentences commensurate with their actions,” said Rep. Stutzman. “The additional training and strengthened enforcement tools included in this bill will assist law enforcement and postal workers to identify fentanyl faster and keep Americans safer.”

“Fentanyl dealers are selling poison that is killing tens of thousands of Americans every year, and Washington’s sentencing laws still treat them with kid gloves. I’m proud to work with Congressman Stutzman to ensure these ghouls get the punishment they deserve,” Sen. Kennedy said.

“Fentanyl is the number one killer of Americans ages 18 to 45. That’s why I am proud to co-sponsor the No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act. For too long, the criminals who profit from poisoning our communities have escaped the full consequences of their actions. That must end,” Rep. Fuller said. “I find no greater joy than putting a fentanyl dealer behind bars. I have seen firsthand the devastation this poison has inflicted on my community in Northwest Georgia, and I will continue to fight here in Washington each and every day to ensure the people responsible are held accountable. If you choose to traffic fentanyl, know this: we will continue to pursue stronger laws, tougher penalties, and every available tool to stop you from destroying more American lives.”

“Fentanyl dealers are poisoning our communities, and I know families who have lost loved ones to fentanyl,” Rep. Bacon said. “Federal law must reflect the deadly reality of this crisis. The No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act strengthens penalties for those trafficking lethal amounts of fentanyl, updates sentencing thresholds and gives the Postal Service more tools to detect and interdict these drugs before they reach our streets. I’m grateful to work with Rep. Stutzman on this effort to hold traffickers accountable and protect American families.”

“It only takes two milligrams of fentanyl to kill a person. That’s just about three grains of table salt,” Rep. Bresnahan said. “Despite this, it takes 40 grams of fentanyl, or roughly three tablespoons of butter, to trigger the federal five-year mandatory minimum sentence for trafficking. That threshold simply does not reflect the deadly reality of this drug. The No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act closes the gap by lowering the amount of fentanyl needed to trigger tougher penalties, helping keep this deadly drug off our streets and out of our communities.”

The legislation has also received support from the National Sheriffs’ Association, the National District Attorneys Association, the Indiana Drug Enforcement Association, the National Alliance of State Drug Enforcement Agencies, the Indiana United Postmasters and Managers of America, the National Narcotic Officers’ Associations’ Coalition, and the United Postmasters and Managers of America. They said the following:

“The lethality of fentanyl demands consequences that match the crime. This legislation closes a dangerous gap in federal law, strengthens enforcement, and helps ensure traffickers are held accountable before more lives are lost. Thank you, Congressman Stutzman, for introducing this much needed legislation,” said Sheriff Mike Chapman of Loudon County, Virginia, chairman of the NSA Government Affairs Committee.

“The No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act takes a critical step toward aligning federal law with the extreme danger fentanyl poses in our communities. Fentanyl is a top public safety concern across the country, and prosecutors need laws that reflect that reality. This bill targets the worst offenders and gives prosecutors the tools they need to disrupt trafficking networks and save lives,” said Nelson Bunn, executive director of the National District Attorneys Association.

“Fentanyl continues to devastate communities across Indiana and the United States, claiming lives at an alarming rate. Individuals take advantage of fentanyl’s low cost to produce as well as its high profit margin. They do so with little to no regard for the people it hurts the most. Those who traffic this deadly substance must be held fully accountable. The Indiana Drug Enforcement Association supports legislative efforts that ensure meaningful consequences for fentanyl dealers and strengthen the ability of law enforcement to protect the public,” said Chris Goergen, president of the Indiana Drug Enforcement Association.

“The National Alliance of State Drug Enforcement Agencies (NASDEA) fully supports the No Leniency for Fentanyl Dealers Act. Given fentanyl’s deadly impact on communities across the country, there must be a zero-tolerance approach toward those who manufacture or distribute this dangerous drug,” said Carlon Stapleton, the organization’s executive director.

“The United Postmasters and Managers of America recognizes the serious threat fentanyl poses to communities nationwide and supports legislation that gives the Postal Service the resources needed to help address that threat,” said Tony Leonardi, national president of United Postmasters and Managers of America.

title: Congresswoman Tenney Introduces SCREEN Act to Revitalize America’s Movie Theaters
text:
Washington, DC — Congresswoman Claudia Tenney (NY-24) alongside Representatives Mike Carey (OH-15) and David Kustoff (TN-08) today introduced the Supporting Cinema Renewal, Enhancement, and Enriching Neighborhoods (SCREEN) Act, legislation to encourage private investment in movie theaters and help revitalize the Main Streets and commercial districts they support.

The SCREEN Act would establish a 30% federal tax credit for qualified movie theater revitalization projects. Eligible improvements include new seating, projection and sound systems, HVAC upgrades, and accessibility improvements. The credit would apply to traditional theaters that have been in operation for at least five years, with a lifetime per theater cap of $250,000 for theaters with three screens or fewer, $375,000 for theaters with four to nine screens, and $500,000 for theaters with ten or more screens. The credit would be available for qualifying investments made through December 31, 2030.

“Strong Main Streets depend on strong local businesses, and movie theaters help bring people into our downtowns where they support restaurants, shops, and other small businesses,” said Congresswoman Tenney. “As theaters work to modernize and compete, they deserve the opportunity to invest in their future. The SCREEN Act encourages private investment, strengthens local economies, creates jobs, and helps preserve these important community gathering places for future generations.”

“Movie theaters are more than just places to see a film. They support local jobs, bring people into our downtowns, and give families a place to spend time together,” said Congressman Mike Carey. “The SCREEN Act will help theaters invest in needed upgrades so they can continue serving their communities, supporting small businesses, and contributing to local economies for years to come.”

This legislation is supported by Cinema United, Marquee Cinemas, Saunders Theatre Properties, and Malco Theatres:

"This timely and important legislation will spur re-investment in one of America’s great Main Street enterprises - the local cinema. Jobs will be created, including local contractors and vendors that do the work, surrounding businesses in the community will benefit, and the result will be a better experience for fans that love seeing their favorite movie on the big screen. We applaud the sponsors of this bill. Because of their leadership, towns of all sizes, in all 50 states, will see a tangible and positive cultural and economic impact in their local communities." - Michael O’Leary, President and CEO, Cinema United

"On behalf of our team at Orchard 14 in New Hartford, NY, and all 13 of our locations, I want to thank Representative Tenney for introducing the SCREEN Act. Our New Hartford theatre employs 44 full and part-time team members and has been proud to serve this community since 2005. Like many in our industry, we're continuing to invest in the guest experience even as costs have risen across the board. The SCREEN Act would help us get there faster, bringing the best possible picture quality to our guests and reinforcing the long-term vitality of movie theatres in communities like New Hartford. We're grateful to Representative Tenney for her leadership on this issue and for supporting exhibition.” - James Cox, Chief Operating Officer, Marquee Cinemas

"Small-town movie theaters are often one of the few places where families, friends, and neighbors can gather and share experiences together. As the owner of four independently owned Ohio theaters, I know how challenging it has become to keep these venues updated while facing rising costs. I have invested millions of dollars into preserving and improving our theaters because I believe small communities deserve exceptional movie-going experiences. The SCREEN Act will help independent theaters continue investing in the places and people we proudly serve, and I thank Representative Carey and the bill's sponsors for championing this important effort.” - Donna Saunders, Owner and Operator of Saunders Theatre Properties

title: Rep. Tlaib introduces a bill to ban AI data centers on federal lands
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Rep. Rashida Tlaib (MI-12) introduced the No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act, a new bill that permanently bans large AI data centers and associated infrastructure on land owned or managed by the U.S., including military bases. The bill also requires the removal of existing qualifying AI data centers and mandates site remediation.

“Everywhere I go in our district, our residents tell me loud and clear, data centers are not welcome in our communities. AI data centers bring noise, light, air, and water pollution, and can increase energy costs by as much as 267%,” said Rep. Tlaib, co-founder of the People’s Environmental Justice Caucus. “Our residents are choking on smog and already paying too much for their utility bills, yet the Trump administration wants to place heavier cost burdens on the shoulders of hardworking Americans. Our corrupt, AI-addicted President cannot be allowed to sacrifice our federal lands so that Big Tech oligarchs can get richer. I will continue to push back against harmful AI data centers alongside our residents to protect our public lands, health, and environment.”

In May, the Department of Defense requested $30 billion to build hyperscale data centers that would integrate largely untested hardware and software used to make life or death decisions into the military. These data centers could be built without Clean Air Act permits under the Trump administration’s new rule that revokes environmental protections. Recently, the Bureau of Land Management approved the first data center on BLM land in Nevada without public input, and the Department of Energy is pushing AI data centers at as many as 16 federal sites nationally. Tlaib’s bill would safeguard public lands from data center destruction, protect military families and surrounding neighborhoods from water and light pollution, and make it more difficult for the Trump administration to outsource military decisions to Big Tech companies.

The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act is endorsed by the Center for Biological Diversity, Climate Justice Alliance, Food & Water Watch, and Win Without War. The bill is cosponsored by U.S. Rep. Jim McGovern (MA-02), Adelita Grijalva (AZ-07), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Mark Pocan (WI-02), and Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12).

“While the Trump administration willingly serves up our environment on a platter to Big Tech and their data centers, Rep. Tlaib’s proposed legislation is drawing a line in the sand,” said Camden Weber, senior climate and energy policy specialist at the Center for Biological Diversity. “Public lands belong to the people, not to Big Tech’s bottom line. This bill is a necessary step toward holding the industry accountable and protecting the air, water and places all species depend on.”

“Everyone deserves clean air, safe water, affordable energy, and healthy neighborhoods. But right now, the accelerated build out of AI data centers threatens this. Communities across the country are calling for accountability, not another giveaway for Big Tech,” Mar Zepeda Salazar, Legislative Director, Climate Justice Alliance. “The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act establishes a critical guardrail to protect our public lands and ensures that the rush to build AI infrastructure does not come at the expense of our health, environment, or democratic voice. Communities have been clear: they deserve transparency, accountability, and the right to shape what gets built in their backyards.”

“With this legislation, Rep. Tlaib is showing the leadership required to protect public lands from massive data center development and industrial destruction,” said Jim Walsh, Food & Water Watch. “At a time when Big Tech is racing to build data centers across the country – including on sensitive public lands – communities are rising up to protect their air, water, health and financial security from this dangerous, exploitative industry.”

“Public lands should not be turned into sacrifice zones for the AI arms race,” said Shayna Lewis, Deputy Director of Win Without War. “This bill is a wake up call and a necessary safeguard that would protect communities from being forced to shoulder the energy, water, pollution, and infrastructure costs of systems designed to accelerate war-making and deepen the Pentagon’s deference to Big Tech.”

title: Tonko, Fitzpatrick Introduce Bipartisan Disability Community Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Representatives Paul D. Tonko (NY-20) and Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-1) today introduced the Disability Community Act, legislation that would bolster workers who support individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD). The bipartisan legislation would propose a Federal Medical Assistance Percentage (FMAP) increase for states over three years to support providers who rely on Medicaid funding and strengthen care for individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities (I/DD).

“Despite delivering compassionate, essential care to those with disabilities, our community-based providers have long been left without proper federal support, forced to shoulder continuously rising costs themselves,” Congressman Tonko said. “Our bipartisan legislation would right this wrong, bolstering these workers by covering costs and wages so that Medicaid-funded providers are able to deliver the best possible care. I urge my colleagues to join us in advancing this bill that will ensure our disability community and those who care for them receive the vital support they need.”

“Community-based care gives individuals with intellectual and developmental disabilities the freedom to live more independently, remain connected to their communities, and pursue greater opportunity — and protecting that care must be a governing priority, not an afterthought,” Congressman Fitzpatrick said. “I have consistently worked with families, providers, and direct-support professionals to strengthen the system they rely on. The bipartisan Disability Community Act brings balance and accountability to that effort — supporting workers, equipping providers to meet new federal requirements, and ensuring that progress does not come at the expense of the individuals and families they serve.”

“ANCOR is immensely thankful to Representatives Tonko and Fitzpatrick for their continued leadership in supporting people with disabilities and community-based providers by reintroducing the Disability Community Act,” said Barbara Merrill, CEO of the American Network of Community Options and Resources (ANCOR). “Providers shouldn’t have to go it alone, and this bill will give states a way to ensure they don’t have to. We’re proud to support the Disability Community Act to make sure providers have the resources they need to deliver the quality services people deserve.”

The Disability Community Act amends Title XIX (Medicaid) of the Social Security Act to temporarily establish a higher federal matching rate with respect to Medicaid expenditures for certain services furnished to individuals with developmental disabilities if such expenditures are attributable to compliance with specified regulations.

title: Rep. Torres Delivers Win for Inland Empire Manufacturers as Trump Administration  Finally Moves to Restore $15.6 Million for a California Manufacturing Extension Partnership Center
text:
Torres led letter in June demanding that the Department of Commerce take steps to restore MEP access in California

Washington D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres, a senior member of the House Appropriations Committee that oversees federal funding, applauded the Department of Commerce's decision to begin restoring California's Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) competition after leading a congressional effort demanding that the Trump Administration provide the state with its fair share of federal manufacturing investments. The released Notice of Funding Opportunity, will provide up to $15.6 million to establish a California MEP Center, giving manufacturers across the Inland Empire and the state access to the technical expertise and resources they need to compete, innovate, and grow. Applications are due August 21, 2026.

The announcement comes just weeks after Rep. Torres led California Appropriators in pressing Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick to immediately restore California's MEP Center, arguing that the nation's largest manufacturing state should not be left without one after the previous center closed in October 2025. California was one of only two states to not have a MEP center in the country. Manufacturing employment has fallen by 75,000 jobs since President Trump took office. In the letter, the Members emphasized that California is home to more than 35,000 manufacturers that contribute over $391 billion to the U.S. economy and urged the Department to quickly execute a new funding competition, consistent with congressional direction.

"California is the manufacturing powerhouse of America, and our workers and small manufacturers deserve the same federal support as every other state," said Congresswoman Norma Torres. "When California's MEP Center was allowed to lapse, I immediately called on the Department of Commerce to restore this critical program because our manufacturers cannot afford to fall behind. Today's announcement is a victory for California businesses, for the Inland Empire, and for the thousands of workers whose livelihoods depend on a strong manufacturing economy."

"This is exactly why we fought for California to receive its fair share," Torres continued. "The Inland Empire is helping build America's future. Restoring an MEP Center in California will help manufacturers innovate, expand production, strengthen our supply chains, and create more good-paying jobs right here in our communities. I encourage eligible applicants in the Inland Empire to apply."

CA-35 is one of California's leading manufacturing hubs, with thousands of businesses producing everything from advanced technologies and aerospace components to food products, logistics equipment, and medical devices. Small and medium-sized manufacturers are the backbone of the region's economy, creating good-paying jobs and strengthening domestic supply chains.

Applications for the California MEP Center are due on August 21, 2026. If selected, the new center will join the nationwide Manufacturing Extension Partnership Network, providing manufacturers across California with technical assistance, workforce development, and advanced manufacturing expertise.

title: Trahan, Obernolte Introduce Bipartisan FRONTIER Act to Strengthen Oversight of Advanced AI
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lori Trahan (D-MA-03) and Congressman Jay Obernolte (R-CA-23), alongside Representatives Scott Peters (D-CA-50), Scott Franklin (R-FL-18), Suhas Subramanyan (D-VA-10), and Erin Houchin (R-IN-09), introduced the Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting (FRONTIER) Act. introduced the Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting Act, or the FRONTIER Act. The bipartisan legislation, which was developed as part of the broader Great American AI Act framework, establishes a national, risk-based framework governing the development and deployment of the most advanced artificial intelligence models.

The FRONTIER Act establishes tiered requirements based on the size of a frontier AI developer, including model cards, risk-management frameworks, independent audits, incident reporting, and ongoing assessments. It also creates a uniform national standard for transparency, auditing, and reporting of catastrophic risk to prevent a patchwork of state regulations.

“As AI systems grow more capable, Americans deserve confidence that the most powerful models are being developed responsibly,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “The bipartisan FRONTIER Act delivers commonsense transparency and independent oversight for the largest AI developers while giving them a single, clear national standard to build on. This is how we protect the public from catastrophic risks without slowing the innovation that keeps America competitive.”

"Artificial intelligence is advancing rapidly, and Congress must ensure our regulatory framework keeps pace without undermining American innovation,” said Congressman Obernolte. “The FRONTIER Act focuses oversight on the largest developers and most advanced models, requiring transparency, independent evaluation, and timely reporting of serious safety incidents. This legislation will protect Americans from catastrophic risk, provide developers with clear rules of the road, and ensure the United States remains the global leader in AI.”

“The window to get AI policy right is closing, and Congress can't afford to miss it,” said Congressman Peters. “I supported Representatives Trahan and Obernolte's initial draft so we could develop a better bill that reflects how this technology works and where it's headed. Thanks to input from researchers, experts, and civil society advocates, that process worked. The FRONTIER Act is a targeted bill with clear, uniform transparency, and safety standards, instead of a fifty-state patchwork. I'm glad to support this bipartisan effort so that Congress acts before this technology outruns us.”

"The FRONTIER Act recognizes that not every AI developer should be regulated the same way. It takes a targeted approach by focusing only on the handful of companies developing the most powerful frontier AI models, not the startups and innovators driving America's AI ecosystem,” said Congressman Franklin. “By tying coverage to substantial AI research and development investments and requiring transparency and independent assessments from those developers, the bill avoids one-size-fits-all mandates and allows smaller innovators to spend their time building new technologies instead of navigating unnecessary federal red tape."

“This is a four-alarm fire. We need to take action now. These frontier models could have the power to create serious chaos and harm without adequate regulations. This bill, while not perfect, is an important, bipartisan step in the right direction. We need a bill like this that can actually pass this Congress and get signed into law. But this is only the first step, and more action needs to be taken to protect people from the harm these models can cause,” said Congressman Subramanyan.

"America must lead the world in artificial intelligence, and we can do that while being clear-eyed about the risks,” said Congresswoman Houchin. “Just this week, one of the most advanced AI systems in the country broke out of its own developer's testing environment, reaching systems it was never supposed to touch. This is exactly the kind of incident that shouldn't stay behind closed doors. The FRONTIER Act delivers transparency and accountability from the largest AI developers. Innovation and guardrails are not opposites—both are necessary to stay ahead of our adversaries."

title: Trahan, DeLauro, Larsen, Walkinshaw, Gillen Introduce Right to IVF Act
text:
Today, Representatives Lori Trahan (MA-03), Rosa DeLauro (CT-01), Rick Larsen (WA-02), James Walkinshaw (VA-11), and Laura Gillen (NY-04) led the introduction of the Right to IVF Act of 2026. Introduced ahead of World IVF Day on July 25th, the sweeping legislative package that would make it easier to access in-vitro fertilization (IVF) and other assisted reproductive technology (ART) for the millions of hopeful parents who depend on it to build their family. This pro-family legislation would establish a nationwide right to access IVF, lower the costs of IVF treatment, expand IVF coverage for military families and require all employer-sponsored insurance programs to cover IVF.

“Like so many people in our country facing fertility challenges, my husband and I turned to IVF as our last hope to have kids. After years of appointments, injections, and setbacks, and thanks to our remarkable physicians, we have two beautiful daughters,” said Congresswoman Trahan. “No one should lose the chance to start or grow a family because of their zip code. The Right to IVF Act guarantees the right to family-creating fertility care in every state and puts it within reach for the millions of families who need it.”

“There are few experiences as hard as wanting to start a family and not being able to,” said Congresswoman DeLauro. “That is why I am fighting to ensure Americans have access to IVF treatments when they want to start one. I am proud to join my colleagues in introducing the Right to IVF Act – because building a family in the United States should never be difficult.”

“For many Americans, fertility treatments like IVF are essential to start families of their own,” said Congressman Larsen. “This comprehensive legislation will guarantee access and expand coverage for IVF and other fertility services. The legislation also includes my bill with Senator Murray, the Veteran Families Health Services Act, to ensure fertility treatments are included in servicemembers’ and veterans’ health benefits. I will keep working with my colleagues in the House and the Senate to make sure that women and men in uniform and working families do not have to sacrifice their dreams of having a family.”

“Deciding when and how to build a family is a deeply personal choice that belongs to families, not politicians,” said Congressman Walkinshaw, Co-Chair of the Federal Workforce Caucus. “For millions struggling with infertility, IVF offers hope and a path to parenthood. I’m especially proud the Right to IVF Act includes my legislation requiring IVF coverage through the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program, ensuring the federal government leads by example. I’m honored to join Senator Duckworth, Congresswoman Trahan, and this coalition to protect IVF nationwide and expand access for servicemembers, veterans, federal employees, and working families.”

“I am proud to help lead this critical bill ensuring millions of Americans can access IVF to build their families, no matter where they live,” said Congresswoman Gillen. “Families struggling to conceive go through indescribable heartbreak and stress. The last thing they should worry about is legal challenges to IVF delaying or outright halting procedures. Infertility is not a partisan issue. I will continue to work across the aisle in Congress to protect access to IVF and adjacent reproductive technologies that have helped countless individuals experience the joy of parenthood.”

Reps. Carter, Dunn, Craig Champion the Improving CARE for Youth Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Congressman Troy A. Carter, Sr. (D-LA), alongside Reps. Neal Dunn (R-FL) and Angie Craig (D-MN) introduced the Improving Coordination and Access to Resources Equitably (CARE) for Youth Act. This bipartisan legislation increases access to mental health services for children enrolled in Medicaid.

“This is a common-sense, no-cost fix that removes a bureaucratic barrier standing between patients and the integrated care model that providers already want to deliver. When a doctor identifies a need for behavioral health support, that patient shouldn't have to wait — they should be able to see a provider down the hall, right then and there,” said Rep. Carter. “The Improving CARE for Youth Act allows Medicaid to reimburse for behavioral health and primary care services delivered on the same day, at the same visit. This is lifesaving care for patients when they need it most.”

Under current Medicaid policy, health care providers generally may only bill for one service per patient per day. As a result, when a child visits a primary care physician and is identified as needing behavioral or mental health services, practices with an integrated mental health provider often cannot bill for both the primary care visit and the same-day mental health service. This outdated billing restriction discourages same-day treatment, forcing many children to schedule a separate appointment and delaying access to critical care.

“Our nation is facing a growing youth mental health crisis, and we should be removing barriers to care, not creating them,” said Rep. Dunn. “As a physician, I know that early intervention can make a profound difference in a child's long-term health and well-being. Protecting the future of the youth in our country is too important to be hindered by a Medicaid billing restriction. The Improving CARE for Youth Act ensures children can receive the care they need when they need it.”

“We are facing a mental health crisis in our country, and we've got to make sure young people have access to the mental health care they need when they need it,” said Rep Craig. “I’m proud to reintroduce this bipartisan bill alongside my colleagues that will remove barriers to mental health care for children on Medicaid and ensure a better future for our kids and grandkids.”

title: Rep. Van Epps Speaks at SST Budget Hearing on Revitalizing American Scientific Research
text:
Washington, D.C.-Rep. Van Epps (TN-07) participated in a Science, Space, and Technology (SST) Committee hearing titled, “Unleashing the Golden Age of Science: Examining the Priorities of the FY2027 Research and Technology Enterprise.”

Watch Rep. Van Epps' statement here.

Read Rep. Van Epps’ opening remarks here:

“Thank you, Director Kratsios, for being here today. In March 2025, President Trump charted out a clear vision for scientific progress and technological innovation: to position America to maintain leadership in emerging technologies like AI, quantum, and nuclear; to revitalize American scientific research; and to ensure that the growth of science and technology stimulates …economic growth.

Director Kratsios and OSTP have delivered by supporting these goals: the National AI Legislative Framework provided clear direction on how Congress should act to spur…on AI innovation that serves Americans, and an executive order signed by the President last month to accelerate U.S. innovation in quantum technologies to strengthen our national security.

One year after executive orders on nuclear energy, we are seeing real-world results. The President’s bold goal of three advanced test reactors achieving criticality before the Fourth of July was not only met but exceeded with four reactors achieving criticality. Just yesterday, Director Kratsios published a report establishing a blueprint for renewing American scientific leadership for the 21st century.

After the Biden administration floundered to position America for technology leadership and energy dominance, we are seeing tangible results from the Trump administration, with OSTP providing critical support.”

Read Rep. Van Epps’ questions here:

Rep. Van Epps asked, “ We must maintain the lead across the board when it comes to AI. Microsoft’s AI for Good Lab found that DeepSeek’s free, open-source models have driven AI adoption across the developing world. Recently, the Chinese company, Moonshot, released…a new open-weight model that performs competitively with American frontier models. US companies are turning toward open-source and open-weight models as they are cheaper, customizable, and… have less guardrails.

Just earlier this morning, the director of your team posted that Moonshot AI conducted large-scale covert distillation to develop their newest K3 model, and so a few questions here: How do we balance an open innovation ecosystem while protecting American technology from IP threat, and how is OSTP responding to the threat to American AI leadership posed by Chinese open source and open weight models?”

Director of White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, Michael Kratsios replied, “I think there's, for starters, an important distinction to be made between open source models and large scale industrial covert distillation of American models, and I think what was made public today was exactly that: the convert industrial distillation of…American technology. The administration deeply believes that the future of American leadership in AI is contingent upon having a…vibrant open and closed source set of models for Americans and the world to use. I think on the first or second page of the AI action plan the president released last year, we emphasized very strongly that the U.S. must lead in…open source. So for us, we're doing everything we can to…kind of push the open source community ahead in the U.S...and provide lots of alternatives for all of our entrepreneurs.

Rep. Van Epps asked, “Great, thanks, director. Modern research and AI model training runs on data, such as biological databases and materials data. American leadership in these fields depends on the quality and accessibility of that underlying data infrastructure. That's why I introduced the Web of Biological Data Act of 2026, which would establish a single point of entry for researchers to access high-quality biological data for use in research and development. Director, what…role does access to high-quality data play in America's science and AI ecosystem, and how would a single point of entry for standardized data sets impact the pace of innovation?

title: Subcommittee Holds Hearing Examining Walberg's Legislation to Bridge Digital Divide
text:
Yesterday, the House Committee on Energy and Commerce Committee's Subcommittee on Communications and Technology held a legislative hearing to discuss legislation to expand access to the reliable broadband needed for the 21st Century. The Subcommittee examined the Proper Leadership to Align Networks (PLAN) for Broadband Act, introduced by Congressmen Tim Walberg (R-MI) and Scott Peters (D-CA).

"Students, families, and small businesses rely on internet connectivity each day, and we can’t allow rural America to get left behind in today’s digital age," said Rep. Walberg. "We must develop a national strategy to streamline our efforts and deliver high-speed broadband across the country. I am proud to see the subcommittee consider my legislation, the bipartisan PLAN for Broadband Act, which would increase coordination among all relevant federal agencies so we can close the digital divide."

Background

The PLAN for Broadband Act is based upon a Government Accountability Office report that found that federal broadband efforts are oftentimes fragmented and duplicative. While enough federal funding exists to bridge the digital divide, a national broadband strategy is needed to avoid duplicative efforts and ensure that funds are available to reach the truly unserved and underserved areas. The PLAN for Broadband Act would require the Administration to develop and implement a national strategy to close the digital divide.

title: Wasserman Schultz Leads 50+ Democrats in Bill to Protect TPS Holders, Restore Checks and Balances
text:
“Hundreds of thousands of families who followed the law, passed multiple criminal background checks, earned work permits, and paid taxes are at risk of being torn apart, thrown in ICE jails, or sent back to a nation overrun by criminal gangs who murder and kidnap at will because of the horrible decisions made by the Trump Administration and a MAGA Supreme Court,” said Wasserman Schultz. “This fight is not over. My TPS Review Act will restore checks and balances on the President’s handling of TPS, because nobody is above the law.”

Washington, DC – Today, U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (FL-25) introduced the TPS Review Act, which would reassert judicial and Congressional review of the executive branch’s decisions about TPS. She was joined by 58 original cosponsors, including Chair of the Congressional Black Caucus Rep. Yvette Clarke, (NY-09), Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus Rep. Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), and Chair of the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus Rep. Grace Meng (NY-06). A federal appeals court gave Haitians a temporary reprieve Wednesday from losing their deportation protections from deportation, which had been set to end Friday. That reprieve could end anytime after Monday, July 27.

The crux of the Supreme Court’s Trump v. Miot ruling that allows this threat to proceed, is that, regardless of whether the Administration’s TPS termination for Haiti and Syria was lawful, courts have no authority to assess if a decision to revoke TPS is legal. This legislation explicitly allows court reviews of TPS determination reasoning, which in the case of Haiti was clearly fueled by Trump Administration racism.

“Hundreds of thousands of families who followed the law, passed multiple criminal background checks, earned work permits, and paid taxes are at risk of being torn apart, thrown in ICE jails, or sent back to a nation overrun by criminal gangs who murder and kidnap at will because of the horrible decisions made by the Trump Administration and a MAGA Supreme Court,” said Wasserman Schultz. “This fight is not over. My TPS Review Act will restore checks and balances on the President’s handling of TPS, because nobody is above the law.”

The TPS Review Act would amend the Temporary Protected Status statute to institute judicial review, establish a cause of action for TPS recipients and their representatives to sue for relief in court, and allow Congress to reverse a TPS termination by simple majority vote under the Congressional Review Act.

This legislation will also require a standardized, documented process for the Executive Branch to review country conditions before TPS can be revoked, creating a paper trail for litigation. It places the burden of evidence on the Government to prove that a challenged TPS decision complies with these requirements.

Under this bill, TPS recipients would maintain their status and work permits automatically and indefinitely while a termination is litigated in court, eliminating the uncertainty that has harmed Florida businesses and consumers over the last year.

Original co-sponsors include: U.S. Representatives Gabe Amo, Wesley Bell, Donald Beyer, Shontel Brown, André Carson, Kathy Castor, Joaquin Castro, Judy Chu, Yvette Clarke, Angie Craig, Danny Davis, Suzan DelBene, Maxine Dexter, Adriano Espaillat, Lois Frankel, Maxwell Frost, Jesús García, Jimmy Gomez, Al Green, Adelita Grijalva, Steven Horsford, Jonathan Jackson, Henry Johnson, Sydney Kamlager-Dove, Rick Larsen, John Larson, George Latimer, Zoe Lofgren, Stephen Lynch, John Mannion, Doris Matsui, Jennifer McClellan, Morgan McGarvey, James McGovern, Gregory Meeks, Jared Moskowitz, Seth Moulton, Eleanor Norton, Nancy Pelosi, Scott Peters, Brittany Pettersen, Stacey Plaskett, Mark Pocan, Ayanna Pressley, Mike Quigley, Deborah Ross, Andrea Salinas, Lateefah Simon, Adam Smith, Darren Soto, Melanie Stansbury, Rashida Tlaib, Paul Tonko, Marc Veasey, Nydia Velázquez, Bonnie Watson Coleman, and Frederica Wilson.

title: Adams, Frankel, Leger Fernández, Watson Coleman, Blunt Rochester Introduce Black Women’s Equal Pay Day Resolution
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Representatives Alma S. Adams, Ph.D. (NC-12),LoisFrankel (FL-22),Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12),Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), and Senator Lisa Blunt Rochester (DE), introduced the Black Women’s Equal Pay Day Resolution, marking July 21st as Black Women’s Equal Pay Day and recognizing the deep, persistent wage gap that Black women continue to face in the United States.

Every year, the date of Black Women’s Equal Pay Day is set to mark the amount of time Black women would have to work to earn what white, non-Hispanic men earned by the end of the previous year. In 2025, Black women earned roughly 65 cents for every dollar white men earned.

“Today, we confront an unacceptable wage disparity facing Black women, and recommit ourselves to correcting it,” said Higher Education and Workforce Development Subcommittee Ranking Member, Congresswoman Alma S. Adams, Ph.D. “For generations, Black women have been compelled to work twice as hard for half the reward. They have faced entrenched barriers, systemic discrimination, and a persistent denial of opportunity. We cannot ask another generation of Black women to wait months, even years, for the pay they rightfully deserve. I am proud to introduce this resolution, and I call on this Congress to act with the urgency this injustice demands.”

“Equal pay is more than a slogan—it’s about whether women can pay their bills, take care of their families, enjoy a good quality of life, and eventually retire with dignity,” said Democratic Women’s Caucus Chair Emerita Lois Frankel. “In 2025, for the second year in a row, the gender pay gap widened, and for Black women the disparity is even greater. It’s long past time for Congress to close the wage gap and ensure every woman is paid fairly for her work.”

“The wage gap has widened for two years in a row - the first time we've seen such an increase since the 1960s,” said Rep. Watson Coleman. “And as we navigate a nationwide affordability crisis, Republican policies have stripped away tools to narrow the pay gap and made it harder for black women to earn good-paying jobs. Black women are foundational to the progress and survival of this nation yet for far too long have been prevented from reaping the fruits of their labor. It’s imperative that we address the racist, sexist policies that cause structural economic inequality in America so Black women are paid what they’ve earned.”

"Women hold this country together. We raise families, care for loved ones, teach our children, heal the sick, grow businesses, harvest our food, and serve our communities," said Congresswoman Teresa Leger Fernández, Chair of the Democratic Women's Caucus. "Yet, year after year, our work is still valued less than men's. That is not just unfair—it is a choice our country continues to make. Black Women's Equal Pay Day reminds us that while all women continue to fight for equal pay, Black women face an even steeper climb. We are well into Summer before their equal pay day rolls around—that’s too late, it’s too tiring and smothering to fathom the disrespect this late date signifies. Congress must finally pass the Paycheck Fairness Act and make equal pay the law of the land so that Black women, and all women earn the pay they deserve.” “Even in the ‘land of opportunity,’ Black women must work 50 percent longer to achieve the same earnings as white men,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “This resolution sheds light on the challenges facing minority communities across the country and reaffirms our commitment to closing the pay gaps. I’m proud to see all my Senate Democratic colleagues join me in making a concerted effort to improve the quality of life for Black women everywhere.”

title: Rep. Watson Coleman Introduces Resolution Condemning All Forms of Hate
text:
Today, Representative Bonnie Watson Coleman (NJ-12) announced the introduction of a Resolution Condemning All Forms of Hate, emphasizing the importance of an inclusive democracy and rejecting hateful discourse targeted at vulnerable populations. This resolution condemns all representations of discrimination, including racism, islamophobia, antisemitism, transphobia, homophobia, sexism, ageism, xenophobia, ableism, and ethnic or religious bigotry.

Just a few weeks ago, two men in Idaho were aggressively beaten and verbally accosted for being in a same-sex relationship. These are not just standalone cases, and they are not limited to just one group. Just this past month, at a family gathering in Georgia, a man armed with an AR-15 rifle opened fire on 20 Black children and adults after verbally accosting them with racial slurs. These actions against our neighbors, in our communities, are unacceptable. Every person has the right to exist freely, without fear.

“This resolution comes at a critical time when incidents of violence and harmful behavior have been on the rise,” said Watson Coleman. “Hatred has no place in our communities, our country, or our world. We must stand together against bigotry, racism, and intolerance. Let this resolution serve as a powerful message that reflects the values of compassion and empathy that are essential for building a more just and equitable society and a small reminder that it is imperative upon all individuals, communities, and institutions to actively reject hate and work towards fostering an environment of understanding and acceptance.”

Specifically, this resolution:

Denounces all representations of discrimination including racism, islamophobia, antisemitism, transphobia, heterosexism, homophobia, sexism, ageism, xenophobia, ableism, and ethnic or religious bigotry

Supports the implementation of comprehensive policies to prevent and respond to hate crimes, including education and training on prevention and response, state and federal intervention, and acknowledgment of the challenges facing vulnerable groups

Reassures victims’ advocacy with communication support, incident reporting, physical and mental health resources, legal representation, and response and recovery

Supports funding for programs that are culturally and linguistically accessible and resources for community-based organizations that reflect the experiences of vulnerable populations.

Upholds the federal government’s promise to combat all forms of hate, bigotry, and violence

This resolution is cosponsored by Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (DC-AL), Hank Johnson (GA-04), Jennifer McClellan (VA-04), Jonathan Jackson (IL-01), and Shri Thanedar (MI-13).

title: Rep. Whitesides Introduces Major Bipartisan Bill to Lower Energy Costs, Modernize the Grid, and Reduce Wildfire Risk
text:
The Lowering Energy Costs through Grid Modernization Act would speed deployment of advanced conductors on existing power line corridors, getting cheaper energy to consumers faster.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Rep. George Whitesides (D-CA) and Rep. Pat Harrigan (R-NC) introduced the Lowering Energy Costs through Grid Modernization Act, with Reps. Sean Casten (D-IL) and Abraham Hamadeh (R-AZ) joining as original cosponsors. The legislation – supported by industry, environmental groups, labor, and both political parties – reflects how reconducting can serve as a strategy to lower costs, enable connection to new sources of energy, and increase safety from wildfire ignitions.

Built in large part decades ago, the nation’s electrical grid was not designed to meet today’s soaring energy demands, and our grid’s electrical capacity is not sized for the power we need. This legislation would lower costs for consumers by upgrading existing infrastructure using high-capacity electrical power line cables on existing power line corridors. Because building entirely new transmission lines can take 10 to 15 years to plan, permit, and construct, the legislation supports a faster path: installing advanced conductors and co-locating new lines on existing rights-of-way, which can then carry significantly more electricity through established corridors while reducing wildfire risk.

“Families and businesses in my district are tired of paying more for power because our grid can’t move electricity where it’s needed,” said Rep. Whitesides.“This is a common-sense, bipartisan fix: instead of waiting over a decade for new transmission lines, we can upgrade the wires we already have and get affordable power flowing faster. I’m proud to lead this effort with Rep. Harrigan to lower costs for consumers, cut wildfire risk, and make our grid more reliable, without the price tag or delay of building from scratch.”

“Our electric grid was built decades ago and wasn’t designed for the demands we’re placing on it today, and I’m proud to team up with Rep. George Whitesides on a fix that actually moves at the speed this problem requires,” said Rep. Harrigan. “Instead of waiting ten or fifteen years to build brand new transmission lines, this bill lets us modernize the wires we already have, cutting through red tape so we can double capacity, lower power bills, and reduce wildfire risk, all in a fraction of the time and cost.”

“Modernizing our electrical grid is essential to improving our ability to deliver affordable clean energy from where it is produced to where it is needed,” said Laura Brannen, U.S. Climate Policy Team Lead, The Nature Conservancy. “Improving transmission in existing corridors, upgrading existing transmission lines and utilizing previously developed lands are quick, cost-effective ways to do so and can lower impacts to communities and nature when done right. The Grid Modernization Act can help make it easier to use these commonsense solutions. The Nature Conservancy thanks the sponsors for their bipartisan leadership on this important issue.”

The Lowering Energy Costs through Grid Modernization Act would:

Lower energy costs for consumers by cutting the time and expense of grid upgrades, using existing rights-of-way and tax incentives instead of multi-billion-dollar new-build transmission projects, so utilities can pass along savings from access to affordable, distant power.

Streamline the environmental review process by establishing a fast-track categorical exclusion under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) for transmission upgrades that remain within existing, previously cleared or permitted rights-of-way, cutting through a process that can otherwise take years.

Speed up grid planning by facilitating the integration of advanced conductor technologies into transmission planning processes, including voluntary transmission modernization studies and public reporting on project outcomes, so utilities and regulators can more easily identify and act on upgrade opportunities.

Reduce wildfire risk by promoting high-performance conductors that experience virtually zero thermal sag under extreme electrical loads, keeping power lines safely away from vegetation below.

Strengthen grid reliability by boosting baseline transmission capacity so the system can absorb severe emergency power spikes without overloading.

The legislation is endorsed by The Nature Conservancy, the Citizens Climate Lobby of California, and ClearPath, among others.

title: Reps. Whitesides and Latta, Sens. Schiff and Banks Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Combat AI Distillation and Other Attacks to National Security
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Representatives George Whitesides (D-Calif.-27) and Bob Latta (R-Ohio-5) and U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Jim Banks (R-Ind.) are introducing new bipartisan legislation to enhance the ability for AI labs and security researchers to combat distillation attacks from foreign adversaries and other frontier AI risks that pose a national security risk to the U.S.

The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act would allow for increased information sharing between industry and stakeholder groups to share information about AI security threats and coordinate their responses with other model developers. It includes strict guardrails, including protection against anti-competitive behavior, and permits the Attorney General to seek an injunction against non-Federal entities that abuse the exemption.

During distillation attacks, foreign labs systematically harvest data from U.S. AI models to produce their own advanced AI models at a fraction of the cost, posing an enormous threat to continued U.S. leadership and investment in developing the most powerful and efficient AI models and staying ahead of foreign competition. With the rise of AI, foreign labs have increasingly attacked proprietary models with millions of queries and use the resulting data to train rival, foreign-based systems, essentially reverse-engineering American technology at a lower cost and with less strain on valuable computational resources.

“As the Representative for a district at the heart of California’s aerospace and technology industry, I’ve seen firsthand how vital American innovation is to our national security. But as AI models grow exponentially more capable, the risk of these systems being exploited or weaponized poses a direct threat to public safety,” said Congressman Whitesides. “By authorizing threat intelligence sharing to defend against hostile foreign attacks, this bipartisan bill prevents our technology from being turned against us. Safeguarding our technological edge isn’t a partisan issue, and I’m proud to help lead this effort to keep America safe.”

“We cannot allow China, or any foreign adversary, to steal American technological advancements in AI, and then weaponize those advances to undermine our own national security,” said Senator Schiff. “The solution we are proposing would protect against AI distillation attacks and other security risks by allowing increased information-sharing among U.S. AI labs to counter the threat of foreign theft. As new AI innovations are developing faster than ever, it’s critical that Republicans and Democrats continue to work together to address potential misuse of AI development by hostile actors at home and abroad.”

“The AI race is one that America can’t afford to lose. Communist China is working every day to steal our technology and close the gap with the United States,” said Senator Banks. “American AI companies must be able to collaboratively defend against our adversaries. This bill gives them the tools to protect America’s technological edge and helps ensure we maintain our competitive edge.”

“Protecting the American people means ensuring the systems they rely on every day, including our hospitals, water systems, and electric grid, remain safe, secure, and reliable,” said Congressman Latta. “Our adversaries are constantly looking for new ways to target our critical infrastructure, and we must make sure we are prepared to respond. This bipartisan legislation, which I am proud to lead alongside Senators Schiff and Banks and Rep. Whitesides will help strengthen collaboration between American companies and ensure that when a threat is identified, we can quickly share information and take action to protect our communities. Our adversaries are working together to undermine us, and we must work together to defend America.”

Specifically, the Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act would create a statutory exemption that allows non-Federal entities to:

Share information related to a covered AI security risk in good faith for the exclusive purpose of preventing, investigating, or mitigating an AI security risk; or

Coordinate with the exclusive purpose of reducing AI security risks by delaying or limiting the deployment of high-risk AI models, with required written notice prior to taking such actions.

The covered coordination efforts include information-sharing and agreements made through coordinating bodies such as the NSA’s AI Security Center, NIST’s CAISI, the Frontier Model Forum, or other industrial consortia. The legislation tracks the Cybersecurity Information Sharing Act, which has successfully enabled the sharing of cyber threat and vulnerability information between and among government and nongovernmental organizations for a decade.

In addition to Schiff, Banks, Latta, and Whitesides, the legislation is cosponsored by U.S. Representatives Pat Harrigan (R-N.C.-10), Darrell Issa (R-Calif.-48), Ted Lieu (D-Calif.-36), Mariannette Miller-Meeks (R-Iowa-01), Nathaniel Moran (R-Texas-01), and Jay Obernolte (R-Calif.-23).

The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act is endorsed by the AI Policy Network (AIPN), Alliance for a Better Future (ABF), Alliance for Secure AI, America First Policy Institute (AFPI), Association for Competitive Technology (ACT), Center for AI Safety (CAIS) Action Fund, Encode AI, Foundation for American Innovation (FAI) Action, Google, Health Information Sharing and Analysis Center (Health-ISAC), Law Reform Institute, SeedAI, and Software & Information Industry Association (SIIA).

“The worst AI security threats — a foreign adversary stealing a frontier model, a serious loss of control — won’t be contained to a single company. Developers need to be able to share threat information and coordinate, and this bill lets them do that. When companies can coordinate on threats without legal risk, they lose the excuse for staying silent and the public is safer for it,” said Sunny Gandhi, Co-Executive Director, Encode AI.

“We urgently need legislation that lets frontier AI developers collaborate on national security risks, such as adversarial distillation, without being deterred by uncertainties regarding antitrust law. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and AI Security Risks Act would provide targeted protections paired with appropriate guardrails against misuse,” said Tim Schnabel, President, Law Reform Institute.

“Building on the proven foundation of CISA 2015, The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act brings a strengthened threat-sharing framework into the AI era. Protecting critical infrastructure and cutting-edge AI systems requires real-time coordination against sophisticated security threats. This bill strikes a vital balance: empowering tech leaders to collaborate on cyber, CBRN, loss-of-control, and foreign adversarial risks while maintaining strong antitrust protections,” said Paul Lekas, Executive VP for Global Public Policy & Government Affairs, Software & Information Industry Association (SIIA).

“AI developers are confronting increasingly sophisticated threats involving model theft, unauthorized access, critical infrastructure, and other serious security risks. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act would extend existing protections to information sharing and coordination around AI-specific threats, promoting real-time situational awareness among frontier labs and other AI developers. Importantly, the bill includes safeguards to ensure this protection is limited to good-faith security collaboration and does not excuse anticompetitive conduct,” said Morgan Reed, President, Association for Competitive Technology (ACT).

“The benefits of the CATS Act extend far beyond AI tech companies. By removing antitrust barriers to sharing critical information about adversarial AI threats, this legislation directly protects downstream critical infrastructure. For Health-ISAC and the health sector, this means safeguarding national public health and patient safety from emerging security risks and ultimately keeping Americans safer,” said Denise Anderson, President & CEO, Health-ISAC.

“Making America AI-ready means making institutions more resilient and equipped to respond to AI security risks. Giving companies a clear, lawful path to share threat information raises the security floor for the whole country while advancing American leadership in AI. Making America AI-ready means making institutions more resilient and equipped to respond to AI security risks. Giving companies a clear, lawful path to share threat information raises the security floor for the whole country while advancing American leadership in AI,” said Joshua New, Director of Policy, SeedAI.

“This bipartisan bill gives the AI industry clear rules of the road to share threat intelligence and collaborate on much-needed standards and benchmarks. We appreciate the leadership of Senators Schiff and Banks and Representatives Whitesides and Latta in working to ensure the continued responsible development of frontier models,” said John Connell, VP of Government Affairs and Public Policy, US & Canada, Google.

“I commend Senators Schiff and Banks for their bipartisan legislation. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Strategic Risks Act improves the speed at which national security risks arising from adversarial espionage and autonomous improvement of artificial intelligence models can be identified and addressed,” said Mark Beall, President AI Policy Network.

“Advanced AI systems could be exploited by foreign adversaries, used to develop biological or cyber weapons, threaten critical infrastructure, or operate beyond meaningful human control. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act is a commonsense step that will help America’s leading AI companies work together to identify and reduce these risks before they become an emergency,” said Brendan Steinhauser, CEO, The Alliance for Secure AI.

“As advanced AI systems increasingly become prime targets for espionage and theft by bad actors and global competitors, AI companies need a secure way to share threat information and coordinate defenses without risking antitrust violations. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act would create a narrow exemption for companies to rely on, while keeping safeguards against price fixing, market allocation, and other anti-competitive behavior fully intact. By strengthening companies’ ability to detect and respond to these risks, this bill will help keep Americans protected from the real-world harms posed by compromised AI systems. The Center for AI Safety Action Fund is proud to support this bill,” said Varun Krovi, Executive Director, Center for AI Safety Action Fund.

The full text of the legislation is available here.
