title: Baldwin, Evers Sound Alarm on USPS Mail Delays and Interference Ahead of Upcoming Elections
text:
WISCONSIN – Today, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) and Wisconsin Governor Tony Evers are sounding the alarm on multiple issues at the United States Postal Service (USPS) that will restrict Wisconsinites’ ability to have their ballots counted in the upcoming elections. Specifically, Baldwin and Evers are calling on the USPS to immediately address severe delays that caused hundreds of Wisconsinites’ ballots to arrive after Election Day in April. The lawmakers also urged USPS to immediately reverse course on implementing President Donald Trump’s unconstitutional order to severely restrict vote-by-mail.

“Hundreds of absentee ballots received by the Postal Service before Wisconsin's Spring Election were delivered after Election Day, preventing them from being counted,” wrote Senator Baldwin and Governor Evers in a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner and members of the USPS Board of Governors. “Now, USPS is rushing to implement President Trump's unconstitutional executive order that would, at best, significantly delay Wisconsinites' mailed ballots from reaching election officials and, at worst, allow the USPS to prevent a Wisconsin voter's fully legal, timely ballot from being counted at all. We call on the Postal Service to immediately resolve the issues that delayed ballots during Wisconsin’s Spring Election, withdraw the rule that will add significant additional delays in ballot delivery, and ensure preparations for Wisconsin’s fall elections prioritizes timely delivery of election mail.”

In the letter, Senator Baldwin and Governor Evers underscore the importance of protecting mail-in voting for Wisconsinites and how President Trump’s proposed rule could further jeopardize Wisconsinites’ access to the ballot box. In 2024, 500,000 Wisconsinites used mail-in ballots, nearly 15% of all Wisconsin voters.

Despite the vital role of mail-in voting, the Wisconsin Elections Commission (WEC), which administers elections in Wisconsin, found that during Wisconsin’s Spring Election this April, two-thirds of local election officials reported problems with the mail, and more than half reported receiving voter complaints and concerns about the Postal Service. According to WEC, one out of every four clerks reported receiving more late ballots than is typical for an election—with some reporting election mail taking 7 to 10 days or more to reach polling locations. Clerks also reported that some of the ballots they received after the election were not postmarked.

The lawmakers called on the Postal Service officials to address these delays ahead of this year’s August 11th primary and November 3rd general election. They also called on the Trump administration to immediately reverse course on President Trump’s executive order that illegally directs the Postal Service to create a federal mail-in voting list made up of states’ absentee voters’ information. In a U.S. Senate Committee hearing, Postmaster General David Steiner confirmed that if the rule is finalized, the Postal Service would refuse to deliver any mail-in ballots from states that did not comply with this new standard. The proposed rule could ultimately allow the Postal Service to determine whether millions of Americans can receive and cast ballots through the mail. A U.S. District Judge blocked the President’s executive order limiting Americans’ use of mail-in voting, but the Trump administration is expected to appeal the ruling.

“Given the history of extremely close elections in Wisconsin, the President’s unconstitutional executive order and the Postal Service’s misguided rule very well could tip the scales of the election and deprive Wisconsinites from having their voices heard accurately,” Baldwin and Evers wrote.

Previously, Senator Baldwin has spoken out in strong opposition and demanded that the USPS abandon this rule. Senator Baldwin has also called for an investigation into USPS delays that caused Wisconsin voters’ ballots to arrive after Election Day this past spring.

A full version of this letter is available here and below.

Dear Postmaster General Steiner, Chairwoman McReynolds, Vice Chairman Kan, Governor Stroman, and Governor Tangherlini:

We write to you about the United States Postal Service’s (USPS) role in ensuring that Wisconsin’s elections are fair and reliable and to express our serious concerns that USPS is threatening Wisconsinites’ ability to exercise their right to vote. Hundreds of absentee ballots received by the Postal Service before Wisconsin's Spring Election were delivered after Election Day, preventing them from being counted. Now, USPS is rushing to implement President Trump's unconstitutional executive order that would, at best, significantly delay Wisconsinites' mailed ballots from reaching election officials and, at worst, allow the USPS to prevent a Wisconsin voter's fully legal, timely ballot from being counted at all. We call on the Postal Service to immediately resolve the issues that delayed ballots during Wisconsin’s Spring Election, withdraw the rule that will add significant additional delays in ballot delivery, and ensure preparations for Wisconsin’s fall elections prioritizes timely delivery of election mail.

In May, the Wisconsin Elections Commission (WEC) sent a letter to the Postmaster General expressing grave concerns about the performance of election mail for Wisconsin’s Spring Election. The Commission is a bipartisan body that administers elections across the State of Wisconsin and assists election clerks in all 72 counties. WEC conducted a survey of Wisconsin’s local election officials and found that two-thirds reported problems with the mail, and more than half reported receiving voter complaints and concerns about the Postal Service. One out of every four clerks reported receiving more late ballots than is typical for an election—with some reporting election mail taking 7 to 10 days or more to reach polling locations. Clerks also reported that some of the ballots they received after the election were not postmarked. This is unacceptable.

We appreciate the work of the men and women who deliver mail for the United States Postal Service every day, including during our elections. Our concern lies with the decisions and actions by USPS that are inconsistent with normal operations and threaten the ability of Wisconsinites to exercise their right to vote. We ask that you resolve any outstanding issues that caused delays in the delivery of Spring Election ballots before Wisconsin’s upcoming elections this fall—the primary election on August 11, 2026 and the general election on November 3, 2026. We also echo the request from the bipartisan Wisconsin Elections Commission to enact extraordinary measures for these elections to help ensure that every ballot reaches its destination as quickly as possible.

To add to these concerns, USPS has proposed a rule to implement President Trump’s unconstitutional executive order that directs the Postal Service to create a federal mail-in voting list using absentee voter information collected from the states. Not only will this rule restrict vote by mail, but if this rule is put in place for the upcoming elections, it will create significant timing and logistical hurdles for Wisconsin voters. It will add days or longer to the process of mailing a ballot. Wisconsin’s Spring Election demonstrated that the Postal Service is already struggling to deliver ballots on time. Adding days or more to the travel time of a ballot will most certainly lead to USPS preventing more eligible voters from having their ballots counted in future elections through no fault of their own. We ask that you abandon this proposed rule immediately.

These changes in USPS service are poised to disproportionately impact Wisconsin’s rural residents. Roughly one in three Wisconsinites live in rural areas with reduced access to polling locations and drop boxes and often rely on voting by mail. These Wisconsinites will be subject to these unnecessary delays and more likely to have their ballots not make it to their clerk on time to be counted.

The implications of these delays cannot be overstated. In 2024, 500,000 Wisconsinites used mail-in ballots, nearly 15% of all Wisconsin voters. Also in 2024, both the Presidential and U.S. Senate elections were decided by less than 30,000 votes. Given the history of extremely close elections in Wisconsin, the President’s unconstitutional executive order and the Postal Service’s misguided rule could very well tip the scales of the election and deprive Wisconsinites from having their voices heard accurately.

The Postal Service has a critical responsibility to ensure that election mail is handled with the urgency and reliability that voters, election officials, and the public rightly expect. To meet this responsibility, USPS must address delays we saw in Wisconsin’s Spring Election and not move forward with the rule restricting vote by mail. Ensuring the timely delivery of election mail is essential to protecting every eligible Wisconsinite’s right to vote and maintaining public confidence in our elections. When ballots fail to arrive in time to be counted, voters are denied the opportunity to participate in our democracy through no fault of their own. These failures not only disenfranchise individual voters, but also erode trust in the reliability and fairness of our elections.

We appreciate your prompt attention to this important matter.

title: Senate HELP Committee Advances Sen. Banks’ SAFE Drugs Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Yesterday, the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee voted to advance the SAFE Drugs Act of 2026, introduced by Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.). The bipartisan legislation would strengthen patient safety and increase transparency in the pharmacy compounding industry. The SAFE Drugs Act passed the Committee with a vote of 17-5 and now heads to the Senate floor.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “Americans deserve to know their medications are safe and coming from legitimate sources. The SAFE Drugs Act makes online pharmacies more transparent and helps the FDA hold compounding pharmacies accountable if they break the rules.”

Sen. Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.): “New Mexicans deserve to know when a medication is not FDA-approved and may carry serious risks. Our SAFE Drug Act helps protect patients by requiring compounders to clearly label medications that are not FDA-approved and report when things go wrong. Advancing this legislation out of committee is an important first step toward increasing transparency, strengthening oversight of pharmacy compounders, and better protecting patients.”

Key Provisions of SAFE Drugs Act of 2026:

Requires 503A compounding pharmacies to report serious adverse events associated with their drug products to the Food and Drug Administration (FDA).

Requires all compounded drug products to be clearly labeled so patients can distinguish them from FDA-approved medications.

Requires 503A compounders that ship significant volumes across state lines to report production volumes to the FDA.

Modernizes federal pharmacy compounding law while preserving patient access to customized medications.

Aligns key safety safeguards between 503A compounding pharmacies and 503B outsourcing facilities.

Background:

Compounding is an important part of the pharmacy profession that provides tailored medications to patients with unique needs. The substantial growth in pharmacy compounding activity associated with the expansion of telehealth and online prescribing necessitates modernizing the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act’s pharmacy compounding procedures. Patients must know the medications they are getting are safe.

Statements from key supporting organizations:

“Manufacturers were glad to see the Senate HELP Committee advance the SAFE Drugs Act, a bill the NAM supported. This is an important step toward protecting patients from potentially unsafe, non-FDA-approved drugs produced by underregulated compounding pharmacies. Congress should move quickly to pass it.” –National Association of Manufacturers, Managing VP of Policy, Charles Crain. “

“The ADA is pleased an amended version of the SAFE Drugs Act passed out the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee today and appreciates the bipartisan support and work to improve patient safety. Compounded medications play an important role in our health care system, but ongoing concerns have been raised of the widespread availability and promotion of non-FDA approved compounded GLP-1 class of medication to treat obesity directly to patients. The amended SAFE Drugs Acttakes an important step to improve transparency, labeling disclosures and adverse event and volume reporting for compounded medications. These are needed changes to address current gaps in transparency for patients, and health professionals.”– Catherine Ferguson, Senior Vice President, American Diabetes Association.

“The Alliance for Safe Online Pharmacies is grateful to Senator Banks and Heinrich for their leadership in advancing the SAFE Drugs Act. This legislation will help close loopholes that allow unsafe, unapproved medicines to reach patients, including through illegal online sellers. We look forward to working with Congress to advance these protections.”– Leigh Verbois, ASOP Global Board Chair.

Full bill text can be found here.

title: Sens. Banks and Schiff Introduce Bill to Help American AI Companies Combat Chinese Espionage
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senators Jim Banks (R-Ind.) and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced the bipartisan Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act, legislation to help American artificial intelligence companies work together to defend against espionage by Communist China and other serious national security threats.

As American companies race to advance Artificial Intelligence systems, foreign adversaries are increasingly attempting to steal U.S. technology through cyber-attacks, model theft, and ‘distillation’ attacks that replicate advanced AI models at a fraction of the cost. While existing laws allow companies to share information about cyber threats, there is no comparable legal framework allowing AI developers to coordinate against emerging AI-specific security risks.

The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act creates a narrowly tailored antitrust safe harbor allowing AI companies to share threat information and coordinate defensive measures in good faith to address defined national security risks while preserving existing antitrust protections against price-fixing, monopolization, and other anticompetitive conduct.

Sen. Jim Banks (R-Ind.): “The AI race is one that America can’t afford to lose. Communist China is working every day to steal our technology and close the gap with the United States. American AI companies must be able to collaboratively defend against our adversaries. The bill gives them the tools to protect America’s technological edge and helps ensure we maintain our competitive edge.”

Sen. Adam Schiff (D-Calif.): “We cannot allow China, or any foreign adversary, to steal American technological advancements in AI, and then weaponize those advances to undermine our own national security. The solution we are proposing would protect against AI distillation attacks and other security risks by allowing increased information-sharing among U.S. AI labs to counter the threat of foreign theft. As new AI innovations are developing faster than ever, it’s critical that Republicans and Democrats continue to work together to address potential misuse of AI development by hostile actors at home and abroad.”

Key Provisions of Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks:

The legislation allows AI developers to collaborate to identify, assess, prevent, investigate, and mitigate defined AI security risks including:

Preventing the theft, distillation, weaponization, or misuse of advanced American AI models by foreign adversaries.

Sharing information on cybersecurity vulnerabilities, unauthorized access, and attacks targeting frontier AI systems.

Addressing AI-enabled chemical, biological, radiological, nuclear, and offensive cyber threats.

Coordinating responses to risks involving loss of operational control over advanced AI systems.

The legislation includes strict guardrails to ensure these protections cannot be used to undermine competition. It explicitly prohibits price-fixing, market allocation, monopolization, boycotts, or any other anticompetitive conduct unrelated to legitimate AI security and national security threats.

Background:

The legislation responds to growing evidence that foreign adversaries are conducting industrial-scale efforts to steal America’s most advanced AI capabilities. According to public reports, Chinese actors have used tens of thousands of fraudulent accounts to extract millions of interactions from leading U.S. AI systems in an effort to replicate frontier models. The White House has also warned that China is conducting deliberate campaigns to distill advanced American AI systems.

The bill has bipartisan, bicameral support and is supported by a broad coalition of organizations and experts.

“Building on the proven foundation of CISA 2015, the Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act brings a strengthened threat-sharing framework into the AI era. Protecting critical infrastructure and cutting-edge AI systems requires real-time coordination against sophisticated security threats. This bill strikes a vital balance: empowering tech leaders to collaborate on cyber, CBRN, loss-of-control, and foreign adversarial risks while maintaining strong antitrust protections.” – Paul Lekas, Executive VP for Global Public Policy & Government Affairs, Software & Information Industry Association (SIIA).

“This bipartisan bill gives the AI industry clear rules of the road to share threat intelligence and collaborate on much-needed standard and benchmarks. We appreciate the leadership of Senators Schiff and Banks and Representatives Whiteside and Latta in working to ensure the continued responsible development of frontier models.” – John Connell, VP of Government Affairs and Public Policy, Google.

“The benefits of the CATS Act extend far beyond AI tech companies. By removing antitrust barriers to sharing critical information about adversarial AI threats, this legislation directly protects downstream critical infrastructure. For Health-ISAC and the health sector, this means safeguarding national public health and patient safety from emerging security risks and ultimately keeping Americans safer.” – Denise Anderson, President & CEO, Health-ISAC.

“Antitrust law was never meant to stop American AI companies from collaborating on security. This commonsense policy would give American AI developers the legal clarity they need to share threat intelligence and security best practices while preserving enforcement against genuine anticompetitive conduct. It’s a reform that strengthens American innovation and puts our national security first.” – Yusuf Mahmood, Policy Director, America First Policy Institute.

“Making America AI-ready means making institutions more resilient and equipped to respond to AI security risks. Giving companies a clear, lawful path to share threat information raises the security floor for the whole country while advancing American leadership in AI.” – Joshua New, Director of Policy, SeedAI.

“The worst AI security threats — a foreign adversary stealing a frontier model, a serious loss of control — won’t be contained to a single company. Developers need to be able to share threat information and coordinate, and this bill lets them do that. When companies can coordinate on threats without legal risk, they lose the excuse for staying silent, and the public is safer for it.” – Sunny Gandhi, Co-Executive Director, Encode AI.

“We urgently need legislation that lets frontier AI developers collaborate on national security risks, such as adversarial distillation, without being deterred by uncertainties regarding antitrust law. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and AI Security Risks Act would provide targeted protections paired with appropriate guardrails against misuse.” – Tim Schnabel, President, Law Reform Institute.

“AI developers are confronting increasingly sophisticated threats involving model theft, unauthorized access, critical infrastructure, and other serious security risks. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act would extend existing protections to information sharing and coordination around AI-specific threats, promoting real-time situational awareness among frontier labs and other AI developers. Importantly, the bill includes safeguards to ensure this protection is limited to good-faith security collaboration and does not excuse anticompetitive conduct.” – Morgan Reed, President, Association for Competitive Technology (ACT).

“I commend Senators Schiff and Banks for their bipartisan legislation. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Strategic Risks Act improves the speed at which national security risks arising from adversarial espionage and autonomous improvement of artificial intelligence models can be identified and addressed.” – Mark Beall, President, AI Policy Network.

“Advanced AI systems could be exploited by foreign adversaries, used to develop biological or cyber weapons, threaten critical infrastructure, or operate beyond meaningful human control. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act is a common sense step that will help America’s leading AI companies work together to identify and reduce these risks before they become an emergency,” – Brendan Steinhauser, CEO, The Alliance for Secure AI.

“As advanced AI systems increasingly become prime targets for espionage and theft by bad actors and global competitors, AI companies need a secure way to share threat information and coordinate defenses without risking antitrust violations. The Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Security Risks Act would create a narrow exemption for companies to rely on, while keeping safeguards against price fixing, market allocation, and other anti-competitive behavior fully intact. By strengthening companies’ ability to detect and respond to these risks, this bill will help keep Americans protected from the real-world harms posed by compromised AI systems. The Center for AI Safety Action Fund is proud to support this bill.” – Varun Krovi, Executive Director, Center for AI Safety Action Fund.

“America’s technology leadership is increasingly jeopardized by the inability of our frontier AI companies to coordinate on issues core to U.S. national security, from countering foreign espionage to cybersecurity information sharing. This bill provides the legal clarity needed for industry to collaborate on urgent AI security threats without undermining market competition.” – Samuel Hammond, Director of Artificial Intelligence & Chief Economist, the Foundation for American Innovation.

“As AI capabilities accelerate, so do the threats posed by foreign adversaries and malicious actors. Representative Latta’s bill removes unnecessary barriers to responsible collaboration, allowing companies to share critical security information in good faith to address covered AI risks. America’s AI leadership depends not only on innovation, but on ensuring our innovators can work together to defend the technologies that are essential to our economic and national security.” – Janet Kelly, CEO, Alliance for a Better Future.

“The Chinese Communist Party is actively seeking to close the AI gap through espionage and distillation of our most advanced AI models. American AI developers should not fear violating antitrust laws for collaborating to defend against those threats. This bill takes a commonsense step toward protecting U.S. technological leadership and preventing America’s most advanced AI systems from becoming tools of our adversaries.” – Autumn Dorsey, Center for Technology and the Human Person, The Heritage Foundation.

“The evidence is increasingly clear. AI companies in the U.S. are facing targeted attacks from PRC-aligned companies. Yet, existing antitrust law can discourage them from coordinating their defenses. A narrow, carefully tailored exemption would give responsible AI companies the confidence to share information and work together on serious threats without running afoul of competition law.” – Will Rinehart, Senior Fellow, AEI.

“Senator Banks’ Collaboration on Adversarial Threats and Securities Risks Act strikes the right balance between important AI security research collaboration and antitrust risk. While information sharing between rivals can create competition risk, the exemption in this bill is well crafted to minimize this concern while ensuring that AI labs are able to coordinate their defenses against our geopolitical adversaries.” – Gale Slater, Competition and Technology Policy Chair, American Compass.

title: Bennet, Hickenlooper, Hurd Introduce Legislation to Protect Glenwood Hot Springs Amid Renewed Gravel Mining Threats
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper and Colorado U.S. Congressman Jeff Hurd led the introduction of the Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act. This legislation would prevent the Department of the Interior (DOI) from expanding the Mid-Continent Limestone Quarry, protecting the Glenwood hot springs, a defining natural resource that supports the local economy and makes the community a key destination for visitors.

Earlier this month, the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) announced that the Rocky Mountain Industrials, Inc. (RMI) proposal to expand the Mid-Continent Limestone Quarry is complete, bringing the company one step closer to restarting operations and tripling the size of the quarry. These mining efforts have faced substantial pushback from local communities because the project could affect the hot springs’ geothermal groundwater network, harming the Glenwood hot springs and the local economy.

“Putting the Glenwood hot springs, a Colorado landmark and a one-of-a-kind resource, at risk would be shortsighted and irresponsible,” said Bennet. “Our legislation would protect Glenwood Springs’ economic future, an important cultural site for the Ute Tribes since time immemorial, and the quality of life of local residents.”

“On a June visit to Glenwood Springs, we heard firsthand from community members and city officials about their concerns over a potential expansion of the Mid-Continent Limestone Quarry, which could hurt water resources and local tourism,” said Hickenlooper. “We stand with the Glenwood Springs community and are committed to doing everything we can to stop the quarry expansion.”

“The Glenwood Hot Springs are one of Colorado’s great treasures and an important part of what makes the Western Slope such a special place to live, work, and visit,” said Hurd. “They support local jobs, small businesses, and a tourism economy that benefits the entire community. We can support responsible resource development while also recognizing that not every location is appropriate for expansion. This isn’t about stopping mining—it’s about protecting an irreplaceable resource from the expansion of a gravel quarry onto adjacent federal lands. That’s a common-sense approach that preserves the hot springs, respects the community’s concerns, and helps ensure future generations can enjoy this Colorado landmark.”

Since 2018, RMI has proposed to expand the Mid-Continent Limestone Quarry near Glenwood Springs. The original proposal would have expanded the quarry permit from about 16 acres to more than 400 acres under the 1872 General Mining Law that is typically employed for mining high-value minerals. The quarry site and RMI’s mining claims are on public lands managed by the BLM.

In 2024, the BLM’s 2024 Determination of Common Variety found that the quarry was mining and selling common gravel rather than a high-quality limestone product that could be permitted under the General Mining Law. Unlike hardrock mines, common-variety materials require stricter environmental review and sales contracts with the BLM. In January 2025, the DOI confirmed this with an official decision requiring the quarry operator to either prove that an actual market exists for high-quality limestone uses, or propose a mineral material sales contract to mine for construction materials. This came about as the result of years of litigation brought by Garfield County and the Glenwood Springs Citizens Alliance to compel BLM to enforce its regulations.

In June, the BLM announced that RMI had completed its application materials for a new plan of operations that would triple the size of the quarry permit from 16 to 56 acres. The local community has raised major concerns with the proposal around safety, increased truck traffic, and damage to the area’s hot springs and cultural resources.

“The Southern Ute Indian Tribe strongly supports the Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act. As the oldest stewards of Colorado, we recognize these hot springs as a place of healing, renewal, and deep cultural significance. Protecting these sacred waters ensures they remain a source of wellness and connection for generations to come. We thank Congressman Jeff Hurd, Senator Michael Bennet, Senator John Hickenlooper, and all those supporting this legislation for their leadership in safeguarding this irreplaceable resource,” said Chairman Marvin Pinnecoose of the Southern Ute Indian Tribe.

“This legislation is an important step in recognizing the bi-partisan, united opposition to expanding the Mid-Continent limestone quarry. Rocky Mountain Industrials’ proposals are simply too dangerous to risk our hot springs and tourism economic engines, valued by locals and visitors alike. We thank Representative Hurd and Senators Bennet and Hickenlooper for their leadership on this critical issue for our community,” said Glenwood Springs Mayor Pro-tem Erin Zalinski.

“The Glenwood Springs Citizens’ Alliance appreciates Representative Jeff Hurd and Senator Michael Bennet recognizing the importance of this issue to our community and working together to introduce bipartisan legislation. This bill will help protect our water supply, preserve the character of our community, and ensure that Glenwood Springs continues to thrive as both a place to live and a world-class visitor destination,” said Jeff Peterson, President, Glenwood Springs Citizens’ Alliance.

“The Glenwood Springs Chamber fully supports the bipartisan Hot Springs Protection Act and sincerely thanks Congressman Jeff Hurd and Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper for their leadership and support. This legislation reflects our community’s longstanding commitment to protecting the natural resources that define Glenwood Springs and support our thriving tourism economy, outdoor recreation, and quality of life for generations to come,” said Angie Anderson, President and CEO, Glenwood Springs Chamber

“Since 1888 the hot springs pool has been a place of wellness and recreation. As one of the oldest standing businesses in Colorado, the pool is gravely concerned about a mining company potentially harming this fragile resource. There are too many unknowns to risk destroying the historic and natural beauty of Glenwood Springs,” said Douglas Hayes, Chief Executive Officer, Glenwood Hot Springs Resort.

“The Glenwood Hot Springs Protection Act is essential to safeguarding the geothermal waters that sustain our resort, our local economy, and the character of our community. Protecting this irreplaceable resource will help ensure Colorado’s hot springs remain healthy and accessible for generations to come. We are grateful to Senator Bennet, Rep. Hurd, and Senator Hickenlooper for driving this forward,” said Aaron McCallister, General Manager, Iron Mountain Hot Springs.

Bennet has supported the Glenwood Springs community in opposing the quarry for years. Earlier this year, Bennet requested language in the FY27 Senate Interior Appropriations bill that would prohibit the use of federal funds to approve the required mining permits at the Mid-Continent Limestone Quarry, either on the existing or the expanded footprint and requested an amendment to the National Defense Authorization Act to prohibit the approval of applications for the expansion. In 2023, he cheered the designation of the Glenwood hot springs as a National Natural Landmark, and he visited the area, committing to continue to support the community’s fight against the quarry. In 2019, he worked with former Rep. Tipton and former Senator Cory Gardner to push back against the original quarry expansion proposal.

title: Bennet Statement on Trump-Saudi Nuclear Deal
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, released the following statement after the Trump Administration signed and announced an agreement under Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act to provide Saudi Arabia with sensitive U.S. nuclear technology without adequate nuclear nonproliferation safeguards:

“President Trump should not agree to any nuclear cooperation agreement that provides Saudi Arabia sensitive U.S. nuclear technology without the ‘gold standard’ set of nuclear safeguards we’ve correctly demanded from other countries.

“The Trump-Saudi deal will not advance a peaceful and prosperous Middle East. Instead, it risks undermining the global nuclear non-proliferation regime while threatening to instigate a nuclear arms race across an already volatile region – including by entrenching Iran’s nuclear ambitions, which will make it even harder to end Trump’s disastrous war. This deal will also alienate partners who agreed to the same standards Trump is waiving for Saudi Arabia.

“The Senate must pass a joint resolution of disapproval under the Atomic Energy Act before this agreement takes effect.”

title: NEWS: Senators Blunt Rochester, Sheehy Introduce Bill to Expand Participation in AI Education, Research, and Workforce
text:
U.S. Senators Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.) and Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.), both members of the Senate Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation, introduced the bipartisan Expanding AI Voices Act, which codifies and expands the National Science Foundation’s ExpandAI program to help more institutions build AI research capacity. The legislation will broaden the range of institutions and communities involved in AI research and workforce development, including first-generation college students, Minority-serving Institutions (MSIs), and rural colleges and universities. The House companion is led by Representatives Valerie Foushee (D-N.C.) and Zach Nunn (R-Iowa).

“AI offers tremendous opportunities for our communities and economies, but as this technology changes the way we live, we must guarantee that our students and our workforce still have the chance to succeed,” said Senator Blunt Rochester. “I’m proud to introduce the Expanding AI Voices Act alongside Senator Sheehy to ensure that no matter where we come from, we can all achieve our goals in the economy of the future.”

“America’s AI leadership depends on finding talent in every corner of the country. That’s why I’m introducing the Expanding AI Voices Act with Senator Blunt Rochester, which helps ensure students and researchers in Montana and other rural states have the opportunity to contribute to the future of AI innovation,” said Senator Tim Sheehy. “Our bipartisan legislation invests in people and institutions that have too often been overlooked, strengthens our workforce, and maintains America’s competitive edge by supporting critical innovation. Let’s get it done.”

The Expanding AI Voices Act would:

Expand AI research capacity by authorizing competitive NSF grants for emerging research institutions, including institutions outside the top 100 in federal R&D expenditures, Minority-Serving Institutions (MSIs), Historically Black Colleges and Universities (HBCUs), Tribal Colleges and Universities (TCUs), and eligible institutional consortia.

Expand AI research infrastructure by supporting access to advanced computing resources, high-speed networking, data facilities, and software engineering support needed to conduct cutting-edge AI research.

Build the AI workforce pipeline by supporting AI education, faculty recruitment and professional development, workforce training, and bridge programs that prepare students for graduate study and careers in artificial intelligence.

Accelerate AI innovation through partnerships by fostering collaboration among colleges and universities, nonprofit organizations, industry, Federal laboratories, state, local, and Tribal governments, and NSF AI Research Institutes.

Expand opportunity nationwide by encouraging geographic diversity, supporting institutions with limited AI research capacity, and increasing opportunities for students—including first-generation college students—to participate in AI research and education.

Promote safe, secure, and responsible AI by integrating safe, secure, and responsible AI practices and principles into AI education and workforce development programs.

Protect Taxpayer Dollars by requiring NSF to ensure awards complement—not duplicate—existing federal AI research programs.

“If we want to win the AI race, we can’t rely on a small handful of schools and people. SeedAI has experienced this first-hand during our AI Across America tour — it’s imperative that we go beyond the coasts and draw from the experiences and ingenuity of all Americans,” said Austin Carson, Founder and CEO of SeedAI. “The Expanding AI Voices Act will help build the AI research capacity needed to make that a reality. SeedAI thanks Senator Blunt Rochester and Senator Sheehy for their bipartisan leadership to strengthen American competitiveness.”

“America’s AI economy is moving faster than our workforce can keep up, and that gap will only widen without action. The Expanding AI Voices Act, introduced by Sens. Blunt Rochester (D-DE) and Sheehy (R-MT), meets that challenge head-on by giving students and teachers the tools to compete in an economy being reshaped by AI in real time. This bill also recognizes that opportunity shouldn’t be limited to those who can already afford a foothold. Its focus on first-generation undergraduate students ensures the next generation of AI talent includes voices from every background. BPC Action applauds Sens. Blunt Rochester and Sheehy for their leadership and urges the Senate to move quickly to pass it,” says Michele Stockwell, president, Bipartisan Policy Center Action.

“For America to lead on AI, we need to expand the pipeline of talent that’s fueling innovation,” said ARI President Brad Carson. “By investing in education, research, and workforce development across a broader range of institutions and communities, the Expanding AI Voices Act helps ensure the future of AI is shaped by the full scope of American talent. It’s exactly the kind of bipartisan, forward-looking policy the U.S. needs to maintain its edge in AI.”

The Expanding AI Voices Act is endorsed by the American Mathematical Society, Americans for Responsible Innovation, Association of Community College Trustees, Bipartisan Policy Center Action, Google, Leadership Conference on Civil and Human Rights, National Hispanic Health Foundation, SeedAI, Society of Hispanic Professional Engineers, IBM, Information Technology Industry Council (ITI), Thurgood Marshall College Fund.

title: Booker, Budd Reintroduce Bipartisan Legislation to Bring Dental Care to Millions of Americans
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ) and Ted Budd (R-NC) reintroduced the Action for Dental Health Act, bipartisan legislation to close the gap in dental care access for communities across the nation facing severe provider shortages. The bill reauthorizes the Health Resources and Services Administration's (HRSA) grant funding to address dental workforce needs at $15 million annually for fiscal years 2027 through 2031, helping states recruit, train, and retain dental providers where they are needed most.

“Oral health is inseparable from our overall health, but for too many Americans, where they live limits their access to routine dental care because of workforce shortages,” said Senator Booker. “By passing this bipartisan legislation, we can strengthen the dental workforce, help states meet the needs of underserved communities, and ensure more Americans receive the preventive care they need and deserve.”

The need is stark: 63 million Americans live in areas without access to dental care, and the country needs 10,700 more dental practitioners just to meet current demand. In 2024, only 66 percent of adults saw a dentist at all–leaving millions to face preventable pain, infection, and costs that routing care could have stopped.

“Americans deserve access to reliable dental care, but with 63 million Americans living in areas impacted by industry workforce shortages, closing the oral healthcare provider gap is needed to put patients first. I am proud to join my colleague, Senator Booker, in introducing this bipartisan legislation to help ensure more Americans can get the care they need,” said Senator Budd.

“Everyone deserves access to oral health care. Reauthorizing Action for Dental Health will maintain and expand proven programs that connect underserved communities with vital dental services they need to improve their health now and for years to come. We thank Senators Booker and Budd for championing this important legislation and helping move us closer to a future where more Americans can access the critical oral health care they need,” said ADA President Richard Rosato, D.M.D.

The Action for Dental Health Act is endorsed by the American Dental Association.

Read a one-pager on the bill here.

title: Booker Leads Colleagues in Urging Surface Transportation Board to Conduct Rigorous Review of Proposed $185 Billion Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern Merger
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ), joined by a group of 22 Senate colleagues, sent a letter to the Surface Transportation Board (STB) urging the agency to conduct a thorough and independent review of Union Pacific Railroad’s proposed $185 billion acquisition of Norfolk Southern Railway, warning that the merger could significantly affect workers, consumers, competition, and the nation’s freight rail system. The proposed transaction would combine two of the nation’s four largest freight railroads, creating the first transcontinental railroad and the largest railroad company in American history.

“As the Surface Transportation Board (STB) considers the proposed merger between Union Pacific Railroad (UP) and Norfolk Southern Railway (NS), we write to express serious concern about the transaction and urge you to thoroughly investigate the potential impacts it would have on competition, workers, and safety in an increasingly consolidated rail industry. If approved, the unprecedented merger would not only create the first transcontinental railroad but it would significantly consolidate our nation’s transportation system, slashing rail jobs across the country, raising prices for customers and consumers, and creating potential supply chain bottlenecks and greater market instability,” wrote the senators.

“The proposed UP-NS merger would affect upwards of 50,000 employees directly, though workers on all railroads within the United States will be impacted either directly or indirectly. While under federal law rail workers are provided standard ‘New York Dock’ labor protections, which provide job security after a merger, recent trends in the rail industry have created risks to these workers’ job protections and collective bargaining agreements under a standard merger agreement,” wrote the senators.

“We also ask the STB to scrutinize any workforce reductions undertaken by UP or NS before consummation of the transaction, as such actions would undermine any commitment to maintain the workforce afterward,” continued the senators.

“In addition to threatening job protections and job stability for rail workers, the proposed merger poses substantial risks for shippers themselves as it will further concentrate market power in an industry that already has limited competitive options. Combining UP and NS would create a single rail handling nearly half of the nation’s rail freight. This significantly increases the likelihood of higher transportation rates and reduces service alternatives for farmers and businesses that depend on reliable, cost-effective rail service,” continued the senators.

The senators are urging the STB to specifically:

Conduct a thorough investigation of whether the proposed Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern transaction meets the STB’s requirements that a combination will enhance competition.

Solicit testimony and evidence regarding the proposed transaction’s impact on rail customers and consumers of goods that are shipped by rail.

Conduct a rigorous assessment of the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger’s impacts on rail safety, staffing levels, workforce quality of life, system performance, and competition.

Solicit testimony and evidence regarding past workplace commitments made by UP and NS, including whether such assurances were measurable, enforceable, and ultimately realized.

Evaluate the broader implications of further consolidation in the industry, including effects on national employment levels, job displacement, and the resilience of the freight rail network.

“Ultimately, the proposed transaction’s likely harms to competition, workers, safety, customers and consumers indicate that the parties are unlikely to demonstrate that this merger would enhance competition and satisfy the public interest standard,” concluded the senators.

Senator Booker was joined by Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT),Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Ed Markey (D-MA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Tina Smith (D-MN), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Peter Welch (D-VT).

title: Booker Leads Congressional Democrats in Renewed Push to Guarantee a Nationwide Right to IVF and Lower Costs for Families
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-NJ), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY), and Patty Murray (D-WA) reintroduced the Right to IVF Act, a sweeping legislative package to tear down the barriers that keep millions of hopeful parents from building their families through in-vitro fertilization (IVF) and other assisted reproductive technology (ART). This pro-family legislation would guarantee a nationwide right to access IVF, slash the cost of treatment, expand IVF coverage for military families, and require every employer-sponsored insurance plan in the country to cover it.

“No one chooses infertility,” said Senator Booker. “It’s a medical condition that leaves too many families and individuals feeling alone long before they ever seek treatment. When people turn to IVF, they’re choosing hope. They’re choosing the chance to build the family they’ve always dreamed of. But that hope comes with a price tag that is simply out of reach for far too many. The medications, procedures, and cycles can cost tens of thousands of dollars. Families and individuals already carrying the emotional weight of infertility are then hit with financial barriers that no one should have to face trying to bring a child into this world. We have to change that. We have to remove those barriers and make IVF affordable and accessible to everyone who needs it. Because the ability to build a family should not be reserved for the wealthy or the lucky, it should be within reach for us all.”

“Almost two years after promising free IVF for all Americans if he were elected, Donald Trump has still failed to deliver,” said Senator Duckworth. “Trump and Republicans’ ‘support’ for IVF is nothing but lip service. They want us to have more babies, yet they’ll do nothing to actually help make it easier for the millions who struggle with infertility to start and grow their families. The Right to IVF Act would immediately make IVF treatment more affordable for millions of hopeful parents across the country. From middle class families, to our brave servicemembers and Veterans, to federal employees and more—every American deserves the right to access the treatment and tools they need to build the family of their dreams without burning through their savings. If Republicans really support IVF, then let’s get this done. No more delays.”

“For millions of American families, IVF isn’t politics—it’s hope,” said Leader Schumer. “Donald Trump ran on a promise that he would make IVF free, and yet he has done nothing but attack women’s reproductive rights and undermine access to fertility care—another lie in his long list of broken promises to American families. Our Right to IVF Act is essential to putting a deeply personal health care decision back in the hands of American families. While Donald Trump and Republicans erect barriers between hopeful parents and IVF, Democrats will never stop fighting to protect access so that every family can build the future they dream of.”

“Republicans are not pro-family and they won’t lift a finger to help families get IVF—the Texas Republican Party just recently made banning IVF a part of their official party platform,” said Senator Murray. “I have fought for a long time to make sure at least servicemembers and veterans, especially wounded warriors, can get the IVF care they need to build a family. But the reality is that we have a Republican Speaker of the House who believes an embryo should have the same rights as an adult woman with children who count on her. America’s pro-IVF majority should wake up to the fact that Trump could not care less about IVF—he broke that promise and he is happy to let Republicans attack IVF and all of our reproductive rights. Meanwhile, Democrats are fighting to make sure all Americans can access and afford health care to build their families.”

U.S. Representatives Lori Trahan (D-MA-03), James Walkinshaw (D-VA-11), Rick Larsen (D-WA-02), Rosa DeLauro (D-CT-03) and Laura Gillen (D-NY-04) are introducing companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

“Like so many people in our country facing fertility challenges, my husband and I turned to IVF as our last hope to have kids,” said Representative Trahan. “After years of appointments, injections, and setbacks, and thanks to our remarkable physicians, we have two beautiful daughters. No one should lose the chance to start or grow a family because of their zip code. The Right to IVF Act guarantees the right to family-creating fertility care in every state and puts it within reach for the millions of families who need it.”

“Deciding when and how to build a family is a deeply personal choice that belongs to families, not politicians,” said Representative Walkinshaw. “For millions struggling with infertility, IVF offers hope and a path to parenthood. I’m especially proud the Right to IVF Act includes my legislation requiring IVF coverage through the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program, ensuring the federal government leads by example. I’m honored to join Senator Duckworth, Congresswoman Trahan, and this coalition to protect IVF nationwide and expand access for servicemembers, veterans, federal employees, and working families.”

“For many Americans, fertility treatments like IVF are essential to start families of their own,” said Representative Larsen. “This comprehensive legislation will guarantee access and expand coverage for IVF and other fertility services. The legislation also includes my bill with Senator Murray, the Veteran Families Health Services Act, to ensure fertility treatments are included in servicemembers’ and veterans’ health benefits. I will keep working with my colleagues in the House and the Senate to make sure that women and men in uniform and working families do not have to sacrifice their dreams of having a family.”

“There are few experiences as hard as wanting to start a family and not being able to,” said Representative DeLauro. “That is why I am fighting to ensure Americans have access to IVF treatments when they want to start one. I am proud to join my colleagues in introducing the Right to IVF Act – because building a family in the United States should never be difficult.”

“I am proud to help lead this critical bill ensuring millions of Americans can access IVF to build their families, no matter where they live,” said Representative Gillen. “Families struggling to conceive go through indescribable heartbreak and stress. The last thing they should worry about is legal challenges to IVF delaying or outright halting procedures. Infertility is not a partisan issue. I will continue to work across the aisle in Congress to protect access to IVF and adjacent reproductive technologies that have helped countless individuals experience the joy of parenthood.”

Last Congress, Senate Republicans shamefully blocked the Right to IVF Act — the fourth time Senate Republicans have blocked legislation to protect nationwide access to IVF — exposing just how hollow their claims to support IVF really are for the millions of Americans who rely on it to build their families. While Senate Democrats keep fighting to protect IVF and reproductive freedom, Senate Republicans keep making it abundantly clear, through their anti-choice extremism and record Medicaid cuts, that they would rather gut basic health care for millions of Americans than make it easier for their own constituents to start and grow a family.

This legislative package builds on Booker's ongoing efforts to protect and strengthen access to IVF, including the Access to Infertility Treatment and Care Act, which would make fertility care — including IVF — more affordable by requiring employer-sponsored and public insurance plans to cover fertility treatments. It would also set a baseline standard of high-quality fertility coverage across private health insurance plans while shielding Americans from excessive out-of-pocket costs.

In addition to Booker, Duckworth, Murray, and Schumer, the legislation is cosponsored by the entire U.S. Senate Democratic Caucus.

The Right to IVF Act is supported by the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM), RESOLVE: The National Infertility and Family Building Association, Center for Reproductive Rights (CRR), Planned Parenthood Federation of America (PPFA), National Women’s Law Center (NWLC), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), GLBTQ Legal Advocates and Defenders (GLAD Law), Academy of Adoption & Assisted Reproduction Attorneys, Stand with IVF, AllPaths Family Building, American Association of People with Disabilities, American Atheists, Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology, Society for Reproductive Endocrinology & Infertility, Society of Reproductive Biologists & Technologists, Society for Reproductive Surgeons, California LGBTQ Health and Human Services Network, Endocrine Society, Equality California, Families USA, GLMA: Health Professionals Advancing LGBTQ+ Equality, Guttmacher Institute, Hadassah, Human Rights Campaign, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, Indivisible, Justice + Joy National Collaborative, Legal Momentum, Military Family Building Coalition, MomsRising, National Asian Pacific American Women’s Forum, National Association of Nurse Practitioners in Women’s Health, National Center for Lesbian Rights, National Council on Jewish Women, National LGBTQ Task Force Action Fund, National Partnership for Women and Families, National Women’s Political Caucus, Physicians for Reproductive Health, Reproductive Freedom for All, Service Women’s Action Network, Silver State Equality, What to Expect Project and Women’s March.

title: Boozman Presses VA on Failure to Establish Oncology Program Partnership with UAMS
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Senator John Boozman, a senior member of the Senate Veterans' Affairs Committee, pushed U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) National Oncology Program Executive Director Dr. Michael Kelley to explain its failure to expand the Precision Oncology Program for Cancer of the Prostate (POPCaP) in contrast to congressional intent. The department was required to extend the prostate cancer initiative, including fostering a new partnership with the Little Rock VA and University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences (UAMS), which has not occurred.

At a VA Committee hearing, Boozman highlighted Chairman Jerry Moran’s (R-KS) introduction of the Precision Oncology Program for Cancer of the Prostate Authorization Act that would designate the Little Rock VA Medical Center, among others, as a Center of Excellence for the POPCaP program.

“Arkansas has built a strong partnership between the Little Rock VA and the University of Arkansas for Medical Sciences, and I believe it is well positioned to become a national leader in precision oncology research and care for veterans,” Boozman said. “Congress provided $5 million to expand the Precision Oncology Program for Cancer of the Prostate to additional VA medical centers and increased academic cancer center partnerships. It is my understanding that VA instead used those funds to establish a broader precision oncology research program covering multiple cancers.”

Expanding access to clinical oncology trials, particularly to areas that currently lack those opportunities, is critical. Boozman worked to secure funding to facilitate a new partnership between UAMS and the VA in the Fiscal Year 2024 appropriations package.

To date, that partnership has not been realized. Instead, the VA utilized the allocated funding to create a broad precision oncology cancer research program without expanding POPCaP sites. The senator has since included language in subsequent appropriations legislation directing the department to submit a report within 30 days after enactment on its plan to maintain the 21 current POPCaP sites and expand to additional locations.

title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt Celebrates $15M Award for HudsonAlpha’s BRIDGES Engine, Following Alabama Delegation Sending Letter of Support
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Katie Britt (R-Ala.) celebrated a recent U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF) award of $15 million to HudsonAlpha Institute for Biotechnology in Huntsville to lead the NSF Biobased Rural Innovation for Domestic Growth and Economic Security (BRIDGES) Engine. The award, granted to just 12 Regional Innovation Engines, comes after Senator Britt joined the Alabama congressional delegation in sending a letter of support for this initiative. The BRIDGES Engine is a partnership across Alabama and Tennessee and has the potential to receive up to $160 million from the NSF over the next decade.

Senator Britt meets with HudsonAlpha VP for Research Administration and Development Dr. Flo Behn, President Dr. Neil Lamb, and Board Chairman Brian Pollack on July 22, 2026.

“I am thrilled to see the National Science Foundation’s $15 million investment in Alabama’s rural communities and manufacturing and agricultural industries,” said Senator Britt. “HudsonAlpha’s groundbreaking initiative will create thousands of jobs and generate millions in economic growth over the next several years. This award from NSF underscores Alabama’s position as a national leader in agricultural dominance and scientific innovation leadership. I look forward to seeing how these transformative efforts showcase the very best of our rural communities while delivering lasting economic opportunity throughout the state.”

Thanks to this historic funding, BRIDGES will work to transform rural economies by advancing domestic biobased manufacturing using locally grown resources. The project combines Alabama’s agricultural and manufacturing strengths and will accelerate rural innovation and broad economic growth by leveraging key partnerships with Auburn University, the University of Tennessee, Volkswagen Group of America, AGgrow Tech LLC, and more than 80 others.

BRIDGES will result in substantial economic impacts to Alabama and is projected to generate at least $7.3 billion in the region over 20 years. The project will deliver more than $30 million in direct farm revenue annually, create around 4,000 rural manufacturing jobs, and bring an estimated $280 million annually in income for Alabama’s rural workforce.

Alabama’s leading role in agriculture, innovation, and manufacturing doesn’t just make a difference across the state—our rural communities are critically important to the entire nation. BRIDGES will help Alabama capitalize on expanding access to high-paying skilled work, diversifying farming and product markets, and amplifying manufacturing capacity.

Senator Britt is a tireless champion of Alabama’s agricultural and manufacturing industries, and was proud to lead the entire bipartisan Alabama delegation in their successful letter of support.

title: Budd, Welch Bipartisan Bill Supporting the Next Generation of American Aviation Advances Out of Committee
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.), member of the Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, and Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) released the following statements after an amended version of their bipartisan Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act passed out of committee. The Senators’ legislation would improve the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) type certification process for American Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) aircraft companies to help them succeed and cement the United States’ role as a global leader in aviation. Updates to the bill reflect further technical assistance from the FAA and the acceptance of a modified amendment by Senator Ed Markey (D-Mass.) to give airline pilots a seat at the table.

“By ensuring that the FAA prioritizes the certification of novel aircraft like eVTOLs, we can quickly incorporate innovative technology into the National Airspace System. I am glad that our common-sense efforts to usher in the next generation of advanced air mobility aircraft will soon be considered by the full Senate,” said Senator Budd.

“Building on generations of leadership in aviation, American companies are spearheading electric aircraft innovation. That includes companies like Vermont’s Beta Technologies, which completed its historic, first-ever electric flight last year in South Burlington. Ensuring the FAA certification process is safe, efficient, and more transparent for emerging AAM companies like Beta is critical to promoting aviation innovation,” said Senator Welch. “I’m thankful for the support of my colleagues on the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, including my bipartisan co-lead Senator Budd, in helping this bill fly through to the Senate Floor to support American ingenuity, good-paying jobs in Vermont, and our global leadership in aviation.”

Joining Senators Budd and Welch as cosponsors of this legislation are Sens. John Curtis (R-Utah), Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.), Jerry Moran (R-Kan.), Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.), and Todd Young (R-Ind.).

“The Committee passage today brings us one step closer to modernizing the FAA certification process for the next generation of aviation,” said Senator Curtis. “This bipartisan bill will provide greater clarity and accountability, helping American Advanced Air Mobility companies innovate, compete, and lead the world in the future of flight. I’m pleased to see it advance and look forward to its passage by the full Senate.”

“New Mexico is a strong leader in aviation technology, and this legislation will help ensure our state continues to shape the next generation of innovation,” said Senator Luján. “This bill will streamline and update the FAA certification processes, accelerate innovation, support new technologies, and strengthen U.S. global leadership in aviation. I’m proud to see this legislation advance and help keep the United States at the forefront of global aviation.”

“Streamlining the FAA’s type certification processes for advanced aviation technologies, such as advanced air mobility, is critical to bolstering America’s global leadership in aviation innovation,” said Senator Moran. “I appreciate the bipartisan support from my colleagues for this legislation, and I’m pleased by this step forward with its passage out of committee today. This legislation would support emerging aerospace technologies and strengthen the aviation industry in Kansas and across the country, and I look forward to its approval by the full Senate.”

“California companies are leading the world in developing the next generation of electric aircraft. I’m proud to see our bill advance to cut through red tape and streamline the FAA certification process, so we can maintain our competitive advantage and keep groundbreaking innovation here at home,” said Senator Padilla.

“As the birthplace of aviation, America must maintain dominance in this critical industry by streamlining outdated bureaucracy and allowing innovators to remain competitive through a transparent, consistent regulatory framework. The bipartisan Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act takes important steps to accomplish these ends, and I’m proud to see it advance out of the Commerce Committee,” said Senator Sheehy.

“Advanced Air Mobility platforms will revolutionize the American economy. The Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act is a crucial step to securing American drone dominance. Our bill will provide much needed clarity and certainty as we seek to establish American leadership in these critical technologies and lay the groundwork for the future of air transportation. The Commerce Committee’s advancement of this bipartisan legislation marks an important step forward, and I look forward to seeing it pass the full Senate,” said Senator Young.

U.S. Representative Troy E. Nehls (R-TX-22), Chair of the House Aviation Subcommittee; Rep. André Carson (D-IN-07), Ranking Member of the House Aviation Subcommittee; Rep. Nicholas Begich (R-AK-AL); Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ-05); Rep. Tracey Mann (R-KS-01); Rep. Jay Obernolte (R-CA-23); Rep. Jimmy Panetta (D-CA-19); and Rep. Tony Wied (R-WI-08) lead companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

The Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act is endorsed by the Aerospace Industries Association (AIA); Aircraft Owners and Pilots Association (AOPA); Airports Council International – North America (ACI-NA); American Association of Airport Executives (AAAE); American Institutes of Aeronautics and Astronautics (AIAA); Archer Aviation; Association for Uncrewed Vehicle Systems International (AUVSI); Beta Technologies; Boeing; Eve Air Mobility; General Aviation Manufacturers Association (GAMA); Joby Aviation; National Air Transportation Association (NATA); National Business Aviation Association (NBAA); Professional Aviation Safety Specialists, AFL-CIO (PASS); Vertical Aviation International (VAI); and Wisk Aero.

Read the full bill text HERE.

BACKGROUND

Specifically, the Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act:

• Establishes non-binding, standard expected timelines for the FAA’s type certification process for AAM aircraft for the Agency to respond to petitions for exemptions of aircraft type, and to develop means of compliance for aircraft outside of the existing types of AAM aircraft.

• Sets transparent and reliable non-binding, standard expected ranges of time for the issue paper process, so that type certification applicants know how long reviews will take, reducing uncertainty and delays.

• Provides the FAA Administration with the sole discretion to exclude safety-critical matters from established timelines to ensure airspace safety is paramount.

• Directs the FAA to define when an issue paper is required in the certification process, while providing flexibility for the Agency on complex, safety issues.

• Directs the FAA to account for performance-based rules in the certification process.

• Directs the FAA to brief the relevant congressional committees on the status of implementing the certification regulations and managing workload.

• Clarifies when the FAA can delegate routine compliance findings to qualified personnel, allowing Agency experts to focus on complex, safety-critical issues.

• Updates delegation guidance for type certification to cover new and novel technologies related to AAM, including eVTOL aircraft.

Senators Budd and Welch published a bipartisan opinion piece in Newsweek in September 2025 entitled: “Congress Should Help Air Innovation Take Flight.” In their op-ed, they urged Congress to build on America’s proud history of global aviation leadership and pass this bipartisan legislation to help AAM take flight.
