title: VIDEO: Senator Moody Works to Increase Competition and Lower Prescription Drug Prices for Floridians
text:
WASHINGTON D.C. — Senator Ashley Moody is working to unlock more competition in the drug market by cutting regulatory red tape. Right now, unnecessary regulation in the biosimilar drug approval process at the Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has led to delays and higher costs for Floridians. Senator Moody’s new legislation would consolidate duplicative regulatory efforts, allow personnel to prioritize getting more biosimilars, which are affordable alternatives to brand name biological drugs, approved, and ultimately lower costs for Floridians. The broader usage of affordable alternatives to expensive brand name biological drugs has been shown to collectively save Americans billions of dollars on their health care.

“One of my top priorities in the Senate is getting control of runaway costs for Florida families, and that includes the cost of prescription drugs. My new legislation will help families save billions by cutting out unnecessary regulation from the approval process, ultimately reining in drug prices. This is an easy bipartisan fix, and that is why I fought hard to sponsor and pass this bill language out of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pension Committee this week,” said Senator Ashley Moody.

“In Maryland, we are proud to have the FDA operating in our own backyard. This bill allows the FDA to streamline its review process, increasing efficiency and incentivizing innovation for our life sciences manufacturers in Maryland by getting drugs to market for patients faster. It will reduce confusion, slash the red tape that delays drug approvals, and ultimately, lower prices for patients. I look forward to working with Senator Moody to get this simple fix requested by the career experts at FDA across the finish line,” said Senator Angela Alsobrooks.

“The Biosimilars Forum commends Senator Moody [and Senator Alsobrooks] for introducing an important bill to streamline and modernize development for safe, effective, and lower-cost biosimilars,” said Juliana M. Reed, executive director of the Biosimilars Forum. “The Forum and its members take immense pride in developing and manufacturing lower-cost biosimilars, and supportive policies are essential to ensure these medicines can reach the patients who need them. Senator Moody’s leadership will help bring more biosimilars to the market more quickly, ensure those biosimilars can reach patients, and improve affordability by lowering everyday health care costs for Americans.”

BACKGROUND:

· Under the Biologics Price Competition and Innovation Act of 2009, FDA must require that all biosimilar applications be reviewed by the same review division that handled the reference product. This statute is preventing FDA from promoting the Office of Therapeutic Biologics and Biosimilars to handle biosimilars exclusively and save resources in the other review divisions.

· This bill simply strikes Section 351(k)(5)(B) of the Public Health Service Act.

· This effort is in line with President Trump’s Great Healthcare Plan to increase health care affordability, making it easier for biosimilar drugs to come to market by reducing regulatory burden.

· The language in Senator Moody’s bill passed out of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pension Committee this week.

# # #

title: PASSED: Committee Approves Sen. Moran’s Legislation to Streamline FAA Type Certification Process for AAM Aircraft
Sens. Moran, Smith Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Lower Cost of Oral Cancer Treatments
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) and Tina Smith (D-Minn.) recently introduced the Cancer Drug Parity Act, bipartisan legislation that would help lower the cost of oral cancer drugs for Americans battling cancer by making certain patients can access these treatments at comparable prices to traditional (IV) anticancer treatments.

“As cancer research and medical innovation continue to expand treatment options for cancer patients, including with orally administered cancer therapies, patients ought to be able to benefit from these medical advancements,” said Sen. Moran. “This commonsense legislation would encourage ERISA health insurance plans to expand access to orally administered cancer drugs. This legislation will help millions of patients access the therapies that best meet their needs. Improving access to new treatments, therapies and cures will help save lives.”

“Oral treatments for cancer are often less invasive than traditional IV medications and can be taken at home, reducing logistical and occupational barriers to treatment,” said Sen Smith. “However, unlike IV treatments, which are covered by a health plan’s medical benefits with moderate to minimal copays, oral medications often have high, unaffordable copays.?It can add up to thousands of dollars in costs for patients each year and can cause many to delay or forego necessary care to treat their cancer. Our bill brings parity to these two kinds of treatments and lowers costs for those taking oral cancer drugs.”

More than 40 states – including Kansas – have passed “oral parity” laws at the state level to prevent insurers from charging more for prescribed oral cancer medicine than IV chemotherapy. The Cancer Drug Parity Act would expand these protections at the federal level. This legislation is supported by more than 35 organizations representing cancer patients and the medical community.

Specifically, this legislation would:

Expand oral parity protections to privately-insured patients whose health care is regulated at the federal level;

Prevent insurers from covering oral and self-administered medicines at different cost-sharing rates than IV chemotherapy; and

Implement these requirements for health plans that already cover both oral and IV anticancer treatments.

title: Murray, Duckworth, Booker, Schumer, Lead Congressional Democrats in Renewed Push to Establish a Nationwide Right to IVF and Lower IVF Costs for Families
text:
The Senators’ Right to IVF Act reintroduction comes nearly two years since Donald Trump promised free IVF for all, which he’s still failed to deliver

***WATCH and READ: Senator Murray’s remarks at a press conference introducing the Right to IVF Act***

Washington, D.C. — Nearly two years after President Donald Trump promised free IVF for all Americans on the campaign trail, U.S. Senators Patty Murray (D-WA), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Cory Booker (D-NJ) and U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY) are reintroducing the Right to IVF Act, a sweeping legislative package that would make it easier to access in-vitro fertilization and other assisted reproductive technology (ART) for the millions of hopeful parents who depend on it to build their family. This pro-family legislation would establish a nationwide right to access IVF, lower the costs of IVF treatment, expand IVF coverage for military families and require all employer-sponsored insurance programs to cover IVF.

“Republicans are not pro-family and they won’t lift a finger to help families get IVF—the Texas Republican Party just recently made banning IVF a part of their official party platform,” said Senator Murray. “I have fought for a long time to make sure at least servicemembers and veterans, especially wounded warriors, can get the IVF care they need to build a family. But the reality is that we have a Republican Speaker of the House who believes an embryo should have the same rights as an adult woman with children who count on her. America’s pro-IVF majority should wake up to the fact that Trump could not care less about IVF—he broke that promise and he is happy to let Republicans attack IVF and all of our reproductive rights. Meanwhile, Democrats are fighting to make sure all Americans can access and afford health care to build their families.”

“Almost two years after promising free IVF for all Americans if he were elected, Donald Trump has still failed to deliver,” said Senator Duckworth. “Trump and Republicans’ ‘support’ for IVF is nothing but lip service. They want us to have more babies, yet they’ll do nothing to actually help make it easier for the millions who struggle with infertility to start and grow their families. The Right to IVF Act would immediately make IVF treatment more affordable for millions of hopeful parents across the country. From middle class families, to our brave servicemembers and Veterans, to federal employees and more—every American deserves the right to access the treatment and tools they need to build the family of their dreams without burning through their savings. If Republicans really support IVF, then let’s get this done. No more delays.”

“For millions of American families, IVF isn’t politics—it’s hope,” said Senator Schumer. “Donald Trump ran on a promise that he would make IVF free, and yet he has done nothing but attack women’s reproductive rights and undermine access to fertility care—another lie in his long list of broken promises to American families. Our Right to IVF Act is essential to putting a deeply personal health care decision back in the hands of American families. While Donald Trump and Republicans erect barriers between hopeful parents and IVF, Democrats will never stop fighting to protect access so that every family can build the future they dream of.”

“No one chooses infertility,” said Senator Booker. “It’s a medical condition that leaves too many families and individuals feeling alone long before they ever seek treatment. When people turn to IVF, they’re choosing hope. They’re choosing the chance to build the family they’ve always dreamed of. But that hope comes with a price tag that is simply out of reach for far too many. The medications, procedures, and cycles can cost tens of thousands of dollars. Families and individuals already carrying the emotional weight of infertility are then hit with financial barriers that no one should have to face trying to bring a child into this world. We have to change that. We have to remove those barriers and make IVF affordable and accessible to everyone who needs it. Because the ability to build a family should not be reserved for the wealthy or the lucky, it should be within reach for us all.”

Companion legislation is being introduced in the House by U.S. Representatives Lori Trahan (D-MA-03), James Walkinshaw (D-VA-11), Rick Larsen (D-WA-02), Rosa DeLauro (D-CT-03) and Laura Gillen (D-NY-04).

“Like so many people in our country facing fertility challenges, my husband and I turned to IVF as our last hope to have kids. After years of appointments, injections, and setbacks, and thanks to our remarkable physicians, we have two beautiful daughters,” said Rep. Trahan. “No one should lose the chance to start or grow a family because of their zip code. The Right to IVF Act guarantees the right to family-creating fertility care in every state and puts it within reach for the millions of families who need it.”

“Deciding when and how to build a family is a deeply personal choice that belongs to families, not politicians,” said Rep. Walkinshaw. “For millions struggling with infertility, IVF offers hope and a path to parenthood. I’m especially proud the Right to IVF Act includes my legislation requiring IVF coverage through the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program, ensuring the federal government leads by example. I’m honored to join Senator Duckworth, Congresswoman Trahan, and this coalition to protect IVF nationwide and expand access for servicemembers, veterans, federal employees, and working families.”

“For many Americans, fertility treatments like IVF are essential to start families of their own,” said Rep. Larsen. “This comprehensive legislation will guarantee access and expand coverage for IVF and other fertility services. The legislation also includes my bill with Senator Murray, the Veteran Families Health Services Act, to ensure fertility treatments are included in servicemembers’ and veterans’ health benefits. I will keep working with my colleagues in the House and the Senate to make sure that women and men in uniform and working families do not have to sacrifice their dreams of having a family.”

“There are few experiences as hard as wanting to start a family and not being able to,” said Rep. DeLauro. “That is why I am fighting to ensure Americans have access to IVF treatments when they want to start one. I am proud to join my colleagues in introducing the Right to IVF Act – because building a family in the United States should never be difficult.”

“I am proud to help lead this critical bill ensuring millions of Americans can access IVF to build their families, no matter where they live,” said Rep. Gillen. “Families struggling to conceive go through indescribable heartbreak and stress. The last thing they should worry about is legal challenges to IVF delaying or outright halting procedures. Infertility is not a partisan issue. I will continue to work across the aisle in Congress to protect access to IVF and adjacent reproductive technologies that have helped countless individuals experience the joy of parenthood.”

Last Congress, Senate Republicans shamefully blocked the Right to IVF Act, exposing the hollowness of Republicans’ empty claims to support IVF for the millions of Americans who rely on it to build their family. This marked the fourth time Senate Republicans blocked Duckworth-led legislation that would protect access to IVF nationwide, with previous instances including her Access to Family Building Act that builds on previous legislation she introduced in 2022.

While Senate Democrats continue their efforts to protect IVF and reproductive freedom, Senate Republicans continue making it abundantly clear through their anti-choice extremism and record Medicaid cuts that they would rather undermine access to basic health care for millions of Americans than make it easier for their constituents to start and build a family.

Building on the lawmakers’ previous efforts to protect and strengthen access to IVF, this pro-family, pro-freedom legislative package includes:

Senator Murray’s Veteran Families Health Services Act, which would expand the fertility treatments and family-building services that are covered under servicemembers’ and veterans’ health care to include—among other things—the option for individuals to cryopreserve their gametes (freeze their eggs or sperm) ahead of deployment to a combat zone and IVF for servicemembers and veterans who are unable to conceive without assistance.

Senator Duckworth’s Protect IVF Act, which would establish a nationwide right for patients to access IVF and other ART services, a right for doctors to provide IVF treatment in accordance with medical standards as well as a right for insurance carriers to cover IVF without prohibition, limitation, interference or impediment. By establishing a statutory right, this would pre-empt any state effort to limit such access and ensuring no hopeful parent—or their doctors—are punished for trying to start or grow a family.

Senator Booker’s Access to Infertility Treatment and Care Act, which would increase affordability of fertility care—including IVF—by requiring employer-sponsored insurance plans and public insurance plans to cover fertility treatments. Additionally, it would standardize a baseline of high-quality fertility treatment coverage under private health insurance plans, while protecting Americans against excessive out-of-pocket costs.

Senator Duckworth’s Family Building FEHB Fairness Act, which would require Federal Employees Health Benefits (FEHB) Program—the largest employer-sponsored health insurance plan in the world—carriers to cover IVF and ART to help more hardworking Americans start and grow their families.

In addition to Murray, Duckworth, Booker and Schumer, the legislation is cosponsored in the Senate by U.S. Senators Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Chris Coons (D-DE), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Dick Durbin (D-IL), John Fetterman (D-PA), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ed Markey (D-MA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Jon Ossoff (D-GA), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Tina Smith (D-MN), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Mark Warner (D-VA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Peter Welch (D-VT), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

Senator Murray was the first woman to join the Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee and the first woman to chair the Committee—and advocating for women veterans and their access to reproductive health care has been a longtime focus for Senator Murray. Senator Murray called on VA to provide abortion care to veterans early in the Biden administration, and she applauded the Biden administration’s announcement later in the year that would begin to provide abortion care for veterans and their eligible dependents to protect the health and life of the individual and in cases of rape or incest. Murray has helped lead the charge in calling out Republicans for their attacks on, and attempts to undo, this limited and commonsense policy.

Senator Murray leads the Veteran Families Health Services Act, comprehensive legislation that would expand fertility treatments—including IVF—and family-building services for servicemembers and veterans who are unable to conceive without assistance, and she has sought unanimous consent to pass the legislation on multiple occasions. She introduced new legislation last summer with Senator Duckworth to help cover IVF costs for servicemembers and military families—and slammed Speaker Johnson for working behind the scenes to strip an amendment mirroring that legislation from the final National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) for Fiscal Year 2026. Senator Murray voted against the NDAA earlier this month, citing—among other things—the failure to include her provision to expand IVF care for servicemembers and veterans. Senator Murray slammed the Trump administration’s initial move to ban abortion care at VA in August, and sounded the alarm again in December when the Trump administration quietly implemented a near-total abortion ban at VA.

The Right to IVF Act is supported by the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM), RESOLVE: The National Infertility and Family Building Association, Center for Reproductive Rights (CRR), Planned Parenthood Federation of America (PPFA), National Women’s Law Center (NWLC), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), GLBTQ Legal Advocates and Defenders (GLAD Law), Academy of Adoption & Assisted Reproduction Attorneys, Stand with IVF, AllPaths Family Building, American Association of People with Disabilities, American Atheists, Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology, Society for Reproductive Endocrinology & Infertility, Society of Reproductive Biologists & Technologists, Society for Reproductive Surgeons, California LGBTQ Health and Human Services Network, Endocrine Society, Equality California, Families USA, GLMA: Health Professionals Advancing LGBTQ+ Equality, Guttmacher Institute, Hadassah, Human Rights Campaign, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, Indivisible, Justice + Joy National Collaborative, Legal Momentum, Military Family Building Coalition, MomsRising, National Asian Pacific American Women’s Forum, National Association of Nurse Practitioners in Women’s Health, National Center for Lesbian Rights, National Council on Jewish Women, National LGBTQ Task Force Action Fund, National Partnership for Women and Families, National Women’s Political Caucus, Physicians for Reproductive Health, Reproductive Freedom for All, Service Women’s Action Network, Silver State Equality, What to Expect Project and Women’s March.

“The American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) welcomes the bicameral reintroduction of the Right to IVF Act, which would achieve accessible and affordable fertility care for all Americans,” said ASRM Chief Advocacy and Policy Officer Sean Tipton. “This visionary and comprehensive effort would protect patients’ ability to build their families through safe, evidence-based treatments like in vitro fertilization (IVF). By safeguarding access to assisted reproductive technology (ART), preserving the physician-patient relationship, and expanding coverage for the individuals and families who need it most, this legislation reflects the standard of care that all patients deserve.”

“No one should have to wonder whether they’ll be able to access the care they need to build their family,” said Danielle Melfi, CEO of RESOLVE: The National Infertility and Family Building Association. “By safeguarding the right to IVF and expanding insurance coverage for veterans, federal employees, and the individuals and families who need it most, this legislation reflects a comprehensive commitment to helping more people build the families they dream of. RESOLVE applauds Senator Duckworth and the bill’s sponsors for continuing to put patients and families first.”

title: Senator Murray Reintroduces Bill to Restore Congressional Authority and Prevent U.S. Weapons from Being Used in Human Rights Abuses
text:
Senator Murray reintroduced her Values in Arms Export Act, which would restore Congressional authority over weapons sales, and create more oversight to prevent United States weapons going towards human rights violations

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, re-introduced the Values in Arms Export Act of 2026, legislation to restore congressional authority over arms sales, and prevent U.S. arms from being used to violate the laws of war and human rights. Murray previously introduced the bill in 2020 and 2022.

“It is long past time for Congress to reassert its authority over international arms sales and ensure U.S. weapons are never used to commit war crimes,” said Senator Murray. “The American people don’t want to see U.S. weapons used to commit war crimes against kids or innocent civilians. That’s why we need to strengthen the role of Congress in future arms deals and keep our weapons out of the wrong hands.”

Senator Murray’s Values in Arms Export Act of 2026 amends the Arms Export Control Act to make clear that partner countries that receive U.S. weapons are expected to use those weapons in compliance with internationally recognized human rights and international humanitarian law. To enforce these requirements, the bill creates a mechanism where the Executive Branch, Congress, or a newly created Human Rights and Law of War Oversight Board can each designate a country as a “country of concern” if the country is violating those principles. A designation would last for three years, and the country would be required to submit to a newly created program of enhanced monitoring.

If a country: commits further violations during the three-year period; is designated a second time within a ten-year period; or fails to make sufficient progress on reforms, the country would be banned from U.S. arms sales for ten years. The country would have to discontinue the use of U.S.-provided weapons or return the arms. The bill would provide a mechanism for early termination of the ban.

The new Human Rights and Law of War Oversight Board would have significant oversight and policy responsibilities. In addition to the authority to make designations, the Board would be empowered to conduct its own investigative and oversight work, monitor compliance, and assess new policies to ensure respect for human rights and law of armed conflict remain central considerations in the future.

The bill would also require assessments by the State Department, the Department of Defense, and the Intelligence Community of the risk of weapons being used to commit human rights and law of war violations before a sale or export license can be approved.

title: Senator Murray Slams Trump for Broken Promise on IVF and Warns of Growing Anti-IVF Extremism in GOP
text:
The Right to IVF Act reintroduction comes nearly two years since Donald Trump promised free IVF for all, which he’s still failed to deliver

Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), a senior member and former chair of the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP), committee delivered the following remarks at a press conference on the reintroduction of the Right to IVF Act.

title: Sen. Ossoff Working to Expand Market Access for Georgia Forestry and Timber Products
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff is working to expand market access for Georgia forestry and timber products into Europe.

Sen. Ossoff is launching an inquiry with Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins and Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service (APHIS) Administrator Kelly Moore on the status of trade negotiations with the European Union (EU) that could open a major new market for Georgia forestry and timber products.

Sen. Ossoff is encouraging Secretary Rollins and Administrator Moore to help open EU markets to American exporters by supporting EU regulatory approval of US fumigation techniques and working to provide a timeline for EU reviewal of US products.

“Georgia is one of the largest producers and exporters of timber and forestry products, and expanding market access for Georgia forestry and timber products is vitally important to the state’s economy,” Sen. Ossoff wrote. “Expanding opportunities for our timber and forestry products in the EU has been a yearslong effort, and it is of the utmost importance to Georgia’s and the country’s forestry sector that we remain vigorous in these efforts.”

Sen. Ossoff continues working to support Georgia’s forestry and timber industries.

In July, Sen. Ossoff urged the USDA Risk Management Agency to ensure Georgia farmers and growers still struggling to recover from damage from high winds during Hurricane Helene receive the support they deserve.

In May, Sen. Ossoff introduced the Farm Disaster Tax Cut Act to provide eligible farmers with a tax cut after natural disasters, revenue losses, or pest outbreaks.

In 2025, Sen. Ossoff cosponsored the bipartisan Jobs in the Woods Act, legislation that would boost Georgia’s forestry industry by establishing a competitive grant program for forestry career training programs.

That same year, Sens. Ossoff and Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS) introduced the bipartisan Emergency Pine Beetle Response Act to help Georgia foresters recovering from pine beetle infestations.

Also in 2025, Sens. Ossoff and Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) introduced the bipartisan Forest Data Modernization Act, which would modernize and improve the U.S. Forest Service’s Forest Inventory and Analysis program to ensure reliable data is available to inform forest management decision making.

title: Padilla, Schiff Welcome Los Angeles Dodgers to Celebrate Back-to-Back World Series Titles
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) hosted players, coaches, and executives from the Los Angeles Dodgers organization at the United States Capitol to celebrate the Dodgers’ 2025 Major League Baseball World Series championship.

“For nearly seventy years, the Dodgers have made Los Angeles proud, and their back-to-back World Series Championships have only reaffirmed their remarkable legacy,” said Senator Alex Padilla. “I’ve been rooting for the Dodgers for as long as I can remember, and it was a privilege to welcome them back to the Capitol today to celebrate their back-to-back championships. Their hard work and diverse talent continue to inspire us all, and I hope to celebrate them again next year.”

“From the first pitch of spring to that final out in October, the Dodgers once again made us believe. And it wasn’t just this season, it was also the one before that, they are champions in every sense of the word. To the players, coaches and staff, thank you for another victory we will never forget,” said Senator Adam Schiff.

The Dodgers’ victory in Game 7 of the World Series marked the ninth World Series championship for the Dodgers franchise and their eighth title since moving from Brooklyn to Los Angeles in 1958. The team won their 12th National League West Division title in the last 13 seasons before defeating the Cincinnati Reds, Philadelphia Phillies, Milwaukee Brewers, and Toronto Blue Jays en route to their World Series title.

Last year, the Senate unanimously passed Padilla and Schiff’s resolution congratulating the Los Angeles Dodgers on their World Series victory, becoming the first team in 25 years to earn back-to-back World Series titles with one of the most diverse rosters in Major League Baseball. The resolution celebrated the dedication and teamwork of the entire Dodgers roster and staff who made their comeback Game 7 World Series victory possible. The Senators also hosted the Dodgers at the U.S. Capitol after their 2024 World Series win.

title: Padilla Unveils Legislation to Counter Trump’s Attacks on American Elections
text:
New bill would provide State AGs and voters with ability to enforce federal election protections and protect voters’ ballots from seizure

WASHINGTON, D.C. — As President Trump escalates his efforts to interfere in the administration of American elections ahead of the upcoming 2026 midterms, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Rules Committee with oversight over federal elections and California’s former Secretary of State, introduced the Stop Harassment and Intimidations in Elections through Legal Defenses (SHIELD) Our Elections Act, legislation that would provide State Attorneys General and voters with a private right of action to enforce federal anti-election interference laws and extend the statute of limitations for bringing federal criminal prosecutions for violations of those laws from five to nine years. Following the seizure of ballots in Riverside County, Calif. and Fulton County, Ga., the bill also further protects ballots from seizure — especially prior to an election being finally settled.

“Donald Trump has said he regrets not sending federal forces to seize election equipment in 2020 and he has made clear he’ll do whatever it takes to put his thumb on the scale of future elections — even if it means intimidating voters, persecuting election officials, or abusing federal power,” said Senator Padilla. “Trump’s cabinet refuses to rule out sending federal forces to the polls, so we can’t wait until after the damage is done to act. Our elections belong to the voters, and I am fighting to protect every eligible voter’s right to cast a ballot freely and sending a warning that anyone who interferes with our democracy will be held accountable — sooner or later.”

The SHIELD Our Elections Act creates a private right to action for State Attorneys General and voters to enforce federal anti-interference laws protecting polling locations and election sites, extends the statute of limitations for election related crimes so that future administrations can enforce them, restricts the seizure of ballots and election equipment from election officials, especially prior to the final resolution of election outcomes, and authorizes a voluntary grant program to support states who have mail and absentee ballot tracking programs to provide confidence and security for voting by mail or drop box. Padilla’s legislation comes following California’s recently enacted SB 73, which prevents election interference at the state level, and the legislation is a proactive federal response to the Trump Administration’s escalating attacks on voting rights and election administration ahead of the 2026 midterms.

Specifically, the bill would secure federal elections by:

Allowing State Attorneys General and impacted voters to sue when federal officials unlawfully interfere with or intimidate them at polling places;

Strengthening accountability by extending the statute of limitations from five to nine years for key federal election crimes, including interference by armed forces and voter intimidation, to enable them to be brought by future administrations for past actions; and

Protecting ballots from improper seizure by limiting when state or federal law enforcement may seize ballots or election equipment and requiring court-authorized election officials to maintain joint custody whenever materials must be seized, especially prior to the resolution of an election.

In addition to Padilla, the bill is cosponsored by Senators Tammy Baldwin (D-Wis.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Mazie Hirono (D-Hawaii), Angus King (I-Maine), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), and Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.).

“Voting is the fundamental right from which all other rights flow. That’s why, in the face of threats to our democracy, California has led the way in enacting laws that strengthen the security of our elections. I’m grateful Senator Padilla is now championing the SHEILD Our Elections Act, which would extend these important safeguards nationwide and provide additional protections. Every voter, in every corner of the country, deserves to cast a ballot free from intimidation and interference,” said California Attorney General Rob Bonta.

“Our nation’s elections must always be free from intimidation and unlawful interference from any source. Senator Padilla’s bill strengthens existing protections and holds accountable those who violate federal laws specifically designed to protect our democracy,” said California Secretary of State, Shirley N. Weber, Ph.D. “Every voter, election worker, and election official deserves the confidence in knowing that casting a ballot and administering an election are protected every step of the way.”

As California’s former Secretary of State, Padilla knows first-hand the importance of taking proactive steps to protect the fundamental right to vote:

To commemorate the legacy of former Congressman and civil rights advocate John Lewis, Padilla hosted a voting rights breakfast roundtable with interfaith and civil society organizations and members of the Senate Democrats’ Election Protection Task Force to discuss their concerns about the Administration’s ongoing threats to federal elections.

Padilla and Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) convened a Rules Committee Democrats and Senate Democrats’ Election Protection Task Force spotlight forum focused on state and local responses to combat efforts by the Trump Administration to undermine election administration in the upcoming midterm elections.

Padilla and his Senate colleagues also demanded answers from Trump Administration officials about their lack of election security preparation, insufficient coordination with Congress and election officials, and unsupported public claims about voting system vulnerabilities.

The need for this legislation has been underscored by recent ballot seizures in Riverside County. Calif. and Fulton County, Ga., threats by Trump allies to send federal forces to the polls, and Trump officials’ refusal to confirm that they will follow clear federal laws that prohibit this kind of election interference.

title: As Measles Cases Hit 35-Year Record High, Reed Slams Trump Admin. for Negligence & Urges Parents to Check with Their Pediatricians About Measles Vaccine
text:
PROVIDENCE, RI – Cases of measles have already surged past last year’s total and now stand at 2,295 — the highest level of measles in the U.S. in 35 years, according to Johns Hopkins University’s U.S. measles tracker. So far this year, 93 percent of the infections involve the unvaccinated or those with unknown vaccination status. Health experts warn the disease is starting to threaten even well-protected regions, where vaccination rates are high, because of the highly contagious nature of the disease and the strain on limited resources.

With children scheduled to head back to school in a few weeks, U.S. Senator Jack Reed is urging families to check with their pediatrician and make sure their children are up to date on immunizations. He is also criticizing the Trump Administration’s dismissive and unproductive response to the outbreak for making children less safe.

Measles is a highly contagious airborne disease caused by a virus that destroys immune cells and can lead to severe complications – including hearing loss, blindness, and cognitive decline -- and even death.

Once quite common, in 2000, the disease was deemed to be officially ‘eliminated’ in the U.S., defined as the absence of endemic measles virus transmission for more than 12 months.

But now, after the Trump Administration targeted federal public health agencies for mass-firings and short-sighted cuts, promoted anti-vaccine propaganda, and focused on unproven treatments, a rash of measles cases is spreading in states across the country. In fact, the U.S. has already seen more cases in the past 18 months than in the previous two decades combined.

Senator Reed accused the Trump Administration of exacerbating the spread of measles by spreading vaccine misinformation and failing to coordinate with state health officials. The Trump Administration’s systemic failure could cause the U.S. to lose its elimination status later this year.

“We had measles beat, but now the Trump Administration is eroding herd immunity and making America contagious again. Measles is a dangerous virus. There appears to be a direct correlation between the resurgence of measles and the Trump Administration’s irresponsible cuts to public health and attacks on vaccines. Too many otherwise healthy children have died from this preventable disease. That is both a tragedy and a national failing that needs to be corrected to prevent future avoidable deaths. For too long, the Trump Administration has pushed an anti-science agenda that has left more Americans, especially kids, at risk. The Trump Administration can help stop the spread of measles with three easy steps: rehire public health experts, stop spreading misinformation and anti-vaccine sentiments, and encourage people to get immunized,” said Senator Reed.

The successful U.S.-led fight to effectively eradicate measles at home and abroad spared countless children from suffering, long-term health damage, and death.

But now, after Trump’s HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., who spent years systemically stoking anti-vaccination sentiment and lobbying for lax vaccination rules – and downplayed the threat of measles -- the disease is creeping back and putting more Americans at risk.

Moreover, it’s not just those that opt out of vaccinations who are at risk. Measles is extremely transmissible. Children don’t get their first vaccine dose until after 12 months, and full protection doesn’t kick in until they get their booster, usually between ages 4 and 6, making young children, especially infants, particularly vulnerable.

Nearly one out of every three children under the age of 5 who catches measles ends up in the hospital, according to healthychildren.org, which offers tips to protect children from the disease.

“The best way to protect people from measles is to prevent it from circulating. Through decades of bipartisan and diligent coordinated efforts, America achieved that goal, but now we’re starting to see measles make a comeback. The Trump Administration has to do a better job. Public health is a relay race, and HHS Secretary Kennedy -- who has no professional public health expertise or experience -- dropped the baton. Instead of misleading people and spreading misinformation, this Administration needs to provide the public with accurate scientific facts and do a better job when it comes to childhood vaccinations,” said Reed.

The states with the most cases include South Carolina, Utah, Texas, Florida and Arizona. This week, a measles outbreak was declared in Delaware. So far this year, Rhode Island has reported two confirmed cases of measles, both of which were unrelated and connected to international travel, according to the Rhode Island Department of Health.

According to the Rhode Island Department of Health, about 97 percent of students entering kindergarten in Rhode Island have received their measles, mumps and rubella (MMR) shot. Due to the state’s high vaccination rate and herd immunity, a serious measles outbreak is less likely to spread widely in Rhode Island than in a place like Texas that has lower rates of childhood vaccination uptake.

Doctors say the most effective way to combat the measles is to get vaccinated: it is 97 percent effective in preventing illness. Health officials suggest individuals born between 1963 and 1967 should check with their physician to see if they need to be immunized again.

title: Reed Statement on Trump’s Latest Round of Price-Hiking Tariffs
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a blow to consumers that is likely to fuel inflation, President Trump replaced his expiring Section 122 “global” tariffs with a new round of dubious, double-digit tariffs that were announced just as Trump’s previous tariffs were forced to expire. The latest price-raising tariffs on imported goods comes after a February Supreme Court ruling that struck down a broad swath of Trump’s trade regime. Today, U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI) issued the following statement:

“Once again, President Trump is driving up prices on the American people and small businesses. These capricious, unwarranted levies are stoking inflation, severing critical economic partnerships, and needlessly causing uncertainty for U.S. businesses that need stability to plan for the future.

“President Trump’s incoherent trade strategy is creating real financial hardships for Americans across the country. Even the Wall Street Journal acknowledged this week: “President Trump is conceding that his blunderbuss border taxes are harming U.S. business as other countries retaliate,” the paper’s editorial board wrote. “So now he’s whacking Canada harder for punching back. The trade brawl could leave both countries with more bruises than a hockey fight.”

“And the New York Times notes: “Effective tariff rates are going to change on Friday for the 45th time in the last 18 months — an average of once every 12 days.”

“As President Trump tries to flout the court and circumvent Congress, it’s past time for Republicans to finally join Democrats in standing up to President Trump to end his price hiking tariff regime. Enough is enough.”

title: Reed Votes to End Iran War as Senate Republicans Allow Trump to Widen Conflict & Continue Bombing with No Coherent Strategy
text:
WASHINGTON, DC -- As President Trump intensifies his bombing campaign against Iran and continues raising prices on American consumers, U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI) today voted once again for a war powers resolution to end the unauthorized war in Iran.

The U.S. Senate voted 47-49 on its war powers resolution that was not agreed to. Meanwhile, the U.S. House of Representatives voted 214-208 to pass a different war powers resolution to restrain President Trump’s military action in Iran.

Reed, the top Democrat on the Senate Armed Services Committee who has opposed the war from the start, supports an end to the war and noted that Congress, not the president, has the power to declare war, as spelled out in the Constitution. Senator Reed also pointed to public reports that U.S. Intelligence has widely held that the kind of bombing the Trump Administration is currently carrying out is unlikely to shift Iran's negotiating position.

“The American people do not want a costly, reckless, endless war. Still, President Trump continues to try and bomb his way to peace. Senate Republicans are shielding him from accountability and allowing him to escalate military action without a complimentary diplomatic, economic, or political strategy. President Trump started this war on his own, without a plan, and now gas prices are over $4 once again. Trump continues to squander U.S. resources, miscalculate Iranian resilience, and double down on an ineffective strategy that our own Intelligence Community agrees is unlikely to change the tide of this conflict. Every day President Trump’s unauthorized war of choice continues, it makes everyday items more expensive for the American people, weakens the U.S. economy, and fails to make America more secure. None of the goals President Trump used as a pre-text for this war have been accomplished, but the formerly open Strait of Hormuz is now effectively closed. It seems President Trump and Secretary Hegseth are only now just learning that military supremacy without a competent strategy and robust diplomatic engagement does not translate to victory. That is another stunning indictment of their poor judgement and lack of civilian leadership. Today, in the Senate and the House, members of Congress across the political spectrum rebuked President Trump and sent a signal that this Administration must change course,” said Senator Reed.

Today's vote comes 145 days after President Trump hastily launched Operation Epic Fury. The War Powers Resolution of 1973 sets a 60-day limit on unauthorized military hostilities, unless Congress votes to authorize military force, with an extra 30-day grace period if the president determines more time is necessary to safely withdraw U.S. forces.

Today’s war powers vote also comes after President Trump vowed on social media: “any time the Islamic Republic of Iran shoots at a ship in the Strait of Hormuz… the United States will bomb and destroy ONE BRIDGE OR POWER PLANT.”

With seemingly no effort toward diplomatic progress, President Trump continues to order a series of costly kinetic strikes and counterstrikes with Iran, which is targeting U.S. bases and causing regional turmoil in the Middle East. The escalated strikes have not shifted the balance of power, but leave the Strait of Hormuz in a state of heightened peril and pushes up the price of oil, which has increased 30 percent over the last year.

“President Trump keeps claiming he will make Iran pay. But as with his tariffs, he is really forcing Americans to pay higher costs,” noted Reed. “Given that President Trump has no endgame and has not achieved the stated objectives he used as a pretext for war, Americans are right to be skeptical of simply throwing more money and military weapons at the problem. The Trump Administration must be more transparent with the American people about the facts of this war. I will not hand the president a blank check to fund it.”

title: Ricketts Op-Ed: It’s Time to Ban Congressional Insider Trading
text:
The following op-ed by U.S. Senator Pete Ricketts (R-NE) was originally published by the National Review on July 22, 2026.

When the American people send lawmakers to Washington, they expect them to serve their constituents. Sadly, polling confirms that many Americans believe politicians are abusing their positions for personal financial gain.

Over 80 percent of Americans believe members of Congress do a bad job keeping their personal financial interests separate from their work in Congress. As a result, it should come as no surprise that only 15 percent of Americans approve of how Congress handles its job.

Polling doesn’t just tell the story. History does, too.

Social media accounts publish routine updates tracking a former speaker’s stock trade. Today, mimicking a few lawmakers’ trades is a legitimate investment strategy. In 2020, the chairman of the Senate Intelligence Committee sold over $1.5 million in stock just days prior to the pandemic-induced market crash. Stories like these underscore the need to act. Even the perception of self-dealing by lawmakers erodes public trust and can negatively impact voter participation in our democracy.

To be clear, no lawmaker should profit from insider information.

My Stop Insider Trading Act is the solution. President Trump has voiced support for this legislation. Just last week, Vice President Vance told House Republicans we need to pass it.

There are a couple of big reasons why we need to get this bill to the president’s desk. First, it eliminates even the appearance of impropriety by prohibiting members of Congress, their spouses, and dependent children from buying new stock. If a lawmaker or their family already owns stock, they can maintain ownership. However, if members of Congress or their families wish to sell stock, they must publicly disclose those plans seven days in advance. Doing so allows the public — and the market — to get ahead of any news that could impact a stock’s price.

Second, my bill carries significant penalties. Any violation would incur a $2,000 fine or a fine that is 10 percent of the transaction — whichever is greater. Additionally, any profit realized by a sale would also be forfeited. Under my bill, if a lawmaker sold $1 million in stock without filing advanced public notice, they would be fined $100,000 — plus forfeit any profits. It’s time Congress made this the standard.

The Stop Insider Trading Act is a product of months of detailed conversations and extensive negotiation. Despite negotiating in good faith, some continue to undermine these potential reforms. Their demands are meant to score political points, not serve the American people. That’s a tactic that only hinders good legislation.

Others have argued that lawmakers should be forced to divest their portfolios. That would have unintended consequences. Forced divestiture would discourage Americans with successful private sector careers from serving in Congress. If we hope to maintain America’s dominance in the global economy, we can’t afford to lose that experience and perspective in Washington.

Americans need trust and transparency from Congress. Voters are demanding action. My Stop Insider Trading Act delivers.

Both the House and Senate need to move this bill quickly to the president’s desk. It has Democratic support. President Trump and Vice President Vance have voiced their support. America has voiced its support. Congress should capitalize on that momentum.

The Stop Insider Trading Act ensures no lawmaker can profit from insider information. By passing it, we can rebuild Americans’ trust in their elected representatives. Democrats had their chance to address this issue when they controlled the House and the Senate. They didn’t. Now, Republicans stand ready to deliver.

It’s time Congress put real safeguards in place for lawmaker stock trading. I’m committed to getting the job done.

title: VIDEO: Rosen Calls on Senate Colleagues to Support Legislation to Fight Rising Antisemitism in the United States
text:
Watch the full speech HERE.

WASHINGTON, DC – Today, U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen called on Senate colleagues to address rising antisemitism in the country and support her bipartisan Jewish American Security Act (JASA). According to a report by the ADL, 2025 represented the third-highest year for antisemitic incidents in the U.S. since the ADL began collecting data. The report also found that physical attacks against the Jewish community were higher in 2025 than they have ever been. To combat these troubling trends, Senators Rosen and James Lankford (R-OK), co-founders and co-chairs of the Senate Bipartisan Task Force for Combating Antisemitism, introduced JASA to strengthen federal efforts to fight antisemitism – including in academic settings, at Jewish communal institutions, and online.

Below is a transcript of the speech:

I rise today to speak once again about a crisis that demands the ongoing attention of the Senate: the disturbing rise of antisemitism in America.

Across our country, Jewish Americans are continuing to face unspeakable acts of hate, threats, violence, and discrimination that are happening at record levels.

Unfortunately, this is not anything new.

In fact, for more than a decade, antisemitism has been on the rise, setting record numbers year after year – particularly since the October Seventh terrorist attack on Israel.

According to an ADL report, 2025 was the third-highest year for antisemitic incidents in the United States since the ADL began collecting data, and physical assaults against Jews were higher in 2025 than ever before.

So, I want everyone to just think about that. Physical assaults against Jews were the highest since ADL began tracking this data nearly 50 years ago.

And FBI data has shown that Jewish Americans are the target of almost 70% of religiously motivated hate crimes in this country, despite making up only 2% of the population. Think about that: 70% of crime against 2% of the population.

Just this past year:

A historic synagogue in Jackson, Mississippi was firebombed.

Jewish congregations were defaced in Austin, Texas; Alburquerque, New Mexico; Hot Springs, Arkansas; and Oak Park, Michigan.

And, in West Bloomfield, Michigan, a man actually drove his car into a building housing a synagogue and preschool and then opened fire.

Even beyond these specific incidents, we’re witnessing worrying trends in how Americans are thinking about Jewish communities. Last week, the Blue Square Alliance Against Hate released a poll that found that nearly one-third of people 18 to 44 viewed Jews as, I’m going to quote here, “a threat to the unity of American society.” 2% of the population – a threat to the unity of American society.

Let that sink in.

The same poll found that one in eight young adults said Jewish people, I’m gonna quote again, “cause problems in the world.” And around one in five younger Americans did not consider slurs against Jews to be harmful to Jewish people.

I really wish these findings were hard to believe. But for many around this country, they aren’t surprising.

For some, they will point to the war in the Middle East and U.S. policy in the region as a driver of these spikes in antisemitism. And of course, we can and we must have open, frank discussions on how the U.S. should handle our foreign policy. But we cannot stand idly by and allow those disagreements to become excuses for turning a blind eye on attacks towards Jewish Americans.

When we return from the August state work period, it will be September and the High Holidays will be in full swing. From Rosh Hashanah to Yom Kippur, this is the holiest time of the Jewish year.

And many Jews – including those who may not go to synagogue any other time of year – will be preparing to attend religious services in observance of these holidays.

But it is the unfortunate reality that these holidays are now marked by a palpable fear. Because large gatherings make communities vulnerable to attacks.

Sadly, what should be a season of reflection, prayer, worship, and renewal is a source of now fear and anxiety for too many American Jews.

As a result, one in four Jewish Americans have skipped Jewish events and Jewish religious observances due to the fear of being targeted.

It’s not right. They don’t go to temple for fear of being targeted, something must be done.

Before I came to the Senate, I was the president of the largest reform synagogue in Nevada, and I know firsthand the preparation that synagogues undertake to keep their congregations safe, especially during the High Holidays.

No one should have to worship behind a barricade. No one should have to go through a police check, and police surrounding your entire building in order to go pray. But as antisemitic harassment and violence continue to be a real threat, heightened security measures are a fact of life for Jewish communities.

Every synagogue leader in this country has to think about hiring professional security, installing cameras, and doing everything they can to protect their congregation. Security the largest line item on the budget now.

And this heavy burden isn’t only an emotional and logistical one. Robust security comes with a steep financial cost, too.

There’s a highly successful federal grant program at FEMA that helps at-risk institutions – including houses of worship like synagogues, churches, and mosques – well it lets them make the security upgrades they need so that Americans can worship peacefully and safely.

And this is why we need to robustly fund the Nonprofit Security Grant Program.

In fact, authorizing one billion dollars for this program – nearly three times its current funding level – is a key component of the Jewish American Security Act, my comprehensive bipartisan bill with Senator James Lankford to address antisemitism and threats to the Jewish community.

But this program can only help institutions if the grant money is actually accessible, and if there’s enough money available for the applicants who need it – all across this country, communities large and small.

Unfortunately, many institutions had less than a month to apply for grants through the NSGP this year…sometimes they only had days to review the program, develop proposals, and gather the necessary documents and supporting assessments. In past years, the application window has been as long as eighty days.

It’s why, in addition to making this historic investment in NSGP, our bipartisan bill would make important reforms to streamline how the program is implemented and allow grant funding to be used to hire security services so that the program truly matches the needs of the congregations it must support.

And it won’t just stop there.

Our bipartisan Jewish American Security Act would also create a new federal grant program to support local police who protect at-risk houses of worship.

I often say antisemitism is the canary in the coal mine. It’s a warning sign.

A warning sign for all other forms of hate and discrimination to come.

Tackling antisemitism sends a strong message that we do not tolerate hate and discrimination in our country – in the United States of America.

If we don’t draw this line now, if we don’t stand up, if we don’t say enough is enough, then when will we? Who’s next?

Jewish Community – Canary in the coal mine.

We must draw the line, we must pass this bill. The Jewish American Security Act is so critical to our safety and security

When will we say enough is enough? Let’s hope it’s now.

###

title: NEWS: Schiff, Matsui, Panetta, and Thompson Urge FCC to Stop AT&T Landline Shutdown
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), U.S. Representatives Doris Matsui (D-Calif.-07), Jimmy Panetta (D-Calif.-19) and Mike Thompson (D-Calif.-04) led a bipartisan group of 28 total members of the California Congressional Delegation in urging Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr to stop AT&T’s effort to discontinue landline services and uphold its obligation to serve California communities.

The push comes just days after a federal court rejected AT&T’s request to temporarily block California from enforcing its Carrier of Last Resort requirements while the company’s lawsuit proceeds.

“This continued attempt by AT&T to cease operations of critical networks in areas that are prone to wildfires, landslides, massive snowstorms, and earthquakes would leave approximately 200,000 California residential and business customers without alternative communications in the event of a cellular outage,” wrote the lawmakers. “Relatedly, as has befallen AT&T in the recent past, these outages could last for days, weeks, and in some cases, months. We urge the Commission to deny AT&T’s various applications because the negative consequences for the public far outweigh any benefits, and the proposed replacement is wholly inadequate.”

AT&T has sought federal approval to discontinue legacy landline service affecting California residents and businesses, relinquish its Eligible Telecommunications Carrier status, and override California’s Carrier of Last Resort protections. Its proposed wireless replacement relies on electrical grids and cellular towers that may be damaged or unavailable during disasters.

“We recognize the importance of modernizing our networks and expanding fiber-optic infrastructure to underserved communities,” the lawmakers continued. “However, these efforts must be carried out in a manner that protects public safety and preserves resilient access for vulnerable communities during emergencies and outages.”

The letter follows a bipartisan 2024 effort by members of the California delegation opposing AT&T’s previous attempt to abandon its Carrier of Last Resort obligations. The California Public Utilities Commission later denied that request after significant public opposition.

The lawmakers call on the FCC to protect California’s authority to set local utility and public safety standards and prevent customers from losing reliable access to emergency communications. At minimum, they request protections for communities prone to wildfires, extreme weather, and locations where indoor cellular coverage is unreliable.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

title: NEWS: Schiff, Padilla Welcome Los Angeles Dodgers to Celebrate Back-to-Back World Series Titles
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) hosted players, coaches, and executives from the Los Angeles Dodgers organization at the United States Capitol to celebrate the Dodgers’ 2025 Major League Baseball World Series championship.

“From the first pitch of spring to that final out in October, the Dodgers once again made us believe. And it wasn’t just this season, it was also the one before that, they are champions in every sense of the word. To the players, coaches and staff, thank you for another victory we will never forget,” said Senator Schiff.

“For nearly seventy years, the Dodgers have made Los Angeles proud, and their back-to-back World Series Championships have only reaffirmed their remarkable legacy,” said Senator Padilla. “I’ve been rooting for the Dodgers for as long as I can remember, and it was a privilege to welcome them back to the Capitol today to celebrate their back-to-back championships. Their hard work and diverse talent continue to inspire us all, and I hope to celebrate them again next year.”

The Dodgers’ victory in Game 7 of the World Series marked the ninth World Series championship for the Dodgers franchise and their eighth title since moving from Brooklyn to Los Angeles in 1958. The team won their 12th National League West Division title in the last 13 seasons before defeating the Cincinnati Reds, Philadelphia Phillies, Milwaukee Brewers, and Toronto Blue Jays en route to their World Series title.

Last year, the Senate unanimously passed Schiff and Padilla’s resolution congratulating the Los Angeles Dodgers on their World Series victory, becoming the first team in 25 years to earn back-to-back World Series titles with one of the most diverse rosters in Major League Baseball. The resolution celebrated the dedication and teamwork of the entire Dodgers roster and staff who made their comeback Game 7 World Series victory possible. The Senators also hosted the Dodgers at the U.S. Capitol after their 2024 World Series win.

title: NEWS: Sen. Schiff Pushes Anti-Corruption Measures to Prevent Malign Influences in Executive Branch, Close Bribery Loopholes
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) is continuing his push to enact updates to federal anti-corruption and ethics laws in the aftermath of the most corrupt presidential administration in U.S. history with the introduction of three pieces of legislation aimed at preventing malign influence in the Executive Branch through bribery, conflicts of interest, and other methods of self-enrichment by government employees.

“The Trump administration has put corporations and their executives in the driver’s seat, letting special interests call the shots and drive government decisions over mergers and contracts to supporters of the President. These bills address the self-enrichment schemes of special government employees and other political appointees of any administration, present or future, and prevent them from so openly profiting from their public service,” said Senator Schiff.

The bills introduced by Schiff today were included as part of his Protecting our Democracy Act, his landmark legislative package, first introduced in 2020, that seeks to curb presidential abuses of power, strengthen checks and balances on the Executive Branch, and add additional guardrails to better protect American democracy.

The measures introduced today are:

The No Corporate Crooks Act, to prohibit corporate executives from serving in the executive branch if they have been convicted of financial or corruption crimes.

This legislation is led by Rep. Chris DeLuzio (D-Pa.-17) in the U.S. House of Representatives.

“The American people are mad about corrupt officials in our government lining their pockets while so many hardworking people struggle to get by,” said Congressman Deluzio. “Part of restoring the American Dream means rooting out this corruption and stopping corporate criminals who are using their insider access for personal gain. The No Corporate Crooks Act would ban criminals convicted of bribery, embezzlement, fraud, or insider trading from the executive branch. I am proud to lead this bill with Senator Schiff.”

The Stop Millionaires Using Service for Kickbacks (MUSK) Act, to require government employees to recuse themselves from any matters affecting the financial interests of previous employers from the four-year period prior.

This legislation is led by Rep. Pat Ryan (D-N.Y.-18) in the U.S. House of Representatives.

“Politicians are elected to serve the people — not themselves. For too long bad actors have been able to put their own gain ahead of what’s best for the American people, and the brazen corruption of this Administration only highlights the need for urgent action,” said CongressmanRyan. “That’s why I was proud to introduce our comprehensive Anti-Corruption Agenda last year – including my Stop MUSK Act, which would make sure those in government cannot use their power to financially benefit themselves or their former employers – and why I am proud to support Senator Schiff’s Protecting Our Democracy Act package. That’s what the American people deserve, and that’s what we’ll keep fighting for.”

3. The Closing Bribery Loopholes Act, to close a loophole created by the Supreme Court in federal bribery statutes by tightening the definition of an “official act” by a public official. After the court’s ruling in McDonnell v. United States, official acts can be defined only by legislative actions, such as casting votes or influencing policy language. The bill would expand that definition to include conduct done in any official capacity as a public official.

This legislation is led by Rep. Emilia Sykes (D-Ohio-13) in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Additional Background:

Schiff’s Protecting our Democracy Act legislative package aims to address numerous new abuses of power that Donald Trump and members of his administration have engaged in during both his first and second term.

Other provisions of the package include bills to:

Reinforce Congress’ power of the purse and discretion over federal spending decisions, and its oversight role over the executive branch

Prevent presidents from granting pardons to family, friends, or themselves, or from using the office to enrich themselves, or utilizing government resources for campaign purposes

Strengthen protections for federal whistleblowers who report government waste, fraud, or abuse

Explicitly prohibit political campaigns and parties from soliciting or accepting foreign assistance to influence an election

More information on the Protecting our Democracy Act can be found here.
