"The pattern is clear: they're determined to fortify every ounce of "pure whiteness" they can and dismantle everything else, all while claiming to be the champions of "equality.”

They started by attacking Black districts — drawing racist lines to remove us from Congress and silence the voices we represent. Apparently, that wasn't enough for them and now, they want to get rid of all the minority caucuses — the Congressional Black Caucus, the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, and the Congressional Asian Pacific American Caucus. Just as the British Colonizers wouldn’t let American Patriots congregate, just like Jim Crow wouldn’t allow Black folks to assemble, now Nancy Mace doesn’t want us to caucus.

Let me be clear: these caucuses were created out of necessity because, for far too long, our communities were denied a voice. Our constituents demanded leaders who would show up, speak up, and fight for their rights. While no ethnic group is a monolith, there are many shared struggles which require shared strategies.

title: Davids Joins KC Diamonds to Highlight Lower-Cost Fuel to Help Kansas Families Save at the Pump
text:
Today, Representative Sharice Davids joined the Renewable Fuels Association and the KC Diamonds for "Fuel Up Friday" at Casey's in Lenexa, where Kansas families received discounts on E15. As gas prices continue to climb, Davids highlighted how expanding access to E15 — a lower-cost fuel made from American-grown crops — can help lower prices at the pump, support Kansas farmers, strengthen American energy independence, and reduce reliance on foreign oil.

"When gas prices go up, Kansas families feel it almost immediately," said Davids. "That's why I've worked across the aisle to make lower-cost fuels like E15 available year-round. It's a commonsense solution that helps families save money, creates new opportunities for Kansas farmers, and strengthens our energy independence at a time when global instability from the war in Iran is driving up costs. We should be making it easier — not harder — for Americans to choose a fuel that's made right here at home."

Earlier this year, the U.S. House passed Davids' bipartisan Nationwide Consumer and Fuel Retailer Choice Act. The bill ensures drivers have permanent, uninterrupted access to E15, which reduces emissions and can lower prices at the pump by 15 to 40 cents per gallon compared to regular unleaded. It would also increase American energy independence and create additional opportunities for family farmers at a time of growing economic uncertainty across farm country.

Rising fuel costs underscore the urgency of expanding access to lower-cost alternatives like E15. Since the outbreak of the Iran war, global oil prices have surged sharply, exceeding $100 per barrel. U.S. gasoline prices have followed, jumping from under $3.00 per gallon before the conflict to more than $4.00, with analysts warning prices could climb even higher if instability continues.

title: Dexter, Raskin, Bacon Celebrate House Passage of Bipartisan Legislation Protecting Pension Payments for NOAA Corps, U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Representatives Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Don Bacon (NE-02) and Maxine Dexter (OR-03) celebrated the House passage of their bipartisan legislation safeguarding pension payments for an estimated 8,000 retired uniformed servicemembers.

The Pensions for Retired Uniformed Servicemembers Act would secure parity between retired members of the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) Commissioned Officer Corps and the U.S. Public Health Service (USPHS) Commissioned Corps and all other federal retirees, ensuring they continue receiving pension payments during a government shutdown. The bill’s passage was also supported by Representatives Don Davis (NC-01), Nick LaLota (NY-01) and August Pfluger (TX-11).

“Legislating in a Republican-controlled House has not stopped me from getting things done,” said Rep. Dexter. “I’m proud to secure this win for every retired public servant who has endured the struggle of going without a paycheck during a government shutdown and for the constituent who reached out to my office and made us aware of this egregious gap in our system. I am honored to have the opportunity to definitively address concerns my community elevates and help thousands of Americans in the process.”

“A government shutdown shouldn’t prevent retired NOAA and USPHS officers from paying rent or putting food on the table,” said Rep. Raskin. "Our bipartisan bill honors their years of public service defending the health and safety of our people. Once the Senate passes this legislation and it becomes law, these patriots will always receive the benefits they earned on time, even if government funding lapses.”

“NOAA Corps and U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps officers serve our nation in moments of crisis, from hurricane response and environmental disasters to disease outbreaks at home and overseas,” said Rep. Bacon. “These uniformed officers have answered the call in national emergencies and times of war, and they deserve a retirement structure that recognizes that service. I’m pleased the House passed this bipartisan legislation, and I look forward to working with my colleagues in the Senate to get it across the finish line and to the President’s desk.”

"The Commissioned Officers Association of the U.S. Public Health Service applauds the effort to place the U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps and the NOAA Commissioned Officer Corps in the Military Retirement Fund. This bipartisan achievement will ensure that retired officers of both uniformed services continue to receive the retirement benefits they have earned without interruption during a government shutdown," said CAPT. Jacqueline Rychnovsky, USPHS (Ret.), Executive Director of the Commissioned Officers Association of the U.S. Public Health Service. "The Association congratulates Representatives Jamie Raskin, Don Bacon, Maxine Dexter, Donald Davis, Nick LaLota, and August Pfluger for their bipartisan leadership in advancing this important amendment and helping safeguard the retirement security of those who have dedicated their careers to serving our nation."

“USPHS and NOAA Corps retirees served and sacrificed during a career in uniform. They stepped up for our nation and its citizens in times of crisis. They earned the benefit of knowing their retirement checks will always arrive and always arrive on time,” said Lt. Gen. Brian T. Kelly, USAF (Ret), president and CEO of the Military Officers Association of America (MOAA). “MOAA thanks Reps. Raskin, Bacon, and Dexter for their work on this issue, and we look forward to solidifying this important step toward retirement pay parity across all services.”

Currently, USPHS Commissioned Officer Corps and NOAA Corps retirees are paid out of funds held in the Coast Guard Pay & Personnel Center. This Center shuts down during shutdowns. As a result, retirees did not receive their pension payments for more than 43 days during the October shutdown. Rep. Raskin learned about this problem by listening to concerns from his constituents in Maryland’s Eighth Congressional District who depend on their pension payments and feared for their ability to make ends meet during last year’s government shutdown.

The U.S. Public Health Service Commissioned Corps was established in 1889 to root out smallpox and yellow fever and is now the largest public health program in the world. Driven by a passion for public service, the Commissioned Corps officers respond to public health crises and national emergencies such as natural disasters, disease outbreaks, and terrorist attacks, both at home and overseas.

The lawmakers introduced their bipartisan legislation in May 2026. It was referred to the House Committee on Armed Services.

The Pensions for Retired Uniformed Servicemembers Act is endorsed by the Commissioned Officers Association of the United States Public Health Service, Military Officers Association of America, Navy League, National Military Family Association, AMVETS, Blinded Veterans Association, Blue Star Families, Fleet Reserve Association, Iraq and Afghanistan Veterans of America, Jewish War Veterans, Military Chaplains Association, Military Family Advisory Network, National Defense Committee, Non-Commissioned Officers Association, Reserve Organization of America, Service Women’s Action Network, Tragedy Assistance Program for Survivors, United States Army Warrant Officers Association, USCG Chief Petty Officers Association, Vietnam Veterans of America and With Honor Action.

title: Leger Fernández, Pingree Condemn Rushed Effort to Gut Tribal Consultation and Historic Preservation Protections
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Representative Teresa Leger Fernández (NM-03), Ranking Member of the House Natural Resources Subcommittee on Indian and Insular Affairs, and Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Interior, Environment, and Related Agencies, condemned a proposal released by the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP) that would rush through sweeping changes to the regulations implementing Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act.

“History is not an obstacle for development. It is the story of who we are, and it should not be bulldozed without thought,” said Leger Fernández. “This week, the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP) will vote on drastic changes to Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act regulations that will gut historic preservation reviews and tribal consultation. Section 106 is one of the most important promises our nation has made: before the federal government destroys, it must listen to the people from the community; listen to tribes and local governments. But the Trump administration wants to destroy that promise. By gutting tribal consultation and stripping protections for places of deep cultural and spiritual significance, they are saying that corporate profits are more important than our shared history. Worse still, they want to rush the proposed changes, giving ACHP members only a week to review and vote on sweeping changes. I call on the ACHP to protect our history and rescind its rushed and ill-conceived changes to the Section 106 historic preservation regulations.”

“The ACHP’s decision to rewrite Section 106—behind closed doors, on an absurdly rushed timeline, and without meaningful input from states, Tribes, preservation experts, or the public—is beyond reckless and will dramatically weaken one of our nation’s most important historic preservation laws,” Congresswoman Pingree said. “For nearly 60 years, the National Historic Preservation Act has ensured that communities have a voice before the federal government moves forward with projects that could affect the places, stories, and cultural resources that help tell our nation’s story. These changes would make it easier for federal agencies to ignore public input, sideline Tribes, and rush ahead with projects that could permanently damage irreplaceable historic and cultural resources. Unfortunately, that is exactly how this Administration operates. They have shown time and again that they’re not interested in respecting the full scope of America’s history—only in fast-tracking the president’s vanity projects and giving sweetheart deals to donors and supporters. As the Ranking Member on the House Appropriations subcommittee that oversees the ACHP, I will fight every attempt to weaken these critical safeguards or silence the communities and experts who deserve to have a seat at the table when it comes to preserving our shared history.”

Background:

On Friday, July 17, the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation (ACHP) released a proposal that would make sweeping changes to the regulations implementing Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act. The ACHP provided only one week for members to review and vote on 50 pages of proposed regulatory changes.

The proposed changes are a stark departure from current practices that would:

Severely limit the inclusion of states and local governments in the historic preservation process within their own jurisdictions; Make tribal consultation an optional rather than required step for nearly all federal projects; Make public participation in the historic preservation process at the discretion of federal agencies; and exclude traditional cultural properties from historic preservation protections that are not “geographically compact,” thereby limiting protection for many tribal cultural resources.

The ACHP is an independent federal agency consisting of 24 members representing federal agencies, state and local governments, tribal governments, and historic preservation organizations. The ACHP advises the President and Congress on historic preservation and oversees the Section 106 process, which forms the bedrock of historic preservation in the United States.

text:
WASHINGTON (WALA) - Alabama Rep. Shomari Figures has introduced the Tuskegee Airmen Memorial Act, a bill that would authorize the construction of a memorial in Washington, D.C., honoring the Black military pilots and support personnel who served in World War II.

The bill is co-sponsored by Alabama’s entire House congressional delegation. If passed. the bill would authorize Tuskegee Airmen Incorporated to establish the memorial on federal land in the nation’s capital.

The Tuskegee Airmen trained in Alabama and went on to become one of the most decorated fighting forces in American history. They broke barriers in the sky while facing discrimination at home.

Figures said the Tuskegee Airmen’s courage helped pave the way for the desegregation of the U.S. military.

title: Rep. Fischbach Leads Letter Urging EPA to Preserve Access to Critical Crop-Protection Tool
text:
WASHINGTON, DC - Representative Michelle Fischbach (MN-07) led a coalition of colleagues in sending a letter to Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin, urging the agency to correct Biden-Era regulatory overreach and restore access to Chlorpyrifos, a vital insecticide relied upon by American farmers.

In the letter, lawmakers called on the EPA to restore science-based review processes that recognize Chlorpyrifos as safe for use on crops.

"America’s farmers produce the safest and most abundant food in the world, but to keep doing that, they need access to safe, proven crop-protection tools," said Rep. Fischbach. "Food security is national security, and taking away tools from our growers threatens their ability to produce crops efficiently. The EPA must correct past regulatory overreach, follow its own scientific risk modeling, and protect the safe crop-management tools our agriculture community relies on."

Key Highlights of the Letter:

The EPA's own scientific record and risk modeling support the safe use of Chlorpyrifos.

Maintaining domestic agricultural output ensures the United States maintains a resilient food supply.

Forcing growers toward alternative pest management options imposes significantly higher costs while providing less effective control against destructive pests.

The letter received strong backing from key national agricultural stakeholder groups, including the American Farm Bureau Federation, American Soybean Association, American Sugarbeet Growers Association, National Association of Wheat Growers, and U.S. Beet Sugar Association.

The full text of the letter can be found here.

Rep. Fischbach was joined in the letter by US Representatives Mariannette Miller-Meeks (IA-01), Mark Alford (MO-04), Adrian Smith (NE-03), Brad Finstad (MN-01), Dan Newhouse (WA-04), Austin Scott (GA-08), Rick Allen (GA-12), David Taylor (OH-02), Sam Graves (MO-06), Mike Flood (NE-01), Mike Bost (IL-12), Pete Stauber (MN-08), Ann Wagner (MO-02), and Mary Miller (IL-15).

title: Fitzpatrick, Quigley Lead Bipartisan Effort to Stop Sweeping Rollback of Endangered Species Protections
text:
The Safeguarding Endangered Species Act would overturn the Administration’s rule eliminating longstanding protections against habitat destruction that kills or injures imperiled wildlife

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressmen Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-1 and Mike Quigley (D-IL-5), ), Co-Chairs of the Congressional Animal Protection Caucus, introduced the Safeguarding Endangered Species Act, bipartisan legislation to nullify the Administration’s recently finalized rule weakening the Endangered Species Act’s protections against destructive habitat loss.

For more than five decades, the Endangered Species Act has prohibited the unlawful “take” of threatened and endangered wildlife. Since 1975, federal regulations have recognized that “harm” can include significant habitat destruction or degradation that actually kills or injures wildlife by disrupting essential activities such as breeding, feeding, and sheltering.

The Administration’s final rule rescinds that definition, narrowing how “harm” will be interpreted and weakening the law’s ability to address habitat destruction that results in the actual injury or death of threatened and endangered wildlife.

The Fitzpatrick-Quigley legislation would nullify the rule and preserve the longstanding, science-based principle that protecting an imperiled species requires protecting the habitat essential to its survival and recovery.

“Congress enacted the Endangered Species Act to prevent extinction—not to document it after the damage has already been done,” said Fitzpatrick. “For more than fifty years, our nation’s protections have reflected a basic legal, scientific, and commonsense truth: when habitat destruction actually kills or injures protected wildlife, that destruction is harm. The Administration’s rule would erase that longstanding safeguard through regulatory action and leave vulnerable species exposed at the precise moment the law is intended to protect them.”

“As Co-Chair of the Congressional Animal Protection Caucus, I am leading this bipartisan effort to stop that rollback and draw a clear line: no Administration—Republican or Democratic—should be permitted to hollow out a landmark law enacted by Congress,” Fitzpatrick continued. “We must, and will, act to preserve the full force of the Endangered Species Act, protect the habitats wildlife need to survive, and uphold our responsibility to the generations that will inherit America’s natural legacy.”

“I’m proud to join Congressman Fitzpatrick in leading the bipartisan Safeguarding Endangered Species Act. This essential legislation will reverse the Trump administration’s recent rule eliminating habitat protections outlined in the 1975 Endangered Species Act,” said Quigley. “As Co-Chair of the Congressional Animal Protection Caucus, I’m honored to continue fighting for our wildlife and the endangered species around us.”

Support for the Legislation

“We cannot effectively protect vulnerable species without considering one of the top reasons these animals are disappearing—habitat degradation. Yet that is the reality of the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service’s attempt to abandon a definition of ‘harm’ that has stood for decades. In a time of increasing biodiversity loss, we should not be intentionally weakening our strongest tool to combat this growing crisis. We urge Congress to pass this bill ensuring safeguards remain in place for wildlife and their habitats,” said Sara Amundson, President, Humane World Action Fund.

“There’s no way around it: Taking away an animal’s home or source of food is causing harm. Habitat loss and degradation are the top threats to wildlife," said Stephanie Wein, Clean Water & Conservation Advocate for PennEnvironment. “Preventing the Endangered Species Act from protecting a species’ habitat eliminates our most valuable tool to conserve America’s wildlife for generations to come. That betrays the entire reason for having an Endangered Species Act.”

“The attempt to strip habitat destruction from the Endangered Species Act’s definition of ‘harm’ is one of the most reckless rollbacks of wildlife protections in decades," said Susan Holmes, Executive Director, Endangered Species Coalition. "We are grateful to Representatives Fitzpatrick and Quigley for introducing a life-saving correction that restores the law’s longstanding safeguards. When nesting beaches disappear, sea turtles are harmed. When rivers are degraded, sturgeon are harmed. When habitat is destroyed, species like Monarch butterflies, manatees, and countless others are harmed. This bill recognizes that reality and puts endangered species protections back on solid scientific footing.”

“Defenders of Wildlife applauds this quick action by Reps. Fitzpatrick and Quigley to reverse this blatant attack on our nation’s cherished wildlife by the Trump administration,” said Mary Beth Beetham, Director of Legislative Affairs, Defenders of Wildlife. “This important legislation to overturn the administration’s elimination of habitat protections under the Endangered Species Act rightly recognizes that, to save imperiled wildlife and address the extinction crisis, we must protect the places where they live.”

“To protect at-risk wildlife, you must protect their homes,” said Oceana Campaign Manager Julia Singer. “Following the Trump administration’s attempt to fast-track extinctions by removing protections for habitat that endangered species need to survive, this bill would reverse this horrendous habitat decision. The Endangered Species Act is one of the nation's most effective conservation laws, saving 99% of species under its care. Oceana applauds Representative Fitzpatrick and Representative Quigley for their bipartisan leadership in upholding and defending this landmark law and urges other members of Congress to follow suit.”

"Save the Manatee Club strongly supports this important bill. Imperiled manatees' greatest long-term threat is habitat loss, particularly loss of warm-water and seagrass habitats that manatees require to survive. Restoring the 40-year-old regulatory definition of 'harm' will ensure that unwarranted and unsustainable habitat destruction will remain prohibited by the Endangered Species Act, consistent with the letter of the law and the drafters' original intent,” said Patrick Rose, Aquatic Biologist and Certified Public Manager, Executive Director, Save the Manatee Club.

title: ICYMI: Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher, Members of Congress Question ICE's Use of Force Following Killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo
text:
Today, Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07) joined Congressional Hispanic Caucus Chair Adriano Espaillat, House Committee on Homeland Security Ranking Member Bennie Thompson, and Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia (TX-29) for an oversight forum on U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement’s (ICE) use of force and abuse of power, following the tragic killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo by ICE in Houston on July 7, 2026.

The forum, entitled “Seeking Justice: Oversight of ICE’s Use of Force in the Death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo,” included testimony from Lorenzo Salgado Araujo’s sons, Ronaldo Salgado Araujo and Lorenzo Salgado Araujo Jr.; Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare; Houston City Council Member Joaquin Martinez (District I); LULAC President & CEO Juan Proaño; East End Communities Director Patricia Cabrera; and Immaculate Conception Catholic Church Rev. Salvatore De George.

Congresswoman Fletcher’s oversight forum remarks as delivered:

Congresswoman Fletcher:

Well thank you, Chairman Espaillat, and thanks to you and Ranking Member Thompson and Representative Garcia for convening this important oversight forum. And I want to thank all of my colleagues who've come from across the country to see and hear from our community. And I want to thank our witnesses from our community for so beautifully explaining and showing this community to the rest of the country. Because people across our community and across the country, as Father De George and Ms. Cabrera explained so beautifully, have been living in fear. And their worst fears were realized again when federal agents killed Lorenzo Salgado Araujo. So I want to thank all of you for testifying and for your leadership in our community, especially at this devastating time.

Ronaldo and Lorenzo, my thoughts have been and will continue to be with you and your mother and your entire family, not just today, but in all the days ahead. You make us proud, and you make us all proud for your advocacy and for your commitment to justice for all. And I hope today's hearing will demonstrate to you and to everyone here our commitment of not only our Houston Congressional Democratic Delegation, but the Congressional Hispanic Caucus and the entire House Democratic Caucus.

It is a failure of this Congress—and many before—that we have not been able to pass laws to address our broken immigration system. The people here have been trying and will continue to do so, but it is a new and utter failure of this Republican-controlled Congress that has not only failed to address—it has refused to address the abuses that this White House is directing in terms of immigration enforcement operations. And that it has done nothing—nothing—when innocent people in this country have been killed at the hands of federal immigration agents this year and during this term.

It is a betrayal of families and communities across the country that we represent. It is a betrayal of the Constitution that we have all sworn an oath to protect and defend, and it is a betrayal of our values as Americans. And yet, what we hear from those who are directing these policies is that these actions are being taken to make us safe. And so, District Attorney Teare, I want to direct my questions—start my questions—with you. Can you tell us from your experience of 20 years in law enforcement whether the policies that we have seen implemented at ICE—and in terms of immigration enforcement throughout DHS—in the last 18 months have made our communities safer?

District Attorney Teare:

Objectively, no. They've had the complete opposite effect.

Congresswoman Fletcher:

And can you tell us why that is? Can you give us some examples of what is making us less safe because of the policies that this administration is implementing?

District Attorney Teare:

We have people who are here unauthorized, who are victims of domestic violence, aggravated robbery, aggravated sexual assault, who are too scared to even call the police, let alone participate in prosecutions of people who are here with documentation or who are citizens. These policies have effectively created a group of our community that are targets, and that's what we're seeing.

And we can't hold the people that prey on them accountable. And that group of people knows it.

Congresswoman Fletcher:

Thank you. In addition, Mr. Green asked about dash cams, and I also want to ask about the increased presence of unmarked vehicles and plainclothes officers for immigration enforcement activities. That's something I know many of us up here have objected to repeatedly, but can you talk about what that does in our communities as well?

District Attorney Teare:

Yeah. It continues the feeling of fear—the floating fear that Father talked about. But it's just not good law enforcement policy. Undercover work is crucial to good law enforcement policy. But undercover officers don't then affect the traffic stops for reasons that we have seen time and again around the fear of the person trying to be stopped. So it is not best practices.

Congresswoman Fletcher:

Thank you. And with the time I have left, Council Member Martinez, I just want to direct this question to you. Can you share with us how you see in the community this affects interactions with law enforcement agencies that come under your jurisdiction, like the Houston Police Department and others, and in the community because of the actions of these federal officers?

Council Member Martinez:

Yes, Congresswoman. So it's important to continue to highlight that calls for services are down. My team, we've done some research. We've gotten data from HPD within our zip codes. And they have gone down. And then even heavier in the southwest part of Houston, where we have an even more diverse immigrant population, called them services have gone down even more. So what we're finding as well is that, when residents—and I've shared my personal number with several community folks—when something is happening, an operation is happening, and folks can’t identify who is heading that operation, we're having to call and figure out what agency this is

in order to try and tamper down those fears.

Congresswoman Fletcher:

Thank you, Council Member, I've gone over my time, I appreciate it. Thank you all for your testimony and for your work. And thank you again for convening this hearing. And I yield back.

title: Congressman Flood Introduces Bill to Prevent COVID-Era Religious Restrictions at Hospitals
text:
LINCOLN, NEBRASKA – This week, U.S. Congressman Mike Flood introduced the Protecting Access to Spiritual Treatment and Organized Religion (PASTOR) Act. The legislation ensures that patients are able to receive the spiritual care they request during times of crisis, serious illness, or at the end of life while hospitalized.

“During the COVID-19 Pandemic, we saw members of the clergy turned away from hospitals even when patients requested their presence,” said Congressman Flood. “This bill ensures that never happens again. If signed into law, it would codify CMS policy requiring hospitals to allow members of the clergy to provide spiritual care, so long as they comply with necessary protective measures.”

Inspired by a clergyman who raised concerns directly to Congressman Flood about access to hospitals during the COVID-19 pandemic, this bill codifies the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services' (CMS) guidance requiring healthcare facilities to accommodate clergy visitation. Those protections were broadly waived during the COVID-19 pandemic. The PASTOR Act ensures these protections remain in place and cannot be reversed by future administrations, public health emergencies, or regulatory changes.

title: Rep. Foushee Introduces Bill to End Price Gouging in Federal Prison Commissaries
text:
WASHINGTON, DC (July 24, 2026) — Yesterday, Congresswoman Valerie Foushee (NC-04) introduced the Stop Prison Price Gouging Act of 2026, legislation to prevent federal prison commissaries from charging prices above fair market value, strengthen oversight of Bureau of Prisons (BOP) contracts, and protect incarcerated people and their families from unfair costs.

The bill would require the Director of the Federal Bureau of Prisons to set commissary prices at no more than the fair market value of each item in the state where the facility is located. By establishing a clear definition of fair market value and excluding prices from correctional institutions and other captive markets, the legislation would ensure incarcerated people are not charged inflated prices for basic necessities. This also comes on the back of reports that the Trump Administration hopes to privatize food service, commissary, and health care across the BOP.

“People in federal custody should not be charged more for basic necessities simply because they have no other place to buy them,” said Congresswoman Foushee. “Inflated commissary prices do not just affect incarcerated people—they also place a burden on the families who sacrifice to help their loved ones afford everyday essentials. The Stop Prison Price Gouging Act establishes a clear, commonsense standard for fair pricing, strengthens transparency and accountability, and ensures that federal prison commissaires are not used as a source of unfair profit from a captive market.”

The legislation would require the Bureau of Prisons to use competitive bidding when awarding commissary contracts and prohibit contracts that include revenue-sharing arrangements. It will also require the Bureau of Prisons to review commissary prices every month, submit an annual report to Congress detailing available goods, prices, and contracts at each facility, and undergo annual audits by the Government Accountability Office to ensure compliance with the bill’s fair-pricing requirements.

The Stop Prison Price Gouging Act of 2026 is endorsed by Brennan Center for Justice, FAMM, the Prison Policy Initiative, and the Vera Institute of Justice.

“At a prison commissary, basic necessities like soap and toothpaste should be sold at market value, not at a markup. Unfortunately, that’s not always the case in federal prison. Overcharging for things like reading glasses hurts the people who are incarcerated and, in many cases, their families who fund commissary accounts. It’s time to make it more affordable for the people behind bars to take care of themselves. This bill is about human dignity, and Congress should pass it into law,” said JC Hendrickson, senior policy strategist in the justice program at the Brennan Center for Justice.

“Incarcerated people and their families spend billions of dollars every year on commissary purchases. FAMM is proud to endorse the Stop Prison Price Gouging Act because no one should be exploited by inflated prices for basic needs such as toiletries and phone calls,” said Kevin Hagan, Esq., Federal Legislative Affairs Director with FAMM (formerly Families Against Mandatory Minimums).

"Prison Policy Initiative is happy to support the Stop Prison Price Gouging Act. People in federal prisons may earn as little as $0.12 an hour from their work assignments and are often among the poorest in the country before their incarceration. Nevertheless, they are routinely forced to pay far more for an item in prison than they would in the community. Families are left to shoulder the burden, spending an average of $4200 each year to support their loved ones during incarceration. This bill recognizes the economic burdens incarcerated people and their families often face and seeks to address them by providing much-needed guardrails for prison contracts and by ensuring that prices in prison reflect fair market value," said Sarah Staudt, Director of Advocacy and Policy at Prison Policy Initiative.

“No one should be forced to pay inflated prices for basic necessities simply because they are incarcerated. When commissary prices are too high, the burden falls not only on incarcerated people but also on the families who often sacrifice to help their loved ones afford everyday essentials. This legislation is an important step toward ensuring that federal prison commissary prices are fair, transparent, and free from profiteering,” said Aiden Cotter, Director of Federal Advocacy, Vera Institute of Justice and Vera Action.

title: Reps. Gillen, Trahan, DeLauro, Larsen and Walkinshaw Introduce Right to IVF Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Yesterday, Congresswoman Laura Gillen (NY-04), alongside Congresswoman Lori Trahan (MA-03), Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-01), Congressman Rick Larsen (WA-02) and Congressman James Walkinshaw (VA-11) introduced the Right to IVF Act. Introduced ahead of World IVF Day on July 25th, the legislative package would make it easier to access in-vitro fertilization (IVF) and other assisted reproductive technology (ART) for the millions of hopeful parents who depend on it to build their family. The pro-family legislation would establish a nationwide right to access IVF, lower the costs of IVF treatment, expand IVF coverage for military families and require all employer-sponsored insurance programs to cover the treatments.

“I am proud to lead this critical bill ensuring millions of Americans can access IVF to build their families, no matter where they live,” said Rep. Gillen. “Families struggling to conceive go through indescribable heartbreak and stress. The last thing they should worry about is legal challenges to IVF delaying or outright halting procedures. Infertility is not a partisan issue. I will continue to work across the aisle in Congress to protect access to IVF and adjacent reproductive technologies that have helped countless individuals experience the joy of parenthood.”

“Like so many people in our country facing fertility challenges, my husband and I turned to IVF as our last hope to have kids. After years of appointments, injections, and setbacks, and thanks to our remarkable physicians, we have two beautiful daughters,” said Rep. Trahan. “No one should lose the chance to start or grow a family because of their zip code. The Right to IVF Act guarantees the right to family-creating fertility care in every state and puts it within reach for the millions of families who need it.”

“There are few experiences as hard as wanting to start a family and not being able to,” said Rep. DeLauro. “That is why I am fighting to ensure Americans have access to IVF treatments when they want to start one. I am proud to join my colleagues in introducing the Right to IVF Act – because building a family in the United States should never be difficult.”

“For many Americans, fertility treatments like IVF are essential to start families of their own,” said Rep. Larsen. “This comprehensive legislation will guarantee access and expand coverage for IVF and other fertility services. The legislation also includes my bill with Senator Murray, the Veteran Families Health Services Act, to ensure fertility treatments are included in servicemembers’ and veterans’ health benefits. I will keep working with my colleagues in the House and the Senate to make sure that women and men in uniform and working families do not have to sacrifice their dreams of having a family.”

“Deciding when and how to build a family is a deeply personal choice that belongs to families, not politicians,” said Rep. Walkinshaw, Co-Chair of the Federal Workforce Caucus. “For millions struggling with infertility, IVF offers hope and a path to parenthood. I’m especially proud the Right to IVF Act includes my legislation requiring IVF coverage through the Federal Employees Health Benefits Program, ensuring the federal government leads by example. I’m honored to join Senator Duckworth, Congresswoman Trahan, and this coalition to protect IVF nationwide and expand access for servicemembers, veterans, federal employees, and working families.”

The legislation comes amid renewed national attention to IVF following recent court rulings in states like Alabama, where embryos created through IVF were legally recognized as children, prompting clinics to suspend services due to legal risks.

The Right to IVF Act of 2026 is comprehensive, bicameral legislation that would establish an enforceable nationwide right to access and provide IVF and other fertility treatments and ensure every family can receive affordable insurance coverage of fertility care. The legislative package includes the text of Rep. Gillen’s Access to Family Building Act (H.R. 2049), which would federally codify the right to access IVF services. Specifically, the Right to IVF Act would:

Create a statutory right for an individual to access, a provider to provide, and an insurer to cover assisted reproductive technology (ART), including IVF and intrauterine insemination (IUI), without prohibition, limitation, or interference.

Ensure coverage for ART, including IVF and IUI, for servicemembers, veterans, government employees, and people with employer-sponsored insurance, Medicaid, Medicare, and ACA plans.

The legislation introduced today was cosponsored by 119 House members and 46 Senators. A copy of the bill can be accessed HERE. A Senate companion bill was introduced by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Patty Murray (D-WA), Cory Booker (D-NJ), and Chuck Schumer (D-NY).

The Right to IVF Act is also supported by the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM), RESOLVE: The National Infertility and Family Building Association, Center for Reproductive Rights (CRR), Planned Parenthood Federation of America (PPFA), National Women’s Law Center (NWLC), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG) and GLBTQ Legal Advocates and Defenders (GLAD).

“The American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) welcomes the bicameral reintroduction of the Right to IVF Act, which would achieve accessible and affordable fertility care for all Americans,” said ASRM Chief Advocacy and Policy Officer Sean Tipton. “This visionary and comprehensive effort would protect patients' ability to build their families through safe, evidence-based treatments like in vitro fertilization (IVF). By safeguarding access to assisted reproductive technology (ART), preserving the physician-patient relationship, and expanding coverage for the individuals and families who need it most, this legislation reflects the standard of care that all patients deserve.”

“No one should have to wonder whether they'll be able to access the care they need to build their family,” said Danielle Melfi, CEO of RESOLVE: The National Infertility and Family Building Association. “By safeguarding the right to IVF and expanding insurance coverage for veterans, federal employees, and the individuals and families who need it most, this legislation reflects a comprehensive commitment to helping more people build the families they dream of. RESOLVE applauds Senator Duckworth and the bill's sponsors for continuing to put patients and families first.”

title: Rep. Gomez Votes to End Trump's War with Iran Following House Passage of War Powers Resolution
text:
Watch Rep. Gomez's video here

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Representative Jimmy Gomez (CA-34) voted for the fifth time in favor of a War Powers Resolution to end President Trump's unauthorized war with Iran. The vote came just days after four American servicemembers were killed in Iranian strikes, with the resolution passing the House with unanimous Democratic support and four Republican votes.

“I just left the house floor where I voted to end Trump's reckless war with Iran, a war that never should have been started in the first place. Just this week four service members have been killed by Iranian strikes,” said Rep. Gomez. “Now we have families that are struggling and suffering because they lost their loved ones, but we also have families who are struggling and suffering because Trump's war is driving up the cost of living in this country. That's why I voted once again to end this war through a war powers resolution.”

Rep. Gomez has consistently opposed President Trump's unauthorized military actions against Iran and has repeatedly voted to reassert Congress' constitutional authority to declare war.

title: Gooden Calls for DOJ Probe Into Foreign Influence of U.S. AI Policy
text:
WASHINGTON –Congressman Lance Gooden (TX-05) sent a letter to Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche urging the Department of Justice (DOJ) to investigate foreign interference in United States artificial intelligence (AI) policy.

In the letter, Gooden cites public reporting detailing efforts by foreign actors to influence U.S. AI policy through state-backed propaganda, foreign-linked nonprofits, and obscure funding streams designed to shape public debate surrounding AI development and weaken U.S. AI leadership.

"Artificial intelligence will shape the future of our economy, national security, and global competitiveness," said Rep. Gooden. "The United States cannot allow foreign adversaries to manipulate our AI policy and compromise our leadership on this technology.”

An excerpt from the letter:

“AI is rapidly becoming a central component of our economic competitiveness and national security. To ensure American policymaking remains free from covert foreign influence, participants in policy debates should not have vested interests or undisclosed financial relationships with our nation’s adversaries. As many Americans remain concerned regarding AI development and expansion, recent public reporting raises questions about the extent to which foreign-linked entities may be shaping these debates in ways that align with the strategic interests of the People’s Republic of China (PRC).

“These recent developments indicate possible vulnerabilities in current foreign disclosure laws and raise important questions about the adequacy of existing safeguards. To ensure the confidence of the American people in critical emerging technologies, these debates must be driven by legitimate domestic concerns that prioritize American interests without being influenced by undisclosed foreign interests.”

The letter was featured in anexclusive article from Fox Digital and is co-signed by Reps. Randy Weber (TX-14), Nathaniel Moran (TX-01), Addison McDowell (NC-06), Tom Tiffany (WI-07), and Pat Fallon (TX-04).

This letter builds on previous efforts by Gooden to combat foreign influence in U.S. policymaking. In 2025, he sent a similarletter to the DOJ urging an investigation into PRC manipulation of U.S. energy and environmental policy, and he introduced theThink Tank and Nonprofit Foreign Influence Disclosure Act, which requires think tanks and nonprofits to publicly disclose significant contributions from foreign governments and political parties.

Read the full letterhere.

title: Goodlander-Backed Bipartisan Bill to Crack Down on Corruption and Expose Billions in Secret Federal Spending Passes the House
text:
Washington, D.C. — This week, the House of Representatives passed the Stop Secret Spending Act, bipartisan legislation Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander (NH-02) helped lead to force the federal government to disclose billions of dollars in spending currently kept off the public books. Goodlander is one of the original cosponsors of the bill and has been a leading voice in Congress for cracking down on corruption and making every federal dollar traceable by the people who pay for it: American taxpayers.

“Public service is a public trust, and the American people have a right to know how every taxpayer dollar is being spent,” said Congresswoman Goodlander. “I am proud to be building a bipartisan coalition in Congress dedicated to a commonsense idea: end secret government spending. Sunlight is the best disinfectant in the fight to crack down on corruption, and our bill will stop secret spending by closing loopholes and giving independent watchdogs the tools they need to hold government accountable. I won’t quit until we get this bill signed into law.”

Last year, the federal government spent a total of $7 trillion taxpayer dollars, and billions of dollars were secretly spent. For example, at the Department of Defense alone, the Government Accountability Office identified $77.5 billion in secret spending between fiscal years 2021 and 2025 that were never reported to USAspending.gov.

This secret spending has been made possible in part by legally binding arrangements outside standard government contracts, grants, and cooperative agreements known as Other Transaction Agreements, or OTAs. OTAs can help the federal government move quickly and work with new partners, but are exempt from many federal procurement laws and requirements. That exemption has created a loophole that allows agencies to hide billions of dollars in spending from USAspending.gov — leaving taxpayers and Congress in the dark about their money is going and why.

The bipartisan bill Goodlander helped lead would require the Department of the Treasury to ensure OTA data is automatically transmitted to USAspending.gov and presented in a centralized view. The Treasury would also publish an annual report identifying the total amount of federal-award spending that has not been posted and explaining why the data remains unavailable. For 10 years after enactment, Inspectors General at specified agencies would periodically assess the quality of agency spending data and compliance with federal data standards.

The Stop Secret Spending Act is led by Congressman Barry Moore (R-AL), and Congressman Jimmy Panetta (D-CA) with Goodlander as an original cosponsor.

The bill advanced unanimously out of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform by a vote of 40 to 0 before passing the full House. Companion legislation led by Senator Joni Ernst (R-IA) passed the Senate unanimously earlier this year.

Goodlander has made cracking down on corruption and cleaning up government a central focus of her work in Congress:

Goodlander is leading the bipartisan Public Service Accountability Act to close ethics loopholes and prohibit senior officials across all three branches of government from trading individual stocks or participating in prediction markets.

Goodlander has repeatedly pushed for greater accountability and transparency at the Pentagon so taxpayers can see how their money is being spent. As a Member of the House Armed Services Committee, she is leading oversight and legislative efforts to force the Department of Defense to conduct and pass a full independent audit,press Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and senior Pentagon officials on the Pentagon’s audit failures and delayed budget, and securing provisions in the National Defense Authorization Act strengthening oversight of Pentagon financial systems and moving the department closer to a clean audit.

She has worked across party lines to bring greater accountability and competition to Pentagon contracting and stop corporate restrictions from wasting taxpayer dollars. Shehelped secure a new system to track defense contractors’ compliance with repair-data requirements, helped introduce the bipartisanWarrior Right to Repair Act of 2025, andco-led a bipartisan amendment adopted by the House Armed Services Committee to strengthen the military’s ability to repair its own equipment.

Goodlander has used independent oversight, legislation, and the courts to challenge waste and unauthorized government spending. Shejoined a call for an Inspector General investigation after the State Department destroyed taxpayer-funded emergency food and millions of dollars’ worth of contraceptives; helped introduce theStrengthening Uniform Procedures to Prevent Loss, Incineration, and Expiration of Supplies (SUPPLIES) Act to prevent similar waste; andjoined a legal brief challenging a proposed $400 million White House ballroom that Congress had neither authorized nor funded.

Goodlander has fought to ensure that Members of Congress are held accountable to the same people they serve. She cosponsored the bipartisanCLEAN Act, which would make the Office of Congressional Ethics permanent;asked the House to withhold her own salary during a government shutdown; and cosponsored the bipartisanNo Pay for Congress During Default or Shutdown Act, which would prevent lawmakers from being paid when Congress fails to fund the government.

Goodlander is a champion for small businesses and is a cosponsor of the Transparency and Predictability in Small Business Opportunities Act, requiring greater disclosure when federal contracting opportunities for small businesses are canceled. The House passed the legislation.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer & White House Announce $42 Million+ in Funding From Washington to New Jersey
text:
Above: Gottheimer announces $42 million+ in funding to New Jersey.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, July 24, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) and the White House announced more than $42 million in Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) funding to strengthen law enforcement and keep Jersey communities safe. This funding comes on top of the $8.5 million previously secured to protect Jersey during the World Cup, totaling more than $50 million clawed back for New Jersey law enforcement since June.

Watch Gottheimer’s announcement here.

Half of the new funding clawed back today — $21 million — will go statewide, to support New Jersey public safety, including State Police, defraying World Cup related expenditures, and other public safety and transit measures up and down the state.

The other half — $21 million — is going directly to New Jersey’s Fifth Congressional District, for public safety in Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties, including local and county law enforcement efforts, transit security, and security for houses of worship and religious schools.

Breakdown of Funds and Their Use:

Gear for cops on the ground: Allows local and state police to invest in updated radios, drones, gear for active shooter and mass-casualty response, and K-9 training.

Protecting places of worship: Provides security upgrades like armed guards, cameras, reinforced doors, fencing, and more for synagogues, churches, mosques, temples, and other nonprofits. Jersey families shouldn’t have to think twice about safety when they go to their place of worship.

Securing transportation hubs: Adds additional security cameras, cybersecurity protections, and physical reinforcement of the Andover train station. This project that Gottheimer has championed for years, will bring rail back to Sussex County for the first time in over 50 years. These added security dollars will help avoid any delays in getting this critical station open.

“Today, building on that, and working with the White House, I am proud to announce that we have clawed back more than $42 million in FEMA grant funding from Washington, DC to New Jersey for public safety right here in Jersey’s Fifth Congressional District. Every single day, rain or shine, late nights, early mornings, weekends, holidays, kids’ birthdays and other family occasions, you put on the uniform, and you respond without hesitation. You get our backs. And I want you to know, as ever, that I’ll always get yours,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “The men and women who wear the badge go above and beyond to protect us, and they’ve earned every bit of support we can give them — for the big events and the everyday calls alike. That’s what this funding is about. I went to bat in Washington, and after months of negotiations and relentless advocacy, I clawed back more than $42 million home to Jersey and put it exactly where it belongs: in the hands of the brave men and women keeping our communities safe.”

“Keeping New Jersey families safe starts with making sure our first responders have the resources they need to do their jobs. Our congressional delegation is essential in delivering federal dollars that help strengthen public safety in communities across our state, and I want to thank Congressman Gottheimer for helping secure this funding for New Jersey. For too long, New Jerseyans have sent far more to Washington than we receive in return. This investment is a step toward ensuring our taxpayers see more of their hard-earned dollars come back home to support our first responders,” said Governor Mikie Sherrill.

Resources will flow to the New Jersey Office of Homeland Security and Preparedness through several grants, including the State Homeland Security Program (SHSP),; the Urban Area Security Initiative (UASI); the Emergency Management Performance Grant (EMPG); the Transit Security Grant Program (TSGP); and the Nonprofit Security Grant Program (NSGP). These resources are dedicated to disaster prevention, supporting the law enforcement and security operations that keep our communities safe and secure.

Gottheimer was joined by Bergen County Prosecutor Mark Musella; Passaic County Prosecutor Camilla Valdes; Sussex County Prosecutor Dan Perez; Bergen County Executive Jim Tedesco III; Senator Gordon Johnson; Assemblywoman Lisa Swain; Fort Lee Mayor Mark Sokolich; Newton Mayor Matthew Dickson; Fair Lawn Mayor Cristinie Cutrone; Englewood Cliffs Mayor Mark Park; Englewood Mayor Michael Wildes; Ringwood Mayor Jamie Landis; Lafayette Mayor Richard Hughes; Ho-Ho-Kus Mayor Thomas Randall; Vernon Mayor Anthony Rossi; Wanaque Mayor Dan Mahler; Bloomingdale Mayor John D’Amato; Andover Deputy Mayor Krista Ghilcrist; Ringwood Councilwoman Yvonne M. Echols; Tenafly Borough Administrator David Fanslau; Wanaque Borough Administrator Rob Hermansen; Tenafly Borough Clerk Omar Stovall; and Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex County first responders.

Below: Gottheimer announces $42 million+ in funding to New Jersey.

###

Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:

Good morning, everyone.

First, I want to start by thanking the hard-working people standing here with us today. Jersey’s finest.

Our local police departments. Our sheriffs and county prosecutors and their teams. Our state troopers. Our firefighters and our EMS crews. Everyone who answers the call, no matter the hour.

You roll up on a call at two in the morning, not knowing what’s on the other side of that door. You chase down a stolen car through a school zone. You answer a 911 call for help because someone’s having a heart attack. You stand post for hours outside a house of worship because a threat came in overnight. The job never slows down, and the risks just keep getting bigger.

Every single day, rain or shine, late nights, early mornings, weekends, holidays, kids’ birthdays and other family occasions, you put on the uniform and you respond without hesitation. You get our backs. And I want you to know, as ever, that I’ll always get yours.

Far too often, our local and county police departments — the men and women protecting the towns you live in, whether that’s in Bergen, Passaic, or Sussex Counties — have been stretched thin, without all the resources they need to protect our families and themselves.

Updated radios and communication systems. Specialty drones. Additional K-9 units. Gear for the worst-case scenarios nobody wants to think about — and all of the training that goes along with it. It’s all expensive. But the truth is that you want them to have it.

Why? Thanks to our phenomenal law enforcement and prosecutors, crime is down in Jersey with a 30% drop in statewide shootings and a 6% overall crime rate reduction over the last year. Auto thefts are down 9% since 2024 due to coordinated federal, state, and local action, but more needs to be done.

Just this past June, our NJ cops busted more than 60 criminals involved in an $8 million auto theft ring that stole more than 90 cars by breaking into homes for key fobs and then shipping the cars to West Africa. Other auto thieves are changing their tactics to steal sensors and airbags out of cars parked on the street to sell on the black market. Cyber theft is also surging across New Jersey, with victims losing more than $435 million, ranking Jersey 5th nationwide for total losses to cybercrime. And organized retail crime continues to be a problem in our state, with highly professional groups targeting our local businesses to seize merchandise that they sell for a profit.

Thanks to social media, cable news, and massive disinformation, one area that has moved in the wrong direction is hate crimes, especially those that are religiously motivated.

Houses of worship, like synagogues, churches, mosques, and temples, are facing elevated threats both in Jersey and across the country. In fact, according to the ADL, Jersey had the third-most antisemitic incidents of any state in the country, with Bergen County having the highest number in the state.

People are being attacked walking to temple, like the young man shot with a pellet gun in Teaneck earlier this year. We saw the horrific attack in New York City just yesterday, with a man screaming “Allahu akbar” as he stabbed a parishioner walking out of a synagogue. Churches, synagogues, schools, and other houses of worship have had to spend their own money, out of their own pockets, when federal dollars don’t go far enough, on security officers, cameras, alarms, and reinforced doors, just so their congregants can pray safely. In the greatest country in the world, people should be able to go to church or temple without fear.

On top of that, World Cup expenses hit our local communities, county, and state — including transit, logistics, infrastructure, and overtime costs. We obviously needed it to keep our communities safe — after all, we were hosting the world, and we did an excellent job. New Jersey at its best. But I don’t want the World Cup to hit the pocketbooks of our families — or our towns. I don’t want it coming out of your state income and local property taxes. The families in Jersey shouldn’t be footing the bill for a global sporting event that FIFA and the federal government have a responsibility to fund.

The bottom line: ensuring our public safety — keeping Jersey families safe — is essential. It’s not optional. But it’s also expensive. To help cover costs, I’ve spent the last few months in Washington working overtime, not just to help cover World Cup costs, but also to do everything we can to support our first responders — to claw more of your federal tax dollars back to North Jersey, so you don’t have to pick up the tab on your state and local taxes. Months of meetings. Months of calls. Months of negotiations. I worked with the White House and with FEMA to make sure Jersey, and especially the towns right here in the 5th District, got the funds we deserve.

In June, I proudly announced that I had clawed back $8.5 million to help cover World Cup law enforcement overtime costs for cops across Bergen County and in and around MetLife — including millions for our state police.

Today, building on that, and working with the White House, I am proud to announce that we have clawed back more than $42 million in FEMA grant funding from Washington, DC to New Jersey for public safety right here in Jersey’s Fifth Congressional District.

My dad told me a long time ago: you don’t get it if you don’t ask — and if you don’t fight hard for what’s yours. Well, I’ve also said that I’ll work with the other side if it’s good for Jersey. Protecting our towns and our state is good for Jersey; standing by law enforcement is good for Jersey; protecting our synagogues and churches to protect religious freedom is good for Jersey. Making sure Jersey is safe and our families are safe is good. This is about solving real problems that our community and our families are facing.

You know what else is good? Fighting the Moocher States and clawing money back to Jersey to help get our taxes down.

Historically, Mississippi gets about $4.38 back for every dollar it sends to Washington. West Virginia gets about $4.23 back. But New Jersey? We get about 67 cents on the dollar. That’s not nearly enough for what we put in, and far too much ends up on your state and property taxes. The less that goes to other states and the more that comes to us means lower state and property taxes for Jersey families.

Keeping score for Jersey taxpayers: in under three months, between today’s $42 million and the $8.5 million for World Cup safety in June, that’s $50.5 million clawed back from Washington to Jersey to protect our families and first responders — in just three months.

That’s all about getting your taxes down and getting money away from the Moocher States.

Those are your tax dollars pouring back into our community, keeping your property taxes down and making real, local improvements for Jersey families.

Here’s how it breaks down. Half of the new funding we clawed back today — $21 million — will go statewide, to support New Jersey State Police, law enforcement efforts up and down the state, transit security, and nonprofit security. And the other half — $21 million — is coming back home to our own Fifth Congressional District, right here for public safety in Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties.

Let me tell you exactly where this money is going, and what it’s going to do.

First: part of the $42 million will go toward protecting law enforcement and our communities, including local, county, and state police, to invest in updated radios to communicate, drones, and equipment for active shooter and mass-casualty response, along with K-9s and training. It will also help towns build and improve their emergency operations centers. That will help ensure that a cop in Hackensack, an officer in Ringwood, or a deputy in Sussex County has the tools they actually need to protect Jersey families — and come home safe at the end of the shift, or when you wake up at 2 a.m. to respond to a health emergency.

These dollars will invest in emergency radio replacement for towns like Fort Lee that need to transition to modern, reliable communication systems. I know radios might not sound exciting, but they’re absolutely vital to helping our officers get the job done in our towns and across the county. When an officer chases a suspect from one town into the next, their radios have to bridge that gap. When they need an ambulance on scene, they have to reach EMS instantly — no delay, no dead air. When a fire crew backs up a neighboring department, they have to be on the same channel. That’s the difference between help getting there in time and not.

We learned that the hardest way possible. On 9/11, our first responders couldn’t communicate. Radios from different departments didn’t talk to each other, servers and radios failed in the towers, and firefighters climbing those stairwells never got the order to get out. Brave men and women died in part because the equipment failed them. We swore we’d never let that happen again, and the technology never stops changing, so neither can we.

That’s why, working hand in hand with the Bergen County Prosecutor, we’re setting up a dedicated fund for radios and communications equipment, hosted right out of the Prosecutor’s office. And we will do the same for the towns I represent in Passaic and Sussex Counties. Any town can come to us and flag that they need radios, and we’ll do our best to get you what you need — or a down payment toward it.

Second, part of the $42 million we’ve clawed back will go to protecting our houses of worship here in the Fifth Congressional District. No family should have to think twice about their safety when they walk into a synagogue, a church, a mosque, or a temple.

This funding provides real security upgrades like cameras, security guards, fences, reinforced doors, and alarm systems for our congregations and our nonprofits right here in North Jersey. And security is expensive.

Historically, thanks to our strong coordination with our houses of worship, and my relentless push in Washington, our district has clawed back the most nonprofit security grant funding of any district in Jersey. That makes sense — we have the highest number of antisemitic incidents of any district in the state.

Antisemitic incidents are up 70 percent since October 7, and hate of all kinds is thriving. Our places of worship, whether synagogues, mosques, churches, or Sikh temples, need the resources to protect their worshippers from this vile hatred, against any religion.

Third, part of the $42 million we’ve clawed back from Washington will help cover costs we got stuck with for the World Cup — which, I’ll mention again, was in Jersey, not New York, by the way. These dollars will help cover security operations, like the intelligence analysts, the traffic officers, the task force deployments, and extra emergency equipment.

Finally, part of the $42 million we clawed back today will go to securing our transportation hubs, including extra security cameras, cybersecurity protections, and physical reinforcements, including to the Andover Train Station project. These added security dollars will help avoid any delays in getting this critical station open for my constituents.

For years, I’ve pushed NJ TRANSIT and Amtrak to stop the bureaucratic delays and finally bring passenger rail back to Sussex County — and specifically Andover Train Station — for the first time in more than fifty years.

There are zero options for folks in Sussex County to get on a train to get to work or to see a family member. I’ve heard from so many residents, businesses, and local elected officials about this issue, and about the urgent need for more transportation options to New York City from across Sussex. I’ve sent letters, done site visits, and clawed millions back in the bipartisan infrastructure bill to keep Andover on the map. Now that we’re finally close to getting trains running again, the least we can do is make sure the station we fought so hard for is safe and secure from day one.

One more point: as I mentioned, half of the $42 million will help protect families and first responders across the state. I am coordinating closely with the Governor and her team to direct these dollars to the most important needs across Jersey — from State Police to our counties and towns. We will announce more specifics about those dollars in the coming weeks. That’s on top of what we’ve clawed back for Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties.

Here’s the bottom line: these are your federal tax dollars. You pay them every single year. The question is always the same: how much of that money actually comes back home to New Jersey, back to the towns you live in, instead of going somewhere else?

My job is to fight for every dollar I can, and claw it back here, where it belongs. That’s what this is: Jersey families’ own federal tax dollars, coming back home to protect Jersey — to protect our families, whether that’s in your neighborhood or at your temple or church.

This isn’t about one headline or one event. This is about the men and women who show up every single day. You’ve earned every bit of support we can give you. And there’s nothing partisan about this. This is about common sense. About solving problems. And putting our country first.

I am so proud to stand here today. I am so grateful for everything these incredible public servants do for every single one of us, every single day.

If we keep working together to support our communities, in the greatest country in the world, our best days will always be ahead of us.

Thank you, may God bless you, your families, and our first responders.

title: Congressman Hamadeh Honored to Accept the Defender of Limited Government Award
text:
Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ-08) today accepted the Defender of Limited Government Award from the Institute for Legislative Analysis (ILA). The award was presented by ILA Chief Executive Officer Ryan McGowan and President Fred McGrath in recognition of Congressman Hamadeh's strong voting record in support of limited government principles.

Congressman Hamadeh was given this award for his service and dedication to Arizonans and the American people. The Congressman received an A+ ILA score with an impressive 86%, 5 points higher than the projected district estimate of 81%. His voting record earned perfect scores in several key policy areas, including energy, national security, free speech, healthcare, and government accountability.

“The Institute for Legislative Analysis is proud to present Congressman Abraham Hamadeh with the Defender of Limited Government Award for a voting record closely aligned with the limited government principles of the U.S. Constitution. In his first term, Congressman Hamadeh has already become a major voice on national security, public safety, and making sure government fulfills its core responsibilities without unnecessary waste or bureaucracy. We especially appreciate his work to improve veterans’ access to the programs and support they have earned, while demanding a federal government that is more responsive, accountable, and focused on results. Congressman Hamadeh and the team he has assembled deserve credit for standing with taxpayers, service members, veterans, and Arizona families who expect Washington to do its job and stay within its proper limits.” said Ryan McGowan, CEO, Institute for Legislative Analysis.

"It is an honor to receive the Defender of Limited Government Award," said Congressman Hamadeh. "The people of Arizona's Eighth District elected me to defend the Constitution, protect their freedoms, and stand against government overreach. I will continue fighting for policies that preserve individual liberty, strengthen our economy, secure our border, and ensure that our government remains accountable to the people, not the other way around."

title: GENESIS MISSION: Harder Celebrates New Partnership Between NIH and Genesis Mission to Accelerate New Cures
text:
Harder led calls for NIH to join national initiative connecting scientists, artificial intelligence, supercomputers, and federal research data

New mission aims to use artificial intelligence to cure cancer, Alzheimer's two times faster

WASHINGTON – Today, following his calls for new biomedical research infrastructure, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) celebrated the launch of a new partnership between the National Institutes of Health (NIH) and the Genesis Mission, a new federal research initiative designed to speed up breakthrough science. Harder pushed language to expand the Genesis Mission and support AI-driven drug discovery at the NIH, which was included in the FY27 LHHS Appropriations bill leading up to this partnership. The NIH’s new Bio Genesis Mission will connect scientists, federal datasets, artificial intelligence and advanced computing to accelerate biomedical research and get new treatments to patients faster.

"The scientists on the front lines fighting cancer, Alzheimer's, and the diseases that touch every American family deserve the best tools this country can offer," said Rep. Harder. "I pushed for NIH to join the Genesis Mission because breakthroughs happen faster when our researchers have AI and advanced computing at their fingertips. This launch is a major step toward finding new cures, lowering the cost of treatments, and getting lifesaving medicine to patients faster."

The Mission will initially focus on six major biomedical challenges:

Unlocking Pediatric Cancer Cures – The mission will apply AI to research across hundreds of rare childhood cancer subtypes to help identify new treatments and accelerate the search for cures.

Faster Drug Discovery – Researchers will use AI and advanced computing to identify promising new medicines and find new uses for treatments that already exist.

Chronic Disease Research – The initiative will combine health, environmental, and biological data to better understand the root causes of chronic diseases.

More Predictive Biomedical Models – Scientists will work to improve their ability to predict how living systems behave, helping researchers develop and test treatments more effectively.

Stronger Biosecurity – The mission will use AI to identify biological threats earlier and strengthen the country’s ability to respond.

American Biomanufacturing – The initiative will help turn scientific discoveries into medicines and technologies that can be produced here in the United States.

Read Harder’s letter to NIH Director Jay Bhattacharya and White House Office of Science and Technology Policy Director Michael Kratsios here.

Harder is also leading bipartisan, landmark legislation to invest in higher-risk, higher-reward research at the NIH by creating a new, four-part funding series at the agency dedicated to foundational discovery, toolbuilding, biomedical regranting, and new institution seeding. Harder also serves as Chair of the bipartisan Build America Caucus, which was founded to pass pro-growth policies across infrastructure, energy, housing, health care, and technology.

title: Congressman Pat Harrigan Co-Leads Bipartisan Bill to Modernize America's Electric Grid and Lower Energy Costs
text:
Contact: Lexi Kranich (814) 380-4408

WASHINGTON, D.C.—Today, Congressman Pat Harrigan (NC-10) joined Congressman George Whitesides (D-CA-27) in introducing the Lowering Energy Costs through Grid Modernization Act, bipartisan legislation to accelerate upgrades to America's aging electric grid by modernizing existing transmission infrastructure, reducing permitting delays, and expanding the capacity of the nation's electric grid.

"The future of AI, advanced manufacturing, and American energy dominance all depends on one thing: reliable, affordable electricity," said Congressman Harrigan. "Our electric grid wasn't built for the demands we're placing on it today. This bill takes a smarter approach by upgrading the infrastructure we already have instead of waiting a decade to build from scratch, delivering more power, lower costs, and a stronger, more resilient grid."

The Lowering Energy Costs through Grid Modernization Act helps utilities deliver more electricity over existing transmission corridors by deploying advanced conductors that can significantly increase capacity without building entirely new power lines. The legislation also streamlines permitting for upgrades within existing rights-of-way and encourages investment in technologies that improve grid reliability while reducing congestion and lowering costs for consumers.

Congressman Harrigan will continue advancing policies that strengthen America's energy security, expand affordable and reliable power generation, and ensure the nation's infrastructure can support the next generation of economic growth, technological innovation, and national defense.

title: Congressman Harris Announces Army Corps Dredging at Ocean City Inlet
