title: Q&A: Making Healthcare More Affordable
text:
Q: How would the Patients Deserve Price Tags Act help lower costs?

A: Making life more affordable is a top concern I hear from Iowans. Recurring expenses for basic necessities – such as groceries, gas, housing and childcare – can soak up the lion’s share of workers’ paychecks and seniors on fixed income. Paying for prescription drugs and medical expenses puts another squeeze on household budgets, making it even harder to put money into savings, let alone afford a vacation. For decades, I’ve worked at the policymaking tables in the Senate Finance and Judiciary Committees to shape federal policies that help patients access healthcare services they need for chronic diseases and complex medical conditions, maternal and child health services, cancer screening and treatment and lifesaving organ transplants so they can enjoy a high quality of life and longevity with their loved ones.

I’m also continuing to push for legislative reforms that would help lower healthcare costs, including a bill I’m cosponsoring called the Patients Deserve Price Tags Act. I’m glad the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee advanced this pro-patient measure to the full Senate for consideration. This is an important step to boost transparency and give patients a clear understanding about the price of their care beforehand, including X-rays, screenings, medications, surgeries and other services. Americans are savvy consumers and public, upfront pricing will boost competition and empower patients to access healthcare services with the best value. Too often, patients are at the mercy of an opaque healthcare system that effectively means they arrive to the hospital, clinic, imaging center or lab with a blank check. Throughout my years of oversight work, I’m guided by a tried and true principle: Transparency brings accountability and boosts competition. The common-sense Patients Deserve Price Tags Act codifies existing price transparency requirements which I’ve long supported, and strengthens them by closing loopholes, increasing oversight, and becoming more patient-focused. The bill would deliver a healthy dose of sunshine to the U.S. healthcare system and deliver cost savings to patients, employers and taxpayers. Upfront pricing and itemized billing would give patients informed purchasing power and peace of mind when they access healthcare services.

Q: How are you working to lower costs for insulin and other prescription medicines?

A: For several years, I’ve led the charge from the helm of the Senate Judiciary Committee to root out shenanigans in the pharmaceutical supply chain that’s inflating prescription drug costs for Americans. I’ve cultivated several legislative measures with bipartisan coalitions in Congress to drive down prescription drug costs. In the past few years, legislation I’ve secured into law has saved taxpayers over $11 billion. I’m glad the Affordable Prescriptions for Patients Act recently passed the full Senate, bringing it a step closer to becoming law. This bipartisan bill would help prevent patent abuse by pharmaceutical companies who game the system to delay lower-priced generic and biosimilar drugs from coming to market. I’ll continue pushing to get this cost-saving bill to the president’s desk.

I’ve got good news for the tens of millions of Americans who depend on insulin to manage diabetes. The Senate HELP Committee recently advanced a bipartisan bill I’m cosponsoring called the INSULIN Act. It would cap the cost of insulin at $35 per month for Americans on private and employer-sponsored insurance. It also would create a five-year pilot program in 10 states to help make insulin available at the same cost to Americans without insurance. This is welcome news for families struggling to pay for this life-saving medication. What’s more, the comprehensive legislation would ensure patients benefit from rebates and discounts that are typically collected by Pharmacy Benefit Managers (PBMs), the middleman in the drug supply chain. Our bipartisan bill would inject competition into the category of medicine known as biologics that are comprised of complex molecules made from living organisms. That includes insulin, a century-old drug. My two-year bipartisan insulin investigation identified anticompetitive business practices between manufacturers and PBMs that’s created an unsustainable cycle of price increases for patients and taxpayers. I’ll continue pushing for reforms that accelerate a safe onramp for biosimilars to help lower prescription drug costs for Americans.

The safety and efficacy of prescription drugs for Americans is non-negotiable. As a cosponsor of the CLEAR LABELS Act, I welcome the overwhelming support for this bill out of the Senate HELP Committee. Our bill boosts transparency to give Americans peace of mind at the pharmacy counter. It would add country of origin labeling requirements to inform Americans where a drug is manufactured, giving pharmacists, providers and patients upfront awareness if a branded or generic drug, including their active pharmaceutical ingredients (APIs), is made in a foreign country. It would strengthen accountability in the drug supply chain, one of my highest policy priorities on behalf of Iowans.

title: ICYMI—Hagerty Joins Fox & Friends on Fox News to Discuss Iran and the SAVE America Act
text:
New York—Today, United States Sen. Bill Hagerty, R-Tenn., a member of the Senate Foreign Relations, Appropriations, and Banking Committees, joined Fox & Friends on Fox News to discuss the latest developments in Iran and the SAVE America Act.

*Click the photo above or here to watch*

Partial Transcript

Hagerty on Iran and the Abraham Accords: I applaud [President Donald Trump] for bringing major allies in the region together. Iran is getting further and further isolated by a deal like this. And joining the Abraham Accords has been a long-term goal for President Trump. The fact that he has gotten Jared Kushner involved, his wonderful team, John Raider—that team put together the Abraham Accords at a time when it was desperately needed. I think they should have gotten a Nobel Peace Prize for this. And by bringing more into the fold, particularly [Saudi Arabia], the largest economy [in the Middle East], I think this is a major step forward. We are talking about economy, we are talking about prosperity, and I think this sends a message for the entire region that we are ready to move forward […] We are not talking about enrichment programs at all. The [United Arab Emirates (UAE)], other partners of ours, are able to have a civil nuclear program. They report, they do not hide, they do not obfuscate. But I think this is something that we are going to work through the details on with Saudi Arabia. My sense is that President Trump’s overarching goal is to bring them into an economic relationship that begets prosperity. I think the sooner we get this wrapped up, the sooner it is taken care of, the more the American public will come on board. I think the issue we have right now is the fact that [the conflict is] dragging out. And I don’t fault those that are trying to negotiate trying to bring this together with terms that work because we are going to have to rebuild Iran. But at this point, I think the American public’s sentiment, at least as I read the data, [is that] they just want this over with. And if you think about the activity there in the Middle East, [Commander of the United States Central Command (CENTCOM) Admiral Brad Cooper], was about 75 to 80% of the way through the target package they initially set. [CENTCOM] stopped when they went to a ceasefire. They stopped that when they went to negotiate. I think [Admiral Cooper] is back on track to complete that target package, and that will put the Iranian situation in a much better negotiating position.

Hagerty on funding the Department of War (DOW): I think you have a lot of support for this. We have a reconciliation package working its way through. This is just an immediate fix [for funding the Department of War]. There is about $73 billion in that package to address the [Department of War], but we are talking about a $1.5 trillion package at a time when the military needs a significant rebuild. For four years, [the department was] distracted under [former President Joe Biden’s administration], focusing on social engineering, not on lethality. And what the team has found as they have come in is a lot of opportunity to make us stronger. We’ve demonstrated exquisite results… but we need to continue this momentum and make certain that we are ready to deal with all of the adversarial situations.

Hagerty on Budget Reconciliation and the SAVE America Act: I think what we need to do is actually put something in front of everybody, because if it’s voter ID, this is an issue that over 95% of Republicans, and even on the Democrat side, over 70% of Democrats approve of. I don’t know why every American does not want to support this. The mail-in balloting issue gets more complicated for some states that are more remote. I understand that issue, but I think that we take it in pieces.

title: Hickenlooper, Bennet, Colleagues Reintroduce Bill to Deschedule Marijuana, End Federal Prohibition of Cannabis
text:
Legislation comes after the administration announced plans to reclassify marijuana to Schedule III

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senators John Hickenlooper and Michael Bennet joined 15 of their Senate colleagues to reintroduce their Cannabis Administration and Opportunity Act (CAOA), which would end the harmful federal ban of marijuana by removing cannabis from the list of federally controlled substances (descheduling) and empowering states to create their own laws.

“Colorado legalized marijuana fourteen years ago and now nearly half of the states have followed our lead,” said Hickenlooper. “Yet, the federal government continues to drag its feet. We need to deschedule and decriminalize marijuana, then finish the job and expunge the records of everyone who was charged with federal marijuana crimes.”

“Congress should follow Colorado’s lead and bring our nation’s marijuana laws into the 21st century,” said Bennet. “The Cannabis Administration and Opportunity Act is long overdue and will help protect the legal cannabis economy as well as address historic inequities in our justice system.”

Specifically, CAOA establishes a federal regulatory framework to protect public health and safety, prioritizes restorative and economic justice to help undo the decades of harm caused by the failed war on drugs, ends discrimination in the provision of federal benefits on the basis of cannabis use, provides major investments for cannabis research, and strengthens worker protections. By decriminalizing cannabis at the federal level, CAOA also ensures that state-legal cannabis businesses or those in adjacent industries will no longer be denied access to bank accounts or financial services simply because of their ties to cannabis.

Hickenlooper has consistently advocated for the federal government to change the classification of marijuana. Hickenlooper previously urged the DEA to completely deschedule marijuana and introduced the PREPARE Act to prepare the federal government for federal legalization of cannabis, modeled after Colorado’s regulatory commission convened under then-Governor Hickenlooper.

In December, Hickenlooper welcomed the president’s decision to reschedule marijuana to Schedule III and pushed the administration to support his PREPARE Act.

title: Hickenlooper Introduces Bill to Hold Federal Law Enforcement Accountable
text:
Legislation comes as ICE and their contractors shot multiple people, killing two in Aurora

WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper joined Senator Richard Blumenthal and U.S. Representative Maxwell Frost in introducing the Right to Record Act, a bill to protect individuals’ First Amendment rights while engaging with federal law enforcement officers.

“Trump’s rogue federal agents are counting on no one watching, but brave Americans are recording and sharing the evidence to hold them accountable,” said Hickenlooper. “Sadly, this administration blames the people recording the violence instead of the people committing it. Our bill would protect every American’s right to record and to protest peacefully, so that we can continue to stand up to anyone violating fundamental rights.”

“Over the last year, I’ve investigated dozens of cases of Americans brutalized by agents of their own government, and across the board, video footage corroborated their testimony – showing the world what they experienced and making sure that justice was served. Without recordings, we wouldn’t know the truth of what happened to Renee Nicole Good, Alex Pretti, Marimar Martinez, George Retes, and so, so many others,” Blumenthal said. “The right to bear witness has never been more important. I’m proud to work with Congressman Frost on bicameral legislation that will strengthen the right to record, observe, and peacefully protest – creating real enforcement tools for the protections of the First Amendment that lay the foundation for our democracy.”

“The First Amendment defends the right to assemble, protest, and record government officials in public. That right has never been more important. In cases like the murders of Alex Pretti and Renee Good, officials and their allies tried to paint the victims as threats despite evidence showing otherwise,” said Frost. “Without firsthand recordings, those false narratives might have become the official story, which is why the Right to Record Act is so important. It would protect the public’s ability to expose the truth without fear, giving individuals a legal path forward if an officer does violate their constitutional rights.”

The Right to Record Act would add new legal consequences for federal law and immigration enforcement officers who prevent or attempt to prevent a person from recording, observing, or peacefully protesting law enforcement activities. In addition, officers must not command that an individual stop recording, demand identification from an individual because they are recording, or retaliate against an individual for exercising their First Amendment rights, including by threatening them, pursuing them to a different location, or surveilling them.

The Right to Record Act has been endorsed by the American Civil Liberties Union (ACLU).

“The right to observe and record law enforcement is fundamental to our democracy,” said Jenna Leventoff, senior policy counsel with the ACLU. “We can’t hold our government accountable if we can’t see for ourselves what they’re doing in our communities. Observing and filming allows people to create an independent record, share information with their communities, and demand better from our government. Protesting for what we believe in is a core American value, and observing and filming government activity can drive the protest movements that spark change. All of these rights are squarely protected by the First Amendment, and we’re hopeful that Congress will codify them into law by enacting the Right to Record Act.”

Hickenlooper has consistently called out ICE’s lawlessness and violence, and pushed for more oversight and transparency. Hickenlooper introduced bills to ban federal immigration law enforcement from wearing masks and prevent immigration enforcement from targeting schools, hospitals, polling locations, and places of worship.

title: Hoeven: DOJ Awards $555,000 to Community Violence Intervention Center in Grand Forks
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator John Hoeven today announced that the U.S. Department of Justice’s (DOJ) Office on Violence Against Women (OVW) has awarded $555,000 to the Community Violence Intervention Center (CVIC) in Grand Forks through the Fiscal Year 2025 Training and Services to End Violence and Abuse Against Individuals with Disabilities and Deaf People Program. The funding will support physical accessibility improvements, advocacy and intervention services, the development of accessible outreach materials, and outreach office hours and cross-trainings with community partners to better serve individuals with disabilities and deaf victims of violence.

“CVIC provides critical services for victims of violence across northeast North Dakota,” said Hoeven. “This funding will strengthen the organization’s ability to serve individuals with disabilities and deaf victims by improving accessibility, expanding outreach and ensuring they receive the support and services they need.”

The award follows Hoeven’s efforts to resolve DOJ funding delays affecting CVIC’s ability to provide these important victim services and violence prevention programming. Earlier this year, Hoeven worked with DOJ leadership to secure commitments for more than $1.8 million in federal funding for the organization, including this $555,000 grant, a $725,000 Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention grant and a $500,000 OVW Consolidated Youth Program grant.

title: ICYMI: Denison University highlights Husted’s recognition of national championship teams in Washington

title: Senators Justice, Kelly Introduce Bipartisan Senior Chatbot Protection Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – This week, Senator Jim Justice and Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) introduced the bipartisan Senior Chatbot Protection Act to enact safeguards for senior Americans using A.I. chatbots.

“A.I. chatbots are an incredible tool for older Americans, but we can’t miss the opportunity to protect our seniors who rely on chatbots for support, companionship, and even important decisions during critical times. The Senior Chatbot Protection Act sets transparency standards, so our seniors know they are speaking with a chatbot and not a real person—whether in everyday conversations or when making high-stakes decisions. I applaud Senator Kelly for spearheading this important legislation that can make a real difference in the lives of our seniors,” said Senator Jim Justice.

“AI is a powerful tool that can help seniors live more independently. It can help them manage their finances, keep track of medications and doctor’s appointments, and navigate everyday tasks that become more challenging with age. But seniors need to know when they’re talking to a machine, what its limits are, and how their information is being used to make sure they aren’t being scammed or put at risk,” said Senator Mark Kelly.

BACKGROUND:

The Senior Chatbot Protect Act will:

Require clear AI disclosures so that users would be told when they are interacting with AI, and companies could not falsely represent that a chatbot is human or that a response came from a licensed professional.

Provide added protections when a conversation involves health care, estate planning, guardianship, or a crisis so that the chatbot would provide additional warnings, direct users toward appropriate support, and make clear it is not a substitute for qualified professional advice.

Protect sensitive conversations by making companies face limits on using covered conversation data for targeted advertising, profiling, sharing with third parties, or AI training without clear consent. Users would have a clear way to delete conversation history.

Address deceptive design practices by ensuring companies take steps to prevent designs that encourage excessive reliance, discourage users from seeking help from family or professionals, or pressure users to keep engaging after they try to stop.

Senator Justice is on the Special Committee on Aging and is a huge advocate for protecting our seniors.

title: Kaine Presses Pentagon on Military Targets During Operation Epic Fury, Raises Concerns Regarding Strike on Iranian School
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA), a member of the Senate Armed Services and Foreign Relations Committees, sent a letter to the Department of Defense regarding the pre-selected lists of targets in Iran used during the initial strikes of Operation Epic Fury. In his letter, he specifically raised concerns about the February 28 strike on a school in Minab, Iran, in which over 150 civilians, including many children, were killed. Kaine requested answers by August 14 about the Department’s procedures for target development and the report on the bombing of Shajarah Tayyebeh Elementary School.

“I write regarding the pre-selected lists of targets in Iran used during the initial strikes of Operation Epic Fury,” wrote Kaine. “I am deeply concerned about the inclusion of a school in Minab, Iran on the lists of verified targets and the death of over 150 civilians, the majority of whom were children.”

“The school was allegedly targeted during the strikes on February 28, 2026, because the Department relied on outdated information provided by the Defense Intelligence Agency,” Kaine continued. “U.S. officials have stated this data indicated that the building housing Shajarah Tayyebeh Elementary School was part of a military base, but public reporting has revealed that one analyst raised concerns about the accuracy of that assessment as early as 2019. Tragically, those concerns were not heeded and the school continued to be revalidated as a legitimate military target.”

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth:

I write regarding the pre-selected lists of targets in Iran used during the initial strikes of Operation Epic Fury. I am deeply concerned about the inclusion of a school in Minab, Iran on the lists of verified targets and the death of over 150 civilians, the majority of whom were children.

The school was allegedly targeted during the strikes on February 28, 2026, because the Department relied on outdated information provided by the Defense Intelligence Agency. U.S. officials have stated this data indicated that the building housing Shajarah Tayyebeh Elementary School was part of a military base, but public reporting has revealed that one analyst raised concerns about the accuracy of that assessment as early as 2019. Tragically, those concerns were not heeded and the school continued to be revalidated as a legitimate military target.

My expectation is that your Department’s report on the bombing will include a detailed analysis of why the analyst’s concerns were ignored.

In addition, I request answers to the following questions no later than August 14, 2026:

1. What formal procedures exist for analysts to report concerns about potential targets?

2. What formal procedures exist for targets to be reviewed after a concern is raised about their accuracy?

3. Why did the Minab school remain on the target list for years after American intelligence warned that it should be removed and after publicly available data clearly showed that it was a school?

4. When will your department’s report on the bombing of Shajarah Tayyebeh Elementary School be released?

5. Where is this report in the review process as of July 23, 2026?

6. Who else in the Department must review and sign off on this report?

7. What criteria are being used to evaluate the report?

Sincerely,

title: Kaine, Young, Colleagues Reintroduce Bill to End Legacy Admissions
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA), a member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee, along with Senators Todd Young (R-IN), Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Tim Scott (R-SC), Andy Kim (D-NJ), and John Kennedy (R-LA), introduced the Merit-Based Educational Reforms and Institutional Transparency (MERIT) Act, bipartisan legislation that would end the longstanding practice of colleges and universities giving “preferential treatment” in the admissions process based on an applicant’s relationship to alumni or donors of the deciding institution. The senators first introduced the legislation in 2023.

“Everyone deserves the same opportunity to pursue higher education if they choose. It shouldn’t be dependent on whether someone’s parents went to college or donated money to a university,” said Kaine. “I’m glad to be introducing this bipartisan bill to provide Americans of all backgrounds the same chance to pursue higher education and help ensure first-generation and low-income students are not at a disadvantage during the admissions process.”

Specifically, the MERIT Act would amend the Higher Education Act to:

Add a new standard for accreditation to prevent accredited colleges and universities from giving “preferential treatment” to applicants during the admissions process.

Clarify that new admissions standards should not be construed to prevent institutions from considering an applicant’s genuine interest in the institution as part of the admissions process.

Ensure that institutions can make admissions decisions in line with their faith-based values, ensuring no infringement on religious freedom.

Require a comprehensive feasibility study to assess improving data collection regarding the influence of legacy and donor relationships on admissions decisions.

title: New Data: Virginia Families Have Had to Spend $2,000 More Under President Trump
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) are highlighting a new congressional report showing that Virginia families have had to spend more than $2,900 extra on a wide range of goods, including everyday essentials, since President Trump took office last year. This new data details the rising costs facing families across the Commonwealth, including higher prices for housing, groceries, gas, electricity, and health care.

“This new data confirms what we’ve been hearing from families across Virginia for months. President Trump promised the American people lower costs, but instead, his reckless war of choice in Iran and his chaotic economic policies have driven up the price of filling up your car, buying groceries, keeping the lights on, and putting a roof over your head,” said the senators. “Virginians deserve leaders focused on lowering costs – not policies that make life more expensive. We'll keep fighting to reverse these harmful policies, end this unnecessary war, and put more money back in Virginians' pockets."

This new report finds Virginia families have faced sharp increases in the cost of essential goods and services since President Trump took office, including:

Housing Costs

Virginians have had to spend $637 more on housing, including rent and mortgage payments.

Energy Costs

Since the start of President Trump’s war of choice in Iran, Virginians have had to spend more than $2 billion extra on gas, averaging $605 more per household.

Virginia families have also paid $170 more for electricity in 2025 under President Trump than they did in 2024. In just the first six months of 2026, Virginia families are projected to spend an additional $181 more for electricity than they did in the first half of 2024.

Grocery Costs

Across the country, Americans paid $310 more for groceries in 2025 under President Trump than they did in 2024.

Grocery prices are more than 4 percent higher than when President Trump took office.

The average price of ground beef and coffee are hitting Americans particularly hard, as beef has risen to a record high of more than $7 per pound and coffee prices have spiked to nearly $10 per pound.

Health Care Costs

Following President Trump and congressional Republicans' refusal to extend enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits, average ACA premiums across the country have increased by more than 50 percent in 2026 compared to last year.

Average deductibles also surged to record highs, rising by more than $1,000.

Read the Virginia fact sheet here and the congressional district fact sheet here.

Sens. Warner and Kaine are fighting the economic consequences of President Trump’s policies for Virginia families. In February, the senators introduced the Tariff Refund Act of 2026, legislation that would require U.S. Customs and Border Patrol (CBP) to quickly refund Trump’s illegal tariffs and prioritize the interests of small businesses when doing so. Earlier this month, Warner and Kaine highlighted data showing how the president’s war of choice in Iran – which the senators are continuously fighting to bring to an end – has driven up gas costs in Virginia and across the country. Additionally, a year after Trump and Republicans’ budget megabill became law, the senators underscored the devastating impact the law has had on Virginia families. The senators will continue to press Trump and his administration to end the dangerous and expensive war in Iran, reverse course on their illegal tariffs, and focus on lowering costs for Americans.

title: ICYMI: In Phoenix, Kelly Packs Back-to-School Supplies with Teachers, Hosts Roundtable on Mentorship and Service
text:
Kelly heard from Arizona teachers and community leaders about the growing need for positive male role models and highlighted his bipartisan legislation to recruit more men into teaching, mentoring, and community service

In case you missed it, today Arizona Senator Mark Kelly joined teachers, coaches, mentors, and community leaders at Sandra Day O’Connor High School in Phoenix to assemble back-to-school supply packages for Arizona educators. He also led a roundtable discussion on strengthening communities through service and expanding opportunities for more men to become teachers, mentors, and volunteers and the need to create more opportunities for boys and young men to connect with positive role models.

Earlier this month, Kelly introduced a two-bill package—the Educators for America Act and the Building Community in America Act—to expand pathways for Americans to serve as teachers, mentors, and volunteers, with a focus on increasing the number of men participating.

During the discussion, Kelly heard from Arizona Teacher of the Year, Emmett Burnton, who shared that many boys are searching for identity and purpose but often struggle to find positive role models. Burnton described asking students to identify historical figures they related to, only to have some teenage boys break down because they didn’t know who they wanted to become. He also spoke about the growing influence of online communities filling the mentorship gap and the importance of educators helping students find purpose both inside and outside the classroom.

Kelly also heard from Michael, a Phoenix father who spoke about intentionally surrounding his 18-year-old son with positive role models through sports and music. He reflected that many young people today turn to social media for guidance instead of neighbors, coaches, and mentors, emphasizing that rebuilding strong communities starts with reconnecting young people to caring adults.

Elementary school educators also shared about the growing impact of social media on young students, including increased behavioral challenges and mental health concerns, reinforcing the need for trusted adults who can help young people navigate those pressures.

title: Kelly, Bipartisan Group of Arizona Delegation Members  Urge Trump to Reverse FEMA Disaster Aid Denial
text:
Today, Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), alongside Representatives Greg Stanton (D-AZ-04), Eli Crane (R-AZ-02), Andy Biggs (R-AZ-05), Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ-07), and Yassamin Ansari (D-AZ-03), called on the Administration to reverse its denial of a Major Disaster Declaration for Gila and Mohave Counties following catastrophic flooding that impacted the region in September 2025.

In a letter addressed to President Trump, Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Mullin, and Acting Federal Emergency Management Administration (FEMA) Administrator Fenton, the lawmakers demanded an explanation for this devastating decision, which prevents the approval of critically needed federal disaster funding to help communities recover from these tragic storms.

“Central Arizona experienced historic rainfall and catastrophic flooding between September 25 and 27, 2025, that decimated public infrastructure and forced more than 180 residents to seek emergency shelter. The storms destroyed entire neighborhoods in Globe, Miami, Claypool, Hayden, and Winkelman, and compromised access to essential services including potable water, power, and wastewater systems,” wrote the lawmakers.

FEMA initially denied Arizona’s request after preliminary estimates put total losses at over $33 million. Updated assessments have documented more than $100 million in damages, far exceeding both the original estimate and the state’s ability to recover on its own. Given these revised damage estimates, Governor Hobbs then appealed FEMA’s initial decision.

Last week, FEMA denied that appeal.

“As Gila and Mohave Counties continue rebuilding public infrastructure and preparing for the flooding risks that accompany each monsoon season, it is essential that affected communities have a clear understanding of how your decision was reached for both the original request and appeal,” continued the lawmakers.

The members are demanding a briefing and detailed written responses by August 7, 2026, pressing FEMA to explain how its decision was reached—including what damage assessments were considered, whether career staff’s technical recommendations were followed, how Arizona’s fiscal capacity was measured against verified losses, and whether the denial was based on the original or updated damage figures.

“Transparency throughout FEMA’s decision-making process is critical both for the communities recovering from these catastrophic floods and for state officials planning for future disasters,” concluded the lawmakers.

title: Kelly, Colleagues Press Hegseth on Inaccurate Iran War Casualty Reporting, Demand Transparency on Human Cost
text:
Senators: “This lack of transparency undermines confidence that military families and the American people are receiving a complete and accurate accounting of the sacrifices made by those serving in uniform.”

This week, Arizona senator, Navy combat veteran, and member of the Senate Armed Services Committee Mark Kelly joined Democratic senators in demanding a full and accurate accounting of all servicemembers who were killed, wounded, and injured in support or in connection with Operation Epic Fury.

In a letter to U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) Secretary Pete Hegseth; Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff, General Dan Caine; Commander of United States Central Command, Admiral Brad Cooper; and Under Secretary of Defense for Personnel and Readiness, Anthony Tata, the senators raised alarms about multiple inconsistencies between the Pentagon’s public casualty number and official statements. The senators pressed DoD to be transparent with the American people, servicemembers, and their families on the human cost of the ongoing war in Iran.

“The American people, Congress, service members, and their families are entitled to a full and accurate accounting of the human costs of war. The information currently available to the public suggests that the Department has not consistently provided timely and comprehensive public casualty reporting throughout the conflict,” wrote the senators.

While DoD has reported that the Pentagon’s Defense Casualty Analysis System (DCAS) is accurate and “regularly updated,” the senators raised inconsistencies both in overall casualty and injury reporting since the beginning of the conflict, and during the month of July. For example, on July 20th, DoD spokesman Sean Parnell publicly stated: “While nearly 100 service members were deemed to have some degree of injury since July 7, 2026, 96% have returned to duty.” These injuries, however, did not include total casualty count and July’s monthly casualty report. In the same report, DCAS listed 14 servicemembers killed, despite wide reporting of 18 service members killed as of July 20th, 2026. While the number of servicemembers killed has been updated as of July 23rd, these inconsistencies raise significant concerns about the DoD’s overall transparency and timely reporting.

“This lack of transparency undermines confidence that military families and the American people are receiving a complete and accurate accounting of the sacrifices made by those serving in uniform,” the senators continued.

The senators requested prompt, detailed responses from DoD by Thursday, July 30th, 2026, including an exact casualty breakdown, an explanation for the total and month-of-July reporting discrepancies, data on traumatic brain injuries, undisclosed attacks in Jordan, and an assessment of mass casualty response capabilities and overall readiness in the theater. They concluded their letter by emphasizing the importance of transparency to servicemembers, their families, and the American people.

“We appreciate your prompt attention to these questions and expect a timely and complete response. Our service members and their families deserve nothing less than a full and honest accounting of the costs of this war,” the senators concluded.

In addition to Senator Kelly, the letter was signed by Senators Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI).

Background:

Kelly has been outspoken about the war in Iran since it began, criticizing the administration for launching the operation without a clearly defined strategy, a coherent plan, or a viable exit strategy. He also joined ten Senate colleagues in filing a new wave of War Powers resolutions to force a Senate vote to end the war in Iran.

Most recently, Kelly spoke out on the human toll of the war, questioning how the administration would explain the deaths of American servicemembers to their families and what the war had actually accomplished.

title: Kelly, Raskin, Whitehouse Introduce Bill to Protect U.S. Elections, Crack Down on Corrupt Influence of Foreign Money
text:
From 1986 to 2020, foreign ownership of American stocks increased from 4 percent to 40 percent

Bicameral legislation would restore the votes and the voices of the American people against the reign of foreign interests

Today, Senators Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), alongside Representative Jamie Raskin (D-MD-08), introduced the bicameral Get Foreign Money Out of U.S. Elections Act to crack down on the corrupt influence of foreign money in American elections.

As foreign ownership in American companies skyrockets, this legislation seeks to close a major loophole that has allowed U.S. companies that are largely owned by foreign entities to pour unlimited sums of money into our elections.

This legislation builds on Kelly’s efforts to get corporate money out of American politics. In January, Kelly led a series of speeches on the Senate floor regarding the 16th anniversary of the Citizens United v. FEC decision, which allowed dark money into American Democracy. A year ago, Kelly reintroduced for the third time his Ban Corporate PACs Act to ban for-profit corporations from funding political campaigns and influencing elections.

“American elections should be decided by the people, not by foreign interests,”said Sen. Kelly. “This bill closes a dangerous loophole that allows foreign-owned corporations to spend money in our elections. It will strengthen our democracy and protect our elections.”

“The Roberts Court’s outrageous decision in Citizens United continues to spell disaster for American democracy, as it allows oligarchs and autocrats from around the world to wield their influence over our elections through corporate ownership and political interference,” said Rep. Raskin. “I’m introducing the Get Foreign Money Out of U.S. Elections Act with Senator Whitehouse to root out foreign corporate corruption of our politics and make sure our elections are going to be decided by the American people and not overseas oligarchs.”

“Thanks to the disastrous Citizens United decision, foreign actors can exploit the same corrupting dark money channels that allow unlimited corporate spending,”said Sen. Whitehouse. “We should get rid of the damned stuff entirely, but this bill would at least safeguard our democracy from foreign adversaries influencing American elections from the shadows.”

In the Senate, the bill is cosponsored by Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Bernie Sanders (D-VT), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Peter Welch (D-VT), Adam Schiff (D-CA), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), and Alex Padilla (D-CA).

Background:

Foreign nationals are buying stock in American companies at record rates. From 1986 to 2020, foreign ownership of American stocks increased tenfold from 4 percent to 40 percent. As foreign ownership of American corporations grows ever larger, we must legislate to make certain that foreign money is not entering our politics.

While current law bars individual foreign nationals from personally spending in U.S. elections, the 2010 Citizens United v. FEC decision enabled corporations to engage in unlimited political spending. This created a loophole that allows unlimited political spending by American-registered corporations that are foreign-owned, foreign-controlled or foreign-influenced. This bill closes that loophole while ensuring individuals living in the United States are not prevented from exercising their constitutional right to contribute to candidates.

This legislation is endorsed by Court Accountability; Center for American Progress (CAP); Citizens For Responsibility & Ethics in Washington (CREW); End Citizens United / Let America Vote Action Fund; Common Cause; Public Citizen; Free Speech For People; Alliance For Democracy; American Federation of State, County and Municipal Employees (AFSCME); Blue Haven Initiative; Citizen Action of New York; Clean Elections Texas; Communication Workers of America; DAWN; Fix Democracy First; Greenpeace USA; Indivisible Santa Fe; MarchOnHarrisburg; Michiganders for Fair & Transparent Elections; Money Out Voters In; National Voter Corps; NETWORK Lobby for Catholic Social Justice; Our Revolution; People For the American Way; People Power United; Represent Us San Diego; Secure Elections Network; Transparency International U.S.; United Church of Christ and Voices For Progress.

title: Kelly’s Bill to Designate Lunar Landing Day Honoring Apollo 11 Passes Senate Unanimously
text:
This week, the Senate unanimously passed the Lunar Landing Day Act, introduced by retired NASA astronaut and Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) and Senator Tim Sheehy (R-MT). The legislation designates July 20th as Lunar Landing Day to recognize America’s leadership in space exploration and science. Senators Jerry Moran (R-KS) and Maria Cantwell (D-WA) co-led the bill.

“On July 20th, 1969, American astronauts landed on the Moon for the first time. It’s one of our country’s greatest achievements,” said Kelly. “As NASA’s Artemis program prepares to take us back to the Moon, there’s no better time to make sure that legacy is never forgotten. Designating Lunar Landing Day will honor the courage and ingenuity that made Apollo 11 possible, inspire the next generation of explorers, and remind us what we can do as a nation when we all work together.”

“The history of the United States is made up of remarkable feats that expand the boundaries of what is believed to be possible. One such feat occurred on July 20, 1969, when American astronauts became the first humans to set foot on the Moon,” said Sheehy. “As we continue to strengthen America’s space superiority with further innovation and new missions, we remember this incredible moment as one of the greatest achievements of human discovery in history. It is only right that July 20th be designated Lunar Landing Day in observance of America’s space superiority, leadership in exploration, and the individuals who made it possible. I’m grateful to my colleagues for supporting this effort to recognize American greatness and inspire our next generation.”

“On July 20, 1969, the Apollo 11 moon landing demonstrated what America can accomplish through innovation, determination and leadership,” said Moran. “Designating July 20 as Lunar Landing Day honors one of our nation’s greatest achievements and the individuals who made it possible. As chairman of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee that funds NASA, I look forward to continuing to invest in America’s space program as we work to return Americans to the surface of the Moon once again, building on the legacy of the Apollo program and bolstering U.S. leadership in space exploration.”

Background:

On July 20th, 1969, American astronauts, scientists, and engineers accomplished the seemingly impossible when the Apollo 11 spaceflight landed humans on the Moon for the first time.

To recognize this incredible moment in history, the Lunar Landing Day Act designates July 20th as Lunar Landing Day by adding it to the list of patriotic and national observances established by Congress in law that set aside specific time periods to recognize, commemorate, and reflect on individuals, events, and moments of national significance.

This legislation encourages proclamations, activities, and educational efforts to commemorate the first successful landing of humans on the Moon on July 20th, 1969, and inspire the continued leadership of the United States in space exploration and science.

If the legislation is enacted, Lunar Landing Day would become the 49th patriotic and national observance. Existing observances include Constitution Day, Mother’s Day and Father’s Day, Memorial Day, Veterans Day, Wright Brothers Day, and Police Week. This legislation is supported by the Lunar Landing Day coalition.

title: Senator Kim Leads Senate Colleagues in Introducing Resolution to Uplift Disability Community and Honor 36 Years of the ADA
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Ahead of the 36th anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), Senator Andy Kim (D-NJ), member of the Senate Health, Education, Labor & Pensions (HELP) Committee, led a group of 29 Senate colleagues in introducing a resolution to honor the disability community, uplift the impact of the historic legislation, and call for continued commitment to increasing inclusivity and accessibility.

The Resolution recognizes: “The importance of independent living and economic self-sufficiency for individuals with disabilities made possible by the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 and calling to protect the right of individuals with disabilities to live in their own homes and communities.”

In the resolution, the Senators outline the ADA’s long-success ensuring individuals with disabilities have the right to live, work, and participate as members of their communities and receive necessary care and support through access to Medicaid home and community-based services. The Senators condemn a June 18th Department of Justice opinion that has since threatened this hard-won progress toward full integration of individuals with disabilities into society and commit to working to stop attempts to dismantle the ADA.

“The Americans with Disabilities Act represents the floor, not the ceiling, of efforts needed to dismantle barriers to full participation, equal opportunity, independent living, and economic self-sufficiency for individuals with disabilities,” reads the Resolution.

The resolution is cosponsored by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Angus King (I-ME), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Jack Reed (D-RI), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Christopher Van Hollen (D-MD), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Chris Coons (D-DE), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), John Fetterman (D-PA), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Patty Murray (D-WA), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Ed Markey (D-MA), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Chris Murphy (D-CT), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI).

36 years since the ADA was signed into law on July 26th, 1990:

More than 8,400,000 individuals receive home and community-based services through Medicaid;

individuals with disabilities are participating in the labor force at a rate of over 41 percent;

on average, it is 3 times less expensive to serve someone through home and community-based services relative to an institution; and

individuals returning to the community from institutions report improved life satisfaction, reduced unmet needs, and enhanced feelings of dignity.

The resolution builds on Senator Kim’s continued work to uplift the disability community in New Jersey and across the country. As a member of the Senate HELP Committee, the Senator has pushed against Department of Homeland Security Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr.’s cuts and actions at the agency that have threatened to leave the disability community without the resources or federal support they need. He continues to fight against the Trump administration’s assault on Medicaid on behalf of the roughly 200,000 New Jerseyans who rely on Medicaid for help with their disabilities and uplift the disability communities’ voice in Congress.

title: Senators Kim, Schiff, Lummis, Barrasso Introduce Bill to Protect Children Online through New Age Reporting Requirements
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Senators Andy Kim (D-NJ), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Cynthia Lummis (R-WY), and John Barrasso (R-WY) introduced the bipartisan Digital Age Assurance Act to protect children online by requiring operating system providers to collect and share users’ ages exclusively with app developers so they can block kids from accessing age-inappropriate content. The bill prioritizes protecting kids’ privacy with a number of provisions preventing kids’ data from being sold or transferred and banning targeted advertisement to children.

“Like most parents, I have a lot of anxiety about keeping my two boys safe from dangers online as they grow up in a world full of ever-evolving technology. We owe it to parents and kids to put guardrails in place before more harm is done. The Digital Age Assurance Act puts kids’ data privacy first as we make sure congress and tech companies do their part to make online spaces safer for our kids,”said Senator Kim.

“Parents deserve the peace of mind of knowing that when their children use the internet and digital applications, they are shielded from inappropriate and harmful content. And tech companies that host kids on their platforms must be held accountable for protecting young users,” said Senator Schiff. “That’s why I’m proud to work with Senators Kim, Lummis, and Barrasso on a comprehensive federal age-assurance framework that follows California’s important work in this space and ensures that the digital content kids see is age-appropriate and that their privacy is protected from invasive data collection. We have seen what happens when an entire generation of young people grow up without technological guardrails and are left vulnerable to cyberbullying, mental health threats, and more. California has been a leader in requiring online platforms to implement necessary safeguards, and it’s time Congress follow its lead in addressing this issue.”

“In Wyoming, we believe protecting our kids and protecting our freedoms go hand in hand, and this bill proves you don’t have to sacrifice one for the other,” said Senator Lummis. “By keeping government IDs and facial scans out of the equation, the Digital Age Assurance Act gives parents real protection for their children while giving platforms a trusted, privacy-protective way to know when those protections should apply.”

More kids are getting online, at earlier ages – with recent data finding that by age 2, 4 in 10 children have their own tablet; by age 4, more than half of children have their own tablet; and by age 8, nearly 1 in 4 children have their own cellphone. The Digital Age Assurance Act works to prioritize kids’ online safety while including substantive child privacy protection rules. Specifically, the bipartisan legislation would:

Establish a device-level age assurance framework requiring operating system providers to collect a user’s age during operating system account creation or from existing account holders,

Require operating systems to convert a user’s age into privacy-protective age brackets—under 13; ages 13–15; age 16; and age 17 or older—rather than sharing the user’s exact age or date of birth,

Create a secure, real-time operating system signal that applications, browsers, application stores, and covered websites must request and use as the primary indicator of a user’s age,

Permit signals to include age verification methods that minimize data disclosure, including the use of verifiable credentials and zero-knowledge proofs,

Require children under age 17 to link their operating system account to a parent or legal guardian account and allow the user or linked parent or guardian to view the child’s age bracket data,

Establish a process for resolving conflicting age information, including user notice, an opportunity to correct inaccurate information, and distribution of an updated age signal,

Prohibit developers and covered website operators from requesting more age information than the standardized signal or sharing age bracket data with third parties,

Impose data minimization requirements limiting the collection, retention, use, and combination of age-related information, including prohibitions on using age bracket data for profiling, engagement optimization, or targeted advertising,

Prohibit the transfer of children’s personal data to data brokers, while preserving contextual advertising that does not rely on personal data or behavioral profiling,

Establish enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General, including civil penalties of up to $2,500 per negligent violation and $7,500 per knowing or intentional violation, which may be multiplied by the number of children affected,

Include competition safeguards preventing operating system providers and application stores from imposing more restrictive age-related requirements on third-party applications or using age bracket data to disadvantage competitors, and

Create a national baseline that preempts only conflicting State requirements while preserving Federal or State laws that provide protections at least as strong as the Act.

The Digital Age Assurance Act is endorsed by: American Psychological Association, Mission Kids Child Advocacy Center, The Arc of New Jersey, Digital Defenders United, and New Jersey Children’s Alliance.

“Parents shouldn’t have to choose between letting their kids participate in the digital world and keeping them safe. That’s exactly the balance I set out to strike with California’s Digital Age Assurance Act — protecting children online without sacrificing their privacy,”said Assemblymember Buffy Wicks (D- CA). “I’m thrilled to see Congress build on California’s leadership with a bipartisan, privacy-first framework that empowers parents, protects children, and establishes a consistent national standard for age assurance. Parents deserve confidence. Kids deserve safety. Families should never have to sacrifice one for the other.”

title: Klobuchar, Smith Urge USPS to Protect Mail Service During Wildfires Impacting Northern Minnesota
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Tina Smith (D-MN) are urging the United States Postal Service (USPS) Postmaster General to provide Minnesota with the necessary resources and support for postal operations impacted by wildfires.

“We have heard from constituents who are concerned about mail delays resulting from the wildfires, and their ability to receive mail in the instance that they must evacuate,” wrote the Senators. “We urge you to ensure that Minnesota post offices receive the resources and support needed to maintain reliable service and communicate effectively with residents.”

The full letter is available here and below.

Dear Postmaster General Steiner:

We are writing regarding serious mail service concerns in Northeast Minnesota due to ongoing wildfires. We have heard from constituents who are concerned about mail delays resulting from the wildfires, and their ability to receive mail in the instance that they must evacuate. We urge you to ensure that Minnesota post offices receive the resources and support needed to maintain reliable service and communicate effectively with residents.

Minnesotans depend on the Postal Service for essential needs like medications, Social Security benefits, business mail, and paycheck that they rely on for their health and livelihoods. We appreciate the hard work of our postal workers who serve their communities and deliver the mail through extreme conditions and road closures.

To that end, we request answers to the following questions:

What is the U.S. Postal Service doing to address delivery issues affecting Minnesota communities affected by wildfires?

Do postal operations in Northeast Minnesota have sufficient resources to ensure reliable delivery?

How is the Postal Service communicating service impacts to customers, including those who have evacuated and need access to medications and other important deliveries?

Minnesotans depend on the Postal Service every day. We urge you to do everything you can to address these postal operations concerns, and ensure Minnesota post offices are able to reliably and safely serve Minnesotans during this emergency.

###

title: Lankford, Coons Introduce Bill to Expand Grant Opportunities for Rural Law Enforcement Officers
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — US Senators James Lankford (R-OK) and Chris Coons (D-DE) introduced the Training Rural Law Enforcement Officers Act of 2026, which would allow qualified nonprofit organizations and state government entities to use Department of Justice grant funding to provide training to small and rural law enforcement agencies at no cost to those agencies.

Nearly half of local police departments in the United States have fewer than 10 sworn officers, three out of four have fewer than two dozen, and eight out of 10 have fewer than 50. Federal law enforcement grants administered by the Department of Justice often carry complex application processes and extensive reporting requirements, and smaller agencies frequently skip applying altogether because they lack the staff and experience to navigate them.

“For too long, federal grant programs have felt out of reach for many small and rural law enforcement agencies,” said Lankford. “The grant process can be cumbersome and difficult to navigate, especially for a department with a handful of officers. Our bill fixes this by letting qualified nonprofits carry the paperwork and bring the training directly to small agencies at no cost to them. Small law enforcement agencies should not be cut off from federal grant dollars.”

“Every community, including those in places like rural southern Delaware, deserves well-trained law enforcement protection,” said Coons. “Rural police departments often have significantly less funding than they need to participate in modern training programs, and we should give them the tools they need to protect and serve their communities.”

“Far too often the brave men and women of our nation’s law enforcement community, especially those from smaller and rural departments, lack the necessary training to effectively and safely resolve incidents they routinely face in the course of their duties. There is an important need for the federal government to allow for law enforcement officers from small and rural departments to receive proper training for such incidents, both routine and often unfamiliar. The Training Rural Law Enforcement Officers Act of 2026 will help ensure that law enforcement personnel from smaller and rural departments will have access to the training so vitally important to helping ensure both a proper and effective response to critical incidents and as a result preserving law enforcement and civilian life and security alike. On behalf of the over 40,000 members of the National Tactical Officers Association, I strongly commend Sen. Lankford and Sen. Coons for bringing this important legislation forward,” said Thor Eells, Executive Director of the National Tactical Officers Association.

“On behalf of the Small and Rural Law Enforcement Executive’s Association, I thank Sen. Lankford and Sen. Coons for introducing this important legislation. The Training Rural Law Enforcement Officers Act of 2026 will significantly increase the access to critical training for smaller and rural law enforcement departments and agencies nationwide at no additional cost to the taxpayer. By expanding DOJ grant eligibility to validated nonprofit organizations to provide vital training to smaller and rural law enforcement agencies, it will ensure that needed training will be received by law enforcement officials nationwide irrespective of their department’s size or resources. This increased training will assist agencies and their respective communities to respond effectively, efficiently, and compassionately to the public they serve,” said Mike Brown, Executive Director of the Small and Rural Law Enforcement Executive’s Association.

Background

The Training Rural Law Enforcement Officers Act would allow qualified nonprofit organizations and state government entities to receive Department of Justice law enforcement training grants to deliver training at no cost to agencies with fewer than 50 sworn officers. Eligible training includes de-escalation, officer wellness, leadership development, victim-centered response to domestic violence, critical incident response and management, and evidence-based safety training for active shooter situations, safe handling of illicit drugs and precursor chemicals, rescue operations, and countering ambush attacks.

The bill also covers training for responding to calls involving people with mental health needs, substance use disorders, disabilities, veterans, vulnerable youth, victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, or trafficking, and people experiencing homelessness or living in poverty. In addition, the bill would allow two or more localities receiving Department of Justice grants under this program to pool their grants to contract with a qualified nonprofit for shared training.

You can view the full text of the bill HERE.

title: Luján, Blumenthal Introduce Bill to Strengthen Social Security
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.) joined U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.) in introducing the Social Security 2100 Act, legislation to increase Social Security benefits and make the critical system financially stable throughout the 21st Century. As our nation’s bedrock social insurance program, Social Security is the most important source of retirement income for 4 out of 5 seniors and provides vital protections for disabled workers and families who have lost a breadwinner.

“Social Security is a lifeline for thousands of New Mexicans. The Trump administration’s cuts and threats to the program are abandoning our seniors and people with disabilities,” said Senator Luján. “For nearly a century, Social Security has been the cornerstone of financial security for retirees and disabled individuals, ensuring that those who have worked and paid into the system receive the support they’ve earned. That’s why I’m joining my colleagues in introducing legislation to strengthen Social Security and protect it from Republican cuts.”

“Social Security is a promise that must be kept. The Trump Administration’s threats to Social Security and skyrocketing costs require common sense steps to expand benefits and ensure financial stability,” said Senator Blumenthal. “Bolstering Social Security guarantees all Americans a standard of living and protects the American dream.”

The Social Security 2100 Act is cosponsored in the Senate by U.S. Senators Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), and Tammy Duckworth (D-IL).

The legislation would increase benefits for current and new beneficiaries by eliminating the Social Security tax cap. Additionally, the bill would utilize an improved cost-of-living adjustment to more accurately take into account true costs incurred by seniors and implement a stronger minimum benefit, so an individual who works their whole life will not retire into poverty.

The bill also includes provisions to fight back against the Trump Administration’s attacks on the Social Security Administration (SSA), including undoing staffing cuts made by the Trump administration, blocking any future efforts by the Administration to close Social Security field offices, and preventing DOGE and political appointees from accessing sensitive data systems at SSA.

The full text of the bill can be found here.

title: Luján, Welch Bipartisan Bill to Support Next Generation of American Aviation Advances Out of Committee
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), a member of the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, joined U.S. Senators Peter Welch (D-Vt.) and U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.) in celebrating the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee’s advancement of their bipartisan bill, the Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act. The Senators’ legislation would improve the Federal Aviation Administration’s (FAA) type certification process for American Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) aircraft companies to help them succeed and cement the United States’ role as a global leader in aviation. This legislation is cosponsored by U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.).

An amended version of the Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act advanced out of Senate Commerce with bipartisan support. Updates to the bill reflect further technical assistance from the FAA and the acceptance of a modified amendment by Senator Ed Markey (D-Mass.) to give airline pilots a seat at the table.

“New Mexico is a strong leader in aviation technology, and this legislation will help ensure our state continues to shape the next generation of innovation,” said Senator Luján. “This bill will streamline and update the FAA certification processes, accelerate innovation, support new technologies, and strengthen U.S. global leadership in aviation. I’m proud to see this legislation advance and help keep the United States at the forefront of global aviation.”

“Building on generations of leadership in aviation, American companies are spearheading electric aircraft innovation. That includes companies like Vermont’s Beta Technologies, which completed its historic, first-ever electric flight last year in South Burlington. Ensuring the FAA certification process is safe, efficient, and more transparent for emerging AAM companies like Beta is critical to promoting aviation innovation,” said Senator Welch. “I’m thankful for the support of my colleagues on the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee, including my bipartisan co-lead Senator Budd, in helping this bill fly through to the Senate Floor to support American ingenuity, good-paying jobs in Vermont, and our global leadership in aviation.”

“By ensuring that the FAA prioritizes the certification of novel aircraft like eVTOLs, we can quickly incorporate innovative technology into the National Airspace System. I am glad that our common-sense efforts to usher in the next generation of advanced air mobility aircraft will soon be considered by the full Senate,” said Senator Budd.

Joining Senators Luján, Heinrich, Welch, and Budd as cosponsors of this legislation are Senators John Curtis (R-Utah), Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.), Jerry Moran (R-Kan.), Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Tim Sheehy (R-Mont.), and Todd Young (R-Ind.).

“The Committee passage today brings us one step closer to modernizing the FAA certification process for the next generation of aviation,” said Senator Curtis. “This bipartisan bill will provide greater clarity and accountability, helping American Advanced Air Mobility companies innovate, compete, and lead the world in the future of flight. I’m pleased to see it advance and look forward to its passage by the full Senate.”

“Streamlining the FAA’s type certification processes for advanced aviation technologies, such as advanced air mobility, is critical to bolstering America’s global leadership in aviation innovation,” said Senator Moran. “I appreciate the bipartisan support from my colleagues for this legislation, and I’m pleased by this step forward with its passage out of committee today. This legislation would support emerging aerospace technologies and strengthen the aviation industry in Kansas and across the country, and I look forward to its approval by the full Senate.”

“California companies are leading the world in developing the next generation of electric aircraft. I’m proud to see our bill advance to cut through red tape and streamline the FAA certification process, so we can maintain our competitive advantage and keep groundbreaking innovation here at home,” said Senator Padilla.

“As the birthplace of aviation, America must maintain dominance in this critical industry by streamlining outdated bureaucracy and allowing innovators to remain competitive through a transparent, consistent regulatory framework. The bipartisan Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act takes important steps to accomplish these ends, and I’m proud to see it advance out of the Commerce committee,” said Senator Sheehy.

“Advanced Air Mobility platforms will revolutionize the American economy. The Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act is a crucial step to securing American drone dominance. Our bill will provide much needed clarity and certainty as we seek to establish American leadership in these critical technologies and lay the groundwork for the future of air transportation. The Commerce Committee’s advancement of this bipartisan legislation marks an important step forward, and I look forward to seeing it pass the full Senate,” said Senator Young.

Advanced Air Mobility (AAM) technology is a novel collection of technologies that will allow new, innovative aircraft to integrate into our airspace system. Emerging U.S.-based AAM companies are also paving the way for new and innovative electric vertical take-off and landing (eVTOL) aircraft. Supporting the United States’ continued leadership in AAM technology development will boost economic growth in American communities across the country.

Since the introduction of the Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act, the Congressional Research Service (CRS) and the Government Accountability Office (GAO) have both released reports on the AAM certification process and actions that can be taken by Congress to promote aviation innovation.

Specifically, the Aviation Innovation and Global Competitiveness Act:

Establishes non-binding, standard expected timelines for the FAA’s type certification process for AAM aircraft for the Agency to respond to petitions for exemptions of aircraft type, and to develop means of compliance for aircraft outside of the existing types of AAM aircraft.

Sets transparent and reliable non-binding, standard expected ranges of time for the issue paper process, so that type certification applicants know how long reviews will take, reducing uncertainty and delays.

Provides the FAA Administration with the sole discretion to exclude safety-critical matters from established timelines to ensure airspace safety is paramount.

Directs the FAA to define when an issue paper is required in the certification process, while providing flexibility for the Agency on complex, safety issues.

Directs the FAA to account for performance-based rules in the certification process.

Directs the FAA to brief the relevant congressional committees on the status of implementing the certification regulations and managing workload.

Clarifies when the FAA can delegate routine compliance findings to qualified personnel, allowing Agency experts to focus on complex, safety-critical issues.

Updates delegation guidance for type certification to cover new and novel technologies related to AAM, including eVTOL aircraft.

U.S. Representative Troy E. Nehls (R-TX-22), Chair of the House Aviation Subcommittee; Rep. André Carson (D-IN-07), Ranking Member of the House Aviation Subcommittee; Rep. title: Senators Markey, Capito, Collins, Van Hollen Introduce Bill to Support Alzheimer’s Research
text:
Bill Text (PDF)

Washington (July 24, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), Ranking Member of the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Subcommittee on Primary Health and Retirement Security, along with Senators Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.V.), Susan Collins (R-Maine), and Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), introduced legislation to reauthorize the United States Postal Service (USPS) Alzheimer’s research stamp for an additional six years, allowing more funds to be raised for Alzheimer’s research at the National Institutes of Health (NIH).

Semipostal stamps are sold by the U.S. Postal Service and are priced above the cost of postage to raise funds for causes of public interest, as directed by Congress. The U.S. Postal Service first issued the Alzheimer’s semipostal stamp in 2017 and has since sold over 11 million stamps in support of Alzheimer’s research.

“My mother fought Alzheimer’s for thirteen years. My family’s story mirrors that of millions of Americans awaiting better treatments and a cure for this terrible disease,” said Senator Markey. “I am proud to lead the reauthorization of the Alzheimer’s semipostal stamp, which has raised almost $2 million for Alzheimer’s research. Every letter sent with an Alzheimer’s stamp offers hope to families, and gets us one step closer to a cure.”

“Reauthorizing the Alzheimer's semipostal stamp will both maintain a source of funding for critically important Alzheimer’s research and will also help honor the memory and courage of those who have faced this heartbreaking disease directly. I have long been dedicated to pursuing a cure for Alzheimer’s disease, and I’m proud to join my colleagues to continue this initiative through the USPS,” said Senator Capito.

“Alzheimer’s is one of the greatest public health challenges of our time, affecting more than seven million Americans, including more than 29,000 people in Maine,” said Senator Collins. “As a founder of the Alzheimer’s Task Force and Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, I recently secured a $100 million increase for Alzheimer’s disease and related dementias research, bringing total annual funding to nearly $4 billion. By allowing Americans to continue to purchase Alzheimer’s research stamps, this bipartisan legislation would build on that funding and support NIH’s efforts to combat this devastating disease.”

“Countless families in Maryland and across our country are facing the pain and loss that Alzheimer’s leaves in its wake. I’ve fought to increase investments in critical research on this disease, and the Alzheimer’s semipostal stamp is a key step towards building on those efforts. That’s why I worked to create this stamp, and why it’s important we pass this bipartisan bill to keep it in circulation for years to come as we continue our fight to defeat Alzheimer’s once and for all,” said Senator Van Hollen.

The Alzheimer’s semipostal stamp reauthorization is cosponsored by Senators Mark Warner (D-Va.), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-Miss.) Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Jim Justice (R-W.V.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.) and Kevin Cramer (R-N.D.).

The legislation is endorsed by Alzheimer’s Foundation of America, Alzheimer’s Association, Alzheimer’s Impact Movement, and Gerontological Society of America.

“The Alzheimer’s Foundation of America wholeheartedly supports the Alzheimer’s Semipostal Stamp Reauthorization Act and is grateful to Senator Markey, Senator Collins, Senator Van Hollen, and Senator Capito for introducing it,” said Charles J. Fuschillo, Jr., President and CEO of the Alzheimer’s Foundation of America. “Since its inception, the sale of over 11 million Alzheimer’s semipostal stamps raised crucial funds for Alzheimer’s disease research and heightened public awareness about a disease impacting more than 7 million Americans.”

“The Alzheimer’s Semipostal Stamp Reauthorization Act preserves a simple but powerful way for Americans to fund the search for treatments and, ultimately, a cure, while raising awareness of the disease with every letter sent. Every family living with Alzheimer’s knows what this disease takes — not just from the person diagnosed, but from everyone who loves them — and continued research funding is how we give future generations a different outcome than the one families face today,” said Robert Egge, Alzheimer’s Association Chief Public Policy Officer and AIM President. “We’re grateful to Senator Markey, Senator Collins, Senator Van Hollen, and Senator Capito for their bipartisan leadership on this bill and their continued commitment to the Alzheimer's and dementia community.”

Senator Markey, as founder and co-Chair of the Bipartisan Congressional Task Force on Alzheimer’s Disease, is a leader in the fight to find a cure for Alzheimer’s disease and to support family caregivers.

On July 15, Senator Markey applauded the Senate’s unanimous passage of the Older Americans Act (OAA) Reauthorization Act, which included provisions from the Senator’s “Caring for Caregivers” agenda including expanding respite care options for family caregivers to older adults who need long-term care. The OAA reauthorization also included provisions from Senator Markey’s Alleviating Barriers for Caregivers Act which requires federal agencies to help family caregivers access government support by improving processes, procedures, forms, and communications.

In April 2026, Senator Markey introduced a package of legislation during Earth Week, including bills to protect seniors by enabling safer and more resilient homes.

In 2025, Senator Markey reintroduced his “Caring for Caregivers” legislative agenda of six bills to support family caregivers’ economic, physical, and emotional health through financial literacy resources, expansion of peer support services and respite care, and access to medically tailored meals.

In 2024, Senator Markey was a lead of the NAPA Reauthorization Act and the Alzheimer’s Accountability and Investment Act(AAIA), which were both signed into law. In the House of Representatives, Markey co-authored the National Alzheimer’s Project Act (NAPA), which mandated the development of a first-ever comprehensive National Plan to Address Alzheimer’s Disease. The plan represented a historic commitment by the federal government to tackling the disease.
