title: Warner, Blackburn Introduce Legislation to Strengthen Cybersecurity in K-12 Schools
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner (D-VA), Vice Chair of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, and Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) reintroduced the Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act, bipartisan legislation to help schools defend against ransomware, data breaches, and other cyberattacks that can expose students’ information, disrupt classroom learning, and strain already limited school resources. Companion legislation was introduced in the House of Representatives by U.S. Reps. Doris Matsui (D-CA) and Zach Nunn (R-IA).

“As cyberattacks grow more frequent and sophisticated, it’s our responsibility as lawmakers to ensure our schools have the tools and resources needed to protect students, parents, educators, and their sensitive information from being compromised,” said Sen. Warner. “Schools should be focused on teaching young people – not worried about fending off ransomware attacks or recovering from cyber incidents. I’m proud to reintroduce this legislation that would help school districts strengthen their cyber defenses, improve coordination with federal experts, and better prepare for the growing threats facing classrooms across the country.”

“Cyberattacks continue to grow in size, frequency, and complexity in critical U.S. institutions, including in America’s schools,” said Sen. Blackburn. “We must ensure that our education sector is equipped to address these threats and keep students’ personal information private. This bipartisan and bicameral legislation will improve the cybersecurity tracking system for schools and provide them with necessary training resources and best practices for prevention.”

“When I thought about my own grandchildren going to school, I wanted what every parent and grandparent wants: for them to be safe and focused on learning,” said Rep. Matsui. “No family should have to worry that a cyberattack could expose a child’s personal information or disrupt their education. This bill gives schools the tools, training, and support they need to protect students’ data, help teachers keep classrooms running, and give administrators stronger resources to prevent and respond to cyberattacks.”

“As a 20-year Air Force intelligence officer and former White House National Security Council member, I’ve spent my whole career tracking threats like these,” said Rep. Nunn. “Now they’re hitting our classrooms — shutting schools down and putting Iowa students’ personal information in the wrong hands. No school should have to fight that alone. Our bipartisan bill gives K-12 schools across the country the backup they need to stop these attacks and protect their students.”

Cyberattacks targeting K-12 schools continue to grow in both frequency and sophistication, exposing sensitive student information, disrupting classroom learning, and forcing schools to divert limited resources away from educating students. According to the 2025 Center for Internet Security (CIS) K-12 Cybersecurity Report, 82% of more than 5,000 K-12 organizations experienced cyber threat impacts between July 2023 and December 2024, underscoring the growing challenge schools face as they rely more heavily on digital technologies.

Federal cybersecurity officials have repeatedly warned that schools remain targets for ransomware and other malicious cyber activity because they often operate with limited cybersecurity personnel and budgets while maintaining large amounts of sensitive data. The Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act would help schools better prepare for these threats by improving access to cybersecurity guidance and resources, strengthening national awareness of cyber incidents affecting schools, and expanding the tools and support available to help school systems.

Specifically, the Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act would:

Promote access to information by directing the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) Director to establish a Cybersecurity Information Exchange to disseminate information, best practices, and grant opportunities to improve cybersecurity.

Improve tracking of cyberattacks by establishing a Cybersecurity Incident Registry within CISA to track incidents of cyberattacks on elementary and secondary schools. Information submitted to the Registry is strictly voluntary and will help improve data collection to coordinate activities related to the nationwide monitoring of the incidence and financial impact of cyberattacks. The bill also directs CISA to make available on the School Cybersecurity Information Exchange an annual report relating to cyber incidents affecting elementary schools and secondary schools.

Provide K-12 cybersecurity capabilities by directing CISA to establish the K-12 Cybersecurity Technology Improvement Program to train schools on cyber threats and best practices, enhance cybersecurity protections of information systems, and install effective cybersecurity tools. This approach will capitalize on the existing services and expertise of organizations like MS-ISAC and others to ensure maximum impact of funds. The bill authorizes $10 million annually for fiscal years 2027 and 2028 to fund the Technology Improvement Program.

The National Principals Association, National Association of Elementary School Principals, Council of Chief State School Officers, National Association of State Chief Information Officers, State Educational Technology Directors Association, and Consortium for School Networking endorsed the legislation.

“Schools are increasingly at risk from cybersecurity threats. NAESP is proud to endorse the Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act, a bill which would give our members practical tools, information, and resources from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to help pre-K-8 school leaders protect student data and privacy and to avoid costly school disruptions,” said L. Earl Franks, Executive Director of the National Association of Elementary School Principals. “We commend Representatives Matsui and Nunn and Senators Blackburn and Warner for their bipartisan leadership on this critically important issue.”

“Cybersecurity remains one of the most urgent technology challenges facing K-12 schools. School districts face increasingly sophisticated cyber threats that can disrupt learning, compromise student and personnel data, and strain already limited technology resources,” said Keith Krueger, CEO of the Consortium for School Networking (CoSN). “CoSN strongly supports the bipartisan Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act because it will strengthen information sharing, improve understanding of the cyber threats facing schools, and expand access to the resources and expertise districts need to better protect their networks. We applaud the bill’s bicameral and bipartisan sponsors for their leadership on this important issue.”

“SETDA strongly supports the bipartisan Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act because it improves collaboration, increases visibility into cyber incidents affecting schools, and expands access to the tools and technical assistance states and districts need to protect students and critical education systems,” said Dorann Avey, SETDA Board Chair. “We commend Representative Matsui and Representative Nunn for their leadership and urge Congress to advance this vitally important legislation.”

The legislators previously introduced the Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act in 2023. In 2021, Sen. Warner urged the Biden administration to ensure that school systems across the country are equipped to fend off the growing number of cyberattacks targeting K-12 schools.

title: Welch and Blumenthal Warn that Trump’s Threats to Bomb Civilian Infrastructure in Iran Could Amount to War Crimes
text:
The Senators request information from Central Command about how CENTCOM ensures U.S. Forces in the Middle East abide by U.S. law prohibiting strikes against targets such as bridges or power plants for the sole purpose of terrorizing civilians

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Subcommittee on the Constitution, alongside U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Homeland Security & Governmental Affairs Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, expressed grave concern to U.S. Central Command (CENTCOM) that President Trump’s recent threats to bomb civilian infrastructure in Iran, including bridges and power plants, could amount to war crimes. In their letter to CENTCOM Commander Admiral Brad Cooper, the Senators seek clarification and answers about the United States’ commitment to ensuring forces under CENTCOM’s command abide by the domestic and international laws of war.

“As you know, intentionally targeting civilian infrastructure could amount to a war crime, prohibited by domestic and international law. The mere threat of such attacks may violate the law of war,” wrote the Senators. “The law of war prohibits attacks against civilian objects, indiscriminate attacks, and attacks expected to cause excessive harm to civilians in relation to the direct military advantage anticipated. The law of war also prohibits threats of violence to spread terror among the civilian population.”

The Senators highlighted that in determining that Russia had committed war crimes in Ukraine, the U.S. State Department specifically cited Russia’s attacks on Ukrainian critical infrastructure: “General Alexus G. Grynkewich, Commander of EUCOM and SACEUR, testified before the Senate Armed Services Committee that such Russian attacks on Ukrainian infrastructure, in addition to being unlawful, were strategically ineffective, noting ‘anytime you attack a civilian population, you usually end up finding that it just hardens their resolve.’”

The Senators concluded: “The U.S. military has a reputation—earned through the hard work and sacrifices of brave men and women who serve our nation— for honorable service and for upholding very high standards under the law of war. Not only is this a reflection of American values, but it is militarily effective. Targeting civilians undermines the mission, creating even more enemies while undermining our national security and damaging the global standing of the United States. Thank you for your service and for ensuring that CENTCOM forces uphold these values.”

The Senators requested answers to the following questions by July 30, 2026:

Are you legally responsible for any targeting decisions by commanders and personnel under your command? Do you consider CENTCOM officials signing off on targeting packages to be legally responsible for such decisions under the law of war?

Are officers under your command aware that under the doctrine of command responsibility they have a duty to ensure subordinate personnel are following the law of war, a duty to investigate potential war crimes, a duty to hold accountable those who commit them, and that dereliction of such duties would likely constitute a violation of the Uniform Code of Military Justice?

Will you ensure that forces under your command conduct a documented case-by-case analysis of the legality for each proposed target in Iran that could constitute civilian infrastructure, assessing whether such targets offer a concrete and direct military advantage and whether the expected harm to civilians is not excessive compared to that anticipated military advantage? And will you commit to maintaining the records of such analysis and providing them to the relevant Congressional committees, including on a classified basis, upon request?

Will you order an investigation of any significant civilian casualty events resulting from U.S. military actions in Iran?

Read and download the Senators’ full letter to U.S. Admiral Cooper.

title: Whitehouse, Wyden Demand Update on DOGE Infiltration of the Social Security Administration
text:
Trump put Americans’ sensitive private data at risk

Washington, DC – U.S. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and Ron Wyden (D-OR), the Ranking Member of the Senate Finance Committee, sent a letter to Social Security Administration (SSA) Commissioner Frank Bisignano urging the SSA to finally detail the now-defunct Department of Government Efficiency’s (DOGE) activities at the Social Security Administration amid public reporting and whistleblower declarations revealing that DOGE personnel received unauthorized access to American’s sensitive personal data.

“We write seeking meaningful transparency regarding the handling of various information security risks involving staff from the so-called Department of Government Efficiency at the Social Security Administration and to follow up on inadequate responses to prior Congressional inquiries on these matters,” wrote Whitehouse and Wyden. “Over the past fourteen months, we have repeatedly sought basic information about DOGE’s activities at SSA. Your responses have either been unresponsive or later disproved by SSA’s own admissions.”

Whitehouse, Wyden and Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) and Bernie Sanders (I-VT) first wrote to Commissioner Bisignano in November 2025 urging the SSA to take all appropriate steps to guarantee that DOGE’s actions did not American seniors exposed to identity theft, fraud, or other risks. In a later Department of Justice (DOJ) court filing, the federal government disclosed that DOGE staffers shared sensitive data on a third-party server – without the knowledge of SSA officials – and shared data with an outside political group. The Washington Post reported in March on a whistleblower disclosure claiming a DOGE employee copied a database of highly sensitive SSA data on a personal thumb drive to share with his new private sector employer.

“These admissions and whistleblower statements damage SSA’s decades-long history of protecting Americans’ sensitive information and discredit your past assurances to protect Americans’ data. It is long overdue you provide the American people a straight answer,” concluded the senators.

The DOGE infiltration of SSA and other administrative agencies posed substantial risks to Americans’ data and wellbeing. New reporting in the Washington Post found that at least two dozen former DOGE staffers remain embedded in the Trump administration, many of whom have been handed key national security or data security positions. Vulnerabilities and bugs left behind in these systems could put Americans at risk of getting scammed, hacked, or even spied on by foreign governments.

Last July, Whitehouse, Wyden, and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) introduced the Pick Up After Your DOGE Act, legislation requiring a comprehensive audit of federal agency computer systems and networks accessed by DOGE staff. Without a proper and total review of security vulnerabilities, the risk remains that Donald Trump’s Big Tech and AI allies are given unfettered access to a massive trove of Americans’ data by former DOGE employees to enrich themselves and undermine their competitors.

A PDF of the letter is available here and the text of the letter is below.

July 22, 2026

The Honorable Frank Bisignano

Commissioner

Social Security Administration

6401 Security Blvd.

Baltimore, MD 21235

Dear Commissioner Bisignano:

We write seeking meaningful transparency regarding the handling of various information security risks involving staff from the so-called Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) at the Social Security Administration (SSA) and to follow up on inadequate responses to prior Congressional inquiries on these matters.

Over the past fourteen months, we have repeatedly sought basic information about DOGE’s activities at SSA.[1] Your responses have either been unresponsive or later disproved by SSA’s own admissions.

During your confirmation hearing, you committed to Senator Whitehouse to conduct a total review of SSA’s databases and security protocols to ensure Americans’ data is protected. In November 2025, we wrote seeking an update on your promised audit of SSA’s systems for vulnerabilities left behind by DOGE.[2] Rather than providing the findings of an audit, your January 6, 2026 response simply offered the assurance that “SSA’s systems and data are secure and managed under strict security protocols, consistent with Federal and industry standards” and asserted that “neither the Numident database nor any of its data has been accessed, leaked, hacked, or shared in any unauthorized manner.”[3]

Your assurance lasted all of a few days. In a January 16 court filing – ten days later – the Department of Justice (DOJ) disclosed that DOGE employees at SSA failed to comply with a federal district court order and may have violated multiple federal and agency data privacy and security policies.[4] Specifically, DOGE employees at SSA shared data via Cloudflare – a third-party server that was not approved for Social Security data – without the knowledge of agency officials.[5] Additionally, a DOGE staffer transmitted an encrypted file that DHS believed to contain the names and addresses of approximately 1,000 individuals drawn from SSA systems to DOGE affiliates outside the agency.[6] To date, SSA has yet to determine with certainty what data was shared in either case.

Most disturbingly, DOJ disclosed in the court filing that a member of SSA’s DOGE team signed a “Voter Data Agreement,” in his capacity as an SSA employee, with a still unnamed political advocacy group that explicitly sought to use SSA data to challenge election results in certain states.[7] SSA rightly recognized the seriousness of this allegation, prompting two referrals to the Office of Special Counsel for possible Hatch Act violations.[8] However, despite repeated requests from Congress, SSA has refused to provide unredacted information related to these complaints, instead providing heavily redacted documents. SSA’s lack of transparency on this matter is made all the more concerning as President Trump continues to double down on dangerous election conspiracy theories heading into the November midterms.[9]

In March 2026, The Washington Post reported on a whistleblower complaint regarding a former DOGE software engineer who had unfettered access to two tightly restricted databases of Americans’ personal information. According to the complaint, the individual copied at least one of those databases onto a personal thumb drive and planned to upload the data to his new job’s databases for its own use.[10] This complaint follows a separate one filed in June 2025 by Charles Borges, SSA’s former chief data officer, who alleged that DOGE staff had uploaded a copy of the Numident database to a cloud environment lacking appropriate oversight.[11] We again wrote to you asking for information about your promised forensic audit of DOGE staff’s activity at the agency in March 2026, and again, your reply failed to respond to the inquiries made in our letter.[12]

These admissions and whistleblower statements damage SSA’s decades-long history of protecting Americans’ sensitive information and discredit your past assurances to protect Americans’ data. It is long overdue you provide the American people a straight answer. In light of the developments described above, we ask that you provide written responses to our outstanding questions we previously sent to you no later than July 31, 2026:

From our March 24, 2026 Letter:

Has SSA conducted a full forensic audit of all devices, accounts, and external transfer mechanisms—including thumb drives, personal email, Cloudflare, and other third-party services—used by DOGE personnel during their tenure at the agency? If so, please provide a copy of the audit report. If not, why not, and when will such an audit be completed?

Has SSA determined whether any of the data allegedly exfiltrated has been accessed, used, shared, or sold by the former DOGE employee or any third party? What steps is SSA taking to retrieve or contain that data?

Have you requested the U.S. Department of Justice to investigate the allegations made by the whistleblower? If not, why not?

From our November 21, 2025 Letter:

We respectfully ask that you provide:

An update on your review of SSA databases and IT systems;

A description of any vulnerabilities, breaches, or irregularities that audit has revealed;

The steps SSA has taken to mitigate any risks created by DOGE’s activities; and

A timeline for completing any outstanding reviews or corrective actions.

We appreciate your attention to these matters and look forward to a substantive response to each of the questions above.

###

[1] Letter from Senator Gillibrand et al. to Acting Commissioner Dudek (April 8, 2025); Letter from Senator Warren et al. to Acting Commissioner Dudek (April 23, 2025); Letter from Senator Gillibrand et al. to Commissioner Bisignano (June 23, 2025); Letter from Senator Whitehouse et al. to Commissioner Bisignano (November 21, 2025).

[2] Letter from Senator Whitehouse et al. to Commissioner Bisignano (November 21, 2025).

[3] Letter from Commissioner Bisignano to Senator Whitehouse et al. (January 6, 2026).

[4] Notice of Corrections to the Record at 5, AFSCME v. Social Security Administration, No. 25-cv-00596-ELH (D. Md. Jan. 16, 2026), https://s3.documentcloud.org/documents/26496273/doge.pdf.

[5] Id at 6.

[6] Id at 3.

title: Wyden, Colleagues Demand FTC Reject X’s Petition to Evade Privacy Obligations
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ron Wyden said today he has joined Senate colleagues to urge the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to reject X’s petition to end the company’s privacy responsibilities under a unanimously approved 2022 order.

In its petition, X makes the extraordinary and baseless claim that rebranding Twitter as X frees the company from the privacy obligations it inherited. Beyond this claim, X’s other arguments that the order’s compliance is too costly, the company should be trusted to self-regulate, and ending the obligations under this order would serve the public interest in the American AI race are similarly frivolous. The senators therefore call for the FTC to reject X’s self-serving attempt to evade its legal responsibilities.

“The 2022 order defines ‘Respondent’ to include Twitter’s ‘successors and assigns,’ and its carve-out for genuinely distinct businesses applies only to entities that do not ‘collect, maintain, use, disclose, access, or provide access to’ data that previously enabled Twitter’s services — a condition X plainly does not meet,” the lawmakers wrote FTC Chairman Andrew Ferguson. “A name change and new leadership do not undo that legal continuity. If they did, any company could escape an FTC order simply by merging with a new entity or changing its name. The Commission should require X to comply with the 2022 order it inherited.”

The lawmakers continued, “X’s claim that compliance with the 2022 order is too costly rings hollow given the company’s scale … Musk, the company’s owner, is the richest person in the world, with sufficient personal wealth to support the company. More importantly, independent privacy and security oversight is not an optional expense to be cut when it becomes inconvenient. A company cannot earn early release from a privacy order simply by saying that compliance costs money.”

The letter was led by U.S. Senator Edward J. Markey, D-Mass. In addition to Wyden, the letter was signed by U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn.

title: Wyden Leads Congressional Democrats in Fifth Circuit Fight to Protect Mifepristone Access, Women’s Health Care
text:
More than 250 House and Senate Democrats filed an amicus brief to the Fifth Circuit arguing that mifepristone has undergone a rigorous FDA approval process and has repeatedly been found to be safe and effective.

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Ron Wyden said today he is leading Senate and House Democrats in filing an amicus brief pushing back against Louisiana’s attempt to reinstate the in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone that would restrict critical access for patients in Oregon and across the nation.

Following the Supreme Court’s stay of the Fifth Circuit Court of Appeals’ nationwide ban on telehealth access to mifepristone, Louisiana v. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) went back to the Fifth Circuit. Louisiana is seeking a ruling that would force the FDA to reinstate the in-person dispensing requirement nationwide for mifepristone—a safe and effective abortion medication that has been FDA-approved since 2000. This medically unnecessary move would end patient access to mifepristone through telemedicine, the method through which more than 1 in 4 women receive their care across the country. The ruling would also remove patients’ ability to get mifepristone directly from their pharmacy, forcing them to find a provider that dispenses the medication.

“For more than a quarter century, FDA has repeatedly and consistently affirmed that mifepristone is safe. Over seven million patients in the U.S. have safely used mifepristone. And as with other drugs, FDA continues to monitor the post-marketing safety data on mifepristone—data confirming that mifepristone is safe without regard to how it is dispensed,” the members wrote.

The lawmakers emphasized that the in-person dispensing requirement was eliminated in 2021, prior to the Dobbs v. Jackson Women’s Health Organization decision of 2022, and not in response to the Supreme Court’s decision.

“The in-person dispensing requirement was first suspended by a court in 2020 and later eliminated altogether by the FDA in 2021, before Dobbs came down,” the members wrote in their brief. “Louisiana knows these facts but continues to make this spurious claim in its attempt to reimpose an unnecessary burden on all Americans, even residents of states that protect abortion. Decades after FDA’s initial approval of mifepristone and years after the in-person dispensing requirement was eliminated, Louisiana now seeks to re-impose this onerous nationwide restriction on all Americans.”

“Granting such relief would undermine the science-based statutory framework Congress requires and threatens patient access to reproductive health care,” the lawmakers continued. “As has been well documented, many Americans in states where abortion is legal live far from any reproductive health care provider. Reinstating an in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone exacerbates an already significant reproductive health crisis by limiting access to the most common method of early abortion.”

Louisiana’s request for a stay of FDA’s 2023 rule would result in the reinstatement of the in-person dispensing requirement for mifepristone nationwide—and if granted, would have no basis in law, and would threaten the congressionally-mandated evidence-based process for drug regulation. The court overturning this decision not only limits who can receive this vital and life-saving medication, putting lives at risk, but it also undermines the longstanding, congressionally mandated, and evidence-based decision-making process at the FDA. The lawmakers argue that the Fifth Circuit should deny the stay, protecting telehealth and pharmacy access to mifepristone.

Wyden has been a strong advocate for mifepristone and preserving access to essential health care. In 1990, Wyden chaired the first-ever congressional hearing on mifepristone, launching decades of federal advocacy to ensure access to the medication remained grounded in scientific evidence. Wyden actively fought early FDA import alerts that restricted research on the drug and introduced legislation to lift those barriers prior to its ultimate federal approval in 2000. Following recent legal rulings aimed at restricting access, Wyden delivered Senate floor remarks calling on executive agencies to protect nationwide availability and defend the drug's proven safety record. He has continued to lead congressional colleagues in filing amicus briefs to uphold the FDA's evidence-based regulatory authority and preserve access to reproductive health care across the country.

The amicus brief was led by Wyden, U.S. Senator Patty Murray, D-Wash., Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, D-N.Y., House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., and U.S. Representatives Katherine Clark, D-Mass., Frank Pallone Jr., D-N.J., Diana DeGette, D-Colo., Jamie Raskin, D-Md., and Ayanna Pressley, D-Mass. The brief was signed by all 47 Democratic U.S. Senators and 212 U.S. Representatives.

title: Young, Colleagues Urge Sanctions on China’s Illegal, Unreported, and Unregulated Fishing Fleet
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Todd Young (R-Ind.) and a group of Senate colleagues sent a bipartisan letter to U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent urging the administration to crack down on China’s illegal fishing practices, which undermine international law, threaten global fish stocks, and harm American fisherman.

In the letter, the senators outline a strategy to target China’s distant-water fishing fleet by sanctioning key support vessels that enable illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing. Their letter identifies 29 currently unsanctioned vessels that they argue should be subject to U.S. sanctions.

“China’s distant water fishing fleet continues to disrupt global and regional fishing economies,” said Senator Young. “Through overfishing and illegal incursions into foreign waters, China seeks to undermine the global fishing industry until there is nothing left. The United States must take steps to combat these activities and promote American fishing practices, which remain the gold standard for sustainable fishing.”

In addition to Senator Young, the letter is signed by Senators Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Tom Cotton (R-Ark.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), Rick Scott (R-Fla.) and Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.).

Full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Secretary Bessent:

The People’s Republic of China (PRC) and Chinese Communist Party (CCP) maintain a distant water fishing (DWF) fleet of between 2,000 and 16,000 vessels, which they direct to engage in illegal, unreported, and unregulated (IUU) fishing at a scale that constitutes ecocide conducted via gross human rights abuses.

We write to urge you to counter Chinese IUU fishing by identifying the support vessels that enable the Chinese DWF fleet – reefer carriers, bunker tankers, and floating bases – and adding them on the Specially Designated Nationals and Blocked Persons List (SDN List) maintained by the U.S. Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), as well as adding known owners and beneficial owners. We have attached a list of 29 such vessels, and we reaffirm our commitment to providing you with the resources and authorities necessary to designate them and enforce such designations.

The Chinese DWF fleet is subsidized with billions of dollars from the PRC, and between 2022 and 2024 it accounted for 44 percent of global fishing across 110 million hours in the waters of 90 countries. Chinese ships are regularly caught having killed hundreds of critically endangered animals and thousands of illegally caught sharks, whales, and dolphins, and they have destroyed tens of thousands of acres of coral reefs. The fleet exploits forced laborers, who are subjected to physical abuse, malnutrition, overwork, and withheld pay, in some cases spanning years.

There is a bipartisan, bicameral, and interbranch consensus across the United States government that Chinese IUU fishing poses an acute threat to the U.S. and our allies, and that it should be countered. In July 2025, Congress passed and the President signed into law H.R. 1, which appropriated to the Coast Guard $170 million for maritime domain awareness, technology which is critical to identifying and tracking Chinese IUU fishing vessels. In December, Acting PDAS for Ocean, Fisheries, and Polar Affairs Perry testified to the Senate Africa Subcommittee that China uses its fleet to “exploit [African] fisheries resources at all levels of the ecosystem and create ecocide.”

In January, the House Select Committee on China released a report on Chinese IUU that concluded the CCP “wields the [DWF] fleet with the precision of a military command, fusing fishing vessels, state subsidies, processing plants, and overseas infrastructure into a unified geopolitical weapon.” In March, the Senate passed the Fighting Foreign Illegal Seafood Harvests Act, which would establish as the policy of the United States “to continue the broadeffort across the Federal Government to counter IUU fishing, including any potential links to forced labor, human trafficking, and other threats to maritime security.”

The United States has already imposed sanctions on persons and vessels involved in Chinese IUU fishing. In December 2022, OFAC sanctioned two Chinese individuals and the networks they controlled pursuant to Executive Order (EO) 13818, which targets perpetrators of serious human rights abuse and corruption. The action included adding over 150 vessels to the SDN List.

Such designations are normally crippling for vessels and their owners. Ships require flagging, financing, insurance, fuel, port services, customers to purchase their goods, and crews which themselves require food and medical care, and they have difficulty evading sanctions because they can be tracked through their automatic identification systems (AIS). DWF fishing vessels are in theory particularly vulnerable: they require significant fuel for long-distance travel, their crews operate in hazardous conditions and are disproportionately subject to illness and injury, and they must offload their catches in a port each time their holds are filled. Designated vessels find it extremely difficult, and in some cases functionally impossible, to secure those goods, services, and financing.

However, the CCP has developed an elaborate hub-and-spoke logistical network that both makes their fishing vessels more efficient and blunts the application of sanctions to those vessels. Chinese IUU fishing fleets travel with support ships that insulate their fishing boats from sanctions. Their fishing vessels transship catches to refrigerated reefers which then sell in bulk during port trips, enabling the fishing boats both to avoid ports and clear out their holds for further fishing.

Tankers provide those vessels with fuel and floating bases provide their crews with medical care and other services. Meanwhile they turn off their AIS, stymying efforts both to detect sanctionable activity and to track already-sanctioned vessels. The network allows Chinese IUU fishing fleets to operate at sea indefinitely, with the fishing boats able to conduct activities without ever having to go to ports where they would otherwise be vulnerable to sanctions.

In any case, the sheer scale of the Chinese IUU fishing fleet renders untenable any effort to counter the fleet’s activities by designating IUU fishing boats. The supply ships themselves – however – are in fact acutely vulnerable to American sanctions. They require access to ports and customers. They cannot indefinitely turn off their AIS, if only so they can be found by Chinese fishing vessels requiring their services, and must also conduct repeated rendezvous and enter ports. They are relatively limited in number, according to the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party. 55 reefers accounted for nearly half of all transshipment events recorded during 2024 and 10 tankers represented 61 percent of all global bunkering activity.

Those supply ships participate in the human rights abuses and corruption that enable the Chinese IUU fishing fleet and should be sanctioned pursuant to E.O. 13818. Once placed on the SDN List, supply vessels will find it difficult to secure port services or insurance, and reefers specifically will have trouble conducting transactions for selling their cargo. Anyone linked to the vessels, including through beneficial ownership, will be exposed to reputational and financial crime risks. The vessels would switch from being assets to liabilities, greatly complicating the ability of the CCP to continue their IUU fishing activities.

title: Rep. Young Kim Questions State Department Officials on U.N. Reform, Countering CCP Influence
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, Congresswoman Young Kim (CA-40) participated in a House Foreign Affairs Committee hearing titled “United Nations Accountability and Reform: Advancing an America First Foreign Policy Through Strategic Diplomacy and Burden Sharing at the United Nations.”

Ambassador Mike Waltz, U.S. Representative to the United Nations, and Ambassador Jeff Bartos, U.S. Representative for United Nations Management and Reform, testified on efforts to reduce waste at the U.N. and ensure American taxpayer contributions deliver results.

During the hearing, Rep. Kim applauded U.S. leadership in delivering more than one billion dollars in savings at the United Nations and raised concerns about the Chinese Communist Party’s growing influence at the United Nations while seeking an update on efforts to expand Taiwan’s meaningful participation in international organizations. She warned that when the United States and its allies cede leadership in global standard-setting bodies, adversaries like China fill the vacuum and shape the rules to their advantage.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON MS NOW: “IT’S TIME TO MOVE THE COUNTRY IN A DIFFERENT DIRECTION”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on MS NOW’s PoliticsNation, where he reiterated that nearly 100 days until the midterm elections, Democrats are united in our commitment to lowering the high cost of living, fixing our broken healthcare system and holding crooks accountable.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Joining me now, the Congressman from Brooklyn, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Thanks very much for being with us this weekend. I want to start with the news unfolding today in Maine, where Democrats have chosen Troy Jackson to run against Senator Susan Collins in November. My first question is, are you satisfied that Democrats are now in a better position to win the seat in Maine and possibly retake the Senate in the fall?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, good afternoon, Rev. Great to be with you. First of all, I’m very confident that we have extraordinary candidates on the House side and we’re on our way to taking back control of the House of Representatives. And what we see on the Senate side, and I think Maine today will complete that picture, is a strong set of candidates to make the Senate competitive, which no one thought was the case just about a year ago. The Maine Democrats seem to have rallied behind Troy Jackson, and I expect that they’ll be unified moving forward and put up a very good fight against Susan Collins, who clearly—it’s time for her to go.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, Democrats chose to hold Graham Platner accountable, and they have switched their candidates in Maine in the middle of a must-win race for the party. But take a listen to your House colleague, Speaker Mike Johnson, when asked about how he intends to handle allegations against two Members of his party on Tuesday.

RECORDING OF SPEAKER JOHNSON: The key word there is allegation. We have a process here—the House Ethics Committee works on those things. If allegations are made, they work through a process. So I’m not in the business of commenting on investigations as they are in process. And we’ll see how it shakes out. That’s how this always works. And, by the way, it’s done for Rs and Ds on both sides of the aisle.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, we should note both Representatives Miller and Mills deny the accusations against them, but isn’t it the case that the two parties hold their Members to a very different ethical standard?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think, as Democrats, we’re going to continue to try to uphold an American standard of decency and fairness and ensuring, of course, that people get their due process in an administrative or legal or congressional process, while at the same time trying to uplift American values. And what Republicans are trying to do, of course, is just take a partisan approach to everything, and that’s just the reality. We’ve seen it over the last 18 months. And at the end of the day, Republicans are just all consumed with power, and not power to actually make life more affordable for the American people in the midst of a crisis where life is too expensive, they’re continuing to just lean into lifting up the wealthy, the well-off, and the well-connected.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Let’s switch gears to the House. As we mentioned, we’re closing in on 100 days until the election, and Democrats are honing their message and laying out their priorities. You’ve said the first bill of a new Democratic session would be focused on affordability. This week, Democrats in the House passed another resolution to halt U.S. military action in Iran, gaining four Republican votes in the process. You’ve called the Trump administration’s strategy with Iran, quote, ‘Operation Epic Failure,’ end of quote. Are voters responding to what you’re doing and saying, and are you confident your party can regain power in Congress this fall?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re definitely confident that we’re on the right side of the American people in terms of our commitment to drive down the high cost of living, to make sure that we actually deliver affordable healthcare for every single American and that we hold the crooks accountable in the midst of a level of corruption, the likes of which have never been seen in America’s 250-year history. Our agenda, of course, begins aggressively with addressing the affordability crisis. And we’re committed to lowering the cost of groceries, the cost of gas, the cost of housing, the cost of everyday goods, the things that are making life untenable for far too many Americans. We believe when you work hard and play by the rules in this country, you should be able to live a middle-class life, an affordable life, live the good life. That’s not the case right now. Far too many Americans are drowning in this failed Trump economy, and it’s time to move the country in a different direction.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Fox News polling out this week shows nearly 40% of voters want dramatic change right now, and Democrats are favored over Republicans on nearly every issue, including the economy and foreign policy. Republicans hold only slight edges on national security and crime, yet with their poll numbers plunging, Trump and Republicans have been focused on rigging the electorate in their favor. Tomorrow we’re going to be talking to your colleague Congressman Cleo Fields, who announced he will not be seeking re-election this week, after his majority-Black Louisiana district was eliminated in the wake of the Supreme Court Callais decision. You’ve been very clear that you view what happened to Representative Fields a form of voter suppression. A gut check question now: how deeply will this country be impacted in November by what Republicans and the courts have done to Black representation, and how are Democrats working to overcome it?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Congressman Cleo Fields will be deeply missed. We’re going to work closely over the next six or so months so he can finish out his term strong. He’s a tremendous champion for the people of Louisiana, and it’s a shame that his seat has been carved up as a result of the unprecedented attack on the Voting Rights Act by the Supreme Court, and then the Jim Crow-like tactics that have been unleashed in states like Louisiana as well as Tennessee and Alabama, signed off on by the United States Supreme Court, which is why we believe dramatic change is necessary in a whole host of areas—that’s dramatic campaign finance reform, dramatic electoral reform, including, of course, passage of the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act so we can end the era of voter suppression in the United States of America once and for all. And certainly we need dramatic Supreme Court reform because this right-wing Supreme Court extremist majority is totally out of control and they need to be reigned in.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, President Trump and his allies continue to push for the so-called SAVE Act that includes many of the President’s vote supressing—suppression priorities and, like, voter ID. This week, House Republicans tucked elements of the SAVE Act into a budget reconciliation bill that passed along party lines, that Senate Majority Leader John Thune has said will not pass the Senate in its current form. Are you concerned Republicans could still find a way to push through parts of the SAVE Act before the midterms, and what are the Democrats doing to counter this?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’re going to continue to stand strong against the voter suppression efforts of the Republican Party led by Donald Trump. Clearly, they have no agenda that they feel comfortable in selling to the American people because they’ve broken all their promises, including promising not to start forever wars in the Middle East, but to stop them. And then Donald Trump and Republicans turned around—they’ve gotten us involved in this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran. That, of course, has skyrocketed gas prices through the roof and are hurting everyday Americans day after day after day. And so, from our standpoint, we know that Republicans are going to try to rig the midterm elections. They’re doing it in real time. We’ve got to stop them from jamming this voter suppression bill down the throats of the American people. Democrats have been strong in the House and in the Senate in holding the line. We have to continue to do that. At the same period of time, we’re putting together the largest voter protection effort in the history of the country, working, of course, with Senate Democrats, House Democrats, the Democratic Governors Association, the Attorneys General Association on the Democratic side, the Democratic Secretaries of State, as well as civil society, which includes the faith community, civil rights groups, democracy protection groups, civil liberties groups, good government groups as well as organized labor. And together I’m confident we’re going to ensure that there’s a free and fair election in November.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Last question. I’m out of time, but I must ask you. Your Caucus is heading into an August recess with momentum toward the election but plenty of uncertainty. We don’t know what Trump and Republicans will do, how far they will go to try and undermine our democracy as they cling to power. We don’t know how tensions will play out between progressives and centrists inside the Democratic Party. So what’s your message to Members and to the candidates out there as we enter this critical stretch, the final 100 days?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Important for all of us to continue to keep the main thing the main thing. And that’s our commitment to fighting for an affordable America. Wherever one falls on the Democratic spectrum, we know that everyone is unified behind that fight. We want to lower the high cost of living for the American people. We want to make sure that there’s affordable healthcare for every single American. And we’re all committed to holding the crooks accountable and dealing with the rampant corruption that is undermining the Congress’ ability and our government’s ability to actually deliver for hardworking American taxpayers. Let’s keep the main thing the main thing. Let’s run through the finish line over the next 100 days or so. And then together, we can end this national nightmare, take back control of the Congress and continue our country’s march toward a more perfect union.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Well, thank you for being with us as we start the 100-day countdown to the election, Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: Rep. Menefee Joins Congressional Leaders in Houston to Demand Answers in the Killing of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Yesterday, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) joined Congresswoman Sylvia Garcia (TX-29), Congressman Adriano Espaillat (NY-13), Chair of the Congressional Hispanic Caucus, Congressman Bennie G. Thompson (MS-02), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Homeland Security and 7 additional Members of Congress from across the country for a congressional hearing in Houston examining the fatal shooting of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo by U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE).

Held at the Harris County Commissioners Court, right in Congressman Menefee’s district, the hearing brought Lorenzo's family, local officials, faith leaders, legal experts, and community advocates together to examine ICE's use of deadly force, the agency's lack of transparency, and the urgent need for accountability following Lorenzo's death.

Congressman Menefee questioned Harris County District Attorney Sean Teare about ICE agents' failure to wear body cameras during the fatal encounter, highlighting what both agreed is a striking departure from modern law enforcement practices.

Rep. Menefee: "Throughout your career, you've worked on thousands of cases involving local law enforcement, correct?"

District Attorney Sean Teare: "Yes."

Rep. Menefee: "It's standard practice in 2026 for law enforcement officers on the street to wear body cameras, correct?"

District Attorney Sean Teare: "Congressman, you and I have been in this very room talking about things like this. We have 86 law enforcement agencies that operate in Harris County alone. The only one that doesn't have body cameras is ICE."

Following the hearing, Congressman Menefee condemned the agency's lack of accountability.

"This is an agency that needs to be torn down to the studs and rebuilt into one that enforces immigration law while recognizing the dignity of every person it encounters," said Congressman Menefee. "We all know that won't happen under this Administration, and it won't happen under this Republican-controlled Congress."

Congressman Menefee also emphasized that meaningful oversight will require a change in congressional leadership, stating that if Democrats regain control of the U.S. House of Representatives after the November midterm elections, one of their first priorities will be conducting a full congressional investigation into the death of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and other deaths involving ICE agents since President Donald Trump returned to office in 2025.

Since Lorenzo's death, Congressman Menefee has repeatedly called for the immediate release of all unedited evidence, including body camera and dash camera footage, demanded an independent investigation into the shooting, and pushed for transparency and accountability for Lorenzo's family and the Houston community.

title: Capito, Justice, Miller, Moore Support Major Disaster Declaration Request for West Virginia
text:
CHARLESTON, W.Va. – Today, U.S. Senators Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) and Jim Justice (R-W.Va.), and U.S. Representatives Carol Miller (R-W.Va.-01) and Riley Moore (R-W.Va.-02) joined together in sending a letter to President Donald J. Trump and FEMA Region 3 Regional Administrator Andre McCoy in support of Governor Patrick Morrisey's (R-W.Va.) request for an expedited Major Disaster Declaration for the State of West Virginia. The request follows the severe storms, tornadoes, and flooding across the state beginning last Tuesday, July 21, and would provide support for Barbour, Doddridge, Harrison, Lewis, Pleasants, Ritchie, and Upshur Counties.

“As members of the West Virginia Congressional Delegation, we write in strong support of Governor Patrick Morrisey's request for an expedited Major Disaster Declaration for the State of West Virginia following the severe storms, straight-line winds, tornadoes, flash flooding, and landslides that struck our state beginning on July 21, 2026,” the West Virginia Congressional Delegation wrote.

“Our state and local officials responded immediately and decisively. First responders, emergency management personnel, law enforcement officers, members of the West Virginia National Guard, volunteer organizations, faith-based groups, and countless neighbors have worked tirelessly to protect lives and support recovery efforts. Despite these extraordinary efforts, the scope of this disaster exceeds the capacity of local governments and the State of West Virginia to recover without federal assistance,” the West Virginia Congressional Delegation continued.

“Thank you for your consideration of this request and for your continued support of the people of West Virginia. We stand ready to work with your Administration, FEMA, and state and local officials to ensure these communities receive the assistance they need to recover and rebuild,” the West Virginia Congressional Delegation concluded.

Full text of the letter can be found hereand below:

Dear Mr. President and Regional Administrator McCoy,

As members of the West Virginia Congressional Delegation, we write in strong support of Governor Patrick Morrisey's request for an expedited Major Disaster Declaration for the State of West Virginia following the severe storms, straight-line winds, tornadoes, flash flooding, and landslides that struck our state beginning on July 21, 2026.

This disaster has left a profound impact on communities across Barbour, Doddridge, Harrison, Lewis, Pleasants, Ritchie, and Upshur Counties. Homes have been destroyed or rendered uninhabitable, roads and bridges have been damaged, businesses have been disrupted, and critical public infrastructure has sustained significant losses. Tragically, two West Virginians lost their lives, and countless others are now facing the difficult task of rebuilding their homes and their lives.

Our state and local officials responded immediately and decisively. First responders, emergency management personnel, law enforcement officers, members of the West Virginia National Guard, volunteer organizations, faith-based groups, and countless neighbors have worked tirelessly to protect lives and support recovery efforts. Despite these extraordinary efforts, the scope of this disaster exceeds the capacity of local governments and the State of West Virginia to recover without federal assistance. Joint Damage Assessments in Lewis and Upshur Counties alone highlight the catastrophic nature of this event, revealing 33 homes destroyed, 91 with major damage, 235 with minor damage, and 182 otherwise impacted. Using FEMA's Individual Households Program Cost Estimator, the initial assistance needs for just these two counties are nearly $4.9 million. Because full assessments across all requested counties are still underway, these figures capture only a fraction of the destruction, underscoring that the scale of unmet needs will grow substantially and far outpace state and local resources.

Federal Individual Assistance will provide critical support to families working to secure temporary housing, repair damaged homes, replace essential personal property, and begin rebuilding their lives. Likewise, Public Assistance is essential to help local governments restore emergency services, repair damaged infrastructure, remove debris, and safely reopen the public facilities on which these communities depend. Authorization of the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program will also help reduce future disaster risk by strengthening infrastructure and improving community resilience across West Virginia.

We appreciate FEMA's partnership with state and local officials as damage assessments continue. West Virginians are resilient and are doing everything possible to recover from this disaster, but the need for assistance is abundantly clear. For these reasons, we respectfully urge you to approve Governor Morrisey's request for a Major Disaster Declaration, including Individual Assistance for Barbour, Doddridge, Harrison, Lewis, Pleasants, Ritchie, and Upshur Counties; Public Assistance for Categories A through G in those counties; and the Hazard Mitigation Grant Program statewide.

Thank you for your consideration of this request and for your continued support of the people of West Virginia. We stand ready to work with your Administration, FEMA, and state and local officials to ensure these communities receive the assistance they need to recover and rebuild.

Sincerely,

# # #

title: Heinrich Statement on Trump Admin Admitting it Canceled Energy Project Grants in Democratic-Led States Due to Partisan Politics
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, released the following statement in response to news that the Trump administration admitted in court documents that it canceled grants and funding for energy projects in Democratic-led states due to partisan politics:

“This reporting proves what we’ve known all along: the Trump administration’s decision to cancel energy project grants in states where Donald Trump lost in 2024 was nakedly political and vengeful.

“Since President Trump was sworn into office, he’s played a dangerous game of politics with our energy sector – slow-walking solar and wind project approvals, outright canceling offshore wind project approvals and energy project grants, killing thousands of made-in-America jobs and tanking billions in private sector investment.

“President Trump promised to lower costs for working families. Instead of working to find solutions to lower costs for Americans, his attacks on American-made energy and his war with Iran have skyrocketed energy bills and gas prices. The American people deserve a government that works for them, not one that plays politics with their lives and jobs.”

Heinrich has been vocal against the Trump administration’s cancellation of these clean energy project grants:

This is not the first time the Trump administration has admitted in court documents that these cancellations were political. Senator Heinrich grilled Secretary Wright on cancellations when the Secretary appeared before the Committee on April 21st of this year:

“When you came before this Committee almost a year ago, I asked you if it was the case that political appointees were on review boards for the cancellation of $3.7 billion in awards. You responded, ‘Well, it's absolutely the case.’ Those are your words,” Heinrich said. “Since then, it has become abundantly clear that politics are indeed calling the shots in your Department of Energy.”

“Last October, DOE unlawfully canceled $8 billion in federal investments in 223 energy projects, almost entirely in states with Democratic leadership. DOE then confirmed in federal court that the cancellations were based on whether a project was in a blue state.” Heinrich continued. “Satisfying a President’s desire for political revenge or intimidation is not a lawful basis for terminating projects that were on track to help reduce soaring electricity prices.”

Last October, Heinrich led 36 senators in sending a letter demanding that U.S. Department of Energy Secretary Chris Wright and the U.S. Office of Management and Budget Director Russ Vought restore funding for 223 energy projects in Democratic-led states that were unlawfully canceled.

Last October, in response to the news that the Trump administration was canceling funding for 223 projects, Heinrich called the move “nakedly political, unhinged, and unlawful,” and spotlighted the ten projects in New Mexico that were impacted by the Trump administration’s actions.

title: Sen. Ossoff Statement on Designation of Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge as Georgia’s First UNESCO World Heritage Site
text:
In February 2023, Sen. Ossoff led a bipartisan group urging National Park Service to nominate the Okefenokee refuge for UNESCO’s World Heritage Site list

Sen. Ossoff has worked for years to protect the Okefenokee

Okefenokee becomes Georgia’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site

Washington, D.C. — After years of U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff’s advocacy, UNESCO has designated the Okefenokee as Georgia’s first World Heritage Site.

Following Sen. Ossoff’s bipartisan push over the last few years, the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) announced today that the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge has been designated as Georgia’s first-ever UNESCO World Heritage Site.

This announcement follows a bipartisan effort by Sen. Ossoff, who led a group of Georgia’s Congressional delegation in 2023 urging the Department of the Interior to pursue this prestigious designation. Following the group’s urging, in September 2023, the National Park Service announced it intended to nominate the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge for UNESCO’s World Heritage Site list, and then in December 2024, the U.S. Department of the Interior announced that it would nominate the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge for the UNESCO World Heritage List.

In response to today’s historic announcement, Sen. Ossoff released the following statement.

“For years I’ve worked to protect Georgia’s beloved Okefenokee Swamp from dangerous strip mining, and now, following our bipartisan push, it’s been named Georgia’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site,” Sen. Ossoff said. “The Okefenokee is an irreplaceable natural treasure in our state, and this significant designation will help protect this renowned natural treasure for generations to come, promote tourism, and support Southeast Georgia’s economic growth.”

The World Heritage designation places the Okefenokee alongside global landmarks such as the Grand Canyon and Yellowstone National Park. With its inscription, the Okefenokee becomes Georgia’s first UNESCO World Heritage Site and the first National Wildlife Refuge in the United States to receive the prestigious designation.

This recognition is expected to boost environmental protection efforts and promote economic prosperity through increased tourism and international recognition. According to a 2024 study, the World Heritage Site designation by UNESCO could double visitation at the Okefenokee Swamp Park, create about 750 long-term jobs, and deliver $60 million in annual economic impact.

Sen. Ossoff has worked for years to protect the Okefenokee.

In February 2023, Sen. Ossoff led a bipartisan coalition urging the U.S. Interior Department to nominate the Okefenokee Refuge for the honor, a crucial step in getting considered by UNESCO.

Following his urging, in September 2023, the National Park Service announced it intended to nominate the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge for UNESCO’s World Heritage Site list, and then in December 2024, the U.S. Department of the Interior announced that it would nominate the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge for the UNESCO World Heritage List.

In April 2024, Sen. Ossoff submitted formal public comments to Georgia’s Environmental Protection Division opposing mining permits near the Okefenokee, citing the threat of “irreversible damage” to the swamp and surrounding ecosystem.

In January 2025, following Sen. Ossoff’s push, the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service announced it would expand the Okefenokee National Wildlife Refuge’s acquisition boundary by 22,000 acres.

In May 2025, Sen. Ossoff pressed the Trump Administration’s Department of the Interior in a Senate Appropriations Subcommittee hearing, securing a public commitment from Interior Secretary Doug Burgum that no part of the Okefenokee would be sold.

In June 2025, Sen. Ossoff welcomed the announcement of a land acquisition deal in which The Conservation Fund will purchase roughly 8,000 acres from Twin Pines Minerals, as well as the underlying mineral rights — effectively halting the proposed titanium mine near the swamp.

In August 2025, Sen. Ossoff passed an amendment through the U.S. Senate Appropriations Committee to encourage greater expanded protection of the Okefenokee Swamp.

# # #

title: Reed: Trump Administration’s Response to Nationwide Diarrhea Outbreak Stinks
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – After the Trump Administration cut $11.4 billion from state and local health departments, slashing public health staff, and winnowing the scope of a U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) program known as Foodborne Diseases Active Surveillance Network (FoodNet), that surveilled trends in foodborne illness, America is experiencing a massive, prolonged outbreak of cyclospora, a foodborne parasite that causes severe diarrhea, and in some cases has led to hospitalizations.

Currently, the ‘explosive diarrhea parasite,’ cyclosporiasis -- which can cause weeks of intestinal illness marked by "frequent and sometimes explosive bowel movements" -- is running rampant across the U.S., with thousands of cases pushing the outbreak to a record high. Cyclospora spreads via contaminated food or water.

Last year, Trump officials ordered the CDC to stop the mandatory monitoring of cyclospora, as well as five other foodborne illnesses. Instead, the agency just monitors Salmonella and a form of E. coli. Surveillance of cyclospora had previously been mandatory since 1997, before the Trump Administration cut it. Now the country is facing the largest cyclosporiasis outbreak in years.

According to the CDC, cyclosporiasis cases have been reported in 41 different states this year, including Rhode Island. Nine midwestern states have been hit especially hard: Illinois, Indiana, Kansas, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, Oklahoma, Pennsylvania, and West Virginia.

Noting that the FDA said illnesses started on May 17, yet the Trump Administration failed to issue a public notice until July 16, U.S. Senator Jack Reed says the Trump Administration’s short-sighted cuts of staff, resources, and scientific professionals has directly contributed to the nationwide outbreak and likely worsened and prolonged it.

“The Trump Administration cut CDC funding, fired food-safety inspectors, and chose to fracture America’s food-safety system. Now thousands of people are sick, and the Trump Administration is playing catch up while more Americans are at risk from this nasty foodborne parasite,” said Senator Reed. “In past years, this is something the CDC should have been able to identify and help contain. But they no longer have the resources, mandate, or manpower they did under previous administrations. For Trump there’s plenty of money for a new White House ballroom, a 250-foot arch, a failed reflecting pool repair, but basic public health measures just don’t get prioritized. This is just another example of the Trump Administration’s misplaced and short-sighted cuts putting Americans at risk.”

After weeks of trying to keep a lid on the national numbers, the CDC revised its national count on July 14 from the 843 confirmed cases it was reporting late last week upward to 1,645 lab-confirmed, plus more than 5,100 under investigation — totaling nearly 7,000 people nationwide, with 141 hospitalized. Now the Trump Administration says those numbers have climbed to over 4,100 cases and 300 hospitalizations. But the CDC has an additional 7,400 cases that are still awaiting testing and health experts say the real numbers is likely much higher.

Health experts note that cyclosporiasis cases are reported every year in the United States, commonly between May and the end of August, but case counts are typically much lower than they have been this year. For example, Michigan, which has been an epicenter of this outbreak, usually reports roughly 59 cases annually, compared to over 8,000 reported so far this year.

“This is a leadership failure, not the fault of CDC staff on the frontlines. This Administration willfully weakened the federal public health system’s ability to track and respond to foodborne illness outbreaks. President Trump hasn’t saved taxpayers a dime. Instead, he’s prioritizing more money for wars, ballrooms, and whatever other shiny objects he cares about,” said Reed. “As cases continue to spike, this administration needs to be accountable for its failures. President Trump has time to get on the phone to complain to FIFA about red cards. He needs to get on the phone to Secretary Kennedy and do something about this massive and disgusting outbreak.”

Despite the spike in cases, Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. claims the multi-state outbreak is “under control,” telling ABC News: “We have an extensive forensics, epidemiological forensics, and we’ve identified the source of the outbreak. We and the companies that are involved have implemented a recall.”

After some confusion over testing, lettuce grower Taylor Farms initiated a voluntary recall of all its iceberg lettuce sourced from central Mexico, but the problem persists. And WPRI notes some local restaurants who are not part of the outbreak are being unfairly hurt by the lack of clarity and many consumers are forgoing safe, healthy greens because the Trump Administration’s failure to clearly communicate with the public about what is safe and what is not.

Senator Reed is urging the Trump Administration to get its act together and ensure federal and state partners are coordinating to investigate this multistate outbreak and protecting the public by removing tainted products from the market.

The senator wants an investigation that includes Trump health officials briefing Congress and testifying before the Appropriations Committee about the funding needed to effectively contain this outbreak and to restore funding for federal and state food safety programs to prevent future outbreaks.

According to the Rhode Island Department of Health (RIDOH), the Ocean State has not seen a major outbreak of cyclospora cases this year, but has identified 10 cases so far. Last year, RIDOH tallied 6 cases of the infection last year, and 12 cases in 2024.

title: Hoyer Statement on the 36th Anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Congressman Steny H. Hoyer (MD-05) released the following statement today recognizing the 36th anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA):

“Today, I join in celebrating the thirty-sixth anniversary of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) – pivotal legislation that reshaped the lives of millions of Americans living with disabilities, guaranteeing them equal access and equal opportunity.

“Championing the ADA in the House was one of the proudest moments in my career. Over the past thirty-six years, we have continued to strengthen this progress through the ADA Amendments Act of 2008 and seen it advanced through the 1999 Supreme Court decision in Olmstead v. L.C., which reaffirmed our original intent to secure full inclusion and equality for all.

“As we reflect on these accomplishments, we are reminded that the fight is not over. We must acknowledge the dangers of this moment as the Trump Administration undermines the progress we have achieved, seeking to erode opportunities for Americans with disabilities and overturn Congress’s clear intent as recognized by Olmstead. So, our work continues, and we will keep fighting diligently so that every American may enjoy the promises upon which our nation was founded – liberty and justice for all.”

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON CNN: “WE ARE FIGHTING FOR AN AFFORDABLE AMERICA”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on CNN’s State of the Union, where he outlined how with 100 days until the midterm elections, Democrats are going to continue to push back on Republican extremism and fight to lower costs for hardworking American taxpayers.

DANA BASH: Here with me now is the House Democratic Leader, Congressman Hakeem Jeffries. Mr. Leader, thank you so much for being here. I know that you are launching what Democrats are calling 100 Days Out Weekend of Action with more than 400 grassroots events in competitive states, including Pennsylvania, where you’re going to be speaking later today. At the same time, your party is fighting over whether the path back to the majority runs through the center or the activist left, who want to defund the police, abolish ICE, end aid to Israel, open borders. I know that you call the Democratic Party a mosaic, but are you going to push any of those positions if you win the majority back?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well what unites the party, and certainly what will take place over the next 100 days, beginning today, is a focus on us fighting for an affordable America, based on the reality that life in this country is far too expensive and everybody agrees that that’s the dynamic that the country confronts. Too many people are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and they can barely survive. Not enough food on the table, not enough gas in the tank, unable to actually regularly and consistently afford to pay the rent or pay the mortgage. We want to drive down the cost of groceries, drive down and lower the cost of gasoline, drive down the cost of housing and also make sure that healthcare is affordable for every single American.

DANA BASH: Right, but to do those things, which is the messaging that I’ve heard you say, especially recently, you need to come up with policy proposals. So will those policy proposals be in line with what some of the more progressive members who keep getting elected are pushing? Or will you sort of move more towards the moderate area, where if you do win the majority, it will be likely because they pick up swing districts?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we want to make sure that we are solving problems on behalf of the American people, and that’s in every possible area. It is clear that what unites Democrats, for instance, we forcefully have been pushing back against the One Big Ugly Bill and the effort to enact the largest cut to Medicaid in American history. That’s a disgrace, and clearly that needs to be reversed. We need to make sure that we do things like extending the Affordable Care Act tax credits so that more than 20 million people actually can have healthcare that they can afford restored to them as opposed to the situation that they confront right now because of MAGA extremist policies, which is that they’ve experienced dramatic increases in their health insurance premiums in some cases more than $1000 per month. It certainly is the case, as we’ve already demonstrated unanimously on the House Floor, that we need to stop this reckless and costly war of choice that has skyrocketed gas prices on everyday Americans, and we need to stop the Trump tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year.

DANA BASH: You, according to my colleague Manu Raju, clash with Senator Bernie Sanders over the fact that he is campaigning for progressive candidates, some of whom are challenging incumbents you back, including Members of the Congressional Black Caucus. Are Senator Sanders and other progressives in the party making it harder for you to win in November? Is that what you said to Senator Sanders?

LEADER JEFFRIES: No, I wouldn’t describe it as a clash. It was a candid conversation along with Congressman Greg Meeks, the Chair of the Congressional Black Caucus PAC, with respect to one particular race in North Carolina at the beginning of the primary cycle and trying to get a sense of his approach to that race. I do think that Senator Sanders and Democrats in both the House and the Senate understand the stakes that are in front of us, particularly as we are one hundred days out. And that’s making sure that we actually take back control of the Congress so we can end this MAGA extremism that has been unleashed on the American people that is actively hurting hardworking American taxpayers and actually commit to making life more affordable for the American people. That’s clearly what the American people want to see done, and that’s not what Republicans have been able to accomplish during their time in office since Trump was sworn in back in January of last year.

DANA BASH: I think one of the things that some of those who are winning their primaries and will likely be in office want to know is if you are going to agree to hold votes on abolishing ICE, opening borders, things of that nature. Will you?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I’ve spoken to several of the incoming Members of Congress across the ideological spectrum. Not a single person has raised those issues, other than obviously what they’ve seen from Democrats in pushing back against an out-of-control ICE because we believe that immigration enforcement in this country clearly should be fair, just and humane, and that’s not what’s taking place. That’s the reason why House Democrats have taken a strong position as it relates to not giving a dime to Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine until, of course, there is dramatic reform in this country and that ICE agents actually start to conduct themselves like every other cop, police officer and law enforcement agent in the country.

DANA BASH: Your next-door neighbor, New Jersey, just disclosed that 6,600 non-citizens were mistakenly registered to vote there from 2023 to 2024. 400 of them actually voted in elections since then. It is a small number compared to the 7 million voters in New Jersey and there’s no evidence that that swayed any election. But this is one of the most significant disclosures of non-citizen registration. Democrats have repeatedly said that non-citizen voting doesn’t happen. It happened. Is this a problem?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I think that I continue to have confidence in state and local authorities in making sure that there’s going to be a free and fair election in November. And if modest or minor challenges emerge, such as the one that was disclosed voluntarily by the authorities in New Jersey, that it is immediately corrected. And that’s what I expect will continue to happen. Unfortunately, what we’ve seen from Donald Trump is that, in this particular case, Republicans have adopted voter suppression as an electoral strategy because they have failed to actually deliver on making life more affordable for the American people. It was Donald Trump who promised to lower costs on day one, but we know that costs haven’t gone down in this country, costs have gone up. It was Donald Trump, I believe, who said that he was elected not to start wars—endless wars in the Middle East—but to stop them, and then turned around and has gotten us involved in this reckless war of choice in Iran that has skyrocketed gas prices on the American people. By the way, it was Donald Trump who said they were going to love and cherish Medicaid, and then Republicans enacted the largest cut to Medicaid in American history, ripping healthcare away from more than 14 million Americans. They have nothing to run on. We’re going to run on fighting for an affordable America.

DANA BASH: Mr. Leader, before I let you go, President Trump ordered signs placed outside the Museum of American History, warning that it promotes inaccurate history. It comes, of course, as the White House is attacking the Smithsonian, accusing the institution of promoting left-wing ideology. Is there anything you can do to stop those signs from going up?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to explore every legislative avenue and every litigation avenue, as we’ve repeatedly done up until this point. Here’s the thing. Black history is American history, and we are not going to let the extremists whitewash it. Not now. Not ever.

DANA BASH: Hakeem Jeffries, Democratic Leader of the House of Representatives. Thanks so much for being here. I appreciate it.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you.

Full interview can be watched here.
