title: Rep. Sewell Releases New Report Detailing the Affordability Crisis Facing Alabama's 7th Congressional District
text:
Report outlines rising cost of groceries, housing, utilities, gas, and healthcare under President Trump and Congressional Republicans

Birmingham, AL – Today, U.S. Rep. Terri Sewell (AL-07) released a new report examining the growing affordability crisis facing families across Alabama's 7th Congressional District. The report details how President Trump's economic policies and congressional Republicans' legislative agenda have driven up the cost of everyday essentials while threatening access to healthcare and food assistance for thousands of Alabamians.

The report comes as House Democrats unveil their "Fighting For An Affordable America Agenda," with exactly 100 days until Election Day. The agenda involves three pillars: lowering the cost of groceries, gas and housing, providing affordable healthcare for every American, and cleaning corruption by holding the crooks accountable.

Watch Rep. Sewell's video message here.

Among its findings, the report notes that Alabama families are paying an average of $2,700 more for basic living expenses, families in Alabama's 7th District now spend an average of $1,110 per month on groceries, and approximately 70,000 people in AL-07 are expected to see their health insurance costs rise because Republicans allowed enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits to expire. The average Alabama household has paid $686 more for gasoline since President Trump launched his unauthorized war in Iran, and more than 81,800 Alabamians have already lost SNAP benefits under Republicans' budget law.

"One hundred days before Election Day, Alabama families deserve to know the truth about who is driving up their costs," said Rep. Sewell."President Trump promised to lower prices on Day One. Instead, families across Alabama's 7th District are paying more for groceries, housing, electricity, gas, and healthcare while Republicans in Congress have chosen to cut Medicaid and food assistance to help pay for tax breaks for billionaires."

"It doesn't have to be this way," continued Sewell. "House Democrats are fighting for an Affordable America by lowering the cost of groceries, gas, and housing, making healthcare more affordable, and holding corporations accountable when they exploit consumers and drive up prices. Alabama families deserve an economy that works for them—not just the wealthy and well-connected."

The report highlights several economic challenges facing Alabama families, including:

Alabama families are paying an average of $2,700 more for basic living expenses under President Trump and congressional Republicans.

Families in Alabama's 7th District paid an average of $233 more for electricity in 2025.

The average monthly grocery bill in AL-07 has reached $1,110.

The average Alabama household has paid $686 more for gasoline since the start of President Trump's war in Iran.

The average annual cost of child care for two children in Alabama has climbed to $16,640.

Approximately 24,353 people in Alabama's 7th District are projected to lose health coverage because of Republican cuts to Medicaid and the Affordable Care Act.

More than 81,800 Alabamians have already lost SNAP benefits.

More than 20,000 Alabama individuals and families filed for bankruptcy in 2025, a 6.7 percent increase over the previous year.

The full report, "The Affordability Crisis in Alabama's 7th Congressional District: How President Trump and Congressional Republicans Are Driving Up Costs for Alabama Families," is available here.

title: Senator Murray Calls on ICE to Stop Deportation of Seattle Small Business Owner, Return Him to Washington State
text:
***VIDEO OF EDUARDO’S DETAINMENT ALONG WITH OTHER PHOTO AND VIDEO OF EDUARDO AND HIS WIFE ARE AVAILABLE TO THE PRESS HERE***

Seattle, WA – Today, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, issued the following statement upon hearing news that Eduardo Aguirre Esparza, the husband of an American citizen, was forcefully detained and in the process of being deported before courts can consider emergency relief:

“On Thursday, ICE needlessly detained Eduardo Aguirre Esparza, a local Seattle small business owner with no criminal history. This is a man who is married to an American citizen and with deep ties to our local community who was working hard to pursue a legal pathway to lawful permanent residence. For the federal government to waste its resources to forcefully detain and deport Eduardo and tear apart an American family is plain sick. Our immigration enforcement should be focused on violent criminals and keeping Americans safe—deporting hardworking people like Eduardo makes no one safer, it’s just cruel and wrong.

“I am demanding that DHS return Eduardo to Washington state so that he may receive due process and have access to counsel—flying Eduardo to Texas away from his lawyers to try and deport him is fundamentally wrong and un-American. I hope others in Washington state will join me in calling for Eduardo’s immediate return home so that the courts can fairly consider his case.”

Eduardo Aguirre Esparza is an undocumented immigrant, married to an American citizen. He’s a hardworking small business owner who owns a remodeling company in Seattle. He’s lived in Seattle for 23 years. Following his detainment to the Northwest ICE Processing Center (NWIPC) on Thursday, Eduardo was flown out of Washington state on ICE Air at 2 AM on Saturday morning without notice to anyone, including his attorney and family. After several stops along the way, Eduardo is now being held in Texas where his family suspects ICE intends to conduct an expedited deportation hearing to remove Eduardo from his home as quickly as possible and without representation of counsel. Senator Murray is joining Eduardo’s family in demanding that he be returned to Western Washington to receive his due process protections.

title: As ADA Turns 36, Reed Cosponsors Resolution to Uplift Disability Community and Honor Decades of Progress
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – On July 26, 1990, President George H.W. Bush signed the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA), prohibiting discrimination based on mental or physical disabilities.

Celebrating the thirty-sixth anniversary of the ADA, U.S. Senator Jack Reed (D-RI) joined U.S. Senator Andy Kim (D-NJ) and a group of 28 Senate colleagues in introducing a resolution to honor the disability community, uplift the impact of the historic legislation, and call for continued commitment to increasing inclusivity and accessibility.

The Senate Resolution recognizes: “The importance of independent living and economic self-sufficiency for individuals with disabilities made possible by the Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 and calling to protect the right of individuals with disabilities to live in their own homes and communities.”

In the resolution, the Senators outline the ADA’s long-success ensuring individuals with disabilities have the right to live, work, and participate as members of their communities and receive necessary care and support through access to Medicaid home and community-based services. The Senators condemn a June 18th Department of Justice opinion that has since threatened this hard-won progress toward full integration of individuals with disabilities into society and commit to working to stop attempts to dismantle the ADA.

“The Americans with Disabilities Act represents the floor, not the ceiling, of efforts needed to dismantle barriers to full participation, equal opportunity, independent living, and economic self-sufficiency for individuals with disabilities,” reads the Resolution.

Senator Reed stated: “The ADA has made a tremendous difference for individuals, families, communities, and our country. The law broke down barriers, expanded opportunities, made communities more inclusive, and improved equal access and independence for Americans with disabilities. The ADA’s broad benefits strengthen our society and make public places more welcoming for all. As the ADA turns 36, we must continue pushing for progress to ensure every American can participate fully in their community and our democracy.”

The resolution is also cosponsored by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Angus King (I-ME), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Dick Durbin (D-IL), Christopher Van Hollen (D-MD), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Chris Coons (D-DE), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), John Fetterman (D-PA), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Patty Murray (D-WA), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Ed Markey (D-MA), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Chris Murphy (D-CT), and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI).

Thirty-six years since the ADA was signed into law on July 26th, 1990:

More than 8,400,000 individuals receive home and community-based services through Medicaid;

Individuals with disabilities are participating in the labor force at a rate of over 41 percent;

On average, it is 3 times less expensive to serve someone through home and community-based services relative to an institution; and

Individuals returning to the community from institutions report improved life satisfaction, reduced unmet needs, and enhanced feelings of dignity.

Throughout his career, Senator Reed has championed the ADA and accessibility law to improve accessibility. He supported full Senate ratification of the international Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities (CRPD) and helped secure the implementation of technology updates like the 21st Century Communications and Video Accessibility Act for sensory impairments. Since 2020, Rhode Island has received nearly $400 million in cumulative federal funding under the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA). Senator Reed has also fought cuts to Medicaid, which provides long-term care, behavioral services, and medical support to hundreds of thousands of disabled and vulnerable Rhode Islanders.

title: Democratic Veterans Demand Transparency on Iran War Casualties
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Following disturbing reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, Rep. Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06) joined 14 fellow Democratic veterans in urging the Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

“As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers,” wrote the lawmakers.

“The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports,” they continued. “We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.”

Following public outcry, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names of the four U.S. servicemembers removed from the Iran War death toll over the weekend. The Administration has not provided an adequate explanation as to why the servicemembers were removed in the first place.

The letter, led by Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04), was also signed by Representatives Pat Ryan (NY-18), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Jared Golden (ME-02).

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear President Trump,

As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers.

The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.

We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.

Sincerely,

title: Arrington Joins Effort to Protect American Businesses from EU Regulatory Overreach
text:
Washington, D.C. – House Budget Chairman Jodey Arrington (TX-19) was joined by Rep. Craig Goldman (TX-12) and Rep. Greg Steube (FL-17) in introducing H.R. 9892, the Stop EU Overreach Act. The legislation directs the U.S. Trade Representative to investigate the European Union's policies to impose costly foreign regulations on American businesses operating on U.S. soil.

"America should never allow foreign bureaucrats to discriminate against our companies,” said Chairman Arrington. “While President Trump is opening new markets for American energy exports and strengthening our economy, the European Union continues to impose unfair regulations that target American energy producers and put our businesses at a competitive disadvantage. I'm proud to join my colleagues in introducing the Stop EU Overreach Act to promote American energy, protect U.S. businesses from foreign regulatory overreach, and ensure our trading partners treat U.S. producers fairly.”

“This important legislation will protect American businesses from the EU’s woke regulations and extreme green energy mandates. These radical regulations on U.S. businesses would not only cost American businesses more than a trillion dollars, but also represent a clear overreach into American sovereignty,” said Rep. Goldman. “I’m grateful for the incredible support of my colleagues on this issue, as we fight to protect American businesses.”

“American businesses should answer to American law, not to regulators in Brussels,” said Rep. Steube. “The EU’s sustainability mandates are a backdoor tax on our farmers, manufacturers, and small businesses that never voted for a single one of these rules. I’m co-leading the Stop EU Overreach Act with Reps. Goldman and Arrington to make sure USTR pushes back before this costs American jobs.”

The Stop EU Overreach Act would:

Direct the U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) to launch a Section 301 investigation, under the U.S. Trade Act of 1974, in response to the EU’s “sustainability” regulatory regime that places extraterritorial requirements on American companies.

Require the USTR to consider if the EU’s use of the Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive (CS3D), Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD), Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), and Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) constitutes an unreasonable or discriminatory trade practice burdening U.S. commerce.

Instruct the USTR to identify appropriate remedies to counter these burdens and promptly report its findings to the relevant committees in the U.S. House and Senate.

Background:

The EU is seeking to impose extreme environmental mandates on American companies operating outside of the EU. By forcing American businesses to adhere to costly foreign regulations on supply chains, reporting requirements, and environmental practices, these mandates distort free market competition, threaten American jobs, and disadvantage American producers and manufacturers in global markets.

The Stop EU Overreach Act is an America First policy that ensures American businesses answer to American law – not foreign bureaucrats.

title: Biggs's Bipartisan Amendments Included in National Defense Authorization Act Package
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.- Last week, the U.S. House of Representatives passed the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, which included two of Congressman Andy Biggs’s (AZ-05) bipartisan amendments.

The first amendment was the Audit the Pentagon Act. This legislation was one of the first bills Congressman Biggs introduced when he entered the U.S. House in 2017. It restores financial oversight to the Department of Defense (DoD), which has failed eight straight audits while billions of taxpayer dollars remain unaccounted for in this critical department. In fact, the DoD is the only federal agency without a successful audit. Americans demand that their government officials know where their tax dollars are going and that every dollar is used as effectively as possible. By doing so, our government can help ensure the United States has the strongest, most-effective military in the world for generations to come.

The second amendment addresses the disparity between Chinese and American mining engineering workforces. The United States graduates just over 200 mining engineers each year, paling in comparison to China’s reported annual graduation of 3,000 to 10,000 mining-related engineers. Due, in part, to this gap, the United States is 100 percent import reliant for 16 nonfuel minerals and more than 50 percent reliant for dozens more, compromising American defense systems, semiconductors, and infrastructure. States like Arizona know how mining supports both economic strength and critical mineral independence, reinforcing the need to open additional pathways to build this specific workforce. This amendment ensures federal support focuses where it belongs: on the accredited mining engineering programs that directly strengthen America’s workforce pipeline and national security.

“I’m grateful for the support of my colleagues on both sides of the aisle for these amendments,”said Congressman Biggs.“My amendments address critical issues within America’s massive national defense apparatus, ensuring more transparency and accountability within our government and closing the gap between China and the United States for a critical workforce. I look forward to seeing these commonsense amendments soon signed into law by the president.”

Both the amendments passed with overwhelmingly bipartisan support.

title: Rep. Judy Chu Commends Local Peaceful Demonstrations Against ICE Killings
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Following peaceful demonstrations and vigils in Pasadena to demand justice and accountability for the killings of Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and Joan Sebastián Durán Guerrero by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers, Rep. Judy Chu released the following statement:

“I stand in solidarity with everyone in our community who gathered this weekend to demand justice for Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, Joan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, and every person who has lost their life during an ICE operation or while in ICE custody.

It is abhorrent, unconscionable, and utterly indefensible that with each passing week, another family is mourning a loved one who never came home from an encounter with ICE. Instead of reining in an agency plagued by violence, abuse, and a staggering lack of accountability, the Trump Administration and Republicans have handed ICE hundreds of billions of taxpayer dollars to expand the violent, cruel operations that are terrorizing immigrant communities.

That is why I was proud to join nearly 200 of my Democratic colleagues to demand ICE be held accountable through an independent investigation into Mr. Salgado Araujo and Mr. Guerrero’s deaths. Their families deserve answers, they deserve justice, and the American people deserve an immigration system that values human life over fear and intimidation.

We will not look away. We will not be intimidated into silence. And we will never stop fighting until every family can live without fear that an encounter with ICE could end in detention, tragedy, or death.

For more than a decade, I have fought to expose ICE's abuses and demand accountability. I have repeatedly called for the closure of the Adelanto ICE Processing Center after witnessing appalling conditions, medical neglect, retaliation against detainees, and preventable deaths. I have demanded investigations into fatal ICE shootings, challenged the Trump Administration's abuse of immigration enforcement, and fought to stop Congress from writing blank checks for an agency that continues to operate with no transparency or accountability. I will continue using every tool available to me in Congress to expose these abuses, hold ICE accountable, and demand justice for every person who has been wrongfully targeted, killed, detained, and deported.”

On July 7, 2026, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, the father of three U.S. citizens and a 35-year resident of the United States, was stopped by officers in an unmarked ICE vehicle while driving to work in Houston, Texas. Mr. Salgado Araujo was not the target of the ICE operation but was fatally shot by an ICE agent after the agent alleged he had “weaponized” his vehicle, a claim that neither ICE nor the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) has substantiated with publicly released evidence.

Six days later, on July 13, 2026, ICE fatally shot 25-year-old Colombian national Joan Sebastián Durán Guerrero in Biddeford, Maine. Mr. Guerrero, a father who was authorized to work in the United States, was not the target of the enforcement operation. He was shot after attempting to flee in a vehicle. Video footage shows ICE officers handcuffing Mr. Guerrero after he had been shot in the head.

title: Ciscomani Supports Defense Legislation to Strengthen Military Readiness and Improve the Quality of Life for Our Men and Women in Uniform
text:
Washington, D.C. - Representative Juan Ciscomani welcomes the passage of the annual legislative package that strengthens military readiness, supports Arizona’s defense industries and improves quality of life for our servicemembers and their families.

The Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) passed the House of Representatives recently with a bipartisan vote of 216-212.

"Arizona's Sixth District is proud to be home to Fort Huachuca and Davis-Monthan Air Force Bases," said Rep. Juan Ciscomani. "Supporting our nation's heroes has always been one of my top priorities in Congress, and I will continue fighting to ensure they have the resources, tools, and capabilities needed to carry out their vital missions. The FY27 National Defense Authorization Act strengthens our military, invests in the quality of life of our troops and their families, and advances a peace through strength agenda that keeps America safe. I'm proud to support legislation that honors the service and sacrifice of our armed forces while ensuring they remain the strongest fighting force in the world."

The NDAA makes critical investments in the men and women who serve our nation, including a 5-7% pay raise for junior-enlisted servicemembers, $1.8 billion for new barracks and military housing construction, and more than $226 million to design and build childcare centers for military families. The legislation also includes landmark reforms to improve benefits for servicemembers, including enhanced cost-of-living adjustments for troops stationed in high-cost areas, increased paid leave allowances, fertility care coverage, and expanded dental coverage for junior reserve component servicemembers.

The bill also cuts nearly $30 billion in unnecessary spending while ensuring taxpayer dollars are directed toward strengthening national defense and supporting America’s military.

"Fort Huachuca is the backbone of Sierra Vista and a cornerstone of Cochise County’s economy and national security mission. Home to thousands of active-duty servicemembers and civilian personnel, the installation plays a vital role in defending our nation while supporting our local communities," said Huachuca 50 President Dr. Randy Groth. "The National Defense Authorization Act, which passed the House with Congressman Juan Ciscomani’s support, makes critical investments in our military, strengthens missions at Fort Huachuca’s, and ensures our servicemembers have the resources they need to carry out and protect our nation for generations to come."

Since taking office in 2023, Rep. Ciscomani has been a strong advocate for servicemembers in Congress. Through his role on the House Appropriations Committee, he has worked tirelessly to deliver resources that strengthen Arizona’s military installations and support the missions carried out at Fort Huachuca and Davis-Monthan Air Force Base. Congressman Ciscomani has always been a staunch advocate for military families and has maintained a robust track record of supporting the NDAA to ensure America’s military remains ready, equipped, and prepared to meet evolving global threats from adversaries.

The FY27 NDAA will now advance to conference negotiations with the Senate.

title: Rep. Angie Craig Helps Introduce Legislation to Protect TPS, Fight Trump’s Attacks on Immigrants
text:
EAGAN, MN – U.S. Representative Angie Craig recently joined Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz (D-FL-25) in introducing legislation to protect Temporary Protected Statuses (TPS) and fight President Trump’s continued attacks on our nation’s immigrants.

The Temporary Protected Status Review Act would require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to follow a clear, evidence-based process before terminating TPS and allow Congress to reverse TPS terminations under the Congressional Review Act.

Rep. Craig’s bill comes after last month’s Supreme Court decision in Mullin v. Doe, which ruled that the Administration’s termination of TPS for Haitians and Syrians cannot be reviewed by the courts. As a result, 1.3 million TPS recipients who fled violence, natural disasters or brutal political repression are at risk of losing their legal status and work authorization and could potentially face detention, family separation or deportation back to their home countries.

“The Trump Administration has repeatedly targeted TPS and used those who have come to our country to flee some of the most horrific situations as political pawns,” said Rep. Craig. “Reversing TPS actively endangers the lives of TPS holders forced to return to the violence they fled. I’m proud help introduce this critical legislation to protect Minnesota’s TPS holders, take back control from this out-of-control president and combat his administration’s continued attacks on our immigrant neighbors.”

Rep. Craig has repeatedly spoken out against President Trump's attacks on TPS, especially on behalf of Minnesota’s Somali community, for whom TPS was cancelled earlier this year.

In April, Rep. Craig and her Democratic colleagues successfully forced a vote on legislation requiring the Trump Administration to reinstate TPS for Haitians. Earlier this year, she joined a group of 26 Senators and 157 House Members in filing an amicus brief challenging the Trump Administration’s illegal termination of TPS protections for Haiti and Syria in Trump v. Miot. Ultimately, the Supreme Court’s conservative-majority ruled TPS terminations could proceed lawfully.

Rep. Craig is also an original cosponsor and longtime supporter of the American Dream and Promise Act, which would protect TPS holders and provide them with a path to lawful permanent residence.

title: TIME: Jason Crow's Road From Paratrooper to Democratic Power Player
text:
The death threats arrived almost immediately.

Representative Jason Crow, along with five other Democrats in Congress with national-­security backgrounds, had recorded a video last November reminding those working in military and intelligence roles that they did not have to follow illegal orders. A message careful to stick to the letter of the law prompted President Donald Trump to call for its makers to be arrested and charged with treason. “HANG THEM GEORGE WASHINGTON WOULD!!” read a social media post that Trump publicly shared. A federal grand jury in Washington declined the Justice Department’s effort to indict the lawmakers. That victory hasn’t mitigated Crow’s anger at how he believes the President’s response put his family’s safety at risk.

“I’m really bad at sitting in a foxhole and having people lob grenades at me,” Crow, a former paratrooper and Army Ranger, tells TIME on a June afternoon at Democratic National Committee headquarters. “I’m going to lob them back.”

The fallout from the viral video placed Crow, 47, in the strongest national spotlight since 2019, when he was a House freshman tapped to be a prosecutor in Trump’s first impeachment trial. In the interim, his stature on Capitol Hill has steadily grown, as Crow emerged as a go-to voice for his party on national security. The midterm elections could further elevate his standing, as he’s helped lead candidate recruitment for House Democrats, prioritizing veterans and others with backgrounds in national security.

In Crow’s mind, these elections will show voters that Democrats have learned how to run effectively on national-­security issues, while still hammering Republicans on the twin tentpoles of cost and corruption. At the same time, Crow says his party is in need of a hard reset before 2028—though, like many, he is still workshopping ideas for what might work.

“There is actually an opportunity to build something new—not rebuild, not go back, not try to reconstitute what once was, because Americans don’t want that,” he says.

Should Democrats take the House this fall, Crow is in prime position to be a senior member of the House Intelligence Committee’s ­majority. Should a Democrat reclaim the White House in 2028, his name is likely to come up on the short lists for Cabinet positions. He also has his eye on Colorado’s Senate seat, and is not shy about a possible White House run down the line.

First, though, Crow has to navigate this tricky political moment, one that has Democrats feeling ascendant but still staring down low approval ratings. It’s not entirely unfamiliar terrain for Crow, who rode an earlier anti-Trump wave while vowing to stand up to party leaders he viewed as failing to meet the moment. Only this time, he’s on the inside.

Impeachment and Iran

Eight years ago, Crow was one of House Democrats’ top recruits—a lawyer and veterans’ advocate who served three tours in Iraq and Afghanistan.

Even still, he was far from a sure thing when he challenged Representative Mike Coffman, a fixture in Colorado Republican circles since Crow was in middle school. “This was an unwinnable race, remember?” Crow recalls with a smirk.

To show he wasn’t running against just Trump, but Washington writ large, Crow vowed not to vote for Nancy Pelosi for Speaker if Democrats won a House majority, which they did. When it came time for the vote, Crow defied the most powerful Democrat in Washington by casting his ballot for Tammy Duckworth, a fellow veteran representing Illinois in the Senate.

“I explained that this was not personal. This was part of a larger effort to usher in that next generation,” Crow recalls.

Ten months later, when it became clear that the Trump impeachment train was leaving the station for its first go-round, Pelosi rang up her former detractor. It was, Crow said later, “like being called into the principal’s office.” Pelosi needed someone with his skill set and temperament to convey the stakes of Trump’s attempts to pressure Ukraine without coming off as a partisan hack. While the House voted to impeach, the Senate declined to convict.

For Crow during that period, death threats became routine. He had an armed guard outside his house. A security detail walked his kids to school. Which brings him to last year. The security had to be called back. His “illegal orders” video brought about another round of threats—including some from Trump that Crow’s office referred to the Capitol Police, according to an email obtained by TIME.

Crow’s national-­security background has helped propel his reach in Congress, where he’s a top Democrat on the House Intelligence Committee as well as the top Democrat on the Armed Services Committee’s spy panel. When House Democrats needed someone to run point on a panel investigating the failed assassination against Trump in Butler, Pa., they tapped Crow. Last week, Crow and Rep. Pramila Jayapal, a Washington Democrat, forced a House vote to halt the war in Iran, with the measure passing 214-208.

Recruiting "streetfighters" to Congress

But it’s his work helping Democrats win back the House that may win him the most chits. As a leader in candidate recruitment for the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee, Crow has his hands in just about every contested race in the country, and is making a point of finding people he believes voters will view as “street fighters.”

“The oath of service I took doesn’t expire,” says JoAnna Mendoza, a retired Marine Corps drill sergeant and Crow recruit who is taking on Representative Juan Ciscomani, an Arizona Republican, in one of the top toss-up races in the country.

Mendoza has the support of Crow and the DCCC well before her primary. It’s a different story in some House races in other states where the DCCC either professed neutrality or backed a different candidate from whomever Crow endorsed through his political action committee, Service First.

Crow’s theory is that some of his preferred candidates—Marine drill sergeants, federal prosecutors—are more likely to excite those who are down on both parties.

The DCCC's chair, Rep. Suzan DelBene from Washington state, is hardly trying to curb his instincts.

“Jason brings a servant leadership ethos and a soldier’s discipline to the job. He knows that voters want fighters who put their local communities first, not undying loyalty to partisan ideology," she tells TIME. "His tireless work at recruiting, mentoring, and raising money to support candidates has been essential in our path back to the majority.”

If his instincts prove right, Crow may bring a whole raft of newcomers to Congress who are loyal to a mentor who helped get them there. Whatever Crow’s future ambitions, a cohort of fellow street fighters might come in handy.

“I have an independent streak to me,” he concedes. “But, you know, when we win, people will be pretty happy about that.”

title: Deluzio Launches Build America Plan to Reindustrialize America
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Pennsylvania Congressman Chris Deluzio (D-PA-17) announced his new Build America Plan to reindustrialize America and grow solid manufacturing jobs. Congressman Deluzio’s plan rejects the era of half-measures and piecemeal tax credits. Instead, it lays out a real industrial strategy to rebuild American manufacturing, invest in skilled workers, and make foreign polluters pay instead of letting them undercut cleaner, American-made products. Congressman Deluzio also released a video highlighting his Build America Plan.

This industrial policy plan follows the Trump Administration’s announcement of additional tariffs on trade partners, including Canada, and analysis showing that the last six years of President Trump’s signature United States Canada Mexico Trade Agreement (USMCA) saw a net loss in United States manufacturing jobs and failed to rebalance our North American trade deficit. This economic approach is failing. Congressman Deluzio believes it is time for America to build big things again—and that means investing in a strong 21st century industrial policy that can herald in a new era of booming American manufacturing.

"Today I’m proud to announce my Build America Plan—a bold vision to reindustrialize our country,” said Congressman Deluzio. “For too long, we’ve seen factories close, job shipped overseas, and entire American communities hollowed out alongside rising costs. The United States used to be the manufacturing powerhouse of the world—and I think it can be again if we stop letting our economic foes undercut us, fighting fire with fire, and make real investments in our workers. I want the next generation to know and inherit an America that builds and creates amazing things.”

Congressman Deluzio's Build America Plan has three pillars and three bills. They are as follows.

Build it HERE

Build America Fund: (bill text)

This bill creates a Manufacturing Sovereign Wealth Fund.to make direct investments and take equity stake in American manufacturing companies to bolster domestic manufacturing

This would allow the nation to keep up with our global economic competitors that subsidize their domestic industry

Extends direct benefit to all Americans through the Build America Dividend: an annual dividend paid out from the revenue raised in the Fund’s investments

The Build America Fund is endorsed by the United Autoworkers (UAW), Teamsters, United Steelworkers (USW), New American Industrial Alliance (NAIA), International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail, and Transportation Workers (SMART), and AFL-CIO.

“Rebuilding our nation’s manufacturing infrastructure requires sustained effort and creative approaches that focus on both onshoring and creating good, community-sustaining jobs. Rep. Deluzio’s “Build America Fund Act” offers new ideas that helps put us on a path toward that goal. The USW looks forward to working with Rep. Deluzio and his congressional colleagues to grow U.S. jobs and industrial capacity.” – United Steelworkers (USW) President Roxanne Brown

“After decades of plant closures and union busting, we need a federal reinvestment strategy that can actively shape markets and take on corporate greed. Congressman Deluzio’s Build America Fund Act is a major step forward in aligning our country’s trade and industrial policies to make that happen. This legislation will ensure the next era of American manufacturing lifts up the working class and supports communities devasted by deindustrialization, offshoring, and a race to the bottom in labor standards." – Rajiv Sicora, United Auto Workers (UAW) Legislative Director

"The Teamsters Union commends Congressman Deluzio for his legislation to bring good union manufacturing jobs back to this country. The United States is home to the most skilled manufacturers and tradespeople in the world—workers who deserve meaningful jobs, family-sustaining wages, and thriving local economies. This bill marks a bold investment in Teamsters and their communities, and we’re proud to support it." – Teamsters General President Sean M. O’Brien

"Building in America again requires an all-of-the-above policy approach. The Build America Fund, a sovereign wealth fund that would invest directly in American manufacturing and industrial capacity, would expand builders' access to needed capital. We thank Rep. Deluzio for his leadership and ongoing support of American manufacturing." – Julius Krein, CEO, New American Industrial Alliance

"This is a common-sense bill that invests in SMART members, American jobs and our country’s manufacturing industry — prioritizing our national interests while supporting the people who build and move our nation every day. We thank Rep. Deluzio for introducing this bill, and we urge every pro-worker member of Congress to support it.” – International Association of Sheet Metal, Air, Rail and Transportation Workers Union (SMART) Spokesperson

Build it STRONG (bill text)

Pathway to Trades Act

Brings the trades back into the classroom by tying federal dollars to career and technical education

Expands opportunities for America’s young people beyond four-year college programs

Build it RIGHT

Fighting Foreign Polluters Act

Puts a fee on foreign polluters flooding our markets with their high-emission products and dirtying our air and waters

Specifies which goods are subject to this fee

Includes an incentive structure for domestic manufacturing

Reinforces the ideal that when the U.S. builds, we do it better and cleaner than anywhere else

title: Maryland Democrats Urge FERC to Protect Marylanders from Rising Electricity Costs Due to Out-of-State Data Centers
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Congresswoman Sarah Elfreth (MD-03) joined U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks and U.S. Representatives Steny Hoyer, Kweisi Mfume, Jamie Raskin, Glenn Ivey, April McClain Delaney, and Johnny Olszewski (all D-Md.) in calling on the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to take action to ensure Marylanders are not forced to bear skyrocketing electricity costs due to increasing energy demand from data centers located outside of the state. The lawmakers urged FERC to require PJM Interconnection (PJM) to implement strong protections that would ensure fair energy costs for Marylanders after PJM, the grid operator responsible for coordinating electricity transmission in the region, assigned roughly $2 billion in costs to Maryland ratepayers for infrastructure that is needed primarily to serve out-of-state data centers. The lawmakers’ letter supports a complaint at FERC filed by the Maryland Office of People’s Counsel challenging PJM’s existing transmission cost allocation rules.

“As members of the Maryland Congressional Delegation, we write regarding a pressing matter that has the potential to significantly raise energy costs for our constituents. PJM Interconnection LLC’s (PJM) existing transmission cost allocation rules result in the unjust assignment of billions of dollars in costs to Marylanders, contributing to unaffordable electricity bills,” the lawmakers begin.

On the rising costs of electricity due to data centers outside of Maryland, the lawmakers write, “Data centers being built outside of Maryland are driving one of the largest transmission expansions in PJM’s history. Across its three most recent regional transmission planning rounds, PJM has advanced $22 billion in projects needed principally to serve data centers. Under PJM’s current cost allocation rules, roughly $2 billion of those costs have been assigned to Maryland ratepayers rather than the data centers that are driving the demand.”

“Marylanders are already shouldering the immense burden of skyrocketing electricity costs, and it is unjust and unreasonable to force our constituents to subsidize the energy infrastructure needs of the wealthiest companies in the world. Unless the Commission acts, our constituents will pay an estimated $1.6 billion on their electric bills over the next ten years for these projects alone, and $823 million of that total cost will fall on residential customers, which equates to roughly $345 for the average customer,” the lawmakers continue.

On PJM’s current cost allocation rules, the Maryland lawmakers note, “PJM’s cost allocation rules have not kept pace with the build out of hyperscale data centers, just one of which can equal the electricity demand of a small city. PJM’s current rules spread costs broadly across the region regardless of where, and for whom, the underlying projects are actually needed. Maryland regulators have no ability to assign such costs to data centers located in other states, and with tens of thousands of megawatts of additional data center demand growth projected across PJM over the next two decades, our constituents face billions of dollars in further charges absent Commission action to address this unjust and unreasonable cost allocation. Furthermore, because much of the forecasted growth in data center energy demand is speculative, our constituents bear the unacceptable risk of paying for projects built to serve potential data centers that are never built due to any number of external reasons.”

“We urge the Commission to act expeditiously to provide relief from these costs for Maryland ratepayers, including as requested in OPC’s complaint. Thank you for your consideration of this important issue that is essential to ensuring just and reasonable energy costs for our constituents,” the lawmakers conclude.

The full text of the letter is available HERE.

title: Fedorchak applauds Committee passage of bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act
text:
Washington, D.C. – Congresswoman Julie Fedorchak (R-N.D.) was among the 52 members of the U.S. House Energy and Commerce Committee who unanimously passed the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act (H.R. 9340) this week.

The legislation directs utilities to protect American families and small businesses from increased electricity costs driven by data centers by requiring them to cover the full costs of service. The bill also requires up front financial assurances to mitigate the risks of demand changing after grid investments are made. The bill now advances to the full House for consideration.

“No American should pay higher utility bills because of the infrastructure needed to serve new, large electricity users like data centers. Republicans and Democrats are united in this belief and support the commonsense principle: those who cause costs on the system must pay for those costs—not hardworking families, seniors on fixed incomes, or small businesses,” Fedorchak said. “North Dakota requires large-load customers to cover the costs they impose on the electric system, protecting existing ratepayers while supporting economic growth. That's a model the rest of the country should follow, and the bipartisan Ratepayer Protection Act advances this principle.”

"We have met with numerous stakeholders, including the data center industry and big tech, state regulators, utilities, and others," said Chairman Guthrie. "But it has become clear that across the entire industry there is one entity uniquely positioned to stand up for families and communities who are the ones paying electricity bills-and that is this Committee, and our colleagues in Congress. The Ratepayer Protection Act will ensure that data centers pay their own way, instead of passing costs onto hardworking families. Thank you to Congressman Gabe Evans for leading this vital legislation that will protect Americans from rising electricity costs while ensuring the United States is positioned to win the race for AI dominance."

The Ratepayer Protection Actestablishes a framework for states to evaluate policies that prevent costs from being shifted to existing ratepayers. Specifically, the bill:

Requires state utility commissions to consider policies that allocate the costs of serving new large-load customers fairly.

Reinforces the longstanding "cost causation" principle that customers creating the need for new infrastructure should bear those expenses.

Helps protect residential customers and small businesses from subsidizing infrastructure built primarily to serve data centers and other large electricity users.

Encourages transparent and predictable cost allocation for companies making significant investments in new facilities.

As a former member of the North Dakota Public Service Commission, Fedorchak has long advocated for policies that prevent costs from being shifted onto families while supporting responsible economic development. North Dakota has successfully implemented rate structures requiring large-load customers to cover costs they imposed on the electric system, leading to over $30 million in savings for customers.

RELEASE: Friedman Unveils $1,031,000 Federal Investment to Strengthen Community Safety in Glendale Ahead of the 2028 Olympic Games
text:
Above: Friedman announcing a new federal investment in community safety at the Glendale Police Department.

GLENDALE, CA — Today, July 27, 2026, U.S. Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30) announced a new $1,031,000 federal investment to strengthen community safety in Glendale ahead of the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic Games. Friedman secured the investment after Glendale officials asked for help securing these tools needed to keep the community safe as the region prepares to welcome the world and for years to come.

A recording of the press announcement can be found here.

The federal investment Friedman secured allows Glendale to expand and modernize its Real Time Information Center without putting the cost on local taxpayers or diverting funds from other essential city services.

“Glendale came to me with a real need, I made it a priority, and I fought in Washington to get it done,” said Congresswoman Laura Friedman (CA-30). “Keeping our neighborhoods safe should never depend on the size of a city’s budget. This is a million dollars to help our officers respond faster, prevent crime, and protect our families, and not a cent of it comes out of the pockets of Glendale taxpayers. The Games come and go, but this investment stays. I will keep fighting to bring our tax dollars home and keep our communities safe long after the closing ceremony.”

“Congresswoman Friedman has always understood the importance of utilizing technology to keep communities safe, and she continues that hard work now in Congress, bringing very necessary funds that will not cost Glendale's taxpayers additional dollars. Sometimes even more important than the person who wears the badge is the information that arrives before they arrive. We need to give them information that helps them do their jobs better and safer, and that's what this investment of over $1,000,000 is about,” said Glendale Mayor Ardy Kassakhian. “We couldn't ask for a better partner as someone who came out of local government and went up the ranks at the state level and the federal level.”

“I want to start off by thanking Congresswoman Laura Friedman for her continued investment into the city of Glendale and her continued support for public safety, not just with the police department, but with the fire department as well,” said Glendale Police Chief Robert Williams. “Our real-time intelligence center has already helped investigators solve murders, violent crimes, and residential burglaries by providing critical leads that might otherwise be unavailable. At the end of the day, this isn't about equipment. It's about giving our officers every advantage to respond more quickly and investigate more effectively.”

THE $1,031,000 FEDERAL INVESTMENT WILL:

Nearly double the city’s public safety camera coverage in public spaces, from 44 cameras today to between 90 and 100.

Upgrade Glendale’s Real Time Information Center.

Strengthen the city’s real-time information capabilities using the existing team of four specialists, with no new staff required.

Improve response times so officers can respond faster and with better information when someone calls for help.

The investment keeps all data under local control. Video is stored on the city’s own systems, is not accessible to any outside vendor or other agency, and is retained for 30 days before deletion.

Any request to share footage goes through the City of Glendale’s own policies and process first, keeping decisions in the hands of officials accountable to the community.

The announcement is the latest in a series of federal investments Friedman has secured to prepare the region for the 2028 Games, all at no cost to local taxpayers. In April, she unveiled a $1,092,000 investment to replace the nearly 100-year-old water and wastewater systems at the Rose Bowl Stadium. In July, she announced $500,000 to bring shade, seating, and real-time arrival information to LA Metro bus stops and Metrolink rail stations across the district.

Friedman was joined today by Glendale Mayor Ardy Kassakhian, Glendale Police Chief Robert Williams, and officers from the Glendale Police Department.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Hosts First Responder Roundtable in Paramus to Hear Directly from North Jersey Police, Fire, and EMS Leaders
text:
Above: Gottheimer meets with first responders and public safety leaders from across the Fifth District.

PARAMUS, N.J. — On July 24, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted a First Responder Roundtable in Paramus with more than seventy fire chiefs, police chiefs, sheriffs, prosecutors, and union leaders from across North Jersey to hear directly about the challenges facing local departments and to discuss his work in Washington to support the hard-working people who keep Jersey families safe.

“This room is full of people who run toward danger while everybody else is running the other way,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “On behalf of the entire Fifth District, thank you for your service and your sacrifice. I’m proud of what we’ve done, but I’m not satisfied. I’m going to keep fighting for it in Washington, the same way I have for the last decade, because the people in this room are the reason our towns are safe.”

Immediately following the roundtable, Gottheimer announced more than $42 million in Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) funding to strengthen law enforcement and keep Jersey communities safe. This funding comes on top of the $8.5 million previously secured to protect Jersey during the World Cup, totaling more than $50 million clawed back for New Jersey law enforcement since June.

Gottheimer highlighted the pressures he hears across the District: fire departments running pumpers 25 or 30 years past their service life while new trucks approach a million dollars; smaller police departments struggling to compete for recruits; and EMS squads funded call by call but expected to stand ready around the clock. More than 94 percent of local police departments nationwide have fewer than 100 sworn officers.

Since 2017, Gottheimer has clawed back more than $17 million in Community Oriented Policing Services (COPS) resources, more than $11 million in Assistance to Firefighters Grants (AFG), and nearly $7 million in Staffing for Adequate Fire and Emergency Response (SAFER) grants.

This year, he helped push Edward Byrne Memorial Justice Assistance Grant (Byrne JAG) resources from $499 million to $964 million nationally and COPS resources from $417 million to $800 million, and secured $8.5 million for World Cup security and $30 million for bulletproof vests.

As the Co-Chair of the Law Enforcement Caucus and a member of the Fire Services Caucus, Gottheimer helped pass the Fire Grants and Safety Act into law and introduced the Invest to Protect Act, which passed the House, to help small departments recruit, retain, and support their officers. He also helped pass the Social Security Fairness Act, repealing the Windfall Elimination Provision (WEP) and Government Pension Offset (GPO) penalties, and secured full funding for the World Trade Center Health Program for the life of the program.

title: ICYMI: Hinson Honors Vietnam Veteran with Purple Heart
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congresswoman Ashley Hinson (IA-02) presented Vietnam veteran Specialist Lewis Robinson with the Purple Heart he earned for wounds sustained while serving in Vietnam more than five decades ago. After Robinson's request to correct his military record was denied in 2012, Hinson's office worked alongside him for more than a year to help secure reconsideration of his case. In 2025, the Army approved the request, corrected his military record, and authorized the award.

During the ceremony, Hinson reflected on Robinson's service and our responsibility to ensure America's veterans receive the care, benefits, and recognition they have earned.

— Remarks as Delivered —

"Specialist Robinson answered the call in 1969, serving in the United States Army during one of the most difficult periods in our country's history. Like so many veterans, he did his duty without asking for recognition. He served because he felt it was the right thing to do. As Americans, we enjoy freedoms that so many around the world can only dream of.

"Those freedoms were secured by brave men and women who answered the call to serve, often at tremendous personal sacrifice. In March of 1971, while serving with the 14th Engineer Battalion during operations in Vietnam, his battalion came under enemy attack. Rocket-propelled grenades and small arms fire struck the convoy, and Specialist Robinson was wounded from the shrapnel. For his courageous service, the wounds he sustained, and being in the direct line of fire, he earned the Purple Heart medal. Unfortunately, that recognition did not come when it should have. No veteran should have to spend years pushing to receive a medal they earned in combat.

"After Specialist Robinson's request to correct his military record was denied, he never gave up. Working alongside our office, and after years of waiting, the Army corrected his record and approved the award he had earned all those years ago. While we cannot give back the years that passed, we can make sure history is set right. We have a responsibility to keep our promises to the men and women who served. That means making sure veterans receive the care, benefits, and recognition they've earned promptly — not years later.

"Specialist Robinson, thank you for your courage under fire, your sacrifice, and your unwavering service to our nation. We are grateful to your wife, Barbara, and to your family and friends who have stood beside you through this journey."

title: Houchin Introduces Bipartisan Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act
text:
July 27, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Erin Houchin (R-IN-09) and Congresswoman Kim Schrier, M.D. (D-WA-08) recently introduced the bipartisan Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act, alongside cosponsors Representatives Jefferson Shreve (R-IN), Glenn "GT" Thompson (R-PA), Jill Tokuda (D-HI), and Jennifer McClellan (D-VA). Companion legislation was introduced in the Senate by Senators Josh Hawley (R-MO), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), and Mark Kelly (D-AZ). The legislation strengthens cybersecurity at rural hospitals by directing the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to develop a comprehensive rural hospital cybersecurity workforce strategy, expand cybersecurity training resources, and improve preparedness against growing cyber threats.

"Rural hospitals are often operating with limited staff and resources, yet they're expected to defend against increasingly sophisticated cyberattacks," said Rep. Houchin. "When a rural hospital is forced offline, patient care is put at risk. This bipartisan bill is a practical step toward giving rural providers the workforce, training, and tools they need to strengthen their cybersecurity and continue serving their communities."

“As a doctor and a patient, I know we must protect hospitals from cyberattacks," said Rep. Schrier, M.D. “Rural hospitals in particular often lack the funding and workforce necessary to prevent cyberattacks and some in Washington have already been impacted. This bill will give rural hospitals the tools they need to keep patients safe, protect personal data, and secure medical systems."

"Rural hospitals in Indiana's Sixth District are often the only option for Hoosier families who need care close to home,” said Rep. Shreve. “These hospitals don’t have the resources to hire a cybersecurity team, but they still need to keep their patients’ private information secure. This bill gives them the training and tools they need to do that. I'm glad to join Rep. Houchin on this important legislation."

"In our complex world, it is imperative that we safeguard sensitive personal information and medical records from cybercriminals," Rep. Thompson said. "The Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act aims to protect patient information by helping develop, promote, and expand the rural hospital cybersecurity workforce, particularly through education and training programs tailored to the needs of rural hospitals, such as those in Pennsylvania."

"For rural hospitals, a cyberattack isn't just a disruption to technology, it can become a disruption to care,” said Rep. Tokuda. “This legislation helps ensure rural providers can continue delivering lifesaving care by having the resources, training, and workforce support they need to protect patient data, respond to threats, and continue serving their communities."

“In our rapidly changing digital age, cybersecurity threats continue to grow. Rural hospitals and health clinics often lack the resources and personnel to defend against these threats,” said Rep. McClellan. “The Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act develops a comprehensive workforce training program to protect our rural communities from attacks that could exploit vulnerabilities in our health care system and undermine access to care. I am pleased to work on a bipartisan basis with Congresswoman Houchin to bolster our security measures to help maintain a strong care network.”

“For many years, TRIMEDX has worked with, and provided medical device service for, small town and rural hospitals throughout the country. Already challenged by increasing cost pressures, we have seen first- hand how vulnerable rural hospitals are to cybersecurity attacks and we support any efforts for the development of strategies to address cyber challenges,” said Kristi McDermott, TRIMEDX Chief Operating Officer. “Accordingly, TRIMEDX applauds Rep. Houchin and Rep. Schrier for introducing this strong bipartisan bill which seeks to address growing cybersecurity challenges, to include workforce development strategies, in rural hospitals throughout the country.”

The Rural Hospital Cybersecurity Enhancement Act requires HHS to:

Develop a comprehensive rural hospital cybersecurity workforce development strategy that considers public-private partnerships, cybersecurity curricula, workforce training, and policy recommendations.

Make instructional materials available to help rural hospitals train staff on fundamental cybersecurity practices.

Provide annual updates to Congress on the implementation of the strategy and any related workforce development initiatives.

Cyberattacks against hospitals have become more frequent and more sophisticated, placing patient care, medical records, and critical healthcare infrastructure at risk. Rural hospitals are particularly vulnerable because they often lack the resources to recruit and retain dedicated cybersecurity professionals.

The legislation is endorsed by the American Hospital Association, Blue Cross Blue Shield Association, National Rural Health Association, American Academy of Family Physicians, TRIMEDX, and the Alliance for Quality Medical Device Servicing.

The Senate companion legislation has twice advanced out of the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

Read the full bill text here.

title: Huffman: Trump's Loyalist-Stacked Council Votes to Bulldoze America's History
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman (D-Calif.) issued the following statement after the Advisory Council on Historic Preservation voted to gut Section 106 of the National Historic Preservation Act, the rule that requires the federal government to consider harm to historic and sacred places, and to hear from the people affected, before approving construction projects:

“Donald Trump packed this council with loyalists and gave them one job: tear down the safeguards that protect America's history so he and his billionaire friends can build whatever they want, wherever they want. Today they delivered.

“Right now, a developer has to stop and listen before paving over a tribal burial ground, a Revolutionary War battlefield, or the church where your grandparents were married. Trump's council wants to end that and cut tribal nations, states, counties, towns, and communities out of that conversation entirely.

“This is what Trump does. He tore up national monuments for his donors. He's spending hundreds of millions on gold ballrooms and birthday parades while Americans struggle to afford groceries and rent. Now he wants to bulldoze the places that hold our history so his cronies can get richer.

“Sacred sites and historic places belong to all of us, and they don't come back once they're gone. The council should kill this proposal before permanent damage is done. Democrats will fight this every step of the way. Trump's billionaire buddies bought their seats at the table. We're going to make sure the American people never lose theirs.”

title: Smith Tours Flood Damage in Reynolds County
text:
REYNOLDS COUNTY, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) toured flood damage across Reynolds County today, including at Valley Springs Youth Ranch and Black River Baptist Church. On July 9 and 10, Reynolds County saw as much as 12 inches of rain in a three-hour time frame, causing extensive damage to homes, farms, and community buildings across the area.

Congressman Smith said, “What I saw today in Reynolds County was heartbreaking. Families have lost their homes, farmers have lost equipment and livelihoods they spent decades building, and a church that feeds well over a hundred people through its food drives had its sanctuary destroyed. The scale of what this community is facing is enormous, and I’m grateful for every first responder, volunteer, neighbor, and local leader who has stepped up to help during this difficult time. My office will continue working to connect these families and organizations with every state and federal resource available as they rebuild.”

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON BLOOMBERG: “PEOPLE ARE DROWNING IN THIS FAILED TRUMP ECONOMY”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on Bloomberg TV, where he emphasized that with less than 100 days until the midterm election, Democrats remain committed to fighting for an affordable economy and to lower costs, protect access to healthcare and hold the crooks accountable.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Life has gotten far too expensive under Donald Trump and the Republican-controlled Congress. Donald Trump promised to lower the high cost of living on day one. But what we’ve seen is that costs haven’t gone down, of course, in America, costs have gone up. Democrats have been focused on doing a variety of different things to push back aggressively against the policies that Republicans have jammed down our throats, which is making life more expensive. For instance, we’re pushing back against the Trump tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year in terms of increased groceries and goods and other household items. At the same period of time, Democrats are focused on ending Donald Trump’s reckless war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed gas prices all across the country, while actually putting Iran in a stronger position than they were in prior to the war starting.

JOE MATHIEU: I want to get specific. If you in fact win the House, if you’re the majority party in the House, what you might be able to do to address prices. And you talked about some ideas yesterday, including repealing what the President calls his One Big Beautiful Bill. Is that the answer here? Is there more that Democrats have in mind?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we want to make sure that healthcare is affordable to every single American. And there are several steps that we need to take, including…making sure that the Affordable Care Act tax credits actually are extended, and repealing…the Medicaid cuts in the One Big Ugly Bill, which have created a situation where the healthcare of more than 14 million Americans is at risk.

JOE MATHIEU: How do you do that? Do you need to see the Senate turn Democratic as well to actually repeal what’s been already put in place?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, here’s the thing—we saw a couple of weeks ago the Congress be able move a bipartisan bill forward on housing affordability that is designed to alleviate some of the cost pressures that exist from the housing market. And we got that bill into law over the objection of Donald Trump. So what is clear is that, even in a context where Republicans have complete control of government, we’ve been able to move some things forward. Certainly, if we have the House and the House plus the Senate, we’ll be in a stronger position to drive the affordability agenda forward.

JOE MATHIEU: You mentioned the President’s war with Iran. We’ve already seen the House and the Senate pass War Powers legislation. Leader Jeffries, presuming you take the gavel, knowing that the President has blown right through these War Powers Acts, is there anything else that you can do to put collars on this effort?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to continue to aggressively push the effort to push back against this reckless war of choice. It’s deeply unpopular with the American people, and we have to sustain the intensity. Donald Trump has unfortunately got us involved in this situation without any plan, any objective, any clear exit strategy and now the American people are clearly paying the price. One of the things we have to take a look at is the amount of taxpayer dollars that are being spent to fund Donald Trump’s reckless war machine and effort in the Middle East. It’s clear to us that the American people would much rather their taxpayer dollars being spent to make their life more affordable. That’s why we’re committed to lowering the cost of groceries, lowering the cost of gas, lowering the cost of housing and making sure that healthcare is affordable for every single American.

JOE MATHIEU: How do you lower the cost of gas without ending the war, though? We’re at $4.11. Mr. Leader, it’s been suggested even by the President we eliminate the federal gas tax. Is that something that you would support?

LEADER JEFFRIES: The most significant thing that could be done right now to lower the price of gas for everyday Americans who are suffocating at the pump is to end Donald Trump’s reckless war of choice in the Middle East and we’re going to continue to relentlessly make the case that that needs to happen.

JOE MATHIEU: Where are you on the gas tax then? Is that something that should be removed at least temporarily?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, the gas tax, of course, is something that’s in place to help fund our desperately needed infrastructure on highways and beyond. And so I think it’s something that—the Republicans put it on the table, we’ll have to evaluate it, but clearly, the most significant thing that could be done at this moment, as opposed to a temporary measure, is to end the war in Iran.

JOE MATHIEU: You know, we start talking about affordability, Mr. Leader, it creeps into all kinds of other stories, including now data centers, which have become a massive political issue. We’ve been struck by how often it comes up when we talk to voters around the country. And of course, the state of New York, where you’re right now sitting, has become an important guidepost here, at least for some who believe that there should be restrictions on data centers. As you well know, the Governor has put a one-year moratorium on new data centers in the state. There are a lot of different ways to get to this. We spoke with Byron Donalds the other day, the Republican from Florida, who has a bill that wouldn’t put on a moratorium, but would take data centers off the grid and would compel them to have their own water supply. How do you get to this in a way that makes voters happy?

LEADER JEFFRIES: House Democrats have launched a Commission on Artificial Intelligence and the Innovation Economy to thoughtfully engage with community-based organizations and groups, advocacy organizations, as well as industry stakeholders, to try to evaluate the best possible path forward. But what is clear is that we have to put—at the center of any effort—making sure we’re not doing anything to exacerbate the affordability crisis that everyday Americans are experiencing in every area of life. And that, of course, includes figuring out how to drive down utility costs and the cost of water bills, for instance, as opposed to increasing the strain on the system in ways that would actually drive up costs. And so I think this has been a state-by-state effort up until this point, with states landing in a variety of different places in terms of approach. I do think in the new Congress, we’re going to have to come together and think about how we can address many of these issues nationally.

JOE MATHIEU: Well, I’ll tell you what, I’d love to ask you about some of the strokes behind this midterm cycle, which is what we’re talking about with 99 days to go. And I can’t walk into a room in Washington without hearing about the SAVE America Act. That’s, of course, because of the amount of attention the President has paid to it. Leader Jeffries, were Republicans successful in salvaging this? Will it cost Democrats votes if it becomes law? Where are you on this? Have you talked to John Thune about it?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I haven’t talked to John Thune, but he’s made clear repeatedly that the so-called SAVE America Act, which is really all about voter suppression, is actually dead on arrival in the Senate and there’s nothing that Donald Trump can do about it. What’s extraordinary to me is that he continues to actually waste time trying to rig the midterm election in a variety of different ways, as opposed to actually solving problems for everyday Americans, including the problems that he promised to address, like lowering the high cost of living on day one. And instead, of course, has done the opposite. He’s made clear he thinks the affordability crisis is a hoax. Donald Trump has said very publicly he doesn’t think about the personal financial situation of the American people. It’s all very extraordinary. He’s even said he loves the inflation. Now, our focus is going to be quite different because it’s clear people are paying too much at the gas pump. People are paying too much for food. People can’t afford their rent or their mortgage. And that shouldn’t be the case in America, the wealthiest country in the history of the world. We want to work together—

JOE MATHIEU: Do you expect troops at polling places, Leader Jeffries? I’m sorry to interrupt, but are we going to see ICE agents at polling places if SAVE America does not go into effect?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I certainly think the American people would outright reject that, and we are going to put together the largest voter protection effort in the history of the country. We know we won’t see troops at polling places because the Supreme Court, in a 6-3 decision in December, has ripped away Donald Trump’s efforts to try to actually federalize the National Guard. He does not have the power to do that. In terms of ICE agents, we’re continuing to push for a ban on ICE agents showing up at sensitive locations. That includes polling sites, but it also includes schools, it includes hospitals and it certainly includes houses of worship. The American people want to see immigration enforcement in this country that’s fair, just and humane.

JOE MATHIEU: I’m wondering where you’re looking here as we consider the money in this midterm election cycle. There’s been some tough reporting about the DNC. And you probably saw the write-up in The New York Timeswith a frustrated Chair, Ken Martin, throwing his phone in one scene. It was described as dysfunction and despair. Leader Jeffries, when you talk to the DCCC, though, they’ve got a lot of candidates who are outraising their Republican rivals. But the fact is, on the party level, there’s a great disparity. And I’m wondering if you care, if history is at your back to a point where the money will not make a difference?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We certainly need to continue to raise the resources necessary to both reelect all of our incredible frontline incumbents who are in the battleground districts across the nation, while making sure that our candidates who are trying to flip red seats blue have the ability to communicate their message. We’re all fighting for an affordable America. That’s what unites us. That is a very powerful narrative that we’ll have available to us as we communicate with voters over the next 100 or so days. Now, as you pointed out from a DCCC standpoint, we just recently reported outraising Republicans, our House counterparts. We’ve been competitive with them all cycle. And, of course, some of the outside groups that work in support of House Democratic candidates have posted record-breaking numbers.

JOE MATHIEU: If you take the House, does Ken Martin keep his job?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, listen, I’m focused right now, I think we all are, including Ken Martin, on November 3. And under the DNC’s partnership, what we have seen—Ken Martin’s leadership—is Democrats winning races all across the country for the last 18-plus months. And the DNC has quietly been involved in a lot of those races where we have seen success. And so let’s all keep the main thing the main thing. I know that’s what Ken Martin is doing. And he’s focused on helping Democrats win elections all across America, and then all of us will figure out the path forward. But I think Ken Martin’s term is four years, and there’s no reason to believe at this point that he’s going anywhere.

JOE MATHIEU: Okay, I appreciate your answering that. And I guess I’d wrap by asking you about—some of those candidates who won in those races you point to were Democratic Socialists. And there’s been a big question about big tent, Leader Jeffries. You don’t need me to tell you that. And I’m wondering if you see that as being part of the recipe to take the House in the midterm elections, or if a more moderate approach is the long-term success story for Democrats.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Our success is going to hinge on convincing the American people that, as Democrats, we’re fighting for an affordable America. We recognize the cost of living is way too high. Far too many people are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive. They can barely survive. People are drowning in this failed Trump economy. And we’re committed to making a difference in all of the areas that matter. That’s lowering grocery costs, lowering gas prices, lowering housing costs and, of course, making sure healthcare is affordable to every single American. Let me make sure as well to point out—look, I believe that the Democratic Party is at its strongest, and America is at its strongest, when we—our country—focus on having a strong floor and no ceiling because in this country you work very hard, right? You play by the rules. You should—there should be no ceiling to the success that you can achieve for yourself, for your family, for your community. At the same period of time, America, the wealthiest country in the history of the world, should always have a strong floor. And we know what that looks like. That’s Social Security, that’s Medicare, that Medicaid, that’s the Affordable Care Act, that’s veterans’ benefits, that’s nutritional assistance. By the way, every single one of these things brought to you by your friendly neighborhood Democratic Party, designed to ensure that there’s a strong floor for working-class Americans, for middle-class Americans and for everyday Americans. And I think that, at its core, is what the Democratic Party has been about, is about and will continue to be about into the future.

JOE MATHIEU: And the DSA helps to reinforce that floor?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I mean, the DSA can speak for themselves. I’m not a part of the DSA. I’m not a member of the DSA. The DSA can speak to their particular platform. We’ve got 215-plus Democrats in the House of Representatives. And what I can tell you is that what unites all of us and our candidates out throughout the country, who are working hard, is that we’re committed to actually making life more affordable for the American people.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: $333K Awarded to CUC For Sinlaku Recovery Efforts
