Introduced the HELPER Act to make homeownership more obtainable for Florida heroes, including law enforcement officers;

Co-Sponsored the HALT Fentanyl Act, which was signed into law by President Trump. The new law assists law enforcement officers get fentanyl traffickers off the streets and permanently classifies fentanyl-related substances under Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act;

Sponsored the RIPPLE Act, which would expand the 287(g) program and provide resources to state law enforcement to more efficiently get criminal illegal aliens out of communities; and

Advanced six bills to support law enforcement, strengthen public safety and deliver critical tools to officers out of the Judiciary Committee during Police Week earlier this year.

As Florida’s Attorney General, Senator Moody created many programs to recognize the selfless efforts of law enforcement officers, including her Back the Blue, Thin Line Tribute, and Sunshine Salute programs. title: In Letter, Murray Demands Answers from DoD on Delayed PFAS Cleanup at Military Bases, Including Joint Base Lewis-McChord and Yakima Training Center
text:
***LETTER HERE***

Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), Vice Chair of the Senate Appropriations Committee, sent a letter to Assistant Secretary of Defense Dale R. Marks expressing her concern over recent reports that the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) is delaying its planned investigations and remediation efforts for perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS), also known as “forever chemicals.”

In her letter, Senator Murray expressed concern about the Department of Defense’s latest delays to PFAS cleanup efforts at military installations across the country, including in Washington state and called for greater clarity. She also requested a briefing by August 21 explaining the delays and the Department’s plans to protect affected communities and pressed DoD to get answers about the delayed cleanup timeline, PFAS remediation efforts, funding, and communication with impacted communities.

“Now, after delaying its PFAS cleanup program last year, the Department has announced additional delays that push cleanup timelines back by an average of a decade. The delays will affect sites in 42 states across the nation, including two installations in my home state of Washington: Yakima Training Center will be delayed by 13.5 years and Joint Base Lewis-McChord will be delayed 17 years. Not only am I concerned by the delay itself, but I am also disappointed by the way the Department executed this decision. Instead of consulting with community leaders and announcing the delays to the public, the Department instead chose to quietly remove the previous cleanup schedule from its website and publish new timelines. This is ultimately a violation of trust between military leaders and their surrounding communities,” Senator Murray wrote in her letter to Assistant Secretary of Defense Dale Marks.

Senator Murray has been persistent in pushing for oversight and resources to address PFAS contamination for many years and, as the top Democrat on the Senate Appropriations Committee, she has secured major investments in remediating PFAS pollution through annual appropriations bills.

When Senator Murray chaired the Appropriations Committee, she secured $473.6 million for PFAS and aqueous film forming foam (AFFF) clean up and remediation in the Fiscal Year 2024 defense funding bill, and an additional $50 million above the President’s budget request for PFAS-related cleanup activities at former military installations in the Fiscal Year 2024 Military Construction funding bill—both bills were signed into law in March 2024. In a previous letter sent in October 2024, Murray urged DoD to use the funding she helped secure to meet new EPA standards on PFAS contamination and redouble their efforts to address PFAS at military bases.

In 2025, Senator Murray fought to secure additional resources for PFAS cleanup. In the Senate Military Construction funding bill for Fiscal Year 2026, she secured an additional $50 million above the President’s budget request for PFAS remediation and cleanup.

Over the years, Murray has called on the EPA to deliver on its PFAS Action Plan, pressed DoD and EPA for answers on reports of efforts to weaken contamination standards and pushed for additional federal resources to address water contamination near military bases. Senator Murray has also fought to include firefighters in studies on the effects on workers exposed to PFAS on the job, and demanded that the Navy take every step necessary to address PFAS contamination in Kitsap County, among much else.

The full letter is available HERE and below:

Dear Assistant Secretary Marks:

I am writing to express my deep concern regarding the latest delays to the Department’s efforts to remediate water sources contaminated with perfluoroalkyl and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS). This most recent delay, which will push back the Department’s remediation timelines by an average of a decade, will have severe consequences for military communities living around nearly 200 military installations with PFAS-contaminated water.

PFAS chemicals, which are commonly referred to as “forever chemicals” due to their inability to degrade naturally, persist in soil and water for decades. When people drink water contaminated with PFAS, these chemicals can build up in the body over time and cause serious health problems. Growing research shows that PFAS exposure is linked to major health concerns, including certain types of cancers, fertility issues, and can damage the immune system. Military bases and their surrounding communities are particularly affected by PFAS due to their long history of using Aqueous Film Forming Foam (AFFF) for firefighting.

In 2017, the Department began investigating the extent of contamination at individual military installations. Since then, Congress has appropriated over $3.1 billion to support the Department’s PFAS remediation efforts. In last year’s defense spending bill, I provided an additional $107 million for PFAS cleanup and related activities.

Despite these efforts, this administration has failed to prioritize providing safe drinking water for military communities even within its massive $1.15 trillion budget request for the Department. Additionally, it has attempted to distance itself from this responsibility. In May, the Department submitted a legislative proposal to Congress that would eliminate reporting requirements for PFAS contamination.

Now, after delaying its PFAS cleanup program last year, the Department has announced additional delays that push cleanup timelines back by an average of a decade. The delays will affect sites in 42 states across the nation, including two installations in my home state of Washington: Yakima Training Center will be delayed by 13.5 years and Joint Base Lewis-McChord will be delayed 17 years.

Not only am I concerned by the delay itself, but I am also disappointed by the way the Department executed this decision. Instead of consulting with community leaders and announcing the delays to the public, the Department instead chose to quietly remove the previous cleanup schedule from its website and publish new timelines. This is ultimately a violation of trust between military leaders and their surrounding communities.

In order to provide greater clarity for residents affected by these delays, I request a briefing no later than August 21 with an explanation for the most recent delays and how they relate to the delays announced in 2025. Additionally, please provide written responses to the following questions:

1. Why did the Department extend the timelines in the investigation of PFAS contamination at Joint Base Lewis-McChord and Yakima Training Center?

a. How was it determined which bases would be impacted by the delay?

b. How is the Department working in the short-term and the long-term to support communities impacted by the delays in PFAS cleanup?

2. Has any funding dedicated to PFAS contamination remediation been redirected to other priorities unrelated to PFAS? 3. Does the Department still plan on banning the purchase and use of firefighting foam containing PFAS by September 30, 2026?

a. What actions is the Department taking to find alternative chemicals to use to put out fires on the airfield?

4. How were the changes in timelines associated with PFAS investigations communicated to the affected military installations and their surrounding communities?

a. Who was notified of the timeline changes?

b. How will you work with community leaders near affected installations to provide clean water to residents?

c. Why was there no public announcement prior to the adjustment of timelines?

The Department has a responsibility to ensure the health and safety of its service members, their families, and surrounding communities. These delays are a danger to people’s health and could have other long-term consequences.

Thank you for your time and attention to this important matter.

###

title: As Trump Escalates Attacks on Immigrants, Padilla Renews Push to Expand Pathways to Lawful Permanent Residency
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — As the Trump Administration continues its cruel and systematic attacks on immigrant communities in California and across the country, U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Immigration Subcommittee, renewed his call to pass his legislation to provide a pathway to lawful permanent residency for millions of long-term U.S. residents. Padilla’s bill would provide a commonsense fix to our outdated immigration system to counter President Trump’s targeting of long-term undocumented immigrant communities.

Introduced a year ago, Padilla’s Renewing Immigration Provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929 would update the existing Registry provision of the Immigration and Nationality Act by adjusting the Registry date to meet current circumstances so that an immigrant may qualify to apply for lawful permanent resident status if they have lived in the U.S. continuously for at least seven years before filing an application, do not have a criminal record, and meet all other current green card eligibility requirements.

“A year ago, I introduced this bill to push back against the Trump Administration’s cruel treatment of hardworking immigrants,” said Senator Padilla. “Since then, President Trump’s campaign of fear has only escalated, with families living under constant uncertainty despite having built their lives in this country. Congress cannot continue to ignore millions of long-term residents who contribute to our economy and communities every day. It’s past time to modernize our immigration laws and create a fair pathway to lawful permanent residency.”

This long overdue update would provide a much-needed pathway to a green card for more than 8 million people, including Dreamers, forcibly displaced individuals (TPS holders), children of long-term visa holders, essential workers, and highly skilled members of our workforce, such as H-1B visa holders, who have been waiting years for a green card to become available.

Section 249 of the Immigration and Nationality Act, also known as the Registry, gives the Secretary of Homeland Security the discretion to register certain individuals for lawful permanent resident status if they have been in the country since a certain date and meet other requirements. Section 249 was first codified in 1929 and Congress has modified it four times, most recently during the Reagan Administration in 1986. No changes have been made since 1986, and the cutoff date for eligibility remains January 1, 1972 — more than 50 years ago.

Specifically, the Renewing Immigration Provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929 would:

Amend the existing Registry statute by moving the eligibility cutoff date so that an immigrant may qualify for lawful permanent resident status if they have been in the U.S. for at least seven years before filing an application under Registry.

Preempt the need for further congressional action by making the eligibility cutoff rolling, instead of tying it to a specific date, as it is now.

In addition to Padilla, this bill is co-led by Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-Ill.) and cosponsored by U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.). Representative Zoe Lofgren (D-Calif.-18) is leading companion legislation in the House of Representatives.

The bill is endorsed by over 30 organizations, including Service Employees International Union (SEIU), the Coalition for Humane Immigrant Rights (CHIRLA), UNITE HERE, LiUNA!, United Food and Commercial Workers International Union (UFCW), T’ruah: The Rabbinic Call for Human Rights, LatinoJustice PRLDEF, Center for Gender & Refugee Studies, CASA, FIRM Action, African Communities Together (ACT), United Farm Workers (UFW), UFW Foundation, The Southern Border Communities Coalition, Refugees International, the National Korean American Service & Education Consortium (NAKASEC), NAKASEC Action Fund, National Immigration Law Center (NILC), Quixote Center, Civic Empowerment Coalition, Alianza Americas, FWD.us, The National Partnership for New Americans (NPNA), Bend the Arc: Jewish Action, the Economic Policy Institute, AFL-CIO, and NETWORK Lobby for Catholic Social Justice.

A full list of endorsers is available here.

“Three-quarters of Americans say that the mass deportation agenda goes too far and that immigrant workers deserve a path to citizenship. Senator Padilla is advancing the only solution that makes sense to protect workers and their families from deportation—or worse—and instead create a process for them to apply for permanent residency and the ability to become citizens,” said UNITE HERE President Gwen Mills. “The White House’s cruel enforcement policies and the push to strip legal statuses like TPS away from American workers and families is endangering whole industries like hospitality and tourism, which threatens the livelihoods of all our members, immigrant and native-born alike. UNITE HERE is proud to support the Renewing Immigration Provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929 Act.”

“As immigration policy is increasingly used as a political tool to divide and silence workers, America’s unions are committed to working with Congress to pursue common-sense pro-worker policies that help lift standards in our workplaces and guarantee equal and enforceable rights for all,” said AFL-CIO Director of Government Affairs Jody Calemine. “Work permits are not enough. Only permanent residency and citizenship will ensure that workers have full rights on the job and prevent unscrupulous employers from using the threat of immigration-based retaliation to scare workers into silence. Passing the Renewing Immigration Provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929 will offer long-term members of our workforce, our communities, and our unions the more secure future they need and deserve.”

Padilla is a leading voice in Congress for providing long-term undocumented immigrants with pathways to citizenship or permanent legal residence. Since the introduction of the Renewing Immigration Provisions of the Immigration Act of 1929, he has consistently called for action on commonsense immigration reforms that strengthen communities, protect long-term residents, and unlock America’s economic potential.

Last month, Padilla marked the 14th anniversary of the Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals policy by calling Congress to take immediate action to deliver permanent protections for millions of families, parents, and individuals who are increasingly at risk amid President Trump’s mass deportation agenda.

In May, Padilla visited McAllen, Texas to conduct an oversight visit at the Hidalgo Port of Entry and met with immigrants’ rights groups and individuals impacted by the Trump Administration’s unprecedented and lawless mass deportation agenda.

In November, Padilla and Durbin slammed the Administration’s unlawful efforts to force states to surrender their voter registration lists to the Department of Justice to build an unauthorized national voter registry and pressure states to remove eligible voters from the rolls.

Last September, Padilla reintroduced the bipartisan, bicameral America’s CHILDREN Act to provide a pathway to citizenship for long-term residents who were brought legally to the United States as children as dependents on their parents’ work visas.

Prior to this bill, Padilla introduced the VISIBLE Act to require immigration enforcement officers to display clearly visible identification during public-facing enforcement actions. In 2021, as his first bill in Congress, Padilla introduced the Citizenship for Essential Workers Act, which would create a pathway to citizenship for immigrant essential workers, including Dreamers.

title: Padilla, Schiff Object to Trump FCC Attack on Freedom of Speech and Freedom of the Press, Demand Renewal of Broadcast Licenses for ABC-owned Television Stations Across California
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Alex Padilla and Adam Schiff (both D-Calif.) urged the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to review broadcast license renewal applications impartially and without political interference.

In a letter to the FCC, the Senators expressed support for the renewal of the broadcast licenses for KABC-TV (Los Angeles), KGO-TV (San Francisco), and KFSN-TV (Fresno), California television stations intended for local journalism and owned by the American Broadcasting Company (ABC). This letter comes in response to the FCC requiring the Walt Disney Company to file early license renewal applications, approximately two years before the licenses would typically be due for renewal, and public statements by the Trump Administration criticizing ABC and Disney over editorial news content.

The Senators expressed concern over the FCC’s possible motive for the early license renewals as politically motivated retaliation for protected editorial speech.

“The FCC’s licensing authority is intended to ensure that broadcasters serve the public interest not to influence or punish constitutionally protected editorial judgments,” wrote the Senators. “Public confidence in the Commission depends on its adherence to viewpoint neutrality and the rule of law. And as it relates to these stations and the FCC’s relationship with their parent company, it strongly appears that the FCC is abusing its authority.”

The Senators highlighted the stations’ extensive record of serving Californians through trusted local journalism, emergency coverage, public safety reporting, and community engagement. They further underscored the importance of these stations to California’s economy and the public’s trust in journalism.

“Their renewal applications present extensive evidence of decades of exemplary public service, and that record—not political disagreement with a parent company’s editorial choices—should govern the Commission’s decision,” continued the Senators. “Together, they employ hundreds of Californians, maintain local newsrooms and reporting bureaus, produce hundreds of hours of original local programming, provide free over-the-air access to trusted news and emergency information, and partner with countless nonprofit, educational, and civic organizations across our state.”

The Senators urged that broadcast licensing decisions be based on the statutory public-interest standard, not on disagreement with a broadcaster’s editorial viewpoints or programming.

“We respectfully urge the Commission to evaluate these renewal applications based solely on the factual record and the governing statutory standard, free from political considerations, and to promptly renew the licenses of KABC-TV, KGO-TV, and KFSN-TV,” concluded the Senators.

Full letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Dortch,

We write in strong support of the renewal of the broadcast licenses for KABC-TV, KGOTV, and KFSN-TV, three California television stations that have long served millions of Californians through trusted local journalism, lifesaving emergency coverage, civic engagement, and extensive public service programming.

At the outset, we are compelled to express our serious concern regarding the unprecedented circumstances surrounding these renewal proceedings. The Commission’s decision to require early renewal applications from ABC-owned stations, following repeated public statements by Chairman Brendan Carr criticizing Disney and ABC’s editorial decisions, creates the strong appearance that the FCC’s licensing authority is being used to pressure or retaliate against protected speech rather than to neutrally administer the Communications Act of 1934. The FCC’s licensing authority is intended to ensure that broadcasters serve the public interest, not to influence or punish constitutionally protected editorial judgments. Public confidence in the Commission depends on its adherence to viewpoint neutrality and the rule of law. And as it relates to these stations and the FCC’s relationship with their parent company, it strongly appears that the FCC is abusing its authority.

Now, as to whether these stations have served the public interest, the record demonstrates overwhelmingly that they have. Each station has invested heavily in local journalism, emergency preparedness, consumer protection reporting, public affairs programming, and community partnerships that directly benefit Californians. Their renewal applications present extensive evidence of decades of exemplary public service, and that record—not political disagreement with a parent company’s editorial choices—should govern the Commission’s decision.

Although each station serves a distinct region of California, they share a common commitment to sustained investment in local journalism and meaningful public service. Together, they employ hundreds of Californians, maintain local newsrooms and reporting bureaus, produce hundreds of hours of original local programming, provide free over-the-air access to trusted news and emergency information, and partner with countless nonprofit, educational, and civic organizations across our state.

At a time when local journalism faces extraordinary economic pressures, these stations continue to invest in the reporters, photographers, producers, engineers, and technical infrastructure necessary to deliver high-quality local news. Their work strengthens public safety, promotes civic participation, informs consumers, and helps connect Californians with the information they need during both everyday life and moments of crisis.

The Communications Act of 1934 directs the Commission to determine whether license renewal serves the public interest, convenience, and necessity. The extensive record submitted by KABC, KGO, and KFSN demonstrates that these stations have not merely satisfied that standard, they exemplify it.

For these reasons, we respectfully urge the Commission to evaluate these renewal applications based solely on the factual record and the governing statutory standard, free from political considerations, and to promptly renew the licenses of KABC-TV, KGO-TV, and KFSNTV.

Sincerely,

###

title: Reed & Whitehouse Renew Push to Establish a Nationwide Right to IVF and Lower IVF Costs for Families
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Parenthood is a key life goal for many, but due to infertility and the high cost of fertility treatments, many Americans are fiscally constrained from accessing in vitro fertilization (IVF) as an option to help start a family.

Now, two years after President Donald Trump failed to follow through on his promise of free IVF for all Americans on the campaign trail, U.S. Senators Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) are teaming up with U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) and several colleagues in reintroducing the Right to IVF Act, a sweeping legislative package that would make it easier to access IVF and other assisted reproductive technology (ART) for the millions of hopeful parents who depend on it to build their family.

This pro-family legislation would establish a nationwide right to access IVF, lower the costs of IVF treatment, expand IVF coverage for military families and require all employer-sponsored insurance programs to cover IVF.

Unfortunately, many Republican lawmakers who see IVF as akin to abortion because they view all embryos as children, have undermined IVF protections and scared President Trump into retreating from his IVF campaign promises.

“Almost two years after promising free IVF for all Americans if he were elected, Donald Trump has still failed to deliver,” said Duckworth. “Trump and Republicans’ ‘support’ for IVF is nothing but lip service. They want us to have more babies, yet they’ll do nothing to actually help make it easier for the millions who struggle with infertility to start and grow their families. The Right to IVF Act would immediately make IVF treatment more affordable for millions of hopeful parents across the country. From middle class families, to our brave servicemembers and Veterans, to federal employees and more—every American deserves the right to access the treatment and tools they need to build the family of their dreams without burning through their savings. If Republicans really support IVF, then let’s get this done. No more delays.”

“Helping aspiring parents start a family should be a bipartisan priority. Despite pledging to help make IVF and other fertility treatments more affordable and accessible for American families, President Trump has not followed through. His IVF pledge was just another hollow platitude that became a broken promise. The Right to IVF Act is a pro-family bill that would prioritize affordable IVF care. It would help more Americans who experience infertility issues afford fertility care to they can start a family and put down roots,” said Senator Reed.

“It’s no surprise that President Trump completely abandoned his campaign pledge to make IVF and fertility treatments free. The second Trump administration has been a disaster for health care across the board, from skyrocketing insurance costs to runaway disease outbreaks,” said Senator Whitehouse. “Democrats are working to make it easier for Americans facing fertility challenges to realize their dream of becoming parents.”

Last Congress, Senate Republicans shamefully blocked the Right to IVF Act, exposing the hollowness of Republicans’ empty claims to support IVF for the millions of Americans who rely on it to build their family. This marked the fourth time Senate Republicans blocked Duckworth-led legislation that would protect access to IVF nationwide, with previous instances including her Access to Family Building Act that builds on previous legislation she introduced in 2022.

While Senate Democrats continue their efforts to protect IVF and reproductive freedom, Senate Republicans continue making it abundantly clear through their anti-choice extremism and record Medicaid cuts that they would rather undermine access to basic health care for millions of Americans than make it easier for their constituents to start and build a family.

In addition to Duckworth, Reed, and Whitehouse, the bill is sponsored by the entire U.S. Senate Democratic Caucus, including: U.S. Senators Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Patty Murray (D-WA), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-DE), Maria Cantwell (D-WA), Chris Coons (D-DE), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Dick Durbin (D-IL), John Fetterman (D-PA), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie K. Hirono (D-HI), Tim Kaine (D-VA), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ed Markey (D-MA), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Chris Murphy (D-CT), Alex Padilla (D-CA), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Bernie Sanders (I-VT), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Adam Schiff (D-CA), Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Tina Smith (D-MN), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Mark Warner (D-VA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), Peter Welch (D-VT), Ron Wyden (D-OR), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Jon Ossoff (D-GA), Gary Peters (D-MI), Michael Bennet (D-CO), Andy Kim (D-NJ), Ben Ray Luján (D-NM), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) and Raphael Warnock (D-GA).

Companion legislation is being introduced in the House by U.S. Representatives Lori Trahan (D-MA-03), James Walkinshaw (D-VA-11), Rick Larsen (D-WA-02), Rosa DeLauro (D-CT-03) and Laura Gillen (D-NY-04).

The Right to IVF Act is supported by the American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM), RESOLVE: The National Infertility and Family Building Association, Center for Reproductive Rights (CRR), Planned Parenthood Federation of America (PPFA), National Women’s Law Center (NWLC), American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists (ACOG), GLBTQ Legal Advocates and Defenders (GLAD Law), Academy of Adoption & Assisted Reproduction Attorneys, Stand with IVF, AllPaths Family Building, American Association of People with Disabilities, American Atheists, Society for Assisted Reproductive Technology, Society for Reproductive Endocrinology & Infertility, Society of Reproductive Biologists & Technologists, Society for Reproductive Surgeons, California LGBTQ Health and Human Services Network, Endocrine Society, Equality California, Families USA, GLMA: Health Professionals Advancing LGBTQ+ Equality, Guttmacher Institute, Hadassah, Human Rights Campaign, In Our Own Voice: National Black Women’s Reproductive Justice Agenda, Indivisible, Justice + Joy National Collaborative, Legal Momentum, Military Family Building Coalition, MomsRising, National Asian Pacific American Women’s Forum, National Association of Nurse Practitioners in Women’s Health, National Center for Lesbian Rights, National Council on Jewish Women, National LGBTQ Task Force Action Fund, National Partnership for Women and Families, National Women’s Political Caucus, Physicians for Reproductive Health, Reproductive Freedom for All, Service Women’s Action Network, Silver State Equality, What to Expect Project and Women’s March.

“The American Society for Reproductive Medicine (ASRM) welcomes the bicameral reintroduction of the Right to IVF Act, which would achieve accessible and affordable fertility care for all Americans,” said ASRM Chief Advocacy and Policy Officer Sean Tipton. “This visionary and comprehensive effort would protect patients' ability to build their families through safe, evidence-based treatments like in vitro fertilization. By safeguarding access to assisted reproductive technology (ART), preserving the physician-patient relationship, and expanding coverage for the individuals and families who need it most, this legislation reflects the standard of care that all patients deserve.”

title: El Senador Rick Scott visita la instalación de GEM en Miami tras el esfuerzo de ayuda humanitaria para Venezuela
text:
MIAMI, Florida – El Senador Rick Scott visitó la instalación humanitaria de la organización Global Empowerment Mission (GEM, por sus siglas en inglés) en Miami para agradecer a los voluntarios y organizaciones asociadas que trabajan incansablemente para preparar ayuda humanitaria crítica para el pueblo venezolano mientras la nación se recupera de la devastación causada por los recientes terremotos y avanza hacia una transición democrática.

Durante la visita, el Senador Scott recibió un informe de Michael Capponi, CEO de Global Empowerment Mission, sobre los esfuerzos de recuperación en curso y la respuesta humanitaria. El Senador Scott también se reunió con el personal de GEM, voluntarios, líderes comunitarios y organizaciones aliadas que han dedicado incontables horas a recopilar, organizar y preparar suministros que salvarán vidas y que apoyarán a las familias venezolanas.

El Senador Rick Scott dijo: "Es maravilloso estar aquí en Doral con Global Empowerment Mission y agradecerles el por increíble trabajo que están realizando. Desafortunadamente, muchas personas han perdido la vida o han resultado heridas en Venezuela, y gracias a Dios por la Misión de Empoderamiento Global y todo lo que hacen cada día para salvar vidas. Vamos a seguir luchando—no vamos a dejar de luchar—por la libertad y las oportunidades para el pueblo de Venezuela. Ahora mismo, debemos hacer todo lo posible para garantizar que la ayuda humanitaria llegue a quienes más la necesitan."

Desde el primer día, el Senador Scott ha luchado junto al pueblo venezolano en su búsqueda de la libertad, pidiendo repetidamente la máxima presión sobre el régimen de Maduro, apoyando sanciones contra funcionarios del régimen, abogando por la asistencia humanitaria y apoyando a líderes democráticos que buscan restaurar la libertad y el Estado de derecho.

Mientras continúan los esfuerzos humanitarios, el Senador Scott reafirmó su compromiso de trabajar junto al Presidente Trump, el Secretario Rubio y sus aliados en toda Florida para garantizar que el pueblo venezolano reciba el apoyo que necesita mientras comienzan a reconstruir una nación libre, democrática y próspera.

title: Sen. Rick Scott Visits Global Empowerment Mission facility in Miami Ahead of Humanitarian Aid Effort for Venezuela
text:
MIAMI, Fla. – Today, U.S. Senator Rick Scott visited the Global Empowerment Mission (GEM) humanitarian facility in Miami to thank the volunteers and partner organizations working tirelessly to prepare critical humanitarian aid for the Venezuelan people as the nation recovers from the devastation caused by the recent earthquakes and moves toward a democratic transition.

During the visit, Senator Scott received a briefing from Michael Capponi, CEO of Global Empowerment Mission, on the ongoing recovery efforts and humanitarian response. Senator Scott also met with GEM Staff, volunteers, community leaders, and humanitarian partners who have dedicated countless hours to collecting, organizing, and preparing life-saving supplies that will support Venezuelan families in the days ahead.

Senator Rick Scott said, “It’s wonderful to be here in Doral with Global Empowerment Mission and thank them for the incredible work they are doing. Unfortunately, so many people have lost their lives or have been injured in Venezuela, and thank God for Global Empowerment Mission and everything they do each and every day to save lives. We are going to continue fighting—we are not going to stop fighting—for freedom, liberty, and opportunity for the people of Venezuela. Right now, we must do everything in our power to ensure that humanitarian aid reaches those who need it most.”

Since day one, Senator Scott has fought alongside the Venezuelan people in their pursuit of freedom, repeatedly calling for maximum pressure on the Maduro regime, supporting sanctions against regime officials, advocating for humanitarian assistance, and standing with democratic leaders seeking to restore liberty and the rule of law.

As humanitarian efforts continue, Senator Scott reaffirmed his commitment to working alongside President Trump, Secretary Rubio and partners across Florida to ensure the Venezuelan people receive the support they need as they begin rebuilding a free, democratic and prosperous nation.

title: ICYMI: Rounds Discusses Funding for Iran Conflict with DoD Officials at Appropriations Committee Hearing
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Mike Rounds (R-S.D.) discussed the President’s supplemental funding request of $87.6 billion for national defense with Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth and Chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff General Dan Caine at a hearing of the Senate Committee on Appropriations.

“I had the opportunity to serve as governor of South Dakota for eight years. During that time, we deployed over 5,000 young men and women into harm's way, National Guard members from South Dakota,” said Rounds. “I attended their departure ceremonies, I attended their welcome home ceremonies, and I attended 31 funerals. One of the main reasons that I decided to come to Washington was because I never wanted to see young men and women going into harm's way again if they didn't have the best leadership, the best training and the best equipment possible.”

“You've offered a supplemental request, and I recognize that it's part of a $1.5 trillion overall. But is this enough money to get the job done, or is this going to just get us far enough until we've got to come back in here?” asked Rounds.

“I can't answer the question on what it will cost because the enemy has a vote. What I'll commit to you, as this plays out, we'll make sure that the Congress is informed,” answered Caine.

Click HERE to watch Rounds’ full questioning. Read a transcript of the exchange below.

+++

Rounds: Thank you, Madam Chair. I had the opportunity to serve as governor of South Dakota for eight years. During that time, we deployed over 5,000 young men and women into harm's way, National Guard members from South Dakota.

I attended their departure ceremonies, I attended their welcome home ceremonies, and I attended 31 funerals. One of the main reasons that I decided to come to Washington was because I never wanted to see young men and women going into harm's way again if they didn't have the best leadership, the best training and the best equipment possible.

Now, this body, the Senate, with regard to the Iranian war, to date this body has chosen not to impose war power limitations on the president, nor have we pushed for the withdrawal of forces from the theater. I think the decision to take out Iran's nuclear program and their missile production capacity was the right one, and it should have been done a long time ago. But when the president did that, we also assumed that there would be risk involved. And when you put young men and women in harm's way, you want to do everything you can to make sure that you get in, you get the job done and you get out. I think that's what we talk about.

Now today, it has been since February that we now have the Iranians that are shooting back. We haven't finished the job. I think the question that the American people have is when the difficult decision comes, because I don't think diplomacy is necessarily working, and I think most people would say we've got more issues in front of us before this is complete. For General Caine, when the time comes, and the president is asking for the decisions about the options available to him to appropriately end this war favorable to the United States and to take care of this problem permanently, are you prepared to provide him with the appropriate options that he is going to have to make a decision to choose from?

Caine: Sir, I always provide the president with appropriate options and risks that he can choose from.

Rounds: And those options that he will have to choose from will cost money, and that's our role here. Because if we don't do it right, young men and women die. The question to you, sir, is this. You've offered a supplemental request, and I recognize that it's part of a $1.5 trillion overall. But is this enough money to get the job done, or is this going to just get us far enough until we've got to come back in here? And in the meantime, we may very well not have these young men and women out of harm's way yet. That's my question.

Caine: Sir, I want to first start with recognizing your 31 fallen from home and mourn their losses. We carefully consider the use of military force every single day. And the most important thing that I do is make sure that the president and the other leaders understand the risks and carefully consider the Dover test, a place you've been many times. And that is, are we willing to go to Dover, as we will tomorrow, to bring back the fallen? I can't answer the question on what it will cost because the enemy has a vote. What I'll commit to you, as this plays out, we'll make sure that the Congress is informed. But because I'm not quite sure how this is going to play out yet, it would be unwise for me to comment on what a future cost may or may not be, depending on what they choose.

Rounds: In general, you will provide a plan to Congress at whatever the appropriate classification level is on what resources are required to execute what the president's intent will be to successfully end this conflict.

Caine: Sir, I will always make sure that, as we have, that we're moving data as appropriate to Congress. Yes, sir.

Rounds: Let me come back in just in terms of follow up on this a little bit. Some have criticized Operation Epic Fury for expending many of our munitions stockpiles. Were our munitions, the inventories of those munitions, and the capacity of our munitions industrial base sufficient for great power competition with near peer adversaries like China prior to Operation Epic Fury? Secretary Hegseth?

Hegseth: Senator, as I laid out, because the previous administration short funding shortfalls, munitions transferred to Ukraine and not replaced, and then ignoring threats, it built a lot of risk that requires this kind of investment. So you'd look at the $67 billion alongside the remainder for $1.5 billion. That's the kind of generational investment that not just matches peer adversaries, but far surpasses them, which I think is your expectation, having been to those ceremonies, which is mine, having been to them and going to them, is that we give everything possible to the warfighter that they deserve.

title: NEWS: Schiff Introduces Bill to Improve Transparency of Paid Influencers Promoting Political Campaigns
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) introduced legislation that would require clear and prominent disclaimers on posts by online influencers that have been paid for by political committees or candidates.

“As more and more information in American life is shared through informal communicators like influencers, we need to recognize the risks of proliferating paid political speech without the guardrails that apply to all other forms of political advertising. An influencer can reach far more than a billboard or even a broadcast ad in 2026, but people deserve the same understanding of who is behind that post and if they are paid for it. The PAID Act is a bicameral solution to apply the same bipartisan standards we’ve applied to other advertising to this new class of political speech,” said Senator Schiff.

The Promoting Authenticity with Influencer Disclaimer (PAID) Act would formalize in law changes that the Federal Election Commission has attempted to make for more than a decade but have lacked the statutory clarity to do so.

The PAID Act would amend the Federal Election Campaign Act to require any person paid by a political committee or candidate to post a clear disclaimer that they were paid to post. Representative Mark Takano (D-Calif.-39) is the lead of the House companion legislation.

“Our social media feeds must be fixed,” said Congressman Takano. “Users deserve to know if a creator has been compensated by a campaign to post for them. Senator Schiff and I introduced the PAID Act because current campaign disclosure laws have not kept up with this new creator economy, and voters deserve to know who is financing their feeds before they vote.”

This bill is also supported by Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW), Common Cause, End Citizens United, and Public Citizen.

“Our campaign finance laws must keep pace with today’s media landscape,” said Abigail Bellows, Senior Policy Director for Anti-Corruption & Accountability, Common Cause. “Content creators hold immense trust with their audiences, so when influencers are paid to shape our elections, the public has a right to know who is footing the bill. Voters deserve full transparency on political spending, whether they are watching television or scrolling social media.”

“Transparency within our electoral system has historically been a bulwark of our democracy. The increasing use of social media influencers in political campaigns necessitates the need for transparency requirements to be updated and adapt to the way that political actors communicate with voters,” said Debra Perlin, Vice President for Policy, CREW. “The Promoting Authenticity with Influencer Disclaimers (PAID) Act is crucial legislation meant to let voters know whether the content they are seeing was paid for by political committees. CREW is proud to endorse this legislation introduced by Senator Schiff and Representative Takano, and urges Congress to act on this important legislation.”

“A number of special interest groups, even some foreign governments, are now paying social media influencers to repeat their propaganda, without disclosing that these are paid messages,” said Craig Holman, Ph.D., Public Citizen. “Those who follow these influencers are deceived into thinking these messages are genuine independent thought, when the messages are simply paid commercials. This legislation would require proper disclosure of such ads and is firmly endorsed by Public Citizen.”

“Social media has become one of the most powerful forces in American politics, and right now, Big Money groups are exploiting it with zero accountability,” said Tiffany Muller, President, End Citizens United. “The reality is that many people get their political news from social media feeds, so we have to hold creators to the same disclosure standards as anyone else. If a TV ad has to say who paid for it, so should a sponsored post. Senator Schiff’s bill closes that loophole, and we are proud to support this commonsense legislation.”

The full text of the legislation is available here.

title: NEWS: Schiff, Padilla Object to Trump FCC Attack on Freedom of Speech and Freedom of the Press, Demand Renewal of Broadcast Licenses for ABC-owned Television Stations Across California
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) urged the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to review broadcast license renewal applications impartially and without political interference.

In a letter to the FCC, the Senators expressed support for the renewal of the broadcast licenses for KABC-TV (Los Angeles), KGO-TV (San Francisco), and KFSN-TV (Fresno), California television stations intended for local journalism and owned by the American Broadcasting Company (ABC). This letter comes in response to the FCC requiring the Walt Disney Company to file early license renewal applications, approximately two years before the licenses would typically be due for renewal, and public statements by the Trump Administration criticizing ABC and Disney over editorial news content.

The Senators expressed concern over the FCC’s possible motive for the early license renewals as politically motivated retaliation for protected editorial speech.

“The FCC’s licensing authority is intended to ensure that broadcasters serve the public interest not to influence or punish constitutionally protected editorial judgments,” wrote the Senators. “Public confidence in the Commission depends on its adherence to viewpoint neutrality and the rule of law. And as it relates to these stations and the FCC’s relationship with their parent company, it strongly appears that the FCC is abusing its authority.”

The Senators highlighted the stations’ extensive record of serving Californians through trusted local journalism, emergency coverage, public safety reporting, and community engagement. They further underscored the importance of these stations to California’s economy and the public’s trust in journalism.

“Their renewal applications present extensive evidence of decades of exemplary public service, and that record—not political disagreement with a parent company’s editorial choices—should govern the Commission’s decision,” continued the Senators. “Together, they employ hundreds of Californians, maintain local newsrooms and reporting bureaus, produce hundreds of hours of original local programming, provide free over-the-air access to trusted news and emergency information, and partner with countless nonprofit, educational, and civic organizations across our state.”

The Senators urged that broadcast licensing decisions be based on the statutory public-interest standard, not on disagreement with a broadcaster’s editorial viewpoints or programming.

“We respectfully urge the Commission to evaluate these renewal applications based solely on the factual record and the governing statutory standard, free from political considerations, and to promptly renew the licenses of KABC-TV, KGO-TV, and KFSN-TV,” concluded the Senators.

Full letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Dortch,

We write in strong support of the renewal of the broadcast licenses for KABC-TV, KGOTV, and KFSN-TV, three California television stations that have long served millions of Californians through trusted local journalism, lifesaving emergency coverage, civic engagement, and extensive public service programming.

At the outset, we are compelled to express our serious concern regarding the unprecedented circumstances surrounding these renewal proceedings. The Commission’s decision to require early renewal applications from ABC-owned stations, following repeated public statements by Chairman Brendan Carr criticizing Disney and ABC’s editorial decisions, creates the strong appearance that the FCC’s licensing authority is being used to pressure or retaliate against protected speech rather than to neutrally administer the Communications Act of 1934. The FCC’s licensing authority is intended to ensure that broadcasters serve the public interest, not to influence or punish constitutionally protected editorial judgments. Public confidence in the Commission depends on its adherence to viewpoint neutrality and the rule of law. And as it relates to these stations and the FCC’s relationship with their parent company, it strongly appears that the FCC is abusing its authority.

Now, as to whether these stations have served the public interest, the record demonstrates overwhelmingly that they have. Each station has invested heavily in local journalism, emergency preparedness, consumer protection reporting, public affairs programming, and community partnerships that directly benefit Californians. Their renewal applications present extensive evidence of decades of exemplary public service, and that record—not political disagreement with a parent company’s editorial choices—should govern the Commission’s decision.

Although each station serves a distinct region of California, they share a common commitment to sustained investment in local journalism and meaningful public service. Together, they employ hundreds of Californians, maintain local newsrooms and reporting bureaus, produce hundreds of hours of original local programming, provide free over-the-air access to trusted news and emergency information, and partner with countless nonprofit, educational, and civic organizations across our state.

At a time when local journalism faces extraordinary economic pressures, these stations continue to invest in the reporters, photographers, producers, engineers, and technical infrastructure necessary to deliver high-quality local news. Their work strengthens public safety, promotes civic participation, informs consumers, and helps connect Californians with the information they need during both everyday life and moments of crisis.

The Communications Act of 1934 directs the Commission to determine whether license renewal serves the public interest, convenience, and necessity. The extensive record submitted by KABC, KGO, and KFSN demonstrates that these stations have not merely satisfied that standard, they exemplify it.

For these reasons, we respectfully urge the Commission to evaluate these renewal applications based solely on the factual record and the governing statutory standard, free from political considerations, and to promptly renew the licenses of KABC-TV, KGO-TV, and KFSNTV.

title: NEWS: Sen. Schiff, Rep. Khanna Reintroduce Landmark Bill to Combat Fraudulent AI Generated Campaign Ads
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Representative Ro Khanna (D-Calif.-17) reintroduced the AI Ads Act to prohibit fraudulent misrepresentation of political candidates or committees through content generated by AI, and to codify bipartisan recommendations made by the Federal Election Committee (FEC). Schiff first introduced this legislation in the 118th Congress while serving in the U.S. House of Representatives.

“AI-generated fraudulent advertising which uses the likeness or voices of candidates to misrepresent their positions, campaigns, or causes, or otherwise misrepresents a candidate’s point of view is not only wrong – it poses a serious threat to our democracy that should concern all Americans regardless of their party,” said Senator Schiff. “Fraudulent AI advertising has already proliferated in races across the country, and if Congress does not act, this runaway challenge will only get worse as AI becomes increasingly capable of blurring the lines between fact and fiction. With November elections around the corner, time is of the essence to reign in false political advertising.”

“AI will transform our lives and our society in many ways, but it can’t be used to mislead voters or undermine our democracy. I’m proud to lead the AI Ads Act with Senator Schiff to ban AI-generated content that deceives the public about candidates or elections,” said Congressman Khanna.

Specifically, the AI Ads Act would:

Extend the prohibition of fraudulent misrepresentation, for solicitation of funds or otherwise, to content generated in whole or in part by AI;

Revise the prohibitions on fraudulent misrepresentation of campaign authority to encompass all persons purporting to act on behalf of candidates and real or fictitious political committees and political organizations; and

Remove the requirement that the fraudulent misrepresentation must pertain to a matter that is “damaging” to another candidate or political party.

This bill is supported by Campaign Legal Center, Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington (CREW), Common Cause, Protect Democracy, and Public Citizen.

“Deceptive AI content online can manipulate voters, which is why we need this commonsense bill to ban AI ads that misrepresent candidates,” said Abigail Bellows, Senior Policy Director for Anti-Corruption & Accountability, Common Cause. “This legislation will ensure new technology doesn’t outpace election transparency.”

“Deep Fakes in campaign ads — in which Artificial Intelligence is used to produce computer-fabricated videos or voices of candidates doing or saying something they never did — has become a serious and deceptive problem in federal, state and local elections,” said Craig Holman, Ph.D., Public Citizen. “Some 30 states have passed laws to protect the conduct of state elections from such deceptive practices. It is well past time that Congress approve similar legislation to protect federal elections as well. Sen. Schiff is proposing to do precisely that with the “AI Ads Act,” which Public Citizen earnestly supports.”

“The advancement of AI technology has created new challenges and threats to our democracy. As this technology continues to evolve, we must counter these threats and regulate the improper use of AI in our elections,” said Debra Perlin, Vice President for Policy, CREW. “CREW is proud to endorse the AI Ads Act introduced by Senator Schiff and Representative Khanna, which would help protect against the potential use of AI to confuse or mislead voters.”

The full text of the legislation is available here.

title: NEWS: Senators Schiff, Kim, Lummis, Barrasso Introduce Bill to Protect Children Online Through New Age Reporting Requirements
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Senators Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.), and John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) introduced the bipartisan Digital Age Assurance Act to protect children online by establishing a privacy-first, operating system-based age assurance framework that enables age-appropriate online experiences while minimizing the collection and sharing of sensitive personal information. The bill prioritizes protecting kids’ privacy with a number of provisions preventing kids’ data from being sold or transferred and banning targeted advertisement to children.

“Parents deserve the peace of mind of knowing that when their children use the internet and digital applications, they are shielded from inappropriate and harmful content. And tech companies that host kids on their platforms must be held accountable for protecting young users,” said Senator Schiff. “That’s why I’m proud to work with Senators Kim, Lummis, and Barrasso on a comprehensive federal age-assurance framework that follows California’s important work in this space and ensures that the digital content kids see is age-appropriate and that their privacy is protected from invasive data collection. We have seen what happens when an entire generation of young people grow up without technological guardrails and are left vulnerable to cyberbullying, mental health threats, and more. California has been a leader in requiring online platforms to implement necessary safeguards, and it’s time Congress follow its lead in addressing this issue.”

“Like most parents, I have a lot of anxiety about keeping my two boys safe from dangers online as they grow up in a world full of ever-evolving technology. We owe it to parents and kids to put guardrails in place before more harm is done. The Digital Age Assurance Act puts kids’ data privacy first as we make sure congress and tech companies do their part to make online spaces safer for our kids,” said Senator Kim.

“In Wyoming, we believe protecting our kids and protecting our freedoms go hand in hand, and this bill proves you don’t have to sacrifice one for the other,” said Senator Lummis. “By keeping government IDs and facial scans out of the equation, the Digital Age Assurance Act gives parents real protection for their children while giving platforms a trusted, privacy-protective way to know when those protections should apply.”

More kids are getting online, at earlier ages – with recent data finding that by age 2, 4 in 10 children have their own tablet; by age 4, more than half of children have their own tablet; and by age 8, nearly 1 in 4 children have their own cellphone.

The Digital Age Assurance Act works to prioritize kids’ online safety while including substantive child privacy protection rules. Specifically, the bipartisan legislation would:

Establish a device-level age assurance framework requiring operating system providers to collect a user’s age during operating system account creation or from existing account holders,

Require operating systems to convert a user’s age into privacy-protective age brackets—under 13; ages 13–15; age 16; and age 17 or older—rather than sharing the user’s exact age or date of birth,

Create a secure, real-time operating system signal that applications, browsers, application stores, and covered websites must request and use as the primary indicator of a user’s age,

Permit signals to include age verification methods that minimize data disclosure, including the use of verifiable credentials and zero-knowledge proofs,

Require children under age 17 to link their operating system account to a parent or legal guardian account and allow the user or linked parent or guardian to view the child’s age bracket data,

Establish a process for resolving conflicting age information, including user notice, an opportunity to correct inaccurate information, and distribution of an updated age signal,

Prohibit developers and covered website operators from requesting more age information than the standardized signal or sharing age bracket data with third parties,

Impose data minimization requirements limiting the collection, retention, use, and combination of age-related information, including prohibitions on using age bracket data for profiling, engagement optimization, or targeted advertising,

Prohibit the transfer of children’s personal data to data brokers, while preserving contextual advertising that does not rely on personal data or behavioral profiling,

Establish enforcement by the Federal Trade Commission and State Attorneys General, including civil penalties of up to $2,500 per negligent violation and $7,500 per knowing or intentional violation, which may be multiplied by the number of children affected,

Include competition safeguards preventing operating system providers and application stores from imposing more restrictive age-related requirements on third-party applications or using age bracket data to disadvantage competitors, and

Create a national baseline while preserving Federal or State laws that provide protections at least as strong as the Act.

The Digital Age Assurance Act is endorsed by: American Psychological Association, Mission Kids Child Advocacy Center, and Digital Defenders United.

“Parents shouldn’t have to choose between letting their kids participate in the digital world and keeping them safe. That’s exactly the balance I set out to strike with California’s Digital Age Assurance Act — protecting children online without sacrificing their privacy,” said Assemblymember Buffy Wicks (D-CA). “I’m thrilled to see Congress build on California’s leadership with a bipartisan, privacy-first framework that empowers parents, protects children, and establishes a consistent national standard for age assurance. Parents deserve confidence. Kids deserve safety. Families should never have to sacrifice one for the other.”

title: SCHUMER, GILLIBRAND, RYAN SECURE CRITICAL USDA DISASTER RELIEF FOR UPSTATE NEW YORK FRUIT AND SPECIALTY CROP GROWERS HIT BY DEVASTATING SPRING FROST
text:
In April, Upstate New York Farms Suffered Crop Loss After Frost Damaged Early Growth Of Fruits And Vegetables – With Farmers Losing Anywhere From 15 To 100 Percent Of Their Crops

Following Sustained Advocacy, Schumer, Gillibrand, And Ryan Deliver The Federal Resources Upstate New York Farmers Need To Recover And Get Ready For The Next Growing Season

Schumer, Gillibrand, Ryan: Fed Relief On The Way To Help Upstate NY’s Farmers!

After calling on the USDA to provide relief for New York farmers suffering losses following a devastating frost in April, U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand, and U.S. Congressman Pat Ryan today announced U.S. Department of Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins heeded their call and has approved federal aid for New York fruit and specialty crop growers. The New York State Department of Agriculture and Markets estimates more than $30 million in losses to date, with apple, grape, stone fruit, onion, and other specialty crop growers potentially losing anywhere from 15 to 100 percent of their crops to the frost.

“Upstate farmers work hard every season to put food on our tables and keep New York’s agricultural economy growing. When April weather severely damaged crops just as they were beginning to bloom, I stood up for the farmers who were hit hardest and fought to make sure they had the federal support they needed to recover. I’m proud to announce that USDA Secretary Rollins has heeded my call to help our farmers and is making critical resources available to growers, from the vineyards of the Finger Lakes to the orchards of the Capital Region,” said Senator Schumer. “I encourage farmers in impacted counties to get the assistance they need to weather this tough season and lay the groundwork for a stronger harvest next year. I’ll always stand up for Upstate farmers and fight to ensure they have the resources they need to recover, keep growing, and protect New York’s economy.”

“I am pleased that New York State’s request for a Secretarial disaster designation has been granted,” said Senator Gillibrand. “I fought to secure this approval and bring home the federal resources our farmers and growers urgently needed following the loss of their crops in the devastating April frost. Now, growers in affected regions across the state can access low-interest USDA loans to help them recover. I will always fight for New York’s farmers, and I look forward to seeing these federal dollars at work to bring them the relief they need and deserve.”

“The freeze this spring was absolutely devastating to our farmers and growers in the Hudson Valley. Many of our apple growers told me they lost nearly 100% of their crop. Hearing and seeing the damage firsthand made it crystal clear we needed urgent action from the USDA,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “For months, I’ve been pushing at every level to help secure this official Disaster Designation, which will now unlock millions of dollars in emergency loans and resources to help our farmers and growers begin to recover. I’m grateful for the USDA’s action, but this is just the first step. I’ll be ready to help all those who were impacted by the frost apply for and get access to this assistance, so their businesses can continue to thrive in the Hudson Valley.”

The lawmakers last month sent a letter to USDA Secretary Brooke Rollins urging her to approve a Secretarial Disaster Designation, allowing affected farmers to apply for USDA low-interest emergency loans. The counties the lawmakers called for relief for included in the Disaster Designation are the primary counties of Albany, Columbia, Dutchess, Erie, Greene, Niagara, Chautauqua, Onondaga, Orange, Putnam, Schuyler, Sullivan, Ulster, Westchester, and Yates Counties, and the contiguous counties of Cayuga, Chemung, Cortland, Delaware, Erie, Madison, Monroe, Ontario, Orleans, Oswego, Rensselaer, Rockland, Saratoga, Schenectady, Schoharie, Seneca, Steuben, Tompkins, and Wayne Counties. The letter was also signed by Reps. Paul Tonko (D-NY-20), Josh Riley (D-NY-19), and Tim Kennedy (D-NY-26). The full text of the letter can be found here.

According to USDA’s 2022 Census of Agriculture, New York is one of the top-ranking specialty crop states in the country, including second in apples and third in grapes. Many specialty crop farms also support New York’s agritourism and economy through pick-your-own operations and value-added products, such as hard cider and wine.

title: Shaheen Helps Introduce New Bipartisan Legislation to Promote Renewable Fuels
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) joined her colleagues to introduce new bipartisan legislation that would expand the use of biomass from wood waste and low-value timber for renewable fuels. The Wildfire Reduction Market Expansion Act proposes to modernize the definition for renewable biomass under the Renewable Fuel Standard, establishing a strong market for woody biomass generated through responsible forest management activities.

“The forest products industry is crucial to the stewardship of the Granite State’s forests and fuels economic opportunity in our state’s rural communities,” said Senator Shaheen. “By allowing for timber byproducts to be used for renewable fuels, the legislation creates new markets for the material while also incentivizing continued sustainable management of our state’s working forests.”

The bill is supported by more than 74 organizations, including the National Alliance of Forest Owners (NAFO), Intertribal Timber Council (ITC), Alliance for Wildfire Resilience, American Forest Resource Council and American Farm Bureau Federation.

You can read the full bill text HERE.

Shaheen has long advocated for the Granite State’s forest products industry, including securing federal investments. Shaheen recently introduced the Community Wood Facilities Assistance Act, bipartisan legislation that supports innovative and sustainable wood products and energy from biomass made from small-diameter timber left over from forest thinning projects, including projects that reduce the risk of wildfire. The Community Wood Facilities Assistance Act builds on Shaheen and Collins’ Community Wood Energy Innovation Act which was signed into law in the 2018 Farm Bill and expanded the Community Wood Energy Program to better incentivize investments in energy-efficient wood energy systems and facilities that repurpose low-grade, low-value wood that would otherwise be sent to landfills.

title: Shaheen Joins Colleagues in Investigating Whether IRS Misled Congress and Public About Agency Staffing Shortage While Customer Service Dropped Off During Filing Season
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) joined 13 of her Senate colleagues in investigating whether Frank Bisignano, Chief Executive Officer of the U.S. Internal Revenue Service (IRS), misled Congress and the public about his agency’s staffing problems after the Trump Administration gutted the IRS workforce—leaving Americans struggling to reach customer service at the agency during the past tax filing season. New reporting reveals that the IRS is scrambling to hire thousands of new workers after the agency fired or pushed out nearly 30,000 workers last year—more than a fourth of its staff.

The Senators wrote, in part: “We write regarding recent reports that after cutting 27 percent of its staff in 2025, the Internal Revenue Service (IRS) is now scrambling to hire thousands of new staff. These reports raise questions about whether you misled Congress and the public about the Trump administration’s reckless cuts at the agency. Earlier this year, you stated that the IRS had no additional staffing needs, despite the fact that the Trump Administration spent its first year in office firing or pushing out nearly 30,000 workers. You defended the staff cuts on numerous occasions […] You indicated in April 2026 that there was “no staffing shortage” at the IRS […].”

They continued: “But independent reports were telling a different story. In January, the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration warned that staffing shortages were serious and could impact customer service at the IRS. Press reports described internal IRS communications explaining that the agency was struggling […] And contrary to your claims about improved customer service, an independent watchdog found that, during this filing season, time on hold for taxpayers more than doubled while IRS customer service representatives answered 20% fewer phone calls […] New reporting suggests that the IRS understood the need for more agency staff […] Yet when addressing Members of Congress, you did not mention the ‘ongoing staffing shortages [that] put the 2026 Filing Season at risk’ that IRS officials identified in the memo—instead, you repeatedly denied the existence of a staffing shortage.”

They concluded: “This discrepancy requires an explanation […] Therefore, to better understand whether you misrepresented the IRS’s staffing shortage to Congress and the public, we request that you answer the following questions by August 5, 2026: 1. Are the reports that the IRS requested and received special authority to hire new employees on an expedited basis accurate? If so: a. What authority was used for this hiring? b. When did the IRS request this authority? c. When was this authority granted? d. How many employees have been hired under this authority to date? e. Where have these employees been assigned? 2. Were you aware of the internal memo sent in February by Chief Human Capital Officer Alex Kweskin? If so, when did you become aware? If not, why not? 3. Had you read the memo prior to your appearances in front of the Congressional tax writing committees? If not, why not? 4. What was your basis for telling Congress and the public that there was ‘no staffing shortage’ at the IRS while at the same time seeking hiring authority due to a ‘critical hiring need’?”

The full letter can be read HERE.

Simplifying the tax system and ensuring Americans have the resources they need to file their taxes has been a long-time priority for Senator Shaheen. Ahead of this past tax season, Shaheen joined her colleagues in a letter warning that the IRS was woefully unprepared to assist the American people due to mass layoffs and chaos at the agency. Shaheen is a staunch supporter of the highly successful Direct File program, helping to introduce legislation earlier this year to reverse the Administration’s decision to cancel the popular program. Shaheen has also worked to protect Granite Staters who experienced challenges when using online tax services like TurboTax and introduced the Tax Filing Simplification Act to ease the tax filing process for millions of Americans and lower costs.

title: WHAT THEY ARE SAYING: Slotkin, Moreno Bill to Ban Chinese Vehicles Passes Key Senate Committee With Bipartisan Support
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Last week, legislation from U.S. Senators Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) and Bernie Moreno (R-OH), the Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026, passed the Senate Commerce Committee with unanimous bipartisan support. The legislation will ban Chinese cars from the United States.

The legislation is designed to defend the American auto industry against the increasing threat of Chinese-manufactured vehicles. By cutting off Chinese vehicles, software, and critical hardware at every stage, from the factory floor to the dealership parking lot, the bill ensures that data collected on U.S. roads cannot be funneled back to the Chinese government.

The Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 has drawn broad support from across the American auto industry and national security community – with statements of support from labor unions, the car companies, and auto industry trade groups.

WHAT THEY ARE SAYING ABOUT COMMITTEE PASSAGE OF THE CONNECTED VEHICLE SECURITY ACT OF 2026:

U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI):

“Chinese connected vehicles pose a serious threat to American jobs and Americans’ safety. I am proud to have worked with my Democratic and Republican colleagues to take a step forward in our fight to prevent China from collecting our data and help keep Wisconsin workers and families safe.”

UAW:

“Today’s action by the Senate Commerce Committee marks an important step toward protecting American manufacturing and preserving the American Dream. The UAW applauds every member of the committee who voted to advance a strong version of the bill, and we thank the bill’s sponsors, Senators Bernie Moreno and Elissa Slotkin, for their leadership.

“The committee recognized that America needs an auto industry that invests in American workers—not one that rewards dependence on China, whose industrial strategy has leveraged Western brands to expand its market influence while advancing a business model built on low wages and weak labor standards. As the legislation continues to advance, we reiterate our opposition to carve-outs for all multinational corporations. No company should get special treatment. If they want to benefit from policies that strengthen American manufacturing, they should meet the same standards as everyone else.

“This legislation will help ensure that the next generation of auto investment creates good union jobs, strengthens communities, reinforces America’s manufacturing base, and keeps the future of auto production here in the United States.”

United Steelworkers:

“Thousands of USW members are directly dependent on a healthy U.S. auto industry. Manufacturers and state-linked investors from foreign entities of concern must not be allowed to gain access to the U.S. market through minority ownership stakes, joint ventures, and supply relationships with U.S. manufacturers. Millions of jobs, a resilient supply chain, and our economy are at stake. For these reasons, we strongly support the Act’s clear guardrails on investment policies that restrict domestic firms from allowing foreign entities of concern to gain a foothold in the ownership and direction of companies within the U.S. auto supply chain. The bill’s equity thresholds, which limit FEOC ownership beyond 15 percent for vehicle manufacturers and 25 percent for suppliers, are key for holding all multinational corporations accountable and for protecting the U.S economy.”

General Motors:

“General Motors applauds the efforts of Senator Moreno (R-OH) and Slotkin (D-MI) in securing strong bipartisan support and passage of S. 4429, the Connected Vehicle Security Act, via voice vote out of the Senate Commerce Committee. GM supports policies that protect and strengthen American manufacturing and the global competitiveness of U.S. automakers, and we remain committed to long-term investments in our domestic workforce, facilities, and technology, and we look forward to continuing to work with all stakeholders throughout the process. As we have said many times, we can compete with anyone in the world when we are given a level playing field.”

Machinists:

“The IAM represents thousands of highly trained automotive technicians across the country who are responsible for helping ensure the safety and reliability of the vehicles on America’s roads. Fulfilling that responsibility is becoming more complex as connected vehicle technologies introduce potential national security risks, particularly when critical components are linked to nations of concern such as China.

“…we strongly support the bill’s clear guardrails on investment policies that restrict domestic firms from allowing foreign entities of concern to gain a foothold in the ownership and direction of companies within the U.S. auto supply chain. The bill’s equity thresholds, which limit Foreign Entity of Concern (FEOC) ownership beyond 15% for vehicle manufacturers and 25% for suppliers, are key for holding all multinational corporations accountable and for protecting the U.S economy.”

American Iron and Steel Institute:

“When U.S. automakers compete on a fair and secure basis, American steelmakers thrive alongside them. Unfortunately, they don’t compete on a level playing field as Chinese state-subsidized vehicles, produced outside the bounds of fair trade and with serious national security implications, threaten to undermine the entire domestic supply chain. This bipartisan legislation takes an important step toward ensuring that the future of American mobility is built with American steel.”

Statement from MEMA, The Vehicle Suppliers Association:

“The Connected Vehicles Security Act of 2026 (CVSA), as adopted by the Senate Commerce committee, strikes an important balance that addresses key national security concerns associated with today’s technology-enabled vehicles while also ensuring that vehicle suppliers can comply with the requirements. MEMA appreciates the leadership of Senators Moreno and Slotkin on this legislation, and we look forward to working with them on the CVSA as it continues to move through the legislative process.”
