title: Smith Visits Charles Tool Company
text:
EMINENCE, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) visited Charles Tool Company in Shannon County this week, where he met with founder Bill Charles and toured the shop to discuss the company’s manufacturing work and the impact of the Working Families Tax Cuts on small manufacturers.

Congressman Smith said, “Charles Tool Company is a great example of what small manufacturers in rural Missouri can accomplish. Bill Charles built this company from the ground up, and his team right here in Shannon County makes components for the aerospace, automotive, and heavy machinery industries across the United States. Provisions like Section 199A and 100 percent bonus depreciation, both of which the Working Families Tax Cuts made permanent, have made a real difference for businesses like Charles Tool Company, and I’ll keep fighting for policies that help them grow and succeed.”

Bill Charles founded Charles Tool Company in Illinois in 1987 and relocated the business to Eminence in 1998, drawn to Shannon County to be closer to the Current and Jacks Fork Rivers. The company specializes in hot-forming components for the aerospace, automotive, and heavy machinery industries. All Charles Tool Company employees were trained on the job, with some having been at the company for more than a decade.

As a small business organized as an LLC, manufacturers like Charles Tool Company benefit directly from Section 199A, which allows small business owners to deduct 20 percent of their eligible pass-through business income. They also benefit from 100 percent bonus depreciation, which lets companies immediately deduct the cost of new machinery and equipment. The Working Families Tax Cuts, which Congressman Smith authored, permanently extended both provisions, giving small manufacturers like Charles Tool Company long-term certainty to invest and grow.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES IN BUFFALO: “WE’RE GOING TO FIGHT TO MAKE HEALTHCARE AFFORDABLE FOR EVERY SINGLE AMERICAN”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries joined Rep. Tim Kennedy and local leaders for a press conference, where he emphasized that House Democrats remain united in the fight against Republican efforts to rip healthcare away from everyday Americans and will continue working to lower the high cost of living.

LEADER JEFFRIES: What an honor to be here in the great city of Buffalo with your Congressman Tim Kennedy, who represents this community in such a phenomenal way. I think he’s one of the hardest-working Congressmembers in the United States of America. I call him Timmy on the spot because he’s always present, always fighting for all of you, always lifting up your voices and fighting to make sure that the quality of life here in Western New York can be the best possible quality of life here in our great country.

It’s certainly good to be back here in the 716 area code. I’m from Brooklyn. That’s the 718 area code. And even though our area codes may be different, the issues that you confront here in Buffalo, that we confront in Brooklyn, that the American people are confronting all across this nation, remain the same. Life has become too expensive. Healthcare, of course, inaccessible in ways that should not be the case here in the wealthiest country in the history of the world. And we’re in the midst of the largest assault on healthcare in modern American history. Thankful, of course, for the work that’s done here at this amazing clinic by Ray and this great team. Thankful for Pastor Blue and your leadership and all the advocates who are here today and the people who have come together on one accord to make it clear we’re going to cancel the cuts, we’re going to lower costs and we’re going to save healthcare in the United States of America.

In the midst of this great assault on healthcare, the One Big Ugly Bill included a $1 trillion cut to Medicaid, the largest cut to Medicaid or healthcare in American history, putting hospitals and nursing homes and community health centers like this at great risk. And we know, in fact, many are beginning to close all across the country, including in rural America. Republicans refused to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits, putting in jeopardy the healthcare of more than 20 million hardworking American taxpayers all across the country, including right here in Western New York and in some cases resulting in premium increases of as much as $1,000 a month on working-class New Yorkers, middle-class New Yorkers and everyday Americans.

The same group of extremists, led by the current occupant of 1600 Pennsylvania Avenue—they have launched an assault on medical research, an assault on the Centers for Disease Control, an assault on the National Institutes of Health, an assault on the Food and Drug Administration, an assault on vaccine availability and an assault on public health here in the United States of America. But they thought the American people would step back. We’re not going to step back. We’re going to fight back. And make it clear: hands off Medicaid, hands off Medicare, hands off the Affordable Care Act and hands off the healthcare of the American people.

This is the wealthiest country in the history of the world. And as House Democrats, we’re going to fight to bring a reality to life that in this country, access to high-quality, affordable healthcare cannot simply be a privilege available only to the wealthy, the well-off and the well-connected. Access to high-quality, affordable healthcare must be a right available to every single American.And that’s what we’re going to fight to bring to life here in Western New York and all across the country.

98 days until we can change direction in the United States of America. 98 days for all of us to show up and stand up and speak up to make this country the best version of herself. And I’m confident that that’s exactly what’s going to happen. We’re going to fight for an affordable America. We are going to fight to lower the cost of groceries and gas and housing. We’re going to fight to make healthcare affordable for every single American. And at the same period of time, we’re going to combat the corruption, the folks who are stealing from you to enrich themselves. And we have a message for those folks who were doing that: on day one of a new Democratic majority, we’re going to hold the crooks accountable.

So it’s an honor to be back here in Western New York, this great all-American city of Buffalo. I’m a long-suffering Jets fan, y’all, so I wish you all well. Now, long-suffering means we regularly lose to the Buffalo Bills. But as New York’s only resident football team, I got nothing but love for the Buffalo Bills. And certainly, after the Knicks won the championship, we’re looking forward to what comes next in Western New York. And together, together, we’ll do all that’s necessary to cancel the cuts, lower the cost, save healthcare. Keep your hands off of our Medicaid. Thank you very much.

title: Kamlager-Dove Convenes Fireside Chat and Panel with Federal and Local Housing Leaders to Examine the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act’s Impact in Los Angeles
text:
LOS ANGELES, CA – Today, Congresswoman Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) convened a fireside chat with Adrianne Todman, former Acting Secretary of the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development, and a panel discussion with local housing leaders to examine what the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act means for families and communities across Los Angeles.

The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act took effect on July 11, 2026. This bipartisan housing package aims to address challenges related to housing production, affordability, preservation, and coordination between federal and local partners. Read the full bill text here.

The panel featured leaders from the Los Angeles County Development Authority, the Los Angeles Housing Department, the Housing Authority of the City of Los Angeles, Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles, Abundant Housing Los Angeles, Enterprise Community Partners, and Strategic Actions for a Just Economy.

“Whether it’s seniors on fixed incomes or working families, too many Angelenos are struggling to keep a roof over their heads,” said Rep. Kamlager-Dove. “Addressing the housing crisis takes more than just a whole-of-government approach—it demands close collaboration with community partners to pinpoint areas of need and deliver real solutions. I was proud to convene federal and local leaders to help ensure Los Angeles can turn the opportunities created by the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act into shovels in the ground and more affordable homes.”

“We applaud Congress for working diligently to pass this monumental housing reform legislation that is poised to significantly address the affordable housing crisis felt not only within Los Angeles County but by communities across the nation,” stated Emilio Salas, LACDA Executive Director. “This comprehensive approach to enhance housing at multiple levels requires that we collaborate with our local and State partners to ensure successful implementation, which we are prepared to do, but we must also advocate to our Congressional leadership to ensure that the proposed reforms are fully funded and supported by the Federal government, to see actual change.”

“The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act represents one of the most significant federal housing achievements in a generation providing critical tools to preserve affordable housing, revitalize public housing, and strengthen pathways to stability for families across Los Angeles," said HACLA President & CEO Lourdes Castro Ramirez. "We applaud Congresswoman Waters for her unwavering leadership on affordable housing and appreciate Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove for bringing housing leaders together to implement this transformative legislation. Turning these historic policies into real, lasting change requires building solid partnerships across every level and I'm excited to see such collaboration taking shape."

"I am so pleased to work with my colleagues on the local, State and Federal levels on finding ways to expedite the development of much needed affordable housing," said Tiena Johnson Hall, General Manager of LAHD. "Finding creative ways to work collaboratively is so vital as we work to house Angelenos."

“The 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act creates important new opportunities to increase housing production, preserve existing housing, and expand pathways to homeownership,” said Erin Rank, President of Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles. “We appreciate Congresswoman Kamlager-Dove for bringing together local leaders to focus on implementation and impact. At Habitat for Humanity of Greater Los Angeles, we believe success will ultimately be measured by the number of homes built, homes preserved, and families who can achieve long-term stability and build wealth through affordable homeownership in Los Angeles County.”

“With overwhelming bipartisan support, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act included 47 provisions that broaden public-private investments, strengthen existing federal programs, and create new tools to boost housing supply and affordability,” said Jimar Wilson, Vice President of Enterprise Community Partners. “One proven provision is the expansion of HUD's Rental Assistance Demonstration program by 100,000 units, unlocking private capital to preserve aging public housing. This is the tool effectively used in the $664 million transformation of Jordan Downs over the course of a decade, which has delivered to date 787 new affordable homes in Watts."

“Tenant protections are a key to solving our affordable housing crisis,” said Cynthia Strathmann, Executive Director of Strategic Actions for a Just Economy. “Protecting renters from evictions, harassment, and unreasonable rent raises not only keeps people housed, but it also helps keep rents stable. Without strong tenant protections in place, California will continue to see rising homelessness, overcrowding, and economic strain on working- and middle-class households.”

title: Kamlager-Dove, Murray, and Houchin Introduce Legislation to Break Down Barriers to Higher Education for Homeless and Foster Youth
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Representative Sydney Kamlager-Dove (D-CA-37), Senator Patty Murray (D-WA), and Representative Erin Houchin (R-IN-09) reintroduced the bipartisan Higher Education Access and Success for Homeless and Foster Youth Act to remove barriers to higher education for homeless and foster youth and help ensure they can pursue a higher education and get the support they need to thrive.

“Everyone deserves a fair shot at pursuing higher education. But too often, foster youth and youth experiencing homelessness are priced out of pursuing their dreams or fall through the cracks once enrolled,” said Rep. Kamlager-Dove. “I’m proud to reintroduce this bill alongside Rep. Houchin and Sen. Murray to help even the playing field and ensure that these youth are supported throughout their education journeys. As a Representative of Los Angeles County—home to over 30,000 foster youth—I will continue to champion our most vulnerable young people.”

“Homeless and foster youth face barriers most students never have to think about, from proving their independence for financial aid to having nowhere to go over winter break—our country should have their back to make sure they have the same opportunities as any other students. These young people have already shown more grit than most of us will ever need. The least we can do is stop making access to higher education harder,” said Senator Murray. “Our bill can make sure that higher education is more affordable and accessible for homeless and foster youth—in-state tuition for kids without a stable address, prioritization for work-study programs, a real person at every institution to help these young people get the support they need, and more. We know that education can be the great equalizer and help these kids find financial security and stability—so let’s pass this bipartisan bill and make it happen.”

“Higher education should be an opportunity available to every child in America, including students who have faced unimaginable circumstances like homelessness or aging out of foster care,” said Rep. Houchin. “As a former child services worker, I am proud to cosponsor the bipartisan Higher Education Access and Success for Homeless and Foster Youth Act to ensure students facing these challenges have greater access to resources, opportunities, and support they need to succeed.”

In the 2023-2024 school year, the number of families staying in homeless shelters and those who were visibly unsheltered increased by 12.5%. States identified more than 1.5 million students in public schools across the country as experiencing homelessness during that school year.

The Higher Education Access and Success for Homeless and Foster Youth Act of 2026 requires colleges and universities to take steps to improve outreach to and support for homeless and foster youth, prioritizes homeless and foster youth for Federal Work Study opportunities, provides in-state tuition rates for students without stable residency, and improves data collection and reporting to better reach and serve homeless and foster youth—among other steps. Prior versions of the legislation proposed a number of critical improvements to the financial aid process for homeless and foster youth, which were subsequently enacted into law as part of the FAFSA Simplification Act.

The legislation is endorsed by SchoolHouse Connection, ACTION Ohio (Alumni of Care Together Improving Outcomes Now), All4Ed, Association of Children's Residential & Community Services (ACRC), Center for Higher Education Policy and Practice at SNHU, Child Welfare League of America, Children's Advocacy Institute, County Welfare Directors Association of California, Covenant House International, Dave Thomas Foundation for Adoption, EDGE Partners, Education Law Center, Foster Care Alumni of America, Foster Greatness, Foster Success, Fostering Academic Achievement Nationwide (FAAN), Hildreth Institute, The Hope Center for Student Basic Needs, iFoster, Institute for Educational Leadership, John Burton Advocates for Youth, Juvenile Law Center, Lutheran Services in America, National Association of Counsel for Children, National Association of County Human Services Administrators, National Center for Housing & Child Welfare, National Education Association, National Network for Youth, Overcoming Hurdles in Ohio Youth Advisory Board (OHIO YAB), Sayra and Neil Meyerhoff Center for Families, Children and the Courts, Swipe Out Hunger, Teacher Education Division of the Council for Exceptional Children, VOICES for Alabama's Children, Washington state Post Secondary Basic Needs Coalition, Youth Law Center, and Youth Villages.

title: MassLive: Healey urges senate to extend Haitian protections, warns of economic, healthcare disruption
text:
Gov. Maura Healey is urging the U.S. Senate to pass legislation extending Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haitians, warning that a failure to act will severely disrupt the state’s economy and healthcare sectors.

TPS for Haitians ended Monday following a U.S. Supreme Court decision that upheld President Donald Trump’s plan to end the protections, which have been in place since 2010. Legislation to extend the status for Haitians has already passed the U.S. House of Representatives.

In a statement, Healey argued that allowing the protections to expire would strip thousands of residents of their legal status and work authorization, devastating families and private employers across the state.

“Haitian TPS holders are essential contributors to our state’s workforce, filling roles that are vital to our economic stability and growth. The sudden loss of their legal status and work authorization would be devastating for our state,” Healey said in a statement. “I urge Congress to take immediate action to extend TPS protections for Haiti. Forcing Haitian TPS holders to return to a country that has faced repeated natural disasters, economic crisis, widespread violence and political instability goes against the very purpose of TPS, which protects individuals already in the United States who cannot safely return to their home country.”

Massachusetts is home to more than 45,000 Haitian TPS holders, who widely serve in roles such as nurses, home health aides, construction workers and transportation employees, the governor said.

According to Healey’s office, Haitian TPS holders contribute an estimated $5.9 billion annually to the U.S. economy. Nationally, TPS holders from all designated countries pay an estimated $7.8 billion in federal, state and local taxes each year.

The state’s health care system is expected to bear a significant burden if the protections lapse. The Massachusetts Senior Care Association estimates that up to 2,000 workers in its member facilities could lose work authorization if the Senate fails to act, exacerbating existing staffing shortages.

“At a time when demand for vital services for older adults in Massachusetts is rapidly growing, the loss of up to 2,000 experienced Haitian caregivers in our nursing facilities will make it even more difficult to ensure access to the care our state’s seniors rely on,” Tara Gregorio, president and CEO of the Massachusetts Senior Care Association, said in a statement. ”The impact will be felt not only by these workers and their families, but also by the older adults who depend on a stable, reliable long‑term care system.”

State business leadership echoed these concerns, emphasizing that the workforce relies heavily on immigration programs to function seamlessly.

“Massachusetts employers depend on a stable workforce to keep our economy strong and competitive,” JD Chesloff, president and CEO of the Massachusetts Business Roundtable, said in a statement. ”Haitian TPS holders have filled critical roles across industries for years, and we are concerned that an abrupt loss of these experienced workers would increase costs, worsen existing labor shortages and disrupt businesses across the state. We appreciate Governor Healey’s leadership in bringing attention to these impacts.”

The push for a Senate vote carries strong backing from the Massachusetts congressional delegation. Both U.S. Sen. Elizabeth Warren and U.S. Rep. Katherine Clark stressed the humanitarian and community crises that would emerge if thousands of legal immigrants were suddenly subjected to deportation.

“Haitians are a powerfully important part our communities – they run small businesses, staff hospitals, and are our neighbors,” Warren said. “It is wrong for the Trump administration to rip these hardworking, legal immigrants out of our communities and deport them into imminent danger. I cosponsored a bill to reinstate Haiti TPS and I won’t stop fighting to protect the Haitian community.”

U.S. Rep. Ayanna Pressley, who helped champion the bipartisan extension bill that passed the House in April, noted that the Senate’s inaction puts the state’s economic stability in jeopardy.

“Haitian TPS holders are essential to our communities and economy, and ending TPS for Haiti would be devastating for Massachusetts and our country,” Pressley said. ”The Senate must do right by our Haitian siblings and pass our bill to extend TPS for Haiti and deliver the critical protections they deserve. I’m grateful to Governor Healey for her partnership in standing up for our neighbors.”

In response to the looming expiration, the Healey-Driscoll administration has ordered state agencies to support impacted communities and has issued guidance to employers.

Meanwhile, the United Way of Massachusetts Bay has launched a United Response Fund to deliver emergency assistance to impacted Haitian families throughout the transition.

title: Kean Tours Springfield PD Upgrades with Local Leadership
text:

title: Rep. Mullin Introduces Bill to Standardize Autonomous Vehicles Protocol During Emergencies
text:
Washington, D.C. – In response to hazardous cases of autonomous vehicles (AV) blocking emergency responders from helping people in danger, driving through construction zones, failing during power outages, and contributing to large-scale traffic jams, U.S. Rep. Kevin Mullin (CA-15) is introducing the AV Emergency Response Coordination Act.

Rep. Mullin announced the bill at a joint press conference in San Francisco alongside Mayor Daniel Lurie, Fire Department Chief Dean M. Crispen, Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety President Cathy Chase, Police Chief Derrick Lew, San Francisco Municipal Transportation Agency Director Julie Kirschbaum, San Francisco County Transportation Authority Executive Director Tilly Chang and Department of Emergency Management Deputy Director Adrienne Bechelli.

The bill would direct the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) to establish minimum safety standards and protocols requiring AV operators to improve how they work with local public safety personnel.

“Seconds count during a crisis, and we’ve seen too many terrifying incidents of AVs interfering with police, fire fighters, and paramedics. Public officials have been asked to be guinea pigs in figuring out how to interact with this emerging technology. AV companies have to do better. While it is exciting that the Bay Area is leading the nation in autonomous vehicle innovation, recent disruptions like widespread power outages or the holiday traffic fiasco on Fourth of July in San Francisco, have shown how malfunctions can hamper emergency response,” said Rep. Mullin. “Autonomous vehicles have tremendous potential to improve safety on our roads, but federal regulators need to make sure they’re not inadvertently getting in the way of emergency responders and that public officials are able to quickly work with AVs in an emergency.”

The list of incidents involving emergency responders is mounting in cities across the United States where driverless vehicles are operating, including in Austin, Pheonix, Las Vegas, Dallas, San Francisco and others. Across these locations, there have been reports of AVs obstructing ambulances and paramedics, driving into active crime scenes, blocking fire trucks, and failing to recognize basic safety conditions like flashing lights, flares, smoke, and traffic cones. AV companies are also not providing sufficient information and training to emergency responders to ensure the safety of vehicle occupants, pedestrians, and other road users when there are collisions, malfunctions, and other incidents involving AVs.

Rep. Mullin’s AV Emergency Response Coordination Act is the first legislation of its kind to directly address this issue, which has bipartisan interest. The Trump Administration’s NHTSA Administrator Jonathan Morrison recently sent a letter to AV companies demanding that they address the issue of AVs interfering with first responders and law enforcement.

Specifically, the AV Emergency Response Coordination Act would:

Require AV companies to provide clear, standardized emergency response protocols for first responders;

Establish a 24/7 hotline for public officials to communicate directly with AV companies during autonomous vehicle incidents;

Direct NHTSA to develop minimum national emergency response standards across AV operators; and

Create a process for public officials to issue “geofence notices” so that AVs avoid certain areas during an emergency or while there is an ongoing safety hazard.

“Emergency responders must be able to reach people in danger or distress without being delayed or obstructed by autonomous vehicles (AV). The AV Emergency Response Coordination Act would establish much-needed, commonsense federal standards for coordination between AV companies and emergency personnel. Advancing innovation cannot threaten public safety. We commend Rep. Kevin Mullin for introducing this important legislation and urge Congress to enact it,” said Cathy Chase, president of Advocates for Highway and Auto Safety.

“San Francisco is the global center of innovation, and we’ve been on the cutting edge of autonomous vehicles and street safety. Because we were one of the first cities to welcome autonomous vehicles at scale, we have learned more than almost any other city about how they operate in a dense, complex urban environment,” said San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie. “This legislation will help keep San Franciscans safe while taking the lessons we’ve learned to the rest of the country. My number one priority is public safety, and I want to thank Congressman Mullin for his leadership in supporting our first responders so they can do that critical work.”

“A top priority of the San Francisco Fire Department is ensuring that our personnel can respond quickly and safely to emergencies. During several recent large-scale events we have experienced challenges involving autonomous vehicles. We have been working closely with AV companies and welcome this technology, provided it is deployed in a manner that supports public safety and emergency response operations. We appreciate Representative Mullin introducing thoughtful legislation that will move our mission of public safety forward,” said San Francisco Fire Department Chief Dean M. Crispen.

“I want to thank Congressman Kevin Mullin for his leadership and his steadfast commitment to ensuring public safety as autonomous vehicle technology continues to evolve,” said San Francisco County Transportation Authority Chair and District 7 Supervisor Myrna Melgar. “This timely legislation recognizes that advancing innovation must be matched by strong standards for emergency management and preparedness. The San Francisco County Transportation Authority looks forward to working alongside Congressman Mullin, our public safety partners, and the autonomous vehicle industry to ensure first responders have the tools, information, and coordination they need to protect our communities.”

Rep. Mullin has prioritized strengthening oversight and transparency around the development of driverless cars, including previously introducing the AV Safety Data Act, which would require companies to collect and report key safety data to NHTSA. He has also authored several letters urging the agency to require more comprehensive reporting on AV operations, safety incidents, and performance data.

title: Khanna, Markey Reintroduce Green New Deal for Health to Invest in Patients, Workers, and Infrastructure for Today’s Climate-Health Threats
text:
Washington (July 28, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), top Democrat on the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Subcommittee on Primary Health and Retirement Security, and Representative Ro Khanna (CA-17) today reintroduced the Green New Deal for Health, legislation that will equip our country’s healthcare system to respond to the growing impacts of climate change and ensure all Americans have access to care in their communities.

“This summer, Massachusetts has been hit with record-breaking temperatures, smoky air from wildfires, and flash floods. Every year that Washington waits to address the climate crisis, more people pay for it with their health,” said Senator Markey. “The Green New Deal for Health is a blueprint for a healthcare system that can withstand the crisis we're already living through, while putting patients and workers first. Our communities cannot afford for Congress to keep treating climate and health as separate issues. I’m thankful to partner with Congressman Khanna to fortify our health infrastructure with the urgency it requires.”

“Across the world, hundreds of millions of people are already feeling the effects of climate change and the health consequences that often follow. From increased cases of asthma due to air pollution to disruptions at care facilities after extreme weather events, it's clear we need to take steps now to protect public health,” said Representative Khanna. “I’m proud to join Senator Markey in reintroducing the Green New Deal for Health, a sweeping bill that reimagines what our health care system can look like when we prioritize our people and our planet.”

The Green New Deal for Health boldly reimagines a healthcare system that is prepared to protect the health and well-being of our workers, our communities, and our planet. Specifically, the legislation would:

On healthcare access: Invests $130 billion over five years in community health centers through the Community Health Center Fund.

On climate-resilient infrastructure: Revives the landmark New Deal-era Hill-Burton program by authorizing $100 billion in federal grants to public and nonprofit medical facilities to improve climate resilience and disaster mitigation—ensuring uninterrupted access to care during climate disasters and extreme weather, while guaranteeing prevailing wages for workers and requiring facilities to serve neighboring communities.

On protecting communities against hospital closures: Requires hospitals that receive Medicare payments to notify the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) at least 180 days before a full closure or discontinuation of services, so frontline communities are not stranded in health care deserts.

On transparent, green supply chains: Directs HHS to establish a task force to develop policies for mandatory public disclosure of the emissions and climate risk of FDA-approved drugs, devices, and biologics.

On investing in the health workforce: Directs federal dollars toward climate and health education, builds a robust community health workforce, prioritizes grants to facilities that collectively bargain with their workers, and provides hazard pay to workers who respond after a crisis.

On community mental health and resilience: Funds grants for resilient community mental health programs and research on extreme heat risk and response.

On home resiliency for medical needs: Makes solar batteries, heat pumps, and other resiliency measures eligible Medicare expenses so people with disabilities and medical needs can install life-saving home infrastructure.

On research and innovation: Invests $5 billion per year and establishes the National Climate and Health Research and Innovation Initiative to support scientific research into the health impacts of climate change and develop innovative approaches to climate-health resilience.

Bill Text (PDF) | One-Pager (PDF)

The Green New Deal for Health is cosponsored by Senators Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), and Representatives Maxwell Frost (FL-10), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Yvette Clarke (NY-09), and Ilhan Omar (MN-05).

The legislation is endorsed by AFT: Education, Healthcare, Public Services; Alliance of Nurses for Healthy Environments; Alzheimer's Foundation of America; American College of Nurse Midwives; Boston Medical Center; Center for Biological Diversity; Committee of Interns and Residents (CIR-SEIU); Earthjustice Action; Green & Healthy Homes Initiative; Health Care Without Harm U.S.; International Transformational Resilience Coalition (ITRC); Massachusetts League of Community Health Centers; National Hispanic Medical Association (NHMA); National Nurses United; People’s Action Institute; and Transhealth.

title: Reps. Khanna and Luna Introduce the No Campaign Funded Cover-Ups Act
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Representatives Ro Khanna (CA-17) and Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13) introduced the No Campaign Funded Cover-Ups Act to prohibit candidates for federal office and federal officeholders from using campaign contributions or legal expense funds to cover costs related to sexual assault, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment claims. By requiring more detailed reporting of campaign-related legal expenses, the bill will also give the public greater transparency into how political funds are being used.

"Survivors must be heard and respected,” said Congressman Ro Khanna. “Our bipartisan legislation addresses a basic principle: money donated to support a political campaign should not become a personal legal-defense fund for alleged sexual misconduct. Our bill will increase public transparency and help prevent attempts to silence those who come forward about abuse.”

“Those who seek or hold federal office must be held to the highest standard of accountability,” said Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna. “If a candidate is accused of sexual assault, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, campaign donations and legal expense funds should never become a personal bailout. If you commit sexual misconduct, you should foot the bill, not the donors who put their trust in you.”

"Across the country, too many powerful men are relying on the silence of women to win elections or cling to power. This bill sends a strong message: no more campaign funded cover ups," said Cheyenne Hunt, Executive Director, Reckoning Action. "Standing with survivors is not a partisan issue. We were proud to work with Rep. Khanna and Rep. Luna to ensure survivor experiences were centered throughout this process."

Specifically, the legislation will:

Prohibit campaign and legal defense funds from paying legal fees to defend against such claims.

Ban those funds from paying settlements or court-ordered judgments arising from such claims.

Prohibit payments for private investigators or opposition research intended to investigate or uncover damaging information about a person who brought a claim.

Apply these restrictions to payments made during the two years before the law’s enactment. Require campaigns to disclose more information about all legal expenses, including the recipient, amount, date, purpose, type of legal payment, and whose expenses were covered.

title: Larsen in Seattle Times: Trump needs to renegotiate USMCA trade agreement
text:
Today, Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) published an op-ed in the Seattle Times pressing the Trump administration to renegotiate the U.S-Mexico-Canada (USMCA) trade agreement.

“The President has tried and failed to grow the economy through tariffs,” wrote Rep. Larsen. “What the U.S. economy needs instead are strong, mutually beneficial trade relationships that create jobs and lower prices here at home… Renegotiating USMCA gives the U.S. the opportunity to improve and strengthen the agreement, but when all is said and done, it is critical for economic stability and lower prices that USMCA continues.”

Earlier this month, Rep. Larsen sent a report to U.S. Trade Representative (USTR) Ambassador Jamieson Greer summarizing over a hundred meetings and conversations that Rep. Larsen’s office has had with farmers, businesses, municipalities, ports and other stakeholders across Northwest Washington over the past year.

“I wanted to hear directly from the people I represent about how USMCA impacts their families, businesses and communities,” wrote Rep. Larsen. “Recognizing that there are differing perspectives and voices on USMCA and trade policies among the constituents I represent, it is clear that businesses and communities broadly support and benefit from USMCA.”

This year, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appointed Rep. Larsen to be the top Democrat on the U.S.-Canada Interparliamentary Group, an organization that connects American and Canadian legislators to promote information sharing and better understanding on shared issues of concern.

Born and raised in Arlington, Washington, Rep. Larsen has a deep personal history with British Columbia and the U.S.-Canada relationship. As a member of Congress, he has been a leader on issues involving Canada, including trade, environmental protection in the Salish Sea and Pacific Northwest, the Arctic, security and border management.

Rep. Larsen’s full op-ed is available HERE and the text is below.

Why Trump needs to renegotiate U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement

High costs and a failing economy are hurting families and businesses in Northwest Washington. Now, the president’s new 50% tariffs on Canadian goods threaten to drive sky-high prices even higher next month.

The president has tried and failed to grow the economy through tariffs. What the U.S. economy needs instead are strong, mutually beneficial trade relationships that create jobs and lower prices here at home.

In the months ahead, the United States government has the opportunity to enhance and renew the U.S.-Mexico-Canada trade agreement.

The United States, Canada and Mexico signed USMCA in 2020 and the three nations conducted a joint review of the deal this year. The Trump administration chose not to renew USMCA in its current form, opting instead to spend the coming months renegotiating the deal.

In preparation for the joint review, I wanted to hear directly from the people I represent about how USMCA impacts their families, businesses and communities. In the past year my office met with more than 100 farmers, businesses, municipalities, ports and other stakeholders across Northwest Washington.

On July 1, I sent a report summarizing Northwest Washington stakeholders’ perspectives on USMCA to U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, whose agency is leading negotiations with Canada and Mexico. Recognizing that there are differing perspectives and voices on USMCA and trade policies among the constituents I represent, it is clear that businesses and communities broadly support and benefit from USMCA.

A strong USMCA would reduce tariffs and regulatory barriers, helping local businesses better compete and succeed in foreign markets. A long-term agreement would create a predictable and stable business environment, which companies and investors need to make long-term plans. The agreement would also simplify customs procedures, which saves time and money for businesses that move goods and products frequently over the U.S.-Canada border.

Renegotiating USMCA gives the U.S. the opportunity to improve and strengthen the agreement, but when all is said and done, it is critical for economic stability and lower prices that USMCA continues.

Thanks to USMCA, Washington state businesses saved $126 million in direct tariff costs since 2020, according to the Washington Council on International Trade (WCIT). These savings reduce the cost of doing business and get passed along to everyday consumers. The president’s new, petty and pointless tariffs on Canada are just more fees for struggling American families and businesses to pay.

Washington state consumers, farmers and businesses can credit USMCA for keeping agricultural trade in North America largely tariff-free and expanding access to foreign markets for local farmers. USMCA lowers the price of food and other agricultural goods by ensuring that Northwest Washington and other U.S. farmers have buyers for their goods.

USMCA forged commitments and enforcement mechanisms to protect workers’ rights and the environment across North America. A renegotiated USMCA can and should strengthen those commitments and enforcement mechanisms.

Trade with Canada and Mexico supports 320,000 jobs in Washington state. In Northwest Washington, the U.S.-Canada partnership is especially important. Trade between Northwest Washington and Canada supports 2,200 jobs in Whatcom County, 1,400 in Skagit County and 3,800 in Snohomish County, according to Trade Partnership/Connect2Canada data. These jobs help families buy groceries, make rent payments and put gas in the car.

President Donald Trump’s tariffs and reckless rhetoric toward Canada have caused businesses to close in the communities I represent. Rising shipping and manufacturing costs, along with uncertainty resulting from constantly changing tariff policies, have pushed prices up and stopped companies and tourists from bringing their business to Northwest Washington.

Continuing USMCA will help restabilize the economic relationship between the United States and two of our largest trading partners. The Trump administration must cut the BS and get to work. It is time to negotiate in good faith to enhance and renew USMCA, and fully enforce the provisions of the agreement to help lower prices and create good-paying jobs.

Rick Larsen: is the lead Democrat on the House Transportation & Infrastructure Committee. He represents a portion of Snohomish County and all of Skagit, Whatcom, Island and San Juan counties.

title: Rep. Mike Levin Applauds Selection of Potential Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses
text:
DOE Selects Five States for Future Nuclear Waste Depository Sites; Initiative Is Supported by $248 Million Secured by Rep. Levin

Washington, D.C.—Today, Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) applauded the Department of Energy’s (DOE) announcement of five states to serve as potential sites for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses. The Innovation Campuses are intended to house solutions for the nation’s nuclear waste challenges by supporting activities across the full nuclear fuel cycle, including fuel fabrication, enrichment, reprocessing used nuclear fuel, and disposal of used nuclear fuel.

Five states—Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Idaho—signed Memorandums of Understanding (MOUs) with DOE to begin exploring how to officially become host sites for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses. Once these Innovation Campuses are in full operation as envisioned, they will accept spent nuclear fuel from decommissioned nuclear plants like the San Onofre Nuclear Generating Station (SONGS).

Watch Rep. Levin’s video on the announcement here.

Rep. Levin’s statement on the announcement below:

“Today’s announcement of potential sites for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses has been years in the making. It required tremendous bipartisan efforts where policymakers put aside politics and focused on a fix to our difficult nuclear waste challenges. Since my first day in Congress, I’ve prioritized finding solutions to safely remove and dispose of spent nuclear fuel, and today’s selection of states is a monumental step in the right direction. For years I have said that our actions must be based in collaboration with states and local communities, and for the first time in decades, states are raising their hands.

“But there is more work to be done. The hard part is still ahead of us. The federal government has a bad track record on nuclear waste and has not kept its promises to communities for many decades. As we know well, DOE was required by law to start picking up the waste from nuclear power plants like SONGS in 1998, but has fallen woefully behind. DOE must now be consistent, transparent, and honest with states as it completes the selection process for the Innovation Campuses and sets them up for success year after year, and administration after administration.

“I cannot underscore strongly enough that the Innovation Campuses must have solutions for the disposal of spent nuclear fuel if we are to be successful in this endeavor. Any development of new nuclear energy hinges on our country having a workable answer to the spent nuclear fuel challenge.

“Congress must now work in a bipartisan, bicameral fashion to authorize the Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses and write them into law with clear oversight, clear benchmarks, and clear connections to permanent disposal. This will ensure true accountability and real solutions. I will continue to work with the Administration and my congressional colleagues on both sides of the aisle to get this done.”

Since entering Congress in 2019, Rep. Levin has secured over $248 million for the safe removal and management of the nation’s spent nuclear fuel. In January 2026, he wrote to DOE Secretary Chris Wright urging the Department to establish a safe, effective, and long-term management program for spent nuclear fuel. Rep. Levin has also introduced the bipartisan Nuclear Waste Administration Act of 2024, which would modernize our country’s nuclear waste management program by establishing an independent Nuclear Waste Administration to manage the country’s nuclear waste. The safe management and removal of spent nuclear fuel out of SONGS and other decommission nuclear plants across the country remains a top priority for Rep. Levin.

Background on DOE’s Announcement of Potential Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses

The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) today announced the selection of Utah, Tennessee, Oklahoma, Louisiana, and Idaho as potential host states for Nuclear Lifecycle Innovation Campuses, a new effort to strengthen and modernize the nation’s full nuclear fuel cycle. The campuses will attract significant investment, expand domestic manufacturing, and create thousands of new high-paying jobs in their respective regions.

The proposed campuses are designed to support activities across the full nuclear fuel lifecycle, including fuel fabrication, enrichment, reprocessing used nuclear fuel, and final disposition of used nuclear fuel. Depending on state priorities and regional capabilities, the campuses may also host advanced reactor deployment, power generation, advanced manufacturing, and co located data centers.

The proposed innovation campuses have the potential to attract up to $50 billion in capital investment, generate as much as $10 billion in state and local tax revenue, and create nearly 25,000 jobs with an establishment of a campus.

Earlier this year, DOE invited states to submit clear statements of interest and constructive feedback on the structure of the Innovation Campuses. In their submissions, states outlined how a campus would advance goals such as workforce development, infrastructure investment, economic diversification, or technology leadership and described the scope of activities they envision hosting. States submitted responses by April 1, 2026.

States that choose to pursue hosting an innovation campus will sign hosting agreements with the Department at a later date.

title: Maryland Democrats Urge FERC to Protect Marylanders from Rising Electricity Costs Due to Out-of-State Data Centers
text:
WASHINGTON – Congresswoman April McClain Delaney joins Maryland Congressional Delegation members – U.S. Senators Chris Van Hollen and Angela Alsobrooks and U.S. Representatives Steny Hoyer, Kweisi Mfume, Jamie Raskin, Glenn Ivey, Sarah Elfreth, and Johnny Olszewski (all D-Md.) – in calling on the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC) to take action to ensure Marylanders are not forced to bear skyrocketing electricity costs due to increasing energy demand from data centers located outside of the state. The lawmakers urged FERC to require PJM Interconnection (PJM) to implement strong protections that would ensure fair energy costs for Marylanders after PJM, the grid operator responsible for coordinating electricity transmission in the region, assigned roughly $2 billion in costs to Maryland ratepayers for infrastructure that is needed primarily to serve out-of-state data centers. The lawmakers’ letter supports acomplaint at FERC filed by the Maryland Office of People’s Counsel challenging PJM’s existing transmission cost allocation rules.

“As members of the Maryland Congressional Delegation, we write regarding a pressing matter that has the potential to significantly raise energy costs for our constituents. PJM Interconnection LLC’s (PJM) existing transmission cost allocation rules result in the unjust assignment of billions of dollars in costs to Marylanders, contributing to unaffordable electricity bills,” the lawmakers begin.

On the rising costs of electricity due to data centers outside of Maryland, the lawmakers write, “Data centers being built outside of Maryland are driving one of the largest transmission expansions in PJM’s history. Across its three most recent regional transmission planning rounds, PJM has advanced $22 billion in projects needed principally to serve data centers. Under PJM’s current cost allocation rules, roughly $2 billion of those costs have been assigned to Maryland ratepayers rather than the data centers that are driving the demand.”

“Marylanders are already shouldering the immense burden of skyrocketing electricity costs, and it is unjust and unreasonable to force our constituents to subsidize the energy infrastructure needs of the wealthiest companies in the world. Unless the Commission acts, our constituents will pay an estimated $1.6 billion on their electric bills over the next ten years for these projects alone, and $823 million of that total cost will fall on residential customers, which equates to roughly $345 for the average customer,” the lawmakers continue.

On PJM’s current cost allocation rules, the Maryland lawmakers note, “PJM’s cost allocation rules have not kept pace with the build out of hyperscale data centers, just one of which can equal the electricity demand of a small city. PJM’s current rules spread costs broadly across the region regardless of where, and for whom, the underlying projects are actually needed. Maryland regulators have no ability to assign such costs to data centers located in other states, and with tens of thousands of megawatts of additional data center demand growth projected across PJM over the next two decades, our constituents face billions of dollars in further charges absent Commission action to address this unjust and unreasonable cost allocation. Furthermore, because much of the forecasted growth in data center energy demand is speculative, our constituents bear the unacceptable risk of paying for projects built to serve potential data centers that are never built due to any number of external reasons.”

“We urge the Commission to act expeditiously to provide relief from these costs for Maryland ratepayers, including as requested in OPC’s complaint. Thank you for your consideration of this important issue that is essential to ensuring just and reasonable energy costs for our constituents,” the lawmakers conclude.

The full text of the letter is available here and below.

Dear Chairman Swett,

As members of the Maryland Congressional Delegation, we write regarding a pressing matter that has the potential to significantly raise energy costs for our constituents. PJM Interconnection LLC’s (PJM) existing transmission cost allocation rules result in the unjust assignment of billions of dollars in costs to Marylanders, contributing to unaffordable electricity bills. This matter has been brought before the Commission by the Maryland Office of People's Counsel (OPC) (Docket: EL26-63), and the basic principle underpinning this issue is simple: our constituents should not be forced to pay for transmission projects that they did not cause and from which they will not meaningfully benefit.

Data centers being built outside of Maryland are driving one of the largest transmission expansions in PJM’s history. Across its three most recent regional transmission planning rounds, PJM has advanced $22 billion in projects needed principally to serve data centers. Under PJM’s current cost allocation rules, roughly $2 billion of those costs have been assigned to Maryland ratepayers rather than the data centers that are driving the demand.

Marylanders are already shouldering the immense burden of skyrocketing electricity costs, and it is unjust and unreasonable to force our constituents to subsidize the energy infrastructure needs of the wealthiest companies in the world. Unless the Commission acts, our constituents will pay an estimated $1.6 billion on their electric bills over the next ten years for these projects alone, and $823 million of that total cost will fall on residential customers, which equates to roughly $345 for the average customer.

PJM’s cost allocation rules have not kept pace with the build out of hyperscale data centers, just one of which can equal the electricity demand of a small city. PJM’s current rules spread costs broadly across the region regardless of where, and for whom, the underlying projects are actually needed. Maryland regulators have no ability to assign such costs to data centers located in other states, and with tens of thousands of megawatts of additional data center demand growth projected across PJM over the next two decades, our constituents face billions of dollars in further charges absent Commission action to address this unjust and unreasonable cost allocation. Furthermore, because much of the forecasted growth in data center energy demand is speculative, our constituents bear the unacceptable risk of paying for projects built to serve potential data centers that are never built due to any number of external reasons.

We were encouraged by the Commission’s June 18, 2026 orders directing PJM and five other grid operators to justify or reform how they assign the costs of serving large loads, which advance the essential goal of protecting ordinary consumers. Those orders, however, are forward-looking. We also seek to obtain relief for our constituents from the billions in costs PJM has already assigned, and because most of those costs have not yet appeared on customer bills, timely Commission action can prevent much of this harm before it occurs.

We urge the Commission to act expeditiously to provide relief from these costs for Maryland ratepayers, including as requested in OPC’s complaint. Thank you for your consideration of this important issue that is essential to ensuring just and reasonable energy costs for our constituents.

title: Reps. McClain Delaney & Obernolte, Led Bipartisan Letter to the Department of State, Department of Commerce, and Federal Communications Commission Requesting Update on U.S. Strategy for the World Radio Conference 2027
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Last week, Representatives April McClain Delaney (MD-06) and Jay Obernolte (CA-23) led a bipartisan letter, joined by 17 House colleagues, requesting that the Department of State, Department of Commerce, and Federal Communications Commission provide Congress with a written update on U.S. strategy for the 2027 World Radiocommunication Conference (WRC-27), including how agencies are coordinating, structuring leadership, and engaging internationally to protect U.S. spectrum priorities.

The letter, sent to Under Secretary of State Jacob Helberg, NTIA Administrator Arielle Roth, and FCC Chairman Brendan Carr, highlights the significance of the decisions that will be made at WRC-27, which will be hosted in Shanghai, China. It underscores the importance of preserving global momentum for unlicensed 6 GHz access, a critical driver of U.S. innovation, Wi-Fi leadership, and long-term economic competitiveness, as the PRC and aligned countries push to redefine global spectrum standards.

"As other nations, including the People's Republic of China, work to shape global spectrum policy, the United States must lead—not react. Strong coordination across our federal agencies and close collaboration with our allies are essential to protecting American innovation, strengthening our economic competitiveness, and ensuring the technologies that power our homes, businesses, and communities continue to be built on U.S. leadership,” said Congresswoman April McClain Delaney.

“We applaud the House members, led by Reps. Delaney and Obernolte, for reaffirming the importance of preserving U.S. leadership in Wi-Fi and supporting continued access to the full 6 GHz band as preparations for WRC-27 move forward. Their leadership underscores the critical role that 6 GHz plays in powering next-generation Wi-Fi, driving innovation, and ensuring American consumers and businesses continue to benefit from world-leading broadband connectivity,” said NCTA -The Internet & Television Association.

The letter was also co-signed by Reps. Bacon (NE-02), Castor (FL-14), Dingell (MI-06), Elfreth (MD-03), Gottheimer (NJ-05), Houlahan (PA-06), J. Johnson (TX-32), Kamlager-Dove (CA-37), Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), LaHood (IL-16), Moran (TX-01), Morelle (NY-25), Mullin (CA-15), Olszewski (MD-02), Quigley (IL-05), Sorensen (IL-17), and Walberg (MI-05).

title: Congressman Menefee: Killing Minority Business Programs Hurts Every Houstonian
text:
HOUSTON, TX — Today, a federal judge ruled that the City of Houston's Minority and Women-Owned Business Enterprise (MWBE) program is unconstitutional. In response, Congressman Christian D. Menefee (TX-18) released the following statement, warning that the decision is the latest step in a broader effort to dismantle programs that level the playing field for minority- and women-owned businesses.

“This ruling is yet another step by far-right activists, like the lawyers who filed this case, fighting to erase every tool minority and women business owners use to compete on a level playing field,” said Rep. Menefee. “They’ve fought to end diversity programs in our colleges, at corporations, and in government contracts. It’s a shame, and The Supreme Court of the United States has cleared the way for it to happen in ending affirmative action and gutting the Voting Rights Act."

“We’ve seen the data showing that local governments across our region overwhelmingly contract with companies owned by white men,” continued Rep. Menefee. “The gaps in contracting are massive, and they are proof that minority and women business owners still face real barriers when they try to win public contracts. MWBE programs help close those gaps. They are not a favor or a handout.”

Studies conducted over the years, along with evidence presented in the case, show clear racial disparities in who receives contracts from local governments across the Houston area. During the trial, the City's expert witness testified that minority-owned businesses continue to lose out on city contracts, confirming ongoing racial disparities in the City's contracting process. Similarly, a 2020 study of Harris County government contracting found that the county awarded more than 90% of its contracting dollars over a three-year period to businesses owned by white men. These disparities are well documented and are the reason MWBE programs were created in the first place.

title: Moulton, Democratic Veterans Demand Transparency from Trump on Iran War Casualties
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Following disturbing reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, Congressman Seth Moulton (MA-06) joined Congressman Mike Thompson (CA-04) and 13 other fellow Democratic veterans in urging the Trump Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

"As veterans of America's wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers," wrote the lawmakers.

"The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports," they continued. "We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers."

Following public outcry, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names of the four U.S. servicemembers removed from the Iran War death toll over the weekend. The Administration has not provided an adequate explanation as to why the servicemembers were removed in the first place.

In addition to Congressman Moulton and Congressman Thompson, Representatives Pat Ryan (NY-18), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Jared Golden (ME-02) signed the letter.

title: Neguse, Bennet, Hickenlooper Raise Concerns Over Forest Service Proposal to Lease Nearly 14,000 Acres for Potential Oil and Gas Development
text:
Lafayette, CO — Yesterday, Colorado Congressman Joe Neguse and Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper penned a letter opposing the proposed lease of U.S. Forest Service (USFS) lands in Routt and Moffat Counties to the Bureau of Land Management (BLM). In doing so they joined a number of local leaders who have similarly raised concerns about the Forest Service’s plans to lease nearly 14,000 acres of USFS lands to the BLM, a decision that would open the door to future oil and gas development in the area and could jeopardize critical wildlife habitats, sensitive watersheds, and outdoor recreational opportunities.

The Colorado lawmakers have been steadfast in their efforts to protect Colorado's public lands, teaming up to stop President Trump and Congressional Republicans’ plan to mandate the sale of millions of acres of public land across the American West through the budget reconciliation process, while also introducing landmark legislation like the CORE Act to establish new wilderness areas and safeguard outdoor recreation in these treasured landscapes.

Neguse, who has represented Routt County since 2023 and currently serves as the Ranking Member of the Federal Lands Subcommittee, also recently introduced a bill to protect the right of local communities to provide input into proposed oil and gas lease sales on national public lands. The Local Input Act restores the Department of the Interior’s discretion to incorporate public comments and defer nominated parcels that conflict with the public interest.

Changes enacted under the Trump administration last year effectively stripped local communities, landowners, and state and local officials of a meaningful voice in leasing decisions on public lands by eliminating BLM’s authority to defer lease parcels even if legitimate conflicts are identified.

The proposed federal oil and gas lease sale underwent a 30-day public comment period that began June 18 and ran through July 17. As the Colorado lawmakers have made clear, it’s imperative the administration considers local feedback.

Read their full letter HERE and below:

July 27, 2026

Forest Supervisor Dawn Laybolt

Medicine Bow-Routt National Forests and

Thunder Basin National Grassland

3838 Cherrywood East Loop

Laramie, WY 82070

Dear Forest Supervisor Laybolt,

We write to express our concern with the U.S. Forest Service (USFS)’s Routt National Forest Draft Environmental Assessment (EA), proposing to lease 10 parcels in northwest Routt and Moffat Counties in Colorado, to the Bureau of Land Management (BLM). The USFS has received Expressions of Interest to lease these 13,850 acres to the BLM for potential future oil and gas lease, exploration, and development, and initiated a public comment period last month.

Local leaders, including Routt County, members of the Steamboat Springs City Council, and the Western Resilience Center, have expressed concerns with this proposed lease. Six of the 10 parcels currently under consideration within the EA contain sensitive watersheds, and two contain cutthroat trout habitat. These proposed parcels also overlap significantly with habitat and migration corridors for elk, mule deer, Columbian sharp-tailed grouse, golden eagles, and more.

The proposed lease of these areas for future oil and gas development threatens to disrupt critical wildlife habitats and wildlife migrating and living throughout the region, in addition to degrading important watersheds. These parcels overlap with the California Park Special Interest Area, an area of critical ecological significance for Northwest Colorado and where there is active watershed restoration work underway in collaboration with the USFS.

These areas are also important for recreation, and the outdoor recreation economy is a significant economic driver for Routt County and the surrounding communities. Several existing multi-use trails overlap with the proposed parcels, in addition to areas that are valuable for hunting and fishing. Prior oil and gas development efforts within Routt County have historically not been economically viable or demonstrated commercial viability in the areas proposed for lease. We are concerned that this proposed action would significantly jeopardize the existing economic drivers for the region, including outdoor recreation.

We are also concerned that Routt County was not notified of this proposed action prior to the agency’s announcement. Any proposed leasing actions should be accompanied by significant and meaningful public and community engagement, including with the local jurisdictions that would be impacted.

As you consider the proposed lease of these lands to the BLM, we request you take full and fair consideration of the concerns raised by the impacted community and the highest and best use of these public lands.

Sincerely,

title: Nunn Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Protect Students by Strengthening School Cybersecurity Resources
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Representatives Zach Nunn (IA-03) and Doris Matsui (CA-07) last week introduced the Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act, bipartisan legislation to help schools prevent cyber attacks by improving information sharing and giving educators the tools they need to keep classrooms open and student data protected.

“As a 20-year Air Force intelligence officer and former White House National Security Council member, I’ve spent my whole career tracking threats like these,” said Rep. Nunn. “Now they’re hitting our classrooms — shutting schools down and putting Iowa students’ personal information in the wrong hands. No school should have to fight that alone. Our bipartisan bill gives K-12 schools across the country the backup they need to stop these attacks and protect their students.”

Schools are facing an unprecedented rise in cyber attacks as technology becomes more deeply integrated into classrooms. According to the U.S. Department of Education, K-12 schools experience an average of five cyber threats every week. These attacks have forced schools to cancel classes, interrupted instruction for days or even weeks, exposed sensitive student information, and cost districts anywhere from tens of thousands to more than $1 million to recover.

“When I thought about my own grandchildren going to school, I wanted what every parent and grandparent wants: for them to be safe and focused on learning,” said Rep. Matsui. “No family should have to worry that a cyberattack could expose a child’s personal information or disrupt their education. This bill gives schools the tools, training, and support they need to protect students’ data, help teachers keep classrooms running, and give administrators stronger resources to prevent and respond to cyberattacks.”

The Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act would help schools stay ahead of cyber threats by:

Giving schools stronger cyber defenses through a K-12 Cybersecurity Technology Improvement Program to find and fix vulnerabilities and better protect student and school data.

Getting schools threat information faster through the School Cybersecurity Information Exchange, where educators can access real-time threat alerts, best practices, and federal cybersecurity resources.

Learning from every breach through a voluntary Cybersecurity Incident Registry that helps schools identify trends, coordinate responses, and prevent the next attack.

“Schools are increasingly at risk from cybersecurity threats. NAESP is proud to endorse the Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act, a bill which would give our members practical tools, information, and resources from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) to help pre-K-8 school leaders protect student data and privacy and to avoid costly school disruptions,” said L. Earl Franks, Executive Director, National Association of Elementary School Principals. “We commend Representatives Matsui and Nunn and Senators Blackburn and Warner for their bipartisan leadership on this critically important issue.”

“Cybersecurity remains one of the most urgent technology challenges facing K-12 schools. School districts face increasingly sophisticated cyber threats that can disrupt learning, compromise student and personnel data, and strain already limited technology resources,” said Keith Krueger, CEO, Consortium for School Networking (CoSN). “CoSN strongly supports the bipartisan Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act because it will strengthen information sharing, improve understanding of the cyber threats facing schools, and expand access to the resources and expertise districts need to better protect their networks. We applaud the bill’s bicameral and bipartisan sponsors for their leadership on this important issue.”

“SETDA strongly supports the bipartisan Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act because it improves collaboration, increases visibility into cyber incidents affecting schools, and expands access to the tools and technical assistance states and districts need to protect students and critical education systems,” said Dorann Avey, SETDA Board Chair. “We commend Representative Matsui and Representative Nunn for their leadership and urge Congress to advance this vitally important legislation.”

The Enhancing K-12 Cybersecurity Act is the House companion to bipartisan legislation introduced in the Senate by Senators Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) and Mark Warner (D-VA). The bill is endorsed by the National Principals Association, the National Association of Elementary School Principals, the Council of Chief State School Officers, the National Association of State Chief Information Officers, the State Educational Technology Directors Association, and the Consortium for School Networking.

Text of the bill is available here.
