text:
Monterey, CA – Following disturbing reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, United States Representative Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) joined Rep. Mike Thompson (CA-04) and 13 other fellow Democratic veterans in urging the Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran War.

“As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers,” wrote the lawmakers.

“The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran,” continued the lawmakers. “It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.”

Following public outcry, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names of the four U.S. servicemembers removed from the Iran War death toll over the weekend. The Administration has not provided an adequate explanation as to why the servicemembers were removed in the first place.

In addition to Panetta and Thompson, Reps. Pat Ryan (NY-18), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Jared Golden (ME-02) signed the letter.

Full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear President Trump,

As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers.

The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.

We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.

Sincerely,

###

title: Three Pappas-Backed Bipartisan Bills to Fight the Addiction Crisis and Improve Care for Seniors Advance Out of Committee
text:
Three bipartisan bills backed by Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) were voted out of the House Committee on Energy and Commerce last week, and now head to the House floor for a vote before the full House of Representatives.

Pappas introduced the bipartisan, bicameral Combating Illicit Xylazine Act with Rep. Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), which would list xylazine as a Schedule III controlled substance and give law enforcement the tools they need to go after traffickers while protecting the drug’s legal use by veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers. Xylazine, also known as “tranq,” is an easily accessible veterinary tranquilizer that is being used as a low-cost cutting agent for fentanyl.

Pappas cosponsors Tyler’s Law, bipartisan legislation designed to prevent fentanyl overdoses in the United States. This bill requires the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to complete a study on how frequently hospitals test for fentanyl when a patient is experiencing an overdose. Based on these results, the bill instructs HHS to issue guidance to hospitals on implementing fentanyl testing in emergency rooms.

“As we work to combat the ongoing addiction epidemic, we have to make progress across the board on this issue. We must ensure our law enforcement has the resources they need to stop drug trafficking and that our health care centers have the resources for care and recovery,” said Congressman Pappas. “These bills would do that and should be swiftly brought to the floor for a vote.”

Pappas cosponsors the Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2025, legislation to streamline the outdated prior authorization process in Medicare Advantage (MA). With nearly 33 million Americans enrolled in Medicare Advantage, the bill updates a system that has become a top administrative burden for providers and a barrier to timely care. Audits by the HHS Inspector General have found that Medicare Advantage plans subjected enrollees to unnecessary delays, incorrectly denied medically necessary care, and ultimately approved 75% of requests that were initially denied.

“This legislation is about cutting red tape and fixing systems that aren’t working so that seniors can access the care they need when they need it and physicians can focus on their patients, not paperwork,” said Congressman Pappas. “It’s commonsense and it’ll make a real difference for folks in New Hampshire and across the country.”

Background:

The Combating Illicit Xylazine Act would:

Schedule xylazine as Schedule III illicit substance under the Controlled Substances Act;

Ensure veterinarians, farmers, and ranchers can still use the drug for its intended purpose by creating a clear definition of “ultimate user” — someone lawfully permitted to possess a controlled substance for legitimate use;

Enable the DEA to track its manufacturing to ensure it is not diverted to the illicit market; and

Require a report on prevalence, risks, and recommendations regarding xylazine.

The bill is endorsed by 41 state attorneys general, major law enforcement organizations, and veterinary organizations. The Combating Illicit Xylazine Act previously passed the House with overwhelming bipartisan support.

Tyler’s Law is named in memory of Tyler Shamash, a 19-year-old boy who died following a fentanyl ingestion in 2018. He was not tested for fentanyl after being brought to the hospital with a suspected overdose. His mother, Juli, is an advocate for this legislation and is sharing Tyler’s story to prevent others from experiencing the same tragedy. Still to this day, many emergency rooms do not include fentanyl in their drug screenings. According to HHS, fentanyl-related deaths have skyrocketed 103-fold in the United States from 1999–2023. Adding fentanyl testing to emergency room drug screenings could save countless lives. A full list of endorsing organizations is here.

The Improving Seniors’ Timely Access to Care Act of 2025 would:

Require MA plans to adopt an electronic prior authorization (e-PA) system with standardized transaction;

Improve transparency around MA Prior Authorization use and requirements;

Clarify HHS’ authority to set timelines for determinations, including real-time decisions for routine items; and

Mandate HHS and other agencies report on oversight and further improvements to the e-PA process

In the 117th and 118th Congresses, this legislation was endorsed by more than 500 organizations representing patients, providers, medical technology innovators, biopharmaceutical companies, and health plans.

title: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN JOINS REGIONAL FOOD BANK, COMMUNITY PARTNERS, SPEAKS OUT ABOUT STATE OF HUNGER IN HUDSON VALLEY
text:
The Regional Food Bank’s 2026 State of Hunger report shows that more than 12% of their service area – which includes Dutchess, Orange, and Ulster Counties – is food insecure, including 1 in 6 children

The report comes amid the fallout from several harmful Trump Administration actions, including the largest cut to SNAP in history, cost-raising tariffs, and cuts to TEFAP which forced the foodbank to serve 2 million fewer meals in 2025 than 2024

Ryan joined food bank representatives, local electeds, and partner organizations to discuss his work in Washington to bring down food costs, support local farmers, and hold the Trump Administration accountable

NEWBURGH, NY – Today, Congressman Pat Ryan joined local advocates, partners, and electeds at the Regional Food Bank to discuss the State of Hunger in the Hudson Valley. The 2026 report, informed by new research by Feeding America’s annual Map the Meal Gap study on food insecurity, paints a grim picture of growing food insecurity in the Hudson Valley amid harmful Trump Administration policy.

Among the report’s most alarming figures is that 53,390 (1 in 6) children in the Hudson Valley lack access to adequate nutrition. That is 5,000 more children than in 2025. It follows more than a year of cost-raising policies and actions from the Administration, including the largest cut to SNAP in history – which is ripping food assistance from more than 40 million Americans, including up to 70,000 in the Hudson Valley, as well as placing financial strain on farmers – and as prices continue to rise across the board due to Trump’s war in Iran.

Standing with the gathered community Ryan advocated for his bipartisan Lower Grocery Prices Act, and discussed his recently introduced Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act, which breaks up greedy monopolies that jack up prices on hardworking Americans and push out small businesses. When a harmful Trump Administration policy cut two million meals at the Regional Food Bank – and slashed a critical income source for Hudson Valley farmers – Ryan immediately rallied with the community and hosted a Community Speak Out demanding the cuts be reversed.

“Hudson Valley families have to spend way too much of their income just to put food on the table. There are real people behind the data in this new report – children who aren’t getting the nutrients their growing bodies need, seniors pinching pennies to feed themselves, and families on fixed incomes worrying they won’t be able to afford new groceries this week. Especially after thousands lost their SNAP benefits because of Trump’s USDA cuts and as grocery prices continue to rise, I’m so grateful to our exceptional food bank’s tireless work, helping meet this unprecedented demand in our community,” said Congressman Pat Ryan. “One of my top priorities is making life more affordable, and I’ll keep fighting to pass my Lower Grocery Prices Act and to protect SNAP benefits until no one has to go hungry in the Hudson Valley.”

“The challenges we are facing as well as our partners in the charitable food industry have faced in recent months, are truly unprecedented,” said Tom Nardacci, CEO of Regional Food Bank. “With federal cuts to the USDA, the SNAP crises and increasing inflation, our more than 1,000 partner agencies are witnessing longer lines and greater demand. The generosity of industry partners, businesses, groups and organizations, volunteers and our neighbors allowed us to hold the line of food insecurity rates among adults at 12%, but we need more help from our community to meet the demand for our children.”

Last year, Congressman Ryan stood with the food bank and community members in fighting back against the Trump Administration’s cut to The Emergency Food Assistance Program (TEFAP) – which partners local farms with food banks to serve food insecure populations. Trump cut the program by 50%, eliminating crucial business for local farmers and forcing the Hudson Valley branch of the Regional Food Bank to provide 2 million fewer meals in 2025 than 2024.

Hudson Valley families have also been dealing with skyrocketing grocery costs due to the President’s tariffs back in April 2025. In January, following polling that showed 87% of Americans were dealing with increased grocery prices under Trump, Ryan conducted a community inquiry. More than 99% of respondents said they were feeling the burden of higher grocery costs, with 75% of them citing Trump’s tariffs as the main driver.

Congressman Ryan’s bipartisan Lower Grocery Prices Act would require the U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) to analyze the price of groceries over the last 20 years, provide effective solutions on how to lower costs, and develop a national plan to combat the high prices and ease the affordability crisis. Ryan originally introduced the legislation after the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) released a report in March 2024 which detailed how large grocery companies exploited the high-price environment caused by the pandemic to jack up their prices and pad their profit margins, unfairly raising prices for consumers as well as snubbing smaller competitors’ profits.

Most recently, Ryan introduced the Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act, landmark legislation breaking up greedy monopolies and ending unfair pricing practices that raise costs for American families and box out local farmers and ranchers.

###

title: Pfluger, Colleagues Introduce the RESCUE Act to Fix Broken Ambulance Payment System
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman August Pfluger (TX-11) introduced the Reimbursing Emergency Services for Critical Urgent Encounters (RESCUE) Act to amend the outdated Medicare payment structure that is straining ambulance services across rural Texas and the country.

Medicare's ambulance fee schedule has not been updated since 2002, and current rates are still based on cost data collected from 1998. The RESCUE Act would require the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to update the ambulance fee schedule every three years based on current, actual cost data, replacing a system still anchored to decades-old numbers. Meanwhile, the fuel, equipment, staffing, and vehicle costs required to keep an air or ground ambulance ready to respond have only continued to climb, widening the gap between what it costs to respond to a call and what Medicare actually pays.

"EMS providers and first responders show up for our communities every single day, often in the most difficult moments imaginable, and they deserve a Medicare system that shows up for them in return. I'm proud to help lead the bipartisan RESCUE Act to ensure EMS is reimbursed based on the real cost of the care they provide, just like other healthcare providers already are. This is especially critical in rural Texas and rural communities across the country, where a funding shortfall can mean the difference between an EMS agency staying open or shutting its doors. We will keep working to close this gap and make sure rural America never loses access to the emergency care it depends on," said Rep. August Pfluger (TX-11).

The legislation is co-led by Reps. Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Beth Van Duyne (TX-24), Kim Schrier (WA-08), John Joyce (PA-13), Brad Schneider (IL-10), Claudia Tenney (NY-24), and Terri Sewell (AL-07).

Read full text of the legislation here.

"As Co-Chair of the Congressional Air Medical Caucus, I know that every second counts when it comes to getting patients to lifesaving care," said Rep. Jill Tokuda (HI-02). "For people living in rural America, medical care isn't always around the corner—it often requires long drives or emergency flights, especially to reach specialized treatment. We cannot allow outdated Medicare payment rates to jeopardize the air and ground ambulance services our rural and remote communities rely on. The RESCUE Act is essential to protecting access to emergency care when it matters most."

“Every second matters when an ambulance is racing to save a life — first responders are already stretched thin, and rates that haven't kept pace with real costs shouldn't be one more thing standing in their way,” said Rep. Van Duyne. “I’m glad to help introduce the RESCUE Act to fix this deficiency and make sure the fee schedule keeps up with real costs," said Rep. Beth Van Duyne (TX-24).

"We all know the value our emergency responders provide," said Rep John Joyce, M.D. (PA-13). "Whether they're first on scene at a fire, a medical emergency, or an accident on the road, these men and women are integral servants in our community. Yet too often, ambulance services aren't reimbursed for the true cost of the lifesaving care they provide, especially in rural districts like mine, where providers travel long distances to reach patients. This bill fixes that imbalance and helps ensure no community loses access to emergency care.”

title: Rep. Pfluger Announces Service Academy Night in San Angelo
text:

title: WATCH: Pressley Tours Dilley ICE Detention Center, Renews Her Demands for Its Immediate Closure & the Release of Families
text:
“The world is watching as the Trump administration separates immigrant families, destroys the lives of children and parents, and locks them away without due process or access to adequate water, food, education, and medical care,” said Congresswoman Pressley in a statement. “What we witnessed in this facility was harrowing and horrific. I leave today clear as ever that Congress must close Dilley, end the practice of family detention, and abolish ICE now. We must put an end to Trump and ICE’s campaign of terror, and keep fighting for dignity, humanity, and freedom for every single one of our neighbors.”

“Today, I met again with the children and families being detained in Dilley. For months I have been visiting Dilley, where there still remains no access to proper medical care, food, or education. Despite repeated and continued calls from myself, my colleagues, and our communities demanding, this cruel and inhumane treatment continues. The children and families being held at Dilley must be freed and the center closed immediately.” – said Rep. Joaquin Castro (TX-20)

“What we saw today at Dilley was nothing short of horrific. No child, woman, or family should be locked up like this. We must close Dilley now and release these families. Children are being jailed and traumatized while private contractors profit from it, all at the expense of American taxpayers.” – said Rep. Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03)

“Every American needs to know what we saw at the ICE Detention Center in Dilley today because it is the opposite of what we say we stand for as Americans. What we saw when we went to the facility to conduct oversight was desperation and indefinite detention for some—many women waiting for months and months with no information about their cases. By definition, no one at Dilley has a criminal record, but there we spoke with women who had little contact with the world outside, little information, and little hope. They are experiencing trauma while the rest of the country goes on without insight into their conditions or their cases because the U.S. government is not being honest with the American people about what, how, and why it is doing what it is doing. It must stop. This mass detention of women, children, and families does not serve the interests of the American people and does not represent who we are or aspire to be as a people.” – said Rep. Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07)

“ICE is being increasingly secretive about their actions at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. We were only allowed to speak to one child out of 112 children – and even that interaction was cut short.ICE is traumatizing over 500 individuals – including pregnant women, children, and infants as young as 2 months old – and subjecting them to inhumane conditions for extended periods of time. These individuals should be living their lives, welcoming their newborn children, playing with their friends, and raising their families outside of ICE detention. The Trump Administration must be held accountable for the trauma it is inflicting on immigrant families. Children should not be detained, and I am continuing to call for the Dilley Detention Facility to be shut down, immediately.” – Rep. Luz Rivas

“The inhumane conditions at Dilley are well-documented and we must end family detention. This includes shutting down Dilley and releasing these children and families immediately. Dilley lacks basic necessities for anyone, especially children: no access to clean water, medical care, or proper education. Dilley reflects a broader pattern that should not be expanded with additional, unprecedented taxpayer funding. Yet, Congress has committed more than $260 billion to expand enforcement, on top of the regular appropriations to ICE and CBP of roughly $30 billion for FY25. This will only cause irreparable harm to children and communities. Thank you to the Members who continue to call for the release of families and we join them in their calls for Dilley’s closure.” – said Todd Schulte, President of FWD.us, at the press conference.

Transcript: Rep. Pressley’s Remarks Following Oversight Inspection of Dilley ICE Detention Center

San Antonio, TX

July 28, 2026

My name is Ayanna Pressley. I’m a Congresswoman representing the Massachusetts Seventh congressional district, which includes the city of Boston, also home to the third largest Haitian diaspora in the country. And so I’ve been on the front lines of this, these grave injustices in many ways.

I do want to also just commend Congressman Castro and his entire team, and Fwd.us, for your vigilance.

It’s so important that we not normalize this. It’s so important that we not acquiesce to this.

This, this fascist administration, this dictator in the Oval Office—history has shown us time again appeasement does not work. The only way to beat a dictator is with defiance. The only way to beat fascism is to refuse to accept this segregated, divided, dark, dystopian view that they have for our country. To reject it as an inevitability.

So we have to resist, reject, condemn at every turn, and shine a light.

And so I’m so grateful for the leadership of Congressman Castro. This is his eighth oversight visit to the Dilley detention facility.

I want to do some quick level setting here. So, and please correct me if my notes were inaccurate. So there are currently 539 individuals, 84 families. 50 out of those 84 families are male, head of household. 16 are female, head of household, and then there are 18 that are dual. There are also four pregnant women.

And I want to correct the record because earlier I said when we first came out of Dilley after our, after our oversight visit that they characterized all the detainees as low-level non-violent criminals. That’s inaccurate. They characterize them as low-level non-criminals.

That’s how they were all—that’s, that’s how, when we were getting our orientation and asking our questions of the officers, that’s how they characterize the detainees: low-level non-criminals.

So it seems their only crime is that they exist?

These are law-abiding people that are our neighbors, people we love, we live next to, we work and worship with, who were just going about their lives and met with such an aggressive disruption that they will be recovering from for the rest of their lives.

And I also just want to say that this these are two sides of a very evil for-profit coin. I have worked my entire life to dismantle mass incarceration, and I need people to understand that if you are outraged by the number of Black and low-income people that are incarcerated, the same for-profit system is driving the unlawful detainment and deportation of our immigrant neighbors.

CoreCivic is worth over a billion dollars, so this for-profit infrastructure, this for-profit evil, is for child abuse. They are for child neglect. They are for childhood trauma. They are for family separation.

One of the young women that I met with—and I have to say, every time I leave a detention facility, I am conflicted. Because I want to uplift these stories, but I don’t want to further endanger anyone. And I know very often when we leave these facilities, they are met with great hostility, and I don’t want to put them in any more harm’s way.

But one young woman that I met with, 30 years old, she is the mother of two children, a five-year-old girl and a three-year-old girl.

She fell into my arms within a matter of seconds, sharing with me that she was unable to wish her five-year-old daughter a happy birthday.

She also talked to me about how she arrived, how she ended up there. She was delivering packages. She’s a delivery driver, and there was a problem with her hazards. So she pulled over her car and had the lights blinking while she went in to deliver the package.

When she came out, law enforcement was there. They asked for an ID. She said, you know, “Why?” But she provided it. It was a Mexico ID. So this young lady, this 30-year-old young woman, she was here on a tourist visa from Mexico. Her mother, who brought her here at the age of four years old, developed cancer and died. So she’s been living here since the age of four, working, law-abiding.

She fell into an abusive relationship, and there were many, many times that the police were called on her husband, who was a violent abuser, and she is so upset because that abuser currently has the custody of her children.

So here she is, someone who is a survivor of domestic violence, law-abiding, making positive contributions, an incredible mom, and she asked me, “My husband was released on a bond of $150 after he beat me for hours and even tried to run me over with his car, and I was told that if I wanted to bond out, I would need to pay $9,000, and I’ve committed no crime.”

I asked her if her faith is some of what keeps her strong in this moment, and she said, “My faith in God is being tested every day. My faith in this country.”

And then just as I close this, I want to say, so many of the detainees that I have met, whether I was in Louisiana or Texas or in Massachusetts, they are some of the greatest patriots you will ever meet.

They love this country, and they are making positive, they have been making positive contributions to it every day, and it is a great betrayal.

And you see that. You see that betrayal in their eyes. You see the vacancy in their eyes. You see the trauma in their eyes.

So Dilley must be shut down. We have to abolish ICE, and then I’m going to take it one step further and say, any of those agents that have contributed to and caused the injury, the harm, and even fatalities, they must also be held accountable. And we should abolish qualified immunity for these federal law enforcement officers. There must be some recourse and some restitution.

And with that, we’ll now turn it over to another incredible member and colleague in the Democratic Women’s Caucus. Again, this is a joint oversight visit with Congressman Castro and the women of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, Rep Rivas.

title: Moore, Ramirez, McGarvey Visit Constituents with Health Concerns at Campbell County Detention Center
text:
Newport, Kentucky — Yesterday, Congressmembers Gwen Moore (WI-04), Delia C. Ramirez (IL-03), and Morgan McGarvey (KY-03) visited the Campbell County Detention Center in Kentucky to provide oversight of the facility and conduct a welfare check on three constituents suffering from a lack of medical care. The members heard from Ricardo, Octavio, and Anabell, who have experienced inhumane conditions, lack of proper food to manage their well-being, delays in medication, and inadequate medical care.

Ricardo and Octavio are both residents of Illinois’ Third Congressional District who suffer from diabetes. During their time in detention, Ricardo and Octavio have been denied care and access to insulin. Anabell is a constituent of WI-04 who suffered a miscarriage in ICE custody and was denied the necessary and adequate medical care.

“As a member of Congress, I conducted oversight of the Campbell County Detention Center to check on my constituents, who are being denied needed medical care, including access to insulin. What I saw inside was devastating, and the lack of medical care was appalling: detainees pleading for help, medicine for purchase at the commissary, sickeningly inhumane conditions, and jail leadership attempting to gaslight us,” said Rep. Ramirez. “DHS continues to demonstrate gross disregard of our health, dignity, personhood, and safety. It is clear: We must end detention, dismantle DHS, and MELT ICE!”

“I visited Campbell County Detention Center in Kentucky with my colleagues, Representatives Ramirez and McGarvey, out of concern for my constituent, Anabell, and others who are suffering from medical neglect. I will continue honoring my oversight responsibilities and fighting for my constituents, wherever that might take me,” said Rep Gwen Moore.

“What we saw yesterday is exactly why Congressional oversight matters. We talked to diabetics who told us they can’t get their medicine and detainees who said they can’t get so much as an aspirin, all while the Trump administration has given ICE billions in taxpayer money. I’m grateful to Reps. Ramirez and Moore for coming to Kentucky, and we will continue holding this administration accountable,” said Rep. McGarvey:

The oversight visit comes as new ICE data shows that immigrant detention remains at a record high, with 65,765 detained immigrants, and over 20 deaths documented in detention during the first half of 2026. According to data, primary causes include delayed and denied medical care.

According to DHS’s data, despite the increase in the detained population, medical claims decreased by nearly $300 million from 2024 to 2025, reflecting both unpaid bills and detainees who may never have received care. On October 3, 2025, the VA suddenly terminated its agreement with ICE to process medical claims, leaving ICE with no capabilities to continue paying for off-site medical care for detainees, including prescription medications for individuals in ICE custody. From October to May, at least 29 people died in detention. Ramirez has opened a Congressional inquiry into the medical claim lapse.

title: RILEY DELIVERS MAJOR WIN FOR UPSTATE APPLE GROWERS FACING $30 MILLION IN LOSSES
text:
Riley took growers’ case directly to Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins and pushed USDA to deliver relief

WASHINGTON, DC — Congressman Josh Riley (NY-19) today announced that he secured a U.S. Department of Agriculture disaster declaration for Upstate New York growers devastated by this spring’s extreme weather.

The declaration allows eligible growers to apply for low-interest emergency loans and other disaster assistance through the USDA Farm Service Agency. New York growers reported more than $30 million in losses, with some farms losing nearly their entire crop.

“After April’s freeze, growers across Upstate New York told me they were facing catastrophic losses. I took Saunderskill Farms’ story straight to Secretary Rollins because when a farm loses nearly half its crop, it still has workers to pay, equipment loans to cover, and another growing season to finance—with half the income to do it,” said Congressman Riley. “These growers deserve support to recover, rebuild, and stay afloat until the next growing season. I worked with Secretary Rollins to get this disaster declaration approved, and we got it done.”

Following April’s freeze, Riley’s office heard directly from farms across Upstate New York about severe damage to apples, grapes, strawberries, stone fruits, and other specialty crops.

One of those farms was Saunderskill Farms in Accord, where the family was facing the loss of nearly half its apple crop.

During a June 4 hearing of the House Agriculture Committee, Riley brought Saunderskill’s story directly to U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins and called on her to work with him to approve New York’s disaster declaration as quickly as possible.

After the hearing, Riley visited Saunderskill Farms to meet with the family, inspect the damage firsthand, and discuss what federal relief would mean for the farm’s recovery.

Less than eight weeks after Riley took the issue directly to Rollins, USDA approved the disaster declaration.

The designation gives eligible producers eight months to apply for emergency loans through their local Farm Service Agency office. The loans can help growers restore or replace essential property, cover production costs, pay essential family living expenses, reorganize farming operations, and refinance certain debts.

Riley is also fighting to make sure Upstate growers are better protected before the next disaster. He secured provisions in the House-passed Farm Bill to improve crop insurance and strengthen disaster assistance for apple growers and other specialty-crop producers.

###

title: Congresswoman Luz Rivas Conducts Oversight at Dilley Family Detention Facility in Texas, Raises Alarm Over ICE Secrecy
text:
Dilley, Texas — Congresswoman Luz Rivas (CA-29), representative for California’s 29th Congressional District, conducted a Congressional oversight visit of the Dilley Immigration Processing Center in Texas with her colleagues, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20), Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03), Congresswoman Lizzie Fletcher (TX-07), and Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07). The Members visited the Dilley Immigration Processing Center to meet with women, children, and families who have been detained for extended periods of time and conduct oversight on the conditions of the facility, which has been consistently reported as inhumane and dire.

“My colleagues and I met with 20 people, including a 16-year-old, who have been detained at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center for months,” said Congresswoman Rivas. “I spoke with a woman from Maryland who was attending her court hearing in March when she was detained and sent to the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. Her 12-year-old son with special needs has a court hearing tomorrow and is worried that he, too, will be sent to the Dilley Immigration Processing Center or even deported. This is one story among hundreds – of mothers detained, children pulled away from school, families separated, and lives being disrupted in ways that often go unseen. We owe it to these families to listen and respond.”

Unfortunately, ICE officials on-site severely limited access to Members. More specifically, the Members were only able to talk to one child, even though over 100 children are detained. Members were not shown the medical unit nor classrooms, which were of particular importance especially to determine the conditions of the facility. Members observed that ICE is becoming more secretive and more restrictive, including not even providing the number of federal workers on site. This is concerning and only underscores the continued calls to shut down the Dilley Detention Facility. During their visit, Members were shown a courtroom where cases are heard, an intake facility where pregnant women, children, and infants are processed, and a small plastic playground that offers no shade to children from the Texas sun.

Congresswoman Rivas continued: “ICE is being increasingly secretive about their actions at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. We were only allowed to speak to one child out of 112 children – and even that interaction was cut short. ICE is traumatizing over 500 individuals – including pregnant women, children, and infants as young as 2 months old – and subjecting them to inhumane conditions for extended periods of time. These individuals should be living their lives, welcoming their newborn children, playing with their friends, and raising their families outside of ICE detention. The Trump Administration must be held accountable for the trauma it is inflicting on immigrant families. Children should not be detained, and I am continuing to call for the Dilley Detention Facility to be shut down, immediately.”

Background:

Congresswoman Luz Rivas has conducted seven oversight visits at immigration detention facilities in California and Texas, including at the Edward R. Roybal Federal Building, the Adelanto Detention Facility, the California City Detention Facility, and the Dilley Immigration Processing Center. ICE blocked Congresswoman Rivas from conducting oversight of detention facilities three times.

Congresswoman Rivas joined Congressman Joaquin Castro and over 100 of their House Democratic Caucus colleagues in calling for the Dilley Immigration Processing Center to be shut down.

Congresswoman Rivas has also sent five letters to ICE leadership calling for accountability into the conditions at detention centers and joined her colleagues for field hearings into ICE abuses in Los Angeles and Minneapolis-St. Paul.

Dilley Immigration Processing Center, also known as the South Texas Family Residential Center, was built in 2014 to detain women and children. 539 individuals are currently being held at the Dilley Immigration Processing Center.

A report on the Dilley Immigration Processing Center from Refugee and Immigrant Center for Education and Legal Services (RAICES) found that families are routinely being held longer than the 20-day legal limit, with many being held for months. The report noted unsafe and degrading conditions, including inadequate access to food, water, personal hygiene, and basic care that are particularly harmful to children. Pregnant women face inadequate prenatal care and unsafe medical practices, putting them and their unborn babies at risk. Many are deported without a meaningful opportunity to seek protection, raising concerns under U.S. and international law.

The report also mentions that facilities at the Dilley Immigration Detention Center lack educational resources for children, noting that classes are taught by a prison guard.

title: Ross, Foushee, Panetta Introduce Legislation to Support Foreign Language and International Education Programs
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Representatives Deborah Ross (NC-02), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), and Jimmy Panetta (CA-19) introduced the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act to support foreign language and international education programs at colleges and universities by reauthorizing Title VI of the Higher Education Act. For decades, the Title VI/Fulbright-Hays programs have provided a strong foundation for international, research, and world language studies, especially in less commonly taught foreign languages that hold strategic importance for the United States.

Despite their proven importance, this administration has taken steps to undermine and dismantle these critical programs. The President’s Fiscal Year (FY) 2026 Budget proposed zeroing out funding for international education programs at the Department of Education. The department has separately proposed eliminating the regulations governing Title VI and Fulbright-Hays, potentially allowing the administration to eliminate these programs entirely. The Higher Education Act has not been reauthorized since 2008.

The United States lags far behind European nations and other countries in foreign language proficiency, with approximately 10% of Americans speaking another language proficiently compared to 65% of Europeans. As demand grows for professionals with language skills and cross-cultural expertise in fields such as health, cybersecurity, and engineering, America’s competitiveness depends on our ability to communicate across languages and cultures.

“In Congress, I’m proud to represent world-renowned universities, colleges, and HBCUs, home to students driving cutting-edge research and innovation,” said Congresswoman Ross. “At a moment of unprecedented global competition, the United States cannot afford to fall behind in foreign language proficiency or international education. Yet the Trump administration has sought to eliminate funding for critical programs and attempted to dismantle key federal education funding entirely. It’s clear we must invest in the language and international education programs that strengthen our national security, expand opportunity, and keep America competitive.”

“Keeping Americans prepared to enter the workforce must include access to foreign language education. Continuing to struggle to keep pace with other nations in language education will threaten our global leadership and our ability to equip the next generation with the proper tools to become civil leaders,” said Congresswoman Foushee. “I’m proud to work with Congresswoman Ross and Congressman Panetta on this legislation that will make critical investments in language education to ensure our nation’s continued leadership for years to come.”

“Language education can broaden horizons and expand opportunities for Americans within our borders and beyond,” said Congressman Panetta. “As the co-chair of the America’s Languages Caucus, I’m proud to support the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act, which would extend language programs that are critical to building a workforce ready to compete around the world. By investing in language and international education programs today, we ensure our nation can continue leading the world and the global economy.”

Specifically, the Advancing International and Foreign Language Education Act would:

Reauthorize and extend programs for international and foreign language studies, including National Resource Centers, Language Resource Centers, Undergraduate International Studies, and American Overseas Research Centers.

Reauthorize Foreign Language and Area Studies Fellowships, allowing graduate students to receive stipends for studying foreign languages.

Extend and update the International Research and Innovation program, including establishing a national database on international and foreign language education.

Reauthorize and update programs for international business skills and education, including renaming and expanding activities in professional and technical training curricula.

title: Rep. Peters, Businesses, and Labor Leaders Call on Trump Admin to Stop Stalling DACA Renewals
text:
San Diego, CA – Today, Rep. Scott Peters convened business, labor, and community leaders to urge the Trump Administration to process Deferred Action for Childhood Arrivals (DACA) renewal applications in a timely manner. Delays at U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), which seem intentional and politically motivated, have slowed renewal processing time to almost double what it used to be.

“Nearly 9,000 DACA recipients call San Diego home. They work hard, pay taxes, and contribute tens of millions of dollars to our local economy every year. For many of them, the U.S. is the only home they’ve ever known,” Rep. Peters said. “I spoke out when Donald Trump attacked DACA the first time, but our work is not over. We need answers from this Administration about the never-ending delays at USCIS. How do they plan to address the backlog they created? Are DACA recipients being detained because of this lag?”

President Trump’s immigration policies have impacted the cost of healthcare, groceries, rent, and electricity. This is in part due to the delays in renewals which threaten the livelihoods of legal immigrants and put undue stress on businesses who are faced with uncertainty as their valued employees await decisions about their status. In San Diego alone, Dreamers, including DACA recipients, contribute $968 million annually to the local economy.

"Every day a DACA renewal sits in a backlog is a day a San Diego business risks losing one of its own employees," said Chris Cate, President & CEO, San Diego Regional Chamber of Commerce. "After more than a decade of temporary protections, it's time for Congress to deliver a permanent, bipartisan solution that gives Dreamers the stability they deserve and gives San Diego employers the certainty they need.”

“Delays in processing DACA renewals are inexcusable and negligent,” said Dr. Arcela Nunez-Alvarez, Co-Founder and Co-Director, Universidad Popular. “These delays expose applicants to unnecessary suffering, including loss of work authorization, income, health coverage, and educational opportunities, and most importantly, loss of immigration protection. The delays create an adverse domino effect, increasing vulnerability for applicants and their families.”

“For a small business barely making payroll, DACA renewal delays mean shorter hours, slower service, lost revenue, and thousands of dollars in turnover costs – money that should be going to wages, growth, and this community,” said Trevor Moore, Vice President, Cush Enterprises. “DACA recipients have done everything by the book their entire lives. They register with the federal government and ask permission to keep working and paying taxes. Our economy is nothing without the effort and loyalty of these people.”

"For 18 months, this Administration’s chaotic, capricious, and arbitrary approach to immigration enforcement has been fundamentally about sowing fear and disrupting our communities,” said Carol Kim, Executive Secretary-Treasurer, San Diego and Imperial Counties Labor Council. “It also disrupts the ability of anyone to do business and reliably work, not just the workers who are targeted, but every working person whose specific tasks or projects are derailed by disappearing coworkers, disappearing funding, and disappearing basic government functions. Every American who expects that work to come through pays the price, too.”

DACA must be renewed every two years, and work authorizations cannot be renewed until DACA status is renewed. Rep. Scott Peters’ office is seeing the highest volume of immigration casework requests during his time in Congress, driven by these mounting delays which affect our community and economy.

title: Sorensen’s Bipartisan Bill to Fight Robocall Scams Clears Key Step
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — Congressmen Eric Sorensen (IL-17) is celebrating an important step forward for his bipartisan Quashing Unwanted and Interruptive Electronic Telecommunications (QUIET) Act. The legislation was recently included in a House Energy and Commerce Communications and Technology Subcommittee hearing focused on protecting communications networks and combating illegal robocalls and robotexts.

As part of the hearing, Sorensen submitted a statement for the record urging the committee to advance the QUIET Act. The legislation has also been endorsed by AARP, which submitted a letter backing the bill.

“Every day, families are bombarded with scam calls and fake text messages designed to steal their money and personal information,” said Congressman Eric Sorensen. “Congress has a responsibility to act. My bipartisan QUIET Act will hold scammers accountable and better protect seniors, families, and consumers from fraud.”

“AARP research shows that consumers are already deeply concerned about the use of AI-generated voices in scams and continue to experience scam and illegal robocalls at alarming rates. Americans should not have to wonder whether the voice on the other end of the line is a loved one in distress, a government official, or a sophisticated AI-generated impersonation designed to steal their savings,” said Bill Sweeney, Senior Vice President of Government Affairs at the AARP. “Older adults deserve the confidence to answer the phone without fear of being targeted by increasingly sophisticated scam operations.”

The QUIET Act increases penalties for violators who use AI to impersonate individuals or organizations with the intent to defraud, cause harm, or wrongfully obtain anything of value. This measure would strengthen protections for seniors and vulnerable communities who are often the biggest targets of these scams.

The Subcommittee hearing marks an important milestone as the legislation continues moving through the committee process toward consideration by the full House Energy and Commerce Committee.

Since coming to Congress, Sorensen has made fighting scam robocalls and robotexts a priority. Last Congress, he led a bipartisan effort urging the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to outline its plans to combat these scams, which disproportionately target older Americans.

title: Rep. Stansbury and Rep. Guest Introduce Legislation to Boost Tribal Schools and Teacher Pay
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representatives Melanie Stansbury (D-NM-01) and Michael Guest (R-MS-03) introduced the Indigenous Students Excel through Parity Act, bipartisan legislation that directs the Secretary of the Interior to recommend updates to the Indian School Equalization Formula, which governs funding for Bureau of Indian Education (BIE) funded schools. This includes funding for 183 schools across 64 tribal communities in 23 states that serve nearly 47,000 students through BIE-operated and Tribally controlled schools.

For years, BIE-funded schools have been severely underfunded by the federal government, from operational funding to construction and maintenance of schools. This has left schools without adequate funding to meet student needs and left teachers and educators without parity in teacher salaries compared to other school systems. The Indigenous Students Excel through Parity Act works to address this issue by reexamining the formula funds that fund these schools and discovering ways to ensure teachers and staff have competitive salaries, small and rural Tribal schools have adequate funding, and new revenue sources are identified to bring BIE-funded schools into parity with other school systems.

“Every student deserves the opportunity to thrive, and every teacher deserves to be paid what they’re worth. This bill is to ensure Bureau of Indian Education and Tribally controlled schools have the resources they need to succeed,” said Rep. Stansbury. “I'm proud to introduce the bipartisan Indigenous Students Excel through Parity Act, legislation to advance BIE funding, support Native students and teachers, and create new educational opportunities. Working with our Tribal nations and schools, we are fighting every day to ensure our schools have the resources they need!”

“I am honored to co-lead the ISEP Act with Congresswoman Stansbury," said Rep. Guest. “Our students deserve access to a quality education. Schools funded through the Bureau of Indian Education often face unique funding, staffing, and rural challenges that can make it difficult to recruit and retain qualified educators. This bipartisan bill will help identify those disparities and provide Congress with the information needed to improve educational opportunities for our Native American students.”

Key provisions of the legislation include:

A Formula Study: Within one year of enactment, the Secretary of the Interior, in coordination with the Assistant Secretary for Indian Affairs and the Director of the BIE, will evaluate updates to the Indian School Equalization Formula, including alternative methods for equitable distribution of funds.

A Competitive Compensation Benchmark: The study will evaluate a compensation standard equal to the higher of either the highest quartile or average state-by-state salaries for non-Bureau public school staff, or the rate of basic compensation for Department of Defense overseas teaching positions. \

Consideration for Small and Rural Schools: The study will weigh factors specific to tribally controlled schools, schools with fewer than 100 students, and schools located in rural areas.

A Report to Congress: The Secretary will submit a report to Congress and make it publicly available to Indian Tribes describing the adequacy of the current formula and program, along with recommendations for improvement.

A Revenue Source Study: Within one year of enactment, the Secretary will also conduct a separate study to identify potential revenue sources to help bring Bureau-funded schools into parity with other school systems.

The bill is endorsed by key Tribal organizations including the National Indian Education Association (NIEA) and the National Congress of American Indians (NCAI).

Companion legislation was introduced in the United States Senate by Senators Martin Heinrich (D-NM) and Cynthia Lummis (R-WY).

You can read the full text of the bill here.

Additionally, Rep. Melanie Stansbury also introduced the Indigenous Students Excel through Parity Act (II), which would enact changes in formula funding studied in the bipartisan Indigenous Students Excel through Parity Act described above.

This bill actualizes the Secretary of the Interior’s recommended updates to the Indian School Equalization Formula, requiring the Interior Department to update the Indian School Equalization Formula within one year of the bill’s enactment. Additionally, this bill would ensure that Tribally controlled, small, and rural schools have access to more equitable funding by bringing BIE teacher salaries in line with top-quartile state pay. The bill also requires the President to request full funding for this program every single year in his annual budget request, protecting Tribal funding.

The full text of the Indigenous Students Excel through Parity Act (II) can be found here.

title: Rep. Summer Lee, State Sen. Maria Collett, and Pennsylvanians Sound Alarm on Medicaid Rule Threatening Those With Serious Illnesses and Disabilities as Deadline Looms
text:
VIDEO: Full Press Call

PITTSBURGH, PA – JULY 28, 2026 — Today, Congresswoman Summer L. Lee (PA-12) joined Pennsylvania State Senator Maria Collett, Medicaid recipients, caregivers, and health care advocates for a press call warning that a harsh new Trump administration rule could rip health coverage away from Pennsylvanians with serious and chronic illnesses.

The call, hosted alongside Unrig Our Economy, Action Together NEPA, and Affordable Pennsylvania, came just days before the public comment period for the proposed rule closes on July 31, 2026.

The proposed rule follows Republicans’ passage of the largest Medicaid cuts in the program’s history. Pennsylvania Republicans in Congress voted for the Republican tax law that opened the door to these new restrictions while providing additional tax breaks to billionaires and giant corporations.

Participants warned that the rule could put patients with cancer, multiple sclerosis, HIV/AIDS, hepatitis, end-stage renal disease, sickle cell disease, and other serious and debilitating illnesses at risk of losing their health coverage. They also urged Pennsylvanians to submit public comments opposing the rule before the July 31 deadline.

“Medicaid is a lifeline for millions of Pennsylvanians. It is how parents take their children to the doctor, how seniors and people with disabilities receive care, and how people managing cancer, diabetes, HIV, sickle cell disease, and other chronic illnesses access lifesaving treatment,” said Congresswoman Summer Lee (PA-12). “The new Medicaid policies from Trump and Republicans will only make it harder for folks in my district and across the country. Nearly 20,000 people in my district alone could lose their coverage. Instead of making health care more affordable, these policies will force families to navigate more paperwork and place lifesaving care further out of reach.”

“Pennsylvania families should not lose health care because Washington politicians decided to make Medicaid harder to access,” said Pennsylvania State Senator Maria Collett. “I was a registered nurse before coming to the state legislature, and I cared for patients at the bedside. I made sure that Pennsylvanians had access to quality, affordable health care, and it is a top priority of mine to continue doing that. Unfortunately, we have seen time and again that that is not a priority that the Trump administration and Washington Republicans share. These new Medicaid rules will force recipients to navigate a confusing list of exemptions and repeatedly prove their eligibility. We should be cutting costs, not cutting people off from care.”

"Medicaid gave me the chance to heal and eventually return to work. People who are recovering from catastrophic injuries deserve the dignity of making medical decisions with their doctors – not having to prove over and over that they deserve health care,” said Krysten, a Medicaid recipient in Scranton. “Instead of making sick and injured Pennsylvanians jump through more hoops, Congress should be asking why billionaires and large corporations are getting another tax break at our expense. Congressman Rob Bresnahan should stand with families like mine and protect the health care that made my recovery possible."

"Medicaid allows me to care for my partner, who has cerebral palsy, so he can live safely and with dignity at home," said Lynn, a homecare worker in Allentown. "People with disabilities and their families know what they need to live healthy, independent lives – they shouldn't have to prove it over and over again through more paperwork and bureaucratic hurdles. If Congress wants more oversight, it should start with the billionaires and large corporations receiving massive tax breaks, not families who depend on Medicaid to survive. Congressman Ryan Mackenzie should stand with caregivers like me and protect the health care that allows our loved ones to live with dignity."

"When I suffered a stroke at 20, Medicaid made it possible for me to receive the around-the-clock care I needed to recover," said Grace, a Medicaid recipient in Cresco. "Living with a disability already means navigating challenges every day. People like me deserve the dignity of knowing we can access the care we need without constantly having to fight to prove we're sick enough or disabled enough. Instead of creating new barriers for people with serious illnesses, our leaders should be asking why billionaires and giant corporations are receiving tax breaks while basic health care is being put at risk. Congressman Rob Bresnahan should stand with his constituents and protect Medicaid."

“Republicans in Congress like Rob Bresnahan, Ryan Mackenzie, and Scott Perry voted for massive cuts to Medicaid to fund tax breaks for billionaires. Now, Pennsylvanians with serious illnesses are at-risk of losing health care coverage altogether due to this Medicaid rule,” said Unrig Our Economy Campaign Director Leor Tal. “This is not an accident — this is the consequence of putting the wants of the ultra-rich over the needs of their constituents. We need everyone to speak out against this rule before the July 31 deadline, and, even better, we need Republicans in Congress to undo these devastating cuts to Medicaid that are jeopardizing Pennsylvanians’ lives.”

“At Action Together, we hear from people who are struggling to make impossible decisions regarding the health care that they need every single day. Last year, Ryan Mackenzie, Rob Bresnahan, and Scott Perry all voted to drastically cut Medicaid just to give billionaires and big corporations a tax break,” said Kristin Volchansky, Advocacy Director for Action Together NEPA. “As someone who has relied on Medicaid for treatments for a chronic disorder, I know that struggle all too well. We need to raise our voices against this new proposed rule that would only make it harder to access the care they desperately need. Members of Congress need to undo the damage they’ve done — the lives of Pennsylvanians depend on it.”

"Ryan Mackenzie, Rob Bresnahan, and Scott Perry voted to gut Medicaid so billionaires and giant corporations could get another tax break. This new rule is exactly what they voted for," said Rachele Fortier, Executive Director of Affordable Pennsylvania. "When eligible Pennsylvanians lose Medicaid, they don't lose a government program — they lose chemotherapy appointments, home health aides, medications, and the care that keeps them out of the hospital. Our members of Congress should be fighting to protect their constituents, not defending policies that put their health at risk."

Congresswoman Lee has made protecting and expanding affordable health care a core priority throughout her time in Congress. She has fought RepublicanMedicaid cuts, voted to extendACA tax credits, introduced theDrug Deal Disclosure Act, backed legislation addressingwrongful denials, and cosponsoredMedicare for All. She continues working to lower costs, hold powerful health care corporations accountable, and ensure every family can access quality care without going into debt.

Watch the full press call HERE.

title: Representative Lee Highlights $850,000 in Funding She Secured for Opportunity Village
text:
Watch and download video here

LAS VEGAS, NV – Today, during Disability Pride Month, Congresswoman Susie Lee (NV-03) joined Opportunity Village to host a roundtable discussing federal funding Lee secured to help build Opportunity Village’s northwest campus. Opportunity Village, a non-profit organization that serves people in the Las Vegas community with intellectual disabilities, plans to open its northwest campus location in fall 2026 at 5080 W. Rome Blvd. The project will provide housing, direct employment, workforce development and day habilitation services to hundreds of Nevada residents with intellectual and developmental disabilities.

Rep. Lee was joined by Nicholas Aguilar, who will be moving into the new northwest campus, and his mother, Patty Aguilar. Opportunity Village’s Chief Program Officer, Chuck Neuwohner; Director of Program Services, Sarah Quinn; and Director of Development, Taylor Palmer, also participated in the discussion.

title: Rep. Sykes Secures $20,000 in Federal Arts Funding for Akron Performance Series
text:
AKRON, OHIO — Today, U.S. Representative Emilia Sykes (OH-13) announced the National Endowment for the Arts has awarded $20,000 to Art Resources Transformations to support a multidisciplinary performance series.

title: ICYMI: Taylor’s Bill Promoting American Gun Manufacturing Passes in NDAA
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Dave Taylor (OH-02) celebrated the passage of his Make American Guns Again (MAGA) Act in the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) on July 22, 2026, by a vote of 216-212.

“America’s military was designed to be the world’s most lethal fighting force, and I’m proud to support this legislation that will ensure our warfighters are equipped to win," said Congressman Taylor. “My MAGA Act will shield our weapons supply chain from dependence on foreign countries, and I’m proud to see it included in the FY27 NDAA. Our servicemembers’ success starts with confidence in the weapons they carry into battle, and my bill will do just that as they fight to protect the freedoms we hold dear.”

The FY27 NDAA aims to revitalize America’s defense industrial base by expanding U.S. production capacity, unleashing private-sector investment, and creating thousands of jobs for skilled Americans. By strengthening nuclear deterrence, expanding missile defense, and targeting resources to counter adversaries, the NDAA prioritizes investment in the capabilities needed to maintain a strong U.S. posture on the world stage.

Additionally, the NDAA improves servicemembers’ quality of life by raising servicemembers’ pay by 5% to 7% and improving housing, education, and access to childcare for military families.

Background:

Congressman Taylor initially introduced the MAGA Act on July 17, 2025. This bill would require the Secretary of War to submit a report to congressional defense committees no later than March 15, 2027, on the prevalence of government-issued small arms and light weapons used by America’s military that were either manufactured outside of the United States or in the U.S. by a subsidiary of a foreign-owned entity.

This bill would additionally require the Secretary of War to issue recommendations for procuring more small arms and light weapons from companies that are American-owned, operated, and located in the United States.

title: PRESS STATEMENT: Congressman Shri Thanedar Leads Letter Demanding Transparency from Trump Administration on Cyclosporiasis Crisis
text:
Washington, DC - Last week, Congressman Shri Thanedar urged greater transparency from the heads of the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) and the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) regarding the recent surge in cyclosporiasis cases. In a letter to Dr. Kyle Diamantas and Dr. Jay Bhattacharya, Acting Commissioner of the FDA and Acting Director of the CDC respectively, Thanedar laid out the public health threat posed by cyclosporiasis and called on the officials to improve efforts to keep the public informed.

“The American public deserves accurate information about potential public health risks and the confidence that every possible step is being taken to identify the cause of these illnesses, prevent future infections, and ensure access to appropriate treatment,” wrote Congressman Thanedar. “We are urging the FDA and CDC to continue working closely with state health departments and local public health agencies to strengthen food safety measures, improve outbreak detection, and identify all other sources as immediately feasible. The FDA should continue to collaborate with the CDC to invest in the Cyclospora Prevention, Response, and Research Action Plan to support research on prevention, detection, treatment, and improved surveillance of cyclosporiasis.”

Cyclospora outbreaks have increased across America over the past year, but Michigan, especially Southeast Michigan, has been the hardest hit for cyclosporiasis cases in the country. As of July 23, 2026, Michigan has experienced 8,176 reported cases since late June 2026, with 160 hospitalizations.

Congressman Shri Thanedar was joined on this letter by Congressman Eric Sorensen, Congressman Joaquin Castro, Congressman Tom Suozzi, Congresswoman Nanette Díaz Barragán, Congressman Chuy García, Congressman Gil Cisneros, and Congresswoman Sarah McBride. The full text of the letter can be viewed here.

Congressman Shri Thanedar proudly represents Michigan's 13th Congressional District, which includes Detroit, Downriver, and the Grosse Pointes. As a champion for working families, Shri is committed to advancing economic opportunities, education, healthcare access, and entrepreneurship for underserved communities. Drawing from his journey from poverty to success, he works tirelessly to uplift Metro Detroit, ensuring every resident has the resources and support they need to thrive.

title: Thompson, Colleagues Introduce Legislation to Support Young Farmers
text:
BELLEFONTE, Pa. – This week, United States Representatives Glenn “GT” Thompson (R-PA), Joe Courtney (D-CT), Monica De La Cruz (R-TX), and Nikki Budzinski (D-IL) introduced the Young Farmer Success Act. This bipartisan legislation would help America’s young farmers and ranchers manage their student loan debt by making them eligible for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness (PSLF) program, preserving America’s agriculture economy and easing financial concerns for young farmers.

"In recent years, the average age of the American farmer has steadily increased, making it imperative to support the next generation in order to secure our food supply. The Young Farmers Success Act will offer incentives to young people entering the agricultural workforce, and invests in our future and national security,” Rep. Thompson said.

“Now more than ever, we need to support the next generation of farmers. The number of small farms nationwide is declining, the average age of American farmers is rising, and the agriculture industry is being hit hard by high costs,” Rep.Courtney said. “For young farmers entering the profession, student loan debt can hold them back from being able to make needed investments in farming equipment. Farmers keep us fed and take care of our land. That’s true public service that should be recognized with eligibility for the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program. Thank you to Congressman Thompson for again partnering with me in this effort to support young farmers and to the strong grassroots advocates, including eastern Connecticut’s Susan Mitchell of Cloverleigh Farm in Columbia, who have been a driving force behind the Young Farmer Success Act.”

"Investing in the next generation of farmers is essential to sustaining the future of our food security. Only 9% of U.S. farmers are under the age of 35. By giving young farmers access to Public Service Loan Forgiveness through the Young Farmer Success Act, we can provide more young men and women with the opportunity to pursue farming," Rep. De La Cruz said.

"Agriculture is the No. 1 economic engine in Illinois, but we need to make sure the next generation is set up for success," Rep. Budzinski said. "Too many young people who want to farm or work in agriculture are held back by the cost of student loans. That's why this legislation is a commonsense way to help more young people build careers in agriculture, strengthen family farms, and keep our rural communities strong. I'm proud to co-lead this bill and ensure we are investing in the people who will grow our food and keep this industry moving forward."

"As a first-generation farmer, I can relate to the struggles our prospective young farmers and ranchers face when looking to pursue a career in agriculture,” said Tommy Nagle, President of Pennsylvania Farm Bureau. “The USDA's Agriculture Census showed a nationwide average age of 58 years old for producers, with the average age in Pennsylvania being a little bit higher than the national average. Agriculture is the backbone of Pennsylvania's economy, so it is crucial that we support legislation that promotes reducing barriers for younger generations in the industry. We recognize one of the most prominent financial burdens for young farmers and ranchers is their outstanding student loans because the agriculture industry's salaries are not the highest paying, yet their jobs are critical for food and national security. Having a robust agricultural workforce for years to come is imperative because American families depend on our producers to supply their food, fiber, and fuel. For these reasons, Pennsylvania Farm Bureau is proud to support the Young Farmer Success Act."

“We applaud Chairman "GT" Thompson and Representative Joe Courtney for leading this bipartisan effort to support the next generation of farmers,” said Gregg Doud, President and CEO of National Milk Producers Federation. “The Young Farmer Success Act is a commonsense investment in rural America that will help young producers manage the financial challenges of starting and growing a farm. By expanding access to student loan repayment assistance, this legislation strengthens the future of agriculture and helps ensure dedicated farmers can continue producing nutritious food for families here at home and around the world.”

“Young farmers across the country are passionately growing food for their communities and working the land. At the same time, they are struggling to find secure access to land, persisting through increasingly severe climate change impacts, and balancing rising farm input costs, inflation, market disruptions, and student loan debt,” said Vanessa Garcia Polanco, Policy Campaigns Director of National Young Farmers Coalition. “For many farmers getting started, their student loan debt burden is keeping them from realizing their farming ambitions. National Young Farmers Coalition supports efforts to secure a long overdue update to the Public Service Loan Forgiveness Program that would extend the program's benefits to the next generation of farmers and reduce their financial burden to stay and enter the agriculture workforce."

"The next generation of American family agriculture needs more support now than ever before. As the average age of the family farmer continues to rise, it is crucial that we remove as many barriers as possible to incentivize young producers to stay in the field. We commend Chairman Thompson and Representatives Budzinski, Courtney, and De La Cruz for introducing this bill to provide a pathway of support for the next generation of farmers and ranchers," said Rob Larew, President of National Farmers Union.

Read the full bill text here.

title: Congresswoman Torres Statement on FBI Raids in San Bernardino County
text:
Ontario, CA – Today, Congresswoman Norma Torres (CA-35) issued the following statement:

"I am deeply troubled by reports that the FBI has executed warrants against elected officials in San Bernardino County. I am awaiting further information, but our community has zero tolerance for corruption at any level of our government, from the President down to the City Council."

title: What They’re Saying: Broad Coalition Lauds Bipartisan FRONTIER Act
text:
Less than a week after Congresswoman Lori Trahan (D-MA-03) and Congressman Jay Obernolte (R-CA-23) introduced the Frontier Risk Oversight, National Transparency, Independent Evaluation, and Reporting (FRONTIER) Act, a broad coalition of stakeholders is praising the bipartisan legislation that would establish a federal risk-based framework governing the development and deployment of the most advanced artificial intelligence models.

The FRONTIER Act would establish a tiered, risk-based national framework for oversight of the most advanced AI models, requiring the largest developers to publish safety frameworks, submit to independent third-party audits and verification, and report critical safety incidents to a new Under Secretary of Commerce for AI Security. It is an updated version of the Commerce-focused portions of the lawmakers’ Great American AI Act (GAAIA) discussion draft, reworked over seven weeks of stakeholder feedback to narrow its preemption of state law and sharpen its auditing and reporting provisions.

“Not too long ago, a bipartisan bill this good and serious would have been a pipe dream. But things change quickly. This is by far the best AI safety bill ever introduced, in any jurisdiction,” said Charlie Bullock, Senior Research Fellow at the Institute for Law & AI. “There are still some flaws that I would like to see fixed, and some improvements to be made, but overall I'm very impressed with how well Reps. Trahan and Obernolte did on this. The next step is actually *passing* this kind of legislation, which unfortunately still seems like a pretty heavy lift. But this is a very promising first step.”

“AI governance keeps running into the same wall. The technology is hard to measure and it moves faster than any law can keep up with,”said Andrew Freedman, Co-Founder and CEO of Fathom. “Trying to write the perfect rules and freezing them in place won’t work. What will work is a competitive market of independent verifiers who are accountable for real-world outcomes and who the government can actually count on. The FRONTIER Act shows we can move fast and still get this right.”

“The latest version of the bipartisan Obernolte–Trahan framework, FRONTIER Act, is a serious step forward. It's one of the strongest efforts yet to establish a federal AI framework that protects Americans while preserving America's leadership in AI,” said the Alliance for a Better Future. “The bill gets several things right. Frontier developers would publish safety frameworks, file transparency reports before deployment, report serious safety incidents, and provide rapid notification when an imminent threat emerges. It also establishes meaningful emergency response authority and independent oversight for the most advanced AI systems. That's a targeted, risk-based approach that puts oversight where it's actually needed.”

“Rep. Lori Trahan and Rep. Jay Obernolte's bipartisan FRONTIER Act deserves a lot of credit here; they are clearly engaged with stakeholders and civil society across the spectrum and have incorporated extensive feedback,” said Caleb Knapp, Senior Policy Manager and Secure AI Now. “In an ideal world, federal standards for frontier AI model pre-deployment would have crossed the finish line a year ago. Strongly addressing these issues is even more imperative as the technology develops further. We are seeing more instances of AI misalignment with OpenAI/Hugging Face, Kimi, and otherwise. Is the bill perfect? No. But it is the strongest federal frontier bill to date and builds on all the great work occurring at the state level in CA, NY, IL, and elsewhere.”

“The FRONTIER Act is a meaningful bipartisan effort to strengthen oversight of the most advanced Al systems, and it's the strongest federal proposal to date. It builds on state regulations in many ways and incorporates a lot of the feedback that various stakeholders gave on the earlier discussion draft,” said the AI Verification & Evaluation Research Institute (AVERI). “There are some remaining areas for improvement, including making sure that state laws are not preempted until their federal replacements are ready and clarifying some of the auditing provisions. But this is undoubtedly a step in the right direction and we look forward to working with Representatives Trahan and Obernolte, their staff, and other members of Congress to strengthen this proposal and advance effective oversight of frontier Al.”

“Like a lot of people on [Twitter], I had some concerns regarding the initial federal framework discussion draft that Reps. Lori Trahan and Jay Obernolte released a couple weeks ago. I am happy to say that, after substantial engagement and feedback, they’ve crafted the strongest ai safety proposal to date in the FRONTIER Act. There’s still some improvements I’d like to see in the text, and I look forward to continued conversation with the sponsors. But! The narrower preemption and strong auditing provisions should inspire confidence that congress is evolving their approach quickly and worth engaging,” said Nat Purser, Director of U.S. Policy at AVERI.

“The revised FRONTIER Act is meaningfully better than GAAIA, the earlier draft from Representative Trahan and Representative Obernolte. They deserve credit for engaging constructively with stakeholders and taking feedback seriously,” said Nathan Calvin, General Counsel Encode AI. “Overall, this is very much a step in the right direction. Some important issues remain, but we’ll continue engaging with the authors and appreciate the work they’ve put into improving the bill.”

“It's a good bill—actually worth going for, I think,” said Anton Leicht, a Fellow with the Carnegie Endowment’s Technology and International Affairs team. “[Especially] after the past few weeks, federal third-party evaluation seems like a very good way to build capacity beyond exec branch scrambles fast, and to get actual insight into labs-as-entities and their internal deployments.”

“The FRONTIER Act gets the AI regulatory balance right: focus transparency and oversight on the handful of companies pushing the frontier through a coherent federal standard, and leave the rest of the ecosystem alone. Rather than micromanaging model development, it builds audit-and-disclosure infrastructure so that Congress, courts, and the American people can stay informed. Independent verification organizations make the framework adaptive in a way static rules never could, letting oversight evolve as fast as the technology. This is what right-sized AI governance looks like: light-touch with dynamic, third-party oversight where the risks are greatest,” said Samuel Hammond, Chief Economist & AI Policy Director at the Foundation for American Innovation.

“Seven weeks from discussion draft to introduced legislation is fast for Congress on anything; for AI, where the complaint is that they’ve been asleep at the wheel, it’s astounding. This wasn’t a panic bill scribbled over a weekend; the revision shows seven weeks of actual work, with gaps closed, clocks tightened, and new teeth added. The sponsor statements make it clear that they were watching the same news as the rest of us,” said Daniel Parshall, Ph.D., Founder and Director of the Canary Institute for AI Policy.
