title:
As Wildfires Burn 1+ Million Acres Across Oregon, 
Merkley, Wyden Press FEMA on Denial of Emergency Federal Assistance
text:
Salem, OR – Oregon’s U.S. Senators Jeff Merkley and Ron Wyden demanded urgent answers from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) in response to the agency’s denial of Fire Management Assistance Grants (FMAGs) for two wildfires in Oregon: the East Evans Creek Fire and Rowe Creek Fire Complex.

Both fires were under Level 3 “Go Now” Evacuation at the time of application, and the Rowe Creek Fire Complex was the largest in the nation. The current fire situation in Oregon remains the worst in the nation.

“FEMA’s decision to deny these FMAGs is a significant departure from FEMA’s historical criteria and agency guidance,” wrote the Senators. “According to State officials, FEMA’s criteria for an FMAG has been, in part, that 150 primary residences must be in immediate threat of wildfire, gauged often as Level 3 ‘Go Now’ Evacuation status. In recent years, State officials have seen an increase to over 200 primary residences as a threshold—which the East Evans Creek Fire and the Rowe Creek Fire Complex had still surpassed.”

The State of Oregon requested financial assistance from FEMA through FMAGs, which help cover costs relating to emergencies and firefighting activities for fires that have the potential to become major disasters. FEMA’s decision to deny these specific FMAGs comes as Oregon faces an increasingly dangerous fire season—with at least 86 active fires burning over 1 million acres and over 33,000 Oregonians under evacuation orders as of July 27, 2026.

“FEMA has also indicated that the East Evans Creek Fire and the Rowe Creek Fire Complex were denied an FMAG because they did not meet the criteria for a major disaster declaration,” the Senators continued. “This is a major shift in administrative policy and contrary to Federal regulation and FEMA’s own policy manual, which states that an FMAG designation is warranted when a fire ‘threatens such destruction as would constitute a major disaster.’ This program is meant to provide resources to fires that have the potential to become major disasters if left unchecked. Resources should not—and are not supposed to be—withheld until a fire becomes so destructive as to receive a major disaster declaration.”

Merkley and Wyden highlighted how FEMA’s inconsistent approval of FMAGs threatens to cause disruptions for first responders and at-risk communities. The Senators pressed FEMA for clear answers on its decision-making and criteria for FMAGs and stand ready to assist in ensuring Oregon has the necessary federal resources to respond to wildfires and keep communities across the state safe.

“We want to stress that this is not the time for creating new or different criteria for accessing this critical funding to support initial attack. As you know, Oregon is strained for resources, and the State is still at the beginning of its wildfire season. We urge the agency to provide clarity and maintain consistency with prior years’ approval process,” the Senators directed.

Full text of the letter can be found by clicking here and follows below:

Dear Mr. Fenton and Mr. Maykovich,

We write to express deep concern over the Federal Emergency Management Agency’s handling of the Fire Management Assistance Grant (FMAG) program in light of recent events. The State of Oregon is currently in a dire wildfire situation—the worst in the nation—with 86 active fires, as of July 27th, burning over 1 million acres with over 33,000 Oregonians under some level of evacuation and widespread impacts to critical infrastructure, including water and power, affecting alert and warning and 911 capabilities.

While we appreciate FEMA’s approval of FMAGs for select recent fires, including the Lower Dry Creek Fire, Akawa Butte Fire, and Grasshopper Fire, we are deeply concerned by the agency's denial of FMAGs for the East Evans Creek Fire and Rowe Creek Fire Complex, which at the time of application was the largest fire in the country.

In the case of the East Evans Creek Fire, the State reported that the fire had reached nearly 16,000 acres with over 230 homes at a Level 3 “Go Now” Evacuation and was denied by FEMA on July 22, 2026. The fire was also threatening county, state, and federal roads and bridges, radio and cell towers, gas and private electric utilities, campgrounds, trails, retail businesses, irrigation infrastructure, and agricultural operations.

The Rowe Creek Fire Complex was denied an FMAG under similarly severe circumstances with over 401 people at a Level 3 “Go Now” Evacuation on July 24, 2026. The fire was also threatening private electrical cooperatives, public safety radio, private commercial radio, and transmission lines. Since that denial, the fire has surpassed 200,000 acres and the State is preparing for the Complex to merge with the nearby Brewer Fire.

FEMA’s decision to deny these FMAGs is a significant departure from FEMA’s historical criteria and agency guidance. According to State officials, FEMA’s criteria for an FMAG has been, in part, that 150 primary residences must be in immediate threat of wildfire, gauged often as Level 3 “Go Now” Evacuation status. In recent years, State officials have seen an increase to over 200 primary residences as a threshold—which the East Evans Creek Fire and the Rowe Creek Fire Complex had still surpassed.

FEMA has also indicated that the East Evans Creek Fire and the Rowe Creek Fire Complex were denied an FMAG because they did not meet the criteria for a major disaster declaration. This is a major shift in administrative policy and contrary to Federal regulation and FEMA’s own policy manual, which states that an FMAG designation is warranted when a fire “threatens such destruction as would constitute a major disaster.” This program is meant to provide resources to fires that have the potential to become major disasters if left unchecked. Resources should not—and are not supposed to be—withheld until a fire becomes so destructive as to receive a major disaster declaration.

Inconsistent criteria for the approval of FMAGs is creating unnecessary confusion for emergency responders. For this reason, we request further information on FEMA’s decision-making and criteria for FMAG approvals and denials. Please provide a response to the following no later than August 10, 2026:

Pursuant to 44 CFR 204.21, what criteria is being used to determine a fire’s eligibility for an FMAG? Please include all quantitative metrics.a) Explain how the East Evans Creek Fire and Rowe Creek Complex Fire did not meet each of these criteria.

Who at the Department of Homeland Security and FEMA is involved in determining an FMAG designation, and what guidance has been issued to the officials involved in determining an FMAG designation? Please provide copies of all relevant guidance, including informal communications and official documents.

Which FMAG eligibility criteria changed from 2025 to 2026? How were these changes developed and who was consulted prior to implementing them?

What data, in addition to the state-provided data, is FEMA relying on to make their determination?

Broken down by state, how many FMAGs have been approved and denied per year in the past 10 years?

We want to stress that this is not the time for creating new or different criteria for accessing this critical funding to support initial attack. As you know, Oregon is strained for resources, and the State is still at the beginning of its wildfire season. We urge the agency to provide clarity and maintain consistency with prior years’ approval process.

title: Wyden, Merkley Announce $1.2 Million for Rural Health Clinic
text:
Funding to renovate health clinic to benefit the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde

Washington D.C.—U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley today announced $1,275,246 in federal funding from the Indian Health Service (IHS) to help support the renovation of the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde Health & Wellness Clinic in Grand Ronde, OR.

“Every community in Oregon deserves access to safe and reliable health care,” Wyden said. “And this federal award to the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde will support the renovation of their community’s essential health care facilities. I will continue to fight for more resources to expand health care opportunities for native tribes across Oregon.”

“Tribal communities too often face barriers to accessing the care they need and deserve,” said Merkley, who serves as ranking member of the Senate Interior-Environment Appropriations Subcommittee, which funds the IHS. “This federal investment in the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde Health & Wellness Clinic will strengthen the clinic’s infrastructure—creating a safer and more energy efficient space for patients and providers in the years to come. I’ll keep fighting to strengthen Tribal health care and secure the federal investments that help communities thrive.”

The $1,275,246 federal award from the Indian Health Service will support upgrades to the Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde Health & Wellness Clinic’s HVAC system.

“The award of these funds by the IHS fills an important need for the Grand Ronde Tribe and its Health and Wellness Center. For almost 30 years, our Health and Wellness Center has been taking care of our Tribal Members and its surrounding community. These resources will go a long way in replacing the outdated infrastructure at our facility, increasing our energy efficiency, and reducing our environmental impact. We’re grateful to Senator Wyden, Senator Merkley, and all of those who championed these funds for tribal communities like ours,” said Kelly Rowe, Executive Director of Health Services for Confederated Tribes of Grand Ronde.

title: Wyden, Merkley Join Colleagues in Effort to Guarantee Nationwide Access to IVF
text:
Oregon senators: Nearly two years after Trump’s broken promise of free IVF, the Right to IVF Act aims to protect access to fertility care and lower health care costs.

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley joined Senate colleagues today in reintroducing a landmark legislative package designed to establish a nationwide right to in-vitro fertilization (IVF) and hold insurance companies accountable to cover essential fertility treatments for families.

The Right to IVF Act, comes nearly two years after Donald Trump promised free IVF for all Americans, despite his continued attacks on reproductive freedom. IVF provides a critical path toward building a family for millions of Americans struggling with infertility, yet treatments frequently come with inflated prices, putting care out of reach for middle and lower-income households.

“Deciding when and how to start a family is deeply personal, and Americans deserve access to the full spectrum of quality health care to make those critical decisions,” Wyden said. “It is unacceptable for politicians or insurance companies to stand between families and the essential care they need to conceive.”

“IVF should be accessible and affordable to all – it’s critical care for folks wanting to start or expand their family,” said Merkley.

The Right to IVF Act guarantees a federal right for patients to access IVF, protects doctors providing treatment, and shields insurers from state-level interference. Beyond basic protections, the legislation mandates that private health policies include comprehensive fertility coverage that will protect families from predatory medical debt.

The legislation also expands health coverage for federal workers, active-duty servicemembers, and veterans to include a full range of fertility treatment options.

The bill was led by Senators Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), Cory Booker (D-NJ), Patty Murray (D-WA) and Leader Chuck Schumer (D-NY). In addition to Wyden and Merkley, the legislation is cosponsored by the entire U.S. Senate Democratic Caucus.

title: Wyden Urges Senators to Reject Jay Clayton's Nomination for Director of National Intelligence
text:
Watch a video of Senator Wyden's remarks here.

As Prepared for Delivery

M. President, I speak today in opposition to the nomination of Jay Clayton to be Director of National Intelligence (DNI). Mr. Clayton has repeated baseless conspiracy theories about American elections, refused to acknowledge who won the 2020 election, participated in an abusive investigation of American journalists, and provided false testimony to Congress about that investigation.

It has been clear for months that, under this administration, the main qualification to be DNI is the willingness to use the position to spread conspiracy theories about elections and to help Donald Trump make it harder for Americans to vote. Even before his nomination, Mr. Clayton decided he’d show how eager he is to serve as Trump’s election conspiracy wingman. Mr. Clayton is the U.S. Attorney in the Southern District of New York. Yet there he was on television, talking about elections in California and insisting, without any evidence, that America was doing a “terrible job” with election integrity.

I was particularly alarmed by his conspiracy mongering about vote-by-mail, which is how Oregon has been voting successfully for decades. On June 8th, just a few days before he was nominated, Mr. Clayton was on television talking about how “one group” was using vote-by-mail “dishonestly.” This is ridiculous. The first two Senators elected by mail were a Democrat and a Republican. Vote by mail benefits rural voters who live far from polling stations. Vote by mail benefits older voters who may not be able to drive. It has never been partisan – not until Donald Trump, aided by people like Jay Clayton, made it part of his attack on American democracy.

Mr. Clayton didn’t offer a shred of evidence to support his conspiracy theories, so I asked him – who were these mythical election bandits? In his responses to written questions, he said he was only asking the question. M. President, that is the stock in trade for conspiracy theorists. The moment they are asked to provide some evidence – any evidence – for their claims, they fall back on the “I was just asking a question” excuse. It’s fundamentally dishonest. It’s also behavior that should not be tolerated in someone responsible for providing Congress and the public assessments based on actual intelligence.

As we all saw during his disastrous nomination hearing, Mr. Clayton also refused to acknowledge the simple fact that Joe Biden won the 2020 election. Everyone knows the truth here. The only reason to avoid the question is to satisfy Donald Trump’s delicate ego. But that’s what Mr. Clayton did, signaling to Donald Trump, and to the whole country, that he will never, ever stand up to Trump.

I am also deeply concerned about Mr. Clayton’s role in the abusive subpoenas issued to New York Times journalists. Mr. Clayton is the U.S. Attorney in the Southern District. He signed the subpoenas. He is responsible for this effort to intimidate the press. He is also responsible for the numerous mistakes and errors committed by the attorneys under him, which even included issuing a subpoena to a journalist’s mother. This whole mess came out in a court hearing last week where, not only did the judge criticize the government’s attorneys, the government itself acknowledged its numerous errors and mistakes before eventually withdrawing the subpoenas.

All that’s bad enough. But it also raises serious questions about Mr. Clayton’s testimony to the Intelligence Committee. Eight days before that court hearing in which the government acknowledged its mistakes, Mr. Clayton testified – repeatedly – that the government had followed all the required procedures. That was obviously false. The only question is whether Mr. Clayton knew at the time that his testimony was false. If he didn’t know, then he had no idea what his own office was doing, despite having signed the subpoenas, which isn’t a great qualification for someone to lead our intelligence agencies. If he did know, then he may have willfully misled Congress. This is a vitally important question that the Senate should look into, rather than rushing to confirm Mr. Clayton.

There are other examples of how Mr. Clayton is willing to say anything in defense of Donald Trump’s corruption and abuses.

In May, Mr. Clayton went on television and defended the decision to immunize Donald Trump and his family from a tax audit. He said it was a “pretty good deal for the government.” Well, it was certainly a good deal for Trump and his family. But it wasn’t so great for everyday Americans who don’t control the IRS. And it wasn’t a good deal for the government either. In fact, a judge recently found that the so-called “settlement” was “improper,” had “no viable basis in law or fact,” and was an abdication of the government’s “responsibility to zealously defend the interests of the United States.” Yet, Mr. Clayton was happy to go on television and defend this blatant corruption.

Finally, as U.S. Attorney, Mr. Clayton has been the lead of the administration’s investigation into Jeffrey Epstein. He was responsible for the inexcusable release of information on Epstein’s victims. As for his other actions related to the investigation and the Epstein files, he has refused to say. But someday there will be transparency about how this administration handled the Epstein case and Mr. Clayton’s full role will come out.

Jay Clayton has no business being confirmed for this role. He has repeatedly demonstrated his eagerness to support Donald Trump’s conspiracy theories and corruption. He participated in the abuse of the justice system to try to intimidate the press. And he has provided false testimony to Congress during his own confirmation hearing. I urge Senators to oppose this nomination.

title: Young, Kim Introduce SAFE Act to Crack Down on “Chameleon Carriers”
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Todd Young (R-Ind.) and Andy Kim (D-N.J.) introduced the Safety and Accountability in Freight Enforcement (SAFE) Act, legislation to crack down on so-called “chameleon carriers” – unsafe trucking companies that evade federal oversight by shutting down and reopening under new identities to avoid penalties, enforcement actions, and poor safety records.

The legislation would require a comprehensive study to determine the scope and severity of the problem and direct the Federal Motor Carrier SafetyAdministration (FMCSA) to develop a mechanism to accurately detect chameleon carriers in the registration process, ensuring they are subject to enforcement for violations under the law.

An identical bill was introduced in the House by Representative Harriet Hageman (R-Wyo).

“In recent years, we’ve seen chameleon carriers become a major issue on Indiana’s roads, putting Hoosiers at risk and punishing law-abiding truckers,” said Senator Young. “When unsafe trucking companies evade enforcement by reopening under a new identity, everyone who shares the road with them is put at greater risk. Our bill will help federal regulators to identify these fraudulent operators before they hit the road, strengthening highway safety and potentially saving lives.”

“When anyone tries to skirt regulations on the road, it can cost people’s lives. The SAFE Act works with our truckers and the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration to take on unsafe operators so that our roads are safer for everyone and truckers can continue to keep our economy moving with greater peace of mind,” said Senator Kim.

“For too long, chameleon carriers have been able to shed their identities, reopen under new names, and escape accountability for serious safety violations. By exploiting weaknesses in the federal registration system, they have created an uneven playing field where responsible carriers invest in compliance, training, and safe operations while bad actors simply start over with a clean slate,” said Gary Langston, President and CEO, Indiana Motor Truck Association “The SAFE Act would give federal regulators stronger tools to identify suspicious registration applications and stop these rogue operators from operating on our highways. We applaud Senator Young for his longstanding leadership to improve highway safety and support the hardworking trucking companies that play by the rules every day.”

“Chameleon carriers are a plague on our nation’s highways, putting all motorists at risk while undercutting the vast majority of trucking companies that operate safely and play by the rules,” said Alex Rosen, SVP of Legislative Affairs,American Trucking Associations. “This legislation will give FMCSA a more powerful and proactive tool to identify and stop these bad actors before they can evade accountability by reappearing under new names, ownership, or USDOT numbers. By leveraging advanced automation to flag suspicious registration applications, the agency will be better equipped to detect fraud, close loopholes, and keep unsafe carriers off our roads. Safety is a priority for our members, which is why we are grateful for the leadership of Senator Young and Senator Kim to strengthen federal oversight and build on the progress we’ve made alongside USDOT to remove high-risk carriers from our nation’s highways.”

“America’s trucking industry relies on a regulatory system that rewards safe and responsible operators. When bad actors evade enforcement and reenter the market through affiliated entities, both safety and fair competition are compromised,” said Jim Mullen, President, Truckload Carriers Association. “The SAFE Act will strengthen industry trust by promoting accountability, protecting responsible carriers, and preventing those with serious violations from gaining an unfair advantage. This legislation fosters a healthier freight marketplace where safety and compliance are prioritized, and shippers can have greater confidence in their carriers. Ultimately, these measures will benefit motor carriers, drivers, customers, and the public by reinforcing a safe and competitive trucking industry. We applaud Senator Young and Senator Kim’s commitment to advancing transportation safety and urge Congress to enact the SAFE Act without delay.”

“Every motor carrier should be held to the same standards for safety accountability. Chameleon carriers undermine that principle by exploiting loopholes to evade enforcement, endangering the motoring public while creating an unfair disadvantage for responsible and compliant carriers,” said Ryan Streblow, President and CEO, National Tank Truck Carriers. “The SAFE Act will strengthen FMCSA’s ability to identify these bad actors before they can return to our roads under a new identity. NTTC strongly supports this commonsense legislation and commends Senator Young and Senator Kim for their leadership in protecting the integrity of the trucking industry and improving highway safety.”

“American Truckers United supports the introduction of Senators Young’s and Kim’s SAFE Act, which reinforces oversight within the USDOT registration process and enhances accountability measures for carriers seeking to obtain or retain a USDOT number,” said Shannon Everett, Founding Partner, American Truckers United Inc.

“Chameleon carriers have undermined America’s highway safety and damaged the professionalism of the trucking industry by evading enforcement, dodging penalties, and reopening under new identities,” said Todd Spencer, President, Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association (OOIDA). “Law-abiding small business truckers strongly support Senator Young and Senator Kim’s bipartisan SAFE Act. This legislation will help identify and weed out bad actors before they have the opportunity to ever become chameleon carriers, helping stop fraud before it occurs. OOIDA and our members applaud the introduction of this important bill in the Senate.”

“I lost three generations of family in a preventable truck crash caused by a chameleon carrier,” said Abby Godines, victim-volunteer, Truck Safety Coalition. “It’s not a question of if, but when, these bad faith carriers will kill more people on our roads. The SAFE Act will save lives, and I am grateful for Senator Young and Senator Kim’s commitment to truck safety.”

The Safety and Accountability in Freight Enforcement (SAFE) Act would:

Require the Government Accountability Office to study the prevalence of chameleon carriers, the crashes and fatalities associated with them, and provide recommendations for strengthening enforcement.

Direct FMCSA to develop, test, and implement an advanced automated tool that identifies applications exhibiting characteristics commonly associated with chameleon carriers, while ensuring final decisions remain with agency personnel.

Improve information sharing among federal and state agencies to better detect fraudulent registration applications.

Establish an appeals process for applicants incorrectly flagged by the system and require an audit of the tool’s effectiveness after implementation.

title: Alford Secures F-15E Strike Eagle Mission in Historic Victory for Whiteman Air Force Base and the 442d Fighter Wing
text:
Over the past several years, Congressman Alford worked alongside community leaders, Airmen, military advocates, and Department of the Air Force leadership to advocate for a follow-on mission for Whiteman Air Force Base. His efforts includedengagement with senior Air Force officials, advocacy through the House Armed Services Committee, and continued support for maintaining a combat-ready fighter presence in Missouri.

The Department of the Air Force’s decision supports its broader goal of increasing fighter capacity, modernizing the fighter force, and replacing aging aircraft with a capable and sustainable platform. The planned transition will bring 24 F-15E Strike Eagles to Whiteman Air Force Base, preserving a critical Air Force Reserve combat-coded fighter unit and the experience of the 442d Fighter Wing.

“This decision saves the 442d,” Alford said. “It saves countless jobs for our Airmen, our civilian workforce, and the surrounding communities. It keeps families here in Missouri. And, most importantly, it ensures the proud tradition of excellence at Whiteman Air Force Base continues.”

Congressman Alford also expressed hisgratitude to the leaders and Airmen across the Department of the Air Force who listened to the concerns of the community and worked toward a solution that preserves critical combat capability.

“I want to sincerely thank the leaders throughout the Department of the Air Force, Air Force Reserve Command, Governor Kehoe for bringing this matter to President Trump's attention, Missouri's State Senators for their efforts, and the many Whiteman Air Force Base Airmen who took the time to give their concerns and help make this mission possible,” Alford continued. “This outcome reflects what can happen when a community comes together, when our military leaders listen, and when we work toward a shared goal.”

“The men and women of the 442d Fighter Wing have proven for decades that they are among the finest Airmen in the world. Their professionalism, readiness, and dedication earned this opportunity. Missouri is proud of them, and we will continue standing behind them.”

The AFRC F-15E basing action represents the recommended course of action for an economical, timely, and effective fighter replacement. The current plan anticipates aircraft arrival in Fiscal Year 2031, followed by the establishment of initial and full operational capability as the mission transitions forward.

“This is a new chapter for Whiteman Air Force Base — but it is built on the same foundation of excellence that has defined the 442d for generations,” Alford said. “The mission continues.”

title: Ansari Calls for Closure of the Dilley ICE Detention Center & Release of Families in Detention
text:
DILLEY, TX — Yesterday, Representative Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03) conducted a congressional oversight visit to the Dilley Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) Detention Center alongside Representative Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and members of the Democratic Women’s Caucus, FWD.us and Families Belong Together calling for the immediate release of the women, children, and families detained at the facility and urging DHS to permanently close Dilley.

“What we saw today at Dilley was nothing short of horrific. No child, woman, or family should be locked up like this. We must close Dilley now and release these families,” said Rep. Ansari. “Children are being jailed and traumatized while private contractors profit from it, all at the expense of American taxpayers.”

“The inhumane conditions at Dilley are well-documented and we must end family detention. This includes shutting down Dilley and releasing these children and families immediately. Dilley lacks basic necessities for anyone, especially children: no access to clean water, medical care, or proper education. Dilley reflects a broader pattern that should not be expanded with additional, unprecedented taxpayer funding,” said Todd Schulte, President of FWD.us. “Yet, Congress has committed more than $260 billion to expand enforcement, on top of the regular appropriations to ICE and CBP of roughly $30 billion for FY25. This will only cause irreparable harm to children and communities. Thank you to the Members who continue to call for the release of families and we join them in their calls for Dilley’s closure.”

title: Barrett Meets with Health Care Professionals at UM Health-Sparrow, Visits Williamston Construction Site

title: Beyer, Garamendi, Sherman: Congress Must Reject Dangerous Trump-Saudi Nuclear Deal Without Safeguards
text:
The co-chairs of the Nuclear Weapons and Arms Control Working Group in the House of Representatives, Representative Don Beyer (VA-08) and Representative John Garamendi (CA-08), and Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa Brad Sherman (CA-32) issued the following statement in response to the recent announcement of a deal to provide Saudi Arabia with nuclear technologies without safeguards that prevent weaponization.

“As leaders who have long supported non-proliferation, we are deeply concerned about the failure of the proposed U.S. – Saudi civilian nuclear agreement to include key protections to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons. It is unacceptable that this Administration would push forward a deal without comprehensive safeguards to prevent Saudi Arabia from weaponizing the nuclear technology that President Trump has agreed to give them. Without these safeguards, we could give Saudi Arabia the tools it needs to become a nuclear-weapons state – something Crown Prince Mohammad Bin Salman has openly aspired to achieve.”

“If the Trump administration submits this so-called deal for the required Congressional review, we will take all available steps, including legislative action, to reject any deal that fails to include the safeguards necessary to prevent Saudi Arabia from developing nuclear weapons.

“Any nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia should include the strongest safeguards, including both a requirement that the nation signs the ‘Additional Protocol’ with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) guaranteeing robust inspection of nuclear facilities, and agrees to the ‘Gold Standard’ prohibiting uranium enrichment and the reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel—capabilities that are necessary to produce nuclear weapons. The Additional Protocol and Gold Standard are reasonable and are included in our nuclear cooperation agreement with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which allows them to generate electricity efficiently without posing a nuclear weapons threat.

“President Trump is currently waging a disastrous war against Iran ostensibly to prevent it from acquiring nuclear weapons. It was the United States that provided preliminary nuclear technology to Iran when it was ruled by a friendly, pro-Western monarch – and all of the technology in the hands of the Shah in 1978 fell into the hands of the Ayatollah in 1979. We cannot make the same mistake with Saudi Arabia.

“Preventing Saudi Arabia from developing nuclear weapons has long been an area of bipartisan consensus here in Congress – because America’s national security depends on it. We will fight to make sure Congress rejects any nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that fails to protect the American people from a nuclear-armed Saudi state.”

title: Scott Slams Trump Administration Failing to Hold Coal Operators Accountable
text:
As originally released by the Committee on Education and Workforce, Democrats

WASHINGTON – Ranking Member Robert C. “Bobby” Scott (VA-03), House Committee on Education and Workforce, released the following statement after the Department of Labor’s (DOL) Office of Workers’ Compensation Programs (OWCP)proposed an overhaul of the Black Lung Self-Insurance Rule.

“Congress established the Black Lung Benefits Act to provide compensation and medical coverage for coal miners who develop black lung disease. And while the law requires coal operators to purchase insurance that covers benefits for miners and their survivors, the federal government failed for years to conduct oversight and update regulations to guarantee that self-insured companies maintain adequate resources to cover their benefits liabilities. As a result, coal operators in recent years have shifted an estimated $1 billion of their black lung liabilities onto taxpayers and threatened to drive the Black Lung Disability Trust Fund (BLDTF) into insolvency.

“Today, President Trump is once again siding with the wealthy and well-connected and taking a sledgehammer to worker protections. Today’s proposed rule would undermine a Biden-era rule that held coal operators accountable for covering the benefits owed to miners and their families suffering from black lung disease and ensured the responsibility did not fall on taxpayers. Instead of the simple, straightforward Biden-era rule that was easy to implement and guaranteed full protection for taxpayers, the new Trump proposal reverts to a complicated formula that the Labor Department struggled to enforce in the past.

“Families are already stretched thin, and wages are not keeping up with inflation. Taxpayers should not be forced to foot the bill for the harms caused by corporate negligence. Americans deserve a government that will stand up for their safety and economic security, not one that lets negligent coal operators off the hook at their expense.”

Background:

In 2024, the Biden Administration issued a final rule, which improved oversight of the program to hold bad actors accountable and protect taxpayers from bearing the cost that should be borne by coal operators.

On December 1, 2025, Ranking Member Scott and Subcommittee on Workforce Protections Ranking Member Ilhan Omar (D-MN) urged DOL to enforce the Biden- era Black Lung Self-Insurance Rule.

title: Rep. Eric Burlison Releases Statement on President Trump's UAP NDA Directive
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congressman Eric Burlison (MO-07) today released the following statement regarding President Trump's directive waiving certain nondisclosure agreements for individuals with information related to unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP):

In light of President Trump directing the Department of War and the intelligence community to waive prior nondisclosure agreements (NDAs) signed by individuals who have relevant information regarding unidentified anomalous phenomena (UAP), if you are a current or former government employee or contractor interested in taking advantage of this directive, I am offering my office’s assistance in contacting and getting your information to any agency.

Principal Deputy Director of National Intelligence Aaron Lukas has stated that the Office of the Director of National Intelligence (ODNI) will soon issue guidance to ensure that the intelligence community implements the president’s directive. My office has requested to see the directive to understand how this process will work and to assist in facilitating whistleblowers’ participation in a manner and at a pace that is comfortable for them.

Independent congressional oversight is a critical part of UAP disclosure, and we are uncertain whether the abrogation of NDAs will apply to testimony received by Congress before referral to the executive branch. Therefore, at this time, if you are thinking of speaking to the executive branch pursuant to this directive, I strongly recommend that, in addition to an attorney, you request that either I or another member of Congress be present with you.

Waiving UAP-related NDAs is something I have been calling for the administration to do, and I hope to understand the procedures established by the president’s directive soon and am calling on ODNI to issue its guidance publicly. In the meantime, my office will serve as a resource to begin shepherding qualified individuals through the process.

title: Casten, 17 House Democrats Scrutinize New Trump Coal Plant
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Representative Sean Casten (IL-06) led 17 House Democrats in a letter to Department of Energy Secretary Chris Wright scrutinizing DOE’s decision to award $18.5 million for the construction of a new coal plant to a QAnon conspiracy theorist with no relevant experience.

“We are especially concerned about the apparent lack of due diligence conducted by your Department regarding this project. The purpose of the LPO is to provide funding to energy projects that will meaningfully lower costs for all Americans, but only after rigorously evaluating the economic and technical viability of the projects and regardless of any political agenda or intention to advance a favored technology,” the lawmakers wrote. “...The last coal plant in the U.S. was constructed in 2013. Older coal-fired power plants incur higher operating and maintenance costs, making it more expensive to operate existing plants than transition to cleaner, renewable sources.”

The lawmakers also noted the award applicant's lack of experience in the energy industry. Notably, the award applicant holds political ties to the president.

“We raise these concerns in light of the applicant Alex Phillips's lack of relevant experience, his political ties to the President, and the fundamental economic unsoundness of the proposal,” the lawmakers continued. “The decision to award funds to a political ally for a utility-scale generation project represents a major step backward for the stability and affordability of our electric grid and sets a dangerous precedent for more politically influenced deals that will jeopardize progress towards building an electric grid that supports a thriving U.S. economy.”

In addition to Rep. Casten, the letter was signed by Reps. Bonamici, Quigley, Khanna, Levin, Matsui, Mullin, Deluzio, McCollum, Ansari, Jonathan Jackson, Foushee, Pingree, Ross, DeGette, Trahan, Krishnamoorthi, and Beyer.

Text of the letter can be found below. A copy of the letter can be found here.

Dear Secretary Wright:

We write to express our concerns regarding the $18.5 million loan awarded by the Energy Department’s Loan Programs Office (LPO) to TerraSpark, an “eco-friendly” energy developer, for the construction of a new coal- burning plant. We are especially concerned about the apparent lack of due diligence conducted by your Department regarding this project. The purpose of the LPO is to provide funding to energy projects that will meaningfully lower costs for all Americans, but only after rigorously evaluating the economic and technical viability of the projects and regardless of any political agenda or intention to advance a favored technology.

We raise these concerns in light of the applicant Alex Phillips's lack of relevant experience, his political ties to the President, and the fundamental economic unsoundness of the proposal. The decision to award funds to a political ally for a utility-scale generation project represents a major step backward for the stability and affordability of our electric grid and sets a dangerous precedent for more politically influenced deals that will jeopardize progress towards building an electric grid that supports a thriving U.S. economy.

We write as well in the belief that the hard-working people of West Virginia do not need more false promises. The last coal plant in the U.S. was constructed in 2013. Older coal-fired power plants incur higher operating and maintenance costs, making it more expensive to operate existing plants than transition to cleaner, renewable sources. Since 2021, the cost to operate a coal plant has increased by 28%. Almost one quarter of active coal power plants are slated for retirement by 2029.

Residents of West Virginia in particular have seen a 34% increase in utility bills from 2019 to 2024. Three of the active coal plants under Appalachian Power, accounting for 87% of West Virginia’s electricity, lost a combined $81 million in 2025. Overreliance on expensive coal generation significantly contributes to rising utility costs and lack of economic growth in the region. Meanwhile, onshore wind and utility-scale solar costs have dropped 90%. The myth that coal power energy is better or cheaper helps no one – not the energy consumer, not the taxpayer, and certainly not hard-working people ready for a future in a modern energy economy.

Additional elements of the TerraSpark proposal raise further concerns. The inclusion of a 1 gigawatt artificial intelligence (AI) data center requires significant technical and managerial expertise to ensure electricity demand can be properly met. Also, TerraSpark claims to have an unconventional approach to carbon capture that differentiates it from other coal companies on the market, a chilling assertion given the rarity of a successful power plant/carbon capture combination. It will be essential to examine this technology with rigorous scrutiny to ensure emission reduction targets are met without any harmful impacts on the surrounding community and environment.

In order to confirm that your Department conducted appropriate due diligence, we respectfully request submission of the following information by September 1, 2026:

The biographies of the principals, key project leads, and partners of TerraSpark and any contractors or subcontractors on this project, including relevant experience in building similar projects.

Any application fee collected related to TerraSpark’s proposal.

Documentation that TerraSpark is in compliance with standard prohibitions against conflicts of interest, including with regard to Mr. Alex Phillips, the longtime Trump political ally running TerraSpark.

Letters of firm or contingent project financing, with the contingencies and evidence of financial resources given in detail.

Any executed term sheets or letters of intent with offtakers, financial partners, etc.

Pro forma projections and key assumptions regarding energy costs, operating efficiencies and off-take agreements.

The anticipated debt/equity structure of the deal and likely partners, including key interest rate assumptions, whether equity partners have step-in rights, and under what contingencies these rights may be exercised.

Documentation that TerraSpark has secured the $21.5 million in private capital necessary to receive the federal funds.

The details of the insurance coverage used for this project, including wrap-up insurance, if used, the entities providing the coverage, and evidence of their financial capacity.

The details of any commitment to meet job creation targets and labor standards.

Any milestones, contingent draws or recapture provisions in the event that TerraSpark fails to deliver on any of its commitments.

Thank you for your immediate attention to this critical matter.

Sincerely,

title: Rep. Ciscomani Honors the Final A-10 Flight at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base
text:
Tucson, AZ - U.S. Representative Juan Ciscomani is honoring today’s final A-10 flight at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base (AFB) in Tucson. Today’s flight was flown by the 357th Fighter Squadron Commander, Lieutenant Colonel Ryan "Clutch" Rutter, and the 355th Operations Group Commander, Lieutenant Colonel Rodney Dwyer, and marked the end of an incredible 50-year chapter of A-10 operations at Davis-Monthan AFB.

"Davis-Monthan Air Force Base and the Tucson community have a longstanding connection to the A-10," said Rep. Ciscomani. "Although A-10 operations at the base have now ended, the aircraft’s legacy will live on. For half a century, the A-10 aircraft played a pivotal role in our community. While it will no longer be used at Davis-Monthan AFB, the A-10 will forever remain and be remembered as a key component in our city’s history and military strength. Congratulations to Lieutenant Colonels Rutter and Dwyer, the 357th Fighter Squadron, and everyone at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base on today’s milestone and an impressive 50 years of A-10 operations!"

Among the hundreds attending today’s event was Sam Moreland, a retired Air Force lieutenant colonel who once served as the squadron commander for the 357th Fighter Squadron.

"It’s an emotional event, seeing this mission end," said Moreland, who flew A-10s for most of his military career. "It’s near and dear to our hearts. We did it for the troops on the ground and I hope we never forget what this plane did."

Along with those who have served or who currently serve at Davis-Monthan AFB, today’s flight is also recognized among other members of the local military community as a significant moment for Tucson.

"The final A-10 flight at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base signifies the close of a crucial chapter in Tucson’s military history," said TJ Hogan, 1989 Air Force Academy Graduate and career A-10 pilot. "The A-10 represents American strength and has been crucial tool of our nation’s military for decades. As a former A-10 pilot, I understand firsthand the significance of operating this unique aircraft and how much of an honor it is to do so. I want to congratulate everyone at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base for half a century of A-10 operations and look forward to the A-10 remaining a critical piece of history here in southern Arizona."

Ahead of today’s flight, Davis-Monthan AFB celebrated the final graduating class of A-10C Thunderbolt II student pilots from the 357th Training Squadron this spring, whose graduation marked the end of A-10 training at Davis-Monthan AFB.

The completion of A-10 operations at the base reflects both historical significance and a longstanding relationship between the A-10, Davis-Monthan AFB, and the Tucson community.

While the chapter of A-10 operations has closed at Davis-Monthan AFB, this aircraft will remain a crucial asset to the United States military. The A-10 Thunderbolt II nicknamed the “Warthog,” has been critical to maintaining the United States’ national defense for decades. Designed during the Cold War to combat Soviet tanks in Europe, the A-10 is the Air Force’s only aircraft built exclusively for close air support (CAS). Its unique strength and design will continue to be critical in defending and combating threats to the United States’ national security.

Ahead of today’s last official A-10 flight at Davis-Monthan AFB, Rep. Ciscomani had the honor of delivering a speech on the House floor to recognize this significant milestone.

title: Representative Ciscomani Joins Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins as USDA Announces $25 Million Sterile Fly Dispersal Facility in Arizona and Reopening of Douglas Port to Livestock Trade
text:
Tucson, AZ - Following months of advocacy to strengthen Arizona’s defenses against the New World screwworm, Representative Ciscomani today joined U.S. Secretary of Agriculture Brooke Rollins in Douglas as the U.S. Department of Agriculture announced a $25 million investment to reestablish a sterile fly dispersal facility and the reopening of the Douglas Port of Entry in Southern Arizona, safely resuming cattle imports from Sonora while strengthening the nation’s response to the New World screwworm threat through robust biosecurity measures.

The two announcements came during Secretary Rollins’ second visit to Arizona’s Sixth Congressional District this year, highlighting the Administration’s continued partnership with Southern Arizona’s agricultural community.

"I was proud to join Secretary Rollins for today’s announcement of the reopening of the Douglas Port of Entry alongside this critical investment in Arizona," said Rep. Ciscomani. "Local agriculture leaders and I have been fighting to deliver this sterile fly dispersal facility because Arizona’s livestock industry cannot afford to wait on the New World screwworm threat. This $25 million investment is the direct result of that work, and I’m grateful to Secretary Rollins for listening to Arizona’s producers and delivering on it. Her responsiveness and willingness to act swiftly on commonsense solutions has made a real difference. This is Secretary Rollins' second visit to Arizona in just a few months, reflecting her commitment to hearing directly from those on the ground and delivering real results for our farmers, ranchers, and rural communities."

Earlier this month, Ciscomani also championed the University of Arizona’s successful application for a $3.74 million USDA New World Screwworm Grand Challenge Grant, which will expand research, surveillance, education, outreach, and the development of innovative detection technologies to strengthen Arizona’s preparedness and rapid-response capabilities. Together, these investments reinforce Arizona’s leadership in preventing and combating the New World screwworm threat.

Representative Ciscomani has worked closely with Secretary Rollins, USDA officials, and Arizona producers to advance science-based solutions to combat New World screwworm, and consistently advocated for a domestic sterile fly dispersal facility as a key part of the nation’s long-term response.

Today’s announcements were applauded by John Ladd, President of Cochise-Graham Cattle Growers Association.

"And after today, let's go for it. This is what we need to do. And this has been a really good example of all of the representative, senators, and secretaries of how it works when you have quality people and I'm proud to be here. Thank you," said Ladd.

Today’s announcements by the USDA built on the representative's longstanding advocacy to strengthen Arizona’s agricultural economy through targeted investments in research and biosecurity while supporting the lawful trade between the United States and Mexico.

title: Rep. Cisneros Leads Letter to the Department of Defense Requesting Additional Information on Concerning Changes to the Military Promotion Process
text:

title: REP. CORREA PRESENTS $500,000 IN FEDERAL FUNDING TO REVITALIZE ORANGE COUNTY RIVERWALK
text:
Funding is part of nearly $3.4 million Rep. Correa has secured in total for the project

ORANGE, CA — Today, U.S. Representative Lou Correa (CA-46) presented a check for $500,000 in federal funding to the City of Orange to revitalize the natural landscape, improve biodiversity, and create shaded, green spaces in the Orange County Riverwalk area.

"For decades, I've fought to protect and expand green space along the Santa Ana River, going back to when I authored the legislation that created the Santa Ana River Conservancy as a state senator," said Rep. title: Courtney Statement on New $76.6 Billion Contract Awards to Electric Boat for Block VI Virginia-Class and Build II Columbia-Class Construction
text:
NORWICH, CT – Today, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee and a senior Member of the House Education and Workforce Committee, released the following statement after the Navy officially executed contract awards to Electric Boat for construction of nine Virginia-class Block VI fast-attack submarines and five Columbia-class Build II ballistic missile submarines. Electric Boat is awarded $42.1 billion for the Virginia-class program and $29.5 billion for the Columbia-class program. Combined with an additional $5 billion for shipyard enhancements, the contracts total $76.6 billion in value, representing the largest shipbuilding contracts in modern history. Congress authorized both the Virginia-class Block VI contract in 2023 in the FY24 NDAA and this Columbia-class Build II contract in 2025 in the FY26 NDAA. The legislative language in both bills originated in the Seapower subcommittee’s marks.

“These Block VI and Build II construction contracts, which Congress authorized in 2023 and 2025 respectively, provide a surging, unwavering demand signal to the entire submarine industrial base. Together, the Block VI and Build II contracts represent the biggest shipbuilding award in modern American history,” Courtney said. “These multiyear commitments by Congress and the Navy secure work at submarine shipyards and thousands of supply chain companies well into the late 2030s, further boosted by the AUKUS security agreement and the sale of three in-service Virginia-class submarines to Australia in the 2030s.”

“These contract awards will be the driving force to stimulate growth across the submarine industrial base. Crucially, the thousands of small business manufacturers who are essential to the industrial base now have the certainty they have been asking for to make needed investments in hiring, facilities, and equipment,” Courtney continued. “Congress and the Navy must now double-down on industrial base investments that are moving delivery schedules to the left. These are targeted investments, such as the record shipbuilder wage improvement funded by Congress and secured through collective bargaining in 2025 that is fueling record hiring and workforce retention at Electric Boat this year. We must continue expanding the successful workforce training programs that have rejuvenated southern New England’s manufacturing sector so they can skill-up more students and jobseekers for long-term submarine careers.”

Earlier this month, Courtney wrote the op-ed, “Building the 21st Century Arsenal of Democracy,” which highlighted the recent milestone of 10,000 graduates from the Southeastern New England’s Defense Industry Alliance’s network of submarine workforce training pipelines. In the piece, Courtney details the effort, dating back to the launch of the Manufacturing Pipeline Initiative in 2016, to rebuild the region’s manufacturing base.

In March, Courtney wrote a letter to the Department of Defense calling on the Navy to execute delivery of the Virginia-class Block VI construction contract.

In April, in a Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee hearing on shipbuilding, Ranking Member Courtney, referring to the Block VI contract, called multiyear procurement the “Da-Vinci Code” to stimulate growth in the shipbuilding industrial base. text:

title: Emmer, Minnesota Republican Delegation Applaud President Trump, Secretary Rubio, and Secretary Mullin for Deporting a Convicted Child Rapist Following Walz’s Pardon
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Congressman Tom Emmer (MN-06), Congresswoman Michelle Fischbach (MN-07), and Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) joined Congressman Pete Stauber (MN-08) in sending a letter to President Donald J. Trump, Secretary Rubio, and Secretary Mullin, thanking them for their decisive leadership and commitment to making America a safer place by deporting a convicted child rapist, previously pardoned by the Walz administration.

In June, Governor Tim Walz and Attorney General Keith Ellison pardoned Tou Lue Vang, an illegal alien who was convicted of repeatedly sexually abusing a 10-year-old girl in Minnesota in 2006. Thanks to the Trump administration, he has finally been deported, despite Governor Walz’s efforts to pardon him and avoid his deportation.

“Not only did Tim Walz pardon an illegal alien convicted of repeatedly raping a 10-year-old-girl, but he continues to defend the decision. This monster had no business being back on our streets,” said Congressman Tom Emmer. “Thank God for President Trump and his administration's swift and decisive action to deport this child rapist and correct Walz’s misguided and dangerous choice to free a child predator.”

Background

Tou Lue Vang, an illegal alien from Laos, was first convicted in 2006 of first-degree criminal sexual conduct for repeatedly sexually assaulting a girl between 2002 and 2004, starting when she was ten years old. Vang once offered $10 for the girl’s silence and, when interviewed by police, he attempted to explain his crimes as “a cultural thing” and stated that the victim was just as guilty as he was. In 2006, a Department of Justice Immigration Judge issued a final order of removal for Vang, yet he stayed in the United States.

In December 2025, Vang was arrested and detained by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), and in February 2026, a District Judge in Minnesota ordered his release by ICE. On June 10, 2026, in order to keep him in the country, the Minnesota Clemency Review Commission, composed of Governor Walz, Attorney General Ellison, and Chief Justice Natalie Hudson, voted to pardon Vang. Following the pardon, Secretary Rubio revoked Vang’s legal status, and he was deported by ICE on July 10, 2026.

After outraged reactions from Minnesotans about the pardon of a rapist, Governor Walz doubled down on his decision. When asked about the Trump administration’s deportation of Vang, he stated, “Does that make us any safer? Did that make the children that are left behind any more stable? Did it improve the idea that we cannot all be judged on our worst days?”

title: Rep. Figures warns Social Security in jeopardy for Alabama seniors.
text:
MONTGOMERY, Ala. (WSFA) - Congressman Shomari Figures (D-AL) delivered a warning at the Montgomery Area Chamber of Commerce briefing on Wednesday, highlighting how looming federal issues, specifically the solvency of Social Security, threaten to disproportionately impact Alabamians.

“We know that seniors here in the State of Alabama, for a lot of them, for many of them, they weren’t fortunate enough to have big 401(k)s, big IRAs,” Figures said. “Their retirement plan looks like this: own my own home, have children that can help take care of us, and Social Security.”

Figures pointed to updated projections showing the Social Security Trust Fund is on track to run out of money ahead of schedule, with the exhaustion date now expected in 2032.

“What that means in the State of Alabama is that the average Social Security benefit at that time that our seniors receive will be reduced by about 20% to 30%,” Figures warned. “That is real. That is a real problem.”

Figures said that more than 50% of seniors in Alabama rely on Social Security as their primary source of income.

In June 2026, approximately 75,000 Alabamians were receiving Social Security or Supplemental Security Income (SSI).

The financial strain is compounded by low average incomes across the state. While the individual median income in Alabama sits at approximately $34,000, Figures noted that “for seniors in the State of Alabama, that number is even lower.”

The threat to retirement benefits is not the only federal issue impacting Alabamians. Figures noted that legislation passed in Washington, D.C., including the Big Beautiful Bill Act, could signal significant financial shifts for the elderly.

Figures said that other sectors of Alabama’s economy and community are also feeling the squeeze of federal policy decisions, including agricultural tariffs and changes to food assistance programs that have caused some parents to lose SNAP benefits.

title: Garamendi, Sherman, Beyer: Congress Must Reject Dangerous Trump-Saudi Nuclear Deal Without Safeguards
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Ranking Member of the House Foreign Affairs Subcommittee on the Middle East and North Africa Brad Sherman (CA-32), and the co-chairs of the Nuclear Weapons and Arms Control Working Group in the House of Representatives, Representative John Garamendi (CA-08) and Representative Don Beyer (VA-08), issued the following statement in response to the recent announcement of a deal to provide Saudi Arabia with nuclear technologies without safeguards that prevent weaponization:

“As leaders who have long supported non-proliferation, we are deeply concerned about the failure of the proposed U.S. – Saudi civilian nuclear agreement to include key protections to prevent the spread of nuclear weapons. It is unacceptable that this Administration would push forward a deal without comprehensive safeguards to prevent Saudi Arabia from weaponizing the nuclear technology that President Trump has agreed to give them. Without these safeguards, we could give Saudi Arabia the tools it needs to become a nuclear-weapons state – something Crown Prince Mohammad Bin Salman has openly aspired to achieve.”

“If the Trump administration submits this so-called deal for the required Congressional review, we will take all available steps, including legislative action, to reject any deal that fails to include the safeguards necessary to prevent Saudi Arabia from developing nuclear weapons.

“Any nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia should include the strongest safeguards, including both a requirement that the nation signs the ‘Additional Protocol’ with the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) guaranteeing robust inspection of nuclear facilities, and agrees to the ‘Gold Standard’ prohibiting uranium enrichment and the reprocessing of spent nuclear fuel—capabilities that are necessary to produce nuclear weapons. The Additional Protocol and Gold Standard are reasonable and are included in our nuclear cooperation agreement with the United Arab Emirates (UAE), which allows them to generate electricity efficiently without posing a nuclear weapons threat.

“President Trump is currently waging a disastrous war against Iran ostensibly to prevent it from acquiring nuclear weapons. It was the United States that provided preliminary nuclear technology to Iran when it was ruled by a friendly, pro-Western monarch – and all of the technology in the hands of the Shah in 1978 fell into the hands of the Ayatollah in 1979. We cannot make the same mistake with Saudi Arabia.

“Preventing Saudi Arabia from developing nuclear weapons has long been an area of bipartisan consensus here in Congress – because America’s national security depends on it. We will fight to make sure Congress rejects any nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia that fails to protect the American people from a nuclear-armed Saudi state.”

title: Congressman Hamadeh Urges Secretary Doug Collins to Implement Veterans Community Care Program Audit Findings
text:
Congressman Abe Hamadeh (AZ-08) joined Congressman Paul Gosar (AZ-09) in urging Department of Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins to implement recommendations from a recent Office of Inspector General (OIG) audit identifying significant deficiencies in the Veterans Community Care Program (VCCP).

Congressman Gosar urged Secretary Collins and Acting Undersecretary Figueroa to take action in a letter following the OIG's Audit of Veterans' Community Care Eligibility Determinations, which found widespread failures in the Department of Veterans Affairs' administration of the program.

The audit revealed that nearly one in four veterans referred to community care did not meet eligibility requirements, while millions of veterans receiving care through the VA lacked proper documentation showing they had been evaluated for community care or had voluntarily declined that option.

The OIG estimated that more than $440 million in unnecessary spending occurred during the first quarter of Fiscal Year 2025 alone due to inaccurate eligibility determinations. An amount that could total $1.7 billion annually if left unaddressed.

“The findings of the audit show that not only are we wasting money, but we are depriving our veterans of the care they so rightfully deserve” stated Congressman Hamadeh. “I have faith that the administration will take the appropriate action to ensure that the recommendations are implemented and quality care is delivered when needed by our veterans.”

title: ICE: Harder Conducts Unannounced Oversight Inspection of Stockton ICE Facility
text:
Earlier this month, Harder demanded details on current operations, updates on legally-required identification, warrant orders

WATCH: Rep. Harder’s reaction leaving the Stockton ICE facility

STOCKTON – Today, following ICE’s failure to respond to his letter demanding details on current operations, Rep. Josh Harder (CA-09) conducted an unannounced oversight inspection of the Stockton ICE facility to get in-person answers. Harder first inspected the facility in January, but after a federal judge overturned mandatory scheduling rules, Harder led a surprise inspection of the field office and pressed ICE agents for updates.

“I just conducted a surprise inspection of the Stockton ICE facility to get face-to-face answers to the questions that this agency has been dodging for months, and I’m still outraged at the answers we’re not getting,” said Rep. Harder. “The chaos we’re seeing across the Valley proves that this agency is out of control. That’s why I’m opposing any new funding for ICE, and we’re going to keep up the pressure with more oversight until our families get the answers and the accountability that they deserve.”

Harder’s demands about ICE operations in the Valley:

Oversight Inspection – Complete written responses to questions provided in writing and in-person to personnel at the Stockton ICE facility.

Community Concerns – Past, current, and upcoming enforcement activities, as well as details on access to counsel, food, water, medical care, interpretation services, and accommodations for children during detainments at the local facility.

Policy Compliance – Current policies used by agents operating out of the Stockton ICE facility regarding unmarked vehicles, activities near schools and other locations used by children, and compliance with legally-required court orders and federally-mandated policies.

Read Harder’s full letter to Acting Director David Venturella here.

Harder has been pushing for reforms at ICE and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) for months, including leading successful calls for former Secretary Kristi Noem’s firing. Following her departure, Harder demanded the new Secretary Markwayne Mullin prioritize clear standards for enforcement, bans on face coverings, mandatory identification, new use-of-force policies, and bans on racial profiling. Harder has also continued to oppose any new federal funding for ICE until these reforms are enacted.

title: American Flood Coalition Recognizes Representative Erin Houchin as a Federal Champion
text:
July 29, 2026

WASHINGTON, DC — The American Flood Coalition (AFC) recognized Representative Erin Houchin (IN) as a Federal Champion for her leadership, public service, and commitment to finding solutions to challenges posed by flooding.

“Flooding is a serious challenge for many communities across Indiana's Ninth District, especially those along the Ohio River,” said Rep. Houchin. “I've worked closely with local leaders to improve infrastructure and flood mitigation efforts, and have secured federal funding for stormwater projects in communities like Madison, Austin, and Clarksville. I'm proud to partner with the American Flood Coalition to help protect lives and reduce the impact of future flooding.”
