title: Congressman Brian Jack Hosts Roundtable on Speaker Tom Murphy’s Legacy with Speaker of the Georgia House of Representatives Jon Burns
text:
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE

Contact: Regan Hinson

CARROLL COUNTY, GA – Today, Congressman Brian Jack hosted a roundtable discussion at the University of West Georgia’s Ingram Library on the legacy of the late Speaker Tom Murphy with the current Speaker of the Georgia House of Representatives, Jon Burns. Together, Congressman Jack and Speaker Burns toured a replica of Speaker Murphy's office exhibited in the Ingram Library, and hosted a wide-ranging discussion on lessons learned from the leadership of Speaker Murphy.

Congressman Brian Jack said, “I am honored to welcome Speaker of the Georgia House of Representatives Jon Burns to the University of West Georgia to discuss the legacy and leadership of the late Speaker Tom Murphy.

As we celebrate our country’s 250th anniversary, I am proud to honor the memory of one of the greatest Georgians to ever come from our district: the longest-serving Speaker of the Georgia House of Representatives in our state’s history, Tom Murphy.

“Speaker Burns and I toured Speaker Murphy’s replica office preserved in the Ingram Library, and we had an insightful discussion with Speaker Murphy’s children, former aides, and legislators who previously served in the General Assembly with him.

Thank you to Speaker Burns, the University of West Georgia, and the Murphy family for working with me to organize this historic event!”

Speaker Jon Burns said, “Few individuals have held such long and impactful careers in public service as the late Speaker Tom Murphy. Today’s event honoring his legacy alongside his family, colleagues, and friends was an incredible reminder of the profound mark he left on our state. Speaker Murphy dedicated his life to strengthening Georgia and expanding opportunities for future generations, and his unwavering commitment to moving our state forward continues to shape Georgia to this day.”

Joining Congressman Jack and Speaker Burns at the roundtable were: the son and daughter of Speaker Murphy, former Judge Michael Murphy and Martha Long, Public Service Commissioner Lauren “Bubba” McDonald, State Representatives Vance Smith and Don Parsons, former Congressman Lynn Westmoreland, former Dean of the Georgia House of Representatives Calvin Smyre, former president pro tempore of the Georgia Senate Wayne Garner, former aide Steve Anthony, and Mo Thrash – whose father was a former aide – and University of West Georgia leadership, including President Mike Johnson, Dean Blynne Olivieri Parker, and Dean Karen Owen.

Speaker Tom Murphy represented Haralson County in the Georgia House of Representatives for 42 years, and served as Speaker of the Georgia House of Representatives for 29 years – the longest tenure of any Speaker in Georgia history. His replica office is preserved at the University of West Georgia’s Ingram Library as part of the university's ongoing effort to document his legacy of public service and leadership in the state.

Congressman Jack represents Georgia's 3rd Congressional District, which includes all of Carroll and Haralson Counties. If Congressman Jack may be of service to you and your family, please visit jack.house.gov.

title: ICYMI: Rep. Ronny Jackson Highlights the Need to Protect America’s Troops on the Digital Battlefield in New Op-ed
text:
WASHINGTON — In an opinion editorial published by Breaking Defense, Representative Ronny Jackson (TX-13) highlighted the growing national security threat posed by ubiquitous technical surveillance (UTS) and the need to better protect America's servicemembers from digital vulnerabilities. He explains how commercially available data can expose military movements and operational patterns to America's adversaries.

In case you missed it…

Protecting America’s Troops on the Digital Battlefield

Breaking Defense

Rep. Ronny Jackson

July 29, 2026

Earlier this year, a naval officer’s routine use of the app Strava revealed the location of the French nuclear-powered aircraft carrier Charles de Gaulle while it was operating in the eastern Mediterranean, amid the US-Israeli conflict with Iran. No classified system was hacked. No network was deliberately penetrated. The information came from ordinary digital behavior that most people would never think twice about.

That is the danger of ubiquitous technical surveillance, or UTS.

UTS is the constant collection and monitoring of digital information through the combination of physical and environmental sensors, cameras, smartphones and mobile devices, fitness apps, financial transactions, connected devices, and the countless other technologies that quietly record where we go, who we meet, and what we do. One data point may seem harmless, but in the aggregate, these data points can quietly reveal actionable insights, such as military movements, operational patterns, and the identities of the people behind them.

If publicly available data can expose the location of an allied aircraft carrier, we should assume sophisticated, near-peer adversaries like China are already intentionally using the same methods to track and undermine the operations of US warfighters. And with the pace of technology, that threat is only growing.

We have already seen how digital carelessness becomes battlefield vulnerability. During the early stages of the war in Ukraine, the Russian military acknowledged that a Ukrainian strike killed scores of its soldiers and blamed the losses on cellphone use that exposed the soldiers’ position. The lesson is clear: digital discipline is now force protection.

During my 25 years of service in the United States Navy, including deployments to Iraq during the height of the insurgency, force protection meant physical barriers, guards, patrols, and hardened perimeters. Today, the threat is broader and more dangerous. Every smartphone, every app, every connected device, and every camera can become another sensor to be exploited by our adversaries.

As Chairman of the House Armed Services Committee’s Intelligence and Special Operations Subcommittee, I have the opportunity to focus Congressional oversight on the growing risks of the modern information environment. During a hearing in our subcommittee in March, Adm. Frank Bradley, head of US Special Operations Command, specifically called out the UTS threat, labeling the information we expose in the digital domain a “boon for our adversaries.” Just a few weeks later, Bradley Hansell, the Under Secretary of War for Intelligence and Security, testified that the Defense Intelligence Enterprise is actively investing to “transform the human enterprise to Watch experts discuss foreign influence risks, evolving DoD policy, and strategies for balancing security with scientific collaboration.

It’s encouraging to see Department of War leaders clear-eyed about this threat. However, responsibility for countering UTS remains fractured; today, no single office has been given clear ownership of the responsibility to confront it at a department-wide level.

That changes with Section 1098 in this year’s House National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). I was proud to lead this provision to help ensure the Department treats UTS as the persistent national security threat it is and institutionalize accountability across the entire enterprise.

For the first time, federal law would require the Department of War to designate a single head of an organization within the department as being responsible for identifying UTS vulnerabilities across the force. It would direct the department to develop a comprehensive strategy for the research, development, and procurement of secure communications and obfuscation technologies, develop UTS training and techniques to enhance force protection, and produce a plan for a long-term program of record to meet counter-UTS needs.

President Donald Trump has made rebuilding the world’s most lethal fighting force a top priority. But military strength is not just measured in platforms. It also depends on whether we can protect our servicemembers from the invisible threats that they are exposed to each and every day.

As Congress works to conference the House and Senate versions of this Fiscal Year 2027 NDAA, this critical provision should be preserved in any final package and signed into law. We would never send American troops into combat without body armor. We should not send them onto today’s digital battlefield without the appropriate protection either.

title: Smith Visits Current River Packing
text:
DONIPHAN, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) visited Current River Packing in Ripley County this week, where he toured the facility to discuss the company’s growth and the impact of the Working Families Tax Cuts on small businesses in rural Missouri.

Congressman Smith said, “Current River Packing is a major facility in Ripley County, and their eggs will end up on tables all across this country. These families are building something from the ground up, and they’re creating good-paying jobs and certainty for local families right here in Ripley County. That’s the kind of investment rural Missouri deserves, and I’ll keep fighting in Washington for the tax relief and regulatory reforms that let businesses like this one grow instead of just get by.”

Current River Packing is owned by the families of Ben Samons, Brock Ray, Sissy Gray, and Corey Kaczmarski. The facility will employee roughly 30 people, with plans to hire additional employees as they begin processing later this summer. Its grading machine can process 90,000 eggs per hour, and as the operation grows, Current River Packing is expected to strengthen competitive wages and stabilize jobs across the region.

As a growing small business, Current River Packing benefits directly from provisions in the Working Families Tax Cuts, which Congressman Smith authored. Permanent 100 percent bonus depreciation allows the company to immediately deduct the cost of new equipment as it expands operations, while the permanent small business deduction helps keep more money in the business to reinvest and create more jobs. Together, these provisions give small businesses like Current River Packing long-term certainty to invest and grow.

title: Kamlager-Dove Announces Bill to Ensure Medical Care for ICE Detainees
text:
LOS ANGELES, CA – Today, Rep. Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) held a press conference to announce the upcoming introduction of her Stop ICE’s Medical Neglect Act of 2026, legislation that creates a standardized system to report medical neglect in ICE detention facilities, requires each complaint to be investigated, and ensures adequate follow-up care. The congresswoman was joined by Reps. Judy Chu (CA-28), Lou Correa (CA-46), and Gil Cisneros (CA-31). A livestream is available here.

This legislation is in direct response to ICE repeatedly denying proper medical care to Carlitos Ricardo Parias, a constituent of Rep. Kamlager-Dove, following a gunshot wound he suffered during an immigration enforcement traffic stop in October. He has been detained at Adelanto since December.

“Our humanity does not end at the doors of an ICE detention center. No one should suffer in government custody because their medical needs were ignored,” said Rep. Kamlager-Dove. “Yet for nearly a year, my constituent Ricardo has repeatedly sought medical care at Adelanto, only to watch his pleas go unanswered and his condition worsen. Tragically, Ricardo’s story is not unique. That’s why I’m introducing the Stop ICE’s Medical Neglect Act to track these instances of abuse and ensure every detainee receives the timely and appropriate care they deserve.”

"We will not stand by while our immigrant neighbors are abused, denied basic human dignity, and treated as though their lives do not matter," said Rep. Judy Chu. "Rep. Kamlager-Dove’s legislation is so important because it will provide permanent protections for detainees by allowing them and their advocates to report medical neglect, and ensure those complaints are reviewed by board-certified medical professionals. Those responsible for the suffering and deaths in U.S. custody must be held accountable.”

"Nobody should be denied basic care because they're in federal custody,” said Rep. Correa. "There are too many stories of untreated injuries, ignored medical requests, and unsafe drinking water in these facilities. That's not right, and it's not who we are as a country. This bill gives people in detention a real way to speak up about abuse or neglect without fear of retaliation.”

"Adelanto is a private prison. Owned and operated by the GEO Group with one goal in mind, padding their balance sheet. They do this by cutting back on service like medical treatment. This is happening across the country, and our neighbors are suffering because of it. This rampant mistreatment at ICE detention centers must end now. The bill introduced today will implement measures to hold ICE accountable for their disturbing pattern of mistreatment at detention centers across the country, requires them to provide adequate care, and takes significant steps to protect detainees’ access to the constitutional rights they continue to be denied. It’s long past time for the lawless actions of ICE to be reined in," said Rep. Cisneros.

The Stop ICE’s Medical Neglect Act would:

Require the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to create an accessible database for detainees or legal counsel, advocates, and family members on their behalf, to file complaints of medical neglect or abuse while detained.

Assign contracted, board-certified medical practitioners to review each complaint and provide appropriate treatment or medication to detainees, either in-person or through telehealth video conference call, until appropriate relief is provided.

The medical practitioners will have substantial experience administering care in correctional or detention facilities.

Maintain a confidential filing process to protect detainees against retaliation or adverse treatment.

No information will be shared without the detainee’s expressed consent.

Inform detainees of language-appropriate interpretation services and provide translators during medical visits.

You can read the full bill text here.

Background:

Carlitos Ricardo Parias has been detained at the Adelanto ICE Processing Center since December and has received inadequate medical care for the gunshot wound he sustained during an immigration enforcement traffic stop in October.

In April, the Parias family reached out to the office of Rep. Kamlager-Dove seeking help securing access to medical care, and caseworkers began submitting inquiries to DHS regarding his treatment plan. In May, Rep. Kamlager-Dove conducted an oversight visit at Adelanto to check on Parias and press staff to provide appropriate care. Parias has described suffering from pain, limited mobility, swelling/discoloration, fevers, and persistent headaches. There are also concerns that he may have developed a bone infection.

Earlier this month, following advocacy from Rep. Kamlager-Dove and others, a federal judge ordered sweeping changes to improve conditions for detainees at Adelanto. Last week, Rep. Kamlager-Dove took to the House Floor to once again demand that ICE provide Mr. Parias the medical care he needs.

title: Kean Hosts Congressional Art Competition Winner Recognition Event
text:
(July 29, 2026) WARREN TOWNSHIP, NJ – Last night, Congressman Tom Kean, Jr. (NJ-07) hosted an event to recognize the winners of the 2026 Congressional Art Competition in New Jersey’s Seventh District.

“Each year, I am inspired by the extraordinary creativity and talent of the young artists in our community,” said Congressman Kean. “Through this year’s theme, ‘Celebrating America’s 250 Years,’ these students brought our nation’s history to life in thoughtful, original, and deeply personal ways. Their work reflects both the pride we share in America’s past and the promise of its future. Congratulations to Kaylie and all of this year’s outstanding winners!”

Kaylie Gao of Warren was this year’s winner with her piece Allegiance. Reflecting on what inspired her artwork, Kaylie said, “As a former swimmer of over a decade, I wanted to use my passion and experience in swimming to demonstrate the importance of unity, sportsmanship, and patriotism.”

Kaylie continued, “In my painting, I referenced the Women’s Team USA win at the 2016 Olympics in the 400 meter freestyle relay, where the athletes showed strong courage and care for their teammates that ultimately earned them a gold medal. The rippling American flag and mid-flight bald eagle symbolize allegiance, the title of the piece, and team spirit.” Her work is currently on display in the U.S. Capitol, where it will hang for one year alongside the other top winners throughout the country.

Two students were recognized as runners up, Mia Li of Warren for American Spirit and Vivien Xu of Westfield for Our Worker. Their artwork will be exhibited alternatively at the Congressman’s D.C. and District offices.

Five students received an honorable mention; Thanushri Krishnakumar of Bridgewater for United we soar – a 250-year journey, Sophia Liu of Branchburg for Fleeting Youth, Evelyn Ouyang of Warren for From Roots to Future, Julia Sun of Mendham for Columbia Meets Her Successor, and Nathan Veillard of Hackettstown for Stars, Stripes and Stories.

This year’s competition was judged by Catherine Benton and Colleen Furnari, both art educators in New Jersey’s Seventh District. Catherine Bethon is a high school art educator specializing in Art History and Mixed Media. She serves as the Warren County Chair for NJ Art Educators, is a practicing artist and served as a judge for this Competition last year. Colleen Furnari, who attended last night’s event, teaches art at the Midland School in Branchburg, New Jersey. She holds a Bachelor of Fine Arts from Mason Gross School of Arts at Rutgers University with a concentration in drawing and painting.

Ms. Furnari said, “It truly was an honor to judge the Congressional Art Contest. It was a challenging task narrowing down the many entries deserving of acknowledgment. The varied and thoughtful interpretations of the theme ‘Celebrating America’s 250 Years’ reveal that young people in our community have a broad awareness of history and good intentions for the future. Seeing their artistic talent celebrated by their families, nurtured by their teachers, and honored in this way was a feel-good overall.”

Learn more about the Congressional Art Competition and view the winning artwork HERE.

title: One Year Later: Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries Joins Congressman Tim Kennedy at Evergreen Health to Condemn the GOP's Healthcare Cuts
text:
Clinics Have Closed, Hospital Beds and Jobs Have Been Cut, and an Erie County Nursing Home Is Slated to Shut Down - With More Cuts Set to Hit Western New York in 2027

BUFFALO, N.Y. - House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (NY-08) joined Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) at Evergreen Health on Tuesday to mark one year since Republicans in Congress passed the Big, Ugly Bill, enacting the largest healthcare cuts in American history. Leader Jeffries and Congressman Kennedy detailed its mounting toll on Western New York, including coverage losses for 470,000 New Yorkers who relied on the Essential Plan as of July 1, 2026. On top of that, clinics have closed, hospital beds and jobs have been cut, and a local nursing home in southern Erie County is slated to shutter, with additional cuts to Medicaid scheduled to take effect in 2027.

“I stood shoulder-to-shoulder last year with doctors, nurses, union leaders, and healthcare leaders, and we warned what would happen when Republicans in Washington voted to enact the largest healthcare cut in American history in order to pay for permanent tax cuts for the wealthy and well-connected,” said Congressman Kennedy. “Clinics have closed, hundreds of thousands of New Yorkers have lost coverage, and premiums skyrocketed for those who were lucky enough to keep their insurance. A nursing home in our community is closing, with many more on the brink of financial collapse. As a direct result of these cuts, hospitals have been forced to cut hospital beds and jobs, weakening our healthcare safety net. Republicans own every single one of those losses. When Leader Jeffries is elected Speaker of the House in 2027, canceling the cuts and delivering for families struggling to make ends meet will be our top priority.”

“Extreme MAGA Republicans have imposed the largest assault on healthcare in modern American history. Their One Big Ugly Bill included a $1 trillion cut to Medicaid, putting hospitals, nursing homes and community health centers at great risk all across the country,” said House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries (NY-08). “Access to high-quality, affordable healthcare must be a right available to every single American. That's what House Democrats are going to work to bring to life here in Western New York and all across the country. Together, thanks to the work of fighters like Rep. Tim Kennedy, we will win back the House of Representatives and do all that is necessary to cancel the cuts, lower the cost and save healthcare.”

"The 'Big Ugly Bill' is exactly what its name suggests: a giveaway to the wealthy paid for on the backs of working families,” said Senator Jeremy Zellner. “One year later, Americans are already seeing the consequences through higher healthcare costs, reduced access to care, and growing uncertainty, with even deeper Medicaid cuts still on the horizon. Healthcare should never be treated as a bargaining chip. I stand with Congressman Kennedy and Leader Jeffries in demanding these harmful cuts be reversed before even more families lose the care they depend on."

Assemblymember Jon D. Rivera said, “A year after the passage of the so-called ‘One Big Beautiful Bill,’ Western New Yorkers are already feeling the consequences of Washington’s reckless healthcare cuts. These policies have put affordable healthcare further out of reach for working families, seniors, children, and individuals with disabilities who rely on Medicaid and other critical programs to access the care they need. At a time when families are already struggling with rising costs, these cuts have created even greater uncertainty and hardship for our communities. I am grateful to our Democratic leadership in Congress for continuing to shine a light on the real-world impact of these decisions and for their commitment to reversing these harmful cuts. I stand with them in the fight to protect access to care, strengthen our healthcare system, and ensure that every New Yorker can receive quality, affordable healthcare regardless of their income or ZIP code.”

“Federal cuts to healthcare funding are devastating our Western New York community, creating job losses, limiting the availability of nursing home beds, eliminating critical care services, and shutting down healthcare facilities. Cuts to healthcare impact every Western New Yorker – whether you need reproductive care, elective surgery, or a place for your elderly loved one. When nursing homes like Jennie B Richmond in Springville, Weinberg Campus in Amherst or Absolut Care of Westfield closed – hundreds of nursing home beds were no longer available in our community. Without these beds, hospital patients must wait longer to be discharged into our long-term care system, creating longer wait times for hospital patients and limiting the list of available facilities where loved ones can be placed within our community. We must work together to cancel federal healthcare cuts and fully fund healthcare because quality healthcare for everyone is at risk,” said Grace Bogdanove, 1199SEIU Vice President for WNY Nursing Homes.

“The United Steelworkers stand with Leader Jeffries and Congressman Kennedy as they fight for all working class women and men with their commitment to reversing the devastating effects of this disastrous bill,” said David Wasuria, United Steelworkers District 4 Director.

"When women lose access to healthcare, our entire economy feels the impact," said Sheri Scavone, CEO of the Western New York Women's Foundation. "The One Big Beautiful Bill's more than $1 trillion in Medicaid reductions threaten the health and financial stability of the women who make up the majority of our healthcare, retail, hospitality, and caregiving workforce. Medicaid covers more than 40% of births in the United States and nearly half of all children, while 93% of women enrolled in Medicaid are already working, attending school, caring for children or family members, or living with an illness or disability that limits their ability to work. Women also comprise 77% of healthcare workers with direct patient contact and 84% of the long-term care workforce, making these cuts especially damaging to both the people who provide care and those who depend on it.

"The healthcare cuts enacted last year have had real consequences for working families, seniors, and the most vulnerable members of our community," said Erie County Legislator Lawrence Dupre. "Access to quality, affordable healthcare should never be treated as a political bargaining chip, and I appreciate Congressman Kennedy and Leader Jeffries for continuing to fight against these harmful cuts and for standing up for the people who depend on these critical services."

Western New York is already living with the consequences of the Big, Ugly Bill. Buffalo Therapy Services clinics in Amherst and North Tonawanda have closed, along with an outpatient surgery center in Amherst and the Family Planning Clinic on Main Street in Buffalo. Meanwhile, beds have been cut for rehabilitation services, and approximately 150 jobs have been cut at Erie County Medical Center, the region’s only Level 1 Trauma Center. In nearby Springville, the Jennie B. Richmond Nursing Home has received state approval to close, putting dozens of caregiving jobs and residents' care at risk.

The damage extends statewide. The Big, Ugly Bill eliminated $7.5 billion in federal funding for New York’s Essential Plan, and as of July 1, an estimated 470,000 New Yorkers have lost coverage[1], faced with the choice of sharply higher premiums or no insurance at all. Beginning in 2027, new Medicaid work requirements will threaten coverage for hundreds of thousands more New Yorkers.

Leader Jeffries and Congressman Kennedy demanded House Republicans cancel these cuts before more clinics, nursing homes, and hospital units are lost, and vowed that a Democratic majority would restore the funding that Republicans transferred to billionaires through permanent tax cuts.

title: Statement from Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) on USPS Decision to Rescind Curbside Delivery to Whistling Straits Community in Wheatfield
text:
“USPS is failing and disrespecting the residents of Whistling Straits, and they have every right to be furious. Weeks ago, USPS told these families this matter was resolved after years of advocacy by the community. Now, USPS admits, in writing, that its own postmaster broke their own policy. Instead of owning that mistake, USPS is punishing residents for it.

“This is a bureaucracy protecting itself at the expense of the people it’s supposed to serve. USPS leadership would rather chase Donald Trump’s fantasy of gutting mail-in voting than do their fundamental job of guaranteeing families get their mail delivered to their homes.

“These residents never asked for special treatment, only equal treatment: the same practical, commonsense mail service that exists for the rest of their neighborhood. Instead, USPS strung them along, admitted its own failure, and is now forcing them to pay for a mistake it made. This entire situation is a prime example of why Americans have lost faith in the federal government.

“I will not allow USPS to ignore these residents. I’m demanding answers, I’m demanding accountability, and I am prepared to pursue every legislative option to force this agency to treat these families with the respect they are owed. Western New Yorkers deserve a Postal Service that is competent, accountable, and worthy of the public’s trust. They have run out of patience with USPS’s excuses. So have I.”

title: Congressman Langworthy Announces Nearly $1.4 Million for Schuyler Head Start to Expand Early Childhood Education
text:
Washington, D.C.—July 29, 2026… Congressman Nick Langworthy today announced that Schuyler Head Start, Inc. has been awarded a $1,373,892 federal grant from the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services to support Head Start services for children and families in Schuyler County.

The funding, awarded through the Head Start Projects program, will help provide high-quality early childhood education, health services, nutrition, and family support programs that prepare young children for success in school and beyond.

"Investing in our children is one of the best investments we can make in the future of our communities," said Congressman Langworthy. "Head Start has long played a vital role in our rural communities, helping children build the skills they need to succeed while giving families access to educational, health, and support services that set them up for long-term success. I'm proud to announce this nearly $1.4 million investment for Schuyler Head Start and will continue working to ensure that this program continues to receive the federal resources it needs to serve families across Western New York and the Southern Tier.”

The $1,373,892 award will support Schuyler Head Start's ongoing efforts to provide comprehensive early childhood education and family services, helping children develop the academic, social, and emotional foundations necessary to thrive in the classroom.

title: Congressman Mackenzie to Introduce New Congressional Stock Reform Legislation
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07), representing the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos, will introduce legislation this week aimed at cracking down further on congressional stock trading. The Candidate Investment Transparency and Ethics (CITE) Act of 2026 will require candidates for all federal elected offices — including the U.S. House, Senate, and Presidency — to divest from individual stocks and other securities or place them in a blind trust.

“The best way to stop members of Congress from trading stocks is to prevent them from ever starting,” said Congressman Mackenzie. “It’s not enough for candidates to make promises on this issue; they need to put their money where their mouth is. That’s why the CITE Act requires candidates for federal office to divest from individual stocks — or put them in a blind trust — before they even get to Election Day. Now more than ever, lawmakers need to earn the trust of the American people by rooting out profiteering and personal self-interest from the halls of Congress.”

Congressman Mackenzie has been a leader in the fight against congressional stock trading. Since taking office in January of 2025, the Congressman has co-sponsored three bipartisan bills aimed at cracking down on the practice of members abusing their access in order to profit off of securities. Last week, a bipartisan majority in the U.S. House passed the Stop Insider Trading Act, of which Congressman Mackenzie is an original co-sponsor. That legislation includes a range of measures, including a ban on stock purchases by members of Congress, strict reporting requirements for sales of stock, and tough new penalties for violations.

Stock trading by members of Congress has come under growing scrutiny in recent years. In 2025 alone, 14,451 trades were made by members totaling over $700 million in volume.

The Cite Act of 2026 requires divestment from individual stocks and calls for investments to be moved to other generally accepted investments or for assets to be moved to a blind trust managed by an independent trustee. Commonsense exceptions are permitted for “widely diversified mutual funds” and other funds that track a “broad market index,” like the Dow Jones or the S&P 500. Under the Cite Act, candidates for federal office would be required to take these actions within 90 days of filing for office. The prohibition on acquisition of covered securities extends until an individual is no longer a candidate or member.

title: Rep. Celeste Maloy Introduces the ATOMIC Act to Strengthen AI Nuclear Security
text:
This week, Rep. Celeste Maloy (UT-02) introduced the bi-partisan AI Threat Output and Monitoring Incident Containment Act (ATOMIC Act), legislation directing the Department of Energy to establish a national program to evaluate the most advanced artificial intelligence systems for nuclear-related risks before those risks become national security incidents. The bill is being co-led by Rep. Sara Jacobs (CA-51).

The ATOMIC Act creates the Advanced Artificial Intelligence Nuclear Evaluation Program, which would leverage the Department of Energy's National Laboratories to test advanced AI systems for vulnerabilities such as generating sensitive nuclear information, bypassing safety guardrails, exhibiting deceptive behavior, or acting unpredictably in high-stakes environments. The program would also help develop practical containment protocols, mitigation strategies, and technical standards to address emerging AI-related nuclear threats.

“As AI capabilities continue to advance, we have a responsibility to understand the risks before they become real-world crises," said Rep. Maloy. "The United States already has the world's leading nuclear security experts in our National Laboratories. This bill builds on that expertise to ensure we can identify emerging threats, strengthen safeguards, and have the information we need to make informed decisions about future AI policy.”

The legislation applies only to the largest developers of advanced AI systems, specifically those that have invested at least $2 billion in AI development over the previous five years. Covered developers would provide the secure access and technical information necessary for meaningful evaluations, while the bill includes strong protections to safeguard proprietary business information and trade secrets.

“No one wants another Three-Mile Island or any other major nuclear incident,” said Rep. Jacobs. “As AI becomes more powerful, we have a responsibility to identify and guard against new risks before they become real-world threats. That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan ATOMIC Act to identify AI-related nuclear risks, establish safeguards, and develop mitigation plans. These common-sense guardrails are an important first step to help us harness AI for good while protecting against worst-case scenarios.”

Under the bill, the Department of Energy would provide Congress with an initial report within one year identifying trends, capabilities, and risks observed through the evaluation program, along with recommendations on whether additional legislation is warranted. Annual updates would continue throughout the program's seven-year duration.

The ATOMIC Act has been endorsed by the AI Policy Network.

title: McClellan Announces Launch of the 2026 Congressional App Challenge for Virginia’s Fourth
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Congresswoman Jennifer McClellan (VA-04) announced the launch of the 2026 Congressional App Challenge for all middle and high school students in Virginia’s Fourth Congressional District. This annual competition challenges students to create an original software application written in any programming language and encourages exploration of STEM fields.

Last year, winner Akash Arun Kumar Soumya designed ElderLink AR, an application that utilizes AI to provide targeted physical and emotional wellness guidance for seniors.

“The 2026 Congressional App Challenge serves as an opportunity for all middle and high school students in the district to showcase their coding skills to solve real-world problems,” said Congresswoman McClellan. “I can’t wait to see the creative and innovative solutions that our students design. In an age of rapid technological innovation, the Congressional App Challenge will help prepare students in the Fourth District to become leaders in STEM fields.”

Students may compete as individuals or in teams of up to four. Submissions will be chosen by a panel of expert judges, and the winning app for Virginia’s Fourth District will be featured on the Congressional App Challenge’s website (2025 Nationwide Winners), Congresswoman McClellan’s website and social media platforms, and may be displayed in the U.S. Capitol building. The winning students will be invited to Washington, D.C. to meet Congresswoman McClellan and attend the annual #HouseOfCode science fair.

Submission deadline: October 26, 2026 at 12 PM ET. Registration link can be found here. Full rules, eligibility requirements, and submission guidelines are here.

title: Congressman Morgan McGarvey Demands Records from ICE on Constituent with Serious Medical Condition
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (July 29, 2026) – Today, Congressman Morgan McGarvey sent an urgent Congressional inquiry and records request to a senior U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) official demanding information related to the detention of Sarafinah Bukirwa, who was taken into custody by ICE at Muhammad Ali International Airport in Louisville.

Rep. McGarvey has been working with family and advocates of Bukirwa since she was detained on July 22 and has called for her immediate removal and prompt medical care.

Read the full letter to ICE below:

Dear Mr. Venturella,

On July 22nd at the Louisville Muhammad Ali Airport, Sarafinah Bukirwa (“Ms. Bukirwa”), a resident of Kentucky’s 3rd Congressional District, was taken into custody by Immigration and Customs Enforcement at Muhammad Ali International Airport in Louisville, Kentucky and transported to the Grayson County Jail.

This detention is particularly troubling because Ms. Bukirwa entered the United States legally, has a valid work authorization, and a pending asylum claim. Furthermore, based on the information reviewed by my team, as well as the information made available to Ms. Bukirwa’s attorney, there are no criminal charges pending or resolved against Ms. Bukirwa.

Ms. Bukirwa is the executive director of Sarafinah Sickle Cell Society (SASCELL), an organization that works to provide lifesaving medical care, awareness programs, and support services for those with sickle cell disease throughout the world. She was on her way to address a conference in California when ICE agents grabbed her and took her to Grayson County.

Of immediate concern, Ms. Bukirwa herself has sickle cell disease and had all her necessary medication and doctor’s instructions regarding her condition at the time of her arrest.

Our office has received reports that, upon arrival at the Grayson County Jail, Ms. Bukirwa was denied medication for her sickle cell disease. We have also been told Ms. Bukirwa was hit by officers, and was stripped of her hijab and all clothes in the presence of male officers.

As such, I am requesting the following information and materials no later than 5:00 PM on

August 5th, 2026:

All body-worn-camera footage recorded during Ms. Bukirwa’s arrival, removal from the transport vehicle, entry into the Grayson County Detention Center, and intake or booking process.

All fixed-camera, handheld-camera, surveillance, audio, or other recordings depicting Ms. Bukirwa’s arrival, intake, booking, searches, medical screening, housing assignment, movement through the facility, or first night in custody.

All video and audio recordings from the housing unit, cell, holding area, medical unit, intake area, booking area, hallway, sally port, or other location in which Ms. Bukirwa was held during her first 48 hours in custody.

The complete intake and booking file, including property inventories, search records, classification assessments, housing determinations, photographs, fingerprints, screening forms, acknowledgment forms, and orientation materials.

The names, titles, employers, and identification numbers of all ICE, DHS, Grayson County, contractor, correctional, and medical personnel who participated in or were present for Ms. Bukirwa’s intake.

Copies of all logs documenting welfare checks, cell checks, rounds, meals, medication distribution, medical encounters, requests for assistance, and movements involving Ms. Bukirwa.

All incident reports and grievances filed with DHS (including the Ombudsman and OIG and any other relevant subagencies who have jurisdiction over these issues) regarding any officers involved in Mrs. Bukirwa’s intake process.

Any and all incident reports that DHS (including any subagencies who have jurisdiction over these issues) has received regarding Grayson County staff and medical facilities since March 2025.

For any requested record that ICE contends is held by the Grayson County Detention Center, a contractor, another DHS component, or another governmental entity, please:

identify the custodian and location of the record;

state whether ICE has the contractual, legal, or practical ability to obtain it;

immediately direct the custodian to preserve it; and

provide my office with the name and contact information of the appropriate official from whom the record may be obtained.

This is an urgent congressional inquiry involving the liberty, health, and safety of a constituent with a serious medical condition.

Sincerely,

Morgan McGarvey

Member of Congress

###

Congressman Morgan McGarvey represents Kentucky’s Third Congressional District, including Louisville and Jefferson County. He serves on the House Veterans Affairs, Small Business, and Budget Committees.

title: Congresswoman Analilia Mejia Marks First 100 Days in Congress with Bold Action for NJ-11 Families
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Analilia Mejia (NJ-11) today marked her first 100 days in Congress, a period defined by robust legislative action, sustained oversight of the Trump administration, and direct engagement with constituents across New Jersey's 11th District.

In her first week in office, Representative Mejia introduced her first bill, the Living Wage for All Act. The legislation raises the federal minimum wage to $25 an hour and has since been introduced in the Senate. Since then, she has co-sponsored 85 pieces of legislation, including Medicare for All, the College for All Act, and the John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act, along with measures to reform the Supreme Court, guarantee universal child care and paid leave, overturn Citizens United, protect LGBTQ+ rights, enact tax fairness, lower housing and energy costs, and support parents and caregivers.

In the district, Rep. Mejia recently secured more than $5 million in federal grants from the Department of Health and Human Services for health care and child care programs. She has held two town halls to hear directly from constituents and, as a member of the House Small Business Committee, has visited local business owners across the district while voting to invest greater resources in Main Street.

"My first 100 days have been about carrying our district with me into every room I walk into down in Washington, D.C., from Randolph to Belleville and everywhere in between," said Congresswoman Analilia Mejia. "When I introduced a bill to raise the minimum wage to $25 an hour, I was thinking about families working multiple jobs just to keep up. When I launched the 14th Amendment Task Force, I was thinking about our neighbors whose rights and safety are under threat. Every hearing, every town hall, every visit to a small business on Main Street comes back to this community. I'm committed to showing up for New Jersey every single day, and for the next 100 days and far beyond, I'm fighting for an economy and a democracy that works for everyone."

As a member of the House Homeland Security Committee, Rep. Mejia regularly conducts oversight of the Delaney Hall and Elizabeth detention centers and tracks the conditions facing medically vulnerable people held inside them. In one of her first hearings, she sharply questioned Secretary Mullin, who was unable to answer basic questions about medical care for chronically ill detainees.

As the administration and the Supreme Court continue to threaten fundamental rights, Rep. Mejia formed the Defend the 14th Amendment Task Force with the support of House Democratic leadership to protect the constitutional guarantees of due process, equal protection under the law, and birthright citizenship through public education and coordinated congressional action.

title: Rep. Kennedy, and Rep. Hayes Introduce Bill to Improve College Graduation Rate Transparency
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Mike Kennedy (UT-03) and Congresswoman Jahana Hayes (CT-05) introduced the Time for Completion Act, legislation to ensure community colleges more accurately report graduation rates and provide increased transparency for students when selecting an academic institution. Under current law, community colleges and other higher education institutions are only required to report graduation rates for first-time, full-time students. Non-traditional students are often omitted in reporting, leading to critical data gaps.

According to theCommunity College Research Center, community colleges serve about 8.6 million students per year – or about 40% of all undergraduates. Current law excludes these students from reporting on graduation rates. The Time for Completion Act expands existing reporting requirements to ensure schools provide data on all student populations, including part-time and returning, students with disabilities, and others who are earning a full-time degree or certificate at community colleges. By including all students, community college reporting will more accurately reflect student success and allow students to better evaluate institutions of higher education.

“Students deserve the full picture when making a decision as important as choosing a college,” said Congressman Mike Kennedy. “Right now, official graduation rates leave out a large portion of community college students. The Time for Completion Act will ensure schools provide data on all student populations. Counting everyone’s success is a common-sense fix that helps students make more informed decisions, find their ideal institution, and have the best chance at success.”

“Selecting a college is one of the most consequential decisions a student can make. This decision should be guided by accurate and transparent information,” said Congresswoman Jahana Hayes. “Current data does not fully capture the range of student experiences and outcomes at community colleges, limiting the quality of information available to prospective students. The Time for Completion Act helps ensure students have a complete and more reliable picture of community college success so they can choose the institution that is right for them.”

“Now more than ever, students, parents, and policymakers need accurate, comprehensive data on college completion rates,” said Salt Lake Community College President President, Dr. Greg Peterson. “For too long, the success of community college students — in completing their studies and earning credentials, certificates, and degrees — has gone underreported. I commend Congressman Kennedy and Congresswoman Hayes for sponsoring the Time for Completion Act, which will bring greater transparency to graduation-rate reporting and ensure it truly reflects the achievements of community colleges and their students.”

“Utah’s community colleges play a crucial role in providing accessible, workforce-aligned education opportunities to all, especially for Utahns balancing college with work, parenting, and other responsibilities,” said Geoffrey Landward, Utah Commissioner of Higher Education. “Expanding the reporting timeline for completion data helps paint a clearer picture of the positive impact these institutions have on their communities and Utah’s broader economy and workforce.”

“The American Association of Community Colleges enthusiastically supports the Time for Completion Act,” said American Association of Community Colleges President and CEO, Dr. Derionne Pollard. “By providing a more accurate picture of community college student achievement, it allows metrics to better capture the progress that 10.5 million community college students in this country make every year. Not everyone follows the traditional four-year route to earning a college degree. Many do so while working, raising a family, or returning for a second career and their successes deserve to be recognized too.”

The Time for Completion Act has been endorsed by American Association of Community Colleges (AACC), Utah Systems of Higher Education (USHE), Salt Lake Community College (SLCC),.

title: Nadler, Schumer, Gillibrand Call on USPS to Immediately Cancel Planned Closure of the Bryant Park Post Office, One of Midtown Manhattan's Busiest Retail Postal Facilities
text:
New York, N.Y. – Congressman Jerrold Nadler (NY-12), Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer, and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand today sent a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner calling for the immediate cancellation of the planned closure of the Bryant Park Post Office, located at 23 West 43rd Street in Midtown Manhattan, and demanded a full accounting of how and when the U.S. Postal Service made that decision. The Postal Service is planning to close the facility on August 8th. Nadler, Schumer, and Gillibrand wrote that the Postal Service has not made a serious effort to properly inform and engage the public with full transparency or to adequately solicit public input.

“USPS’s unilateral decision to shutter the Bryant Park USPS Station will hurt thousands of New Yorkers, workers, visitors, and small businesses. Every day, the Bryant Park station provides necessary postal services in one of the most prominent economic, cultural, and financial hubs in America, and ripping these services away without any participation from the Bryant Park community is a clear violation of federal regulations,” said Congressman Nadler. “I am glad to be working with Leader Schumer and Senator Gillibrand to hold USPS accountable and protect NY-12’s access to public services.”

"The Bryant Park Post Office is staffed by dedicated postal workers and is a lifeline for Midtown businesses, non-profits and residents, and the Postal Service wants to slam the doors shut without regard for how the closure will impact New Yorkers and without having made a serious attempt to inform and engage the community," said Senator Schumer. "Federal rules require the Postal Service to fully satisfy a public review process, which I don’t feel they executed adequately. I am telling Postmaster General Steiner to cancel this closure now, come clean about how this decision was made, and let New Yorkers be heard."

“USPS must immediately reverse its decision to close the Bryant Park Post Office, which will harm the families, workers, and small businesses who rely on the branch’s critical services every day,” said Senator Gillibrand. “By failing to provide the Bryant Park community with public notice or adequate opportunity to give feedback on the closure, the Postal Service violated federal standards and stifled the voices of New Yorkers who deserve a say in their community. I will work with my colleagues to cancel this closure and restore New Yorkers’ access to the public services they need to thrive.”

The representatives said: “The Bryant Park Post Office is a pillar of USPS's postal services in Midtown Manhattan and beyond, and is one of Midtown Manhattan's busiest retail post offices, serving millions of New Yorkers, workers, visitors, and small businesses every day.”

Nadler, Schumer, and Gillibrand wrote that closing the facility would mean millions of New Yorkers and visitors see reduced access to retail postal services and increased wait times at nearby post offices, and that small businesses that rely on daily postal services will see services disrupted, leaving lasting harm to the community and the local economy.

Under federal regulations, the Postal Service is required to provide public notice, solicit community input, evaluate local impacts, and consider alternatives before permanently discontinuing a retail facility. Schumer, Gillibrand and Nadler raised concerns that their constituents were not properly informed by the Postal Service of the planned closure and the opportunity for public comment, and that the Postal Service cannot proceed until the mandatory public review process has been fully satisfied and has seriously engaged the community on its plans.

Nadler, Schumer, and Gillibrand demanded answers to a series of questions, including the Postal Service's full justification for the closure, for how long has USPS known about the potential expiration of the current lease, whether an extension or renewal of the current lease was pursued, what alternatives to closing the Bryant Park Post Office were considered, when the decision was made, when the public was notified and whether the opportunity for public comment was provided, what analysis USPS has conducted regarding impacts the closure may have on the community and employees at the facility, what plans are in place to ensure that the quality and availability of postal services will not be impacted should the closure proceed, and whether and when the Bryant Park Post Office will be relocated.

The letter to Postmaster General Steiner can be found below:

We write with serious concern regarding the planned closure of the Bryant Park Post Office, located at 23 West 43rd Street, New York, NY 10036. It has come to our attention that the Postal Service is planning to close the Bryant Park Post Office on August 8th and that in making this determination, the Postal Service has not made a serious effort to properly inform and engage the public with full transparency or to adequately solicit public input. Therefore, we urge you to immediately cancel the planned closure of the Bryant Park Post Office.

The Bryant Park Post Office is a pillar of USPS’s postal services in Midtown Manhattan and beyond. As one of Midtown Manhattan’s busiest retail post offices, the Bryant Park Post Office serves many thousands of New Yorkers, workers, visitors, and small businesses every day. Located in the center of the world’s greatest business, cultural, and financial hub, the Bryant Park Post Office serves to keep the essential public infrastructure of postal services running for Midtown Manhattan. Closing this postal facility would mean that the millions of New Yorkers and visitors will see reduced access to retail postal services and see increased wait times at nearby post offices. Small businesses which rely on daily postal services will see their services disrupted and without reliable postal access. The harm to the community and local economy is clear and negative.

Under federal regulations, the Postal Service is required to provide public notice, solicit community input, evaluate local impacts, and consider alternatives before permanently discontinuing a retail facility. Specifically, pursuant to 39 C.F.R. § 241.3, the public must be given a 60 days’ notice of a proposed closure of a postal facility and be provided an opportunity for public comments.[1] Regrettably, we are hearing from our constituents that the Postal Service did not properly inform the residents of its plans to close the Bryant Park Post Office and furthermore, failed to seriously engage the community regarding its decision to close this postal facility. This is unacceptable. The Postal Service cannot proceed with its plans to close the Bryant Park Post Office until the public review process under 39 C.F.R. § 241.3 has been fully satisfied.

We request that you provide written responses to the following questions no later than July 31, 2026:

Please provide, in detail, justification for the Postal Service’s decision to close the Bryant Park Post Office.

When does the current lease of the Bryant Park Post Office expire?

For how long (in months, years) has the Postal Service known about the expiration date of the current lease?

For what reason will the current lease of the Bryant Park Post Office expire?

i. Is it due to the landlord’s decision to not provide an option to the Postal Service with a lease renewal, or is the Postal Service choosing not to renew the existing lease?

ii. Was an extension of the current lease pursued by the Postal Service?

If the Postal Service is choosing not to renew the current lease despite the landlord providing an option for a lease renewal, what are the Postal Service’s justifications for doing so?

In deciding to close the Bryant Park Post Office, did the Postal Service consider any other alternatives? If so, please list each consideration in detail and the reasons for not pursuing such alternatives.

When did the Postal Service make the decision to close the Bryant Park Post Office? Please provide a specific date.

When was the public notified of the Postal Service’s decision to close the Bryant Park Post Office? Please provide a specific date.

Did the Postal Service provide an opportunity for public comment?

i. If yes, please provide a specific date of this notice to the public and include documentation of this invitation for public comment.

ii. If yes, did the Postal Service provide clear, transparent instructions to the public on how the public can submit input on the proposed closure?

iii. If yes, was this notice to the public list a clear deadline for the public to submit input?

Has the Postal Service made any other effort to engage the public and solicit public input?

Has the Postal Service conducted an analysis of the expected impacts on the community, employees, and quality of mail delivery services as a result of the proposed closure of the Bryant Park Post Office?

If yes, what will be the impact on the community served? Please provide a detailed description.

If yes, what will be the impact on the employees at the Bryant Park Post Office? Please provide a detailed description.

Should the Postal Service proceed with closing the Bryant Park Post Office on August 8, 2026, what are the plans in place to ensure that the postal services are not impacted by the closure of the Bryant Park Post Office? How will the Postal Service ensure that residents, workers, businesses, and visitors will continue to have the same quality and availability of postal services?

Should the Postal Service proceed with closing the Bryant Park Post Office, will the Bryant Park Post Office be relocated to another building? If so, what will be the exact timeline?

Thank you for your attention to this important matter. We look forward to hearing your response.

Sincerely,

title: Pallone Convenes Local Immigration Leaders as NJ Ranks Eighth in Nation for Arrests by Trump’s ICE
text:
RED BANK, N.J. — New Jersey now ranks eighth in the nation for immigration arrests, with arrests increasing 159 percent since President Donald Trump's return to office, according to the Deportation Data Project. Against that backdrop, Congressman Frank Pallone, Jr. (NJ-06) today convened the Deputy Mayor of Red Bank, Kate Triggiano, and immigrant rights organizations to discuss the impact of expanded ICE enforcement under the Trump administration, deplorable conditions inside Newark's Delaney Hall ICE detention facility, and the congressional oversight and legislative actions he is pursuing to rein in ICE.

The discussion focused on the recent increase in immigration enforcement across New Jersey, deplorable conditions inside Delaney Hall, the Know Your Rights resources available to immigrants and their families, and the billions of dollars Republicans in Congress recently approved to supercharge Trump’s ICE operations. Congressman Pallone also stressed the need to reform our immigration system that provides a pathway to citizenship.

"The dramatic increase in immigration arrests of hardworking people under President Trump is tearing apart families and communities across New Jersey. Every American deserves to know their rights, and Congress must hold this administration accountable," Pallone said. "My visits to Delaney Hall have uncovered serious concerns about how people are being treated and whether basic human standards are being met. Republicans should not be giving President Trump’s ICE your tax dollars. I will continue fighting for an immigration system that upholds due process, keeps families together and treats everyone with dignity while providing a pathway to citizenship.”

The roundtable included Deputy Mayor of Red Bank, Kate Triggiano, and representatives from the New Jersey Alliance for Immigrant Justice, Make the Road New Jersey, the ACLU of New Jersey, the National Day Laborer Organizing Network, CASA Freehold, Cosecha, American Friends Services Committee, Pax Christi, La Casa de Don Pedro, Ironbound Community Corporation, and New Labor.

PHOTOS OF THE ROUNDTABLE MAY BE DOWNLOADED HERE.

“As ICE continues to brutalize our communities, New Jersey must take every available action to hold the Trump administration accountable,” said Ami Kachalia, Senior Policy Strategist for the ACLU of New Jersey. “We’re grateful for Rep. Pallone’s leadership in ensuring our state does all it can to protect all people from the Trump administration’s abuses of power.”

"In the Ironbound, I watch children go to school each morning terrified they'll return to an empty house. Mothers memorize escape routes instead of helping with homework. This is what happens when we let fear replace humanity. We must create pathways to citizenship that honor the most basic truth: families belong together. When you rip a parent from their child, you don't just break one family you shatter an entire community's soul,” said Hazel Applewhite, Ironbound Community Corporation.

“New Labor recognizes the profound impact that ongoing immigration enforcement policies have on working-class families across the United States. ICE has made our communities and workplaces less safe, separating families, undermining workers' rights, and creating fear that prevents people from reporting abuse, wage theft, and unsafe working conditions. We recognize ICE as a threat to worker safety, dignity, and collective power. New Labor is committed to exploring and implementing strategies that empower immigrant workers, build resilient communities, and ensure every worker can exercise their rights without fear of detention or retaliation. We recognize that achieving these goals requires addressing the systems that perpetuate fear and exploitation. New Labor believes that abolishing ICE is an essential step toward creating communities where all workers can live, organize, and work with safety, dignity, and justice,” said Amanda M. Domínguez, Community Organizer & Language Program Coordinator, New Labor.

"Immigrant families across New Jersey are living under a level of fear this state has never seen, and that fear is eroding their trust in the schools, hospitals, and public safety they depend on. It is the product of a the detention and deportation regime that stress-tests every constitutional protection we have," said Dante Apaéstegui, Federal Policy and Advocacy Strategist with New Jersey Alliance for Immigrant Justice. "Warrantless raids, force against protesters and lawmakers, inhumane detention conditions, pressure to commandeer our state and local police—New Jersey has become the proving ground. We are grateful to Congressman Pallone for demanding solutions that protect our communities and hold this administration to account."

"We thank Congressman Pallone for convening this roundtable discussion on the state of immigration. One in four New Jerseyans is an immigrant. The Trump administration sees our diversity as an opportunity to surveil, detain and deport our communities to accomplish it's racist anti-immigrant agenda," said Viri Martinez, Legislative & Political Action Manager with Make the Road New Jersey. "That is why we will continue to fight for state and federal policies that protect us, not disappear us."

title: Pallone Demands Answers from SpaceXAI About Its Data Center Threats to Tennessee & Mississippi Communities
text:
Washington, D.C. – Top Energy and Commerce Committee Democrat Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ) sent a letter to SpaceXAI Founder and CEO Elon Musk demanding answers for the threats that the company’s Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 data centers are posing to Tennessee and Mississippi communities. The letter comes as Americans are increasingly concerned about the rapid pace of AI data center construction across the country.

“Communities across the nation are frustrated and angry about the pace of giant data centers being constructed in their back yards,” Ranking Member Pallone wrote in his letter to Musk. “Americans are concerned about what data centers and Big Tech’s push for more AI means for their communities, jobs, property values, and future. Electricity prices are skyrocketing, the electric grid is strained, our clean air and water are being polluted, and noise is wearing on communities’ health and patience.”

Today’s letter comes after Democratic Committee staff have met with companies over the last four months regarding their AI and data center strategies, energy consumption, environmental impacts, and commitments to local communities. Pallone said those conversations are ongoing to assess what federal guardrails need to be put into place to ensure data centers are not causing harm to communities.

“What has also become apparent from my examination of data centers is your company’s disregard for the health and well-being of local communities,” Pallone wrote to Musk. “Your rapid rollout of gas-powered turbines into vulnerable communities without adequate oversight or regulation creates a massive health risk to those communities. And any potential savings to the community’s electricity costs resulting from trucking in off-grid gas turbines comes at great cost to their health. This is an unacceptable trade-off.”

SpaceXAI’s Colossus 1 data center is powered by 35 gas-powered turbines, making the site the third-largest source of ozone-causing pollution in Shelby County, Tennessee – ahead of a nearby refinery and power plant – all without any air permits or protections, in violation of the Clean Air Act.

Just five miles away, on the other side of the border in Mississippi, SpaceXAI has trucked in at least 60 gas-powered turbines for its Colossus 2 data center – all of which are also operating without air permits or safeguards. According to one analysis, this makes the Colossus 2 turbines the largest source of pollution in the Memphis area – five times as polluting as the next largest source, the Memphis airport – and the largest emitter of nitrogen oxide in Mississippi, Tennessee, and Arkansas.

“The Trump Administration has essentially claimed that it alone decides whether SpaceXAI and other companies get a free pass to pollute unimpeded,” Pallone continued in his letter to Musk. “But just because the Trump Administration will bend over backward to give tech companies free rein over community air, water, and land does not make your actions legal.”

Of all the companies involved in the meetings with Committee staff, SpaceXAI has been the least willing to answer questions. At a meeting with Committee staff last month, SpaceXAI representatives were unwilling to engage in serious discussion and were the least knowledgeable about the company’s actions and plans.

Given SpaceXAI’s inability to provide time or information to the Committee during its scheduled meeting, Pallone is requesting detailed information from the company, including:

A list of all turbines in use at any point for the purposes of powering either the Colossus 1 or Colossus 2 sites, as well as their emissions and permitting application details;

All communications and records relating to Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 between employees or representatives of SpaceXAI and various state, local, and federal entities – including the White House; and

Analyses, reports, and documentation related to the emissions, power consumption, and water usage of both the Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 data center sites.

Pallone also wrote that his staff would reach out to SpaceXAI to discuss dates when he and Committee staff could visit the Colossus 1 and Colossus 2 sites, including their energy generation sites.

The full letter is available HERE.

title: CONGRESSMAN PAT RYAN AND DEMOCRATIC VETERANS DEMAND TRANSPARENCY ON IRAN WAR CASUALTIES
text:
When Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth testified before Congress earlier this year, Rep. Ryan slammed his handling of a deadly Iranian drone strike that killed six US troops in Kuwait

WASHINGTON, DC – Following disturbing reports that the Department of Defense removed the names of four American troops from the official Iran War death toll, Congressman Pat Ryan – a member of the House Armed Services Committee, Iraq war combat veteran, and the first West Point graduate to represent the Academy in Congress – and 14 of his fellow Democratic veterans are urging the Administration to accurately and transparently account for U.S. servicemembers killed and wounded in the Iran war.

“As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers,” wrote the lawmakers.

“The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports,” they continued. “We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.”

Following public outcry, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names of the four U.S. servicemembers removed from the Iran War death toll over the weekend. The Administration has not provided an adequate explanation as to why the servicemembers were removed in the first place.

In addition to Ryan, Representatives Mike Thompson (CA-04), Seth Moulton (MA-06), Chris Deluzio (PA-17), Derek Tran (CA-45), Jimmy Panetta (CA-19), Ted Lieu (CA-36), Maggie Goodlander (NH-02), Eugene Vindman (VA-07), Chrissy Houlahan (PA-06), Jason Crow (CO-06), Bobby Scott (VA-03), Salud Carbajal (CA-24), Gil Cisneros (CA-31), and Jared Golden (ME-02) signed the letter.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear President Trump,

As veterans of America’s wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers.

The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the War with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports. Inaccurate and delayed reports from the Department of War about U.S. casualties is bad for morale and undermines our U.S. servicemembers.

We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers.

Sincerely,

title: Pingree Backs Scarborough Town Council's Call for Federal Review of ICE Facility
text:
Ahead of the Scarborough Town Council's special meeting Wednesday evening, Congresswoman Chellie Pingree (D-Maine) sent the Council a letter supporting their proclamation calling for a federal review of the U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility at 40 Manson Libby Road. In the letter, Pingree urged the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) to seriously reconsider whether the facility should continue operating in Scarborough if its presence is undermining public trust and making residents feel less safe.

“The facility at 40 Manson Libby Road has become a symbol of fear, uncertainty, and intimidation for many immigrant families and their neighbors,” Pingree said. “That should concern every one of us.”

In her letter, Pingree emphasized that the Town of Scarborough has every right to question whether continuing to host the ICE facility serves the interests of the community. She called on DHS and ICE to conduct a serious review of the facility's continued operation and to give meaningful weight to the concerns raised by local residents and elected officials.

“When a federal facility reaches the point where its very presence undermines the public confidence and leaves residents feeling less safe, the federal government has a responsibility to reconsider if that facility belongs there at all,” she said.

Pingree also reiterated that her office has been conducting aggressive oversight of ICE's activities in Maine following the fatal shooting of her constituent, Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, in Biddeford. She has demanded answers from DHS, called for a transparent investigation, pursued legislative and appropriations oversight, and remains committed to holding the agency accountable to the communities it serves.

“Federal agencies must carry out their responsibilities in a manner that respects human dignity, civil rights, due process, and the communities in which they operate. When they fail to do so, local communities have not only the right but the responsibility to speak out,” Pingree said.

The full letter is available here and copied below.

Pingree has conducted official oversight visits of ICE facilities in Scarborough, Burlington, Mass., and Dilley, Texas.

Earlier this month, Pingree sent a letter to DHS Secretary Mullin demanding answers about the fatal shooting of her constituent, Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, by ICE officers in Biddeford, Maine, on July 13.

Pingree also joined the other members of Maine’s Congressional Delegation in sending a letter to Secretary Mullin calling for a comprehensive, transparent, and expedited investigation. In addition, Pingree and Reps. Jayapal (D-Wash.), Garcia (D-Texas), Raskin (D-Md.), and Thompson (D-Miss.) led nearly 200 Members in calling for independent investigations into Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and Johan Sebastian Guerrero’s deaths and demanded that ICE halt removal proceedings against the witnesses.

+++

Dear Council Members,

I write to express my support for your proclamation regarding the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facility at 40 Manson Libby Road. I commend the Town Council for giving voice to the significant and growing concerns in Scarborough and across Maine about ICE’s presence in our communities.

The tragic death of Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero has profoundly shaken our state. While investigations into the shooting continue, many Mainers are once again confronting a larger and deeply troubling reality: ICE is operating in our communities with no transparency, accountability, or regard for the people who live here. The facility at 40 Manson Libby Road has become a symbol of fear, uncertainty, and intimidation for many immigrant families and their neighbors. That should concern every one of us.

Residents should not have to wonder whether heavily armed enforcement actions will occur in their neighborhoods, whether federal officers are operating under appropriate oversight, or whether a facility in their town is contributing to tactics that erode trust between neighbors and government. This affects whether people feel safe attending school, seeking medical care, reporting crimes, practicing their faith, or simply going about their lives.

The Town of Scarborough has every right to ask whether continuing to host this facility serves the interests of the community. In my view, that question deserves serious consideration from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). When a federal facility reaches the point where its very presence undermines the public confidence and leaves residents feeling less safe, the federal government has a responsibility to reconsider if that facility belongs there at all. I believe ICE and DHS should undertake a serious review of the continued operation of this facility and proceed in accordance with the community’s wishes.

Please know that I am exploring every available avenue to address enforcement operations and the continued presence of ICE in Scarborough. My office has been conducting aggressive oversight of ICE’s activities in Maine and demanding answers from DHS regarding the preventable circumstances that led to Mr. Guerrero’s death. I have demanded a transparent and collaborative investigation, pressed the agency to justify its actions, sought greater accountability, and continue to pursue legislative, appropriations, and administration options to challenge policies that undermine public trust. I remain committed to using every tool available to me as a Member of Congress to ensure that federal agencies are accountable to the communities they serve.

Your proclamation appropriately recognizes that the immigration process and community trust are not mutually exclusive. Federal agencies must carry out their responsibilities in a manner that respects human dignity, civil rights, due process, and the communities in which they operate. When they fail to do so, local communities have not only the right but the responsibility to speak out.

Thank you for your leadership and your willingness to stand with the people of Scarborough during these difficult times. I am proud to stand with you, and I will continue working alongside you to pursue every available opportunity to reevaluate the federal government’s continued operation of this facility.

Sincerely,

###
