title: Reps. Sara Jacobs, Celeste Maloy Introduces the ATOMIC Act to Strengthen AI Nuclear Security
text:
Reps. Sara Jacobs (CA-51) and Celeste Maloy (UT-02) introduced the bi-partisan AI Threat Output and Monitoring Incident Containment Act (ATOMIC Act), legislation directing the Department of Energy to establish a national program to evaluate the most advanced artificial intelligence systems for nuclear-related risks before those risks become national security incidents.

The ATOMIC Act creates the Advanced Artificial Intelligence Nuclear Evaluation Program, which would leverage the Department of Energy's National Laboratories to test advanced AI systems for vulnerabilities such as generating sensitive nuclear information, bypassing safety guardrails, exhibiting deceptive behavior, or acting unpredictably in high-stakes environments. The program would also help develop practical containment protocols, mitigation strategies, and technical standards to address emerging AI-related nuclear threats.

“No one wants another Three-Mile Island or any other major nuclear incident,” said Rep. Jacobs. “As AI becomes more powerful, we have a responsibility to identify and guard against new risks before they become real-world threats. That’s why I’m proud to co-lead the bipartisan ATOMIC Act to identify AI-related nuclear risks, establish safeguards, and develop mitigation plans. These common-sense guardrails are an important first step to help us harness AI for good while protecting against worst-case scenarios.”

“As AI capabilities continue to advance, we have a responsibility to understand the risks before they become real-world crises," said Rep. Maloy. "The United States already has the world's leading nuclear security experts in our National Laboratories. This bill builds on that expertise to ensure we can identify emerging threats, strengthen safeguards, and have the information we need to make informed decisions about future AI policy.”

The legislation applies only to the largest developers of advanced AI systems, specifically those that have invested at least $2 billion in AI development over the previous five years. Covered developers would provide the secure access and technical information necessary for meaningful evaluations, while the bill includes strong protections to safeguard proprietary business information and trade secrets.

Under the bill, the Department of Energy would provide Congress with an initial report within one year identifying trends, capabilities, and risks observed through the evaluation program, along with recommendations on whether additional legislation is warranted. Annual updates would continue throughout the program's seven-year duration.

The ATOMIC Act has been endorsed by the AI Policy Network.

title: SCHNEIDER, PFLUGER INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN RESCUE ACT TO ENSURE FAIR AMBULANCE REIMBURSEMENT FOR FIRST RESPONDERS
text:
LINCOLNSHIRE, IL – Today, Congressman Brad Schneider (IL-10) joined Reps. August Pfluger (TX-11), Jill Tokuda (HI-02), Beth Van Duyne (TX-24), Kim Schrier (WA-08), John Joyce (PA-13), Claudia Tenney (NY-24), and Terri Sewell (AL-07) to announce the introduction of the Reimbursing Emergency Services for Critical Urgent Encounters (RESCUE) Actto amend the outdated Medicare payment structure that is straining ambulance services across Illinois and nationwide.

Medicare's ambulance fee schedule has not been updated since 2002, and current rates are still based on cost data collected from 1998. The RESCUE Act would require the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) to update the ambulance fee schedule every three years based on current, actual cost data, replacing a system still anchored to decades-old numbers. Meanwhile, the fuel, equipment, staffing, and vehicle costs required to keep an air or ground ambulance ready to respond have only continued to climb, widening the gap between what it costs to respond to a call and what Medicare pays.

"We all depend on our local EMS and firefighters’ dedication to the health and well-being of our communities, and they deserve our support in return,” said Schneider. "I am glad to join my colleagues to introduce the bipartisan RESCUE Act to ensure our first responders are reimbursed appropriately for ambulance services. Passing the cost along to our state and local agencies puts the readiness of our emergency services at risk. We will continue to work together to support community safety and the public servants who answer every call."

"EMS providers and first responders show up for our communities every single day, often in the most difficult moments imaginable, and they deserve a Medicare system that shows up for them in return. I'm proud to help lead the bipartisan RESCUE Act to ensure EMS is reimbursed based on the real cost of the care they provide, just like other healthcare providers already are. This is especially critical in rural Texas and rural communities across the country, where a funding shortfall can mean the difference between an EMS agency staying open or shutting its doors. We will keep working to close this gap and make sure rural America never loses access to the emergency care it depends on," said Pfluger.

"As Co-Chair of the Congressional Air Medical Caucus, I know that every second counts when it comes to getting patients to lifesaving care," said Tokuda. "For people living in rural America, medical care isn't always around the corner—it often requires long drives or emergency flights, especially to reach specialized treatment. We cannot allow outdated Medicare payment rates to jeopardize the air and ground ambulance services our rural and remote communities rely on. The RESCUE Act is essential to protecting access to emergency care when it matters most."

"Every second matters when an ambulance is racing to save a life — first responders are already stretched thin, and rates that haven't kept pace with real costs shouldn't be one more thing standing in their way," said Van Duyne. “I’m glad to help introduce the RESCUE Act to fix this deficiency and make sure the fee schedule keeps up with real costs."

"We all know the value our emergency responders provide," said Joyce. "Whether they're first on scene at a fire, a medical emergency, or an accident on the road, these men and women are integral servants in our community. Yet too often, ambulance services aren't reimbursed for the true cost of the lifesaving care they provide, especially in rural districts like mine, where providers travel long distances to reach patients. This bill fixes that imbalance and helps ensure no community loses access to emergency care."

View the full text here.

title: Rep. Peters Announces Bill to Name Post Office After Pacific Beach Icon
text:
San Diego, CA. — Today, Representative Scott Peters (CA-50) introduced a new bill to rename a Pacific Beach Post Office in his district in honor of Mary Wilding, a dedicated public servant and community leader.

Mary served the people of Pacific Beach for over 50 years. She sat on the Pacific Beach Town Council in a variety of capacities, from booster to board member to executive secretary. As a testament to her work, Mary was named honorary mayor of Pacific Beach in 1991 and was recognized as Woman of the Year by the California State Assembly

Image

“Mary was an iconic figure and fierce champion for the Pacific Beach community. She touched the lives of everyone who crossed her path, far beyond the Town Council” said Rep. Peters. “Naming this post office after Mary will ensure that her contributions to Pacific Beach are remembered and that her legacy of compassion and service lives on.”

“Few individuals have left as profound of a mark on Pacific Beach as Mary Wilding. Mary established traditions of civic service and appreciation that continue to this day,” said Pacific Beach Town Council President Charlie Nieto. “Her legacy lives on not only through the lasting improvements she made to Pacific Beach, but also through her family, who have continued her commitment to serving the community. Renaming this post office in Mary's honor is a fitting tribute to the decades of dedication, leadership, and advocacy she devoted to Pacific Beach.”

“Our mom, Mary Wilding, was an English Literature major and had a profound love for the written word. Multiple trips to this post office allowed her masterful letters and clever ideas to reach far and wide,” said Mary’s daughter, Katy. “Her many talents and hard work helped gain support for the PB Town Council. This contributed greatly to her legacy, as well as to the betterment of her beloved Pacific Beach.”

“Mary certainly had a special way with people. Her sincerity and witty sense of humor, allowed her to bring people together to work toward common goals,” said Mary’s family. “She had great initiative and a wonderful imagination. It was often said that she knew everyone in Pacific Beach! Mom’s pleasing personality was truly a gift.”

Mary dedicated herself to improving the Pacific Beach community through practical beautification projects, including the addition of a pedestrian walkway, seawall, and landscaping on Ocean Boulevard.

She was also a strong advocate for small businesses and local law enforcement. She founded the Police and Emergency Services Appreciation Night (PAESAN), an annual community block party and barbecue honoring local first responders. She also spent several years as a docent at the San Diego Museum of Art.

Mary passed away in 2016 and is survived by her eight children, all of whom have continued their mother's legacy of public service.

title: Congresswoman Simon Secures Federal Funding for the Lincoln Avenue / Marshall Way / Pacific Avenue Corridor Improvement Project, Improving Safety and Accessibility
text:

This federal funding will support the creation of bike lanes, a roundabout, modernized traffic and pedestrian and bicycle signals, lighting and signage improvements, and more. This Community Project Funding (CPF) is a part of the $11.2 million dollars that Congresswoman Simon secured for 15 projects across the East Bay in Fiscal Year 2026. Each fiscal year, members of Congress can submit Community Project Funding requests for consideration with the House Committee on Appropriations.You can read about the 15 projects that Congresswoman Simon secured funding for in her first year here.

“Our families and neighbors deserve to safely and reliably reach work, school, and childcare whether they are on foot, on bike, or public transportation, that’s why I am proud to announce $850,000 in federal funding for the City of Alameda to continue to upgrade and improve a major part of the city.” said Congresswoman Simon. “Modernizing our streets not only keeps people safe by reducing traffic incidents, it also supports small businesses by increasing customer access and improves usage for seniors and members of the disability community by increasing mobility. I look forward to seeing the impact of this federal funding in Alameda.”

“The Lincoln Avenue/Marshall Way/Pacific Avenue Corridor is one of Alameda’s most important thoroughfares — connecting the West and East Ends of Alameda, lined with schools, parks, neighborhoods, and businesses, and served by public transit — but also one of Alameda’s highest injury networks. We are thrilled that the $850,000 in Community Project Funding secured by Congresswoman Lateefah Simon will make this corridor safer, more accessible, and welcoming for all users,” said Mayor Ashcraft.

title: Stanton Statement on Passing of Congressman Harry Mitchell

title: Today, Rep. Van Epps Celebrates the Anniversary of NASA’s Founding
text:
Today, Rep. Van Epps released the following message in celebration of NASA’s founding. As a member of the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, Rep. Van Epps is focused on ensuring the United States remains at the forefront of innovation, particularly in space technology. With an abundance of commercial investments in NASA and the space industry, Tennessee is helping lead the space race. Currently, Tennessee has $224.2 million in economic output due to NASA contracts alone. There are 26 Tennessee suppliers that contribute to NASA’s Artemis program, and more Tennessee companies support the Kennedy Space Center.

Image

Watch Rep. Van Epps’ message by clicking above or here.

On July 29th, we celebrate the birthday of NASA, an agency that has embodied one of the most powerful qualities of the American spirit: the belief that there is always something greater ahead.

For generations, NASA has reminded us of what is possible when Americans come together with a common purpose. It represents the dreamers who looked up at the night sky and wondered what lay beyond, the engineers who turned impossible ideas into reality, and the astronauts who climbed into rockets knowing they were carrying the hopes and aspirations of an entire nation.

When Americans first reached the Moon, we did more than plant a flag. We showed what a free people can accomplish when we refuse to accept the impossible.

That moment reflected something deeply woven into the American character. We are a nation of explorers. A nation of builders. A nation that has always looked beyond the horizon and asked, “What’s next?”

The story of NASA is the story of American perseverance. It is found in every scientist working late to solve a problem, every student inspired to pursue a career in science and engineering, and every astronaut who looks back at our beautiful planet and sees the incredible nation we are blessed to call home.

From the Moon landings to the discoveries of the Hubble Space Telescope, and from exploring Mars to the Artemis program preparing for humanity’s return to the lunar surface, NASA has expanded our understanding of the universe and strengthened our belief in what America can achieve.

As we celebrate NASA’s birthday, we remember the generations of Americans who made these achievements possible. We honor their courage, their creativity, and their commitment to pushing the boundaries of human knowledge.

But we also look forward. The next great discoveries are waiting. The next generation of explorers is ready. And the next chapter of America’s story in space is still being written.

Because the spirit that carried us to the Moon is the same spirit that has carried our nation forward for nearly 250 years: a belief that tomorrow can be better than today, that challenges can be overcome, and that when Americans set our sights on a goal, there is no limit to what we can accomplish.

Happy birthday to NASA. May we continue reaching higher, dreaming bigger, and taking one small step for mankind.

title: Van Orden Secures CMS Approval Protecting Wisconsin Hospitals and Medicaid Funding
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS) announced the approval of Van Orden’s request to grandfather the state’s six percent hospital provider tax, preserving enhanced federal Medicaid funding for hospitals across Wisconsin.

Prior to the passage of the One Big Beautiful Bill, Congressman Van Orden urged Governor Tony Evers in a letter highlighting the critical need to promptly enact Wisconsin's FY 2025–2027 state budget so the state's hospital provider tax increase could take effect before the anticipated federal deadline. In a letter to the Governor, Van Orden urged Evers to "act swiftly to sign the budget and secure the provider tax increase in time to meet this critical federal deadline."

CMS’s announcement follows Congressman Derrick Van Orden’s continued advocacy with CMS and the Trump Administration to ensure Wisconsin qualified for the grandfathering protections included in the One Big Beautiful Bill (OBBB). The approval allows Wisconsin to continue drawing down enhanced federal Medicaid matching funds and protects critical health care resources across the state. Without this action, Wisconsin’s enhanced federal Medicaid payments would have expired on October 1, 2026.

In addition, CMS approved Wisconsin's Medicaid state plan preprint for all of calendar year 2026, ensuring the state will continue receiving the higher federal Medicaid reimbursement throughout the year.

"This is a major win for Wisconsin. When I learned Wisconsin hospitals were at risk of losing critical Medicaid funding, I immediately got to work with CMS and the Trump Administration to fix it. I fought to make sure Wisconsin's provider tax was grandfathered exactly as intended under the One Big Beautiful Bill Act, and today that work paid off. With this rule, Wisconsin's Medicaid reimbursement rate is jumping from 1.8% to 6%. This decision protects our hospitals and gives providers the certainty they need to continue caring for Wisconsin families." Van Orden said.

During CMS Administrator Dr. Oz’s visit to Eau Claire, he stated"We're going to make sure the Badger State is taken care of and that the funding that's required to improve rural healthcare is at the level that it should be at," and praised Van Orden for ensuring that Wisconsin’s provider tax rate was aligned with other states across the nation.

For Wisconsin’s rural hospitals and health care providers, this decision provides critical stability and ensures they can continue serving patients in communities across the state. This approval is the latest example of Van Orden fighting to deliver for Wisconsin families and ensuring federal policies work for the communities he represents.

The proposed rule can be found here: https://www.federalregister.gov/public-inspection/2026-14897/medicaid-program-indirect-hold-harmless-threshold-of-health-care-related-taxes

title: Walberg Sends Letter to Sec. Lutnick Regarding Risks of Foreign Humanoid Robot Technology
text:
Yesterday, Congressman Tim Walberg (MI-05) sent a letter to Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick urging the Department of Commerce to investigate the national security risks associated with Hypserscale Data in Dowagiac, Michigan, assembling humanoid robots made with components from AGIBOT, a Shanghai, China based manufacturer.

"Foreign adversaries, especially the People’s Republic of China, remain a threat to America," Rep. Walberg writes. "Their military-civil fusion strategy and national intelligence laws that require citizens and companies to assist the Chinese government intelligence efforts when requested create risks for American companies who may choose to partner with them in key fields such as humanoid robotics."

"Recently, a U.S. robotics company, Omnipresent Robotics, and its parent company

Hypserscale Data have partnered with AGIBOT a Shanghai, China, based humanoid robotics manufacturer to import humanoid robotics components and control software, assemble them, operate them, and eventually sell them to other U.S. companies under the Omnipresent Robotics logo," Rep. Walberg continues. "Currently, Hyperscale Data plans to import, assemble, and field a fleet of 143 robots and is producing the first batch which will be called OPR-R2. They will begin using them at their datacenter and robotics lab campus in Dowagiac, Michigan, to 'support the development of embodied artificial intelligence applications, autonomous workflows, and advanced robotics systems.'"

"These intelligent robots made with components from AGIBOT could pose an

unacceptable risk to U.S. companies, infrastructure, and national security," Rep. Walberg concludes. "AGIBOT was founded in 2023 and has previously received financial backing from BYD and the Shanghai Embodied Intelligence Fund. The Department of Commerce has the authority to investigate these products and if it deems it necessary take action to keep the U.S. safe."

You may view the full letter here.

Congressman Walberg is a cosponsor of H.R. 9129, the Guarding the U.S. Against Adversarial Robotics Dominance (GUARD Act), which would mandate that any components, communications equipment, or software used in humanoid or quadruped robotics originating from a foreign country of concern be added to the Department of Commerce or Federal Communications Commission's covered entity list.

title: Baldwin, Colleagues Introduce Bill to Counter Trump’s Attacks on American Elections
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – As President Donald Trump escalates his efforts to interfere in the administration of American elections ahead of the upcoming 2026 midterms, U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) and her colleagues introduced legislation to protect voters and combat unlawful election interference attempts. The Stop Harassment and Intimidations in Elections through Legal Defenses (SHIELD) Our Elections Act would give voters and state Attorneys General tools to stop interference in elections, strengthen accountability for people who illegally meddle in elections, and protect ballots from being improperly seized.

“Donald Trump has been actively laying the groundwork to undermine our 2026 elections to evade accountability for his cost-raising policies – and I refuse to stand idly by amidst his repeated efforts to stop Americans from having their voices heard,” said Senator Baldwin. “Our Democracy relies on people being able to show up to the ballot box and their vote to be secret and counted. And, if someone tries to interfere with that right, they need to be held accountable – no matter who they are.”

The SHIELD Our Elections Act creates a private right to action for State Attorneys General and voters to enforce federal anti-interference laws protecting polling locations and election sites, extends the statute of limitations for election related crimes so that future administrations can enforce them, restricts the seizure of ballots and election equipment from election officials until after an election outcome has been finalized, and authorizes a voluntary grant program to support states who have mail and absentee ballot tracking programs to provide confidence and security for voting by mail or drop box.

Specifically, the bill would secure federal elections by:

Allowing State Attorneys General and impacted voters to sue when federal officials unlawfully interfere with or intimidate them at polling places;

Strengthening accountability by extending the statute of limitations from five to nine years for key federal election crimes, including interference by armed forces and voter intimidation, to enable them to be brought by future administrations for past actions; and

Protecting ballots from improper seizure by limiting when state or federal law enforcement may seize ballots or election equipment and requiring court-authorized election officials to maintain joint custody whenever materials must be seized, especially prior to the resolution of an election.

The bill comes as President Trump has taken an all-of-the-above approach to try to interfere in the upcoming 2026 elections. In March, President Trump issued an executive order directing the Postal Service to create a federal mail-in voting list made up of states’ absentee voters’ information. Following this unconstitutional directive, USPS proposed a rule that would ultimately allow the Postal Service to determine whether millions of Americans can receive and cast ballots through the mail. Baldwin has spoken out in strong opposition and demanded that the USPS abandon this rule.

President Trump has openly floated sending Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and other federal agents to local polling locations and has said Republicans should nationalize voting in at least 15 states. Trump has also attempted to seize ballots in Georgia, Michigan, and Arizona, and sued 30 states for their voter rolls. Senator Baldwin and her colleagues introduced the Protect Our Polls Act to protect Americans’ constitutional right to vote and prevent federal interference by armed military or federal law enforcement.

The bill is led by Senator Alex Padilla (D-CA) and also co-sponsored by Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), John Hickenlooper (D-CO), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Angus King (I-ME), Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), and Elissa Slotkin (D-MI).

title: Banks Delivers Remarks on the Senate Floor Calling for Immediate Action to Protect American Elections
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Senator Banks (R-Ind.) delivered remarks on the Senate floor calling for immediate action to secure America’s elections. He warned that foreign adversaries, particularly Communist China, are actively working to interfere with America’s elections and urged Congress to pass the SAVE America Act to immediately protect American Democracy.

Click the image above or view the full speech here.

See remarks below:

“Mr. President, President Trump recently confirmed what many of us already knew: that foreign adversaries like China are working daily to interfere in our elections and our democratic society. China especially seeks America’s decline in hopes that they can establish a world order that runs through the Chinese Communist Party. We must do everything that we can to stop them.

“Historically, when countries have held that kind of ambition, they have started big, catastrophic wars. It should come as no surprise then that the People’s Liberation Army is undertaking the largest peacetime military buildup in human history.

“That’s why it is incumbent upon this body to fully fund our military, including President Trump’s $1.5 trillion defense budget request, so that we can deter exactly that kind of conflict. It is an abomination that the Democrats are holding up the bipartisan NDAA at a time when our military desperately needs our support.

“Yet even if we successfully deter a hot conflict, we could still lose in other ways. That’s because every day, the CCP is waging economic and political warfare against us. The CCP is trying to nurture dependency, exploit our divisions, cause us to question the justness of our cause, and erode our democracy.

“Mr. President, this political warfare campaign is not confined to the shadows. In many cases, it operates right out in the open.

“Take a look at Neville Roy Singham. Singham is a 72-year-old American tech mogul who sold his company and immediately moved to China. From his Shanghai office, which he shares with a CCP propaganda outlet whose avowed mission is to ‘tell China’s story well,’ Singham began funding a complex network of leftwing NGOs and nonprofits that advance the interests of the Chinese Communist Party.

“This is all a matter of public record. Even the New York Times has marveled at the hundreds of millions of dollars that Singham-linked groups have funneled to radical nonprofits that ‘mix progressive advocacy with Chinese government talking points.’

“Code Pink, that radical organization that chases me and other Senators throughout the halls of Congress, used to on occasion condemn CCP human rights abuses. After Singham started lavishly funding the group—and married its co-founder—Code Pink stopped criticizing the Chinese government and started defending it.

“In recent years, Code Pink has even provided cover for the CCP’s shocking genocide in Xinjiang. Meanwhile a newer Singham nonprofit, No Cold War, is entirely dedicated to advocacy designed to ensure America is defenseless against the CCP’s economic, military, and political warfare.

“But the Singham network is not limited to China-specific advocacy. Singham groups advance a wide variety of causes that are united only by their hatred of America, our allies, and the rule of law.

“From anti-ice boycotts, violence against law enforcement, rioting, obstruction, and support for Hamas’ attempted genocide of Jews in Israel, Singham groups and their members advance division, chaos, and hatred.

“All of this advances CCP interests and poisons our society. Thankfully, under President Trump’s leadership, the Department of Justice is now investigating whether Singham has been fueling this lawlessness in violation of US law. At the same time, the State Department under Secretary Rubio is leading from the front in identifying left-wing violence and building an international coalition to counter it.

“It should come as no surprise that as the CCP seeks to interfere in our society, it also seeks to interfere in our elections. As President Trump disclosed earlier this month, China perpetrated the largest known compromise of U.S. voter information in history, stealing the personal data of over 220 million Americans in 2020. The President also exposed ongoing vulnerabilities when it comes to American elections.

“As one newly declassified intelligence assessment found, ‘We judge that U.S. adversaries, including at a minimum Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea, as well as non-state groups, have the capability to compromise U.S. election infrastructure.’

“Mr. President, our adversaries are actively coming for our elections. If that is not enough to sound the alarm, I don’t know what is.

“All Americans, especially my colleagues in the Senate, should be outraged by this vulnerability. We know that our adversaries like the CCP seek to do us harm, and yet we standby and do nothing about it. Our inaction has no excuse.

“We need to safeguard our democracy and we need to do it right now.

“If this chamber does anything this year, it must ensure that American elections are for Americans only, now and always. And that’s precisely why we need to pass the SAVE America Act right now. In the face of the CCP’s coordinated campaign, we need more election integrity, not less. We need to ensure that all votes in American elections come from Americans, not illegal aliens or foreign manipulation.

“And by the way, it’s not only because of our international adversaries that we need to pass the SAVE America Act. Just last week, the Democrat governor of New Jersey announced that 6,600 non-citizens were ‘accidently’ added to the New Jersey voter rolls.

“That’s one hell of an ‘accident’. But not only that. Nearly 400 of those non-citizens cast illicit ballots in previous elections between 2023 and 2025.Democrats keep saying that stories like this are a figment of our imagination. They keep saying that these stories are just ‘accidents’ or ‘software glitches’. The fact of the matter is that these stories keep happening, and we need to do everything we can to put an end to them.

“And if we have to cancel the August recess to protect our elections and pass the SAVE America Act, then let’s do it. Protecting our elections from fraud and international interference is more important than vacation time.

“Mr. President, our adversaries like the Chinese Communist Party will stop at nothing to distract, divide, disrupt, and destroy America. Their campaign is not confined to Election Day, but Election Day is our last line of defense.

“Americans must always be free to reject the CCP and its values, while choosing a path that embraces the timeless truths that have always been at America’s core. The day that the CCP chooses the outcome of our elections will be the day it has won. And by then, it will be far too late to correct course.

“We cannot wait for that day. I urge my colleagues to act now, and pass the SAVE America Act. With that, I yield the floor.”

title: ICYMI: The Hill: “To Fix Birthright Citizenship, Declare a Foreign Invasion”
text:
Click here to read the full story from The Hill or read below.

OPINION: Just before the United States celebrated its 250th birthday, the Supreme Court of the United States issued what might become its most egregious ruling of my lifetime. In Trump v. Barbara, the court ruled that children born to parents who are in our country illegally, or even just visiting as tourists, are citizens of the United States because of birthright citizenship. I have absolutely no doubt that we will look back upon this ruling as being as wrong and legally perverse as Roe v. Wade.

The fate of our republic rests on being able to minimize the damage the court has inflicted upon the country. The court’s decision is simply incompatible with the Constitution and what it means to cohere as a nation. If the reward for illegal immigration is birthright citizenship, then why bother with borders and rules at all? What does it even mean to be a citizen if that coveted titled, “American Citizen,” can be achieved by illegal means?

Though the situation is bleak, the story is not yet over. President Trump called on Congress to act to fix the court’s mess. Congress has the power and duty to do so. My bill, the Citizenship Act of 2026, will curb birthright citizenship and help save our nation by declaring illegal immigration a foreign invasion into the United States.

Section 4, article IV of the Constitution of the United States imposes a constitutional duty on the United States to “protect each [state] against invasion.” And Section 8 of article I of the Constitution gives Congress the power to “establish a uniform Rule of Naturalization,” which, as James Madison noted in the Federalist Papers, is designed to protect states from being forced to accept liberal immigration policies. The Supreme Court’s decision on birthright citizenship amounts to the most liberal immigration policy I’ve ever heard of.

The court’s decision exacerbates what is already a national security crisis of the highest order. Under President Joe Biden, millions of migrants flooded our country’s borders or were otherwise permitted to enter into the country. President Biden let in known cartel members, violent criminals and terrorists. He also abused emergency temporary programs like parole and Temporary Protected Status to allow millions of illegal immigrants to remain in the United States and receive public benefits. Not only does Mexico know this is happening, the Mexican government encourages mass migration to the United States in order to retake the territory lost in the Mexican-American War.

But it’s not only at the southern border that this invasion took place. Birth tourism, too, has seriously affected our country. As many as 1.5 million Chinese nationals have United States citizenship after being born in the country by surrogates, a practice encouraged by the Chinese Community Party.

Illegal immigration into the United States amounts to nothing less than a foreign invasion, and it is our constitutional duty to stop it.

Children of foreign invaders born on U.S. soil are not entitled to birthright citizenship under the 14th Amendment. The Framers of the Citizenship Clause understood it to exclude children of invaders, and all nine currently serving Supreme Court justices agree. Trump v. Barbara allows us to withhold birthright citizenship from the children of invaders. Not only that, it’s the political branches, not the courts, that get to decide who is considered a foreign invader.

On his first day in office last year, President Trump issued a proclamation declaring that the mass migration of illegals into the United States constituted a foreign invasion. My bill codifies the president’s declaration of an invasion and amends federal law to deny birthright citizenship to the children of illegal immigrants and birth tourist invaders. This is the way forward, and it is the only way forward that’s consistent with the Supreme Court’s decision.

Benjamin Franklin once remarked that we will have a republic only if we can keep it. We will be able to keep our republic safe and secure if we can see the illegal immigration and birthright citizenship crisis for what it really is: a foreign invasion meant to destroy not only what it means to be an American, but America itself. The stakes could not be higher. If we fail to act, America as we know it might not get to see its 251st birthday.

title: Senator Banks Holds Hearing on The Impact of AI on the Workforce
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This afternoon, HELP Employment and Workplace Safety Subcommittee Chairman Jim Banks (R-Ind.) delivered the following opening statement at a hearing titled “The Impact of AI on the Workforce”:

Click here or the image above to view full opening statement.

“First, it is an honor and a pleasure to lead the subcommittee. I plan to examine the challenges that American workers face and explore policy solutions to increase opportunity, promote fairness, and support families.

“I appreciate being able to work with you, Ranking Member Hickenlooper, and I intend to be very active in the time we have left.

“Before I go any further, I ask unanimous consent for Senator Blunt Rochester to waive onto the Subcommittee for the purpose of today’s hearing. I want to welcome our witnesses this afternoon. We have a distinguished panel of artificial intelligence researchers and workforce development leaders to put the impact of AI on the workforce in perspective.

“According to Goldman Sachs, AI will drive 7 trillion dollars of worldwide investment and economic activity over the next decade.

“The 7 trillion-dollar question is, who benefits from that?

“But it’s not a question for the future. AI is all around us, and employers, workers, and governments are exploring the answer right now.

“AI promises to raise productivity and reshape work. It can also disrupt how the workplace is organized and create anxiety.

“There’s no shortage of doom-and-gloom predictions about mass displacement of workers, but we haven’t seen that begin to happen.

“Based on all the evidence, three things seem to be happening so far: (1) Hiring of entry-level workers is somewhat weaker; (2) AI is transforming tasks more than jobs; (3) And the skills that employers need and how workers learn those skills is changing.

“The downturn in entry-level hiring is due to several factors, and AI is just one. Some researchers believe the Federal Reserve is partly responsible. I look forward to delving into that today.

“Even in the most AI-exposed occupations, we haven’t seen any significant change in employment, but the way workers allocate their time is changing.

“In some occupations, things like data entry and simple coding are already mostly automated, but checking AI output is a whole new discipline.

“Finally, when we consider how workers acquire and use skills, we have to think about employment pipelines.

“A lot of workforce training happens on the job. Entry-level workers aren’t just hired to do their jobs, they’re hired to gain experience and grow into more advanced jobs.

“Every master craftsman was once an apprentice, every doctor started out as a resident, and most of our staffers started as interns.

“The real challenge is for graduates and young workers to acquire the AI-related skills they need to enter the workforce and get on the first rung of their career ladders.

“If those opportunities dry up or some young workers can’t access them, it will be a big problem in the labor market over the long term.

“Helping workers master the skills they need to succeed in the AI economy starts with getting better data.

“Existing labor statistics too often fail to tell us how occupations’ tasks are changing, what skills are needed, which occupations will grow and shrink, and how workers move through the labor force because of AI.

“That is why I introduced the AI Workforce Prepare Act with Sen. Hickenlooper, Sen. Husted, and Sen. Hassan.

“The Census and the Bureau of Labor Statistics need more expertise to analyze and forecast AI’s impacts. They need to share more data with state and local governments and collaborate with private researchers.

“Billions of dollars of spending on workforce development programs rely on good data. But better data is not a goal in itself. We need to make better decisions to beat China in the AI race.

“We need to train and equip American workers in nearly every industry to compete and win in the AI economy. We also need to make sure small and medium-sized businesses don’t get left behind while the biggest companies race ahead.

“America will win the AI race with China by maximizing the capabilities of all of our companies and all of our workers.

“I look forward to hearing our witnesses’ perspectives on exactly how we can accomplish that.”

title: Committee Passes Barrasso Bill to Unleash Wyoming Coal Production
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee passed U.S. Senator John Barrasso’s (R-Wyo.) bill to reduce barriers to coal leasing and unleash American coal production. The legislation extends the bonus payment period for coal mine leases from five to ten years, allowing coal companies to defer payment on a portion of their investment until after new mines become profitable.

“Nearly half of all coal produced in America comes from Wyoming. Wyoming coal provides our nation with safe, reliable, and affordable energy,” said Senator Barrasso. “My legislation would extend the bonus payment period for coal mine leases, which allows coal companies to spread out their financial risk when investing in new mines. This will give coal mines in Wyoming and across the country the certainty they need to power homes and businesses and lower energy prices for American families. Today’s committee vote is an important step to getting this energy security bill across the finish line.”

The bill is co-sponsored by Sens. Cynthia Lummis (R-Wyo.) and Mike Lee (R-Utah). In March 2026, Rep. Harriet Hageman (R-Wyo.) introduced companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives.

Background:

Currently, coal companies pay bonuses to the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) as part of the competitive bidding process for coal mine leases. These bonuses are required to be paid over a five-year period, which often concludes before new mines begin generating revenue. In line with President Trump’s executive order to revitalize the American coal industry, the legislation extends the bonus payment period to ten years, reducing the upfront risk for coal companies looking to build new mines.

The legislation is endorsed by the Wyoming Mining Association, the Wyoming Energy Authority, and the National Mining Association.

Full text of the legislation can be found here.

title: Passing the Lindsey Graham Sanctions Bill Will Cripple Russia’s War Machine
text:
“Energy is the cash cow of Putin’s war machine. It is also Russia’s Achilles’s Heel. Cut it off, and Russia cannot continue to fight. Russia’s biggest customer is Communist China. The next is India. They will be hit hard.”

WASHINGTON, D.C. – Senate Majority Whip John Barrasso (R-Wyo.) today spoke about the importance of passing the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026.

Last night, the Senate voted 86-12 to begin consideration of the bill. The bill is designed to strengthen national security and deter aggression from our adversaries.

Click HERE to watch Senator Barrasso’s remarks.

Sen. Barrasso’s remarks as prepared:

“Yesterday, the Senate honored the life of our friend, Senator Lindsey Graham. Today, it is time to honor his tremendous legacy. The way to do that is to pass the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act. It is a peace through strength bill. No tribute would be more fitting or more forceful.

“This bill strengthens America’s national security while pressuring our adversaries to pursue peace. The sanctions in this bill are historic. They target Russia’s largest oil exporters. They target Russian leadership. They target Russia’s so-called shadow fleet. Russia uses that shadow fleet to evade sanctions on its illegal oil.

“Most importantly, they target other nations that buy Russian oil, natural gas, and uranium. That is the way Russia is financing its brutal war in Ukraine. The penalties are swift and severe. Energy is the cash cow of Putin’s war machine. It is also Russia’s Achilles’s Heel. Cut it off, and Russia cannot continue to fight. Russia’s biggest customer is Communist China. The next is India. They will be hit hard. This is the way to cripple Russia’s war machine.

“Allies of Ukraine can qualify for exemptions. Those exemptions come from taking serious steps to end their dependency on Russian energy products. For years, Europe spent more money on Russian energy than it sent in aid to Ukraine. That must change.

“Of course, Russia is not fighting Ukraine alone. In Putin’s war of aggression, Iran is both Russia’s partner and its beneficiary. Iran has supplied Russia with drones, missiles, and munitions. Russia has used these weapons to kill Ukrainian civilians and destroy Ukrainian infrastructure. In return, Russia has shared with the Iranian regime: technology, intelligence, and military support. Iran has used this support to attack American troops and hold the Strait of Hormuz hostage.

“Russia and Iran both employ a shadow fleet of illegal oil tankers. They share sanctions-evading networks. They sell oil to many of the same buyers. They both fund murder and terrorism. They do it with revenue from their energy products. That is why Iran has rightfully been added to this sanctions bill. Together, Russia and Iran have built an Axis of Aggression. Sanctioning those who buy oil from Russia and Iran disrupts that entire Axis at once.

“Passing this bill will make our country safer. It makes our adversaries weaker.

“Senator Graham visited Ukraine shortly before he died. Lindsey was a friend of freedom in Ukraine. He never stopped working to build support for their cause. Lindsey succeeded. This is a bill that has united a broad coalition of United States Senators. I am one of the many cosponsors. Now is the time to pass this bill. Now is the time to push for peace.

“Today, Russia is at a point of maximum weakness. So is Iran. Critical pieces of Russia’s energy infrastructure are in shambles. A significant portion of its oil refinery capacity is no longer operable. Energy shortages are being felt all across Russia. At the same time, Iran’s military has been severely degraded. Both Russia and Iran still refuse to accept plans for lasting peace. Russia and Iran respond only to strength, not statements.

“It is time for the Senate to act decisively to bring lasting peace. It is time to pass the Lindsey Graham Sanction bill.”

title: Bennet, Hickenlooper, Colleagues Reintroduce Bill to Deschedule Marijuana, End Federal Prohibition of Cannabis
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senators Michael Bennet and John Hickenlooper joined 15 of their Senate colleagues to reintroduce their Cannabis Administration and Opportunity Act (CAOA), which would end the harmful federal ban of marijuana by removing cannabis from the list of federally controlled substances (descheduling) and empowering states to create their own laws.

“Congress should follow Colorado’s lead and bring our nation’s marijuana laws into the 21st century,” said Bennet. “The Cannabis Administration and Opportunity Act is long overdue and will help protect the legal cannabis economy as well as address historic inequities in our justice system.”

“Colorado legalized marijuana fourteen years ago and now nearly half of the states have followed our lead,” said Hickenlooper. “Yet, the federal government continues to drag its feet. We need to deschedule and decriminalize marijuana, then finish the job and expunge the records of everyone who was charged with federal marijuana crimes.”

Specifically, CAOA establishes a federal regulatory framework to protect public health and safety, prioritizes restorative and economic justice to help undo the decades of harm caused by the failed war on drugs, ends discrimination in the provision of federal benefits on the basis of cannabis use, provides major investments for cannabis research, and strengthens worker protections. By decriminalizing cannabis at the federal level, CAOA also ensures that state-legal cannabis businesses or those in adjacent industries will no longer be denied access to bank accounts or financial services simply because of their ties to cannabis.

Bennet has repeatedly advocated for the support of the legal cannabis economy. In June 2024, he urged U.S. Senate Committee on Appropriations leaders to allow legal cannabis small businesses to access programs and resources from the Small Business Administration. He also introduced the Secure and Fair Enforcement (SAFE) Banking Act and the Secure and Fair Enforcement Regulation (SAFER) Banking Act to provide legally operating cannabis businesses access to critical banking services.

In addition to Bennet and Hickenlooper, U.S. Senators Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), John Fetterman (D-Pa.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Gary Peters (D-Mich.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and Peter Welch (D-Vt.) cosponsored this bill.

The text of the bill HERE.

title: Bennet Joins Bipartisan Legislation to Repeal Outdated Jackson-Vanik Trade Restrictions on Central Asia
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a senior member of the Senate Finance Committee, joined legislation to repeal outdated Jackson-Vanik trade restrictions on certain countries in Central Asia. The legislation is led by Senators Steve Daines (R-Mont.), Senate Foreign Relations Committee Chairman Jim Risch (R-Idaho) and Ranking Member Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), and Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), as well as Representatives Carol Miller (R-W.V.) and Jimmy Panetta (D-Calif.) in the House.

The Jackson-Vanik Amendment is a set of trade restrictions in the Trade Act of 1974 that denied unconditional normal trade relations to certain countries that had non-market economies and that restricted emigration rights during the Cold War. While Congress has repealed the amendment’s application to most countries – ranging from Armenia to Vietnam – since the Soviet Union’s collapse, Jackson-Vanik still applies to Central Asian countries including Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan, despite broad support for its removal.

“As China and Russia deepen their foothold across Central Asia, outdated Jackson-Vanik restrictions are undermining our relationships with key regional partners,” said Bennet. “Passing this bill will remove this Soviet-era relic – so we can compete effectively and advance U.S. interests in the region.”

Bennet has consistently worked to deepen U.S. alliances and partnerships with countries seeking to diversify their relationships beyond China and Russia, and to bolster mutually-beneficial trade to open international markets to American companies and advance U.S. interests.

Bennet and U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy (R-La.) lead the bicameral and bipartisan Americas Act, which is the only major strategic economic plan to counter China’s geopolitical and economic influence in the Western Hemisphere. Bennet also leads the bipartisan Medical Supply Chain Resiliency Act, legislation that would bolster the United States’ ability to engage in trade negotiations with partners – such as Costa Rica, Japan, and the United Kingdom – to ensure the safe and efficient delivery of critical medical goods and services to U.S. patients and providers.

In addition to Bennet, Daines, Risch, Murphy, Shaheen, Miller, and Panetta, Senators Gary Peters (D-Mich.), David McCormick (R-Pa.), and Tim Scott (R-S.C), and Representatives Robert Alderholt (R-Ala.), Don Beyer (D-Va.), Trent Kelly (R-Miss.), and Joe Wilson (R-S.C.) co-sponsor the legislation.

title: Bennet Statement on Vote to Hold Russian Oil Purchasers Accountable for Supporting Putin’s War in Ukraine
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, released the following statement after voting to advance the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia Act of 2026, legislation he co-sponsors to impose sanctions on Russian President Vladimir Putin’s inner circle and his enablers across Russian industry and financial institutions, the Russian shadow fleet, and firms supporting Russia’s defense industrial base:

“For the past four years, Ukraine has fought bravely against Vladimir Putin’s aggression, showing us what it looks like to fight and die for democracy, for their country, and for the West.

“Amid Putin’s intransigence at the negotiating table and daily attacks across Ukraine, our bipartisan sanctions bill will impose greater pressure on Putin to end his unprovoked war, especially as Ukraine seizes the momentum and increasingly takes the fight to Moscow. I am pleased to see the Senate take the first step today to get this done.

“We must do everything we can to back the Ukrainian people in their fight – including by passing this bill and my legislation to ensure continued intelligence-sharing and to strengthen drone cooperation. Backing Ukraine today will be our best deterrence against authoritarian ambitions tomorrow.”

title: Bennet Statement on Voting Against the Confirmation of Jay Clayton as Director of National Intelligence
text:
Washington, D.C. — Colorado U.S. Senator Michael Bennet, a member of the Senate Select Committee on Intelligence, released the following statement after he voted not to approve President Trump’s nomination of Jay Clayton to serve as the Director of National Intelligence:

“I’m concerned Jay Clayton lacks the independence necessary to successfully lead our intelligence community. While I recognize his prior public service, Clayton’s repeated deference to the Trump White House – whether in indulging Trump’s false claims about the integrity of our election system or the improper issuance of subpoenas to reporters who wrote a story that President Trump disliked – suggests his top priority will be placating Donald Trump. On that basis, I cannot support his nomination. I hope he will not follow in the footsteps of other nominees who have surrendered their personal reputations to curry favor with the President. Our national security depends on it.”

title: Blackburn to Newsmax: Senate Should Remain Until SAVE America Act Passes
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-Tenn.) called on the Senate to remain in session until it passes the SAVE America Act during an appearance on Newsmax’s Wake Up America. Last week, Senator Blackburn led her colleagues in taking to the Senate floor to urge the Senate to pass the bill following President Trump’s address to the nation on election integrity. Watch the video Senator Blackburn released on her X account here.

Click here to download Senator Blackburn’s interview on Newsmax.

Click here to watch the video Senator Blackburn posted on X.

Sen. Blackburn to Newsmax: Senate Should Remain Until SAVE America Act Passes

Brian Freeman

Newsmax

Senate Republicans are prepared to remain in Washington as long as necessary to pass the SAVE America Act, backing President Donald Trump's call to delay the chamber's planned summer recess until election integrity legislation reaches his desk, Sen. Marsha Blackburn told Newsmax on Tuesday.

The Tennessee Republican said on ?Newsmax's "Wake Up America" that the GOP is willing to work weekends, split the legislation into smaller pieces, or pursue any other legislative strategy necessary to enact the bill, which would require proof of U.S. citizenship to register to vote in federal elections.

"Whatever it takes, if it is staying here, if it's breaking the bill in pieces, doing pieces one at a time, whatever we need to do to make certain that we pass the SAVE Act is what we need to do," Blackburn said. "We're all in on getting the SAVE Act passed."

Her comments came after Trump urged Senate Republicans to remain in session until the legislation is approved, writing on Truth Social that Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., "should not allow the United States Senate to leave town until it passes the SAVE America Act," while also renewing his call to eliminate the legislative filibuster if necessary.

Although Thune has indicated there are not enough votes to abolish the filibuster, Blackburn dismissed suggestions that Republicans are wavering on the underlying legislation, arguing the conference remains united behind strengthening election security.

"No one has worked harder than President Trump to make certain that we exercise election integrity," she said. "Those of us that comprise the steering committee, which is the conservatives in the Senate, have been saying for months, we will stay here weekends and until we can get this passed, because we know this is important."

Blackburn said she has already begun advancing portions of the legislation individually after leading Senate Republicans last week in an effort to move forward with a voter identification provision.

She also highlighted legislation she has introduced that would encourage states to verify voter registration rolls against the federal Systematic Alien Verification for Entitlements (SAVE) database, which contains information on individuals who are not U.S. citizens and are therefore ineligible to vote in federal elections.

According to Blackburn, 26 states already compare their voter rolls against the federal database, while 24 do not. She said expanding that practice would strengthen election integrity nationwide.

title: Blumenthal and Booker Introduce Food Labeling Modernization Act
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Today, U.S. Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-CT) and Senator Cory Booker (D-NJ) introduced the Food Labeling Modernization Act to combat confusing and misleading information printed on food packages. Companion legislation was introduced in the House of Representatives by U.S. Representatives Frank Pallone, Jr. (D-NJ) and Rosa DeLauro (D-CT).

“Current food labels are a confusing maze designed to protect corporate profits over American families,” said Blumenthal. “Federal standards have not kept pace with the modern food industry. The Food Labeling Modernization Act will ensure serving sizes are updated, allergens are clearly labeled, and nutritional information is transparent, giving people the tools they need to make healthier choices and avoid misleading, deceptive pitches and promotion.”

“For decades, food companies have gotten away with making junk foods seem healthier than they really are," said Booker. “This legislation will protect families from misleading labeling, helping them make informed decisions, eat healthier, and get more value from every dollar they spend on groceries.”

Most food labeling requirements in the Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act have not been updated in more than thirty-five years – and in some cases have not been changed since 1938. As a result, food labels often don’t provide the information that today's consumers need to evaluate and compare products.

The Food Labeling Modernization Act would direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services to establish a single, standard front-of-package nutrition labeling system in a timely manner for all food products required to bear nutrition labeling. The bill would also strengthen current law to address trends in marketing that confuse or mislead consumers when they are attempting to compare food products. This includes defining terms like “Ultraprocessed” and “Not Ultraprocessed.” The bill also ensures consumers have access to the same nutrition information when shopping for food online as they would in brick-and-mortar locations.

Over the last few years, the Food and Drug Administration has moved to update requirements for food labels. The Food Labeling Modernization Act would build on that progress by ensuring consumers have access to easy-to-read and transparent information in order to make informed purchasing decisions.

“Federal food labeling laws are not aligned with the transparency that Americans from across the political spectrum are demanding,” said Center for Science in the Public Interest (CSPI) senior policy scientist Eva Greenthal. “It’s time for Congress to pass bold legislation that will give people the information they need to make healthy choices.”

title: Republicans Block Blumenthal Effort to Pass Take Care of America's Veterans Act Without Unprecedented Cuts to Veterans' Benefits
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – Today, Republican leadership blocked Senate Veterans’ Affairs Committee Ranking Member Richard Blumenthal’s (D-CT) attempt to pass an amended version of the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act. Blumenthal’s legislation would replace the controversial Republican proposal to cut veterans’ benefits with an alternative proposal to cover the costs of the legislation with a small portion of the $75 billion in unobligated and unspent funds appropriated to the Department of Defense in H.R. 1.

Blumenthal emphasized his proposal’s bipartisan support: “It would utilize unspent Department of Defense funds from H.R.1, the so-called Big Beautiful Bill, to cover the entire cost of the bill. It’s the only offset proposal for the Take Care of Veterans Act that has garnered bipartisan support, and it is the one that doesn’t pit some veterans against other veterans…More than $75 billion of the Department of Defense funds in H.R. - a bill signed into law more than one year ago - remain unspent and unobligated. And CBO has confirmed, absolutely confirmed, enactment of my proposal prior to the Department’s obligation of those funds would provide the savings we need.”

Blumenthal objected to the Republican proposal to cut benefits for more than one million veterans who are currently eligible to receive benefits for tinnitus or sleep apnea: “These disabilities are not hypothetical or abstract. They're real, and they do disable people. And often, they are the result directly from combat or training…It may seem like an abstract principle, but to veterans who would lose sleep apnea and tinnitus benefits, it's a big deal. In fact, it can be a life-changing deal…We are creating a new generation of combat-injured veterans. It is unconscionable to claim that we can only care for them by forcing other veterans to sacrifice.”

Blumenthal rejected Republican leadership’s defense of these cuts: “(Their) argument essentially is that VA is going to take away these benefits through rule-making. And therefore, we should take advantage of the savings by action that is wrong, unconscionable, and deeply hurtful to veterans.”

Blumenthal concluded by calling on his colleagues to abandon these cuts: “We need to do the right thing. Veterans deserve meaningful results from a grateful nation, and they should never be handed an invoice when the costs of war come due.”

Last month, House Republicans pull a planned vote on the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act, following a bipartisan House vote to replace the Republican benefit cuts with Blumenthal’s proposal to utilize unobligated Department of Defense funds. Congressional Democrats and many Veterans Service Organizations have publicly opposed the Republican funding proposal included in the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act.

The Senator’s amended legislation would also have replaced the watered-down version of the Major Richard Star Act currently included in the Take Care of America’s Veterans Act with the Blumenthal-authored version of the legislation that fully repeals the wounded veteran tax.

A video is available here.
