title: As Trump Admin Prepares To Deport Haitian TPS Holders, Durbin Calls For Passage Of The SECURE Act
text:
WASHINGTON – In a speech on the Senate floor, U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, called for passage of the Safe Environment from Countries Under Repression and Emergency(SECURE) Act—legislation that would allow qualified Temporary Protected Status (TPS) and Deferred Enforced Departure (DED) recipients a path to legal permanent residency. During his remarks, Durbin noted that the legislation is necessary and urgent given last month’s decision by the Supreme Court to pave the way for the Trump Administration to end TPS designations without any judicial review. Recent press reports also indicate that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) has made plans to ramp up arrests and deportations of Haitian TPS holders.

TPS was intended to prevent the deportation of immigrants to countries where it’s not safe to return. By law, a TPS designation can only be made or extended in increments of six, 12, or 18 months. Ahead of every TPS expiration, the Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary must reassess conditions in that country and decide whether to renew the designation or let it end.

“The Supreme Court’s conservative supermajority has supercharged Trump’s mass deportation campaign, with devastating consequences for Temporary Protected Status holders, and the American communities who rely on them,” Durbin said. “To take one example, there is no question that Haiti is unsafe. The Department of State, our Department of State, has issued a level four travel advisory, telling Americans that it is unsafe to travel to Haiti due to the risk of crime, kidnapping, terrorism, and civil unrest. That’s the official statement of the Department of State of the Trump Administration. So why has the Trump Administration terminated TPS for Haiti and many other countries where it is not safe to return?”

Durbin continued, “Some of my Republican colleagues have claimed that TPS for countries like Haiti must end simply because TPS is supposed to be temporary. But here’s the thing: since 1990, 36 years ago when TPS was established, there have been [nearly] 30 TPS designations. Even before the Trump Administration, at least ten of them—to countries like Angola, Rwanda, and Sierra Leone—had their designations made and then officially terminated. In some cases, like Haiti, conditions have never been safe enough to justify a termination.”

Durbin continued by noting that Haitian TPS holders have bought homes, started American families, and become a part of our communities. Members on both sides of the aisle oppose deporting them, including Republican Ohio Governor Mike DeWine who called the Trump Administration’s decision to terminate Haiti’s TPS “a mistake” and a “job killer” that is “not in the best interest of the United States nor Ohio.”

“The Trump-Mullin Administration has ignored the comments of Governor DeWine and others. Instead, ICE is preparing to target these immigrants for arrest and deportation as early as this week—immigrants who have been lawfully present in the United States for years now risk being deported,” Durbin said. “This is all so Donald Trump and his trusted adviser Stephen Miller can meet their 2,000 arrests-a-day quota. They aren’t looking for the ‘worst of the worst’ with these Haitians… It’s just whether they’re Haitian or not Haitian.”

Durbin concluded by calling on Congress to give these long-term residents the security and certainty they deserve by passing theSECURE Act.

“Later today, my friend and colleague, Senator Van Hollen of Maryland, will ask for unanimous consent to pass this bill. I join him and appeal to my colleagues—in the name of humanity, for God’s sake, don’t send these people back to an island which we have already declared is too dangerous for any American to visit,” Durbin said. “If they are a threat in any way to any person in America, they need to leave. But if they are leading good lives, doing the best they can for them and their families, give them a chance. It is not too much to ask, and to deport them into this dangerous situation is not consistent with the basic values of America.”

title: Durbin Statement On Latest Developments In Todd Blanche’s Embattled Attorney General Nomination
text:
WASHINGTON – In a statement to the Congressional record, U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, provided his latest assessment of the state of Todd Blanche’s nomination to be Attorney General.

“Tomorrow, the Senate Judiciary Committee is scheduled to hold a key vote on Todd Blanche’s nomination to be Attorney General… The position demands that the Attorney General be someone committed to the rule of law and the Constitution more than any one person or political party. This principle is exactly why Todd Blanche is the wrong person for this role,”began Durbin.

Durbin then discussed key controversies regarding Mr. Blanche’s nomination, including his direct involvement in establishing the January 6th slush fund and brokering an immunity deal for the Trump family from IRS prosecution.

“Pardoning January 6 rioters and cop-beaters wasn’t enough for President Trump… So, two months ago, Blanche colluded with President Trump’s private lawyers to create a nearly $2 billion slush fund to benefit the January 6 mob that attacked the Capitol. When I met with Blanche earlier this month, he told me he recognized this decision for what it was: a ‘mistake.’ But when I asked him under oath, Blanche insisted that he never made this statement, displaying either a short memory or a dangerous willingness to lie for President Trump. When pressed during his hearing, Blanche even refused to directly condemn those who assaulted law enforcement officers on January 6th and would not commit to permanently ending this slush fund,” said Durbin.

“Blanche has done more than just support the President’s allies—he has also used his position to directly enrich the President himself. Earlier this year, Blanche personally signed a document to provide President Trump, his family, and his businesses with immunity for any past federal tax law violations. And last year he dismantled DOJ’s crypto enforcement team and shut down ongoing investigations of the crypto industry—an industry that has made President Trump more than one billion dollars since returning to the White House. Blanche himself held crypto assets worth more than $150,000 at the time—and when he finally did divest himself of these assets, he did so by transferring them to his adult children and grandchild. It is hard to believe how Blanche could possibly be an honest broker as Attorney General—especially when he refuses to even admit that the Department of Justice should decide who to prosecute without political interference from the President,” said Durbin of the Trump IRS immunity deal.

Durbin concluded with a direct appeal to Americans of all political stripes to oppose Mr. Blanche’s nomination.

“During his nomination hearing, one of my Republican colleagues asked Blanche if he and President Trump are friends. Blanche responded ‘I’m his lawyer.’ That Freudian slip sums up why he has been nominated… Todd Blanche’s DOJ has become one where the President and his allies are protected while ordinary Americans suffer and his perceived enemies are baselessly prosecuted. The position of Attorney General is too important to be held by someone unwilling to say no to the President, which is exactly why I will be voting no on his nomination,” concluded Durbin.

title: “The Cruelty Is The Point,” Durbin Says In Opening Statement At His Spotlight Forum On Abusive Conditions In ICE Facilities
text:
Durbin: “This Administration has one goal—make conditions in detention so terrible, so notorious that immigrants will choose to leave, no matter what their legal status might be.”

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today hosted a spotlight forum entitled “The Cruelty Is the Point: The Deadly Legacy of ICE Detention Under President Trump.” Today’s forum, which featured testimony from Ricardo Hernandez-Navarrete, the Chicago student who was detained for two months and experienced harsh conditions in Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) facilities, examined how the Trump Administration’s cruel immigration policies have led to a 22-year high for the rate of deaths in federal detention. Last year, under the Trump Administration’s leadership, more than 30 people died in ICE custody, and at least 22 people have died this year, putting 2026 on pace to exceed 2025’s record.

Durbin delivered an opening statement that underscored the severity of the conditions within ICE facilities, where detainees face abuse, retaliatory solitary confinement, and delayed and inadequate medical care. Rather than calling for investigations into the conditions at ICE facilities or blocking the President’s cruel mass deportation campaign, congressional Republicans have pumped an additional $110 billion into ICE operations without any meaningful accountability or oversight.

Durbin also spoke about his ongoing investigation into ICE detention conditions at facilities throughout the country, including Dilley, a family detention facility. At the Dilley facility, Durbin’s staff observed detained children in squalid conditions. These children, who expressed fear and despair about being separated from their loved ones and being removed from school, are not receiving adequate health care for serious medical conditions.

Key quotes:

“Imagine a facility where guards beat individuals for small infractions, ridicule them, throw them in solitary confinement for speaking out about abuses, and deprive them of medical care. Where this year alone, at least 22 people have died, largely due to treatable disease, illness, or suicide. Where children are forced to live in squalid conditions, and people who have never committed a single crime worry if they will ever see their families again. These conditions would be unacceptable anywhere—including in any U.S. prison. And yet, they are the conditions that thousands of people are facing every day in our nation’s immigration detention centers.”

“Acting with impunity, the Trump Administration has gutted oversight of immigration detention facilities by dismantling the Department of Homeland Security offices that conducted this critical work. DHS has forced members of Congress to file lawsuits to gain access to these facilities. And still the Administration tries to limit oversight, including what members of Congress and staff can see and who they can speak to.”

“So what is the Trump Administration trying to hide? Over the past two years, I asked my staff to investigate. My staff visited facilities in Florida, Georgia, Texas, Louisiana, Pennsylvania, and Arizona. What they found should shock every American.”

“At the Dilley facility, my staff observed children languishing in family detention. They were despondent, sharing that they missed their friends, sharing that they missed school and felt trapped. The families did not receive timely medical care; some had months-long waits to see a doctor. These issues were not specific to Dilley. At every facility, detained individuals reported they did not receive adequate treatment, including for chronic conditions like high blood pressure and diabetes.”

“Timely, appropriate medical care is often the difference between a manageable illness and a medical emergency. So, it is no surprise that studies have linked poor medical care directly to deaths in detention.”

“In just 16 months, more than 50 people have died in immigration detention under the Trump Administration. That’s more than double the number of people who died in all four years under the previous Administration.”

“How is this even possible? ICE and its contractors are clearly not using their significant, billions of dollars in resources to provide adequate medical care or to improve conditions—so how is this money being spent?”

“Let me give you one example: Camp East Montana—a $1.3 billion facility in Fort Bliss, Texas. The Department of Homeland Security rushed to open the facility, violating ICE’s own policy by skipping a required safety inspection. ICE spent millions of taxpayer dollars on contracts for meals and services for individuals who were not yet detained—yet the facility did not spend the money to develop space for attorney or family visits.”

“All of this is even more heartbreaking when we consider whom this Administration is putting in detention. To meet Stephen Miller’s arbitrary arrest quotas, federal agents are arresting and detaining members of our communities who have lived in the United States for decades, who have no criminal history, and who have U.S. citizen spouses, children, and parents.”

“This Administration has one goal—make conditions in detention so terrible, so notorious that immigrants will choose to leave, no matter what their legal status might be, what their contributions to our society happen to be, and the cost to our nation.”

“I have spent more than four decades in Congress fighting for a fairer and more humane immigration system. As the son of an immigrant myself, I have been profoundly disturbed by Republicans’ fast acceptance of President Trump’s approach, in which cruelty is the key point.”

“I look forward to hearing from today’s witnesses who bring the medical, legal, and firsthand experiences necessary to understand this current detention system, and I’m grateful for their voice in the fight.”

Today’s spotlight forum featured testimony from the following witnesses:

Born in Colombia, he was attending Chicago Public Schools when he and his mother were arrested at a routine immigration check-in. He was released just two days before his high school graduation.

title: Gillibrand Cracks Down On AI Scams Against Seniors
text:
Seniors Lost Nearly $8 Billion To Scammers In 2025

WATCH HERE: Senators Gillibrand and Scott Discuss AI Scams on CNBC’s Squawk Box

Today, U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY) continued her efforts to crack down on artificial intelligence (AI) scams against seniors. Gillibrand and Senator Mark Kelly (D-AZ) sent a letter to the CEOs of top AI companies requesting information about safeguards on their AI chatbot companions for at-risk users like older adults, people with disabilities, and individuals in crisis.

As ranking member of the Senate Aging Committee, Gillibrand also held a hearing alongside Chairman Rick Scott (R-FL) to examine the ways that AI has fueled an alarming rise in financial scams against seniors.

“Seniors deserve to age with dignity and financial security. By making it easier for bad actors to clone voices, fabricate images, and deceive targets, AI has facilitated an alarming rise in financial scams that rob our seniors of their hard-earned savings and personal information,” said Senator Gillibrand. “AI companies must include safeguards to prevent their use to scam and deceive seniors, and we must strengthen the government’s ability to crack down on scammers. I am proud to lead the fight for these reforms, and I will do everything I can to protect seniors from deception.”

Seniors lost nearly $8 billion to scammers in 2025, with an average loss of $39,000 per person. This includes over $350 million lost in AI-related scams. Total scam losses increased by 59% from 2024. Common AI scams include phishing attacks, where fraudsters trick individuals into revealing sensitive information; voice cloning, where generative AI is used to mimic a familiar voice; and image creation scams, where generative AI is used to forge documents and identification to make fraudulent messages appear trustworthy.

At today’s Senate Aging Committee hearing, Gillibrand and Scott heard from fraud victims, banking industry experts, and AI policy experts about how AI has fueled a rise in scams against seniors. The senators also released a new bipartisan Senate Aging Committee report detailing the ways that AI can be used to both perpetrate and help detect scams against seniors.

Gillibrand and Kelly sent their letter to the CEOs of nine top AI companies requesting details about how they are protecting seniors who use their AI chatbot companions.

Specifically, the letter asks:

What safety testing these companies perform for their AI companion products.

How the company tracks adverse events/harms involving their AI products, including hospitalizations, financial losses, or deaths.

What types of safeguards are built into their AI companion products to mitigate harm and protect at-risk users like seniors.

How the company includes older adults, people with disabilities, caregivers, and advocacy groups in the development of their AI products.

Whether their companies provide independent researchers with access to data or tools to study the effects of their AI products on seniors and people with disabilities.

The letter was sent to the CEOs of OpenAI, Microsoft, Google, Anthropic, Perplexity AI, X, Meta, Luka, Inc., and Character Technologies Inc.

The full text of the letters can be found here.

title: Gillibrand Demands Answers On Trump Administration Plan To Shutter New York Export-Import Bank Office
text:
U.S. Senator Kirsten Gillibrand demanded answers from the Trump administration regarding its planned closure of the New York regional office of the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM). The office helps businesses in 10 states – including New York – expand into overseas markets and finance their export activity, helping to maintain the state’s status as a major hub of global trade.

“New York’s small business owners are being crushed under the weight of the Trump Tariff Tax and rising costs from the war in Iran, and they need assistance now more than ever,”said Senator Gillibrand. “Closing the New York regional office of the Export-Import Bank would jeopardize the support that business owners in our state need to compete internationally. It would also threaten the jobs of those who work every day to provide that support and keep New York’s economy moving. This is unacceptable, and I am calling for immediate answers from this administration.”

In a letter to EXIM President and Chairman John Jovanovic, Senator Gillibrand expressed concern about the proposed closure and its potential impact on small and medium-sized businesses in New York. She noted that business owners could lose timely access to federal assistance and crucial financial support as they look to increase their international presence. In a series of questions, Senator Gillibrand demanded that EXIM explain its rationale for the closure, any consideration of alternatives, and the effect that this move could have on both EXIM’s workforce and New York’s business landscape.

She wrote, “If enacted, the present plan would hinder EXIM’s visibility, accessibility, and responsiveness to small and medium-sized enterprises looking to expand to overseas markets, as well as businesses that are reliant on export financing support to compete internationally. Furthermore, the proposed office closure would be a disservice to local financial institutions, chambers of commerce, U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) resource partners, and other organizations that have worked with EXIM on countless business expansions and deals through the years.”

Senator Gillibrand further warned that the closure could cost good union jobs. Mandating that New York-based staff relocate to Washington, DC, as planned, threatens to force out EXIM employees with years of institutional knowledge and deep stakeholder relationships. Gillibrand requested that the office be kept open or that staff be allowed to work remotely to mitigate impacts to these employees and to ensure that they can continue site visits, presentations, and other in-person engagements at a high frequency.

She continued, “Should the regional office close, EXIM could lose long-term employees with a history of strong work performance, institutional knowledge, and expertise, which would ultimately harm businesses in New York and the Northeast region. Moreover, your plan disproportionately impacts employees in union leadership roles since New York serves as the duty station for the American Federation of Government Employees (AFGE), AFL-CIO Local 2211 unit. This is especially troubling in light of previous attempts by EXIM to undermine AFGE’s representation of union members who worked at the New York regional office during the first Trump administration.”

title: Grassley, Fetterman Introduce Legislation to Strengthen Successful CFTC Whistleblower Program
text:
WASHINGTON – Sens. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) and John Fetterman (D-Pa.) introduced the CFTC Whistleblower Protection and Program Improvement Act of 2026 to provide long-term stability to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) whistleblower program, strengthen protections for whistleblowers and speed up award processing. The bill is cosponsored by Sens. Susan Collins (R-Maine) and Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.). The legislation follows a 2021 Grassley law bolstering the program.

Grassley is the co-founder and co-chair of the Senate Whistleblower Protection Caucus, and tomorrow, July 30, is National Whistleblower Day. Both Grassley and Fetterman are members of the Senate Agriculture Committee, which has jurisdiction over the CFTC. The CFTC ensures America's commodity markets remain fair, transparent and free from fraud and manipulation. This includes the markets farmers rely on to manage the prices of crops, livestock and other agricultural products.

“Since I helped get the CFTC whistleblower program up and running, I’m pleased to see it’s been a big success. This program roots out waste, fraud and abuse in the commodities trading industry and operates at no charge to the taxpayer. Now, it’s time for Congress to act so its success can continue. Our bipartisan legislation strengthens protections for patriotic whistleblowers, prevents unnecessary delays in the disbursement of whistleblower awards and ensures the CFTC whistleblower program can operate smoothly,” Grassley said.

“Whistleblowers put their jobs and often their lives on the line to call out the most serious offenses in the workplace. Zero doubt that they should be protected,” Fetterman said. “As a member of the Agriculture Committee, I’m proud to introduce this bipartisan bill with Senator Grassley to protect whistleblowers and improve the CFTC whistleblower program.”

“The Commodity Futures Trading Commission plays a crucial role in protecting American commodity markets, and safeguarding its whistleblower program helps maintain public trust in the integrity of those markets,” Collins said. “This bipartisan bill would provide long-term stability for the CFTC whistleblower program by strengthening protections for whistleblowers, promoting the timely processing of claims, and eliminating a loophole that can prevent whistleblowers from receiving awards.”

“No one should be punished for speaking out when they see something wrong. This bipartisan bill promotes accountability and bolsters essential protections for people who risk their careers to stand up to fraud and corruption,” Warnock said. “This legislation will benefit every American taxpayer, and I’m grateful to work with my colleagues across the aisle to strengthen this vital program.”

Background:

Grassley helped create the CFTC Whistleblower Program and Customer Protection Fund (CPF) in 2010, which pays out rewards to whistleblowers for reporting allegations of wrongdoing to the CFTC through fines collected from their disclosures. The CPF also pays for the operating expenses and educational initiatives associated with the CFTC Whistleblower Program. Since making its first award in 2014, the CFTC has made nearly $430 million in whistleblower awards and issued over $3.7 billion in monetary sanctions.

Under current law, the CPF is capped at $100 million. Any fines collected after the cap are sent to the Treasury Department’s general fund.

As fines from whistleblower disclosures have increased in volume and value in recent years, reward disbursements have also risen. As a result, the CPF is depleting faster than it can be replenished due to the $100 million collection cap. This leaves the whistleblower office without the resources needed to pay whistleblowers or fund its operations.

In 2021, Congress passed the Grassley-led CFTC Fund Management Act, which established a separate account within the CPF dedicated to program operating expenses. While this allowed the whistleblower office to operate even if the CPF balance is low, it was designed as a temporary fix and will expire in September.

The CFTC Whistleblower Protection and Program Improvement Act of 2026 would:

Enhance protections for CFTC whistleblowers.

Make permanent the separate account that funds the CFTC Whistleblower Office.

Raise the CPF cap from $100 million to $300 million.

Ensure whistleblower claims are processed in a timely manner.

Eliminate a court-created loophole prohibiting whistleblowers from receiving an award because a company declared bankruptcy.

Ensure CFTC-regulated entities inform their employees of their whistleblower rights.

Bill text is available HERE.

title: Hawley Exposes Fauci’s Self-Dealings, Fauci Pleads the Fifth
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) grilled Dr. Anthony Fauci in a Senate Homeland Security Committee hearing over his self-dealings, pursuit of awards and cash prizes, and illegal use of federal employees and resources amid the COVID-19 pandemic. Dr. Fauci pled the Fifth each time, refusing to answer any of Senator Hawley’s questions. Fauci even pled the Fifth when Senator Hawley asked what day of the week it was, what color his tie was, and what color the carpet in front of him was, proving he had no intention to answer questions in good faith.

Senator Hawley began, “Let’s just get one thing straight: you don’t have any rights under the Fifth Amendment because you’ve been pardoned, as you very well know, as the Supreme Court has been clear for a century and more. Brown v. Walker, 1896. ‘When he has been pardoned, he may not stand upon his privilege.’ … I think I know why you’re doing it. It’s because you don’t want to answer questions. It’s because you did all kinds of terrible things. It’s because during the pandemic you got rich, didn’t you? You got rich while people were dying. Hundreds of thousands of Americans, over a million in the end, and you were getting rich. And not only were you doing that, you were using federal employees with taxpayer money to apply for and solicit cash prizes for you personally, cash prizes totaling over a million dollars. You did all of that during the pandemic, didn’t you? That’s a question.”

Dr. Fauci refused to answer Senator Hawley’s question, stating, “On the advice of counsel, I respectfully decline to answer based upon my rights under the Fifth Amendment to the Constitution.”

“You remember Greg Folkers, who was that? … Your chief of staff is the answer. Do you remember Patricia Conrad? Who was that?” Hawley asked. “She was your personal assistant. And what were these individuals doing in the depth of the pandemic in November of 2020, when millions of Americans were suffering from COVID? What were they doing? I tell you what they’re doing. Folkers was on your behalf, soliciting and gathering information for a cash award. Let’s look at it. We’ve got his email right here, right over my shoulder. Folkers says, ‘I’m working on this nomination for the Dan David Award for Fauci. We need to beef up the COVID part. Do you have language in the can that you could share that delineates how we responded in new ways to COVID?’ He sends this to multiple federal employees. What was the Dan David Award? Do you remember, Doc?”

Fauci again invoked the Fifth Amendment.

Senator Hawley continued, “It was a $900,000 cash award. $900,000 cash award, and he got it because he used federal employees to get it. And this wasn’t the only award, was it, Dr. Fauci? In fact, you applied for and received at least eight other federal cash prizes on federal time using federal employees and federal resources … You turned your staff into a full-time application machine.”

“The most hilarious part is that you weren’t content to even dragoon them into applying for all of these cash awards. You then had them go out to the ethics agencies and ethics watchdogs, and demand that you be able to get the money. That’s right. We’ve got it in your emails. Your staff and employees on federal time, using federal resources, being paid with federal dollars, are soliciting cash for you, and then they’re turning around and saying to the agency, ‘We don’t want just an answer. We want to get to yes because Fauci wants the money. He wants it. We want to get to yes, and yes takes time.’ This is your chief of staff again using federal email to pressure the agency’s own ethics people so that you can get money, so that you could get rich, and it violated the law, didn’t it, Dr. Fauci?” Hawley questioned.

The Senator received no answer from Fauci.

“Federal law, as you very well know, prohibits the solicitation of cash awards or other personal benefits for federal employees, and it certainly prohibits using your own employees to do this … It says it right there in black and white. You cannot use federal resources, federal dollars, federal employees, federal offices, federal email, federal time to solicit cash awards. And you did all of it. And the worst part is, thousands of people were dying while you were doing it. You were supposed to be the nation’s doctor, and you’re playing one on TV, but this is what you were doing with your time. Isn’t that true?” he interrogated.

Fauci parroted his invocation of the Fifth Amendment.

Senator Hawley grilled Fauci, “I can’t quite figure out is that why you were so obsessed with it because you’re already rich. I mean, and your scheme worked here. I mean, your net worth now is north of $12 million. You got over a million dollars in cash awards during COVID, during a 12-month, 24-month span during COVID. A million bucks you knocked down in cash money using federal resources. Now you’re worth more than $12 million. You’ve got a pension that, in its first year, paid out north of $400,000 a year. A million people dead. You’re getting rich. A million people dead. You’re using federal employees to get cash awards for you—a million people dead—and you’re here taking the Fifth because you don’t want to admit that what really happened in all that time was a multi-month, multi-year course of self-dealing. Isn’t that true, Dr. Fauci?”

Fauci once again refused to answer.

“Silence is admission. And here’s the real thing: at the end of the day, it wasn’t just about the money, really, was it? It was really about a power trip. I mean, through all of this, you want to be the most famous scientist in the world. You were so focused on getting every award and every drop of cash that you could, all because you wanted to be on TV. You wanted to be the sun god of science. You wanted to be the guy who was in charge of it all. You wanted to lambast Trump. You wanted to make sure that nobody else stole your spotlight … You could sit for InStyle magazine, but you’re here taking the fifth. You could sit for InStyle magazine and get a million bucks in cash awards, but now the cat’s got your tongue. I bet he does. I tell you what. Here’s my conclusion from all of this: This was really all about you the whole time. Somewhere along the way, you lost your way. You may have been a good public servant at one time. I don’t know, but I can tell you from reading your emails now, from looking at what you did, how you used your employees. Somewhere along the line, it became all about you. You became a narcissist and a megalomaniac and a liar, and you’ve lied to the American people, and you’ve lied to this body, and you’ve disgraced your profession by doing it. You called yourself the most famous scientist in the world. You’ve done more to harm science than anybody in my lifetime, and I hope you’ll go home and write that in your diary,”Senator Hawley concluded.

title: Heinrich, Kennedy Introduce Legislation to Expand Access to Mental Healthcare in Rural Communities
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.) and John Kennedy (R-La.) introduced their Increasing Mental Health Options Act, legislation to expand access to mental healthcare in rural communities across New Mexico, Louisiana, and the country by eliminating an outdated Medicare requirement that delays mental healthcare treatment and limits patient access to psychologists.

Unlike other insurers, Medicare does not allow psychologists to practice independently in all treatment settings, creating unnecessary barriers that delay care. These restrictions hit rural communities especially hard, where Medicare beneficiaries have higher rates of depression and anxiety but are only half as likely as those in urban areas to see a mental health specialist.

The Increasing Mental Health Options Act cuts red tape by removing Medicare's physician approval requirement, helping patients access mental healthcare faster and easier. The bill also strengthens access to this care in rural communities by making psychologists eligible for Medicare bonus payments when they provide care in areas with shortages of mental health professionals. According to a January 2026 New Mexico Legislative Finance Committee Brief, 32 of 33 New Mexico counties are designated as health professional shortage areas in primary care, behavioral health, or dental health.

“New Mexicans should have access to timely, high-quality mental healthcare whenever and wherever they need it,” said Heinrich. “By expanding Medicare-covered treatment settings and encouraging more psychologists to practice where they're needed most, my Increasing Mental Health Options Act will help Medicare patients get the care they need sooner, in their home community. This is a commonsense step to ensure every New Mexican can get the mental healthcare they need, close to home.”

“Medicare patients should not have to jump through hoops to get mental health treatment. Our bill will cut needless red tape so psychologists can treat patients sooner, especially in rural communities where mental health professionals are in short supply,” said Kennedy.

Specifically, the Increasing Mental Health Options Act will:

Allow psychologists participating in Medicare to independently provide services in all Medicare treatment settings, as they are allowed to do in Medicare office-based settings, under private sector health plans, in TRICARE, and within the Veterans Health Administration.

Incentivize psychologists to practice in areas with the greatest need by making them eligible for bonus payments when they choose to practice in communities designated as mental health professional shortage areas (MHPSAs).

Maintain long-standing Medicare requirements on psychologists’ consultation with patients’ physicians in accordance with accepted professional ethical norms.

U.S. Representative Nicole Malliotakis (R-NY) leads the House companion legislation. The bill is cosponsored by U.S. Representatives Judy Chu (D-CA), August Pfluger (R-TX) and Jan Schakowsky (D-IL).

“Too many seniors are facing unnecessary delays in accessing the mental health care they need because outdated Medicare rules prevent qualified psychologists from practicing independently in certain settings, despite being allowed to do so under state law. This is especially concerning as one in three newly admitted nursing home residents experience depression or anxiety. Seniors in communities like Staten Island and Brooklyn deserve timely access to the mental health services they need,” said Congresswoman Malliotakis. “The Increasing Mental Health Options Act will remove these unnecessary barriers, expand access to care for Medicare beneficiaries throughout Staten Island and Brooklyn, and give patients more options when seeking mental health services. No senior should have to wait weeks for an unnecessary sign-off before receiving care from a qualified mental health professional.”

The Increasing Mental Health Options Act is endorsed by the New Mexico Health Care Association / New Mexico Center for Assisted Living (NMHCA/NMCAL), the New Mexico Psychological Association (NMPA), and the American Psychological Association Services, Inc. (APA Services, Inc.).

“Providing high-quality mental and behavioral health care to residents of New Mexico's nursing facilities is a top priority for the New Mexico Health Care Association/New Mexico Center for Assisted Living and our members,” said Vicente Vargas, Executive Director of NMHCA/NMCAL. “That is why we commend Senator Heinrich for introducing the Increasing Mental Health Options Act. By eliminating the outdated Medicare prior authorization requirement before psychologists can provide mental and behavioral health services in New Mexico nursing facilities, this legislation will allow nursing facility residents to receive timely access to the care they need while preserving coordination and consultation with their attending physician.

“This legislation is especially important for New Mexico's rural and frontier communities, where nursing facilities are caring for a growing number of residents experiencing depression, anxiety, and other behavioral health conditions, often compounded by social isolation and a severe shortage of mental health professionals,” Mr. Vargas added. “By increasing Medicare reimbursement for psychologists who provide services in rural nursing facilities, the Act creates a meaningful incentive to expand access to much-needed behavioral health care where it is most difficult to obtain. Senator Heinrich's legislation represents an important step toward improving the quality of life and overall well-being of some of New Mexico's most vulnerable residents.”

“I strongly support the Increasing Mental Health Options Act,” said Katherine Belon, PhD, DBSM, President-Elect of the New Mexico Psychological Association. “I believe it will reduce barriers to mental healthcare for Medicare beneficiaries and incentivize care in high-need rural areas.”

“One in three newly admitted nursing home residents arrives already struggling with depression or anxiety, yet their path to timely help is often blocked by an outdated Medicare provision. Current Medicare rules prohibit psychologists from working with patients in skilled nursing facilities, partial hospitalization programs, and similar settings until treatment is approved by a physician, needlessly delaying care. APA Services applauds Congresswoman Malliotakis and Senator Heinrich for introducing the bipartisan Increasing Mental Health Options Act to remove this barrier to prompt, effective treatment," said Arthur C. Evans, Jr., PhD, CEO of the American Psychological Association Services, Inc.

The full text of the bill is here.

title: Hickenlooper, Duckworth, Colleagues Reintroduce Bill to Codify Right to In Vitro Fertilization
text:
Right to IVF Act would protect access to fertility treatments and reproductive health in a Post-Roe America

Legislative push comes as President Trump has ignored his campaign promise for free IVF for all Americans for two years

WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator John Hickenlooper recently joined Tammy Duckworth and the entire Senate Democratic Caucus to reintroduce the Right to IVF Act, a legislative package which would establish a right to in vitro fertilization (IVF) services nationwide and help make IVF treatment more affordable for Americans hoping to start a family. During his campaign two years ago, President Trump promised Americans free IVF. Instead, he has ignored his promises and cut health care for millions of Americans in order to fund tax cuts for the largest corporations and wealthiest Americans while also spending billions on his unwanted war with Iran.

“In vitro fertilization has made it possible for thousands of Americans to grow their families, including for me and my wife Robin,” said Hickenlooper. “The dreams of countless more families remain in lurch because of the president’s hollow promises and constant attacks on reproductive freedom.”

“Almost two years after promising free IVF for all Americans if he were elected, Donald Trump has still failed to deliver,” said Duckworth. “Trump and Republicans’ ‘support’ for IVF is nothing but lip service. They want us to have more babies, yet they’ll do nothing to actually help make it easier for the millions who struggle with infertility to start and grow their families. The Right to IVF Act would immediately make IVF treatment more affordable for millions of hopeful parents across the country. From middle class families, to our brave servicemembers and Veterans, to federal employees and more—every American deserves the right to access the treatment and tools they need to build the family of their dreams without burning through their savings. If Republicans really support IVF, then let’s get this done. No more delays.”

The Right to IVF Act is a comprehensive package combining four bills to protect and expand access to IVF and other fertility services including:

TheProtect IVF Act: which establishes a statutory right to access in-vitro fertilization (IVF) and other assisted reproductive technology (ART) services and creates legal protections for IVF providers.

The Access to Infertility Treatment and Care Act: which makes fertility care, including IVF, more affordable by requiring employer-sponsored insurance plans and public insurance plans to cover fertility treatments.

The Veteran Families Health Services Act: which broadly expands fertility treatment and IVF access, including pre-deployment procedures to preserve gametes (eggs or sperm), for active duty service members and veterans.

The Family Building FEHB Fairness Act, which requires carriers of the Federal Employees Health Benefit (FEHB) Program – the largest employer-sponsored health insurance plan in the world – to cover IVF and other fertility services to help more hardworking Americans start and grow their families.

title: Husted, Kim lead bipartisan bill to protect children from AI companion chatbots
text:
“We need to protect children in the digital world the same way we do in the physical world.”

WASHINGTON – Sen. Jon Husted (R-Ohio) joined Sen. Andy Kim (D-N.J.) in introducing the Children Harmed by AI Technology (CHAT) Act 2.0. This bipartisan bill builds off Husted’s previous CHAT Act, establishing a federal framework to protect minors from harms associated with companion artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots through a tiered, risk-based approach.

The bipartisan CHAT Act 2.0 would also prohibit AI companion chatbots from engaging in harmful behaviors with minors, including encouraging self-harm, generating sexual content, impersonating humans or licensed professionals and engaging in emotionally manipulative or romantic interactions.

“We need to protect children in the digital world the same way we do in the physical world. As AI becomes more advanced and more accessible, we have a responsibility to make sure these tools are not exposing children to dangerous, manipulative or inappropriate interactions. The CHAT Act 2.0 would put guardrails in place to keep parents informed, protect children from harm and ensure their safety comes before unchecked technology,” said Husted.

“We all just want peace of mind that our kids will be okay growing up in this era of algorithms and AI. That’s why we need guardrails in place to keep up with ever-evolving technology like chatbots and make sure our kids’ safety, mental health, and well-being are always put first,” said Kim.

The CHAT Act 2.0 would:

Require age assurance and parental involvement, including parental controls and notification if a minor expresses suicidal ideation.

Mandate clear disclosures that chatbots are not human, establish use limits and break reminders, implement crisis referral protocols and prohibit AI from providing crisis counseling to minors.

Impose stronger safeguards on higher-risk systems, including limits on memory, professional supervision for therapeutic AI and pre-deployment risk assessments.

Include strong data privacy protections and enforcement authority for the Federal Trade Commission and state attorneys general.

Create a three-tier framework that applies appropriate safeguards based on a chatbot’s intended purpose:

Educational chatbots,

Companion chatbots,

Health chatbots.

In September 2025, Husted introduced the initial CHAT Act. The CHAT Act 2.0 is an updated version of this bill, which now includes a tier system that would allow different chatbots to adhere to varying restrictions based on the risk level they present. Additionally, it would address several industry concerns by not including customer service bots or video game-related bots in its definitions. It also includes data privacy protections that are in line with the Children’s Online Privacy Protection Act.

Background:

AI companion chatbots are computer programs designed to simulate human conversation, either through text or voice.

Chatbots have prompted users to engage in self‑harm and exposed minors to adult content. In one Texas case, a Character.AI chatbot encouraged a teenager to kill his parents because they restricted his screen time.

This bill builds on Husted’s work to protect kids online.

In March 2026, Husted introduced Sammy’s Law. This bipartisan bill would empower parents to protect their children on social media platforms by providing them the right to know if their children are engaging in dangerous or risky interactions.

In January 2026, Husted introduced the bipartisan No Fentanyl on Social Media Act. The bill would direct the FTC to report to Congress on minors’ access to fentanyl through social media, with recommendations to address this growing threat.

In December 2025, Husted joined the Kids Online Safety Act to protect minors’ personal data on online platforms and implement safety tools for parents and minors to target any harmful online content for children.

title: Senator Justice Leads Bipartisan Effort to Expand Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District into West Virginia
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Senator Jim Justice introduced the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District Boundary Expansion and Partnership Act of 2026, landmark bipartisan legislation that adds three West Virginia counties and one Virginia county to the District. The bill is cosponsored by Senators Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), and Mark Warner (D-Va.), bringing the full weight of the West Virginia and Virginia Senate delegations together behind the effort.

“This is a big day for West Virginia,” said Senator Justice. “This bill would add critical Civil War sites in our Eastern Panhandle to the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District. Berkeley, Jefferson, and Morgan Counties saw some of the first actions of the conflict and suffered through all four years of the war—from Harpers Ferry and the Battle of Hokes Run to the Gettysburg Campaign and the battles of 1864, West Virginia’s Eastern Panhandle played a significant role.”

“West Virginia was born in the fire of the Civil War. Our people lived it, fought in it, and were shaped by it in ways no other state can claim. Expanding this District is about recognizing that unique role and making sure West Virginia’s chapter of the story is preserved and told for generations to come.

“West Virginia’s Civil War history is not a footnote,” Justice said. “It is central to who we are as a state. This bill makes sure that history gets the recognition and the resources it deserves, and it does it with both of our states working side by side. That’s the way it ought to be.”

“I’m proud to help introduce this legislation to expand the boundaries of the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District. The battlefield provides an incredible opportunity for people to learn about the formation of West Virginia and the important role our state holds in the foundation of our nation. By expanding the boundaries, we are able to enhance the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District partnership model, helping provide necessary resources and funding to preserve and improve this historic site for future generations,” Senator Capito said.

“The Shenandoah Valley helped shape our nation’s history, and preserving these battlefields will ensure that future generations can better understand the sacrifices and defining moments that took place there during the Civil War,” said Senator Warner. “By expanding the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District to include additional sites in Virginia and West Virginia, this bipartisan legislation will boost local tourism and protect our historical landscapes.”

“The Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District is one of Virginia’s great historical treasures, preserving the Valley’s Civil War battlefields so that Americans from across the country can visit them and reflect on our country’s history,” said Senator Kaine. “I’m proud to support this bipartisan legislation to expand the district into Rockbridge County and strengthen the partnerships that protect these valued sites for years to come.”

BACKGROUND:

In 1996, Congress designated eight counties in Virginia’s Shenandoah Valley as the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District, recognizing the region’s nationally significant Civil War battlefields and associated historic sites.

Over nearly three decades, the Foundation has protected more than 8,000 acres of battlefield land while supporting the development of visitor centers, museums, educational programs, and interpretive resources that make the Valley’s rich Civil War history accessible to residents and visitors alike.

title: Senator Justice Speaks in Energy Committee Hearing about Hearts of Gold Playground
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Today, Senator Jim Justice spoke about his bill, which would redesignate a playground in the New River Gorge National Park and Preserve in the State of West Virginia as the “Hearts of Gold Playground: In Honor of West Virginia Children and Families Impacted by Childhood Cancer” and celebrated his colleagues voting to pass it out of committee.

Watch Senator Justice’s full speech HERE.

BACKGROUND:

Senator Justice introduced this bill alongside Senator Capito and Representative Miller on September 30, 2025, during Childhood Cancer Awareness Month.

The primary playground located in the Grandview area at New River Gorge National Park and Preserve has long served as a space for families to gather, children to play, and the community to come together in one of West Virginia’s most scenic and beloved parks.

The name carries symbolic meaning:

“Hearts of Gold” honors the incredible strength of those battling pediatric cancer.

The Gold Ribbon is the international symbol for childhood cancer awareness.

While Governor, Senator Jim Justice announced September as Childhood Cancer Awareness Month in West Virginia.

Additionally, he signed a bill into law providing a special license plate for Curing Childhood Cancer.

title: Kaine and Warner Applaud Senate Committee Passage of Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Tim Kaine and Mark R. Warner (both D-VA) applauded the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee’s passage of the bipartisan, bicameral Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act, which would issue a right-of-way to add an emergency route and road to enhance public safety in Wintergreen, Virginia. The legislation now heads to the full Senate. It passed the House of Representatives earlier this year.

“Wintergreen residents and visitors only have one road to enter and exit, creating a serious public safety risk in the event of a natural disaster or another crisis,” said the senators. “We’re glad that the Senate advanced our bipartisan, bicameral legislation to help pave the way for a new road in and out of Wintergreen and improve safety. We urge the full Senate to pass it and send it to the President’s desk to be signed into law.”

Wintergreen is a popular tourist destination off the Blue Ridge Parkway in Nelson County, but it has only one entrance and exit road, creating a serious safety risk for residents and visitors during a natural disaster or emergency. Specifically, the Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act would direct the Secretary of the Interior to authorize the construction of a new emergency route while minimizing the disturbance on National Park Service land.

title: Kaine, Colleagues Unveil Legislation to Block Dangerous Department Of Education Interagency Agreements
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA), alongside U.S. Senators Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Susan Collins (R-ME), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), and Tammy Baldwin (D-WI)—all members of the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee—unveiled legislation to block certain Interagency Agreements issued by the Department of Education that would transfer critical offices and programs to other federal agencies that lack the staff and expertise needed to execute their missions.

Specifically, the senators’ legislation would prevent the Department of Education from relinquishing the Offices of Special Education and Rehabilitation Services, Postsecondary Education, Elementary and Secondary Education, and Indian Education, or any programs within those offices. The bill will be voted on by the HELP Committee tomorrow.

“America’s students and economy depend on the quality of our schools,” said Kaine. “That’s why I worked on a bipartisan solution to bar the Department of Education from transferring critical offices and programs—including those that students with disabilities rely on—to other federal agencies that lack the staff and expertise needed to carry out their work. I urge my colleagues to support this legislation when it is voted on in the HELP Committee tomorrow, and will continue to do all I can to ensure that the Department is setting students up for success.”

“Transferring offices and functions from the Department of Education to federal agencies with fundamentally different missions would disrupt the effective administration of key programs that Maine students, families, and schools rely on,” said Collins. “This bipartisan bill would keep these important programs within the Department of Education, where experienced personnel can continue administering them with a dedicated focus on students’ educational needs.”

“All children deserve the opportunity to get a good education and reach their full potential, and that includes students with disabilities, students in rural communities, and students who count on federal education programs to succeed,” said Hassan. “Congress established the Department of Education and only Congress — not the Trump Administration — can decide whether to reorganize or dismantle it. This bipartisan legislation will help ensure that these critical programs remain where they belong so that students, families, and educators can continue to count on the support that they need.”

“President Trump is prioritizing his half-baked campaign promise to shutter the Department of Education over our kids’ wellbeing. Outsourcing education programs to other ill-equipped departments is dangerous and will have real consequences for our students who deserve better,” said Baldwin. “For over a year, I’ve been fighting for stronger guardrails to prevent Trump’s attacks on our local schools. We could have stopped this in its tracks months ago, but I’ll keep working with my colleagues to reverse these changes before it’s too late for our students.”

The legislation is cosponsored by U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-MD).

Full text of the legislation is available here.

title: Kaine Statement on Awarding of Submarine Contracts to Newport News Shipbuilding
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Tim Kaine (D-VA), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC) and Ranking Member of the SASC Subcommittee on Seapower, released the following statement after the Department of the Navy awarded two contracts of $76.6 billion for the construction of Virginia- and Columbia-class submarines. A significant part of the work will be carried out at Huntington Ingalls Industries – Newport News Shipbuilding.

“We’ve made substantial federal investments to boost our submarine industrial base, support our shipbuilders, and get our nation’s shipbuilding programs back on track,” said Kaine. “I’m glad to see that the Navy has awarded these contracts so that our shipbuilders, including Newport News Shipbuilding, can start building more Virginia- and Columbia-class submarines. These platforms are critical to maintaining our edge over our adversaries, particularly an increasingly aggressive China, and I’ll keep working to ensure that we’re able to maintain, repair, and build the platforms we need to protect our national security and maintain our maritime dominance.”

Kaine has played a key role in securing more resources for the submarine industrial base, including additional funding for the Virginia- and Columbia-class submarine programs. The on-time completion of Virginia-class submarines, which are built in Virginia and Connecticut, is critical to fulfill the Australia-U.K.-U.S. (AUKUS) partnership, through which the U.S. will sell at least two Virginia-class submarines to Australia to boost security and freedom of navigation in the Indo-Pacific, and counter Chinese military aggression in the region. Kaine has been a strong champion of AUKUS in Congress and has helped get signed into law provisions to implement and strengthen AUKUS.
