title: Schatz, Colleagues Introduce Legislation To Provide Paid Family, Medical Leave For Federal Employees
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Brian Schatz (D-Hawai‘i) led a group of 8 senators in introducing the Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act, legislation to expand federal paid leave to include 12 weeks of family and medical leave. In addition to Schatz, the bill is co-sponsored by U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Va.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.).

“Right now, our laws are forcing federal workers to make the impossible choice between caring for their families and keeping their jobs,” said Senator Schatz. “Our bill will provide federal workers with 12 weeks of paid leave, giving them the time they need to take care of their own health and their loved ones.”

Currently, under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), employees in the private sector can take up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave to care for a newborn or an ill family member without fear of losing their jobs. For federal employees, while parental leave is paid due to the passage of Senator Schatz’s Federal Employee Paid Leave Act in 2019, family and medical leave continues to be unpaid.

Studies have shown that providing paid leave for federal employees would save the government at least $50 million annually in turnover and replacement costs. With federal agencies struggling to recruit and retain young talent, family-friendly policies are necessary to maintain a robust workforce. Just six percent of the federal workforce is under the age of 30, while roughly 40 percent of the workforce is eligible to retire within the next three years.

The Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act will guarantee 12 weeks of paid family leave for federal employees in all instances covered by the FMLA, including:

In order to care for the spouse, child, or parent of the employee, if such spouse, child, or parent has a serious health condition;

Because of a serious health condition that makes the employee unable to perform the functions of the employee’s position; and

Because of any qualifying exigency arising out of the fact that the spouse, child, or parent of the employee is on covered active duty (or has been notified of an impending call or order to covered active duty) in the Armed Forces.

The Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act is supported by the American Federation of Government Employees, National Treasury Employees Union, International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers, National Federation of Federal Employees, NARFE, National Association of Letter Carriers, American Postal Workers Union, and American Association of University Women.

“AFGE thanks Senator Brian Schatz for once again championing federal workers and their families by reintroducing the Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act. Expanding paid family and medical leave ensures federal employees never have to choose between caring for themselves or a loved one and serving the American people. This legislation will strengthen the federal workforce, improve employee retention, and help the government remain a competitive employer for the dedicated public servants our nation depends on,” said Everett Kelley, National President of the American Federation of Government Employees.

“Federal employees should never have to choose between caring for their loved ones and paying their bills on time. The Comprehensive Paid Family Leave Act would provide federal workers with the flexibility and support they need during some of life's most significant moments. As the federal government works to attract and retain talented public servants, providing comprehensive paid family leave is both the right thing to do and a smart investment in the workforce. NTEU is proud to endorse this legislation and appreciates Senator Schatz's continued leadership in advancing policies that strengthen the federal workforce and support working families,” said Doreen Greenwald, National President of the National Treasury Employees Union.

The text of the bill is available here.

title: NEWS: Schiff, Warren Call on SEC to Investigate Trump Media’s Plan to Give Wall Street Firms Faster Access to Truth Social Posts
text:
“Trump Media’s new data feed product is designed to work in the best interest of only a small few people: President Trump, his family, wealthy insiders, and high-frequency traders on Wall Street.”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.) sent a letter to Paul Atkins, Chair of the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC), calling on the SEC to investigate the Trump Media & Technology Group (“Trump Media”)’s reported plan to sell Wall Street firms faster access to the President’s market-moving posts on Truth Social in exchange for huge fees. The Senators urged the SEC to determine whether the proposed arrangement would violate applicable federal securities laws.

“The Truth API feed—which, according to some reports, will be offered for between $60,000 and $100,000 for a monthly subscription— will provide ‘banks and trading firms the fastest access to posts from the 10 most influential Truth Social accounts,’” wrote the Senators. “The President has the largest number of followers on Truth Social. President Trump has a significant financial interest in Trump Media, based on his ownership of roughly 41% of the company, and, as a result, stands to profit from the launch of this service.”

“President Trump’s posts on Truth Social are one of the principal ways the President communicates with the public. The posts, along with others that will reportedly be offered as part of Trump Media’s ‘Truth API’ data feed, contain what the company’s own representatives bill as ‘market-moving information’…” continued the Senators. “[T]his information and trading speed advantage could result in enormous profits for firms and wealthy individuals that pay the subscription fee because ‘Trump’s social media posts often move markets.’”

“Because of this service, social media posts about the President’s opinion or policy intent will not be available to the public or ordinary investors at the same speed as Wall Street firms and wealthy insiders paying for access… [E]arly access to President Trump’s social media posts for Wall Street firms, wealthy insiders, and high-frequency traders will erode investor confidence in basic fairness of the markets,” wrote the Senators.

“Trump Media’s plan to disseminate market-moving information through the President’s own company, while charging insiders for access ahead of the public for the benefit of his company—and to the detriment of the investing public—represents a shocking abuse of the office of the President and the trust of the American public for his personal gain…This announcement is just the latest example of the President mixing his personal business ventures with his presidential affairs,” the Senators concluded.

The Senators called on the SEC to immediately launch an investigation to determine whether the proposed arrangement violates federal securities law, and they requested answers to their questions ahead of Truth Media’s August 1 launch of their new service.

title: NEWS: Sen. Schiff’s Bill to Designate National Scenic Trail Advances Unanimously from Senate Committee
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources unanimously advanced U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.)’s legislation to help designate the 550+ mile Bay Area Ridge Trail as a National Scenic Trail. This designation would enhance the trail’s visibility as a world-class recreation opportunity and attract new visitors, in addition to helping connect the different routes within the trail.

“The Bay Area Ridge Trail gives visitors to the Bay Area and its residents the opportunity to enjoy more than 500 miles of some of California’s most incredible outdoor beauty, including parks and preserves. Providing federal recognition to this ridgeline trail will help preserve it for future generations, and I’m proud to see colleagues – on both sides of the aisle – support this effort,” said Senator Schiff.

The legislation requires the National Park Service to complete the required feasibility study in consultation with the Bay Area Ridge Trail Council and relevant federal, state, and tribal agencies. The trail meets all the required criteria established in the National Trails System Act of 1968 for National Scenic Trail designation, including:

Extended trail route of more than 100 miles

Provides maximum outdoor recreation potential

Provides for enjoyment of nationally significant scenic, historic, and cultural qualities

Represents desert, marsh, grassland, mountain, canyon, river, and forest

Represents landforms that exhibit significant regional geographic characteristics

Connects with side trails, which provide additional public access

The legislation is led by U.S. Representative Jared Huffman (D-Calif.-02) in the U.S. House of Representatives and is cosponsored by U.S. Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) and every member of the Bay Area delegation.

The full text of the legislation is available here.

title: Schmitt Secures Major Victory for 442d Fighter Wing and Whiteman Air Force Base
text:
U.S. SENATE — Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO), a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, issued the following statement following news the U.S. Air Force would recapitalize the 442d Fighter Wing at Whiteman Air Force Base in Johnson County, Missouri. The announcement follows Senator Schmitt’s advocacy to maintain the Fighter Wing, which has decades of proven combat experience and cost-effective operations.

“This is a major victory for the 442d Fighter Wing, for Missouri, and for our national security. As one of the most historic and highly decorated Fighter Wings in our nation’s history, it carries a storied history and a legacy that has become emblematic of America’s military superiority. However, this legacy didn’t come from nowhere—it is built upon the expertise and knowledge of airmen and engineers who made the A-10 fighter aircraft fleet one of the most lethal in the world, driving countless counterterrorism operations and ensuring America’s aerial dominance. Since my first days in the Senate, I’ve been fighting for the future of this mission, and last year, I wrote to Secretary Hegseth urging him to recapitalize the 442d at Whiteman Air Force Base and ensure decades of combat and operational experience stay in Missouri while keeping our homeland safe. I am proud to see the 442d and the brave patriots who serve in it will continue to protect our skies and carry the legacy of our nation’s heroes,” said Senator Schmitt.

In August 2025, Schmitt sent a letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth to reiterate the value of the 442d Fighter Wing. In the letter, Schmitt urged Secretary Hegseth to recapitalize the fighter mission.

title: Senator Schmitt Celebrates Committee Passage of His Bipartisan Gateway Partnership Act
text:
Bill Creates More Opportunities for Gateway Arch National Park to Benefit St. Louis Communities

U.S. SENATE — Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) praised passage of his bill, the bipartisan Gateway Partnership Act, through the Senate Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. Senator Schmitt’s bill would authorize the Gateway Arch National Park to enter into an agreement with the Gateway Arch Park Foundation allowing the Foundation to manage private events on Park property.

“The Gateway Arch is not just an impressive piece of engineering on the banks of the Mississippi River. This beloved monument helps tell the story of a nation. The Arch’s 630‑foot stainless‑steel arc rises over the very river where a young republic once looked west and saw not just wilderness, but destiny. But for my hometown, the Arch is not simply a relic of the past. It is the front door of the American West, and a symbol of our heritage. And over the last decade, the people of St. Louis proved just how much that monument means to them. Through the City-Arch-River project—a hometown partnership that turned into largest private investment in a national park project to date—Gateway Arch National Park is now, more than ever before, a place to meet, gather, celebrate, and remember. Getting this bill across the finish line will allow visitors from all over to enjoy the Gateway Arch and encourage growth for the St. Louis region,” said Senator Schmitt.

Senator Schmitt originally introduced the Gateway Partnership Act in 2025; Rep. Wesley Bell (R-MO) introduced a companion bill in the House of Representatives.

The Gateway Arch National Park is Missouri’s most visited landmark, drawing more than two million visitors annually.

This legislation will allow the Gateway Arch Park Foundation to assist the Gateway Arch National Park by formally managing private event execution and marketing on behalf of the Park.

As the only National Park located inside a major city, Gateway Arch National Park is uniquely positioned as a prime location for private events in St. Louis. Projections show a potential annual revenue of $780,000 generated from private events under this proposed partnership, all of which will be reinvested into the park.

Schumer: Trump Promised Lower Costs—Then Stuck Families With The Bill

U.S. Senator Chuck Schumer today unveiled a new report from the U.S. Congress Joint Economic Committee showing that New York families have paid more than $4,500 extra for everyday essentials—including groceries, gas, housing, and healthcare—since President Trump took office. New Yorkers are bearing the cost of failed policies, including tariffs, cuts to vital programs like SNAP and Medicaid, and a reckless war in Iran that has driven up food and fuel prices, putting even greater strain on the budgets of Upstate New York families.

“New Yorkers are paying the price for President Trump’s disastrous policies, including rash tariffs and a reckless war. From groceries and gas to housing and healthcare, families are being squeezed by rising costs,” said Senator Schumer. “President Trump promised to lower costs, but instead, working- and middle-class families across Upstate New York are left to foot the bill and pay more while he pads his own bank account. We need real solutions that lower costs and deliver the relief people need—not the constant chaos, cost hikes, and corruption coming from the Trump administration.”

According to district-by-district data, households in New York's 17th Congressional District have spent an estimated $122 million more on gas since the start of Trump’s Iran war, with the average family paying an additional $504. Similar increases have affected neighboring communities, with families in NY-18 paying an estimated $535 more and those in NY-19 paying an estimated $547 more.

Schumer said, “Whether commuting to work, driving kids to summer camp, or making a trip to the grocery store, rising fuel costs from this reckless war are requiring families to stretch tight budgets.”

Schumer has forced a series of votes on a war powers resolution, including this week, to end Trump’s costly war and the ongoing chaos in the Straits of Hormuz that sent gas prices soaring.

Families are also facing shock at the checkout counter, where they are paying an estimated $310 more for groceries than they did a year ago. Since Trump took office, the average price of ground beef has climbed nearly every month, reaching a record high of almost $7 per pound. To help tackle these costs, Schumer introduced his Family Grocery and Farmer Relief Act, landmark legislation that would break up meatpacking monopolies, restore competition, cut out corporate greed, and deliver relief to families struggling to put food on the table.

Even after leaving the store, New Yorkers can't escape rising costs. Back at home, New York families have paid an estimated $983 more for housing costs, including rent and mortgage payments, since Trump took office, while also contending with record-high utility bills. To help address this crisis, Schumer championed the bipartisan ROAD to Housing Act, which President Trump then refused to sign into law. This legislation is a first step towards ending the housing affordability crisis and ensuring Americans don’t have to break the bank to keep a roof over their head.

Despite President Trump’s repeated pledges on the campaign trail that his administration would “end inflation” and bring down costs, Trump has instead sent prices through the roof. In recent months, Schumer has rolled out a series of plans to counter Trump’s failed policies and lower the costs of housing, food, energy, and health care. The report from the U.S. Congress Joint Economic Committee breaks down how much New York families are paying.

title: Sen. Tim Scott honors the late Sen. Lindsey Graham in tribute at Columbia funeral
text:
COLUMBIA, S.C. — U.S. Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.) paid his respects to his friend and colleague, the late Sen. Lindsey Graham, in a tribute during a funeral service in Columbia today. Sen. Scott joined the late senator’s friends, family, and colleagues to honor Sen. Graham’s life and legacy of service.

It is good to be home in South Carolina. We love when the world celebrates our heroes, but it is so good to come home to South Carolina. I miss home. And when we feel pain in our hearts, Richard, we need to be home surrounded by people who love us, who know us, who care for us. We are deeply, deeply sorry for your loss.

To the Graham staffers, thank you. Thank you for stepping up to the plate. Thank you for protecting and insulating the Graham family. Thank you for going the extra mile. It has been a long two plus weeks.

To the Graham family, may the Lord continue to bless you with the strength and the courage that you need to pull together, because this celebration will end in the next day, or two or three, but the wounds won’t go away so quickly. I know you’ll be there for each other.

Darline, what a powerful, grace-filled person to watch you under immense pressure show up and show out is a blessing to South Carolina. I see we’ve got some Presbyterians over here. Praise the Lord. Hallelujah! That was good. That’s good. Good, good, good. Even the Presbyterians step up here and dance in the Baptist church. Someone should say Amen. Never mind.

It is good to be here. I haven’t been here in a couple of years, and we certainly miss Pastor Estep, but it’s good to see him here. I will simply say this that I am going to miss my friend Lindsey Graham, the congressmember who becomes a senator, who becomes a world leader, statesman without any question.

I am going to miss my friend Lindsey Graham. I remember Lindsey had great humor and a lot of wit too right. And so I’ll never forget at my wedding, this Monday will be two years ago, sweetheart. I remember our anniversary is coming up on August the 3rd. Always helpful to remember that. Lindsey’s at our wedding. I only invited three or four senators, and Lindsey is talking to this little kid named Case, and Case is in the arms of one of the parents. And Lindsey leans in and says, “Case, I’m so sorry, buddy, there will be no Social Security for you.”

Sean, it really happened, brother. It really happened. And it was the kind of moment that everybody just, all the adults, bursted out laughing and poor little Case was like what’s Social Security?

I also, President Trump talked about this yesterday, but I think it’s worth repeating. I started a South Carolina prayer breakfast in D.C., and I will tell you that my first call 15 years ago was to Lindsey Graham.

And at that time, I did not know that Lindsey, much like myself, we really don’t like mornings. And so I called Lindsey and said, “Lindsey, I need you to be there at my prayer breakfast at 8:30 a.m.” Lindsey said, “Have you ever thought about having a prayer lunch or a prayer dinner?” I said, “Lindsey, it’s already set, man, I need you there.”

And he said, “I ain’t coming if Jesus comes before 10 a.m., I am not going to be there.” But Lindsey, committed to his friends, did what I hadn’t seen him do since then. At 8:31 a.m., Lindsey walks through the door Because Lindsey Graham was always committed to his friends, even if it was uncomfortable for him.

I did not realize, however, that Lindsey gave lots of advice to kids.

This was a new revelation for me.

I was talking to Katie Britt, who has two young kids, and she told me that Lindsey actually gave her, Trey, legal advice. The head of the Judiciary Committee giving legal advice to a pretty good attorney in her own right. I had to write this down because I just didn’t believe it.

I said, “Well, what did he say?”

Well, the legal advice he gave to her two kids is simply this. All the kids in the room, listen to most of it.

Don’t sell drugs. On school property. Because the enhanced sentencing guidelines is not worth the risk. That’s good advice. But wow, right?

Second advice he gave, not legal advice, was simply this: kids, never do for yourself what someone else will do for you.

Third piece of advice: if you, he said, get away with as much as you can for as long as you can.

And then one of my personal favorites, I practiced this while I was in school myself. He said, don’t work too hard, just pull your friends down. That’s really good advice. Having failed a couple subjects in high school, Spanish and English, I learned how to do that firsthand.

But the advice I most appreciate from Lindsey, he never spoke to me, he lived it.

First piece of advice, and I hope that it helps you too, number one, get really comfortable being yourself. Get really comfortable being yourself. But in order to get comfortable being yourself, he would say, through his actions and not his words, you’ve got to know yourself. Know why God created you. Jeremiah 1:5 reminds us that God made Jeremiah a prophet before he was even in his mother’s womb. Sometimes to be yourself and comfortable in your own skin, you’ve got to walk alone.

God doesn’t want carbon copies. Lindsey was an original. I would challenge each of us to honor Lindsey Graham by living as originals, God’s imprint on each of us, unique and specific. It reminds me of Romans 12:2 to know the acceptable and perfect will of God.

Second lesson that he demonstrated, I actually like when if you’re not a pastor, or the kind of sermon I like to hear is the one that I can only hear with my eyes and feel in my heart.

Second one was simply this: learn to stand up for those who can’t stand for themselves. Over 60 million Americans will never have their little feet on the soils of our country. Lindsey Graham always fought for life. He was 100% pro-life when it was convenient and when it was not, and he never apologized for it.

If you want to have a conversation about the special needs kids, or if you want to have a conversation about the poor, Lindsey Graham, always, according to Proverbs 31:8, stand up for those who can’t stand for themselves.

Lindsey embodied the spirit of that verse, and he did it every single day in a way that you didn’t have to hear it, because you could see it all the time.

And finally, Romans 10:9-10, you see, I am going to miss Lindsey, but when I get to heaven, it will feel like for just seconds, because I know eternity is real. And Romans 10:9-10 reminds me that if we confess with our hearts and believe, if we confess with our mouth and believe in our hearts that Christ was raised from the dead, you shall be saved. And if you’re saved, you get the benefit of spending eternity with the ones you love the most, like Lindsey Graham.

And I will tell you, having watched the sermon every day, and I will concede sometimes the sermon would come in colorful language – not found in 2 Timothy 1:7, or maybe 3 Timothy, which there is no 3 Timothy, but it’s colorful language sometimes. But Lindsey was always authentically himself.

He always found time to fight for the underdog. And we now all know that he believed in the King of Kings and the Lord of Lords, and the Alpha and the Omega.

Let’s make sure we spend eternity with God Almighty, whose son is Jesus, and our good friends like Lindsey Graham.

###

title: After Months of Pressure from Senator Shaheen, Administration Finally Releases Global Health Funds to Vaccinate Children and Prevent Global Outbreaks
text:
**After pressing both Secretaries Rubio and Kennedy on the stalled distribution, Shaheen helped facilitate the release of $600 million in Congressional appropriations to Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance**

(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Foreign Relations Committee, celebrated the release of $600 million in Congressionally-appropriated funds for Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, that was previously withheld by U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) Robert F. Kennedy, Jr. Shaheen facilitated negotiations between HHS and Gavi to help achieve this outcome and sustained public pressure on the Administration to end their blockade of life-saving resources.

“I am glad that the Administration finally announced it would release the $600 million Congress directed to Gavi, ending a months-long, unnecessary stalemate based on baseless obstructionism from Secretary Kennedy. Gavi supports American manufacturing jobs, it helps prevent outbreaks from reaching the United States’ shores and it strengthens global health; since its founding, it has prevented more than 20 million deaths. This resolution, despite being long overdue, is welcome news for global health security,” said Senator Shaheen. “In the context of a raging Ebola epidemic that is growing, this funding is urgently needed to support efforts led by Gavi to enable mass production of a vaccine to treat this lethal strain of Ebola that currently has no cure. I look forward to continuing to conduct rigorous oversight to ensure that the Department of State obligates all $600 million as intended.”

In April, Shaheen demanded answers from U.S. Secretary of Health and Human Services Robert F. Kennedy Jr. as to why crucial global health vaccine funding has not been delivered despite being appropriated by Congress. Specifically, highlighting that millions of children could die if the funding wasn’t fulfilled, Shaheen pressed Secretary Kennedy about whether he was knowingly blocking funding that helps vaccinate millions of children and prevents global health outbreaks. Secretary Kennedy agreed to appoint someone to work with Gavi and Shaheen’s office to reach a solution.

In May, Shaheen led a group of bipartisan lawmakers urging the State Department to restore U.S. contributions to Gavi. Last month, Shaheen again raised the issue with U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio in the context of the current Ebola outbreak, to which Gavi has committed up to $40 million for promising vaccine candidates. Secretary Rubio expressed that he would like to re-engage in resolving the funding impasse.

title: Shaheen Raises Concerns About USDA Rural Development Reorganization
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH), a senior member of the U.S. Senate Appropriations Committee and Ranking Member of the Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration and Related Agencies (Ag-FDA) Appropriations Subcommittee, joined her colleagues in raising strong concerns about the plan to reorganize the Rural Development mission area at the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA). The letter was led by Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN), Ranking Member of the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, and Peter Welch (D-VT), Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Rural Development, Energy, and Credit.

The Senators wrote, in part: “We write with significant concern regarding the reorganization of the Rural Development mission area at the U.S. Department of Agriculture. Rural communities, small businesses, and families will lose access to important services if the proposed reorganization plan moves forward. Rural Development is a unique division within the Department, supporting agriculture and ensuring that rural communities prosper by administering grants and loans to support rural businesses, providing financial support for rural housing, financing the construction of rural health clinics and daycare centers, and championing critical infrastructure projects for water, electric, or broadband.”

They continued: “In order for rural communities to benefit from these projects, the Rural Development agency must have the capacity to process applications and disburse funds. The mission area has already lost about 36 percent of its staff last year, with nearly a third of those who left having more than 20 years of USDA experience. The reorganization plan for Rural Development will result in even further cuts, with 60 percent of staff in the National Capital Region being required to relocate to St. Louis or Dallas […] Rural Development’s depletion of staff has already left rural America without the support it needs as the prices of gas, groceries, and agricultural inputs are skyrocketing as a result of tariffs and foreign conflicts. Without adequate and expert staff, the money that Congress has appropriated to help rural communities will not reach its intended beneficiaries.”

The full letter can be read HERE.

As Ranking Member of the Ag-FDA Appropriations Subcommittee, Senator Shaheen has been outspoken about the misguided plans by the Trump Administration to reorganize USDA. Shaheen successfully pushed back against the closure of New Hampshire’s Hubbard Brook and Bartlett Experimental Forests as part of the reorganization of the U.S. Forest Service earlier this year. Following conversations with Secretary Rollins and New Hampshire Governor Kelly Ayotte, Shaheen secured confirmation that the U.S. Forest Service (USFS) would not close New Hampshire’s Hubbard Brook Experimental Forest and a commitment from Secretary Rollins to review plans at Bartlett Experimental Forest.

title: Sullivan, Murkowski, Hickenlooper Introduce Legislation to Permanently Authorize NSF Office of Polar Programs
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Senator Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), along with Senators Lisa Murkowski (R-Alaska) and John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), have introduced the Promoting Operational Leadership in Arctic and Antarctic Research (POLAR) Act, legislation that will permanently authorize the National Science Foundation (NSF) Office of Polar Programs (OPP) and reinforce NSF’s leadership and Alaska’s role in advancing U.S. interests in polar research and development through education, workforce development, and critical research infrastructure. The bill will strengthen the United States’ ability to observe, understand, and predict the physical, biological, and geological processes in polar regions by supporting informed decision-making, navigational safety, national security, and the long-term resilience of Alaska’s communities.

“In the past few years, we’ve begun to realize a vision I’ve championed for Alaska as an intellectual research hub, anchored by our world-class universities and the major research institutions that have been coming to our state,” said Sen. Sullivan. “The National Science Foundation’s Office of Polar Programs is one piece of this vision, supporting innovative and creative scientific research in Earth’s polar regions and funding Alaska’s Arctic research institutes, which are critical to the preparedness and resilience of arctic communities and strengthening both America’s national security and Arctic defense. This week, Senators Murkowski, Hickenlooper, and I introduced legislation to make this office permanent. Our legislation will secure the polar sciences’ place among other leading scientific fields, clarify how much funding goes to Arctic versus Antarctic research, and strengthen the office that provides the majority of the National Science Foundation’s funding to the University of Alaska Arctic research system for years to come.”

“As the Arctic grows in strategic importance, the United States must continue investing in the research, infrastructure, and expertise needed to strengthen our understanding of this rapidly changing region,” said Sen. Murkowski. “The National Science Foundation's Office of Polar Programs has long provided the scientific and logistical foundation for American leadership in the Arctic and Antarctica. By establishing the Office as a permanent directorate within NSF, the POLAR Act ensures our nation is better positioned to advance critical research, support national security, and maintain U.S. leadership in the polar regions. It also reinforces the University of Alaska's role as our nation's premier Arctic research institution and a cornerstone of America's Arctic future. I appreciate Senator Sullivan's leadership and the close partnership with the University of Alaska in developing this legislation.”

“As a geologist, I’ve seen how research drives discovery and innovation,” said Sen. Hickenlooper. “Colorado is a global leader in atmospheric and polar research, and elevating NSF’s polar programs will support the groundbreaking work happening right here in our backyard.”

“The University of Alaska system extends deep gratitude to Senator Dan Sullivan (R-AK) for introducing the Promoting Operational Leadership in Arctic and Antarctic Research Act or the POLAR Act,” said Michelle Rizk, Interim President, University of Alaska System. “We also commend Senator John Hickenlooper (D-CO) for joining Senator Sullivan on this important legislation. By elevating the National Science Foundation's (NSF) Office of Polar Programs to a full Directorate, this bill raises polar science to its rightful place alongside other important areas of science, including engineering, computer science, biology, and mathematics. NSF is the largest federal sponsor of UA research, and polar programs fund more research than any other component of NSF. We are grateful for Senator Sullivan's leadership in supporting NSF and working to strengthen its polar and Arctic research programs. We look forward to the timely passage of the POLAR Act.”

“As America’s Arctic University, we are very appreciative and supportive of the legislation proposed by Senators Sullivan and Hickenlooper to address the critical need for knowledge of the polar regions,” said Dr. Larry Hinzman, Interim Chancellor, University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF). “The U.S. and international Arctic and Antarctic research and policy communities know that such investments are essential to help our nation address challenges related to food, energy and national security, as well as providing greater understanding of space physics, climate dynamics and oceanic processes. The Promoting Operational Leadership in Arctic and Antarctic Research Act (POLAR) is a vital step in the right direction.”

BACKGROUND:

The University of Alaska Fairbanks (UAF) is a world-class intellectual hub for Arctic research, Unmanned Aerial Systems, and cold weather innovation. Senator Sullivan has been a longtime advocate for UAF, recently securing critical funding and partnerships to grow the university’s Arctic research programs.

In July 2026, following Sen. Sullivan’s advocacy, NSF announced that the Alaska Critical Mineral Collaborative (ACMC), led by UAF, was selected as one of the new NSF Regional Innovation Engines. The Critical Mineral Accelerator Engine could bring up to $160 million in funding to Alaska over the next 10 years and will help advance critical mineral development, innovation and collaboration, across Alaska and the United States.

In May 2026, Sen. Sullivan secured a 3-year agreement between UAF and the Department of War’s Defense Innovation Unit (DIU). The collaboration will fast-track the developments and production of technologies to support the U.S. military, initially focusing on energy, hypersonics, drone operations, remote sensing, and space systems.

title: Thune Discusses the Importance of Russia Sanctions Legislation
text:
Click here to watch the video.

WASHINGTON — U.S. Senate Majority Leader John Thune (R-S.D.) today spoke at a press conference with Senate Republican leadership:

Thune’s remarks below (as delivered):

“With the tragic and sudden passing of Senator Graham, the Democrats and Republicans in the Senate have joined together to cosponsor the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026.

“It’s legislation that I hope we can move across the floor.

“It was probably, I would say, in Lindsey’s last days, the thing he cared most passionately about.

“It’s something he’s worked on for the past year, and I think we all, both Democrats and Republicans, realize not only would this be a great tribute to him and his work and his legacy on national security matters, but it would also be something that would really give the president a tool at his disposal to try and end the war in Ukraine.

“Ukraine is now the largest conflict, literally, since World War II in Europe.

“And the Ukrainian people have been resilient, worked really, really hard to try and bring this war to an end.

“But as long as Putin has Russian oil and gas money, he’s able to continue this war.

“And what this sanctions bill would do would basically cut that off.

“And Lindsey also cared passionately, as you know, about the Middle East, and so the sanctions on Iran, I think, complement what’s in the underlying bill.

“But the fact is, there are 62 cosponsors on the bill.

“We had a motion to proceed vote on it yesterday that got 86 votes in the Senate.

“It is a bipartisan bill.

“It’s an important bill for this country and for our national security interests, and it’s something that I hope we can proceed with and ultimately pass, get across the finish line here in the next few days.”

title: Tuberville, Blackburn Call for Men to Stay out of Daughters of the American Revolution
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) joined U.S. Senator Marsha Blackburn (R-Al) in introducing the Daughters of the American Revolution Membership Integrity Act, which would amend the Daughters of the American Revolution’s (DAR) federal charter by adding a membership eligibility requirement to ban biological men from becoming members.

This comes as the DAR has made headlines for adding a “non-discrimination” clause that allows biological males to become members.

“There’s a reason the founders of this group named it the DAUGHTERS of the American Revolution,” said Sen. Tuberville. “They had the common sense to recognize what a woman is; unlike the woke Left that apparently doesn’t understand the differences between female and male anatomy. Alabama has over 4,000 members in the DAR, and they shouldn’t have to be putting up with this woke nonsense. Amending the eligibility requirements to reflect the founders’ vision is something all of my colleagues should be able to get behind.”

“The Daughters of the American Revolution was founded by women for women, and its founders would be appalled that the organization is now allowing biological males to become members and undermine the legacy of real women who helped build our nation,” said Sen. Blackburn. “The Daughters of the American Revolution Membership Integrity Act would amend the DAR’s federal charter to stop the organization from erasing biological reality and ensure it is reserved for the real daughters of the American Revolution.”

Sens. Tuberville and Blackburn were joined by Sens. Katie Britt (R-AL), Kevin Cramer (R-ND), and Mike Lee (R-UT) in cosponsoring the legislation. U.S. Representative Ben Cline (R-VA-06) led companion legislation in the U.S. House of Representatives earlier this month.

Heritage Action, Concerned Women for America Action Committee, American Principles Project, Senior Legal Counsel for Independent Women, and the Alliance Defending Freedom endorsed the legislation.

Read full text of the bill here.

BACKGROUND:

The DAR adopted a non-discrimination provision that its current leadership has interpreted to allow men masquerading as women to become members. This bill would amend the DAR’s federal charter to add an eligibility requirement that limits membership to an individual that is a woman and otherwise satisfies the genealogical and membership qualifications established by the corporation.

Senator Tommy Tuberville represents Alabama in the United States Senate and is a member of the Senate Armed Services, Agriculture, Veterans’ Affairs, HELP and Aging Committees.

title: Van Hollen Joins Ossoff, Colleagues in Pressuring Trump Administration to Release HIV/AIDS Prevention Funding to CDC
text:
U.S. Senator Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) joined Senator Jon Ossoff (D-Ga.) and over 10 Senate colleagues in urging Secretary of State Marco Rubio to approve the transfer of $2 billion in funds meant for the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) to the CDC. This inquiry comes as new internal guidance by the State Department would end the transfer of PEPFAR funds to the CDC. According to former CDC Directors, without this dedicated funding stream, more than 18 CDC outposts could close before the end of the year, reducing the ability for the agency to launch timely and sufficient global health responses to disease outbreaks.

Senators Van Hollen and Ossoff are joined by Senators Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Ben Ray Lujan (D-N.M.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), and Ed Markey (D-Mass.).

“The rushed abandonment of a proven and effective structure threatens to increase the risk of future global health pandemics and disease outbreaks,” the Senators wrote. “Countries are struggling to maintain the programs set up by USAID and PEPFAR funding, facing more new infections and more deaths.”

“We urge you to immediately rescind any guidance suggesting that State will no longer honor the transfer of $2 billion to CDC and commit to upholding this long-standing transfer that keeps Americans safe,” the Senators continued.

The full text of the letter is available here and below:

Dear Secretary Rubio,

We write to you with alarm at the Administration’s cut to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC)’s global HIV/AIDs program. This decision is particularly troubling as these funds allow CDC to implement the President’s Emergency Plan For AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and support CDC’s critical global health operations that have provided the backbone for PEPFAR and other U.S. global health programs for decades.1 The rushed abandonment of a proven and effective structure threatens to increase the risk of future global health pandemics and disease outbreaks which is wholly antithetical to an America First Global Health Strategy.

Not only does the proposed fee-for-service mechanism threaten to severely gut PEPFAR efficacy and further hinder CDC’s work identifying and mitigating health threats at their source, which is especially alarming given the expanding outbreak of the novel strain of Ebola, but the Administration also seems to be leveraging these agreements for concessions not related to global health, such as for negotiating access to critical minerals.2 This type of coercive diplomacy does not serve U.S. global health interests and is extremely susceptible to risk of corruption.

Therefore, we urge you to immediately rescind any guidance suggesting that State will no longer honor the transfer of $2 billion to CDC and commit to upholding this long-standing transfer that keeps Americans safe. We also ask you to respond to the following questions by August 11th , 2026:

1. What specific problem or concern is State attempting to address through the proposed fee-for-service model?

a. Did State consider alternative approaches? If so, why were these options rejected?

b. What measurable improvements does State expect to achieve with these changes?

c. What are the projected costs of implementing these changes?

2. Please describe the currently proposed timeline for implementation of this new fee-forservice system for FY27.

a. If a country has not signed an MOU purchasing CDC services before State implements this new system, will funding for CDC infrastructure within that partner country be terminated?

b. Please explain the rationale for moving forward with the proposed fee-for-service model that risks undermining CDC’s presence and programs overseas, such as the closure of at least 18 CDC global outposts close before the end of the year, before MOU negotiations are finalized and implementation plans are in place?3

c. Given CDC’s significant presence and infrastructure in both the Democratic Republic of the Congo and Uganda, and the current Ebola outbreak, are there any plans to delay the implementation of this new system until which time the outbreak has been contained, and CDC technical expertise and resources do not need to be surged?

3. How does the State Department intend to bridge the funding gap that will likely occur between the maximum value of CDC services a country could purchase under the fee schedule, and CDC’s necessary PEPFAR operating budget for that country?

a. If there is no intention to bridge this funding gap, please describe any analysis State Department undertook highlighting potential consequences and operational gaps resulting from this gap in funds.

b. If countries are not able to meet their financial commitments, what mitigation efforts is State putting in place to ensure that programming can still continue?

c. How will State ensure that CDC technical expertise is utilized to the maximum possible capacity?

d. Please describe any analysis State did of the risk of service disruption that could occur during the transition.

e. Has State modeled the potential effects on HIV infections, AIDS-related deaths, tuberculosis outcomes, malaria outcomes, or other health indicators? f. How will continuity of care be protected for patients receiving treatment supported by CDC implemented programs?

4. How many CDC personnel will be impacted by this change, including U.S. direct hires and locally-employed staff?

a. What, if anything, is State doing to ensure a minimum number of CDC staff is maintained overseas?

5. In light of the current Ebola outbreak, CDC has surged resources and is providing strategic and technical assistance with disease tracking and contact tracing, risk communication and community engagement, infection prevention and control, among other resources.4 Under this new system, will partner countries be required to pay additional fees for these additional services if a global health outbreak occurs?

6. Will the State Department commit to sharing with Congress the implementation plans of MOUs already signed with partner countries, and any additional MOU that the Administration signs, within 30 days of signature?

a. Will the Administration continue to pursue negotiations on other non-health related topics as part of these bilateral health agreements?

Following this Administration’s dismantlement of USAID, a key implementor of PEPFAR programming, countries are struggling to maintain the programs set up by USAID and PEPFAR funding, facing more new infections and more deaths.5 Without USAID, CDC’s global health infrastructure remains the most effective tool the U.S. has to monitor and prevent global health emergencies. Ceasing the transfer of these funds only further puts the lives of Americans at risk.

Sincerely,

title: Warner, Kaine, and Subramanyam Applaud Major Investment to Dulles
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) and U.S. Rep. Suhas Subramanyam (D-VA-10) applauded an announcement from the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority (MWAA) and United Airlines to invest at least $20 billion to upgrade Washington Dulles International Airport.

“These investments by United and MWAA will help Dulles service almost double the number of planes, passengers, and visitors,” said Sen. Warner. “Dulles will not only be an international gateway to our nation’s capital, Virginia, and the East Coast, but become a destination itself. I look forward to working with United Airlines, MWAA, the Commonwealth, the Department of Transportation, and all other partners to get this done.”

“I’m thrilled that United Airlines is making a significant investment to accelerate improvements at Dulles Airport,” said Sen. Kaine. “I’ve been proud of what we’ve accomplished together so far to grow and improve safety at Dulles, and make it easier for people to get to and from there by extending the Silver Line. I look forward to seeing how these improvements will modernize the airport, improve the customer experience, expand capacity, and grow the region’s economy. I’ll continue working with our partners to make Dulles the premier airport on the East Coast.”

“This investment will bring more jobs to our community and boost our local economy. And by modernizing the airport, it will help Dulles maintain its status as a world-class airport with a better experience for travelers and more flight options for Virginians,” said Rep. Subramanyam. “I will continue to work with MWAA, United, and Dulles employees to make sure this project benefits our community.”

Warner, Kaine, and Subramanyam have secured significant investments in Dulles Airport, including funding for safety improvements and the construction of Concourse E. Warner and Kaine also played a significant role in expanding the Silver Line Metrorail, which includes a stop at Dulles. The Dulles Airport Metro Station has surpassed 5.7 million customer trips since it opened in 2022 and is the busiest stop of the Silver Line Phase II extension.

title: Warner, Kaine Applaud Senate Committee Passage of Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) applauded the Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee’s passage of the bipartisan, bicameral Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act, which would issue a right-of-way to add an emergency route and road to enhance public safety in Wintergreen, Virginia. The legislation now heads to the full Senate. It passed the House of Representatives earlier this year.

“Wintergreen residents and visitors only have one road to enter and exit, creating a serious public safety risk in the event of a natural disaster or another crisis,” said the senators. “We’re glad that the Senate advanced our bipartisan, bicameral legislation to help pave the way for a new road in and out of Wintergreen and improve safety. We urge the full Senate to pass it and send it to the President’s desk to be signed into law.”

Wintergreen is a popular tourist destination off the Blue Ridge Parkway in Nelson County, but it has only one entrance and exit road, creating a serious safety risk for residents and visitors during a natural disaster or emergency. Specifically, the Wintergreen Emergency Egress Act would direct the Secretary of the Interior to authorize the construction of a new emergency route while minimizing the disturbance on National Park Service land.

###

title: Warner, Kaine, Colleagues Lead Bipartisan Effort to Expand Shenandoah Valley National Battlefields Historic District
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Sens. Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) joined Sens. Jim Justice and Shelley Moore Capito (both R-WV) in introducing the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District Boundary Expansion and Partnership Act of 2026, landmark bipartisan legislation that would add Rockbridge County, Virginia, and three counties in West Virginia to the district.

The Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District, which consists of eight counties in Virginia’s Shenandoah Valley, was created by Congress in 1996. It recognizes the region’s nationally significant Civil War battlefields and associated historic sites.

“The Shenandoah Valley helped shape our nation’s history, and preserving these battlefields will ensure that future generations can better understand the sacrifices and defining moments that took place there during the Civil War,” said Sen. Warner. “By expanding the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District to include additional sites in Virginia and West Virginia, this bipartisan legislation will boost local tourism and protect our historical landscapes.”

“The Shenandoah Valley Battlefields National Historic District is one of Virginia’s great historical treasures, preserving the Valley’s Civil War battlefields so that Americans from across the country can visit them and reflect on our country’s history,” said Sen. Kaine. “I’m proud to support this bipartisan legislation to expand the district into Rockbridge County and strengthen the partnerships that protect these valued sites for years to come.”

Over the past three decades, the Shenandoah Valley Battlefields Foundation has preserved over 8,000 acres of land while supporting the development of visitor centers, museums, educational programs, and interpretative resources that make the Valley’s rich Civil War history accessible to all Americans.

###

title: Warnock Joins Bipartisan Effort to Strengthen Whistleblower Incentives
text:
Senator Reverend Raphael Warnock joined a bipartisan coalition to enhance protections for whistleblowers

Since taking office, Senator Warnock has championed legislation to protect whistleblowers from retaliation

Senator Reverend Warnock: “This bipartisan bill promotes accountability and bolsters essential protections for people who risk their careers to stand up to fraud and corruption”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Chuck Grassley (R-IA), John Fetterman (D-PA), and Susan Collins (R-ME) introduced the CFTC Whistleblower Protection and Program Improvement Act of 2026 to provide long-term stability for the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) whistleblower program, strengthen whistleblower protections, and expedite award processing.

“No one should be punished for speaking out when they see something wrong. This bipartisan bill promotes accountability and bolsters essential protections for people who risk their careers to stand up to fraud and corruption,” said Senator Warnock. “This legislation will benefit every American taxpayer, and I’m grateful to work with my colleagues across the aisle to strengthen this vital program.”

“Since I helped get the CFTC whistleblower program up and running, I’m pleased to see it’s been a big success,” said Senator Grassley. “This program roots out waste, fraud and abuse in the commodities trading industry and operates at no charge to the taxpayer. Now, it’s time for Congress to act so its success can continue. Our bipartisan legislation strengthens protections for patriotic whistleblowers, prevents unnecessary delays in the disbursement of whistleblower awards and ensures the CFTC whistleblower program can operate smoothly.”

“Whistleblowers put their jobs and often their lives on the line to call out the most serious offenses in the workplace. Zero doubt that they should be protected,” said Senator Fetterman. “As a member of the Agriculture Committee, I’m proud to introduce this bipartisan bill with Senator Grassley to protect whistleblowers and improve the CFTC whistleblower program.”

“The Commodity Futures Trading Commission plays a crucial role in protecting American commodity markets, and safeguarding its whistleblower program helps maintain public trust in the integrity of those markets,” said Senator Collins. “This bipartisan bill would provide long-term stability for the CFTC whistleblower program by strengthening protections for whistleblowers, promoting the timely processing of claims, and eliminating a loophole that can prevent whistleblowers from receiving awards.”

The CFTC Whistleblower Program and Customer Protection Fund (CPF) rewards whistleblowers for reporting allegations of wrongdoing to the CFTC using funds collected through enforcement actions. The CPF also covers the operating expenses and educational initiatives that support the CFTC Whistleblower Program. Since 2014, the CFTC Whistleblower Program has awarded nearly $430 million to whistleblowers and issued over $3.7 billion in monetary sanctions.

Senator Warnock has long championed efforts to bolster protections for whistleblowers. In December 2022, he successfully secured bipartisan support for the Anti-Money Laundering Whistleblower Improvement Act, which strengthened and expanded the scope of whistleblower reporting standards and financial rewards. Less than a year later, Senator Warnock introduced the SEC Whistleblower Reform Act of 2023 to ensure timely processing of whistleblower claims and protect against retaliation.

###

title: Warnock, Wicker Introduce Bipartisan Bill to Modernize Tire Safety Standards
text:
Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock and Roger Wicker introduced the Tire Safety Modernization Act of 2026 legislation to modernize federal tire safety standards

Georgia is a national leader in tire manufacturing and production

Senator Reverend Warnock: “Georgia’s nation-leading tire manufacturing industry helps keep Georgians safe and connected to boundless opportunities”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) and Roger Wicker (R-MS) introduced the bipartisan Tire Safety Modernization Act of 2026, a bill that updates federal tire testing standards to protect passenger safety and reflect modern best practices in tire production.

“Georgia’s nation-leading tire manufacturing industry helps keep Georgians safe and connected to boundless opportunities,” said Senator Warnock. “By modernizing this critical manufacturing sector, we can help foster innovation and keep Americans connected.”

“Tire manufacturing technology has evolved, but federal regulations have not kept pace,” said Senator Wicker. “This legislation would update performance standards—protecting passenger safety and promoting innovation simultaneously.”

The Tire Safety Modernization Act of 2026 preserves a strong focus on safety. The bill directs the Department of Transportation to replace outdated testing requirements with more relevant, modern-day performance standards, clarifying existing safety criteria and aligning high-speed testing with internationally recognized best practices to keep our roads safe.

Senator Warnock has successfully delivered millions of dollars’ worth of federal grant funding to improve roadway safety across Georgia. Last year, he led an effort to improve access to economic opportunity by investing in transportation infrastructure that is essential to keeping communities connected.

The Tire Safety Modernization Act of 2026 is endorsed by the U.S. Tire Manufacturers Association (USTMA) and several tire manufacturing companies with operational hubs located in Georgia, including Pirelli, Toyo Tire Holdings of Americas Inc., Kumho Tire USA, Inc., Continental Tire Americas, and Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company.

“Modernizing federal tire safety standards is essential to ensuring American drivers have access to the safest, most advanced tire technology available,” said Anne Forristall Luke, president and CEO of U.S. Tire Manufacturers Association (USTMA). “The ‘Tire Safety Modernization Act’ is an important step toward aligning U.S. regulations with today’s innovations, strengthening road safety and supporting a more competitive tire manufacturing sector. USTMA and its member companies are grateful to Senators Warnock (D-GA) and Wicker (R-MS) for their leadership in championing this critical legislation.”

“Toyo Tire commends Senators Raphael Warnock and Roger Wicker for introducing legislation that will help modernize federal tire safety testing requirements,” said Tatsuo Mitsuhata, Chairman & CEO, Toyo Tire Holdings of Americas Inc. “Operating the largest tire factory in Georgia, Toyo understands the importance of maintaining a regulatory framework that supports both consumer safety and continued innovation in American manufacturing. This legislation represents a practical and forward-looking effort to ensure that federal tire standards keep pace with advances in vehicle and tire technology. We appreciate the leadership of Senators Warnock and Wicker in advancing this bipartisan effort and look forward to working with policymakers and industry stakeholders as the legislation moves forward.”

“Kumho Tire USA, headquartered in Atlanta and serving customers through a nationwide distribution network, is grateful to Senators Warnock and Wicker for their leadership in introducing legislation to modernize federal tire safety testing standards,” said Edmund Cho, CEO of Kumho Tire USA, Inc. “With manufacturing and distribution operations, including facilities in Georgia, we support updating FMVSS tire tests to remove outdated requirements and align with global best practices, strengthening public safety and ensuring a fair, level playing field for responsible manufacturers.”

“The introduction of this legislation by Senators Warnock and Wicker represents meaningful progress toward modernizing tire safety regulations,” said Tansu Işık, CEO Continental Tire Americas. “Aligning federal testing requirements with today’s technological advancements will help ensure effective safety oversight while promoting innovation and manufacturing growth in the United States.

“For the Pirelli Group, which has manufacturing facilities in Georgia and is the exclusive tire supplier to the Formula One World Championship™, safety is paramount,” said Pirelli. “Modernizing tire testing requirements will help ensure that federal testing standards continue to foster innovation, recognize the industry’s most advanced tire technologies, and contribute to a lower environmental footprint.”

“We appreciate Senators Warnock and Wicker for introducing legislation to modernize outdated tire testing requirements,” said Brad Heim, Vice President, Product Development — Global Consumer, The Goodyear Tire & Rubber Company. “Tire technology continues to advance rapidly, and federal standards should keep pace with innovation. This legislation will help ensure safety requirements reflect today’s technology while supporting U.S. manufacturing competitiveness.”

title: Welch Celebrates $300 Million in New Federal Funding for Vermont’s GlobalFoundries to Help Make AI More Energy Efficient, Create Jobs
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) celebrated the announcement of $300 million in new federal funding for Vermont’s GlobalFoundries. This federal investment, funded through the Biden Administration’s bipartisan CHIPS and Science Act and administered by the Department of Commerce, will support GlobalFoundries’ research and development of next-generation silicon photonics wafer technologies, which have the potential to substantially increase the energy efficiency of AI and other critical technology infrastructure projects.

“GlobalFoundries is a global leader in semiconductor manufacturing, and I’m glad Vermont will benefit from this $300 million federal investment to help power America’s AI boom in a more energy-efficient way, reducing its impact on ratepayers and the environment,” said Senator Welch. “This funding will help create jobs and support American innovation. I will continue to support collaborative workforce development opportunities that help boost our state’s research and manufacturing economy.”

Senator Welch helped pass the CHIPS and Science Act in 2022 as a Member of the House of Representatives.

Learn more about Senator Welch’s work by visiting his website or by following him on social media.

title: Welch Files Amendment to Graham-Blumenthal Sanctions Bill
text:
Amendment would reassert Congress’ tariff authorities

WASHINGTON, D.C.—U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.) today filed an amendment to the Lindsey O. Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act to remove language in Section 113 of the Act that could enable the Trump Administration to impose tariffs on any country, for any reason.

As written, the legislation grants President Trump new authorities to impose massive tariffs on countries that ‘facilitate’ Russia oil sanctions evasion. However, in practice, the President could impose tariffs of up to 100% on nearly any country, taking this Constitutional authority out of the hands of Congress.

Senator Welch announced his intent to file an amendment on the Senate Floor Tuesday evening:

“…Our language must specify our intent and do so with absolute clarity: Go after the buyers. That was Senator Graham’s goal. And we must have language that makes achieving that goal real. That is why when we take up the Graham-Blumenthal bill, I will offer an amendment to strike the overly-vague delegation of tariff authorities to also target ‘facilitators’ of sanctions evasions. As currently written, the facilitator provision enables the Executive, with full congressional authorization, to impose any tariffs, on any country, for any reason—so long as the Executive labels the tariff country a ‘facilitator.’

“If we delete the facilitator provision, as I propose, we do achieve senator Graham’s goal without his bill being used for any other purposes. In doing so, the bill would retaining the original tariff authority that only targets buyers of Russian oil…Senator Graham, and many of us, myself included—agreed about maximizing the imperative of sanctions and tariff tools to hurt Putin and stop his aggression against Ukrainian civilians. And I hope we can honor Senator Graham by quickly coming together to pass a bipartisan bill that will specifically and effectively target the companies and countries that are buying the oil that Putin is using to pay for the missiles and the bombs that are raining down on the innocent people of Ukraine.”

View and download Senator Welch’s amendment here.

title: Welch Leads STRONG GRID Act to Boost America’s Electric Grid Resiliency to Extreme Weather
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Subcommittee on Rural Development, Energy, and Credit, introduced the Supporting Transformative Resilience, Operations, and Next-Generation Grid Innovation Deployment (STRONG GRID) Act, legislation to increase America’s electric grid resiliency and help prevent power disruptions caused by natural disasters. The STRONG GRID Act aims to spur the adoption of microgrids—localized electric grids that operate independently of the broader energy grid—to reduce strain on America’s electric grid and bolster our energy system from widespread damage created by extreme weather events.

“America’s electric grid is under more pressure now than at any point in our history, and extreme weather events are exacerbating that strain, as we’ve seen in Vermont with brutal floods. By operating independently of the larger energy system, microgrids offer a solution to increase the resiliency of our grid and help reduce the burden consumers face in natural disaster recovery costs. It’s a win-win,” said Senator Welch. “Our bill capitalizes on the potential of microgrids to help keep essential services online and reduce the economic impact of natural disasters.”

Extreme weather events are growing more frequent and intense. From wildfires to floods, hurricanes to tornadoes, Americans across the country experienced firsthand the devastation extreme weather brings to their communities. In 2025, the United States suffered 23 “billion-dollar disasters” that collectively cost more than $115 billion, marking the third costliest year on record behind 2023 and 2024. Natural Disasters cause widespread damage to critical infrastructure—including the electric grid. Utilities then pass these recovery costs along to ratepayers; researchers found that households are spending $35 more per year on average on their electricity bills as a result.

At the same time, America’s electric grid is under immense strain. Forecasts suggest that U.S. electricity demand could increase by as much as 5.7% through 2030, a level of growth not seen since the 1960s. Peaks in electricity consumption during the hottest or coldest days of the year leave the grid ill-equipped to meet this surge in demand, especially when disaster strikes. By operating with self-sustaining electricity generation, storage, and distribution infrastructure, microgrids can alleviate pressure on America’s electric grid and boost resiliency during extreme weather events.

The STRONG GRID Act is endorsed by the GridWise Alliance; Honeywell Technologies; Information Technology Industry Council (ITI); National Association of Electrical Distributors (NAED); National Association of State Energy Officials (NASEO); and the National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA).

“As grid operators issue resource adequacy warnings and utilities revise demand forecasts upward at an unprecedented pace, tapping into local resources is an increasingly important way to protect communities from reliability risks,” said Karen Wayland, CEO, GridWise Alliance. “The GridWise Alliance applauds Senator Welch for introducing the bipartisan STRONG GRID Act, enabling a faster path to microgrid deployment in areas at high risk where extending or hardening traditional infrastructure can take years.”

“Rising electricity demand makes microgrids essential to building a more resilient and reliable electric grid. Senator Welch’s STRONG GRID Act would help deploy the practical solutions needed to modernize America’s energy infrastructure, and ITI is pleased to support this legislation,” said Jason Oxman, President and CEO, ITI.

“The National Association of Electrical Distributors (NAED) applauds Senator Welch for introducing the STRONG GRID Act. Our nation needs practical, flexible, and commonsense approaches to increasing electricity supply and strengthening grid reliability. Microgrids can play an important role by helping communities, businesses, and critical facilities better manage growing demand and maintain power during grid disruptions. The funding and technical assistance in this legislation will reduce barriers to microgrid deployment and make our communities more resilient and productive. With nearly 6,000 electrical distribution facilities across the country, NAED members are ready to provide the equipment, logistics, and technical expertise needed to bring these projects online,” said Wes Smith, President and CEO, National Association of Electrical Distributors.

President of the National Association of State Energy Officials (NASEO) David Terry congratulated Senator Welch on the introduction of the STRONG GRID Act of 2026: “The legislation supports the development and interconnection of microgrids. The bill will support energy security, electric grid resilience, and an enhanced electric system better able to respond to our present and future challenges.”

“America’s electric grid is under growing strain as electricity demand rises at a rapidly accelerating pace, increasing risks to reliability, resilience, and affordability. Protecting American families and businesses from escalating costs and risks of service disruptions requires an ‘all-of-the-above’ energy strategy. The National Electrical Manufacturers Association (NEMA) applauds Senator Peter Welch (D-VT) for introducing the STRONG GRID Act. The bipartisan legislation will help strengthen the nation’s electric infrastructure by accelerating the deployment and evaluation of microgrids. Expanding microgrid deployment will significantly improve grid flexibility and help meet growing electricity demand.”

Learn more about the STRONG GRID Act.

Read and download the full text of the bill.
