title: Davids Meets with Kansans Facing Rising Costs, Highlights Work to Lower Everyday Expenses
text:
OVERLAND PARK, KS — Today, Representative Sharice Davids met one-on-one with Kansans to hear directly about the financial challenges families are facing and discuss solutions to lower costs. During the daylong Cost-of-Living Check-Ins, Kansans shared how rising prices for groceries, gas, housing, and healthcare are impacting their everyday lives and making it harder to make ends meet.

“I know what it’s like to sit around the kitchen table and make tough choices about how to stretch every dollar,” said Davids. “That’s why I spend so much time listening directly to Kansans about the challenges they’re facing. Right now, families are feeling squeezed by rising costs, and they need leaders who understand what that means in their everyday lives. I’ll keep fighting for solutions that lower costs, support working families, and make sure the voices of Kansans are heard in Washington.”

WATCH: Click the following photos to learn more about some of the conversations

Many Kansas households continue reporting financial pressure due to rising inflation and reckless policy decisions in Washington that only favor billionaires. The average family is paying more than $2,500 extra this year due to tariffs and is expected to spend about $740 more on gas. In the past year, residential electricity prices have risen by 13 percent nationally, and families have paid more than $300 more for groceries.

Davids discussed her work to lower costs for Kansans, including efforts to cap insulin at $35 for seniors, lower prescription drug prices through Medicare negotiation, expand affordable housing supply, strengthen Kansas agriculture and local food systems, support year-round E15 fuel access to lower prices at the pump, and extend Affordable Care Act tax credits that help families afford health coverage. She also highlighted her opposition to reckless tariffs and extreme Medicaid cuts that are closing rural hospitals and increasing healthcare costs for Kansas families.

Davids was raised by a single mom who served in the Army for 20 years. She knows what it’s like to struggle to put food on the table, stretch every dollar, and make difficult choices between paying for groceries, healthcare, gas, or rent. That experience continues to shape her focus on lowering costs for working families and making sure everyday people — not just billionaires and large corporations — have a fair shot at getting ahead.

title: DOWNING RECOGNIZES ERIN GRAF AS JULY “MONTANA INNOVATOR”
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Troy Downing (MT-02) recognized Erin Graf as a “Montana Innovator” for the month of July. Conducted in partnership with the Montana 250th Commission, the initiative highlights notable Montanans ahead of America’s 250th anniversary. Each month features a different theme, with July honoring achievements in arts, culture, and literature.

Read the full recognition below:

"This month, I am proud to recognize Erin Graf, a Harlowton native who has dedicated her career to capturing the beauty of God’s creation through the landscapes of rural Montana.

Erin studied fine art at Montana State University from 2001 to 2006, earning a Bachelor of Fine Arts in printmaking and a bachelor’s degree in K-12 art education. She also received MSU’s Award of Excellence for Art, presented to the top graduating students in the department.

Primarily a self-taught oil painter, Erin became a full-time artist in 2015 after spending a decade coaching track and field at Montana State.

In 2019, she held her first solo museum exhibition at the Great Plains Art Museum in Lincoln, Nebraska. The four-month exhibition, titled Montana: Prairies to Peaks, featured 35 works. Erin also served as the museum’s artist-in-residence, and two of her paintings were added to its permanent collection.

Erin co-founded the Three Rivers Artists Guild and previously served as president of Southwest Montana Arts. She also served for five years as chair of the Bozeman Art Museum’s Board of Directors. Her work has appeared in numerous solo and group exhibitions, and she regularly uses her art to support important causes.

Through her work, Erin shares Montana’s remarkable landscapes with audiences across the country. It is my honor to recognize her as a Montana Innovator who embodies the spirit of arts, culture, and literature in our state."

title: Congressman Flood Announces Flyover Fintech Panel on Consumer Payment Tech
text:

Flyover Fintech is right around the corner, and I encourage everyone to register today!"

Michael Duane is Head of Banking Product at Cash App, where he leads product development for Cash App's banking offerings, including Cash App Card, the fourth largest debit card program in the United States. Michael is responsible for driving innovation and growth for products used by more than 25 million customers, with a focus on making everyday financial services simpler and more accessible. He has spent seven years at Cash App building its card and banking products from the ground up. Michael earned his BA in Economics from Dartmouth College.

Ryan Riveland leads partnership and market development efforts for the Zelle Network® and Certos® at Early Warning. title: Department of War Recognizes NAWS China Lake as Global Leader in Advanced Testing and Research
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Vince Fong (CA-20) celebrated the recognition of Naval Air Weapons Station (NAWS) China Lake as the "most advanced Government laboratory and test enterprise in the world" by the Undersecretary of the Department of War for Research and Engineering's Defense Research Enterprise Review.

"NAWS China Lake, as well as our region's defense and space ecosystem, are truly world-class," said Congressman Fong. "The Department of War's recognition of China Lake as a global leader is a credit to the investments that have been made, strong local and regional support, and the hard work of the talented men and women who develop and test cutting edge technology for our nation's warfighters. Combined with the work of the AFRL Rocket Lab, Edwards Air Force Base, NASA Armstrong Flight Research Center, and the Mojave Air and Space Port, our community stands as the nation's premier hub for military and aerospace research, development, test, and evaluation. I applaud NAWS China Lake on this important recognition and thank the Undersecretary for his advocacy to strengthen our nation's defense base."

"The Defense Research Enterprise Review's recognition of NAWS China Lake as 'the most advanced Government laboratory and test enterprise in the world' is a testament to decades of innovation, technical excellence, and the extraordinary dedication of the military, civilian, and industry professionals who make its mission possible. This distinction reinforces China Lake's indispensable role in delivering the next generation of warfighting capabilities and ensuring the United States maintains its technological advantage over our adversaries," said Stephen Farmer, Executive Director, China Lake Alliance.

"The earthquakes of 2019 were a blessing in disguise. Generally, the DoD laboratory and test range infrastructure is WWII vintage. Not China Lake. The Congressional and Navy investment to rebuild China Lake following the earthquakes has rendered it the most modern DoD Research, Development Test and Evaluation facility. Today's weapons systems are highly technical and complex. This investment postures China Lake extremely well to lead and support developing, testing and fielding these systems," said Scott O'Neil, Commissioner on the National Commission on the Future of the Navy & Executive Director of the Indian Wells Valley Economic Development Corporation.

“This report makes it clear: the Aerospace Valley is home to the world’s most advanced government research and test facilities in the world, and that's something every resident of Kern County and the Antelope Valley should know and be proud of,” said Justin Salters, California project lead for Griffiss Institute. “We look forward to deepening our collaboration with our partners at the Navy to leverage the capabilities at China Lake to provide our warfighters with the capabilities they need and support the growth of industry and good jobs in Ridgecrest and the broader region."

The Defense Research Enterprise Review was a 90-day assessment ordered by Secretary of War Pete Hegseth evaluating the Department of War's laboratories, research centers, and testing facilities. Among its key findings, the review recognized NAWS China Lake as the world's most advanced Government laboratory and test enterprise, a direct result of the nearly $4 billion Congressional investment to rebuild China Lake's infrastructure following the 2019 earthquakes. To view the full report, click here.

This recognition reflects years of sustained Congressional investment in China Lake and the broader Indian Wells Valley defense ecosystem. Congressman Fong has fought to secure the following investments to strengthen China Lake's mission and the surrounding community:

Naval Air Warfare Rapid Capabilities Office — $4,000,000

Supports advanced work at NAWS China Lake, ensuring continued progress in naval aviation and electronic warfare systems. FY26 Appropriations Package.

NAWS China Lake Child Development Center — $8,900,000

Funds the design of a new Child Development Center at NAWS China Lake, replacing an outdated facility to meet the growing childcare needs of the installation's workforce. FY26 Appropriations Package.

City of Ridgecrest Wastewater Treatment Plant — $1,000,000

Modernizes a 70-year-old facility serving both the City of Ridgecrest and NAWS China Lake. FY26 Appropriations Package.

Cerro Coso Community College Cybersecurity Program — $1,112,250

Establishes a new cybersecurity education program supporting workforce development in Kern County — directly building the pipeline of talent that installations like China Lake depend on. FY26 Appropriations Package.

Ridgecrest Regional Hospital — $1,321,904

Funds new equipment and related infrastructure improvements at the primary medical facility serving over 28,000 residents of the Indian Wells Valley and the workforce at NAWS China Lake. Included in the FY2027 Labor, Health and Human Services, Education, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, which passed the House Appropriations Committee.

NAWS China Lake is the Navy's largest single landholding, representing 85% of the Navy's land for research, development, acquisition, testing, and evaluation use and 38% of the Navy's land holdings worldwide. Its two ranges and main site cover more than 1.1 million acres — an area larger than the state of Rhode Island — making it the Navy's most critical installation for weapons research and development, and a cornerstone of our national defense.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Hosts Lyme Disease Roundtable
text:
Presses for Passage of Key Bipartisan Legislation

Increased Funding for Public Education, Awareness, Research, Funding

Congressman Hears Directly from North Jersey Experts, Patients, and Community Leaders

New Jersey Ranks Fourth in the Nation for Lyme Disease Cases

Above: Gottheimer hosts roundtable on tackling Lyme disease.

HAWORTH, NJ — Today, July 30, 2026, U.S. Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) hosted a Lyme disease roundtable at the Haworth Library, sitting down with local officials, medical experts, and advocates to confront the growing threat of Lyme and other tick-borne illnesses facing families across New Jersey.

Watch full remarks here.

“There is nothing partisan about a tick bite. This isn’t a Democratic issue or a Republican issue — it’s a Jersey families issue,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Whether you’re hiking the Appalachian Trail, playing in your backyard, or just walking the dog around the block, you deserve to do that without worrying about a disease that can follow you for years.”

“Vector-borne diseases, including Lyme disease, have real impacts on public health in all of our communities. It is so important that we continue to support sustained efforts to keep the public informed of their risk of contracting these diseases, and to further our understanding of these infections — the ways in which they cause the disorders they do, and how best to diagnose and treat them,” said Dr. John Halperin of Atlantic Health.

Lyme disease is the most common disease transmitted from animals to humans in the country, with an estimated 476,000 cases nationally every year, and New Jersey ranks fourth in the nation for reported Lyme disease cases. In 2026 alone, the state has already reported more than 4,000 tick-borne disease cases — over 3,500 of them Lyme disease — according to the New Jersey Department of Health. Since 2010, New Jersey has averaged nearly 4,800 Lyme cases per year. Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties alone have averaged nearly 800 combined cases annually.

Roundtable participants raised the urgent need for greater public awareness, the difficulty of getting an accurate diagnosis, the prevalence of false negatives, and the need for better physician education on Lyme and related tick-borne illnesses such as anaplasmosis, babesiosis, and alpha-gal syndrome. Participants also highlighted the long-term physical, cognitive, and mental health impacts on children whose Lyme disease goes undiagnosed for too long.

Gottheimer outlined priorities he is advancing in Washington to address these concerns:

Passing the Kay Hagan Tick Act. Last week, a bill Gottheimer championed, the Kay Hagan Tick Act, which passed the House overwhelmingly, establishes the federal government’s national strategy on Lyme disease for the next five years and includes funding for research, surveillance, physician education, and public awareness all across the country. Gottheimer is now pressing the Senate to pass the bipartisan measure and get it signed into law.

Securing federal funding. Gottheimer’s appropriations requests this year sought for Lyme and tick-borne disease funding for NIH research through the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, or NIAID; CDC prevention and education; and the Department of Defense’s Tick-Borne Disease Research Program. He secured $5 million for the LymeX Innovation Accelerator, a public-private partnership accelerating the development of new Lyme disease diagnostics and treatments. He is fighting back against the administration’s proposal to reorganize the CDC’s dedicated Lyme Disease Program and consolidate it into the broader Vector-Borne Disease Program and cut funding by $3.8 million.

Advancing new legislation. Gottheimer is continuing to push forward his federal legislation to combat Lyme and tick-borne illnesses: the Tick Identification Pilot Program Act, co-led with Congressman Tom Kean (NJ-7), which would let residents submit a photo of a tick and get expert identification and guidance within 72 hours; the Stamp Out Lyme Disease Act, with Congressman Don Bacon (NE-2), which would direct the Postal Service to issue a Lyme disease research stamp funding NIAID research; and the BITE (Battling Infections Transmitted by Ticks and Exposure) Act, co-led with Congressman Tom Kean (NJ-7), which would build the first fully integrated national vector-borne disease prevention and alert system, with the goal of cutting Lyme disease cases 25 percent by 2035.

Gottheimer also urged residents to take precautions this summer: using repellents, wearing proper clothing, checking themselves and their pets for ticks, and watching for a red bullseye rash, especially after spending time in wooded or grassy areas, and following up with a doctor if a rash or fever develops in the weeks after a possible bite.

Gottheimer was joined by Haworth Councilwoman Alanna Davis; Matt Bickerton, Bergen County Health Department; Joseph Dolan, National Society of Professional Surveyors; Matthew Marinello, Atlantic Health; Dr. John Halperin, Atlantic Health; Dr. Mohini Gurme, Medical Director of Neurology at One Bergen Health; Allana Davis; Dr. Rosalie Greenberg, Child & Adolescent Psychiatrist; Steven Hafif; Melissa Rowe, Executive Director, Central New York Lyme and Tickborne Disease Alliance; Heather Zampino; Samantha Sloves; Olivia Abrams, Founder of TiCK MiTT; Kurt Borowsky; Dennis Sullivan; Ellen Allen; Susan Eisen; Jim McCabe; Sally Goodgold; David Butler, Whitney Klein; Susan Fuhr; Dr. Nicole Anderson; Sofia Ciminello, CLA Fellow; Lisa-Jae Eggert; Dr. Robert Bransfield, Assistant Clinical Professor Hackensack and Rutgers-RWJ Medical School; Alissa Johnson; Gloria Kim.

Below: Gottheimer hosts roundtable on tackling Lyme disease.

Gottheimer’s remarks as prepared for delivery:

Good afternoon, everybody. Thank you all so much for being here today at the Haworth Library, and thank you to all of those who sat with me to talk through something that’s affecting so many families right here in North Jersey: Lyme and other tick-borne diseases.

I want to start by saying thank you to our experts, leaders, and participants in today’s roundtable. The stories you shared today, the questions you asked, the recommendations you made, the frustrations you brought forward — that’s exactly why we’re here.

This isn’t an abstract issue for the people here today, or for far too many across our state and country. This disease is personal for many, including myself. I’ve watched family members struggle with the disease for decades. One of my wife’s closest friends faced years of debilitating symptoms, as well.

And I know so many of you in this room, and so many families across Jersey, have gone through the same thing.

While we are fortunate to have these beautiful places where people can enjoy the outdoors, go for a hike, and barbecue with friends — and that’s one of the great gifts of our state and my district here in Northern New Jersey — we must also be careful, stay alert, and protect against what’s lurking in the grass and trees: the legitimate threat of ticks and the diseases they can carry, including Lyme disease.

Let’s talk about the scope of the problem, because the numbers are stunning. Lyme disease is the most common disease transmitted from animals to humans in the entire country. Nationally, we’re looking at an estimated 476,000 cases every single year. New Jersey ranks fourth in the nation for reported Lyme disease cases. In 2026 alone, our state has already reported more than 4,000 tick-borne disease cases — over 3,500 of them Lyme disease — according to the New Jersey Department of Health, and 1,275 tick-related emergency department visits.

Since 2010, New Jersey has averaged nearly 4,800 Lyme cases every year. And here in North Jersey, Bergen, Passaic, and Sussex Counties alone have averaged a total of nearly 800 Lyme cases a year.

That’s not a small problem. That’s an epidemic hiding in plain sight, in our parks, on our trails, and right in our backyards. While ticks are small, these pests can carry dangerous diseases that pose severe risks to the health and safety of our families.

Now, today, we heard directly from you all about what that looks like on the ground. We heard about the need for greater public awareness, teaching families how to spot a tick early and just how prevalent this disease really is right here in Jersey. We heard about the diagnosis problem: how hard it is to get an accurate test, and how many people get a false negative before they ever get the right answer.

We heard about the need for better physician education, because too many doctors still aren’t trained to recognize Lyme disease or the other tick-borne illnesses that ride along with it — things like anaplasmosis (an-uh-plaz-MOH-sis), babesiosis (buh-bee-zee-OH-sis), and alpha-gal syndrome. And we heard about the need for continued investment in research and innovation — to improve diagnostics, strengthen prevention, and better understand the long-term impacts of Lyme disease. And we talked about our kids, about the long-term physical, cognitive, and mental health impacts when a child’s Lyme disease goes undiagnosed for too long.

Every single one of those concerns is real, and I want to walk you through the three things I’m focused on right now to crush Lyme disease and protect our children and families from tick-borne illnesses. As a member of the Congressional Lyme and Tick-Borne Disease Caucus, I am on the front lines of this issue on Capitol Hill — and always listening for what I can best do to help.

First, just last week, a bipartisan bill I’ve long been championing, the Kay Hagan Tick Act, passed the House overwhelmingly. This bipartisan legislation establishes the federal government’s national strategy on Lyme disease. That means funding for research, surveillance, physician education, and public awareness all across the country for the next five years. That’s a huge win.

But a bill won’t help a single family in this room until it becomes law, and that means getting it through the Senate. So right now, I’m pushing hard to get the Senate to pass this bill and send it to the President’s desk to become law. We cannot let a bipartisan bill that sailed through the House overwhelmingly sit around and die because the Senate didn’t get to it. That’s priority number one: to make it law.

Second, I’m working directly with my colleagues in Congress on the Appropriations Committee to surge investments into this fight. My budget requests this year asked for Lyme and tick-borne disease funding for NIH research through the National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases, or NIAID, CDC prevention and education, and the Department of Defense’s Tick-Borne Disease Research Program. Here’s the good news: we secured $5 million for the LymeX Innovation Accelerator, a public-private partnership accelerating the development of new Lyme disease diagnostics and treatments.

Here’s what makes that funding and this fight so important right now. While we’ve been working to build this up, the administration has been trying to slash funding for these programs and has proposed reorganizing the CDC’s dedicated Lyme Disease Program and consolidating it into the broader Vector-Borne Disease Program. Since 90% of vector-borne diseases are caused by ticks, combining both programs means 90% of those resources may not actually go toward tick prevention and research. That would be a disaster.

The administration has proposed $3.8 million in cuts. Consolidating these programs and cutting funding isn’t streamlining anything; it’s just making sure fewer dollars go where they’re needed most. We’re fighting it and pushing to go in the other direction. So I’m speaking to my colleagues, member by member, to ensure Lyme research and prevention get what they actually need to keep Jersey families safe and informed.

Third, I’m doing a full-court press on the bills I’ve been championing in Congress, because these aren’t just ideas — they’re common-sense, bipartisan solutions ready to go. My Tick Identification Pilot Program Act, which I’m co-leading with Congressman Tom Kean of New Jersey, will fund state programs that let you snap a photo of a tick, submit it, and get an answer back from an expert within 72 hours on what kind of tick it was, what the risk is, and what to do next.

My Stamp Out Lyme Disease Act, with Congressman Don Bacon of Nebraska, will direct the Postal Service to issue a Lyme disease research stamp, with every dollar raised going straight to the NIH’s National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases to fund new research and innovation.

My Battling Infections Transmitted by Ticks and Exposure Act, or BITE Act, with Congressman Tom Kean of New Jersey, will build the first fully integrated national vector-borne disease prevention and alert system in the world. It will combine expert tick identification, AI-powered early warning alerts, insurance and emergency room surveillance to catch outbreaks faster, and public education in our schools and communities — cutting Lyme disease cases by 25 percent by 2035.

I’m also backing other efforts, including the Children Inflicted by Lyme Disabilities Act, which would expand special education protections to children with Lyme and other tick-borne diseases; the TICK Act, to strengthen federal research and prevention efforts to combat Lyme and other tick-borne diseases, including anaplasmosis (an-uh-plaz-MOH-sis), babesiosis (buh-bee-zee-OH-sis), and ehrlichiosis (air-lih-kee-OH-sis), among others; and the Alpha-gal Allergen Inclusion Act, to classify alpha-gal as a major food allergen.

This fight takes an all-hands-on-deck approach, and that’s exactly what we are doing to keep our families safe. We need to use every tool in the toolkit.

Finally, and consider this the PSA of the day, here’s what you can do to protect yourself.

When you go for a hike or even to the beach — yes, they are on the beach — always check yourself after a walk or a day outside, especially if you’ve recently spent time in a wooded or grassy area.

Use repellents that contain DEET or picaridin, wear proper clothing, like long-sleeve shirts and long pants, and tuck your pants into your socks. Consistently check yourself and your pets for ticks, especially in warm, hidden places like armpits, scalp, and behind your ears. If you do see a tick, remove it with tweezers by grabbing close to your skin and pulling in one smooth motion, and thoroughly wash the affected area with soap and water. If you see a red bullseye rash develop on your skin, take a picture with the rash next to a ruler and reach out to your doctor.

I think one thing is clear: there is nothing partisan about Lyme disease. This isn’t a Democrat issue or a Republican issue. This is a Jersey families issue. Whether you’re hiking the Appalachian Trail, playing in your backyard with your kids, or just walking the dog around the block, you deserve to do that without worrying about a disease that can follow you for years.

Working together, we will beat Lyme disease.

I want to thank everyone in this room again, and I want to thank our partners at the Center for Lyme Action, local hospitals and doctors’ offices, and medical professionals for the incredible work you do every single day fighting for patients and families.

If we keep working together and fighting to protect our Jersey families, in the greatest country in the world, our best days will always be ahead of us.

Thank you, and God bless you and your families.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer, Jackson Introduce Bipartisan Bill Targeting Polisario Front Cooperation with Iranian Regime
text:
Bipartisan legislation would trigger a terrorist designation of the Polisario Front over its cooperation with Iran and Iranian-backed terrorist groups

WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representatives Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5) and Ronny Jackson (TX-13) introduced the Polisario Front Terrorist Designation Act, the bipartisan House companion to legislation in the Senate led by U.S. Senator Ted Cruz (R-TX). The legislation requires the Secretary of State to designate the Polisario Front, a Sahrawi paramilitary group based in Algeria, as a terrorist organization if the group is found to be cooperating with Iran or Iranian-backed terrorist organizations.

“The Iranian regime and its terrorist proxies are working overtime to open a new front against the United States and our allies, and the Polisario Front has become one of their instruments,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “When a group takes drones and weapons from the IRGC and coordinates with Iranian-backed terrorists, we should call it exactly what it is: a terrorist organization. This bipartisan bill makes sure that once that cooperation is confirmed, we can bring the full weight of America’s counterterrorism sanctions down on the Polisario Front and cut its leaders off from the global financial system, international travel, and the resources they use to threaten us and our allies. Standing up to Iran and its proxies isn’t a partisan issue.”

“FDD Action supports efforts to designate the Polisario Front which has been armed and trained by elements of Iran’s IRGC and Hezbollah. This important legislation would require the State Department to report on the Polisario Front’s activities including weapons trafficking and the use of armed drones against civilian targets,” said Tyler Stapleton Senior Director of Government Relations – FDD Action.

The bill text can be read here.

The Polisario Front Terrorist Designation Act would initiate a process to designate the Polisario Front as a Foreign Terrorist Organization (FTO) and Specially Designated Global Terrorist (SDGT) if the group is found to be engaging in military and terrorist cooperation with Iran or Iranian-affiliated terrorist groups. Specifically, it requires a report from the Secretary of State on cooperation between the Polisario Front and such groups relating to:

Armed participation in military operations;

Weapons systems, including man-portable individual-use firearms;

Unmanned aerial vehicles, including commercially available component parts;

Systems or components designed to detect, track, engage, or destroy airborne targets; and

Military intelligence support, including surveillance data, targeting information, signals, or human intelligence, and related analysis in raw or processed form.

Original co-sponsors are Representatives Claudia Tenny (NY-22), Greg Landsman (OH-1), Don Bacon (NE-2), and Jared Moskowitz (FL-23). The bill is endorsed by Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD).

title: Hinson Reintroduces Bipartisan Bill to Help New Parents Avoid Surprise Medical Bills
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congresswoman Ashley Hinson (R-IA-02) reintroduced the bipartisan No Surprise Bills for New Moms Act alongside Congressman Jerrold Nadler (D-NY-12), legislation that would ensure parents do not receive surprise medical bills for their newborns.

"Parents shouldn’t be hit with surprise medical bills for their newborn because big health insurance companies prioritize their bottom line over working families. This bipartisan bill holds insurance companies accountable, ensures newborns have seamless coverage, and gives new parents one less thing to worry about so they can focus on keeping their babies healthy and happy.” — Congresswoman Ashley Hinson

The No Surprise Bills for New Moms Act would:

Require health insurers to automatically provide coverage to newborns under their mother’s insurance for 30 days after birth.

Establish a 60-day enrollment period after those first 30 days, giving families additional time to enroll their newborn in a health insurance plan.

Require health plans and insurers to notify parents if they receive a bill for an uncovered newborn.

Hinson has consistently championed pro-family policies that make life easier for Iowa families. This reintroduction builds on her broader bipartisan work to support Iowa families, including expanding access to affordable childcare and strengthening support for mothers and infants.

This bill is co-led by Brian Fitzpatrick (R-PA-01) and Nanette Barragán (D-CA-44). The full text of the bill can be found here.

title: Smith Visits BJG Meat Co. in Carter County
text:
GRANDIN, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) visited BJG Meat Co. in Carter County this week where he met with owner Brad Goodman and toured the facility to discuss the company’s meat processing work and hear about how the Working Families Tax Cuts, which Congressman Smith authored and spearheaded in Congress, is positively impacting their operations, as well as the effect of USDA regulations on small, family-owned processors.

Congressman Smith said, “Brad Goodman and his family have built something special here in Grandin — a business that puts Missouri-raised beef and pork on Missouri tables, while keeping hardworking Missourians on the payroll. From the cattle they process to the farmers and producers they work with every day, BJG Meat Co. is proof that southeast Missouri agriculture is thriving. Family operations like this know their business better than Washington ever will, and that is why I fought to deliver real tax relief for small businesses in the Working Families Tax Cuts to allow businesses like BJG Meat Co to grow their operations, keep more of their hard-earned money, and invest in their employees. I’ll always look for ways to make it easier for processors to keep doing what they do best.”

BJG Meat Co. is a locally owned meat processing and retail company that has been based in Grandin for three years, with an additional retail location in Poplar Bluff. Between its processing operation and retail stores, BJG Meat Co. employs 15 people, and 99 percent of the products it sells are sourced right here in Missouri. In addition to custom processing for cattle and hogs and freezer meat bundles, BJG Meat Co.’s Poplar Bluff storefront also features products from other Missouri vendors, including local honey, candles, soaps, and cutting boards. In just three years, BJG Meat Co. has become a go-to source for locally processed beef and pork in Carter County and across Southeast Missouri.

As a small business, BJG Meat Co. benefits directly from provisions in the Working Families Tax Cuts, including Section 199A’s deduction for pass-through business income and 100 percent bonus depreciation, which allows the company to invest in the equipment it needs to keep processing cattle for local farmers and producers. These are exactly the kinds of investments Congressman Smith had in mind for small, family-owned businesses like BJG Meat Co. when he authored these provisions and fought to get them across the finish line. Additionally, like many small, USDA-inspected processors, BJG Meat Co. spoke with Congressman Smith about navigating federal requirements such as carcass stamping and limits on common ownership. As BJG Meat Co. continues to grow, Smith remains committed to cutting the federal red tape that makes it harder for processors like it to operate.

title: Jayapal, Markey Introduce Green New Deal for Public Schools to Invest in Students, Schools, and a Livable Future
text:
SEATTLE, WA – U.S. Representative Pramila Jayapal (WA-07) and Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), member of the Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee, and the Environment and Public Works Committee, today introduced the Green New Deal for Public Schools Act, legislation that would infuse $1.6 trillion over the next decade to transform our public school system – investing in students, educators, and infrastructure – and respond to the climate crisis.

“Public schools and a strong education system are the bedrock of our democracy. However, for decades, as school buildings have crumbled, as classes have doubled or tripled in size, and as the Trump administration has chipped away at programs to support kids’ mental health, American schools have fallen behind. In the richest country in the world, we should have the best public school system in the world. The Green New Deal for Public Schools, which I’m proud to lead with Senator Markey, would make investments in safe, healthy, zero-carbon classrooms to lift up our students, teachers, administrators, and entire public education system,” said Congresswoman Jayapal.

“Every student in America deserves to learn in a school that lifts them up, not one that’s falling down. Across the country, kids are trying to learn in buildings with broken heat, leaky roofs, and hazardous ventilation systems,” said Senator Markey. “It’s time that we reinvest in our students, our planet, and our future. The Green New Deal for Public Schools Act is a step toward building up the next generation of leaders by securing educational justice, health justice, and environmental justice all in one.”

The Green New Deal for Public Schools Act would invest $1.6 trillion in public and Bureau of Indian Education schools over the next ten years to revitalize the K-12 education system and reduce hazardous pollution. It would also reverse harmful disinvestment in the public school system by investing in schools serving low-income students, tripling funding to support students with disabilities, and giving schools the resources to hire hundreds of thousands of educators, paraprofessionals, and staff – including counselors to support student mental health. Investments from the Green New Deal for Public Schools Act would create 1.3 million jobs annually and eliminate 78 million metric tons of carbon emissions, which is equivalent to taking 17 million cars off the road.

Specifically, the Green New Deal for Public Schools Act would:

Establish grants for healthy green retrofits of public schools, including modifications to optimize air quality, ensure clean air and water, and improve energy efficiency with priority given to highest-need schools

Ensure school upgrades support safe, well-paid union jobs with project labor, prevailing wage, and registered apprenticeship protections

Invest $250 billion in hiring thousands of new teachers, paraprofessionals, and mental health counselors to ensure every student receives a quality education and the support they need

Fully fund the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act and quadruple funding for schools serving predominantly low-income students to fulfill Congress’ promise to every student

“As we face a catastrophic climate crisis caused by unchecked corporate greed, we need to center children and their future. What this comes down to is whether we’re willing and able to provide students with the resources they need to realize their brilliance and have a livable planet. Do we want to continue building a world based on militarization, incarceration, poverty, and destruction of resources? Or will we put our kids and educators first, and treat the climate crisis as the emergency it is? The Green New Deal for Public Schools Act would ensure the production and maintenance of safe and healthy learning and teaching environments for students, teachers, staff, caregivers, and the broader community — and represents the action we need to be on the right side of history,” said Batul Hassan, Labor Director at Climate and Community Institute.

The Green New Deal for Public Schools Act is cosponsored by Senators Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.). and Representatives Eleanor Holmes Norton (D-DC), Valerie Foushee (NC-04), Mike Quigley (IL-05), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Bennie Thompson (MS-02), Rashida Tlaib (MI-12), Dan Goldman (NY-10), Delia Ramirez (IL-03), Chuy García (IL-04), Shri Thanedar (MI-13), Troy Carter (LA-02), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Paul Tonko (NY-20), and Mark Pocan (WI-02).

title: Ranking Members Raskin, Jayapal Demand ICE Agents Wear Functional Body Cameras
text:
Washington, D.C. (July 30, 2026)—Today, Rep. Jamie Raskin, Ranking Member of the House Judiciary Committee, and Rep. Pramila Jayapal, Ranking Member of the Subcommittee on Immigration Integrity, Security, and Enforcement, sent a letter demanding that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) immediately equip all agents interacting with the public with fully functional body-worn cameras. The demand follows a disturbing pattern of deadly immigration enforcement operations carried out without basic accountability measures in place.

“We have watched in horror as Department of Homeland Security (DHS) officials shot over two dozen people and killed six of them, including three U.S. citizens, during immigration enforcement operations since President Donald Trump took office in January 2025.1 In shooting after shooting, we are told that there is no body-worn camera footage of the incident and asked to accept DHS’s account of the incident. Time and again, that account turns out to be a blatant falsehood. It is time for DHS to use the $210 billion that congressional Republicans have given the agency to ensure that every DHS officer is equipped with a fully functioning body-worn camera when conducting immigration enforcement,” wrote the Ranking Members.

Despite repeated DHS promises, body-worn cameras remain absent—or nonfunctional—when they matter most. After ICE agents killed U.S. citizens Renée Good and Alex Pretti in Minneapolis earlier this year, DHS pledged rapid nationwide deployment. Nearly six months later, that promise remains unmet.

The consequences have been deadly. Earlier this month, ICE officers fatally shot Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Texas without body camera footage. Days later, officers killed Johan Sebastian Guerrero in Maine while wearing cameras that were not functioning. In both cases, the public was left to rely solely on DHS’s account—despite its documented record of false and misleading statements about these incidents.

DHS has repeatedly made unsubstantiated claims about victims, including Renée Good, Alex Pretti, Ruben Ray Martinez, and Marimar Martinez—falsely alleging they attacked officers. In case after case, evidence has contradicted these claims, further eroding DHS’s credibility.

Body-worn cameras are a basic accountability tool used by state and local law enforcement nationwide. They protect officers, safeguard the public, and provide essential transparency for courts and Congress. Yet under the Trump Administration, federal immigration enforcement continues to operate without this standard safeguard.

Congress has already provided DHS with more than $210 billion for immigration enforcement in the last year and a half, including $20 million specifically for body-worn cameras. Even Republican lawmakers have urged deployment, but House Judiciary Republicans recently rejected an amendment requiring their use.

Ranking Members Raskin and Jayapal are demanding every agent who interacts with the public be equipped with fully functional body-worn cameras.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES, RANKING MEMBER MORELLE HOST ROCHESTER VOTER PROTECTION SHADOW HEARING
text:
National and local experts discuss election administration, voting rights and coordinated preparation ahead of the 2026 midterms.

Yesterday, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries and Congressman Joe Morelle, the top Democrat on the Committee on House Administration, hosted a shadow hearing at Rochester City Hall focused on protecting the right to vote, supporting election officials and preparing for threats to the 2026 elections.

The shadow hearing featured Bob Bauer, former White House Counsel and Professor of Practice and Distinguished Scholar in Residence at NYU School of Law; Omar Noureldin, Senior Vice President of Policy and Litigation at Common Cause; and Natalie Sheppard, Deputy Commissioner of the Monroe County Board of Elections.

Jeffries and Morelle questioned the panel about how to build voter confidence, protect eligible voters from improper voter-roll removals, support election workers and administrators, preserve bipartisan election administration and strengthen the legal and operational safeguards that protect free and fair elections.

The Rochester hearing is the latest public step in a coordinated House Democratic voter-protection effort led by Morelle at the direction of Leader Jeffries. The effort includes national threat assessment, scenario-planning exercises, congressional oversight, stakeholder coordination and public education ahead of the midterms.

“Our elections belong to the people, not to any president, political party, or powerful interest,” said Congressman Joe Morelle. “House Democrats are prepared to use every tool available to defend voters, support election officials, and make sure the results reflect the will of the American people.”

“Donald Trump and Republicans have broken every promise that they made to the American people and have concluded that their best course of action as it relates to the upcoming midterm election is to suppress the vote, intimidate voters and potentially rig the outcome. It is our collective responsibility, not as Democrats or Republicans, but as Americans, to ensure that we have the largest voter protection effort in the history of the country, that we give everybody an opportunity to have their voice heard,” said Leader Jeffries. “I’m thankful to Congressman Morelle for his extraordinary efforts all across the country in ensuring that the American people and civil society are prepared for a free and fair election this November.”

House Democratic voter-protection work

A dozen election security events, including shadow hearings in Los Angeles, San Francisco, New Haven, Las Vegas and Rochester;

Engagement with civil society allies;

Tabletop exercises and strategy sessions; and

Public education campaigns.

title: Dr. Joyce Participates in Main Street Rx Roundtable Discussion

title: Kaptur Statement on Halt of Brandon Road Lock and Dam Construction
text:
Toledo, OH — Today, Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur (OH-09), Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Energy and Water and Co-Chair of the bipartisan House Great Lakes Task Force, released the following statement about the US Army Corps of Engineers stopping work on the Brandon Road Lock and Dam complex, a project in Joliet, Illinois intended to stop invasive carp from reaching the Great Lakes.

"The Army Corps of Engineers has stopped work at the Brandon Road Interbasin Project. That is terrible news for our Great Lakes. Invasive carp do not belong here. If they reach the Great Lakes, they will destroy our native ecosystem. Lake Erie holds more fish and more boats than all the other Great Lakes combined. Ohio has as much at stake in this fight as any State in the basin — and so does every family that fishes, boats, or earns a living on Lake Erie and in our precious Freshwater Kingdom.

“For years, we have worked on a bipartisan basis to build a barrier program at Brandon Road that meets the needs of every affected State. Congress authorized this project, and Congress paid for it. Multiple states have made financial and land contributions for the project. The President himself directed his agencies to move it with maximum speed. The work had finally begun.

“And yet, now we learned of a stop work order through the news. The Administration and Corps of Engineers did not provide any legally-required notice to Congress nor any public information. That sends a red alert across the Great Lakes basin.

“The Corps of Engineers must resume the work at once. Congress has spoken. The Governors from the Great Lakes States have spoken. This project is under construction, and it must be built. There is no excuse for delay, and as Ranking Member of the Energy and Water Appropriations Subcommittee and a leader of the bipartisan Great Lakes Task Force I stand fully ready to use all the tools in our arsenal to ensure this vital work resumes with great haste.”

title: Krishnamoorthi Applauds Senate HELP Committee Advancement of His Bipartisan College Transparency Act
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions (HELP) Committee voted 21-1 to advance the bipartisan College Transparency Act, legislation led in the House by Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL) and Congressman Mike Kelly (R-PA) and in the Senate by Senator Bill Cassidy (R-LA) and Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA.).

Congressman Krishnamoorthi released the following statement:

“Choosing a college is one of the biggest financial decisions a student and their family will ever make. Just like any major investment, they deserve clear, reliable information before they commit. I'm proud that our bipartisan College Transparency Act advanced out of the Senate HELP Committee today with overwhelming bipartisan support. Our legislation will help students compare college costs, graduation rates, and career outcomes so they can make informed decisions and shop for the best program with confidence. I thank Senators Warren and Cassidy for their leadership, and I look forward to working with my colleagues to get this bipartisan bill across the finish line.”

The College Transparency Act would require the federal government to collect and publicly report comprehensive data on college costs and student outcomes, including graduation rates, post-college earnings, average net price, and average student loan debt across colleges and academic programs. By providing students and families with clear, reliable information, the legislation will help prospective students compare programs, identify affordable options, and make informed decisions about their futures. The bill will also provide colleges, researchers, and policymakers with better data to strengthen America's higher education system.

The College Transparency Act is supported by more than 70 organizations, including the American Association of Community Colleges, the American Association of State Colleges and Universities, the Association of American Universities, the Association of Public and Land-grant Universities, EdTrust, the Institute for Higher Education Policy, the National College Attainment Network, the National Skills Coalition, The Institute for College Access & Success, Third Way, the U.S. Chamber of Commerce, Women Employed, and Young Invincibles.

title: Larsen Introduces Bill to Study Prison Libraries
text:
Today, U.S. Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) and Representative Emanuel Cleaver (MO-05) introduced the Read for Reentry Act, legislation that would authorize a study into state and federal prison libraries in the United States to better understand and further the role of prison libraries in reducing the number of prisoners who return to prison.

“Access to the world of books through libraries changes lives,” said Rep. Larsen. “Prison libraries provide incarcerated people with important tools and opportunities for growth. This bill will study prison libraries and their effectiveness to reinforce the work prison libraries do to help incarcerated people return to society successfully.”

“For years, I’ve said that a prison sentence should not be a life sentence to hopelessness. Libraries give incarcerated individuals access to education, job skills, legal resources, and the opportunity to grow.” said Rep. Emanuel Cleaver. “That’s good for the individual, good for public safety, and good for our communities. Yet we still lack a clear understanding of how prison libraries operate across the country. Better data will help us strengthen these programs, identify best practices, and ensure more people have access to the tools they need to successfully reenter society, and that’s exactly why I’m proud to co-sponsor this bill.”

The latest data from the Bureau of Justice Statistics shows that about two-thirds of state prisoners are rearrested after three years. However, a 2025 report from the American Library Association suggested that access to prison libraries and education materials may dramatically reduce recidivism rates. Initial studies indicate that prison libraries contribute to this reduction by supporting the mental health of incarcerated individuals, bolstering literacy and education, offering job skill training, employment information and providing incarcerated individuals with resources for reentry.

Currently, there are no set standards for prison libraries or requirements for prisons to offer library services, and insufficient data assessing existing prison library programs, their usage and outcomes. The Read for Reentry Act would require the U.S. Government Accountability Office to conduct a study into state and federal prison libraries in the U.S. to fill in these gaps. Its findings could be used to inform and further the work of prison libraries to help incarcerated people, reduce recidivism and improve public safety. Specifically, the study would:

Identify sources of funding for state and federal prison libraries;

Identify demographic information of state and federal prisons that offer library services;

Identify the prison recidivism and parole compliance rates for prisons that offer library services to incarcerated individuals; and

Identify the rate of disciplinary infractions involving an incarcerated individual in a state or federal prison that offers library services.

The American Library Association supports the Read for Reentry Act.

"Prison libraries make a world of difference through the critical services they offer, books and beyond,” said Maria McCauley, American Library Association President. “Data on state and federal prison libraries proposed by the Read for Reentry Act would build a more comprehensive picture of the impact prison libraries have on reducing recidivism and aiding in reentry. Gathering additional data is the first step towards scaling what works.”

U.S. Representatives Hank Johnson (GA-04), Lateefah Simon (CA-12), Shri Thanedar (MI-13) and Sydney Kamlager-Dove (CA-37) signed on as original co-sponsors to this legislation.

Rep. Larsen routinely donates books from the Library of Congress across Northwest Washington and is a strong advocate for funding the Institute of Museum and Library Services.

The full text of the Read for Reentry Act can be found here.

title: Rep. Laurel Lee Hosts VA Secretary Doug Collins to Highlight Historic Investments and Reforms for America's Veterans
text:

The visit highlighted the Department of Veterans Affairs' (VA) ongoing efforts to improve access to healthcare, modernize facilities, streamline benefits, and ensure American veterans receive the care and services they have earned through their service.

title: Congressman Lawler Presses SEC to Prepare America’s Financial Markets for the Quantum Era
text:
Washington, D.C. – 7/30/26… Today, Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) sent a letter to Securities and Exchange Commission Chairman Paul Atkins requesting information on the agency’s preparedness for the emerging opportunities and risks posed by quantum technologies to America’s financial markets.

While quantum technologies could significantly improve fraud detection, risk modeling, and market surveillance, they also present new cybersecurity challenges. Existing cryptographic systems that protect trading, clearing, settlement, and sensitive investor data could become vulnerable as quantum capabilities mature.

“For decades, the strength of America’s financial system has rested on regulatory frameworks that anticipate technological change while preserving space for responsible innovation. Quantum computing, quantum sensing, and quantum communications represent a generational shift, with the potential to reshape financial market infrastructure, operational continuity, and investor protection. We should be preparing now to ensure our markets remain the safest, strongest, and most competitive in the world,” said Congressman Lawler.

title: Rep. Mike Levin Honors Encinitas Resident Michaelle Jinnette as July 2026 Constituent of the Month
text:
Michaelle Jinnette

Encinitas, CA—Today, Rep. Mike Levin (CA-49) named Encinitas resident Michaelle Jinnette as his July 2026 Constituent of the Month for turning a devastating diagnosis into a worldwide effort to bring research and hope to families facing rare KCNH1-related disorders.

Michaelle founded the Cure KCNH1 Foundation after her son Tristan received an ultra-rare genetic diagnosis at just 15 months old.[1] Now 6, Tristan cannot speak, has an intellectual disability, and lives with seizures that can put his health in serious danger.[2] His condition traces to a rare mutation in a single gene, KCNH1. Fewer than 100 children around the world are known to have it.

Rather than face the diagnosis passively, Michaelle and her husband, Kevin Witt, channeled their energy into action and built the Cure KCNH1 Foundation, a patient-led nonprofit dedicated to funding the research that could one day yield treatments and a cure. Relentless and resourceful, Michaelle personally reached out to rare-disease researchers across the globe, eventually connecting with Dr. Alfred L. George, Jr., a Northwestern University pharmacologist and leading expert in the genetic disorders known as channelopathies.[3] That partnership has helped spark new scientific research into KCNH1-related conditions where little existed before.

A licensed Marriage and Family Therapist by profession, Michaelle has brought a therapist's instinct for connection to her advocacy. What began as one mother's search for answers has grown into an international community of affected families, researchers, and supporters united behind a common cause.

See below for Rep. Levin's statement recognizing Michaelle Jinnette in the Congressional Record:

“Mr. Speaker, it is my honor to recognize Michaelle Jinnette, a resident of Encinitas, as my Constituent of the Month for July 2026.

“When Michaelle’s son Tristan was diagnosed with an ultra-rare genetic condition, she and her husband, Kevin, refused to accept that there was nothing to be done. Instead, they founded the Cure KCNH1 Foundation and set out to build related scientific research and inspire hope that did not yet exist for families like theirs.

“Michaelle’s determination has connected families across the globe and helped launch new research into a disorder shared by fewer than 100 children worldwide. She has shown that one parent's love, paired with tireless resolve, can move the frontiers of medicine forward.

“I urge my colleagues to join me in celebrating Michaelle Jinnette, and in thanking her for the strength, compassion, and leadership she brings to families facing rare disease everywhere.”

Rep. Levin’s Constituent of the Month program recognizes outstanding North County San Diego and South Orange County residents who have gone above and beyond to help their neighbors, give back to their community, and represent the best of our country. Rep. Levin’s June 2026 Co-Constituents of the Month were Oceanside Residents Esmeralda Gonzalez and David Ontiveros, both exhibit extraordinary dedication to supporting the LGBTQ community in North County San Diego. Levin’s May 2026 Constituent of the Month was 101-year-old WWII Veteran Alfred Sabory, California native and current San Clemente resident, enlisted in the U.S. Army Air Corps at just 17 years old.

title: Sánchez, CHC colleagues lead amicus brief in fight over IRS-ICE taxpayer data sharing
text:
WASHINGTON – Congresswoman Linda Sánchez (D-Calif.), along with fellow Congressional Hispanic Caucus members Chair Adriano Espaillat (D-N.Y.), Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Senator Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) and Congressman Jimmy Gomez (D-Calif.), led 85 House and Senate Democrats in filing a bicameral amicus brief urging the U.S. Court of Appeals for the First Circuit to uphold a lower court’s order blocking Immigration and Customs Enforcement from using – or even viewing – tens of thousands of taxpayers’ addresses obtained from the IRS.

The brief was filed in Community Economic Development Center of Southeastern Massachusetts v. Bessent, the government’s appeal of preliminary relief ordered by Judge Indira Talwani of the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts.

In February, Judge Talwani found that the IRS’s transfer of more than 47,000 taxpayer addresses to ICE in August 2025 likely violated federal tax law, which permits disclosures to law enforcement only when tied to a specific, individualized criminal investigation. Her order froze the underlying data-sharing arrangement and barred ICE from making any further use of the information it had already received.

The lawmakers’ brief argues that reversing Judge Talwani’s order would gut a confidentiality standard Congress has repeatedly declined to loosen for immigration enforcement – rejecting proposals to do so as recently as 2006 – and that the IRS itself assured ITIN filers for nearly three decades would hold. The brief also warns that ICE’s request was so broad, and so stripped of individual identifiers, that it risked sweeping in the wrong people entirely.

“Amici submit this brief to make clear how the Administration’s actions and change in policy encroach upon powers reserved by the Constitution for Congress and contravenes Congress’s longstanding prerogative to prioritize collection of federal tax revenues by preserving the confidentiality of return information,” wrote the amici curiae. “[The] disclosure to ICE imperils effective tax administration, the reliance of millions of taxpayers, and Congress’s clear prerogative to decide when and how sensitive tax information may be used for non-tax purposes.”

This is the fifth brief CHC members have led in litigation challenging the IRS-ICE data-sharing arrangement, part of a continued push in Congress to hold the administration accountable after IRS leadership has repeatedly declined to answer lawmakers’ questions about the disclosures. Unlike two earlier cases, which addressed the data-sharing agreement on paper and how the IRS carried it out, this case is the only one where a court has stopped ICE from using taxpayer data already in its possession.

A copy of the brief is available HERE.

title: Rep. Lucas Advocates for Fiscal Responsibility, Supports the Common Cents Act
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Representative Frank D. Lucas (OK-03), a member of the House Financial Services Committee and Chairman of the House Financial Services Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity, delivered remarks on the House floor advocating for fiscal responsibility by supporting the Common Cents Act. The legislation would codify President Trump’s order to the Treasury to stop production of the one-cent piece, along with allowing the Mint to produce a more cost-effective nickel.

Remarks as prepared for delivery:

I rise today in strong support of the Common Cents Act. This bill has been over a year in the making with my colleagues Ms. McClain and Ranking Member Waters, and I am proud of the product we have put forward.

The one-cent piece, or the penny as it’s commonly called, costs almost four cents to produce. 2024 was the 19th consecutive year the U.S. government lost money keeping the penny in circulation.

That is why last year the President rightly ordered the Treasury Department to stop wasting hard-earned taxpayer dollars to produce the coin and why we’re excited to move forward in codifying this action.

The Common Cents Act also gives flexibility to the Mint to produce a nickel with cheaper materials. In 1866, Congress mandated the nickel be produced from an ally of copper and nickel, and we haven’t updated the composition since. This bill gives the Mint flexibility to produce a cheaper coin while retaining Congress’ responsibility of coining money.

Finally, the bill provides certainty for businesses in their cash transactions with customers, without mandating price controls from the government. We are proud to boast endorsements from the National Retail Federation, National Grocers Association, United Steelworkers International Union, and the American Bankers Association, among many others.

I want to thank Ms. McClain and Ranking Member Waters for their leadership on this issue, and I look forward to enjoying broad bipartisan support from this Body today.

I reserve the balance of my time.

###

title: Rep. Lucas Delivers Opening Statement at Chairman Warsh’s First Financial Services Committee Hearing
text:
Washington, DC – Today, Representative Frank D. Lucas (OK-03), Chairman of the House Financial Services Task Force on Monetary Policy, Treasury Market Resilience, and Economic Prosperity, delivered an opening statement at the House Financial Services Committee hearing on The Federal Reserve’s Semi-Annual Monetary Policy Report.

The hearing is Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s first testimony before Congress as Chairman of the Fed.

Remarks as prepared for delivery:

Welcome Chairman Warsh to your first hearing as Chairman and congratulations on your confirmation. We look forward to your testimony today on the Monetary Policy Report.

In your first meeting you announced a number of welcome reforms including establishing five task forces that many members are eager to get your thoughts on.

For example, former Chair Powell had committed to a review of the Fed’s communications tools, and though we expected that to be completed last August alongside the review of the consensus statement, it has yet to be done.

A review of the Fed’s communications tools is long overdue, and we look forward to your focus on completing that project through the task force.

We’ve also spent time this Congress examining the composition and size of the Fed’s balance sheet, an effort that you are now undertaking at the Fed.

It is vital that the Fed get this right; we welcome continued collaboration on that front.

We have a lot to talk about today – I look forward to your testimony and our discussion. I yield back.

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces Resolutions to Ban Members of Congress from Sexual Relationships and Cohabitation with House Staff
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C., (July 30, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-SC) introduced two resolutions to close the long-exploited loopholes in House ethics rules, banning Members of Congress from engaging in sexual relationships with or living with any House employee.

The first resolution would prohibit any Member, Delegate, or Resident Commissioner from engaging in a sexual relationship with any House employee. Under current rules, the ban only covers a Member's direct staff and staff of committees the Member sits on, leaving thousands of other House employees with zero protection.

A recent example of a member this resolution would apply to include Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ). According to reports,while serving in the House of Representatives, Gallego had sexual relationships with two aides working for Texas Democratic members of Congress. The reports also described Gallego as "very flirtatious" with other staffers.

"If you're a Member of Congress, your priorities should be serving your constituents and this country, not fooling around with staff," said Congresswoman Mace. "There has been a culture of Members abusing their power over staff for far too long and we're done watching it happen. It's gross, it's a disgrace to the taxpayers who send you here to work for them, and it has gone on long enough. Congress is not your personal dating pool. If you can't do your job without hitting on staff, find another job and leave the women you work with alone."

The second resolution would prohibit any Member, Delegate, or Resident Commissioner from cohabitating with any House employee, unless the employee is the Member's spouse. Shockingly, there is no rule prohibiting this today.

Examples of who this resolution would apply to include former Rep. Eric Massa (D-NY), who lived with as many as five aides in a Capitol Hill townhouse before resigning in 2010 amid allegations he groped and sexually harassed multiple young male aides, including those he lived with. This year, another Member has faced reports of living with a senior male staffer at his Capitol Hill residence. Under current House rules, none of it is prohibited.

"A boss and a roommate should never be the same person," said Congresswoman Mace. "No staffer should ever be coming home at night to the person who signs their paycheck. It's inappropriate, it's a conflict of interest, and it should have been banned decades ago. If you're planning on living with a staffer, you should resign first."

Rep. Mace has been leading the charge in Congress on holding Members accountable for their misconduct, and these two resolutions are the next step in her effort to do so.

title: Mackenzie Introduces Bipartisan Resolution Recognizing Medicare's 61st Anniversary
text:
Washington, D.C. – This week, Congressman Ryan Mackenzie (PA-07), representing the Lehigh Valley and the Poconos, introduced a bipartisan resolution recognizing the 61st anniversary of Medicare's enactment and honoring the program's enduring role in providing health coverage to older Americans and individuals with disabilities.

The resolution is led by Congressman Ryan Mackenzie and Congressman Eugene Vindman (VA-07). It is joined by Representatives Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Monica De La Cruz (TX-15), Dina Titus (NV-01), Don Davis (NC-01), Claudia Tenney (NY-24), and Michael Lawler (NY-17).

Signed into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson on July 30, 1965, Medicare has provided health insurance coverage to millions of Americans for more than six decades. Today, the program serves nearly 70 million seniors and individuals with disabilities.

"For 61 years, Medicare has provided millions of Americans with access to quality health care and greater financial security," said Congressman Mackenzie. "This bipartisan resolution recognizes Medicare's lasting impact while honoring the healthcare providers, caregivers, and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services personnel who work every day to ensure beneficiaries receive the care they depend on. Congress must continue to support, protect, and strengthen Medicare for current beneficiaries and future generations.”

"For 61 years, Medicare has represented a simple promise to Virginians: every person 65 and older or with disabilities deserves access to high quality, affordable health care," said Congressman Vindman. "As we mark Medicare's anniversary, we also reaffirm our commitment to protecting and strengthening this vital program for both those using it today and future generations. Health care is not a privilege reserved for a few — it's a promise we must keep for every eligible American across the country."

"Today, millions of Americans, including seniors and Americans with disabilities right here in the Hudson Valley, rely on Medicare every day, and we have a responsibility to protect it. As we mark Medicare’s 61st anniversary, I want to thank the doctors, nurses, caregivers, and healthcare workers who make this program possible. I will continue working to protect the benefits our seniors have earned and strengthen Medicare for generations to come," said Congressman Mike Lawler.

“Across eastern North Carolina, seniors and people with disabilities rely on Medicare for access to doctors, hospitals, prescription drugs, and the quality care they have earned,” said Congressman Don Davis. “For 61 years, Medicare has provided families with greater health and financial security while supporting the health care professionals and caregivers who serve our communities. We must continue working across the aisle to protect and strengthen this vital program for current beneficiaries and generations to come.”

"Over 600,000 Nevadans are enrolled in Medicare and rely on its services to stay healthy. I am proud to recognize the 61st anniversary of this critical program with my colleagues, committing to support and protect Medicare for those who currently receive benefits and for future generations,” said Congresswoman Titus.

The bipartisan resolution:

Commemorates the 61st anniversary of Medicare's enactment.

Recognizes Medicare's role in expanding access to health care, improving health outcomes, and strengthening the financial security of millions of American families.

Honors the healthcare providers, caregivers, and Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services personnel whose work sustains the Medicare program and its beneficiaries nationwide.

The resolution reflects broad bipartisan support for recognizing Medicare's historic significance and the vital role it has played in the lives of millions of Americans since becoming law on July 30, 1965.

title: Congresswoman McCollum Statement on Suspected Iranian Involvement in Attack on Minnesota’s Water Infrastructure
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Betty McCollum, the Ranking Member of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense, issued the following statement on Thursday in response to reporting from the New York Times indicating that investigators suspect that Iranian hackers were behind the cyberattacks on dozens of Minnesota’s municipal water systems earlier this week:

“This incident demonstrates that Minnesota’s municipalities, businesses, and residents must be prepared not only to ward off cybersecurity threats from cybercriminals, but also from terrorist organizations and nation-states,” said Congresswoman McCollum. “It also shows the urgent need for the federal government to advance critical cybersecurity measures to protect small businesses, large enterprises, and local governments by providing state-of-the-art defensive measures to defend against malicious attacks by bad actors who intend to sow chaos and extract ransom. I have worked closely with the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) in partnership with Metro State University to ensure that our communities are prepared to protect themselves from these attacks, and I will continue to aggressively pursue funding and resources to support defensive measures for Minnesota’s businesses and municipalities.”

“Cybersecurity is inseparable from public safety. Although no contamination or public health impacts have been reported, this attack demonstrates the risks posed when malicious actors gain access to the operational technology that supports essential water and wastewater services,” said Faisal Kaleem, Director and Professor of Cybersecurity, Metro State University. “Minnesota’s communities need trained cybersecurity professionals, secure systems, affordable continuous monitoring, and strong partnerships among federal, state, local, and educational institutions. Metro State University is committed to helping build that resilience through education, workforce development, and partnerships that strengthen the critical infrastructure Minnesotans depend on every day.”

“As these attacks become increasingly common, leaders at every level of government are working tirelessly with academic and industry partners for our common defense in the cyber domain, improving information sharing, coordination and cyber talent development to detect and defend against elevated attacks," said Army Maj. Gen. Stefanie Horvath, Minnesota National Guard’s Assistant Adjutant General. "A united approach is just as important in the cyber domain as it is in the physical domain to defend against attacks.”

Congresswoman McCollum has worked to provide federal resources for cybersecurity initiatives since 2021, when she served as the Chair of the House Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense. She believes that Minnesota must continue to work to take advantage of the opportunities provided by this federal funding. These attacks show the necessity of developing a strong workforce that includes cybersecurity professionals who will be able to support efforts to prevent and defend against cyberattacks.

Congresswoman McCollum has also worked closely with Metro State University in Saint Paul, which continues to be a key leader in this effort, and she has supported the expansion of Metro State’s cybersecurity education programs through Community Project Funding. Metro State University has also led the way in partnering with the Minnesota National Guard on cyber training initiatives, providing a model for how Minnesota’s public and private sectors can work with the cybersecurity professionals in the National Guard to defend our communities. Congresswoman McCollum will continue to support these efforts through her work in Congress to supply them with the resources required to protect Minnesotans.

title: Congressman Rich McCormick Recap of Community Job Fair!
text:
ALPHARETTA, Ga. — Congressman Rich McCormick (GA-07) hosted a successful job fair today that brought together more than 100 employers and 1,200 job seekers from across Georgia, connecting hardworking Georgians with employment opportunities in industries ranging from healthcare and manufacturing to technology, public safety, education, skilled trades, and veterans services.
