title: Whitehouse and Cassidy Bill to Protect Well-Meaning Taxpayers from Harsh Penalties Approved by Senate Finance Committee
text:
Fairness in Foreign Filing Act would benefit ordinary taxpayers while keeping pressure on wealthy tax cheats

Washington, D.C. – The Fairness in Foreign Filing Act, authored by U.S. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI) and Bill Cassidy (R-LA), was approved by the Senate Finance Committee today as part of the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act. The legislation would clarify the Internal Revenue Service’s authority to assess and collect penalties and spare honest taxpayers from steep penalties for unintentionally failing to file certain tax forms.

“Honest American taxpayers shouldn’t have to worry about getting punished with huge fines for failing to file forms they didn’t know they had to file,” said Whitehouse. “Our bipartisan legislation would create a fairer and simpler process for those that miss filing international reporting forms while ensuring wealthy tax evaders aren’t let off the hook.”

Taxpayers in the U.S. who receive money from abroad, have foreign financial interests, or engage in certain foreign transactions are required to file international reporting forms with the IRS. Penalties for failure to file or reporting inaccurate information are severe. Unfortunately, these large penalties are hitting unsuspecting taxpayers—often with lower incomes—who were unaware of their reporting obligations. The IRS has been systematically assessing these penalties and causing greater hardship for taxpayers, only to ultimately abate 74 percent of them upon further review. Another challenge for taxpayers is that certain international reporting forms are due before tax filing, causing inadvertent late filings.

All the while, conflicting court decisions have called into question the IRS’s ability to assess certain penalties, letting wealthy tax cheats off the hook while causing confusion and disparate treatment for taxpayers based on where they live. Farhy v. Commissioner found that the IRS lacks the authority to assess penalties for failing to file a form reporting ownership in certain foreign corporations. Two Circuit Courts have ruled that the IRS can, in fact,assess such penalties, but those rulings only apply in their respective jurisdictions.

The Fairness in Foreign Filing Act would ensure well-meaning taxpayers avoid unnecessary penalties by clarifying their reporting obligations and simplifying the reporting process. Specifically, the bill would create a standardized pre-assessment process for penalties for failing to file certain forms related to foreign businesses, trusts, and gifts to give taxpayers a clear path to get administrative review before assessment. The bill would also establish a default rule clarifying the assessability of penalties or additions to tax in the Code and align filing dates of international reporting forms with tax filing deadlines to prevent taxpayers from inadvertently filing them late.

title: Wyden, Crapo Applaud Committee Passage of Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act
text:
Washington, D.C.—U.S. Senate Finance Committee Ranking Member Ron Wyden (D-Oregon) and Chairman Mike Crapo (R-Idaho) lauded today’s committee passage of legislation that would improve the taxpayer experience by strengthening taxpayer rights and modernizing IRS operations, helping build a more efficient, responsive and taxpayer-focused tax administration system.

The committee’s 26-1 passage of the Taxpayer Assistance and Service (TAS) Act, which includes recommendations from the National Taxpayer Advocate and committee members from both parties, sends the legislation to the full Senate for consideration.

“Today the Finance Committee took an important step towards common sense reforms that will protect taxpayers and modernize the IRS,” Wyden said. “I look forward to advancing these reforms and getting them signed in to law so American taxpayers are no longer scammed by shady tax prep schemes and will get help filing their taxes. This marks a key step towards restoring fairness to the tax system.”

Wyden also spotlighted a provision in the bill that would help farmers and fishermen in Oregon by extending their annual filing deadline from March 1 to April 15.

"I've heard in town halls and other settings throughout the state how confusing it's been for farmers and fisherman to have a filing deadline separate from the standard April 15 date for individuals," Wyden said. "I'm gratified the work to secure the end of this needless confusion for these hardworking Oregonians is in the bill."

“This product reflects years of bipartisan efforts to translate stories of casework frustrations into tangible fixes designed to make the IRS work more efficiently for the American people,” said Crapo. “I thank Senator Wyden and members of the Committee for their partnership in this effort and look forward to advancing this comprehensive, bipartisan bill.”

title: Wyden, Merkley, Colleagues Demand Trump Administration Reinstate Vital HIV/AIDS Prevention Program
text:
Senators fighting $2 billion in funding cuts from the emergency plan for AIDS relief (PEPFAR).

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley said today they have joined colleagues in demanding the Trump administration immediately approve a U.S. Department of State transfer of $2 billion in funding to the U.S. Centers for Disease Control (CDC) for the President’s Emergency Plan For AIDS Relief (PEPFAR).

PEPFAR was established in 2003 and has had longstanding bipartisan congressional support. Trump recently launched his “America First Global Health Strategy,” which aims to end American humanitarian support abroad, particularly for PEPFAR-related programs. In a letter to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, the Senators argued that halting the transfer of essential funding for PEPFAR will do far more harm than good, and open the door to potential new international health epidemics.

“Following this Administration’s dismantlement of USAID, a key implementor of PEPFAR programming, countries are struggling to maintain the programs set up by USAID and PEPFAR funding, facing more new infections and more deaths,” the senators wrote. “Without USAID, CDC’s global health infrastructure remains the most effective tool the U.S. has to monitor and prevent global health emergencies.”

The senators raised concerns over the ethics of the Trump administration’s attempt to move PEPFAR to a fee-for-service program, in exchange for access to natural resources, specifically critical minerals. This administration is using life-saving medication as leverage for its own political agenda and personal gain, in some of the poorest and most underserved countries.

“This type of coercive diplomacy does not serve U.S. global health interests and is extremely susceptible to risk of corruption. We urge the Trump Administration to immediately rescind any guidance suggesting that DOS will no longer honor the transfer of $2 billion to CDC and commit to upholding this long-standing transfer that keeps Americans safe,” the senators continued.

The administration is aiming to phase out PEPFAR in five years, which risks leaving countries in need with little time to prepare for their own health care independence.

The letter was led by Senator Jon Ossoff, D-Ga. In addition to Wyden and Merkley, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Michael Bennet, D-Colo., Cory Booker, D-N.J., John Hickenlooper, D-Colo., Chris Van Hollen, D-Md., Ben Ray Lujan, D-N.M., Tim Kaine, D-Va., Andy Kim, D-N.J., Amy Klobuchar, D-Minn., Edward J. Markey, D-Mass., Bernard Sanders, D-Vt. and Adam Schiff, D-Calif.

title: Young, Coons Introduce Bill to Support Startups and Strengthen Regional Innovation
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Todd Young (R-Ind.) and Chris Coons (D-Del.) introduced the Build to Scale Reauthorization Act, which would reauthorize the Economic Development Administration’s (EDA) Build to Scale program through fiscal year 2030.

Build to Scale is a competitive grant program that helps strengthen regional innovation ecosystems by supporting entrepreneurs, technology startups, and organizations that connect startups with the capital, infrastructure, and expertise needed to grow. Since 2014, the program has awarded more than $272 million to 426 projects across all 50 states, Washington, D.C., and Puerto Rico, helping support more than 58,600 jobs and 6,200 startups.

“America’s long-term economic strength depends on our ability to turn innovation into opportunity,” said Senator Young. “The Build to Scale program helps entrepreneurs, universities, investors, and local organizations work together to develop new technologies, launch businesses, and create good-paying jobs. This legislation will ensure Hoosier innovators and communities across the country have the tools they need to compete in the industries of the future.”

“Delaware is a state built on innovation. We know what it takes to turn a good idea into a thriving business: support, investment, and expertise,” said Senator Coons. “This bipartisan bill brings those needed pieces to startups and entrepreneurs across the country, so Americans can continue to reach for their dreams, create jobs, and grow our economy.”

“Indiana’s future competitiveness depends on our ability to help innovators build companies here at home. The Northeast Indiana Innovation Community was proud to be a past recipient of the EDA’s Build to Scale program, and we’ve seen firsthand how it strengthens the partnerships that move new technologies from idea to marketplace. Reauthorizing this bipartisan program will help ensure that communities across Indiana continue to create jobs, attract investment, and compete in an increasingly innovation-driven economy.”

– Northeast Indiana Innovation Community

“WHIN’s Innovation as a Service program, funded through this EDA grant, has completed 36 projects and has 9 more in progress across 22 Indiana organizations, spanning manufacturers, agricultural operations, and schools, creating or upskilling more than 50 jobs along the way. These sensors are solving real problems: preventing spoiled food during power outages, catching equipment issues before they cause costly downtime, and replacing expensive legacy monitoring systems with more affordable technology. Programs like Build to Scale are exactly what regional innovation networks like WHIN need to keep proving this model works for Hoosier communities and beyond.”

– Wabash Heartland Innovation Network

The Build to Scale Reauthorization Act of 2026 would:

Reauthorize the Build to Scale program through FY2030 at $50 million annually.

Expand access to capital for entrepreneurs and technology startups seeking to commercialize new ideas and products.

Increase outreach to rural, trade-impacted, and economically distressed communities to reduce barriers to participation.

Authorize cost-share waivers for certain economically distressed communities to reduce barriers to participation.

Strengthen coordination among the Economic Development Administration, National Science Foundation, Department of Energy, and related federal innovation initiatives.

Require the Department of Commerce to issue a Notice of Funding Opportunity within 90 days of enactment to help accelerate grant availability.

Text of the legislation can be found here.

The Build to Scale Reauthorization Act of 2026 was introduced in the U.S. House of Representatives in May by Representatives Haley Stevens (D-MI-11) and Jim Baird (R-IN-4).

Since 2018, Indiana organizations have received more than $4 million in Build to Scale awards to strengthen the state’s innovation economy. Recipients include Elevate Ventures, the Northeast Indiana Innovation Center, Purdue University Northwest, The Dimension Mill, the Central Indiana Corporate Partnership, and the Wabash Heartland Innovation Network.

The legislation is supported by a broad coalition of innovation, research, and economic development organizations, including: SSTI, the Association of University Research Parks (AURP), Cornell University, Georgetown University’s Office of Technology Commercialization, the Center on Rural Innovation, US Ignite, Launch Tennessee, JumpStart Inc., Rev1 Ventures, Arch Grants, mHUB, BioSTL, the Maryland Clean Energy Center, the Washington Technology Industry Association, and the Greater Phoenix Economic Council.

title: Rep. Adam Smith Introduces Resolution Calling for Equal Tax Treatment of Wage Income and Capital Gains
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. (July 31, 2026) – Today, Rep. Adam Smith introduced a resolution built on a simple idea: a dollar earned should be a dollar taxed, full stop. This resolution calls on Congress to start simplifying the tax code so working-class Americans and the ultra-wealthy play by the same rules.

"For decades, we've asked working families to play by one set of rules while the wealthiest Americans play by another. A teacher, a machinist, a nurse — they see taxes taken out of every paycheck before they ever see the money,” said Rep. Adam Smith. “Meanwhile, the ultra-wealthy grow their fortunes by trillions of dollars a year; paying next to nothing in taxes due to loopholes emplaced quietly over the past 40 years. It's time we started simplifying the tax code around one basic principle: a dollar earned is a dollar taxed, no matter who earns it or how.”

“This resolution tells Congress and the Ways and Means Committee to stop looking away from a system that treats identical gains completely differently depending on whose name is on them. If we're serious about the debt and serious about fairness, this is where we have to start."

The resolution has drawn early support from tax law experts, including Ray D. Madoff, Professor at Boston College Law School and author of “The Second Estate: How the Tax Code Made an American Aristocracy."

"I've spent years studying this issue, and the fix isn't complicated: broaden the income tax so it captures every form of monetary gain, not just wages. This resolution asks the correct, and long overdue questions. I'm glad to see Congress willing to take a serious look at why our tax code treats income so differently depending on where it comes from," said Ray D. Madoff, Professor at Boston College Law School.

Here's the problem:

The country is $39 trillion in debt — and the tax system isn't bringing in enough money to keep up, because too much income never gets taxed in the first place.

Regular paychecks are carrying the load. Income taxes make up about 49% of all federal revenue, and payroll taxes make up another 35% — meaning 84 cents of every federal dollar comes from taxes on wages. Taxes on investments, inheritances, and business ownership make up the rest.

The wealthiest 1% now hold about $55 trillion in net worth, while most Americans don't have enough savings to cover an emergency. Seventy years ago, top earners paid a 94% tax rate on that income. Today the top rate is just 37% — and many still pay far less through additional loopholes.

Billionaires can grow richer by billions a year and barely pay taxes on it, because that money comes from stock and business ownership going up in value, not a paycheck. A dollar earned that way isn't taxed anywhere near like a dollar earned at a job.

Some of the richest people in America pay a lower tax rate than teachers and nurses. A 2021 investigation into leaked IRS records found several of the wealthiest Americans paid a true tax rate in the low single digits, or no income tax at all due to tax loopholes, compared to how much their wealth grew each year — lower than many middle-class workers pay on their salaries.

The resolution calls on the House Ways and Means Committee to hold hearings on this gap, and urges Congress to start simplifying the tax code so every American — whether they earn a paycheck or sell a stock — is taxed the same way on the same amount of money earned.

title: Amo and 33 Members Send Up Signal to Trump: Restore Vital Weather Balloon Launches Amid Extreme Weather
text:
Washington, D.C.– TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) led 33 Members of Congress in calling on the Trump Administration to restore the twice-a-day weather balloon launch schedule, as extreme weather and high heat hit across the country.

Twice-a-day weather balloon launches collect information from high in the atmosphere that allows for more accurate forecasting. Current disruptions to the balloon launch schedule create data gaps that undermine confidence in forecast accuracy.

The Members write:

We are alarmed by the reduction in weather balloon launches and its impact on the accuracy of weather forecasting across the United States. Timely and accurate weather forecasts are critical to protecting the lives, livelihoods, and property of the American people.

This is a manufactured crisis. President Trump and DOGE haphazardly slashed the NWS workforce by roughly 15 percent without considering the impact on public safety. Now, the American people are paying the price. Current efforts to fill staffing gaps at NWS are too little too late. Severe weather will not wait for NWS to hire and train hundreds of new staff. NWS must immediately restore balloon launch capacity before an inaccurate or delayed forecast puts our constituents in harm's way.

Continued failure to follow the twice-a-day balloon launch schedule undermines the accuracy of NWS weather forecasts and increases the likelihood that the American people will be left unprepared for severe weather events. Forcing our constituents to accept increased risks because of your shortsighted and partisan staffing cuts is unacceptable. You must protect Americans’ lives, livelihoods, and property by immediately returning to the twice-a-day balloon launch schedule.

The full letter can be found here.

The letter was signed by Representatives Wesley Bell (D-MO-01), Donald Beyer (D-VA-08), Suzanne Bonamici (D-OR-01), Julia Brownley (D-CA-26), André Carson (D-IN-07), Ed Case (D-HI-01), Kathy Castor (D-FL-14), Emanuel Cleaver (D-MO-05), Jim Costa (D-CA-21), Jasmine Crockett (D-TX-30), Sharice Davids (D-KS-03), Adriano Espaillat (D-NY-13), Lizzie Fletcher (D-TX-07), Maxwell Frost (D-FL-10), Sylvia Garcia (D-TX-29), Adelita Grijalva (D-AZ-07), Pablo Hernández (D-PR), Jared Huffman (D-CA-02), Sara Jacobs (D-CA-51), Henry Johnson (D-GA-04), Stephen Lynch (D-MA-08), Seth Magaziner (D-RI-02), April McClain Delaney (D-MD-06), Christian Menefee (D-TX-18), Seth Moulton (D-MA-06), Joe Neguse (D-CO-02), Brittany Pettersen (D-CO-07), Emily Randall (D-WA-06), Deborah Ross (D-NC-02), Haley Stevens (D-MI-11), Shri Thanedar (D-MI-13), Jill Tokuda (D-HI-02), and Paul Tonko (D-NY-20).

Background

Ranking Member of the House Science, Space, and Technology Environment Subcommittee, Congressman Amo has fought to reverse Trump’s cuts to the National Weather Service and protect American meteorological might.

In Summer 2025, Amo led the charge to reverse Trump’s damaging Department of Government Efficiency (DOGE) cuts to the National Weather Service staff. After months of public pressure, the National Weather Service announced plans to hire 450 new staff.

title: Amo & Experts Help Seniors Avoid Scams in Kickoff to Fighting for an Affordable America Stops
text:
Lincoln, RI – TODAY, Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI) hosted a panel featuring anti-scam experts to educate older Rhode Islanders on how to avoid scams and keep their hard-earned money from being stolen by bad actors. The experts shared ways to protect yourself and your loved ones from fraudsters, and Congressman Amo shared what he’s doing in Congress to stop the proliferation of scams.

“A key part of making life more affordable is ensuring that as much of your money as possible stays in your pocket,” said Congressman Gabe Amo (D-RI). “With costs on the rise because of Trump’s illegal war with Iran and erratic tariffs, scammers are worsening financial strain by taking advantage and targeting well-meaning Rhode Islanders already affected by Republicans’ affordability crisis. By bringing together law enforcement, elder justice advocates, and financial experts, we were able to provide critical resources to older Rhode Islanders about how to avoid scams. As a founding co-chair of the bipartisan Congressional Stop Scams Caucus, I will keep fighting to stop the scam scourge and pass commonsense legislation like my STOP Scams Against Seniors Act and my National Strategy to Combat Scams Act to make sure that Rhode Islanders ' hard-earned money stays right where it belongs.”

Background

Congressman Amo is a founding co-chair of the Congressional Stop Scams Caucus, a bipartisan group of Members of Congress dedicated to protecting Americans from scams.

Amo introduced the bipartisan, bicameral Strengthening Task Forces to Oppose Predatory (STOP) Scams Against Seniors Act, which would authorize the creation of Elder Justice Task Forces to help local, state, and Federal agencies work together to investigate and prosecute illegal scammers. The bill is co-led by Congressman Jeffersen Shreve (R-IN) in the House and led by Senator Ashley Moody (R-FL) in the Senate.

Amo also introduced the bipartisan, bicameral National Strategy for Combating Scams Act, which would establish a federal working group led by the Federal Bureau of Investigation to coordinate the efforts of more than a dozen federal agencies in combating scams. The bill is co-led by Congressman Derek Schmidt (R-KS) in the U.S. House. Companion legislation was introduced in the U.S. Senate by Senators Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Rick Scott (R-FL), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), and Ashley Moody (R-FL).

title: Barrett Celebrates Local Businesses, Meets with First Responders, Students
text:
Lansing, Mich. — Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) on Thursday and Friday met with first responders, educators, students, and workers across mid-Michigan as he visited Lansing Community College’s Aviation Maintenance Technology Center, Clinton Area Ambulance Service, Livingston County EMS Education, and celebrated Highland Engineering’s 40th anniversary and Merlo Construction’s ribbon cutting.

“Every day, Michiganders across our state are working hard and providing the services that keep our communities strong — from saving lives in emergencies to educating the next generation,” said Barrett. “Meeting with first responders, educators, construction professionals, engineers, and other mid-Michigan workers allows me to hear directly from the people on the front lines about the challenges they face and the policies they need to do their jobs and succeed. I’m committed to supporting our workforce, strengthening our communities, and delivering results for Mid-Michigan.”

On Thursday, Barrett toured the Lansing Community College Aviation Maintenance Technology Center, which is located at the Mason-Jewett Field Airport. Barrett met with college leaders, educators, and students in the aviation technology program, which is recognized as the best in the Midwest. They discussed the program’s success at preparing students for careers and the program’s opportunities for expansion. Barrett recently highlighted the program in a conversation about aviation careers in the House Transportation and Infrastructure Committee.

Barrett then met with leadership at the Clinton County Ambulance Service Authority to hear about their lifesaving work serving northern Clinton County and the needs the agency is facing.

On Friday, Barrett joined Highland Engineering Inc. in Howell for the company’s 40th anniversary celebration. Highland began as a fixture and automation design firm and now provides is a leading defense contractor, providing the military with equipment for classified information facilities, water purification, electricity, medical care, cargo transportation, and more.

Barrett then attended the ribbon cutting for Merlo Construction’s new headquarters in Genoa Township near Brighton. Merlo, a family-owned business previously based in Milford, is a leading contractor providing construction site development, concrete, asphalt, and rigging services.

At Livingston County EMS, Barrett toured the cutting-edge education center and met with instructors and other emergency responders to hear about their service to the community and their program that provides hands-on education for future emergency medical professionals. Barrett also toured the agency’s hangar and ambulance bay.

title: Barrett Joins Michigan Delegation in Bipartisan Effort to Bring Coast Guard Drone Testing to Michigan
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Tom Barrett (MI-07) joined colleagues from Michigan in the U.S. House and Senate in a bipartisan effort to bring Coast Guard drone testing to northern Michigan. Michigan’s decades-long manufacturing legacy has made it a national leader in autonomous systems, with the expertise, strategic location, and partnerships to support Coast Guard testing missions.

Establishing Northern Michigan as a designated site for Coast Guard drone testing would:

Build on the region's growing leadership in autonomous technology.

Create new opportunities for research and workforce development.

Ensure the Coast Guard can test next-generation technologies in real-world Great Lakes conditions.

Help the Coast Guard save lives, respond to disasters faster, improve maritime safety and security, inspect critical infrastructure, and monitor the environment.

Strengthen search-and-rescue operations—all while reducing costs and keeping people out of harm's way.

The letter was also signed by Senators Elissa Slotkin (D-MI) and Gary Peters (D-MI) along with Representatives Jack Bergman (MI-01), John Moolenar (MI-02), Hillary Scholten (MI-03), and Haley Stevens (MI-11).

“Earlier this year, the Administration released its Maritime Action Plan: Restoring America's Maritime Dominance, directing the Coast Guard to make one or more such designations, including in the Great Lakes,” said the lawmakers. “Northern Michigan is an ideal location for this designation given that Coast Guard Air Station Traverse City already possesses the operational expertise, strategic location, and public-private partnerships needed to become the Coast Guard’s premier site for testing autonomous maritime technologies.”

“Serving all five Great Lakes, Air Station Traverse City is uniquely positioned to support Coast Guard missions ranging from search and rescue to homeland security and disaster response,” continued the lawmakers. “Combined with uncongested airspace, significant capacity for expansion, and a community that embraces Coast Guard families and operations, it provides an exceptional platform for continued investment and innovation.”

title: Congressman Biggs’s Response to Final Environmental Impact Statement for the Colorado River Basin
text:
GILBERT, ARIZONA- Today, the U.S. Bureau of Reclamation released its long-awaited Post-2026 Operational Guidelines for Lake Powell and Lake Mead – Final Environmental Impact Statement.

The framework reduces Arizona’s share of the Colorado River usage through 2036 – though not by as much as the Draft Statement proposed earlier this spring.

Congressman Biggs released the following statement:

“While I am grateful for the cooperation of California and Nevada and the federal government's willingness to listen to the concerns of the Lower Basin States, I am extremely disappointed that the Upper Basin States have continuously refused to come to the table to help bring relief to the entire basin. Over many previous years, Arizona has drastically cut its water usage to prove its responsible partnership with both the Upper and Lower Basin States. We cannot afford to take on more cuts, yet here we are with another framework that puts Arizona last.

“Over the past two years, I worked with the federal government on a solution that could be less harmful to Arizona than the options presented by the Upper Basin States. I understood, however, that Arizona could not rely solely on this new framework for its water future security, so I have worked in Congress on other solutions to help our state enhance existing infrastructure and bring relief to stakeholders most affected by existing drought conditions and ongoing cuts. I will continue to take action to bring relief to our state and ensure that we can protect our citizens, agriculture industries, and everyone else relying on this life-giving resource.”

In March 2026, Congressman Biggs led Arizona’s Republican Members of Congress in submitting a formal comment letter to Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum expressing serious concerns about the Draft Environmental Impact Statement.

In April 2026, Congressman Biggs co-led a letter with Congressman Greg Stanton (AZ-09) to Interior Secretary Doug Burgum and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought, successfully urging the Bureau of Reclamation to release federal funds to address the ongoing drought across the Colorado River Basin. Reclamation announced they would release $450 million – $350 million of which will flow to Lower Basin States.

Earlier this month, Congressman Biggs led a letter to U.S. House leadership, urging the inclusion of funds in the recently introduced emergency funding package to address the increasingly dire condition of the Colorado River Basin. The funding would support water infrastructure, investments, upgrades, and long-term planning for the future of this vital resource.

In addition to these efforts, Congressman Biggs worked behind the scenes to meet with federal, state, and local stakeholders to put Arizona in the best-possible position for this new framework. Because, in large part, of this advocacy, the Grand Canyon State received a better share of the new framework than what was previously introduced.

title: REP. BOEBERT INTRODUCES THE FREEDOM TO SHIP ACT
text:
Washington, DC—Today, Rep. Lauren Boebert (CO-04), Co-Chair of the Congressional Second Amendment Caucus, introduced HR 9979 the Freedom to Ship Act, landmark legislation to protect the right of responsible Americans to lawfully ship firearms via common carriers. The bill also repeals the prohibition on mailing handguns through the United States Postal Service.

“For far too long, common carriers have interfered with the lawful transportation of firearms,” said Rep. Boebert. “The Biden Administration’s agenda was to take away our Second Amendment rights, and this legislation helps reverse that. The Freedom to Ship Act prohibits common carriers from forcing Federal Firearms Licensees to sign unjust, non-negotiable contracts and pay exorbitant fees. Discriminating against responsible gun owners hurts small businesses and undermines our Second Amendment right to Keep and Bear Arms.”

“Common carriers like the U.S. Postal Service, UPS, and FedEx often impose harsh and unnecessary bans, restrictions, or excessive fees on shipping firearms, parts, and ammunition,” said Aidan Johnston, Director of Federal Affairs at Gun Owners of America. “Commerce runs on shipping. Denying gun owners and manufacturers access to the carriers every other industry relies on is a denial of the right itself. Gun Owners of America is proud to endorse Rep. Boebert’s Freedom to Ship Act, to bar common carriers from prohibiting the shipment of firearms, parts, and ammunition and infringing on the Second Amendment.”

Background: Under the Biden Administration, some common carriers have forced FFLs to sign non-negotiable adhesion contracts to enforce unconstitutional gun control aligned with the Administration’s war on the Second Amendment and responsible gun owners. Similarly, the federal government has prohibited shipment of handguns through USPS for nearly 100 years. The government’s discrimination against responsible gun owners places an undue burden on Americans exercising their Second Amendment rights and unreasonably restricts commerce. This legislation is needed to reverse the interference and overreach that intensified under the Biden Administration and restore the ability of law-abiding Americans to ship firearms without discrimination.

This legislation supports small businesses, facilitates greater interstate commerce, and ensures that common carriers cannot infringe on the rights of responsible Americans.

The Freedom to Ship Act is supported by Gun Owners of America, the National Rifle Association and the National Association for Gun Rights

Cosponsors of the Freedom to Ship Act include: Rep. Sheri Biggs (SC-03), Rep. Michael Cloud (TX-27), and Rep. Clay Higgins (LA-03).

title: Key U.S. House Committee Approves Case's Bipartisan Bill To Combat Invasive Species
text:
(Washington, DC) – U.S. Representative Ed Case (HI-01) announced that the U.S. House Natural Resources Committee (Committee) has unanimously approved his National Wildlife Refuge System Invasive Species Strike Team Act, which would significantly expand federal efforts to combat invasive species, responsible for severely impacting environments across the country.

“Hawai‘i in particular faces unique challenges from invasive species. Our isolation has led to the evolution of many endemic species that are found nowhere else on Earth,” said Case, who formerly served six years on the House Natural Resources Committee and is in his eighth year on the House Appropriations Committee.

“Unfortunately, these native species often lack the defenses to compete with or resist the pressures of invasive plants and animals, which can rapidly alter ecosystems and displace local species.

“In Hawai‘i, invasive species have caused significant ecological damage, threatening the survival of native birds and plants. Protecting Hawaii’s unique biodiversity is not just an environmental necessity – it is a cultural imperative that reflects the identity and heritage of the Hawaiian people.”

“For island communities like Guam, invasive species are more than an environmental concern—they threaten our native ecosystems, agriculture, economy, and way of life,” said Congressman James Moylan (R-Guam).

“Once an invasive species becomes established on an island, the cost of eradication can be enormous, and in many cases, the damage cannot be undone. This bipartisan legislation takes a proactive approach by strengthening rapid response and early detection efforts within our National Wildlife Refuge System. By investing in prevention today, we can better protect America’s natural resources, preserve our unique biodiversity, and reduce far greater costs in the future.”

"We are pleased with the passage of this measure that prioritizes funds and measures towards early detection through identifying, reporting, and eradicating invasive species and the harm it causes in the National Wildlife Refuge System lands and waters and its surrounding areas,” said Jonnetta "Jonee" Leina'ala Peters, Executive Director of the Conservation Council for Hawai‘i. “Early detection is critical in protecting endangered and threatened species. This is also a major step in eradicating invasive species that harm animals, humans, food sources, and the economy."

“Invasive species are putting increased pressure on native wildlife and are especially damaging across our national wildlife refuges,” said Jill Feldhusen, senior manager of wildlife policy at the National Wildlife Federation.

“By establishing dedicated, regional strike teams, this bipartisan bill helps refuges respond more rapidly to invasive species threats before they cause lasting harm. Thank you, Representative Ed Case, for reintroducing the National Wildlife Refuge System Invasive Species Strike Team Act and broadening the impact of cross-jurisdictional collaboration.

Case continued: “Invasive species are not just a localized problem; they pose a significant threat to the integrity of our natural world. Addressing this crisis requires a coordinated and comprehensive approach, focusing on prevention, early detection, and effective management strategies to safeguard our vulnerable ecosystems.

“This legislation will codify the existing Invasive Species Strike Teams program currently operated by the U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service (FWS). These specialized teams play an essential role in managing emerging invasive species, employing strategies tailored to local conditions across the National Wildlife Refuge System. With multiple teams strategically positioned in all nine FWS regions across our country, they are on the front lines, addressing the unique challenges posed by invasive species.”

Case said formally establishing the Invasive Species Strike Teams program will create a stable and legally supported framework to ensure consistent funding and enhance management efforts. The act also signifies a transformative shift within the FWS, moving from a reactive, species-by-species approach to a more strategic, ecosystem-wide framework for managing emerging invasive species.

“The act also mandates enhanced coordination and reporting through integrated systems and standardized procedures, ensuring transparency and enabling us to track progress with annual reports to Congress and the public,” said Case.

“Furthermore, it authorizes $10 million annually from Fiscal Year 2027 through 2033 to support ongoing initiatives.”

Case introduced the measure after federal invasive species experts toured O‘ahu to research the effects of invasive species on island communities. The bill also directs these experts to produce a report summarizing the Strike Teams’ work and advising how they can continue to help Hawai‘i and island territories. Following approval by the Committee, the measure awaits action by the full House.

title: Texas Democratic Congressional Delegation & Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Urge Answers Before Action Jeopardizing Big
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, Congressman Joaquin Castro (TX-20) and Texas Congressmembers, joined by House Natural Resources Committee Ranking Member Jared Huffman, urged Trump Administration officials to delay work on a proposed road across and over Big Bend National Park’s Mariscal Mountain until specific details of the project are made fully available and questions answered about the potentially irreparable destruction the project poses.

“It is hard to understand the added value of a patrol road across Mariscal Mountain. The existing road just north of the mountain is regularly patrolled and sufficient for Border Patrol operations,” the members wrote. “This new, proposed road would sit 1,700 feet above the border in one of the least trafficked stretches of the entire southern border, where anyone crossing would first climb 1,400-foot cliffs to approach the road. This poses no benefit to border security and would only cause irrevocable damage to the mountain.”

A copy of the letter can be found here.

The letter is addressed to Secretary of State Marco Rubio, Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, U.S. Customs and Border Protection Commissioner Rodney S. Scott, and W.C. “Chad” McIntosh, Commissioner of the International Boundary and Water Commission, United States Section.

The International Boundary and Water Commission (IBWC) is the binational body charged with enforcing the boundary and water treaties between the United States and Mexico. The issue will be of acute interest to both the U.S. and Mexico Sections of the IBWC because of the potential damage to the Rio Grande and immediate environs on both sides of the river.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection has not released details regarding the proposed road aside from a small-scale map with the proposed alignment and that it would be 24 feet wide. The letter asks for road design and engineering details, spoil disposal plans, and line items for rock excavation, controlled blasting, drilling and shooting, vibration monitoring, or embankment placement.

In addition, it asks the IBWC U.S. Section if it has received any notice from the U.S. of the Mariscal Mountain alignment and whether the Mexican Section has been notified. Federal law authorizing waivers that set aside existing regulatory requirements for border wall construction do not apply to U.S.-Mexico Treaty obligations. The letter seeks confirmation that the U.S. acknowledges that fact.

title: OSV News article on new Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Protection and Prevention Caucus'Bipartisan duo announces new anti-trafficking caucus in Congress'
text:
By Kate Scanlon

Published July 31, 2026 at 5:35 PM

WASHINGTON (OSV News) — A bipartisan pair of lawmakers announced July 30 they will form and co-chair a new caucus in the U.S. House aimed at the prevention of human trafficking.

Reps. Chris Smith, R-N.J. and Kweisi Mfume, D-Md., said the Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Protection and Prevention Caucus — named in honor of the abolitionist and statesman — will work to advance legislation to prevent human trafficking, prosecute traffickers, and strengthen support and protection for victims, and facilitate greater cooperation to prevent the trafficking through partnerships between government, law enforcement, private and faith-based organizations.

“I am honored to announce the formation of the Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Protection and Prevention Caucus alongside my Co-Chair, Rep. Mfume, who is fiercely committed to ending the modern-day slavery that is human trafficking,” Smith, a longtime Catholic lawmaker, said in a statement.

Mfume noted they made the announcement on the annual World Day Against Trafficking in Persons.

A group of youths is seen in Togo Feb. 8, 2025, marking the beginning of a campaign called "Restoring Hope in Africa: A Jubilee Call to End Human Trafficking." On July 30, 2026, World Day Against Trafficking in Persons, Reps. Chris Smith, R-N.J., and Kweisi Mfume, D-Md., announced the formation of the bipartisan Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Protection and Prevention Caucus in the House. (OSV News photo/courtesy PACTPAN)

‘A scourge on our collective humanity’

“Human trafficking is modern-day slavery and a scourge on our collective humanity,” Mfume said. “Nearly 27 million people worldwide are trapped in forms of forced labor and human bondage, and Americans in all 50 states have been victimized as well.”

“We owe it to every survivor and victim to pass comprehensive anti-trafficking legislation out of the Congress and send it to the President’s desk,” Mfume continued. “This Caucus and anti-trafficking organizations across the country represent proof of our collective intention to get that done, no matter how long it takes.”

Smith added, “Human trafficking is an ever-evolving crime, as traffickers are constantly finding new ways—both in-person and virtually—to exploit, manipulate, and abuse victims. To meet these changing and challenging demands, this Caucus will work tirelessly to advance new anti-trafficking legislation—especially and including the Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Prevention and Protection Act of 2025 (H.R. 1144), which Rep. Mfume and I introduced earlier this Congress—that uplifts and empowers survivors and raises awareness of this global problem.”

Smith and Mfume urged the House to promptly take up H.R. 1144 for debate and a vote.

Bill would protect critical funding, programs

“The House passage of the Frederick Douglass TVPRA will bring us one step closer to finally eradicating this modern-day slavery,” they said in a joint statement. “Delay means denial for the millions of men, women, and children currently trapped in trafficking situations. We are working every single day—especially and including World Day Against Trafficking in Persons—to get this critical legislation over the finish line to protect critical funding and programs.”

The Frederick Douglass Trafficking Victims Protection and Prevention Caucus will also be bicameral, Smith’s office said, as Sen. Marsha Blackburn, R-Tenn., plans to form a complementary caucus in the Senate. Blackburn’s office did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

If enacted, H.R. 1144 would “reauthorize and bolster anti-human trafficking programs across numerous federal agencies, including the State Department, Department of Justice, Department of Homeland Security, and Department of Health and Human Services; ensure robust prosecutions for human trafficking crimes, along with thorough investigations and jail time commensurate with the crime; and authorize the first-ever housing program for survivors ensuring wrap-around case management, including education, life skills training, mental health services, and employment assistance,” Smith’s office said.

title: Courtney, Electric Boat, Local Officials, & Submarine Industry Leaders Celebrate Block VI Virginia-class & Build II Columbia-class Construction Contract Awards
text:
NORWICH, CT – Yesterday, Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee, Mark Rayha, President of General Dynamics-Electric Boat, Peter Baker, President of the Metal Trades Council of New London County, AFL-CIO, and Chris Jewell, President of Collins & Jewell and Chairman of the Eastern Connecticut Workforce Investment Board’s Board of Directors, joined Jill Rusk, Mayor of the City of Groton, and a large crowd of state and local officials, educators, and leaders in Connecticut’s submarine industrial base to discuss the newly announced $76.6 billion construction contract awards to Electric Boat for nine Block VI Virginia-class submarines and five Build II Columbia-class submarines.

Congress authorized the Virginia-class Block VI contract in 2023 in the FY24 NDAA and the Columbia-class Build II contract in 2025 in the FY26 NDAA. The legislative language in both bills originated in the Seapower subcommittee’s marks.

Congressman Joe Courtney (CT-02), Ranking Member of the House Seapower and Projection Forces Subcommittee

“This is not a normal or incremental contract award announcement that’s coming out of the Pentagon or the Navy. The record size and ‘buying in bulk’ structure of this contract provides the much needed long-horizon demand signal for the submarine industry. This legally enforceable binding contract raises the level of the federal government’s commitment to the Virginia and Columbia programs, and gives shipyards, supply chain companies, and labor contract negotiators the confidence they need to ensure all the pieces come together to ramp up production,” said Rep. Courtney. “At the end of the day, this is about people. If you go back to when Block V was negotiated in 2019, the size of the workforce at Electric Boat was 17,000. Today, in 2026, it’s over 27,000, and if you look at the submarine tonnage output projections, we can’t stop there. It’s going to take a state, region, and nationwide effort by industry and educators to continue the revitalization of our submarine workforce. Everyone’s presence here today with their excitement, passion, and confidence shows that we’re all going to work together as a state to successfully execute these contract awards.”

Mark Rayha, President of General Dynamics-Electric Boat

“These contracts reflect the trust that Electric Boat has earned from the Trump administration, the Congress and the Navy,” said Mark Rayha. “They create stability, opportunity and further solidify the future for EB while providing economic security for thousands of households across Connecticut and Rhode Island. And they allow us to continue playing the critical role we’ve played for generations and take great pride in—delivering freedom.”

Peter Baker, President of the Metal Trades Council of New London County, AFL-CIO

“These really are exciting times at Electric Boat and shipbuilding. Not only is there record growth in ship construction, hiring and training, there are jobs for the building and construction trades to upgrade the shipyard infrastructure. Millions of dollars will be pumped into the local economy, but this does not negate the need for affordable housing, day care, elder care, and public transportation,” said Peter Baker. “Additionally, the hundreds of manufacturers and thousands of employees nationally who produce parts for these ships will be able to stabilize and grow. Most importantly, we will be able to provide to the Navy and to the navies of our allies, the most sophisticated deterrent and defenses needed to protect our nations. The work will not be easy, but it is achievable if we continue to work in partnership. Much of this would not have been possible without the work of Congressman Courtney and his staff, and we owe him a debt of gratitude.”

Chris Jewell, President of Collins & Jewell and Chairman of the Eastern Connecticut Workforce Investment Board’s Board of Directors

“One of the challenges that a lot of suppliers have in the submarine supply chain is the ebbs and flows of work, so we are really confident that these contract awards will help level out those hills and valleys and give us a really good demand signal,” said Chris Jewell. “A lot of businesses are on the cusp of expansion, Collins & Jewell being one of them. Not only does this give me a lot of confidence to move forward with that expansion, but I’m also sure it will give my bankers a lot of confidence as well. The supply chain in eastern Connecticut is really strong. We all work together with one voice to grow our workforce and get people that will hit the floor running right out of the gate better. That’s what the Eastern Connecticut Workforce Investment Board does through the training programs that they offer. I really do think that these contract awards are going to move the needle for the region, and I encourage everyone to stay focused on the objective moving forward: giving the U.S. Navy the best submarines in the world.”

title: Crow, Democratic Veterans Demand Transparency on Troop Casualties
text:
AURORA — Congressman Jason Crow (D-CO), a former paratrooper and Army Ranger who serves on the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence and House Armed Services Committee, along with 14 other Democratic veteran Members of Congress, are demanding the Trump administration release accurate information regarding all troop deaths and injuries during his reckless war with Iran.

"As veterans of America's wars, we have serious concerns about reports that the Department of War is delaying, removing or otherwise mischaracterizing the release of information about wounded and killed U.S. servicemembers," wrote the lawmakers.

"The U.S. government owes U.S. servicemembers, their families, and every American the truth about all U.S. casualties in the war with Iran. It is imperative that these reports are timely, accurate and adequately explain the reason for amended or delayed reports," they continued. "We urge you to commit to releasing timely and accurate information on all injuries and deaths of U.S. servicemembers."

After public reporting uncovered that the Pentagon lowered the number of troop deaths during the war with Iran from 18 to 14, the Department of Defense quietly restored the names. The Administration has provided conflicting explanations as to why the servicemembers names were removed to begin with. The reporting also detailed that DoD has misled the public about the number of troops injured and wounded during the war.

Joining Congressman Crow are Representatives Mike Thompson (D-CA), Chrissy Houlahan (D-PA), Chris Deluzio (D-PA), Gil Cisneros (D-CA), Derek Tran (D-CA), Salud Carbajal (D-CA), Jimmy Panetta (D-CA), Ted Lieu (D-CA), Seth Moulton (D-MA), Jared Golden (D-ME), Pat Ryan (D-NY), Maggie Goodlander (D-NH), Bobby Scott (D-VA), and Eugene Vindman (D-VA).

Crow has repeatedly condemned Trump’s illegal war of choice in Iran, and helped lead a war powers resolution that passed the House last week. As an Army Ranger who grew up in a working-class family and served in Iraq and Afghanistan, Crow saw firsthand the repercussions of forever wars on servicemembers and hard-working Americans. He has demanded answers on how this administration is protecting troops in the region, and on recent civilian deaths, including a U.S. strike on an Iranian girls’ elementary school where at least 175 civilians, many of them children, were killed.

A PDF of the letter can be found here.

title: Dingell, Colleagues Urge Administration to Lift Stop-Work Order on Brandon Road Lock and Dam Complex
text:
U.S. Representatives Debbie Dingell (D-MI-06), Marcy Kaptur (D-OH-09), Bill Huizenga (R-MI-04), and Dave Joyce (R-OH-14) urged the Trump Administration to lift the stop-work order and end the administrative review on the Brandon Road Lock and Dam complex. The critical project is designed to prevent invasive carp from reaching the Great Lakes and devastating the region’s $11 billion fishing and recreation industry, and work was abruptly halted on July 24, 2026, putting Great Lakes ecosystems and the regional economy at severe risk. The lawmakers are calling for the release of federal funds to the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers so construction on the vital multilayer barrier system can resume without further delay.

The four lawmakers are the co-chairs of the bipartisan Congressional Great Lakes Task Force.

A copy of the letter can be found HERE and below:

Dear Director Vought and Assistant Secretary Telle:

We write to express concern over delays affecting the timely construction of the Brandon Road Interbasin Project (BRIP) under the Department of the Army’s Civil Works Program and to urge prompt resolution of these delays. As we emphasized in our April 9, 2026, letter, this project is critical to preventing invasive carp from penetrating the Great Lakes. The project has been thoroughly reviewed by Congress, the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, and local partners. Its funding has been authorized and appropriated by Congress, and the non-Federal sponsors have met all applicable cost‑share obligations and secured the necessary property for construction.

The Corps of Engineers awarded the latest contract for the first phase of the project on April 23, 2026. However, we were informed that on July 24, 2026, the Corps of Engineers issued a stop-work order on the project’s contracts, causing additional delays and putting the Great Lakes ecosystem at direct risk. There is a rapidly closing window to stop the further spread of these harmful invasive species before they inflict irreparable damage on the Great Lakes.

The Great Lakes and their waterways are a way of life—providing fresh water, fish and wildlife habitat, and countless opportunities for recreation, while supporting the economies of eight surrounding States and thousands of good-paying American jobs. Once invasive carp establish reproducing populations, there is little that can be done to stop them from taking over the ecosystem, leading to escalating costs for American taxpayers. Any threat to the Great Lakes is a direct threat to the American economy, the more than 3,500 native species of plants and animals within the Great Lakes ecosystem, and the drinking water supply millions rely upon.

Importantly, we appreciate that the President has publicly conveyed his support for this effort numerous times since issuing his May 9, 2025, memorandum titled “Protecting the Great Lakes from Invasive Carp.” Given the strong support for this project from President Trump, its non-Federal sponsors, and the longstanding bipartisan support for its timely construction by Congress, as Co-Chairs of the Congressional Great Lakes Task Force we respectfully urge you to lift the stop-work orders, conclude any additional administration review of BRIP, and release Federal funds through the Army Corps of Engineers without any further delay.

The issue will be of acute interest to both the U.S. and Mexico Sections of the IBWC because of the potential damage to the Rio Grande and immediate environs on both sides of the river.

U.S. Customs and Border Protection has not released details regarding the proposed road aside from a small-scale map with the proposed alignment and that it would be 24 feet wide. The letter asks for road design and engineering details, spoil disposal plans, and line items for rock excavation, controlled blasting, drilling and shooting, vibration monitoring, or embankment placement.

In addition, it asks the IBWC U.S. Section if it has received any notice from the U.S. of the Mariscal Mountain alignment and whether the Mexican Section has been notified. Federal law authorizing waivers that set aside existing regulatory requirements for border wall construction do not apply to U.S.-Mexico Treaty obligations. The letter seeks confirmation that the U.S. acknowledges that fact.

title: Amid Soaring Utility Bills, Congresswoman Escobar Renews Call for Legislative Package to Lower Energy Costs
text:
As El Paso families continue to face rising utility bills and extreme temperatures, Congresswoman Veronica Escobar (TX-16) is renewing her call for Congress to advance a package of legislation that would strengthen utility oversight, expand energy assistance, and lower costs by accelerating access to affordable, reliable clean energy.

Congresswoman Escobar supports three bills aimed at addressing the energy affordability crisis from multiple angles: the Lowering Utility Bills Act, led by Congressman Greg Casar (TX-35); the Heating and Cooling Relief Act, led by Congresswoman Yassamin Ansari (AZ-03); and the Energy Bills Relief Act, led by Congressmen Mike Levin (CA-49) and Sean Casten (IL-06).

“Families should not have to choose between keeping the lights on, cooling their homes during dangerous heat, and paying for other basic necessities,” said Congresswoman Escobar. “At a time when utility bills are rising, Congress should be focused on delivering meaningful relief—not protecting excessive utility profits or making it harder and more expensive to build the affordable energy our communities need. This legislative package would increase accountability, expand assistance for families struggling with energy costs, and invest in the reliable, low-cost renewable energy that can help bring bills down over the long term.”

The Lowering Utility Bills Act would establish stronger federal and state standards governing how electric transmission providers and investor-owned utilities calculate their authorized rates of return. By increasing oversight and accountability in the rate-setting process, the legislation seeks to ensure that consumers are not forced to pay unnecessarily high utility bills to support excessive returns for utility companies.

The Heating and Cooling Relief Act would expand and modernize the Low Income Home Energy Assistance Program (LIHEAP), helping more low-income households afford heating and cooling costs. The legislation would better account for the growing risks and financial burdens associated with extreme weather—an especially urgent need in communities like El Paso, where prolonged and dangerous heat can make access to affordable cooling a matter of public health and safety.

The Energy Bills Relief Act would prioritize working families by driving down energy costs as President Trump’s war of choice with Iran causes global energy market volatility. Specifically, the legislation would reinstate the 2022 clean energy tax credits for home and system-wide energy improvements that were eliminated by President Trump and congressional Republicans, helping families reduce their energy use and lower their utility bills. It would also incentivize utility companies to improve the efficiency of their energy systems, reward cost-saving investments, provide financial assistance to help prevent families from having their power shut off, and crack down on price gouging by energy companies. The bill would ensure that large energy users—including data centers—pay their fair share of the costs associated with the energy they consume rather than shifting those expenses onto local households. It would also strengthen opportunities for communities to have a voice in energy projects and share in the benefits those projects bring.

These efforts come as the Trump administration and congressional Republicans have worked to dismantle clean energy tax credits and slow the deployment of renewable energy. The Republican-backed One Big Beautiful Bill Act accelerated the phaseout of key clean energy incentives, including credits that helped families invest in energy-efficient home improvements and residential clean energy. The Trump administration has also stalled the permitting process for several renewable energy projects, including offshore wind projects in Texas, creating uncertainty for projects that could help expand affordable electricity generation and reduce costs for consumers.

title: Congressman Flood Announces Flyover Fintech Panel on Payments Technology for Small Businesses and Startups
text:
LINCOLN, NEBRASKA – U.S. Congressman Mike Flood announced today that Flyover Fintech will feature a panel on payments technology for small businesses and startups, bringing together industry leaders from Shopify, Mastercard, Visa, and Stripe to discuss how new payment tools are helping small businesses compete, cut costs, and access capital. The panel will take place at Flyover Fintech in Lincoln, Nebraska on August 4, 2026.

“Small businesses and startups are the engine of American innovation, and payments technology is one of the key tools helping them succeed,” said Congressman Mike Flood. “As new innovations make it easier for entrepreneurs to accept payments, manage cash flow, and access capital, they're leveling the playing field for the businesses driving growth in Nebraska and across the country. I'm looking forward to hosting voices from across the payments industry to talk about how these innovations are helping entrepreneurs compete and succeed.”

Jonathan Bydlak is Senior Lead, Government and Public Affairs at Shopify, the world's leading commerce platform powering 14% of all online commerce in the U.S. and millions of businesses around the world. Jonathan works to advocate for rules that make it easier for American entrepreneurs to start, grow and scale businesses across every state. He previously was the Director of the Governance program at the R Street Institute, where he also served as a senior fellow and oversaw a portfolio of scholars working on issues ranging from budgetary to electoral policy. Earlier, Jonathan was the president and founder of the Institute for Spending Reform, a non-profit organization that conducted research on fiscal policy.

Jimmy Chow is Director of Community Relations at Mastercard. In this capacity, he advances financial empowerment and equity by promoting financial literacy, providing resources, and improving access to electronic payment technologies through the Master Your Card community empowerment initiative. Through Master Your Card, Jimmy collaborates with local governments and community organizations to deliver tailored financial education programs. The initiative also supports small business owners in enhancing operational efficiency, leveraging technology, protecting against cybersecurity risks, and strengthening their digital footprint. Since joining Mastercard in 2016 as Manager of Global Talent Development, Jimmy has been responsible for designing and deploying learning opportunities for all employees and people managers.

Mike Nunes is Vice President and Head of Policy Advisory, Global Government Affairs at Visa. He leads a global team that analyzes emerging policy and regulatory developments and advises Visa on issues shaping the future of commerce and payments. His work focuses on a broad range of topics, including artificial intelligence, digital assets and stablecoins, cybersecurity, data governance, financial regulation, and emerging payment technologies. Working across policy, legal, product, and business teams, Mike helps translate complex regulatory developments into strategies that support innovation, economic growth, and secure digital commerce. Mike has played a leading role in Visa's engagement on emerging technologies, helping policymakers, industry stakeholders, and business leaders better understand the opportunities and challenges associated with AI, digital assets, and next-generation payment systems. Prior to joining Visa, Mike held leadership roles spanning corporate affairs, international business development, and trade policy at Hewlett Packard Enterprise, Boeing Commercial Airplanes, the Telecommunications Industry Association, and the U.S. International Trade Commission.

Christopher Ortner is a senior business leader with over two decades of experience driving revenue growth, building high-performance teams, and scaling partnerships across the global payments ecosystem — from startups to Fortune 500s. At Stripe, Chris leads Go-To-Market for the Enterprise Portfolio, partnering with high-growth and established businesses across the Western U.S. Prior to Stripe, he spent 16 years at PayPal, where he led a $350M portfolio and scaled a customer success organization through a pivotal period of company growth. He began his career in business development at TSL International. Chris holds an MBA from Bellevue University, dual bachelor's degrees in Communication Studies and Psychology from the University of Nebraska, and a Six Sigma Green Belt from Villanova University. He has taught as an Adjunct Professor at Bellevue University's College of Business since 2009. A lifelong Nebraskan, Chris is based in Omaha.

Photos of the panelists can be found here.

Flyover Fintech conferences feature a wide variety of speakers, ranging from members of the House Financial Services Committee to leading voices in the fintech industry. Congressman Flood has previously announced that U.S. Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) Chairman Michael Selig will address this year's conference. More speakers and panelists for Flyover Fintech 2026 will be announced in the coming days.

Registration for the conference is open at www.flyoverfintech.com. Additional details about the location and information about hotels and travel are also available there.

title: RELEASE: Gottheimer Hosts Fifth District “Hometown Heroes” Awards
text:
“Hometown Heroes” Honors Local Veterans, Life-saving First Responders, Community Leaders

Above: Gottheimer honoring Fifth District residents as “Hometown Heroes.”

HACKENSACK, NJ — Today, July 31, 2026, U.S. Congressman Gottheimer (NJ-5) honored local life-saving first responders, veterans, volunteers, community leaders, and residents during his Fifth District Hometown Heroes Ceremony at the Hackensack Performing Arts Center.

Watch Gottheimer’s July, 2026 Hometown Heroes Ceremony here.

Gottheimer honored North Jersey residents as Fifth District Hometown Heroes to acknowledge their dedication to improving the lives of their neighbors, families, and communities.

“Today, we are here to focus on our neighbors, who, even in all the noise, look for ways to put others above themselves,” said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). “Each day, our friends, family, and neighbors quietly go out and change lives through their service to others. They do it all without expecting any special recognition. They do it simply because it’s the right thing to do. They all come from different walks of life, but they all embody our Jersey Values and make our community such a special place to live, work, and raise a family. They help us build that more perfect union of our dreams. We all should work to live up to their example.”

Read about this year’s Hometown Heroes below:

Samuel Kim, Englewood Cliffs — At just seventeen, Samuel has already founded two nonprofits serving local seniors: Aim for Unity, which offers free archery workshops for brain health and has served more than six hundred seniors, and the Senior Shield Project, a fraud-prevention and digital literacy program that has reached more than 150 people. A DECA regional champion and Regeneron science fair winner, he lives with his grandparents, whose care drives his work.

Tom Colwell, Closter — Since 2023, Tom has served as Co-Chair of the Closter Food Pantry, turning a small effort into one of the most efficient operations around. He personally orders, picks up, and delivers food every month, builds the spreadsheets, tracks the finances, and secured grants for its equipment — all while holding a full-time job and volunteering alongside his wife and three kids.

Andrew Dunn, Hillsdale — Andrew has been a Hillsdale resident for fifty-three years, and has devoted his life to Habitat for Humanity. Andy is a U.S. Army veteran and honored English teacher — has served as a Habitat for Humanity construction crew leader for more than three decades, including a dozen trips for post-Katrina rebuilding.

Joan Bohan & Mike Schulman, Northvale — Joan, Northvale’s school nurse for fifteen years, and Mike, its athletic director and a physical education teacher for eighteen and 2025–2026 Bergen County Teacher of the Year, didn’t hesitate when a middle school player collapsed in cardiac arrest this February. Using the district’s AED and CPR training, they brought the student back. Thanks to them, Angelo is alive today.

Jim & Meredith Drobinske, Dumont — Dumont residents for thirty-nine years and married for forty-five, Jim and Meredith are retired Teachers of the Year who now serve as pantry managers for the Food Brigade, logging 1,804 volunteer hours in two years and helping feed 150 families a week. Jim — a fifty-two-year member of the Woodcliff Lake Fire Department — is a two-time Hometown Hero, first honored in 2018 for a CPR save on a golf course.

Officer Frank Stefano, Oradell — Off duty at a Hackensack hockey rink, Oradell Officer Frank Stefano performed CPR and delivered two defibrillator shocks to revive a goalie in full cardiac arrest — who has since fully recovered. It’s far from his first save: Frank has twice been honored by Pascack Valley PBA Local 206, including for using Narcan to revive an unconscious individual.

Paul Coller, Ramsey — A Ramsey resident for forty-one years and U.S. Army Reserve veteran, Paul volunteers twice a week with CHORE, part of Bergen Volunteers, performing home repairs that keep seniors and disabled residents safe at home. He has served there more than a decade, including as Board President. As Bergen Volunteers’ director Shara Nadler puts it, “Paul is a community champion who strengthens Bergen County every day.”

Chief Robert Schlossberg, River Edge — River Edge Fire Chief Robert Schlossberg just completed a career that includes delivering a baby, three CPR saves, and several Unit Citations for courage — and this year was named 2025 New Jersey Fire Chief of the Year. He and his wife Joellen raised a true service family, with three children serving in fire, police, and EMS. His focus as Chief was always training, the best way to keep every member safe.

Michele Weber, Waldwick — A lifelong Waldwick resident and cancer survivor, Michele chairs Access for All, raising awareness of what people with disabilities face and offering guidance on ADA compliance and local resources. She also volunteers every Sunday in her church’s Kids’ Ministry. As Mayor Giordano says, “Michele embodies the spirit of community, service, and dedication that defines a true hometown hero.”

Michael McNamara, Branchville — For nearly four decades, Mike has volunteered with Project Self-Sufficiency — known there as “the guy who always says yes,” he once drove to Maryland for a truckload of donated books. When pulmonary fibrosis slowed him, he kept showing up on oxygen, and after a 2023 lung transplant returned with a spring in his step. He’s also hiked the beginning and end of the Appalachian Trail — just not the middle.

Nick Vanhorn, Sussex — Every day, Nick keeps Sussex kids safe as the town’s crossing guard — but his role goes further: free weather and news updates on Facebook, an Easter Bunny costume for town festivities, and a different costume every day during Halloween week. As Sussex Borough Councilman Ross says, “Nick’s presence and contributions are heavily cherished, and he is a staple to the community of Sussex.”

Keri Marino, Franklin — Keri is the first woman to serve as President of the 200 Club of Sussex County and sits on a remarkable range of civic boards. A domestic violence survivor, she has spent years as a trustee of DASI and teaches free trauma-informed yoga to survivors, and she once testified in Washington on renewing VAWA. She has received a Citation from the New Jersey State Legislature and DASI’s Full Circle Award.

Linda Schaefer, Ringwood — A Ringwood resident for thirty-eight years, Linda served with the Ringwood Ambulance Auxiliary — twenty-five as President — funding equipment and free ambulance service for residents. She also spent twenty-six years as the elementary school secretary and served on numerous town boards. As Ringwood Deputy Mayor Kerr says, she is “a selfless person who has devoted her entire life to working and volunteering in Ringwood.”

Gary Oppenheimer, West Milford — In 2009, Gary founded AmpleHarvest.org, which connects home gardeners’ surplus harvests with nearby food pantries. Seventeen years later it links more than 8,500 pantries across all fifty states to 62 million gardeners — run by a staff of just four. A CNN Hero and two-time TEDx speaker, Gary fights food waste and hunger from right here in the Garden State.

Anthony Pulizzano, Upper Saddle River — An Upper Saddle River police officer and PBA president, Anthony has made Special Olympics New Jersey his cause, founding “Climb with a Cop” and coordinating the Law Enforcement Torch Run. He also founded the Rock Adventure Company for kids and once performed the Heimlich to save a choking woman, earning a lifesaving award from the Bergen County Chiefs Association.

Officers Alex Lospinuso & Jake Rotunda, Franklin — Responding to what seemed a routine call, Franklin Officers Alex Lospinuso and Jake Rotunda found a man with life-threatening injuries and applied a tourniquet and chest seal that saved his life. Alex has also been honored for a crash rescue and a mental health crisis response, while Jake, a lifelong wrestler, earned a MADD award for impaired-driving enforcement and now coaches youth wrestling.

John Herrmann, Englewood Fire Department — An Englewood firefighter and union president, John serves as Clinical Coordinator for the state Professional Firefighters’ Peer Support Team, guiding departments through line-of-duty deaths, suicides, and quiet struggles. Drawing on his own experience with anxiety, he has helped many colleagues through their hardest moments. As Chief Jeff Kaplan says, his peer counseling “sets him apart from everyone” — and he does it without compensation.

Razak Buddha, Teaneck — At ninety-three, Razak is the oldest volunteer at Holy Name Hospital, showing up every day at the Courtesy Desk with warmth and a readiness to help — more than 3,498 hours logged over the years. A retired physical therapist who grew up in India, he still visits elderly patients in their homes several times a week to provide care and companionship.

Laurie Epstein, Haworth — After her daughter’s food allergy diagnosis, Laurie became one of New Jersey’s leading advocates for allergy safety, even bringing her second grader to Washington to testify. She has led Girl Scouts in Haworth since 2005 and now runs the program for more than 130 girls. As Councilwoman Siciliano says, her support “has produced generations of future female leaders who believe in themselves.”

Helen Whalen (Posthumously), Westwood — Honored posthumously, Helen was a Westwood resident for more than seventy years who devoted her life to telling North Jersey’s story through the Pascack Historical Society and Westwood Heritage Society. Her history of Westwood was published this year, after her 2023 passing. Her award is received today by her daughter Kathleen, grandson Marc, and niece Tatiana.

Gottheimer was joined by Bergen County Clerk John Hogan, Commissioner Alan Henderson, Hackensack Mayor Caseen Gaines, Sussex Mayor Robert Holowach, Waldwick Mayor Thomas Giordano, Closter Mayor John Gliddon, Mayor Deirdre Dillon, Hillsdale Mayor Michael Sheinfeld, Westwood Mayor Ray Arroyo, Ringwood Mayor Jamie Landis, Westwood Council President Lauren Leitzia, Westwood Councilwoman Erin Collins, Councilman Paul Rubacky, Englewood Cliffs COuncilman Phillip Liang, Council President Thomas Kelly, Councilman David Bandfield, Closter Councilwoman Alissa Latner, Councilwoman Angela Smith, Fire Chief Jeff Kaplan, Police Chief David Gangemi, Police Chief Gregory Cugliari, Police COmmanding Captain Seamus Geddis, Waldwick Borough Clerk Kelly Halewicz, Englewood Cliffs Mayor Mark Park, Englewood Cliffs Councilwoman Rivka Bieggacz, River Edge Mayor Thomas Papaleo, Franklin Councilwoman Stephen Skellenger, Haworth Councilwoman Dina Siciliano.

Below: Gottheimer presents awards to local heroes and their families.
