title: Rep. Grijalva Statement on Newly Announced Federal Proposal for  Colorado River Water Cuts
text:
Tucson, AZ – Congresswoman Adelita S. Grijalva released the following statement in response to the Bureau of Reclamation’s plan to apportion Colorado River water cuts.

“While we are still awaiting the final operational plans for the next two years, any proposal that imposes the vast majority of cuts on Arizona is unreasonable and unacceptable — especially while Upper Basin states continue to hide behind an outdated legal framework that is disconnected from today’s hydrologic realities, allowing them to avoid making meaningful reductions to their own water use.

I will continue fighting for Arizona’s CAP users in our cities and towns, who have made extraordinary investments and sacrifices over the past several decades to reduce water use. I will also continue advocating for agricultural producers in Yuma County, whose work is essential to keeping America’s food supply strong and reducing grocery prices. I will continue standing with Arizona’s Tribal Nations, whose hard-fought water settlements must be respected.

title: Congressman Harris Tours Army Corps Dredging Operations at Ocean City Inlet
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Andy Harris, M.D. (MD-01), toured the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers' Murden dredging operations at the Ocean City Inlet as crews continue maintenance dredging ahead of the White Marlin Open.

The project will remove accumulated sediment from the inlet to improve navigation for commercial and recreational vessels during one of the Eastern Shore's busiest boating seasons.

Statement from Congressman Harris:

"Touring the Murden gave me a firsthand look at the work required to keep the Ocean City Inlet navigable. Keeping this federal channel open allows commercial fishing vessels, charter boats, and recreational boaters to safely enter and leave the inlet. I'm glad to have been able to arrange this timely dredge as well as the funding for construction of a much-needed second U.S. Army Corps of Engineers shallow dredge."

For media inquiries, please contact Michella Carter at Michella.Carter@mail.house.gov

title: Houchin Introduces 988 Lifeline Location Improvement Act
text:
July 31, 2026

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Congresswoman Erin Houchin (R-IN-09) recently introduced the bipartisan 988 Lifeline Location Improvement Act alongside Congressman Joe Neguse (D-CO-02), Congressman Tom Kean Jr. (R-NJ-07), and Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (D-IL-08). The legislation would improve geolocation capabilities and increase the effectiveness of the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. Companion legislation was introduced in the Senate by Senators John Barrasso (R-WY) and Ben Ray Luján (D-NM).

The legislation directs the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) to initiate a notice of inquiry on the challenges of transmitting geolocation information with 988 calls and instructs the Government Accountability Office (GAO) to study the policy, legal, technical, and financial considerations associated with improving geolocation capabilities. The findings will help inform future legislative and administrative action to better connect individuals in crisis with local emergency services.

"The 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline has been a vital resource for those facing mental health crises, saving lives across the country," said Rep. Houchin. "This bipartisan bill will fine tune location information for 988 calls, ensuring people are connected with local emergency services as quickly as possible when they need them most."

"When someone reaches out to the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline during a mental health crisis, every second matters,” said Rep. Krishnamoorthi. “We should be doing everything we can to connect people with the help they need as quickly as possible. This bipartisan legislation brings together mental health, public safety, and telecommunications experts to identify practical solutions that strengthen the 988 Lifeline and help ensure it works better for the people counting on it."

“It is critical that the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline connects Americans with the help that they need, where they need it,” said Rep. Kean. “This legislation is an important step toward ensuring that people can connect with local resources as efficiently as possible.”

The 988 Lifeline Location Improvement Act would:

Direct the FCC to examine the legal, privacy, technical, and financial challenges of transmitting geolocation information with 988 calls.

Require the GAO to study opportunities and challenges related to implementing geolocation capabilities for the 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline and provide recommendations to Congress.

Evaluate geolocation challenges affecting individuals who are deaf or hard of hearing and access the 988 American Sign Language (ASL) line through Direct Video Calling (DVC) and Video Relay Services (VRS).

The legislation is endorsed by the National Alliance on Mental Illness (NAMI) and APCO International.

The Senate companion legislation passed the Senate by unanimous consent in May 2026.

Read the bill text here.

title: Reps. Huffman, Lawler, Min and Fitzpatrick Call for Stronger Federal E-Bike and E-Moto Safety Standards
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Jared Huffman (CA-02), Congressman Dave Min (CA-47), joined by Representatives Michael Lawler (NY-17), and Congressman Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), sent a letter urging the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to develop comprehensive federal safety standards for electric bicycles and higher-speed “e-motos”.

The bipartisan letter comes in response to the CPSC’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to establish safety standards for lithium-ion batteries used for e-bikes and other forms of micromobility transit. While the lawmakers acknowledged the importance of addressing the serious fire risks posed by low-quality batteries, they keyed in on the CPSC’s failure to address the broader risks posed by unregulated e-bikes and e-motos.

“While we strongly support the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission taking action to address fire hazards posed by counterfeit and low-quality lithium-ion batteries associated with these products, battery integrity is only one component of a broader set of challenges facing consumers and communities,” said the Members. “We urge the Commission to build on this effort by developing separate, comprehensive safety standards for e-bikes and electric motorcycles.”

“Fire-safe batteries matter, but they will not stop companies from marketing devices capable of motorcycle-level speeds to children as ordinary e-bikes,” said Rep. Min. “Parents should not have to become product safety experts just to know what they are buying for their kids. The CPSC must close these loopholes, require clear product labeling, and establish modern standards that distinguish e-bikes from high-powered e-motos.”

The reforms outlined in the letter reflect key provisions of Congressman Min’s Safe Standards for Personal E-Bike and E-Moto Device Specifications Act, Safe SPEEDS Act, which would establish a comprehensive federal safety framework for electric micromobility products.

Between 2019 and 2022, as e-bike sales in the United States nearly quadrupled, injuries involving e-bikes and e-motos increased by nearly tenfold, according to estimates from the CPSC’s National Electronic Injury Surveillance System. Children and teenagers face particularly serious risks. Health care providers at Rady Children’s Health treated one pediatric e-bike crash patient in 2021 and more than 220 in 2025.

The letter also highlights fatal crashes involving young riders and community members, including the death of 20-year-old Huntington Beach resident Kolby Aipa after an e-bike collision.

The lawmakers urged the CPSC to:

Establish minimum labeling requirements clearly disclosing each device’s maximum speed, motor power, recommended minimum age and intended on-road or off-road use.

Modernize the federal definition of an e-bike and create consistent classifications that clearly distinguish conventional e-bikes from higher-powered e-motos.

Support local crash-data collection and public education by helping law enforcement agencies, emergency responders and local governments accurately identify devices and document injuries and fatalities.

The full letter is available here.

The letter is the latest step in Rep. Min’s continued efforts to improve e-bike safety and close gaps in federal oversight. Earlier this week, Rep. Min joined Irvine Councilmember Betty Martinez Franco’s office for an I-Ride Safe Academy panel focused on helping young riders and their families better understand e-bike risks and practice safe, responsible riding.

title: Rep. Ronny Jackson Co-Leads Legislation Targeting Iranian Proxy, Polisario Front
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Representatives Ronny Jackson (TX-13) and Josh Gottheimer (NJ-05) introduced the Polisario Front Terrorist Designation Act. The legislation would strengthen U.S. national security and protect American interests by directing the Secretary of State to designate the Polisario Front as a Foreign Terrorist Organization following a comprehensive evaluation of the group’s involvement with Iran and Iranian-backed terrorist organizations to coordinate military training, weapons deliveries, and intelligence sharing.

"For too long, Iran and its terrorist proxies, like Hezbollah, have used the Polisario Front to project instability across West Africa," said Rep. Jackson. "This bill ensures the Trump administration is equipped to fully investigate the Polisario Front and take decisive action to counter threats to the national security of the U.S. and our allies. We must use every available tool to combat terrorism, dismantle the networks that enable it, and protect the American people."

“The Iranian regime and its terrorist proxies are working overtime to open a new front against the United States and our allies, and the Polisario Front has become one of their instruments,” said Rep. Gottheimer. “When a group takes drones and weapons from the IRGC and coordinates with Iranian-backed terrorists, we should call it exactly what it is: a terrorist organization. This bipartisan bill makes sure that once that cooperation is confirmed, we can bring the full weight of America’s counterterrorism sanctions down on the Polisario Front and cut its leaders off from the global financial system, international travel, and the resources they use to threaten us and our allies. Standing up to Iran and its proxies isn’t a partisan issue.”

title: Rep. Ronny Jackson Applauds Announcement of Contract for Critical Upgrades to USMC H-1 Fleet at Bell Helicopter in Amarillo, Texas, Made Possible by Congressional Defense Funding
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Representative Ronny Jackson (TX-13) announced that as a result of funding he helped secure in the Fiscal Year 2026 defense appropriations bill, Bell Textron Inc. was awarded a contract to support the Structural and Power Improvements for NextGen Effects (SPINE) program, a critical modernization effort that will enhance the performance and longevity of the U.S. Marine Corps' AH-1Z and UH-1Y helicopter fleet.

Rep. Jackson has consistently championed funding for this program during his time in Congress, recognizing both its importance to our national defense and the significant economic impact it has at Bell and in the Texas Panhandle.

The funding will sustain the highly skilled workforce at Bell's Amarillo facility, support advanced manufacturing and engineering jobs, continue to strengthen the region's defense industrial base, and reinforce Amarillo's longstanding role as a premier hub for military aviation production and modernization. It also underscores the enduring partnership between Bell, the U.S. Marine Corps, and industry partners in providing next-generation capabilities to America's warfighters and ensuring the H-1 fleet will remain relevant to the Joint Force for decades to come.

This $300 million investment will tangibly increase lethality and survivability for Bell’s AH-1Z and UH-1Y platforms while delivering real results for Amarillo and the Texas Panhandle,” said Rep. Jackson. “I am proud to continue to support the SPINE program, which will help sustain highly skilled jobs at Bell, reinforce our region's critical role in supporting the U.S. Marine Corps, and ensure our servicemembers have the modernized aircraft they need to accomplish their mission. While in Congress, I will continue fighting to bring defense investments home to Texas Thirteen while ensuring our military remains the strongest and most capable fighting force in the world."

title: Smith Holds Farmers Town Hall in Dunklin County
text:
DUNKLIN COUNTY, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) joined members of the Missouri Rice Council for a Farmers Town Hall in Dunklin County this week, where he discussed the positive impact of the Working Families Tax Cuts, which Congressman Smith authored and championed to passage, on Missouri’s rice industry and fielded questions from farmers concerned about today’s agriculture economy.

Congressman Smith said, “It’s always good to sit down with our rice farmers and hear directly from them about what they’re facing — whether it be export issues, high input costs, or just the day-to-day challenges of running a farm in today’s environment. When you think of the Bootheel, rice farmers are one of the first groups that come to mind, and these families deserve a seat at the table when decisions are made and legislation is written. That’s exactly why I fought so hard to include provisions that benefited them in the Working Families Tax Cuts such as the first increase in reference prices in nearly 20 years. This legislation also made both the small business deduction and 100 percent bonus depreciation permanent, giving family-owned farms long-term certainty, which they need to reinvest, expand, and grow.

“I greatly enjoyed our conversation about their top priorities and concerns, and I will continue to fight for their interests when I return to Washington.”

During the discussion, Congressman Smith answered questions regarding seed prices, bridge payments, and trade enforcement, including an ongoing Section 301 investigation into unfair foreign trade practices affecting U.S. rice exports. Additionally, farmers asked about consolidation in the global fertilizer market, an issue Congressman Smith has raised directly with the Trump Administration after leading a congressional delegation to Morocco earlier this year.

Congressman Smith also highlighted wins for rice farmers in the Working Families Tax Cuts, like the increase in the reference price for rice by 20 percent beginning with crop year 2025. Ninety-eight percent of farms are organized as LLCs, making the bill’s permanent 199A small business deduction and 100 percent immediate expensing especially valuable for rice operations looking to reinvest in their equipment and land.

title: Smith, Missouri Delegation Sends Letter Urging Swift Approval of Governor’s Disaster Declaration Request
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08), along with members of Missouri’s Congressional Delegation, sent a letter to President Trump today supporting Governor Mike Kehoe’s request for a major disaster declaration following the catastrophic flooding that struck southern Missouri from July 9 through July 11, 2026.

“We write in strong support of Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe’s July 28, 2026, request for a major disaster declaration following the devastating severe storms and flooding that took place in Missouri from July 9th through July 11th of this year,” the lawmakers wrote. “Beginning late on July 9th, a series of slow-moving thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall in some areas across south-central and southeastern Missouri, equivalent to a 1-in-1,000-year event according to the National Weather Service. In roughly 12 hours, some areas received an estimated 6 to 12 inches of rain, causing rivers, creeks, and low-lying areas to rapidly rise, including a record crest on the Black River near Annapolis, Missouri… In the days following, it was publicly reported that first responders bravely rescued over 350 people, including over 200 airlifted from the Camp Taum Sauk by Missouri National Guard helicopters.”

“Missouri has repeatedly been faced with natural disasters in recent years,” the lawmakers continued. “In 2025 alone, Missouri received five federally declared disasters—the most of any state—and in 2026, this trend has not changed. Today, Missouri is requesting its third disaster declaration of the year, already holding a declaration for storms that occurred from April 23rd through April 28th… Following the Joint Preliminary Damage Assessments for the July 9th through July 11th storms, more than $26.5 million in eligible infrastructure damage and emergency protective costs were identified across 9 counties… As such, we respectfully urge you to direct your administration to promptly review Governor Kehoe’s major disaster declaration request for the July 9 through July 11 storms and submit it for your approval.”

Congressman Smith recently saw firsthand the devastating flood damage in Reynolds County, visiting Valley Springs Youth Ranch and Black River Baptist Church — two sites hit hardest by the storms.

“The pictures don’t do justice to the damage,” Smith said. “For 12 inches of rain to come within two to three hours, in an area that does not flood, it was horrendous and pretty scary. Families have lost their homes, farmers have lost equipment and livelihoods they spent decades building, and a church that feeds well over 100 families through its food drives had its sanctuary destroyed. The scale of what this community is facing is enormous, and I’m grateful for every first responder, volunteer, neighbor, and local leader who has stepped up to help during this difficult time. My office will continue working to connect these families and organizations with every state and federal resource available as they rebuild.”

Senator Josh Hawley (R-MO), Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO), and Congresswoman Ann Wagner (MO-02) also signed the letter.

title: Smith Visits Pemiscot Memorial Hospital
text:
HAYTI, Mo. – Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08) visited Pemiscot Memorial Hospital in Hayti this week, touring the facility and meeting with hospital leadership to discuss the impact of its recent conversion to Rural Emergency Hospital (REH) status — a designation the congressman worked directly with state and federal health officials to help secure after years of advocating to keep the hospital’s doors open.

Congressman Smith said, “Pemiscot Memorial Hospital is the last hospital left in the Bootheel, and for families in this part of Missouri, that emergency room can mean the difference between life and death. When this hospital was on the verge of closing, my staff and I fought tooth and nail to cut through red tape at CMS, connect hospital leadership with the resources they needed, and push for a fair and timely review of their application for Rural Emergency Hospital status. I’m proud of what we were able to do together, and I’ll keep fighting to make sure rural Missourians never lose access to the care they depend on.”

Pemiscot Memorial Hospital sees roughly 800 patients a month through its seven-bed emergency room — playing a pivotal role in serving families all across the region and delivering care that thousands of families depend on. The hospital faced near closure in both 2023 and 2024 due to financial mismanagement and cash flow shortfalls, at one point struggling to make payroll. Congressman Smith stepped in, working with hospital leadership and state and federal health agencies to help stabilize the hospital’s finances and chart a sustainable path forward.

In November 2025, following sustained engagement from Congressman Smith with the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services, Pemiscot Memorial received Rural Emergency Hospital status — retroactive to May 2025 — along with roughly $2 million in Medicare backpay. The REH designation allows the hospital to receive fixed monthly Medicare payments in place of inpatient reimbursement, plus a 5 percent bonus for emergency and outpatient services. This provides Pemiscot Memorial with a stable funding source to continue serving the Bootheel and gives it the potential to expand services in the future.

The Working Families Tax Cuts, which Congressman Smith authored and spearheaded in Congress, also included a $50 billion investment for rural healthcare through the Rural Health Transformation Program — the largest one-time investment in rural hospitals in American history. As Chairman of the Ways and Means Committee, Congressman Smith has made it a priority to ensure Americans in rural areas like the Bootheel of Missouri have access to quality health care.

title: Kean Visits Branchburg to Spotlight $2.25 Million in Federal Funds for New Emergency Operations Center

title: Kennedy, Gillibrand Demand USPS Reverse Decision to End Curbside Mail Delivery for Whistling Straits Residents
text:
In Letter, Lawmakers Call on Postmaster General to Honor Commitment Made to Residents, Slam Agency’s Bureaucratic Failures

WHEATFIELD, NY - Congressman Tim Kennedy (NY-26) and Senator Kirsten Gillibrand sent a letter to Postmaster General David Steiner demanding that the United States Postal Service (USPS) immediately reinstate its previous implementation of curbside mail delivery to the residents of the Whistling Straits subdivision in the Town of Wheatfield, New York.

After years of advocacy by residents and elected officials, local USPS leadership informed these families that curbside delivery would rightfully be implemented and began delivering it accordingly. However, in an inexcusable display of bureaucratic mismanagement, USPS has rescinded that decision, notifying residents that curbside mail delivery will end on August 28th, 2026.

The lawmakers called on USPS to honor the prior commitment it made to residents, arguing that families should not be punished because the agency failed to follow its own internal approval process. In the letter, Kennedy and Gillibrand criticized USPS for reversing course after beginning curbside delivery, urging the agency to immediately maintain curbside service and hold itself accountable for its own administrative failures. The lawmakers emphasized that Whistling Straits residents deserve the same practical mail delivery provided to surrounding neighborhoods and a Postal Service that keeps its word.

Read the full text of the letter below:

July 30, 2026

Postmaster General David Steiner

United States Postal Service

475 L'Enfant Plaza SW

Washington, D.C. 20260

Dear Postmaster General Steiner,

We write to demand that the United States Postal Service (USPS) immediately cancel its inexplicable decision to reverse its commitment to provide curbside mail delivery to the residents of the Whistling Straits subdivision in the Town of Wheatfield, New York. After years of advocacy by residents, local officials, and our offices, local USPS leadership informed these families that curbside delivery would rightfully be implemented and began delivering it accordingly. Now, in a stunning display of bureaucratic mismanagement, your agency has rescinded that decision, notifying residents that curbside mail delivery will end on August 28th, 2026.

According to the letter your agency sent to affected homeowners, the local Postmaster “improperly changed the established mode of mail delivery” and lacked the authority to do so. Rather than taking responsibility for its own internal failures, USPS has instead chosen to punish the families who relied on the agency’s representations in good faith. That is unacceptable. The facts underlying this case have not changed. Whistling Straits, consisting of Squire Drive and Piedmont Street, received local planning approvals before USPS adopted cluster mailbox units as the default delivery method for new developments in 2012, and the subdivision was designed accordingly. It has no homeowners association, no common property to maintain a centralized mailbox, and no sidewalks – conditions that make the installation and maintenance of a cluster mailbox both impractical and, particularly during Western New York winters, a legitimate public safety concern.

The residents of Whistling Straits have never sought special treatment, they have asked only for the same curbside mail delivery provided to the homes surrounding their neighborhood along Ward Road, Hoover Road, and Lockport Road. For years, they have been forced to purchase post office boxes and travel to retrieve mail because of a bureaucratic technicality that arose through no fault of their own. USPS ultimately acknowledged the merits of their case when it approved curbside delivery. The Postal Service should not now abandon that determination simply because it failed to follow its own internal procedures.

This situation has severely undermined local public confidence in the Postal Service. USPS made a decision and began implementing it, and allowed residents to believe the matter had finally been resolved before reversing course after discovering its own internal breakdown in governance. Postal customers deserve a Postal Service that communicates accurately, follows its own procedures, and accepts responsibility when it makes mistakes. Instead, the agency has demonstrated precisely the opposite.

Accordingly, we demand that USPS immediately reverse this decision and honor the commitment it made to the residents of Whistling Straits by maintaining curbside mail delivery. Families who have spent years advocating for fair treatment should not bear the consequences of the Postal Service’s administrative failures.

The residents of Whistling Straits deserve competent leadership, accountable government, and a Postal Service that keeps its word. We intend to pursue every available avenue to ensure these families receive the equal treatment they have long fought for. Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. We look forward to your timely response.

Sincerely,

Timothy M. Kennedy

Member of Congress (NY-26)

title: Rep. Kiggans Joins EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin for Tour of Hampton Roads Sanitation District’s SWIFT Research Center
text:
SUFFOLK, VA — Congresswoman Jen Kiggans (VA-02) joined U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) Administrator Lee Zeldin, EPA Region 3 Administrator Amy Van Blarcom-Lackey, Hampton Roads Sanitation District (HRSD) leadership, and regional partners for a tour of HRSD’s Sustainable Water Initiative for Tomorrow (SWIFT) Research Center. The visit highlighted the groundbreaking work taking place in Virginia’s Second District to advance water reuse technology, strengthen water security, and protect the long-term sustainability of the region’s groundwater resources.

During the visit, Administrator Zeldin and Congresswoman Kiggans received an executive briefing from HRSD General Manager and Chief Executive Officer Jay Bernas on the SWIFT program before touring the research facility to observe its advanced water purification process and ongoing construction supporting the program’s expansion.

Congresswoman Kiggans said, “I’m proud to see that Hampton Roads is leading the way in developing innovative ways to protect our nation’s most important resource, clean and reliable water. The work taking place at HRSD’s SWIFT Research Center is invaluable to our region, and is strengthening long-term water security and ensuring our communities have the resilient infrastructure they need for generations to come.”

“I’d like to thank Administrator Zeldin for visiting Virginia’s Second District to experience this project firsthand. I look forward to continuing our work together to support investments that drive innovation, preserve our natural resources, and improve quality of life across Coastal Virginia.”

“It was great to join Congresswoman Kiggans this weekend in Suffolk, Virginia, to visit HRSD’s SWIFT Research Center,” said EPA Administrator Lee Zeldin. “Congresswoman Kiggans is a passionate fighter for a clean and healthy environment. Our visit was another example of EPA’s commitment to cooperative federalism, partnering with state and local leaders to deploy advanced technologies and further our research efforts to provide clean air, land, and water to communities across Virginia and the country.”

SWIFT is HRSD’s long-term water sustainability initiative that uses advanced treatment technology to further purify already-treated wastewater to drinking water quality before replenishing the Potomac Aquifer, Eastern Virginia’s primary groundwater source. The program is designed to strengthen the region’s water supply while reducing nutrient discharges to local waterways, protecting against saltwater intrusion, addressing land subsidence associated with sea level rise, and supporting the long-term environmental and economic health of the Commonwealth.

“Congresswoman Kiggans’ support in bringing Administrator Zeldin to Hampton Roads allowed us to show the EPA exactly what SWIFT and HRSD’s innovation programs can do — not as a pilot project, but as a scalable model other regions can adopt. That’s the kind of federal-local collaboration that gets real infrastructure built,” said GM/CEO of HRSD Jay Bernas.

As the representative for Virginia’s Second District, Rep. Kiggans remains committed to supporting innovative infrastructure, strengthening environmental resilience, and advancing federal partnerships that improve the quality of life for communities across Hampton Roads and Virginia’s Eastern Shore.

title: Krishnamoorthi, Colleagues Press HHS on Placement of Migrant Children at Facility with Documented History of Abuse
text:
WASHINGTON — Today, Congressman Raja Krishnamoorthi (IL-08), Congresswoman Summer Lee (PA-12), Congressman Chris Deluzio (PA-17), and Congresswoman Madeleine Dean (PA-04) sent a letter to Department of Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. and Office of Refugee Resettlement Acting Director Angie Salazar demanding answers about ORR's decision to place unaccompanied migrant children at Abraxas Academy in Morgantown, Pennsylvania, despite the facility's documented history of child abuse violations.

The lawmakers raise serious concerns about ORR's decision to award Abraxas Alliance a $9.2 million contract in August 2025 despite Pennsylvania officials documenting repeated deficiencies and revoking one of the facility's licenses. They also urge HHS to immediately review all ORR-contracted facilities, suspend the Abraxas Academy contract pending a full investigation, and provide Congress with a complete accounting of how the placement decision was made.

"It is appalling that ORR nevertheless decided to house unaccompanied minors in a facility with such a record, thereby potentially exposing these children to the possibility of abuse and in violation of federal rules," the Members wrote.

The letter details a decades-long pattern of documented problems at the facility, including repeated state findings of physical mistreatment of minors, allegations of sexual harassment and abuse by staff, and a pattern of institutional failures. Although federal law requires ORR to place children in "the least restrictive setting that is in the best interests of the child," reports indicate children are being housed in locked cells.

The Members also cite concerns stemming from a July 8 congressional oversight visit, during which facility staff were reportedly unable to answer basic questions about allegations of abuse or explain legally required procedures for children who turn 18 while in ORR custody. As the Members wrote, "This utter lack of knowledge of the basic, legally required functions of this facility raises serious concerns about the safety of the children living inside."

The letter requests responses by August 14, 2026, including:

Who approved the decision to place children at Abraxas Academy and what child welfare assessments were conducted.

Why ORR proceeded with the contract despite Pennsylvania's documented findings of abuse and licensing violations.

Whether HHS has reviewed other ORR-contracted facilities for compliance with state and federal child welfare standards.

Why some children with parents or close relatives in the United States were reportedly placed in ORR custody rather than reunited with family.

What safeguards exist to protect children from abuse and how staff are trained.

The financial and operational relationship between Abraxas Alliance and GEO Group.

"The federal government bears a solemn responsibility to ensure the proper treatment and protection of every child in its care," the Members wrote. "Allowing any child to be placed in an environment with a history of abuse is cruel and undermines the moral leadership of the United States."

title: Landsman Statement on Trump Deporting Tens of Thousands of Haitians
text:
Cincinnati, OH – Today, Congressman Greg Landsman (D-OH-01) released the following statement after Temporary Protected Status (TPS) for Haiti has officially ended.

President Trump is about to deport tens of thousands of Haitians. It’s cruel, wrong, and terrible for our country.

Starting this weekend, Haitian families are being told to report to ICE facilities, and we don’t know what will happen next.

What we do know is who these families are. They have dignity. They work really hard. They’ve started businesses, filled manufacturing job shortages, and many of them are home health workers taking care of our families.

The violence in Haiti has been terrifying for years, and it’s only gotten worse. Sending them back would be inhumane. They’d have a difficult time finding housing, healthcare, jobs. Many will starve. Some may not survive.

That’s why the House forced a vote and passed an extension of TPS for Haitian families.

The Senate is still in session for another week and must act before it’s too late.

Everyone deserves to be treated with dignity – Americans, Haitians, everyone. We can’t lose sight of our shared humanity.

title: Larsen Seeks Answers at Ferndale ICE Facility
text:
Today, Representative Rick Larsen (WA-02) released the following statement:

“The President’s cruel immigration agenda has angered many of my constituents and struck fear in families around the region. The Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agency has been at the top of this agenda. I came to the Ferndale ICE holding facility today to get answers about this facility for my community.

“Where I was not able to get complete answers, I will be sending a follow-up oversight letter. I expect to get additional details about ICE’s recent policy changes for this kind of facility and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI) operations locally.

“I was able to get answers to the following questions community members have about the facility’s operations:

“1. The facility has two holding cells that have room for eight people each. The average time a detained person stays in the facility is 4-5 hours. Since July 1, ICE has had a policy that no one can be detained in this type of facility for longer than 12 hours. People held by ICE here are first processed and then transferred to the privately-run detention center in Tacoma.

“2. People detained in the facility have access to a toilet and a sink. There are no kitchen or shower facilities, or medical personnel on staff, because of the short detainment periods. However, there is a process for non-emergent or emergent care.

“3. There are two private rooms with telephones where detained people can call an attorney if they have one.

“4. HSI has been responsible for the operations that detained nearly 50 people in Lynden in recent months. I intend to follow up with the Department of Homeland Security, HSI and ICE about HSI’s role in immigration enforcement and removal operations locally.

“As a service to my constituents, my office is going to work with this local ICE facility in Ferndale to establish a process where people who are detained here can get the necessary paperwork to request support from my staff.

“The President’s immigration enforcement agenda is hurting the local economy and making our communities less safe. My office stands ready to help family members locate their loved ones in ICE custody and access legal services – call 425-252-3188 or go to larsen.house.gov/helping-you/visas-and-immigration.htm.”

Larsen Fights to Hold ICE Accountable

In June 2025, Rep. Larsen toured the privately-run ICE detention facility in Tacoma and met with Lelo Juarez, a Skagit County union leader and activist whom ICE detained in March 2025.

Earlier this month, Rep. Larsen joined nearly 200 House Democrats in calling for independent investigations into Lorenzo Salgado Araujo and Johan Sebastian Guerrero’s deaths and demanding that ICE halt removal proceedings against the witnesses. He also demanded independent investigations into the killings of Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good in Minneapolis in January 2026.

In Congress, Rep. Larsen has refused to vote for legislation that would fund ICE without placing additional guardrails on the agency and requiring that ICE follow the same rules as every other local, state and federal law enforcement agency.

Rep. Larsen supports strengthening accountability and oversight of ICE operations and DHS detention facilities, including:

Prohibiting ICE officers from wearing masks during arrests;

Requiring ICE officers to be trained in de-escalation;

Prohibiting masked ICE officers from using restricted equipment, such as tear gas;

Ending family and child detention;

Ending DHS’s use of private detention facilities;

Providing individuals in immigration detention with unlimited communication with legal counsel;

Repealing the Alien Enemies Act, which President Trump has used to deport immigrants from Venezuela with no due process by accusing them of “invading” the United States; and

A complete and independent investigation into the killings of unarmed civilians.

title: Lawler To Improve Recycling Data, Expand Access To Recycling Nationwide With New Bill
text:
Washington, D.C. – 7/31/26… This week, Congressman Mike Lawler (NY-17) and Josh Gotthiemer (NJ-05) introduced the Recycling Infrastructure and Data Accountability Act, legislation that would direct the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) to study the feasibility of establishing a standardized national database to better track recycling infrastructure, recyclable materials, material recovery outcomes, landfill diversion, and communities that lack access to recycling services.

Across the country, communities, municipalities, and businesses face challenges caused by limited recycling infrastructure, inconsistent data collection, and gaps in processing capacity. The legislation would help provide a clearer picture of America’s recycling system and identify where investments and improvements are needed most.

“Recycling is an important part of protecting our environment, supporting local communities, and ensuring we are making the most of valuable materials. But without accurate, comprehensive data, we cannot effectively address the challenges facing our recycling infrastructure. This legislation will help identify where gaps exist, where capacity needs to be expanded, and how we can build a more efficient and accountable recycling system for communities across the country, including right here in the Hudson Valley,” said Congressman Mike Lawler.

“Every family in North Jersey deserves a cleaner environment and a recycling system that actually works. But right now, we're flying blind without reliable, nationwide data to tell us what's working and where the gaps are," said Congressman Josh Gottheimer (NJ-5). "This commonsense, bipartisan bill will give us a clearer picture of where recycling infrastructure exists, where capacity needs to be expanded, and where new investments can make the biggest difference for our communities. I’m proud to team up with my colleague Mike Lawler to build a more efficient, transparent, and effective recycling system for New Jersey and communities across the country.”

Specifically, this legislation would require the EPA to conduct a study examining the feasibility of a national recycling database that would:

Track recyclable materials, recycling infrastructure capacity, material recovery outcomes, and landfill diversion rates;

Identify geographic areas with limited access to recycling collection services and processing facilities;

Catalog major recycling and waste facilities, including facility type, ownership, capacity, materials accepted, and annual throughput;

Full text of the bill can be found HERE.

Congressman Lawler is one of the most bipartisan members of Congress and represents New York's 17th Congressional District, which is just north of New York City and contains all or parts of Rockland, Putnam, Dutchess, and Westchester Counties. He was rated the most effective freshman lawmaker in the 118th Congress, 8th overall, surpassing dozens of committee chairs.

title: Rep. Luna Introduces Bipartisan Bill to Require Clear Gluten Labeling
text:
Washington, D.C. — On Thursday, Congresswoman Anna Paulina Luna (FL-13) introduced the bipartisan Food Allergy Safety, Treatment, Education, and Research (FASTER) Act of 2026, legislation that would amend the FDA’s major food allergen labeling requirements to include barley, rye, and oats alongside wheat, closing a gap in federal law that leaves millions of Americans with celiac disease and gluten intolerance exposed to hidden sources of gluten.

“I actually have a gluten intolerance myself, and it’s terrifying when labels aren’t clear because that can have serious medical consequences,” said Congresswoman Luna. “Millions of Americans are affected by celiac disease or gluten intolerance; it’s a real and serious issue, and it’s time the food industry respected that. We need transparent labeling so Americans can make informed decisions and safeguard their health.”

The bill amends the Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act by replacing “wheat” in the definition of a major food allergen with “gluten-containing grain,” defined to include wheat, barley, rye, oats, and crossbred hybrids such as triticale. It also directs the Department of Health and Human Services to report to Congress on celiac disease surveillance, diagnostics, prevention, risk reduction, and the development of new treatments.

“People with celiac disease and gluten intolerance should be able to look at a food label and immediately see whether it contains barley, rye, or oats,” said Congressman Van Drew. “This bill makes those ingredients easier to identify instead of relying only on the ingredient list. It is a simple, common-sense change that will help prevent mistakes and keep people safe, and I am proud to join Congresswoman Luna in this effort.”

This action comes amid growing concern over the health risks posed by accidental gluten exposure. An estimated 25.7 million Americans have celiac disease, gluten intolerance, or an IgE-mediated wheat allergy with potential cross-reactivity to barley, rye, and oats. For people with celiac disease, consuming gluten can cause intestinal damage, anemia, malnutrition, immunological scarring, heart disease, cancer, and other serious health complications.

“Americans deserve to know what’s in the food they buy,” said Rep. Randy Weber (TX-14). “More than 3.3 million Americans living with celiac disease rely on accurate labeling to protect their health, and this bill is a first step toward greater transparency for consumers.”

There is no cure or rescue medication for accidental ingestion, and even among those who follow a strict gluten-free diet, 44 percent still report being “glutened” at least once a month.

“Everyone deserves to know what’s in their food, especially when it may contain allergens,” said Congressman Suozzi. “By requiring all packaged foods to clearly label even small traces of rye, oats, and barley, the FASTER Act ensures that Americans with celiac can feel confident that their food is safe to eat. I’m proud to sponsor this common-sense, life-saving legislation.”

Since 2006, federal law has required wheat to be identified as a major food allergen, while barley, rye, and oats have remained outside the mandatory labeling requirement. These grains can be hidden in seasonings, flavorings, and fine print, leaving consumers without the clear information they need to avoid gluten. Meanwhile, 87 other countries require the labeling of wheat, barley, rye, and oats, including Canada, the United Kingdom, and countries across the European Union.

Celiac advocates and affected families have urged the United States to adopt the same protections, an effort that has drawn support from both sides of the aisle and led to the FASTER ACT receiving bipartisan support.

“No one should have to risk their health because of confusing food labels,” said Congressman Rulli. “This legislation strengthens transparency and gives Americans with celiac disease the information they need to confidently choose safe foods.”

The legislation has also been championed by 13-year-old Jax Bari, known as the “MAHA Kid” and co-founder of Celiac Journey, whose advocacy has helped bring national attention to the gaps in federal gluten-labeling requirements.

“I’m grateful to Congresswoman Luna and the original co-sponsors for introducing the bipartisan FASTER Act of 2026 which will require the labeling of barley, rye and oats as Major Food Allergens. My goal is to eat without fear because Celiac is every bite, every day – constant questioning, constant worrying. Just a crumb of gluten is like kryptonite to me. 87 other countries require the labeling of wheat, barley, rye and oats, including in Canada, in the United Kingdom and across the European Union. We’re really behind in the United States, and the FASTER Act will help close the gap and better protect 729,000 kids like me with Celiac,” said Jax Bari.

After meeting with Congresswoman Luna in June, Jax discussed the ambiguity surrounding gluten-containing grains during a June 16 meeting with Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche, who also has celiac disease. Blanche agreed that clearer standards are needed and expressed support for Jax’s efforts to require barley, rye, and oats to be labeled as major food allergens. Blanche’s wife, Dr. Kristine Blanche, and their daughter Sydney, who has celiac disease, have also supported his advocacy.

The FASTER Act was introduced with original cosponsors Reps. Randy K. Weber Sr. (TX-14), Paul A. Gosar (AZ-09), Daniel Meuser (PA-09), Jefferson Van Drew (NJ-02), Chellie Pingree (ME-01), Madeleine Dean (PA-04), Tom Suozzi (NY-03), Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), Tom Barrett (MI-07), and Michael Rulli (OH-06).

title: RI Delegation Joins Seniors on Anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid, Discuss their Fight to Lower Health Care Costs
text:
COVENTRY, R.I. – Today, U.S. Senators Jack Reed (D-RI) and Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), along with U.S. Representative Seth Magaziner (RI-02), joined seniors and Neighborhood Health CEO Peter Marino at the Coventry Resource and Senior Center to mark the 61st anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid, provide an update on health care policy in Washington, and reaffirm their commitment to lowering health care costs for Rhode Islanders.

The event comes as Rhode Islanders continue to face rising health care costs following deep cuts enacted by President Trump and Congressional Republicans, including a nearly $1 trillion cut to Medicaid and the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits that helped make coverage more affordable.

View or download photos from the event here.

“Medicare and Medicaid are cost-effective and critical to the health and well-being of thousands of Rhode Islanders and millions of Americans. These programs have helped lift millions of Americans out of poverty, improved their health, and advanced health care innovations that benefit everyone. The historic success of Medicare is self-evident: Before Medicare was enacted, roughly half of all seniors had health insurance. Today, 99 percent of American seniors -- adults aged 65 and older -- have health insurance,” said Senator Reed. “Working together, we can keep the promise of Medicare and Medicaid and ensure these programs are there for older Americans today, tomorrow, and for another sixty-one years. Supporting Medicare and Medicaid provides quality health care to more Americans, slows rising health care costs, and helps reduce federal budget deficit.”

“For 61 years, Medicare and Medicaid have helped Rhode Islanders access affordable, lifesaving health care,” said Senator Whitehouse. “Republican chaos and corruption are driving up Americans’ costs, and the party’s bizarre obsession with ripping away health care has destabilized our already-fragile health care system. It’s a disgrace, and I remain committed to protecting Medicare and Medicaid from Republican mischief.”

“Medicare and Medicaid have helped provide health care to Rhode Islanders for 61 years,” said Magaziner. “But health care has become increasingly unaffordable and inaccessible because of direct attacks by the President and Congressional Republicans. We must do better. I, along with the entire delegation, will continue fighting for a health care system that is affordable for all Americans.”

“Medicare and Medicaid make a tremendous difference, especially because both programs help people manage chronic conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes, and continue living full lives,” said Peter Marino, President and CEO of Neighborhood Health Plan. “These programs make it more likely that someone will see a doctor when something feels wrong instead of waiting until a health issue becomes an emergency. For people without coverage, the choice too often becomes whether to seek care or pay for other basic needs. No one should have to make that choice. That’s why we need to continue investing in these vital programs – it is how we make sure we are taking care of each other.”

The event commemorated the signing of Medicare and Medicaid into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson 61 years ago while highlighting the challenges Rhode Islanders face today as health care becomes increasingly expensive and inaccessible.

During the event, the Delegation members outlined how recent federal health care cuts are affecting Rhode Islanders and the broader health care system. They also reaffirmed their commitment to protecting Medicare and Medicaid, reversing harmful cuts, and lowering health care costs for working people across the state.

For 61 years, Medicare and Medicaid have helped millions of Americans access quality, affordable health care. Today, more than 309,000 Rhode Islanders rely on Medicaid, including 64 percent of nursing home residents, more than half of adults with disabilities, 37 percent of children, and 43 percent of births in the state. An estimated 34,000 Rhode Islanders are expected to lose health insurance once Medicaid cuts passed by Republicans are in full effect. Another 244,570 Rhode Islanders, nearly one in five residents, depend on Medicare for their health coverage and have seen their health insurance rates skyrocket. Members of the Rhode Island delegation outline how recent Republican cuts to Medicaid and the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits threaten to increase health care costs and put additional strain on the state's health care system. They reiterated their commitment to protecting Medicare, restoring affordable health coverage, and ensuring every Rhode Islander can access the care they need.

title: Amid Dr. Fauci’s Refusal to Answer More Than 100 Questions Before Congress, Congressman McCormick Reintroduces STOP the SWAMP Act
text:
Washington, D.C. — Today, Congressman Rich McCormick (GA-07) reintroduced the STOP the SWAMP Act to strengthen congressional oversight and hold federal employees accountable for obstructing congressional investigations.

This critical piece of legislation would bar individuals from working for the federal government if they refuse to answer certain questions before Congress or are convicted of perjury. This bill authorizes members of Congress to refer witnesses who unlawfully withhold information to the Department of Justice (DOJ), establishing clear consequences for those who obstruct federal investigations.

“If you can hide from Congress, you shouldn’t be able to work for the federal government,” said Congressman McCormick. “Congress has a constitutional duty to conduct oversight, and federal employees have a duty to tell the truth. Full stop. If someone lies under oath or refuses to cooperate with a lawful investigation, there should be consequences. Public service is a privilege, and no one is above the law.”

Congressman McCormick reintroduced the STOP the SWAMP Act following renewed scrutiny surrounding Dr. Anthony Fauci’s testimony before the Senate on Wednesday, July 29, 2026. Dr. Fauci invoked the Fifth Amendment and declined to answer more than 100 questions from senators investigating the federal government’s COVID-19 response. The hearing examined Fauci’s actions during the pandemic, including decisions related to broader federal health care policy.

title: Congressman Menefee Hears from Houstonians Struggling Under Republicans' Rising Cost Agenda

More than 392,000 Texans have lost Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) benefits following passage of Republicans' budget law.

title: Reps. Min, Lawler, Huffman and Fitzpatrick Call for Stronger Federal E-Bike and E-Moto Safety Standards
text:
Washington, D.C. — Congressman Dave Min (CA-47), joined by Representatives Michael Lawler (NY-17), Jared Huffman (CA-02), and Brian Fitzpatrick (PA-01), sent a letter urging the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC) to develop comprehensive federal safety standards for electric bicycles and higher-speed “e-motos”.

The bipartisan letter comes in response to the CPSC’s Notice of Proposed Rulemaking to establish safety standards for lithium-ion batteries used for e-bikes and other forms of micromobility transit. While the lawmakers acknowledged the importance of addressing the serious fire risks posed by low-quality batteries, they keyed in on the CPSC’s failure to address the broader risks posed by unregulated e-bikes and e-motos.

“While we strongly support the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission taking action to address fire hazards posed by counterfeit and low-quality lithium-ion batteries associated with these products, battery integrity is only one component of a broader set of challenges facing consumers and communities,” said the Members. “We urge the Commission to build on this effort by developing separate, comprehensive safety standards for e-bikes and electric motorcycles.”

“Fire-safe batteries matter, but they will not stop companies from marketing devices capable of motorcycle-level speeds to children as ordinary e-bikes,” said Rep. Min. “Parents should not have to become product safety experts just to know what they are buying for their kids. The CPSC must close these loopholes, require clear product labeling, and establish modern standards that distinguish e-bikes from high-powered e-motos.”

The reforms outlined in the letter reflect key provisions of Congressman Min’s Safe Standards for Personal E-Bike and E-Moto Device Specifications Act, Safe SPEEDS Act, which would establish a comprehensive federal safety framework for electric micromobility products.

Between 2019 and 2022, as e-bike sales in the United States nearly quadrupled, injuries involving e-bikes and e-motos increased by nearly tenfold, according to estimates from the CPSC’s National Electronic Injury Surveillance System. Children and teenagers face particularly serious risks. Health care providers at Rady Children’s Health treated one pediatric e-bike crash patient in 2021 and more than 220 in 2025.

The letter also highlights fatal crashes involving young riders and community members, including the death of 20-year-old Huntington Beach resident Kolby Aipa after an e-bike collision.

The lawmakers urged the CPSC to:

Establish minimum labeling requirements clearly disclosing each device’s maximum speed, motor power, recommended minimum age and intended on-road or off-road use.

Modernize the federal definition of an e-bike and create consistent classifications that clearly distinguish conventional e-bikes from higher-powered e-motos.

Support local crash-data collection and public education by helping law enforcement agencies, emergency responders and local governments accurately identify devices and document injuries and fatalities.

The full letter is available here.

The letter is the latest step in Rep. Min’s continued efforts to improve e-bike safety and close gaps in federal oversight. Earlier this week, Rep. Min joined Irvine Councilmember Betty Martinez Franco’s office for an I-Ride Safe Academy panel focused on helping young riders and their families better understand e-bike risks and practice safe, responsible riding.

title: Pappas Introduces ‘Baby Brent’s Bill,’ Legislation to Legislation to Protect Newborns and Hold Formula Manufacturers Accountable
text:
This week Congressman Chris Pappas (NH-01) and Congresswoman Rosa DeLauro (CT-03) announced the introduction of Baby Brent’s Bill, legislation that would require the Federal Trade Commission (FTC) to investigate, report on, issue regulations, and enforce penalties including fines for unfair or deceptive advertising or marketing of preterm infant formula.

Inspiration for the legislation came from the Weymouth family of New Hampshire’s First District. Their son, Brent, was born preterm and contracted necrotizing enterocolitis (NEC) after being given cow’s milk-based fortifier while in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU). NEC is the most common emergency intestinal complication in premature infants, a fast-moving and life-threatening condition with an overall mortality rate of 33%. It is estimated thatone baby dies every day in the United States from NEC and those who survive may be neurodevelopmentally impaired and have lifelong consequences.

Brent contracted NEC multiple times, leading surgeons to remove more than half of his intestines. Now nearly two years old, Brent has been diagnosed with global developmental delay.

“Brent’s life was permanently altered after developing NEC multiple times in the NICU. Naming this bill after him brings a voice to a struggle that many NICU families face,” said the Weymouth family. "Parents deserve complete transparency about what goes into their babies' bodies as well as the power to hold formula and fortifier manufacturers accountable. Our family is so grateful to Congressman Pappas for honoring Brent and fighting to protect future premature infants. We hope to see Congress pass this into law. This isn’t a left or right issue but a moral one.”

Pappas’s legislation comes as formula manufacturers face mounting questions of legal accountability for the risks associated with cow's milk-based preterm formula. Abbott and Mead Johnson currently face nearly 1,000 lawsuits nationwide from families alleging the companies failed to warn about the risk of NEC, including more than 700 cases consolidated in federal court in Illinois. In April, a jury ordered Abbott to pay $70 million to four mothers whose premature babies developed NEC after being fed the company's preterm formula, finding Abbott failed to warn about the risk. In June, a Missouri appeals court upheld a $495 million verdict against Abbott in a similar case. Rather than change their marketing practices, manufacturers have pressed Congress for a legal shield to block families from seeking compensation, an effort Baby Brent's Bill directly rejects by affirming that no manufacturer should be permitted to limit families' ability to pursue legal recourse.

"Every parent deserves complete and honest information about the products being fed to their child," said Congressman Pappas. "Brent's story is a heartbreaking reminder of what is at stake when research is limited and questionable practices go uninvestigated. I will not stand by while the status quo allows manufacturers to market formula without disclosing risks, and we must stop efforts by those same manufacturers to evade accountability. I’m introducing Baby Brent's Bill because families like Brent’s deserve transparency and the ability to seek justice when they’re harmed."

“Preterm infant formula is not like any other product—it is vital to a vulnerable infant’s survival, and parents are understandably risk-averse when it comes to the health and safety of their newborn baby,” said Congresswoman DeLauro. “Our infant formula industry is dominated by two companies, and they compete with one another to ensure their formula is the ‘first bottle fed’, aggressively pushing their products in hospital NICUs in order to get parents hooked as future customers. At a time when hundreds of lawsuits are alleging a connection between bovine milk fortifiers used by big infant formula manufacturers and increased incidence rates of a potentially fatal disease known as Necrotizing Enterocolitis (NEC), it is more important than ever that we shine a light on the preterm infant formula market. Baby Brent’s Bill would require the Federal Trade Commission to investigate preterm infant formula manufactures' marketing and advertising practices to expose any deceptive behavior by these companies trying to secure greater market share. In order to continue putting babies first, we need to know what’s going on behind hospital doors.”

Specifically, Pappas’s legislation:

Directs the FTC to conduct an investigation and submit to Congress a report within one year of enactment on unfair or deceptive acts or practices that may be prevalent in the advertising or marketing of preterm infant formula;

Directs the FTC to issue regulations to prohibit such practices and enforce such regulations no later than 18 months after the submission of their report;

Directs the FTC to enforce fines and penalties for such practices consistent with the current legal maximums under section 18(a)(1)(B) of the Federal Trade Commission Act, including up to $53,088 per violation along with other forms of relief, including the payment of damages to consumers and others resulting from the violation of the rules;

Expresses the sense of Congress that parents should retain the right to be fully informed about, and be able to protect, the health of their preterm infants; that additional research is needed into the potential risks associated with cow’s-milk based fortifiers and the causes of NEC; and that no manufacturer should be permitted to limit or evade families' ability to pursue legal recourse.

title: Raskin, DeLauro, Casten, Jacobs and 111 Colleagues Demand Netanyahu Remove Barbed-Wire Fence Blocking Students’ Path from West Bank Village Umm Al-Kheir to School
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – Today, Representatives Jamie Raskin (MD-08), Rosa DeLauro (CT-03), Sean Casten (IL-06) and Sara Jacobs (CA-51) led 111 Members in demanding Israeli Prime Minister Bejamin Netanyahuremove barbed-wire fencing erected by settlers that is blocking students in the West Bank village of Umm Al-Kheir from traveling to their school. In a letter to Prime Minister Netanyahu, the lawmakers called for an end to settler violence and intimidation in violation of international human rights law.

“For over three months, extremists from the nearby settlement of Carmel have maintained a barbed wire fence blocking the path that the children of Umm Al-Kheir use to travel to their school,”the lawmakers wrote. “This action, which has benefited from the protection of Israeli soldiers, is a violation of the fundamental right to an education.”

Umm Al-Kheir, a Bedouin shepherding community, has faced extremist attacks for years as Israeli settlements have encroached on the village. Across the West Bank, these attacks have intensified as the Israeli military increasingly provides protection to the perpetrators.

In April, children from Umm Al-Kheir first found their path to school blocked by the fencing. Adults from the village called for assistance from the Israeli military, who ultimately shot tear gas towards the students following their arrival. One of the victims was the five-year-old son of Awdah Hathaleen, who was killed by a settler during a July 2025 attack on Umm Al-Kheir. Hathaleen was a major contributor to the internationally acclaimed filmNo Other Land.

“Israeli soldiers’ actions exposed over two dozen children to tear gas, raising serious questions about how the Israeli military is abetting extremist violence against Umm Al-Kheir,”the lawmakers continued. “Rather than intervening in defense of vulnerable students’ basic right to go to school, Israeli military personnel have reportedly been standing along the fence, seemingly granting settlers permission to continue obstructing the road to the school.”

While the Israeli military has tried to suggest a longer alternative route for children from Umm Al-Kheir to reach their school, it comes with significant security risks. The alternative route roughly doubles the distance that students need to travel and forces them to pass Carmel, creating even more daily opportunities for negative and traumatizing interactions with settlers.

Rep. Raskin previously led a letter signed by 100 of his colleaguesurging Prime Minister Netanyahu to immediately halt plans to demolish buildings, including private homes and a community center, in Umm Al-Kheir.

The letter is also signed by Reps. The letter is endorsed by J Street, New Jewish Narrative, Friends Committee on National Legislation (FCNL) and Center for International Policy Advocacy.

Read the full text of the letterhere and below.

Dear Prime Minister Netanyahu,

As Congressional supporters of human rights and democracy all over the world, we write to vigorously condemn the settler violence and intimidation afflicting the West Bank village of Umm Al-Kheir. For over three months, extremists from the nearby settlement of Carmel have maintained a barbed wire fence blocking the path that the children of Umm Al-Kheir use to travel to their school. This action, which has benefited from the protection of Israeli soldiers, is a violation of the fundamental right to an education. Particularly at a time when the American public is increasingly skeptical of Israel’s commitment to peace, it is vital that your government take immediate steps to remove the fence and restore educational access in Umm Al-Kheir.

On April 13, 2026, students in Umm Al-Kheir found their path to school blocked by a barbed wire fence erected by settlers from the adjacent settlement of Carmel. Adults from the village called the Israeli police for assistance, but instead, soldiers arrived and shot tear gas toward the children. One of the victims was the five-year-old son of Awdah Hathaleen, who taught at the school in Umm Al-Kheir before a settler killed him during a July 2025 attack on the village. The fact that Hathaleen, who was a major contributor to the internationally acclaimed film No Other Land, and his young son were subject to state and settler violence not a year apart from one another is a terrible stain on your government and testament to the intergenerational harm Umm Al-Kheir has endured.

Israeli soldiers’ actions exposed over two dozen children to tear gas, raising serious questions about how the Israeli military is abetting extremist violence against Umm Al-Kheir. Rather than intervening in defense of vulnerable students’ basic right to go to school, Israeli military personnel have reportedly been standing along the fence, seemingly granting settlers permission to continue obstructing the road to the school. In recent months, Israeli forces have faced growing criticism for enabling settlers’ harassment of communities in the West Bank. We are concerned that this dynamic is affecting Umm-Al Kheir, whose residents report sustained attacks and threats by settlers. As recently as June 4, 2026, Yosef Haddad, who is a known instigator of violence whom Israeli police have previously arrested, publicly mocked and threatened villagers by the fence, warning that they “haven’t seen anything yet.”

We understand that the Israeli military has suggested an alternative route for students to reach their school. However, this route is associated with significant security risks, and many parents have understandably decided to keep their children at home. The alternative route roughly doubles the distance that students need to travel and forces them to pass Carmel, creating more risks for negative and traumatizing interactions with settlers. Its use will only escalate violence in the community.

Across the West Bank, extremist attacks have intensified as the Israeli military increasingly provides protection to the perpetrators. Your government’s dramatic acceleration of settlement construction—in violation of international law—has sent a similar signal of license to the settlers. Such actions imperil prospects for peace in the region, undermine Israeli security interests and place villages like Umm Al-Kheir at great risk.

At this critical juncture, continuing down the path of settler extremism will further degrade Israel’s international standing and relationship with the United States. You can begin to reverse this dangerous and isolating approach by ordering your soldiers to remove the barbed wire fence in Umm Al-Kheir and to safeguard every child’s right to an education.

We urge you to respect the basic premise that every child deserves to learn in peace.

title: Congresswoman Scanlon Conducts Unannounced Oversight Visit to Moshannon Valley Processing Center, Largest ICE Detention Center in Northeast
text:
Chester, PA — Congresswoman Mary Gay Scanlon (PA-05) this week conducted an unannounced Congressional oversight visit inside Moshannon Valley Processing Center, the largest ICE detention center in the Northeast. After a roughly 30 minute wait, Rep. Scanlon gained entry to the facility and was provided a tour of the Moshannon facility by ICE and GEO administrators for 3 hours. With one exception, she was not allowed to speak with detainees.

The visit occurred without prior notice to ICE after a March 2 court order blocked ICE actions to restrict access to detention facilities by Members of Congress and reaffirmed their legal right to conduct unannounced oversight visits to those facilities.

Moshannon Valley Processing Center is a former prison owned and operated by private prison contractor, GEO Group, and now used solely for immigration detention. While reports of poor conditions at Moshannon have circulated for years, they have dramatically increased since the start of the Trump Administration’s mass deportation efforts, including a hunger strike, reports of inadequate medical care and neglect, allegations of sexual assault, and two detainee deaths.

“The American people are entitled to know how their tax dollars are being spent. Given the billions of dollars in deficit spending that Congressional Republicans and the Trump White House are devoting to mass deportation, it is more important than ever that Congress conduct oversight of ICE and DHS operations to find out how those taxpayer dollars are being spent, and ensure that people being held in custody by the United States government are treated humanely,” said Rep. Scanlon. “Following numerous reports of unsafe living conditions, subpar medical care, and two deaths at this private prison facility, in which dozens of my community members and constituents have been detained against their will, it would be irresponsible not to inspect conditions at Moshannon firsthand. GEO charges us millions of dollars every month to detain people at Moshannon. Taxpayer dollars should be spent to improve the lives of Americans, not to inflict misery and make private prison contractors rich.”

Rep. Scanlon summarized her key takeaways as follows:

Administrators reported that the population at Moshannon during the visit was 1,634 — consistent with increased detention numbers across the country as ICE arrests have escalated in June and July 2026.

Officials at Moshannon indicated that 1,311 of the 1,634 individuals detained at the time of the visit were considered low-security. ICE’s FY2026 statistics confirm that the vast majority (8 out of 10) of people detained at Moshannon have no criminal record.

Only 46 (less than 3%) of detainees were women. This aligns with reports that ICE is targeting male breadwinners for detention in order to pressure self-deportation by entire family units (including children who are U.S. citizens).

The average stay at Moshannon was reported by administrators to be 34 days; current online statistics from ICE list a higher (46 days) average stay.

While ICE and GEO officials on site said that they did not know or could not disclose how much ICE pays GEO to operate the facility at Moshannon, public reporting indicates that GEO is receiving over $5.3 million per month, consisting of a monthly management fee of at least $3.4 million and an additional fee of $10 per person per day up to 800 detainees, and $40 per person per day for over 800 detainees. This fee structure provides a perverse incentive for private prisons to prolong detention. GEO Group representatives also confirmed that it charges the government additional fees for its expanding private transportation services.

If one prorates GEO’s monthly fees as reported for May 2025, before the most recent surge, it is costing taxpayers $43,741 per year to detain someone at Moshannon, which is about what it costs to send a student to Penn State University nearby for a year.

Moshannon Valley Processing Center is a former prison, and is run using prison practices. Detained individuals are required to wear color-coded prison garb and eat in their living quarters. There are severe constraints upon their liberty and their ability to contact family and anyone outside the facility.

By law, immigration detention is supposed to be a form of civil process, not criminal punishment, meaning the system is supposed to be used to manage flight or safety risks and ensure that people attend their court hearings. What detained individuals experience at Moshannon could not be described as anything other than punitive — at best.

Detainees must perform most of the labor at the facility where they are being involuntarily held, including cleaning showers, toilets, and living quarters, and supplying the majority of labor for food service and laundry. Only two full-time janitors service the entire facility, which has a capacity of more than 1,800 people. While GEO and ICE say that such labor is “voluntary,” an administrator acknowledged that these core functions could not be performed without detainee labor. By using detainee labor, rather than hiring employees or contractors at market rates, the private contractor increases its profits.

Many detainees avoid the institutional meals which administrators said are prepared to meet correctional facility caloric and nutrition standards. Due to poor food quality, detainees have initiated two hunger strike protests this year and rely upon food such as ramen noodles purchased from the facility’s commissary, using funds sent to them by friends or relatives. The Congresswoman saw such prepackaged food in the living quarters. She was provided with a lunch tray in the dining hall, which detainees cannot use, but was unable to compare it to what detainees were served.

While the facility denies using solitary confinement for punishment, its “Special Management Unit” currently has 29 detainees in single cells, separate from the general population. The physical setup of the unit, and admissions by management that some detainees were assigned there for infraction of facility rules, at least partially confirmed reports of abuse of solitary confinement standards. All cells were occupied by only one person. Some were on suicide watch. One had been held there for 220 days. Daily recreation for residents of that unit takes place in a cement block hall containing chain link cages in which “natural light and fresh air” is provided by 1’ x 3’ openings in the wall about 12 feet above floor level.

During her visit to Moshannon Valley Processing Center, Rep. Scanlon was able to speak with one of her constituents who had previously completed an ICE Privacy Waiver that authorizes the release of information to a third party, including a Congressional office. Moshannon administrators barred the Congresswoman from speaking with other detainees, which made it difficult to assess their actual treatment and conditions.

The July 29 visit follows an August 2025 visit to Moshannon, when Rep. Scanlon was denied entry under orders of former Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem, and her January 2026 oversight visit to Philadelphia Federal Detention Center, which serves as a temporary holding facility for individuals detained in the area before they are transferred to Moshannon or elsewhere.

Rep. Scanlon, who is a member of the House Judiciary Subcommittee on Immigration, has previously visited a detention center and migrant shelter in Texas, ports of entry on both the northern and southern borders, and a family detention center in Berks County, PA, which has since been closed.
