title: Topeka Capital-Journal: New federal legislation seeks to save rural hospitals in Kansas
text:
New federal legislation seeks to save rural hospitals in Kansas

The Topeka Capital-Journal

By: Stacey Saldanha-Olson

July 31, 2026

Rural hospitals in Kansas could soon have expanded resources and be less at risk of closing.

On July 29, U.S. Sen. Jerry Moran, R-Kansas, and U.S. Sen. Tina Smith, D-Minnesota, introduced the Rural Emergency Hospital Improvement Act, also dubbed REH 2.0.

The bill would allow more Critical Access Hospitals and rural hospitals at risk of closure to sustain health care services in rural communities, and it would make technical improvements to the designation.

U.S. Sen. Jerry Moran's expanded efforts to improve rural Kansas hospitals

Along with REH 2.0, Moran has spent the last year working at the federal level to get Kansas rural hospitals more Medicaid reimbursements.

Now his multi-tiered efforts can work in tandem to improve rural hospitals viability.

“I have visited every hospital in Kansas numerous times, and these conversations help guide my efforts to make certain health care providers across our state have the support they need to provide critical services to patients in their communities,” said Moran in a written statement. “During these visits, providers shared with me their recommendations for strengthening the Rural Emergency Hospital designation so it can better support the struggling facilities it was originally intended to serve.

"The legislation I am introducing with Senator Tina Smith is the direct result of what we have heard from rural hospitals and health care providers in our states, and it makes needed improvements to the program to help make certain patients can continue to access critical health care services in their communities for years to come."

Kansas rural hospital leaders thank U.S. Sen. Jerry Moran for his work

Joel Phelps, Salina Regional Health Center CEO, said the bill would allow more hospitals across the state to stay open, offering closer options for patients in need.

"What this bill is going to allow rural hospitals to do is I believe provide more of an opportunity to take care of patients closer to home," Phelps said. "It's no secret they do better when they're closer to home."

Phelps also told The Capital-Journal it would have a positive impact on other non-rural hospitals by preventing overcrowding of patients. He thanked Moran for working to help rural hospitals.

"We appreciate Senator Moran's continued leadership on behalf of rural healthcare in Kansas," Phelps said. "He's really continued to step up."

Read the full story from the Topeka Capital-Journal here.

title: Moreno Calls for Investigation of CCP-Linked Company Encroaching on Military Base
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, Senator Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) sent a letter to Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent requesting a formal review of SolarSpace’s plan to purchase or lease land near Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. Solarspace, a Chinese solar cell manufacturer with ties to the Chinese Communist Party, is seeking to establish a U.S. foothold near one of the nation’s most strategically sensitive military installations.

“I applaud the Trump Administration’s continued commitment to tracking foreign land ownership,” wrote Senator Moreno. “At a time when the Chinese Communist Party has leveraged American commercial entities to advance its military and intelligence objectives, we cannot let this potential transaction proceed without investigation. While the Supreme Court’s recent decision was, unfortunately, in the words of President Trump, a ‘massive Birthright Citizenship WIN!’ for China, I hope we can work together to ensure that the Chinese Communist Party is never allowed to purchase or lease land near our military installations.”

Read the full text of the letter HERE or below.

July 31, 2026

The Honorable Scott Bessent

Secretary of the Treasury

Chairperson of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States

1500 Pennsylvania Ave. NW

Washington, D.C., 20220

Dear Secretary Bessent,

I am writing to you in your capacity as Chairperson of the Committee on Foreign Investment in the United States to formally request a comprehensive national security review pursuant to a referral for investigation that I have grave concerns about. On June 22, 2026, the Dayton Development Coalition referred a pending real estate transaction involving SolarSpace Technology Co., Ltd. (“SolarSpace”), a Chinese manufacturer of photovoltaic cells and modules, to your office.

It is my understanding that SolarSpace intends to lease or purchase a facility located at 2555 Woodman Drive, Kettering, Ohio, which is approximately 13 miles from Wright-Patterson Air Force Base. Wright-Patterson Air Force Base is a critical military installation with a workforce of approximately 38,000 employees, including military personnel, civilians, and contractors, dedicated to defending our nation against foreign adversaries. The base is not only one of the Department of War’s most strategically significant installations, but also a cornerstone of U.S. air and space superiority, serving as a central hub for aerospace research, engineering, and intelligence, including the Air Force Research Laboratory. Yet, one of our greatest foes is attempting to move in nearly next door.

I applaud the Trump Administration’s continued commitment to tracking foreign land ownership. At a time when the Chinese Communist Party has leveraged American commercial entities to advance its military and intelligence objectives, we cannot let this potential transaction proceed without investigation. While the Supreme Court’s recent decision was, unfortunately, in the words of President Trump, a “massive Birthright Citizenship WIN!” for China, I hope we can work together to ensure that the Chinese Communist Party is never allowed to purchase or lease land near our military installations.

I urge you to investigate this transaction immediately. We cannot allow potential shell companies for the Chinese Communist Party to buy land or facilities near our most sensitive military and critical infrastructure sites, including Wright-Patterson Air Force Base.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter. I appreciate your partnership as we work to safeguard our national security interests.

Sincerely,

BERNIE MORENO

United States Senator

title: Moreno, Slotkin Win Broad Support to Defend American Auto Industry from CCP-Linked Vehicles
text:
WASHINGTON – In case you missed it, Senator Bernie Moreno (R-Ohio) and Elissa Slotkin’s (D-Mich.) Connected Vehicle Security Act unanimously passed out of the Senate Commerce, Science, and Transportation Committee to defend America’s auto industry. Following the passage, organizations from across the American automotive ecosystem—including automakers, suppliers, manufacturers, dealers, trucking organizations, labor unions, and national security advocates—praised the legislation for safeguarding one of America’s most critical industries.

What They Are Saying:

Leading Automakers

“General Motors applauds the efforts of Senator Moreno (R-OH) and Slotkin (D-MI) in securing strong bipartisan support and passage of S. 4429, the Connected Vehicle Security Act, via voice vote out of the Senate Commerce Committee,” said General Motors. “GM supports policies that protect and strengthen American manufacturing and the global competitiveness of U.S. automakers, and we remain committed to long-term investments in our domestic workforce, facilities, and technology, and we look forward to continuing to work with all stakeholders throughout the process. As we have said many times, we can compete with anyone in the world when we are given a level playing field.”

“As the largest auto manufacturer in Ohio, Honda applauds committee passage of the Connected Vehicle Security Act, which seeks to provide a fair and competitive marketplace for U.S. automakers,” said American Honda Motor Co., Inc. “As global competition in the automotive sector intensifies, the bill importantly recognizes how American economic and national security are increasingly connected.”

“We are pleased with the committee approval of the Connected Vehicle Security Act,” said Nissan Motor Co., LTD. “We look forward to continuing to work with Senators Moreno and Slotkin on policies that matter to our customers and strengthen the future of the U.S. automotive industry.”

“Stellantis commends the Senate Commerce Committee for unanimously reporting out the Connected Vehicle Security Act,” said Stellantis N.V. “This is a significant milestone in our collective effort to provide Americans confidence that connected vehicles will remain secure, while supporting innovation and parity across the automotive industry. Stellantis looks forward to continuing to work with Congress to advance this important, bipartisan legislation.”

America’s Automotive Industry

“Alliance for Automotive Innovation represents the manufacturers producing most vehicles sold today in the U.S. These companies can compete with any company on the planet. The challenge they face today is not competing with Chinese companies but with the entire country of China – namely its industrial policy of state-owned enterprises, heavily subsidized vehicles and unfair trade,” said John Bozzella, president and CEO, Alliance for Automotive Innovation. “This threat warrants an immediate policy response from the American government. Congress should enact a ban on Chinese vehicles and connected systems in the U.S. to correct the current imbalances that are distorting and disrupting the global auto market, disadvantaging domestic automakers and undermining American national security.”

“Trucks traverse every corner of our country, and they increasingly rely on sophisticated technologies that help them operate safely, efficiently, and productively. As these systems become more deeply embedded in our nation’s supply chain, it is critical that they remain secure from foreign adversaries like China,” said American Trucking Associations SVP of Legislative Affairs Alex Rosen. “ATA commends Senators Moreno and Slotkin for advancing a smart, targeted approach to protecting our transportation infrastructure. Their legislation would help mitigate potential national security threats while ensuring that America remains a leader in the development and deployment of next-generation transportation technologies.”

“As an organization comprised of international nameplate auto dealers, we firmly believe that more competition benefits consumers and strengthens the American economy,” said AIADA President & CEO Cody Lusk. “However, what Chinese automakers have done in other markets and would like to do in ours is something altogether different. They seek to enter our country with artificially low prices, subsidized by their government and questionable labor practices, and decimate the American automotive industry. They are singularly focused on dominating our auto market and making Americans reliant on Chinese products and technology. Today’s committee vote is a positive first step in crafting legislation that counters those efforts and works for all Americans.”

“The Connected Vehicles Security Act of 2026 (CVSA), as adopted by the Senate Commerce committee, strikes an important balance that addresses key national security concerns associated with today’s technology-enabled vehicles while also ensuring that vehicle suppliers can comply with the requirements,” said MEMA, the Vehicle Suppliers Association. “MEMA appreciates the leadership of Senators Moreno and Slotkin on this legislation, and we look forward to working with them on the CVSA as it continues to move through the legislative process.”

“We congratulate Senator Moreno on the unanimous, bipartisan vote to advance the Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 out of the Commerce, Science and Transportation Committee,” said the CAR Coalition. “As government and industry share a commitment to ensuring the automotive supply chain is free of connections to countries of concern, this legislation is a critical step toward making that a reality. The CAR Coalition stands ready to continue working with Senator Moreno to ensure that the U.S. maintains a robust and secure aftermarket supply chain, one that safeguards economic growth and national security.”

“The Connected Vehicle Security Act addresses a growing national security priority by protecting the U.S. automotive industrial base from potential risks associated with foreign adversary access to connected vehicle technology,” said Association for Uncrewed Vehicle Systems International. “As vehicles become increasingly connected, autonomous and software-defined, this legislation will help safeguard critical technologies and supply chains while supporting American competitiveness. The Connected Vehicle Security Act helps protect America’s automotive industrial base from foreign adversaries as vehicles become increasingly connected and autonomous.”

“OOIDA members, nearly 40% of whom are military veterans, care deeply about both roadway safety and national security,” said Todd Spencer, President, Owner-Operator Independent Drivers Association. “It’s unfathomable that 80,000 lb. driverless commercial vehicles currently operating on American roadways rely upon technology from a global adversary for navigation. That’s why OOIDA and the nearly 150,000 small-business truckers we represent applaud the Committee for passing the Connected Vehicle Security Act and we thank Senator Moreno and Senator Slotkin for their leadership on this legislation. Currently, autonomous systems put Americans, their vehicles, and their personal privacy at risk given so many critical unanswered questions related to cybersecurity, operational safety, and data transparency. The safest operator of an 80,000 lb. commercial vehicle on America’s roadways is a well-trained, professional, human truck driver.”

American Manufacturing and Labor

“Today’s action by the Senate Commerce Committee marks an important step toward protecting American manufacturing and preserving the American Dream. The UAW applauds every member of the committee who voted to advance a strong version of the bill, and we thank the bill’s sponsors, Senators Bernie Moreno and Elissa Slotkin, for their leadership,” said United Auto Workers. “The committee recognized that America needs an auto industry that invests in American workers—not one that rewards dependence on China, whose industrial strategy has leveraged Western brands to expand its market influence while advancing a business model built on low wages and weak labor standards. As the legislation continues to advance, we reiterate our opposition to carve-outs for all multinational corporations. No company should get special treatment. If they want to benefit from policies that strengthen American manufacturing, they should meet the same standards as everyone else. This legislation will help ensure that the next generation of auto investment creates good union jobs, strengthens communities, reinforces America’s manufacturing base, and keeps the future of auto production here in the United States.”

“We applaud Senators Moreno and Slotkin for championing American workers,” Alliance for American Manufacturing President Scott Paul said. “Congress has taken a major step to safeguard the 11 million American jobs that the U.S. auto supply chain supports. Our national security and economic strength depend on this lynchpin industry. We cannot afford to allow the Chinese auto import flood to hit U.S. shores. Our workers are the best in the world, but Beijing has played every trick in the book to advantage its state-backed auto manufacturers. Allowing Chinese autos to enter our market would set the U.S. into a rigged game that stakes our nation’s whole future.”

“The unanimous passage of S.4429, the Connected Vehicle Security Act, through committee is a major victory for American workers, our domestic auto industry, and our national security,” said United Steelworkers International President Roxanne Brown. “This bipartisan legislation recognizes that as technology rapidly changes, it’s essential that we defend our vital automotive supply chain. The USW applauds the Senate for acting decisively to protect good union jobs, strengthen domestic manufacturing, and safeguard the industries that are critical to our nation’s economic and national security.”

“AISI commends the Senate Commerce Committee for advancing the Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026. This bipartisan action is a critical step toward codifying the Commerce Department’s Connected Vehicle rule into law, ensuring that Chinese automakers cannot manufacture or sell connected vehicles in the United States,” said American Iron and Steel Institute. “As with steel, Chinese vehicles are heavily subsidized by the Chinese government. China is determined to expand its automotive footprint globally by any means necessary, including through a wide variety of unfair and predatory practices. Committee passage of this legislation sends a clear signal that Congress will not allow these massively subsidized vehicles that can collect and transmit sensitive data to gain a foothold in the American market. By keeping Chinese-manufactured vehicles, batteries and connected components out of U.S. commerce, this bill protects our national security and strengthens the entire American automotive supply chain, including the domestic steelmakers who supply it. We thank Senators Moreno and Slotkin for authoring this legislation and members of the committee and its leadership for passing this crucial measure.”

“The Steel Manufacturers Association commends the continued leadership of Senator Moreno and Senator Slotkin on behalf of U.S. manufacturing,” said Steel Manufacturers Association Executive Vice President Brandon Farris. “The Connected Vehicle Security Act will safeguard the American auto market from policies by the Chinese government that seek to undercut and overwhelm key industrial sectors. Steelmakers have been on the front lines of this fight, and we support policies such as this that bolster U.S. national security and industrial competitiveness.”

“I commend Senator Moreno and Senator Slotkin for introducing The Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 and for their successful initiative to advance the bill through the Senate Commerce Committee,” said Lourenco Goncalves, Chairman and CEO, Cleveland-Cliffs Inc. “Just like the Chinese steel industry, auto production in China is heavily subsidized and controlled by the Chinese government. The passage of this bill is fundamental to eliminate the risk to our national security embedded into Chinese vehicles and connected components circulating freely within the United States. By eliminating this serious threat from the American homeland, we are also ensuring the Chinese do not undermine President Trump’s commitment to increase manufacturing of cars in the U.S. from a domestic supply chain. Cleveland-Cliffs is the largest supplier of steel to the American automotive industry. Passage of this legislation is critical to protecting more than 25,000 Cleveland-Cliffs steelmaking jobs and millions of American jobs in the auto manufacturing value chain.”

National Security & Policy Experts

“The Senate Commerce Committee should be applauded for advancing the Connected Vehicle Security Act with its strongest protections intact, turning back every effort to weaken them,” said Daniel Kishi, Senior Policy Advisor, American Compass. “Beijing’s subsidies and beggar-thy-neighbor policies are fueling a rapid Chinese advance across the global auto industry, which threatens American workers, industry, and national security alike. By refusing to soften the legislation’s ownership and hardware standards, the Committee held the line where it matters most: adversary capital will not buy its way into the American market through a Western label.”

“The Connected Vehicle Security Act recognizes that cars are now computers on wheels, and we cannot allow the computers on American roads to answer to Beijing,” said Chris McGuire, Senior Fellow for China and Emerging Technologies, Council on Foreign Relations. “This critical piece of legislation would keep compromised Chinese hardware and software out of American vehicles, preventing China from using Americans’ cars to surveil our citizens or map our infrastructure, or even disabling them at will. It would codify commonsense safeguards against real national security risks, protecting US national security and the American auto industry in one stroke. Congress should pass it without delay.”

“ITIF endorses the Connected Vehicle Security Act as a critical bulwark, alongside tariffs on Chinese EVs, to ensure that Chinese vehicles—which have benefitted from a plethora of unfair Chinese trade and economic practices including massive industrial subsidies and rampant IP theft—do not decimate the U.S. auto industry or create national security risks from Chinese vehicles on U.S. roads with connectivity components primed directly to do the pernicious bidding of the CCP,” said the Information Technology and Innovation Fund.

“Connected vehicle technologies carry cybersecurity risks that must be addressed to safeguard America’s national security,” said Alexandria Paolozzi Moore, FDD Action Senior Director of Government Relations. “FDD Action commends Senators Bernie Moreno and Elissa Slotkin for introducing the Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026, which confronts the cybersecurity vulnerabilities in connected vehicle systems and the risks posed by Chinese involvement in the supply chain. As adversaries seek to exploit emerging technologies, securing our transportation infrastructure is critical. This legislation strengthens America’s resilience and ensures the United States is not dependent on adversarial nations for the technology powering its vehicles.”

“SAFE strongly supports the Connected Vehicle Security Act which expands current law to combat the growing threat posed by Chinese automakers and suppliers, and the risks they pose to America’s economic and national security,” said Rachel McCleery, Executive Director of SAFE’s Coalition for Reimagined Mobility. “After gaining market access to Mexico and Canada, our geopolitical adversary is even closer to deploying vehicles on U.S. roads – vehicles that collect and transmit sensitive geolocation, infrastructure, and behavioral data at scale. This new legislation is a crucial step towards building secure and resilient supply chains, protecting our industrial base, and blocking real-time espionage and surveillance by foreign adversaries.”

Business & Economic Leaders

“Ohio is home to a deep automotive supply chain and thousands of manufacturers competing every day in a global marketplace,” said the Ohio Manufacturers’ Association President Ryan Augsburger. “We can compete with anyone, anywhere, when the rules are fair and critical technologies are protected. We appreciate Sens. Moreno and Slotkin for keeping the focus on supply chain security, fair competition and the strength of American manufacturing.”

“For decades, Ohio’s economy has benefitted greatly from the numerous automotive manufacturers and their many suppliers throughout our state,” said JP Nauseef, President & CEO, JobsOhio. “These important businesses provide good-paying jobs for thousands of Ohioans and are at the forefront of technological advancement across the automotive industry. As vehicles become increasingly data-driven, policies that strengthen supply chain resilience and protect national security are critical to Ohio’s long-term growth in the automotive sector. I applaud Sen. Moreno and Sen. Slotkin’s efforts to support these important goals advancing Ohio’s economic development momentum.”

title: Sen. Ossoff Launches Inquiry into App Store Age Ratings to Help Protect Children Online
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff is pressuring Big Tech companies to crack down on apps that put kids at risk.

Today, Sen. Ossoff launched inquiries with Apple and Google about their app store age rating requirements and urged the tech companies to strengthen the default protections for minors and provide further transparency around staffing, reporting, enforcement, and metrics.

A recent report highlighted that developers play a significant role in determining app store age ratings, with little external review. The report also raises concerns that parental controls are heavily reliant on app age ratings, which can result in minors being exposed to harmful material online.

The same report documented an instance where the app store age rating for an app was quietly downgraded from 17+ to 12+ without clear justification, disrupting parental controls for families relying on the 17+ block to restrict access.

“Incorrect age ratings can pose dangers to minors, by facilitating minors’ use of apps that enable communication with online predators or provide access to inappropriate sexual content or other harmful material. Child safety advocates have raised serious concerns that app store ratings may give parents a false sense of security and encourage minors to access content that many families reasonably expect to be restricted,” Sen. Ossoff wrote.

Sen. Ossoff continues working to protect children online.

In April, Sen. Ossoff launched inquiries with Apple, Google, Meta, Amazon, and X over tech companies’ advertisement and distribution of “nudifying” apps that allow users to swiftly create explicit images of children and teenagers.

Last December, the U.S. Senate passed Sens. Ossoff and Chuck Grassley (R-IA)’s bipartisan Preventing Child Trafficking Act of 2025 to strengthen coordination between the U.S. Department of Justice (DOJ) and U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) to better stop child trafficking and protect kids.

In July 2025, Sen. Ossoff cosponsored the bipartisan Kids Online Safety Act, which would impose new requirements on digital platforms to protect children from being targeted online with harmful content.

In March 2025, Sen. Ossoff cosponsored the bipartisan Children and Teens’ Online Privacy Protection Act (COPPA 2.0) to limit use of children’s information for individually targeted advertising.

In 2024, Sen. Ossoff’s bipartisan REPORT Act with Sen. Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) became law, which — for the first time — requires websites and social media platforms to report crimes involving Federal trafficking and enticement of children to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC). Since the law’s enactment, NCMEC has seen a 952% increase in reports of child sex trafficking and a 77% increase in reports of online enticement of children.

In 2023, Sens. Ossoff and Grassley’s bipartisan Preventing Child Sex Abuse Act of 2023 was signed into law, which strengthened Federal protections against the sexual abuse of children, including online exploitation.

Please find Sen. Ossoff’s inquiries here with Apple and Google.

title: Padilla, Schatz Introduce Legislation to Provide Paid Family, Medical Leave for Federal Employees
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-Calif.) and Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), along with seven of their colleagues, introduced the Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act, legislation to expand federal paid leave to include 12 weeks of family and medical leave.

“California is home to 228,000 federal employees, the most of any state. They shouldn’t have to choose between a paycheck and caring for themselves or their loved ones,” said Senator Padilla. “Providing 12 weeks of paid leave will strengthen the federal workforce and ensure our diligent public servants get the care they deserve.”

“Right now, our laws are forcing federal workers to make the impossible choice between caring for their families and keeping their jobs,” said Senator Schatz. “Our bill will provide federal workers with 12 weeks of paid leave, giving them the time they need to take care of their own health and their loved ones.”

Currently, under the Family and Medical Leave Act (FMLA), employees in the private sector can take up to 12 weeks of unpaid leave to care for a newborn or an ill family member without fear of losing their jobs. For federal employees, while parental leave is paid, family and medical leave continues to be unpaid.

California represents 8.5% of the federal workforce. Studies have shown that providing paid leave for federal employees would save the government at least $50 million annually in turnover and replacement costs. With federal agencies struggling to recruit and retain young talent, family-friendly policies are necessary to maintain a robust workforce. Just 6% of the federal workforce is under the age of 30, while roughly 40% of the workforce is eligible to retire within the next three years.

The Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act will guarantee 12 weeks of paid family leave for federal employees in all instances covered by the FMLA, including:

In order to care for the spouse, child, or parent of the employee, if such spouse, child, or parent has a serious health condition;

Because of a serious health condition that makes the employee unable to perform the functions of the employee’s position; and

Because of any qualifying exigency arising out of the fact that the spouse, child, or parent of the employee is on covered active duty (or has been notified of an impending call or order to covered active duty) in the Armed Forces.

In addition to Padilla and Schatz, the bill is co-sponsored by U.S. Senators Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Chris Van Hollen (D-Va.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.).

The Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act is supported by the American Federation of Government Employees, National Treasury Employees Union, International Federation of Professional and Technical Engineers, National Federation of Federal Employees, NARFE, National Association of Letter Carriers, American Postal Workers Union, and American Association of University Women.

“AFGE thanks Senator Brian Schatz for once again championing federal workers and their families by reintroducing the Comprehensive Paid Leave for Federal Employees Act. Expanding paid family and medical leave ensures federal employees never have to choose between caring for themselves or a loved one and serving the American people. This legislation will strengthen the federal workforce, improve employee retention, and help the government remain a competitive employer for the dedicated public servants our nation depends on,” said Everett Kelley, National President of the American Federation of Government Employees.

“Federal employees should never have to choose between caring for their loved ones and paying their bills on time. The Comprehensive Paid Family Leave Act would provide federal workers with the flexibility and support they need during some of life’s most significant moments. As the federal government works to attract and retain talented public servants, providing comprehensive paid family leave is both the right thing to do and a smart investment in the workforce. NTEU is proud to endorse this legislation and appreciates Senator Schatz’s continued leadership in advancing policies that strengthen the federal workforce and support working families,” said Doreen Greenwald, National President of the National Treasury Employees Union.

Full text of the bill is available here.

title: After Pressure from Sen. Reed, Administration Relents and Finally Apportions Affordable Housing Trust Fund Grants to States
text:
With a new $3.3 million boost, Reed’s 2008 law has now resulted in $33.6 million in federal HTF funding to enhance supply of affordable rental housing in RI

PROVIDENCE, RI – As part of his long-standing effort to help Rhode Island build more desirable, affordable rental housing units, U.S. Senator Jack Reed today announced another $3,311,933 is heading to the Ocean State courtesy of the national Housing Trust Fund (HTF), a program Reed created back in 2008.

Reed, a senior member of the Senate Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs Committee, who also serves as a senior member of the Appropriations Subcommittee on Transportation, Housing, Urban Development and Related Agencies (THUD), led the successful effort to create the HTF, which was authorized by the Housing and Economic Recovery Act (P.L. 110–289), which was signed into law July 30, 2008.

Reed celebrated the apportionment of the Housing Trust Fund grants after leading a campaign to successfully pressure the Trump Administration to release the funds. Last month, Reed led 22 of his colleagues in sending a letter to White House Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russell Vought demanding that the Trump Administration release housing construction funds without further delay. Reed also urged Vought to apportion the funds to HUD during a Senate Banking Committee hearing.

“It took them too long, but it’s good news that the Trump Administration finally agreed to release this long overdue federal funding to help states address the severe shortage of affordable rental housing. People need to be able to afford to live in the communities where they work. This is a smart investment in helping working families and strengthening communities, and it also helps generate jobs and economic development,” said Senator Reed. “Rhode Island can use this money to build, preserve, and repair high-quality rental housing. I created the Housing Trust Fund to provide communities with resources to help address the affordable housing shortage. Workers should be able to live closer to their jobs and spend more time with their families. Ensuring a healthy housing market is critical to our economic future.”

Reed wrote the law to ensure the Housing Trust Fund would operate at no cost to taxpayers. Instead, the program is capitalized through a portion of Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac’s profits.

Administered by the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD), the HTF is an affordable housing production and preservation program that complements existing federal, state, and local efforts to increase and preserve the supply of decent, safe, and sanitary affordable housing for extremely low-income and very low-income households, including homeless families.

To ensure that Rhode Island and other small states received a fair amount of funding, Senator Reed included a small state minimum of $3 million in the authorizing legislation.

Since 2016, HTF has allocated $3.5 billion in federal affordable housing assistance to states nationwide, and Rhode Island has now received a total of $33.6 million in federal HTF funding.

In the National Low Income Housing Coalition’s Out of Reach 2026 report, Rhode Island was ranked as the 13th most expensive state for renters, requiring a minimum wage worker to work 68 hours per week to afford a modest two-bedroom apartment.

Overall, HUD is distributing a total of $255.5 million nationwide through the national Housing Trust Fund this year to build, preserve, and rehabilitate affordable rental housing.

title: Sen. Rick Scott, Rep. Ben Cline Push to End Overregulation and Cut Red Tape for Small Businesses
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C.- Today, U.S. Senator Rick Scott announced the introduction of the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act to make it easier for Americans to open small businesses.

Regulations cost the U.S. economy more than $2 trillion annually, and they especially hurt small businesses.

The Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act helps American entrepreneurs by forcing regulatory agencies to examine the true costs of every rule, regulation, or requirement. The bill improves the federal rulemaking by requiring designated agencies to assess the economic impact of a proposed regulation on small businesses and requires detailed descriptions of alternatives to a proposed rule with significant economic impact that would minimize any adverse economic impact or maximize any beneficial economic impact.

Senator Rick Scott said, “A cornerstone of the American dream is the entrepreneurial spirit, but more and more small businesses are giving up because of overregulation and red tape. When I opened my first business, my donut shop only needed a handful of permits. Now, self-absorbed bureaucrats are piling on hundreds of regulations without thinking of the consequences for individual businesses and the U.S. economy. It’s our job to ensure hardworking people can live out the American Dream without the government getting in the way. I’m proud to partner with Rep. Cline to stop these agencies from overregulating and discouraging entrepreneurship.”

This bill was introduced by U.S. Rep. Ben Cline (R-VA) in the House of Representatives in January 2025 and passed out of the House Judiciary Committee in June 2025.

Representative Ben Cline said, “Small businesses across the Nation are at a disadvantage when complying with overly burdensome federal regulation. Facing insurmountable compliance costs, potential entrepreneurs all too often choose never to open their small businesses in the first place. Thank you, Senator Scott, for joining me in introducing the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act, an important piece of legislation that will help American small businesses cut through the overwhelming weight of federal regulation.”

Key Provisions of the Small Business Regulatory Flexibility Improvements Act:

Broader economic analysis: Requires agencies to assess both direct and reasonably foreseeable indirect economic effects (e.g., compliance costs, revenue impact).

Alternatives and benefits: Agencies must describe alternative rule options that either minimize adverse impacts or maximize benefits to small entities.

Expanded applicability: Applies the RFA to more types of actions, including revisions to land management plans and interpretive rules.

Remove waiver authority: Agencies can no longer skip the Regulatory Flexibility Act’s flexibility analysis; they also need to follow procedures set by SBA’s Chief Counsel.

Transparency & accountability:

Requires publications of detailed analyses, numeric or explain-why-not quantification.

Mandates posting final regulatory flexibility analyses online.

Increases avenues for public comment and judicial review.

title: Rosen Joins Colleagues in Demanding Trump Administration Restore Funding for Energy Projects That Were Illegally Canceled
text:
The Letter Follows An Admission From The Trump Administration That The Decision To Cancel Energy Project Grants In States That Did Not Vote For Trump Was “Based Solely” On Politics

WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) joined Senate colleagues in a letter demanding that U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright and Office of Management and Budget Director Russel Vought restore federal funding for the 223 energy projects they canceled in October 2025. The Trump Administration has since admitted to illegally canceling energy grants because those projects were in states that did not vote for Donald Trump in the 2024 election.

“Now that court documents have confirmed what we knew to be true, we write to demand that you restore previously awarded funding that the Trump administration has weaponized in an attempt to punish perceived political enemies,” the Senators began.

“Once an administration begins punishing Americans for how they vote, the threat extends far beyond these projects: no state, community, business, or worker can trust that the federal government will apply the law fairly,” the Senators continued. “This is not only an attack on jobs, affordable energy, and America’s economic competitiveness. It is an attack on the rule of law and the basic democratic principle that the federal government serves the entire country—not merely those who support the President.”

“At a time when energy prices are skyrocketing, the administration is hell-bent on political retribution instead of working to bring down costs for millions of Americans. The American people deserve to have a government that works for them—not one that is willing to push energy prices even higher and put the country’s energy security at grave risk,” the Senators concluded. “For the good of our country, the rule of law, and the American people, we demand that you change course and restore the previously awarded funding.”

The full letter can be found HERE.

Senator Rosen has fought to ensure that energy projects across Nevada have the resources they need to meet the state’s energy demands. In January, she helped secure more than $49 million in Community Project Funding, which included projects to improve energy efficiency. Last year, Senator Rosen joined the rest of the Nevada delegation in sending a letter to express concerns over stalled solar energy projects in Nevada. She also successfully pushed the Trump Administration to release $3.7 billion in funding to help lower Nevadans’ energy costs.

title: Rosen Joins Senate Colleagues in Introducing And Passing Bipartisan Resolution Designating August 1st As “Gold Star Children’s Day”
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – U.S. Senator Jacky Rosen (D-NV) joined Senate colleagues in celebrating the passage of their bipartisan Senate resolution designating August 1, 2026, as “Gold Star Children’s Day.” This effort recognizes the children of fallen servicemembers for their parents’ sacrifice in service to our nation. In the 20th and 21st centuries, nearly 625,000 American servicemembers have made the ultimate sacrifice and over the past 25 years have been survived by nearly 15,000 children.

“The children who lose a parent in military service to our nation live with a sacrifice they carry for a lifetime,” said Senator Rosen. “I am proud to join colleagues from both sides of the aisle to designate August 1st as Gold Star Children’s Day to honor them and recognize their sacrifice when they lose a parent. I will continue fighting for our servicemembers and their families.”

Senator Rosen has made it one of her priorities to support Gold Star families. She recently co-led a bipartisan bill to increase the death gratuity payment given to families of fallen servicemembers in line with inflation and current prices. Senator Rosen also helped introduce the CHAMPVA Children’s Care Protection Act, which would allow children and surviving dependents of disabled veterans to remain eligible for health care coverage through the VA until they are 26 years old, aligning with the Affordable Care Act. Last Congress, Senator Rosen helped introduce and pass the Love Lives On Act in the Senate, which would have allowed surviving Gold Star spouses to retain their benefits upon remarrying before the age of 55. She is also an original cosponsor of the bill this Congress.

title: NEWS: Sen. Schiff Joins Blumenthal, Warren to Raise Concerns about Trump Admin Directing Billions in Taxpayer Dollars Toward Critical Mining Companies Linked to Trump and Lutnick Families
text:
Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) joined Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ranking Member of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass), Ranking Member of the Senate Banking Committee, in two letters raising concerns about potential conflicts of interest surrounding the Trump Administration’s deals with more than a dozen critical mining companies with ties to President Trump’s family, Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick’s family, or both.

In a letter sent to David A. Lorch, the Director of the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) at the Department of Defense, Schiff, Blumenthal, and Warren sought records and information about a $620 million loan committed to Vulcan Elements, a rare earth magnet company backed by Donald Trump Jr.

Pointing to recent reporting from ProPublica that White House Senior Counselor for Trade and manufacturing Peter Navarro intervened directly in the contracting process for this loan, Schiff, Blumenthal and Warren wrote, “These reports raise grave ethical and public safety concerns and the specter that the Pentagon is corruptly prioritizing funding for critical defense components based on ties to the Trump family. The use of funds from the so-called OBBBA to enrich a Trump family member is a further affront to taxpayers from a law that is estimated to add $5.1 trillion to the federal deficit. The loan to Vulcan Elements represents roughly 13% of all capital committed by the OSC as of January 2026.”

The Senators continued, “The American people must be able to trust that our Department of Defense makes decisions based exclusively on furthering national security interests, not political cronyism. Forcing OSC staff to work late nights to complete a contract designed to benefit the Trump family diverts valuable resources away from other, more effective defense capabilities. Further, staffing Department of Defense offices for the benefit of commercial gain risks American lives and wastes taxpayer funding.”

In a separate letter sent to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, Secretary of Energy Chris Wright, Secretary of Commerce Howard Lutnick, Secretary of the Interior Doug Burgum, and President & Chairman of the Export-Import Bank of the United States John Jovanovic, Blumenthal, Schiff, and Warren demanded answers about the deals and President Trump’s role in effectuating them.

Citing recent reporting from The New York Times, the Senators wrote: “Securing supply chains for critical minerals is vital for America’s national security and economic competitiveness, and has accordingly been a priority for recent administrations of both political parties… In the second Trump Administration, funding for efforts to secure in these supply chains has skyrocketed, with the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) providing nearly $13 billion for direct Defense Production Act grants and approximately $350 billion in available financing for critical minerals and other projects. This has resulted in what has been described as ‘a modern-day gold rush in the critical minerals industry.’”

The Senators continued, “Recent reporting suggests that the result has been a host of deals to benefit the Trump and Lutnick families, including deals involving each of your agencies or departments. The 14 deals identified so far show that the government has provided or is considering providing these companies with at least $8.9 billion taxpayer dollars.”

The full text of the letter addressed to Department of Defense’ Office of Strategic Capital can be found here and below:

Dear Mr. Lorch,

We write seeking information regarding the $620 million loan your office committed to Vulcan Elements, a rare earth magnet company backed by President Trump’s son, Donald Trump Jr. Reporting indicates that White House Senior Counselor for Trade and Manufacturing Peter Navarro intervened directly in the contracting process for this loan. Navarro reportedly personally initiated the contracting process for the loan, notwithstanding his close relationship with Mr. Trump Jr., and White House officials apparently pressured Pentagon staff to expedite the deal, forcing them to work “late nights and with little sleep” to complete the loan.

These reports raise grave ethical and public safety concerns and the specter that the Pentagon is prioritizing funding for critical defense components based on company’s ties to the Trump family. The use of funds from the so-called One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA) to enrich a Trump family member is a further affront to taxpayers from a law that is estimated to add $5.1 trillion to the federal deficit. The loan to Vulcan Elements represents roughly 13% of all capital committed by the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) as of January 2026.6

Vulcan Elements’ financial ties to Donald Trump Jr. and the Trump Administration are well reported. Small Business Administration documents show that as recently as November 2025, Vulcan Elements had only eight employees. In August 2025, Vulcan Elements raised $65 million in funding from several Trump-affiliated venture capital firms, including 1789 Capital, which publicly lists Trump Jr. as a partner. The August 2025 funding round was led by Altimeter Capital, whose CEO, Brad Gerstner, lobbied for the passage of the OBBBA and currently runs a nonprofit dedicated to promoting the “Trump Accounts” savings campaign. These relationships appear to have proved profitable for all parties involved; shortly after receiving the $620 million loan, Vulcan Elements’ valuation skyrocketed, increasing the value of Donald Trump Jr.’s initial investment by as much as 90 percent.

Donald Trump Jr. and Peter Navarro, the senior White House advisor that reportedly intervened on behalf of Vulcan Elements, are also deeply intertwined. Trump Jr. reportedly visited Navarro while Navarro was imprisoned in Miami for refusing to provide testimony related to the January 6th insurrection at the United States Capitol. In a podcast promoting Navarro’s recent book, Trump Jr. has referred to Navarro as “great patriot, great friend, great American.” This appearance seemed to be designed to benefit Navarro financially by increasing book sales. Navarro, in kind, dedicated his recent book to Trump Jr., among others, for having “my back when it was against the wall.”

If, as reported, Navarro intervened on behalf of Vulcan Elements, Navarro may have violated the ethical obligations binding executive branch employees. For example, Subpart E of the Executive Branch Standards of Ethical Conduct instructs executive branch employees to recuse themselves from matters that could create the appearance of impartiality, including matters involving persons with whom they seek a “business, contractual, or other financial relationship.” Given Navarro may have benefitted financially from his relationship with Trump Jr., including through book sales from appearances on Trump Jr.’s podcast, he likely should not have intervened on behalf of a company linked to Trump Jr.

This disturbing reporting is only the latest in a series of concerning events sparking concerns that President Trump is attempting to co-opt the Department of Defense and the Office of Strategic Capital to benefit his friends and family. At least ten companies linked to Trump Jr. and Eric Trump have won Department of Defense contracts or loans, raising significant conflict of interest concerns that ethics experts have said “undermines public confidence.”

In response to a Congressional inquiry in March, the Department of Defense implied its policies for identifying corrupt practices extend only to employees of the Department itself, not to the Trump family. Donald Trump Jr. has also acknowledged playing an outsized role in staffing the Department of Defense, including screening candidates for “top jobs” on behalf of President Trump. Trump Jr. publicly admitted to selecting candidates based on their preference for spending more on drones, all while sitting on the advisory board of a drone company currently negotiating for additional funding with the Office of Strategic Capital.

The American people must be able to trust that our Department of Defense makes decisions based exclusively on furthering national security interests, not political cronyism. Pressuring OSC staff to complete a contract that benefits the Trump family, as reported, diverts valuable resources away from other, more promising defense capabilities.

In addition to the information requests below, please preserve all records and communications related to the Vulcan Elements deal. This applies to internal communications, communications with White House officials, Donald Trump Jr., and Department of Defense officials outside the OSC. This includes but is not limited to: records and communications via email, whether official or personal; mobile devices; encrypted or disappearing messaging applications; social media; calendar entries; meeting notes; and voicemail and text messages. To the extent that you use any auto-delete functions, you should immediately suspend autodelete functions and notify persons with control over potentially relevant records of their preservation obligations.

This preservation request covers both past and current efforts, as well as any planned or in development measures responsive to the issues raised in this letter. In light of these concerns, and pursuant to the Senate’s oversight responsibilities, please provide answers to the following questions by August 28, 2026:

Please preserve any documents or communications between OSC staff and Peter Navarro regarding the Vulcan Elements deal.

Please provide a list of all White House officials, including Peter Navarro, who contacted OSC staff regarding the Vulcan Elements deal.

Please provide the exact terms of the Vulcan Elements agreement.

Please provide a complete list of OSC personnel interviewed or recommended by Donald Trump Jr. during their selection process.

Which, if any, of these individuals were involved in the negotiations between OSC and Vulcan Elements?

Explain the nature of their involvement.

The full text of the letter addressed to U.S. Secretaries Pete Hegseth, Howard Lutnick, Chris Wright, Burgum, and President and Chairman of Export-Import Bank of the United States John Jovanovic can be found here and below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth, Secretary Wright, Secretary Lutnick, Secretary Burgum, and Mr. Jovanoic:

We write today regarding troubling reporting concerning the continued use of government funds to benefit President Trump’s friends and family, including Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick and his family. Recent reporting has detailed that at least 14 companies actively working with the federal government on critical mining deals have ties to companies connected to either Mr. Lutnick’s family, President Trump’s family, or both. This reporting has also detailed President Trump’s personal involvement in securing at least one of these deals. We write to request further details regarding the number of current mining deals involving President Trump’s friends and family, and President Trump’s role in effectuating these deals.

Securing supply chains for critical minerals is vital for America’s national security and economic competitiveness, and has accordingly been a priority for recent administrations of both political parties. These materials are the critical ingredients for electronics, semiconductors, batteries, and green technology. In the second Trump Administration, funding for efforts to secure these supply chains has skyrocketed, with the One Big Beautiful Bill Act providing nearly $13 billion for direct Defense Production Act grants and approximately $350 billion in available financing for critical minerals and other projects. This has resulted in what has been described as “a modern-day gold rush in the critical minerals industry.”

Recent reporting suggests that the result has been a host of deals to benefit the Trump and Lutnick families, including deals involving each of your agencies or departments. The 14 deals identified so far show that the government has provided or is considering providing these companies with at least $8.9 billion taxpayer dollars. In one case, it appears President Trump himself spoke with Kazakhstan’s President to ensure that Kaz Resources, a company connected to his son’s and Mr. Lutnick’s family, would have access to tungsten mines in Kazakhstan. The Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM) and the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) have issued letters of interest for $1.6 billion of federal financing, indicating the willingness of these agencies to consider supporting the project, and the company is seeking an additional $400 million loan from the Department of Defense. This may represent only the tip of the iceberg of the true scale of money flowing to interests connected to the Lutnick and Trump families.

It is especially important that federal investments meant to secure vital national security and economic interests like critical minerals are based on the merits, and that decisions to spend taxpayer dollars to secure these resources are made free of conflicts of interest. The circumstances regarding these deals suggest that those goals might not be at the forefront of the Administration’s considerations regarding these transactions. Please preserve all documents, records, and communications related to critical mining deals connected to companies with connections to the Trump and/or Lutnick families, including but not limited to Cantor Fitzgerald, USA Rare Earth, Kaz Resources, Perpetua Resources, ASP Isotopes, Critical Metals Corporation, Vulcan Elements, the Metals Company, Trilogy Metals, American Ocean Minerals Corporation, Guardian Metal Resources, Titan Mining, Westwater Resources, Reelement/American Resources Corporation, and Energy Fuels Incorporated. Please also provide detailed responses to the following requests by August 13, 2026:

Please identify any critical mining deals entered into or contemplated by your department or agency involving Cantor Fitzgerald or any entity affiliated with the Trump or Lutnick families since January 20, 2025 and, for each deal identified, please describe the contractual nature of that deal;

For each deal identified in response to question 1, please describe the criteria used to select these specific companies, including a description of other companies considered and the reason those companies were not selected;

For each deal identified in response to question 1, please describe any communications with the White House regarding the deal;

For each deal identified in response to question 1, please describe any communications with Cantor Fitzgerald or any entity affiliated with the Trump or Lutnick families regarding the deal; and

For each deal identified in response to question 1, please describe any other White House involvement in the deal, including but not limited to any interactions with foreign governments regarding securing the companies access to critical mineral reserves.

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

###

title: NEWS: Sens. Schiff, Padilla Join Heinrich, Murray & Colleagues in Demanding Trump Administration Restore Funding for Energy Projects That Were Illegally Canceled and Politically Targeted
text:
The letter follows an admission from the Trump administration that the decision to cancel energy project grants in states that did not vote for Trump was “based solely” on politics

Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Senators Adam Schiff and Alex Padilla (both D-Calif.) joined Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Patty Murray (D-Wash.), and 35 of their colleagues in demanding that the Trump administration restore funding for the 223 energy projects canceled in October 2025. The Trump administration has since admitted to illegally canceling energy grants because those projects were in states that did not vote for President Trump in the 2024 election.

In California, this move targeted funding for 79 clean energy projects totaling over $2 billion, including $1.2 billion for the state’s ARCHES hydrogen hub and funding for a backup battery system for a children’s hospital. The administration’s politically charged cancellations will lead to higher energy bills for Californians.

In December, the Department of Energy’s Office of Inspector General agreed to launch an investigation into the cancellations after Schiff, Padilla, Lofgren, and colleagues requested they look into improper partisan conduct.

“Now that court documents have confirmed what we knew to be true, we write to demand that you restore previously awarded funding that the Trump administration has weaponized in an attempt to punish perceived political enemies,” the Senators wrote in a letter to U.S. Department of Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Office of Management and Budget Director Russell Vought.

“Once an administration begins punishing Americans for how they vote, the threat extends far beyond these projects: no state, community, business, or worker can trust that the federal government will apply the law fairly,” the Senators continued. “This is not only an attack on jobs, affordable energy, and America’s economic competitiveness. It is an attack on the rule of law and the basic democratic principle that the federal government serves the entire country—not merely those who support the President.”

“At a time when energy prices are skyrocketing, the administration is hell-bent on political retribution instead of working to bring down costs for millions of Americans. The American people deserve to have a government that works for them—not one that is willing to push energy prices even higher and put the country’s energy security at grave risk,” the Senators concluded. “For the good of our country, the rule of law, and the American people, we demand that you change course and restore the previously awarded funding.”

In addition to Schiff, Padilla, Heinrich, and Murray, the letter was signed by U.S. Senators Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Richard Durbin (D-Ill.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawai‘i), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Mazie K. Hirono (D- Hawai’i), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Michael Bennett (D-Colo.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), and Angus King (I-Maine).

Background: Last year,Senators Schiff and Padilla and 28 members of the California congressional delegation urged the Department of Energy’s Inspector General to launch an independent investigation into the unlawful termination of $7.6 billion in grants to California and other states targeted for their perceived lack of support for President Trump.

Schiff and Padilla also previously joined Heinrich and Murray’s effort to demand the Trump administration restore funding for 223 energy projects in Democrat-led states that were unlawfully canceled.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below:

Secretary Wright and Director Vought:

Now that court documents have confirmed what we knew to be true, we write to demand that you restore previously awarded funding that the Trump Administration has weaponized in an attempt to punish perceived political enemies.

In October 2025, we wrote to you to express strong opposition to the Administration’s callous decision to unlawfully terminate $8 billion in federal investments for 223 energy projects. You not only acted outside the bounds of the law, but canceled projects that would have provided jobs, onshored manufacturing, and lowered skyrocketing energy prices. Congress authorized those projects and appropriated funding under the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act, the Inflation Reduction Act, and annual appropriation bills. At the time of the termination of those projects, we expressed outrage that the terminations appeared politically motivated and confined to states that then-Vice President Kamala Harris carried in the 2024 presidential election. The Administration has now admitted in federal court what it denied to Congress and the American people.

On July 24, 2026, citing court filings, The New York Times reported that the Trump Administration acknowledged that it terminated more than $7.5 billion of grants due to political motivations. In a two-step process, the Department of Energy (DOE) first recommended more than 600 grants for potential termination, including grants in states represented by both Republicans and Democrats. It appears the Office of Management and Budget then selected all the grants in “Blue States” for cancellation, which DOE executed. In court filings, DOE’s lawyers conceded that the cancellations occurred “based solely on the political identity of the grant recipient’s state.” Specifically, as the court filings stated, “[w]ith one exception, the 284 terminated grants had a recipient location and/or at least one place of performance in a state that awarded its electoral votes to Kamala Harris in the 2024 election and has two Democratic-caucusing Senators (“Blue State” grants).” Similar grants in Red States, however, remained intact and were not the subject of termination. What’s more, DOE lawyers conceded that the decision to terminate these blue state grants was not “based on any programmatic, statutory, cost-reduction, or performance-based factor.”

Once an Administration begins punishing Americans for how they vote, the threat extends far beyond these projects: no state, community, business, or worker can trust that the federal government will apply the law fairly. This is not only an attack on jobs, affordable energy, and America’s economic competitiveness. It is an attack on the rule of law and the basic democratic principle that the federal government serves the entire country—not merely those who support the President.

At a time when energy prices are skyrocketing, the Administration is hell-bent on political retribution instead of working to bring down costs for millions of Americans. The American people deserve to have a government that works for them—not one that is willing to push energy prices even higher and put the country’s energy security at grave risk.

For the good of our country, the rule of law, and the American people, we demand that you change course and restore the previously awarded funding.

###

title: WATCH: Sen. Schiff Breaks Down Troubled Todd Blanche Nomination, Slams Trump’s Self-Dealings on MS NOW and CNN
text:
Washington, D.C. – Last night, U.S. Senator Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) joined CNN’s OutFront with Erin Burnett and MS NOW’s All In with Chris Hayes to discuss President Trump threatening to withdraw Todd Blanche’s nomination for Attorney General over Trump’s tax immunity deal and proposed billion-dollar slush fund.

In his confirmation hearing in front of the Senate Judiciary Committee, Schiff condemned Blanche’s role in approving the President’s proposed slush fund and compromising his integrity for the president.

During the interviews, Schiff also slammed Trump Media’s new initiative to sell early access to Trump’s Truth Social posts, emphasizing the president’s focus on himself over the well-being of the American people.

View the full interviews here and here.

Key Excerpts on CNN’s OutFront with Erin Burnett:

On Trump threatening to pull Blanche’s nomination:

[…] The Senators are only asking that Blanche live up to what he testified under oath — that the fund is truly dead, this slush fund for insurrectionists and cop beaters. And that this self-dealing IRS settlement will only apply to Trump, his two kids, and the Trump Organization – those were the litigants in this supposed litigation. They are asking for so little, and the fact that the president is willing to walk away from his own attorney general, willing to have the country not have an attorney general, unless he gets the full benefit of this corrupt bargain, is striking for the reason you mentioned. And that is, the American people have nothing to do with it. He could [not] care less what that might mean to the public. It is always, always about Donald Trump and never about anything else.

On Republicans’ possibility of backing down from Blanche’s nomination, the IRS tax settlement and slush fund:

[…] He is so greedy a president. He wants not just himself, his organization, his two kids. He wants all of their subsidiaries, all of their companies. It could be dozens of corporate entities. He doesn’t want the IRS looking into any of them. And what’s more, they’re not even insisting, Cornyn and Tillis, are not even insisting that the Justice Department not pay insurrectionists. They’re getting paid anyway. The president’s cronies are getting paid anyway.

Michael Flynn got paid by the Justice Department anyway. There are these private settlements going on anyway. They just wouldn’t have this massive fund to do it. Now, obviously, I think they should be asking for a lot more to earn their votes, like an end to this corrupt IRS settlement, an end to any use of DOJ funds for cop beaters, but that is not what they’re asking for.

On Trump’s latest self-enrichment scheme:

[…] Here’s a president who made $2.2 or $2.3 billion dollars in his first year as president, and it’s still not enough. He wants even more. And whether it’s this sham of a tax deal that gives him hundreds of millions of dollars more, or whether it’s this new fiasco where they’re going to sell off early access to his Truth Social posts so that his donors or investors in his private business get a leg up on ordinary Americans who might be investing in the market – it’s just one scam after another. But the central core is they all benefit the president financially.

Key Excerpts on MS NOW’s All In with Chris Hayes:

On Republicans holding out Blanche’s nomination:

[…] Cornyn is asking for so little, and the fact that it’s still not enough for Donald Trump is just striking. He will go without an attorney general if he must, but he’s not going to give up an inch of this self-enrichment scheme of his. But the other thing that struck me about what he said also is just how extraordinary it is that they can’t get the Justice Department, the attorney general, or the administration to live up to what they’re promising under oath. I mean, it really does take your breath away when you think about just how modest a requirement or request that is.

[…] I think it’s less vindictiveness on the part of these two senators. I think it’s more freedom, frankly. They don’t have to face the electorate again. They don’t have to worry about another tough primary. They feel liberated to not only speak their mind but liberated to do the right thing when they have so often felt it necessary to carry some really dirty White House water. So, I think it is being liberated. It also may be a little bit of cover for other Republicans that can’t take that position, that wish they could. But at the end of the day, what it all comes back to on the other side of this is a president who really doesn’t give a rat’s ass about the Justice Department, the American people, fighting crime or anything the AG is supposed to do. It is always about Donald Trump and what’s best for him.

On Trump’s all-time low approval rating:

[…] I think those poll numbers reflect the fact that corruption is a powerful issue when it is in combination with the fact that the president isn’t focused on the problems of the American people. And why isn’t he focused on it? Because his only care is making money for himself. The combination of greed, incompetence, broken promises – that’s not a prescription for high poll numbers. And I think we’re seeing that reflected.

title: Schmitt Leads Missouri Lawmakers in Letter Supporting Governor’s Disaster Declaration Request Following Devastating Floods
text:
U.S. SENATE — Today, U.S. Senator Eric Schmitt (R-MO) led Missouri lawmakers in sending a letter to President Trump supporting Governor Mike Kehoe’s disaster declaration request following the widespread flooding that devastated communities across southern Missouri from July 9 to July 11, 2026.

“We write in strong support of Missouri Governor Mike Kehoe’s July 28, 2026, request for a major disaster declaration following the devastating storms that took place in Missouri from July 9th through July 11th of this year,” the lawmakers began.

“Beginning late on July 9th, a series of slow-moving thunderstorms produced torrential rainfall in some areas across south-central and southeastern Missouri, equivalent to a 1-in-1,000-year event according to the National Weather Service… Floodwaters overwhelmed campgrounds and farms, washed out critical access routes, and forced emergency crews to evacuate families and children. Once again, Missouri’s first responders more than answered the call of duty. In dark and dangerous conditions, these heroes worked around the clock to evacuate residents and visitors…” the lawmakers continued.

“As you are aware, Missouri has repeatedly been faced with natural disasters in recent years. In 2025 alone, Missouri received five federally declared disasters—the most of any state—and in 2026, this trend has not changed. Today, Missouri is requesting its third disaster declaration of the year, already holding a declaration for storms that occurred from April 23rd through April 28th. To make matters worse, many communities affected by the July storms were still recovering from these previous disasters, compounding losses and stretching local capacity further beyond its limits… As such, we respectfully urge you to direct your administration to promptly review Governor Kehoe’s major disaster declaration request for the July 9 through July 11 storms and submit it for your approval,” the lawmakers concluded.

Senator Josh Hawley (R-MO), Congressman Jason Smith (MO-08), and Congresswoman Ann Wagner (MO-2) joined Senator Schmitt in sending the letter.

Read the full letter HERE.

title: Schmitt Statement on Big Ten and SEC Endorsing Bipartisan College Sports Deal

title: Sens. Scott, Wicker, colleagues honor Gold Star Children’s Day
text:
WASHINGTON — U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) joined Sens. Roger Wicker (R-Miss.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), and numerous colleagues in celebrating the passage of a Senate resolution designating Aug. 1, 2026, as Gold Star Children’s Day, which recognizes the children of fallen service members.

“Gold Star children bear the unimaginable weight of losing their father or mother in service to our nation. They suffer a loss so few can comprehend, but their bravery and strength should give us all hope and fill our hearts with gratitude,” said Sen. Scott. “With this resolution, we honor all of the children who have lost so much for our freedoms. We will never forget our brave men and women in uniform, and we will never forget the sacrifices made by their children.”

“The sons and daughters of our fallen service members carry on the legacies of their parents. We set aside this day to honor them and to remember the sacrifices of their mothers and fathers,” said Sen. Wicker.

“Gold Star children grow up carrying the weight of losing of a parent who made the ultimate sacrifice in service to our country,” said Sen. Kelly. “These kids deserve to know that their parents’ service will never be forgotten and that this country will always stand behind them.”

America’s Gold Star tradition began in World War I. When a service member deployed, his or her family would often hang a banner bearing a blue star outside the home. If the loved one died in the line of duty, the family replaced the blue star with a gold one. These families came to be known as Gold Star Families. In the wars of the 20th and 21st centuries, nearly 625,000 Americans have made the ultimate sacrifice and have been survived by nearly 15,000 children. Senators recognize August 1 specifically to honor these Gold Star Children.

U.S. Sens. Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Susan Collins (R-Maine), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Ted Cruz (R-Texas), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), John Fetterman (D-Pa.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), John Hoeven (R-N.D.), Jim Justice (R-W.Va.), Tim Kaine (D-Va.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), James Lankford (R-Okla.), Roger Marshall (R-Kan.), Ashley Moody (R-Fla.), John Ossoff (D-Ga.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Mike Rounds (R-S.D.), Rick Scott (R-Fla.), Tommy Tuberville (R-Ala.), and Raphael Warnock (D-Ga.) joined in introducing the resolution.
