title: Shaheen Tours Derry – Londonderry I-93 Exit 4A Project, Leads Discussion with New Hampshire Aerospace Leaders in Merrimack, Delivers Remarks to Honor Korean War Veterans in Boscawen
text:
(Boscawen, NH) – Today, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) visited the site of the Derry – Londonderry I-93 Exit 4A project to tour the site and received a briefing on the status of the project. Prior to her visit to the Exit 4A site, Shaheen began the day by leading a roundtable with Granite State aerospace business leaders in the wake of her Congressional delegation to the Farnborough Air Show in the United Kingdom. She closed the day at the New Hampshire State Veterans Cemetery in Boscawen, where she delivered remarks to honor Korean War veterans.

Photos from today’s events can be found HERE.

In Derry, Shaheen visited the site of the Derry – Londonderry I-93 Exit 4A project, where she toured the active construction site and was given an update on the projected timeline for completion of the project by officials from the New Hampshire Department of Transportation. The I-93 Exit 4A project is a longtime priority for the Derry and Londonderry communities, and once completed, it will improve traffic safety while unlocking access to underdeveloped lands and easing traffic in both communities. The I-93 4A Exit project was funded in part by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which Shaheen helped negotiate and pass in Congress.

“The Derry – Londonderry I-93 Exit 4A project will reduce traffic congestion, promote downtown Derry and Londonderry and improve safety in each community and for travelers across the state,” said Senator Shaheen. “Touring the active Exit 4A site today underscored the importance of continued federal investments in our state’s road infrastructure to boost tourism and spur economic development. I was proud to see the progress made since my last visit to the site and will continue to support this critical project.”

As a key negotiator of the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, Shaheen helped secure a $550 billion investment in our nation’s infrastructure, including more than $1.1 billion for roads, bridges, roadway safety and major projects in New Hampshire. In 2024, Shaheen was joined by then-Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg in a visit to the Exit 4A site to highlight the impact in New Hampshire of federal investments in the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law.

Earlier in the day, Shaheen led a roundtable in Nashua on the heels of the 2026 Farnborough Air Show, the largest biennial trade-show in the world. At the roundtable, Shaheen led a discussion on pathways to unlock new markets for New Hampshire businesses, the state’s status in the global aerospace market and the critical role the Air Show played in connecting Granite State businesses with industry leaders across the globe.

“New Hampshire’s robust aerospace industry remains on the cutting-edge of innovation, building and manufacturing products that spur technological innovation and keep our nation safe,” said Senator Shaheen. “Following record turnout at Farnborough earlier this month, it was great to convene industry leaders from across the state for an insightful conversation recapping this year’s Air Show and discussing the bright future that lies ahead for one of our state’s most valuable industries.”

Just recently, Shaheen led her final bipartisan Congressional delegation to the Farnborough Air Show with the goal of representing New Hampshire’s aerospace sector on the international stage. Aerospace serves as New Hampshire’s top export sector, supporting 24,000 jobs and representing $1.7 billion in exports in 2025 alone. The New Hampshire Department of Business and Economic Affairs, alongside New Hampshire’s Aerospace and Defense Consortium (NHADC), directly connects Granite State talent with the state’s $12.5 billion aerospace, space and defense sector. NHADC featured New Hampshire exhibitors at the Air Show this year through the State Trade Expansion Program (STEP), which provides export assistance to small businesses. Senator Shaheen created the STEP program in 2010 and continues to lead action in support of STEP in Congress.

To close the day, Shaheen attended and delivered remarks at the New Hampshire State Veterans Cemetery to honor New Hampshire veterans of the Korean War and thank them for their service and sacrifice. Hosted by the Korean American Society of New Hampshire following National Korean War Veterans Armistice Day earlier this week, the event was also attended by Governor Kelly Ayotte, Sun Woo Park, President of the Korean American Society of New Hampshire, Jeongyeol Kwak, Deputy Consulate General of the Republic of Korea in Boston and Maj. Gen. David J. Mikolaities, Adjutant General of the New Hampshire National Guard.

“The courage, service and sacrifice of American soldiers in Korea helped preserve freedom for millions and was a proud chapter in the history of our country’s military,” said Senator Shaheen. “Our brave service members who fought in Korea must never be forgotten, and I was honored to join the Korean American Society of New Hampshire to express our gratitude to the veterans of the Korean War for their valor and unyielding commitment to our nation.”

Throughout her time in public office, Senator Shaheen has remained a staunch advocate for our nation’s veterans and for the families of those service members who remain unaccounted for from American conflicts overseas. For years, Shaheen has led the bipartisan Bring Our Heroes Home Act, legislation that would eliminate obstacles preventing families from accessing records needed to learn more about the fates of service members and civilian personnel who went missing. Earlier this year, Shaheen helped secure a provision in the annual Fiscal Year (FY) 2027 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA) based on her Bring Our Heroes Home Act.

title: Sens. Smith, Moran Introduce Bipartisan Legislation to Strengthen Rural Hospitals
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Tina Smith (D-MN) Jerry Moran (R-KS) this week introduced the Rural Emergency Hospital Designation Improvement Act (REH 2.0), bipartisan legislation to expand access to federal resources for rural hospitals through the Rural Emergency Hospital (REH) Medicare designation. This legislation would allow more Critical Access Hospitals (CAH) and rural hospitals at risk of closure to sustain health care services in rural communities, and it would make technical improvements to the designation. The legislation is cosponsored by Sens. Tommy Tuberville (R-AL), Katie Britt (R-AL), Shelley Moore Capito (R-WV), Cindy Hyde-Smith (R-MS) and Roger Marshall, M.D., (R-KS).

“Rural hospitals are vital for families in small towns and rural communities. These hospitals not only provide care close to home, they’re also economic engines for their region,” said Sen. Smith. “But many rural hospitals face increasingly dire financial strain and workforce shortages, forcing them to cut services or even close down altogether. This important legislation is just one tool in the toolbox to help rural hospitals on the verge of closure keep their doors open. Make no mistake, much more is needed to ensure the health and wellness of rural hospitals and families.

“I have visited every hospital in Kansas numerous times, and these conversations help guide my efforts to make certain health care providers across our state have the support they need to provide critical services to patients in their communities,” said Sen. Moran. “During these visits, providers shared with me their recommendations for strengthening the Rural Emergency Hospital designation so it can better support the struggling facilities it was originally intended to serve. The legislation I am introducing with Senator Tina Smith is the direct result of what we have heard from rural hospitals and health care providers in our states, and it makes needed improvements to the program to help make certain patients can continue to access critical health care services in their communities for years to come.”

The REH Designation Improvement Act is also supported by the National Rural Health Association.

The provisions in the REH Designation Improvement Act are the result of numerous conversations Sens. Smith and Moran held with rural health care providers and CEOs of hospitals that are eligible for the REH designation. REH is a Medicare provider designation that offers certain rural hospitals the opportunity to convert and continue operating with limited services rather than closing.

The Rural Emergency Hospital Designation Improvement Act would:

Allow previously closed rural hospitals to re-open and apply for the Rural Emergency Hospital designation if they can demonstrate they met all eligibility requirements between Jan. 1, 2015, and Dec. 27, 2020.

Direct the Secretary of Health and Human Services (HHS) to create a waiver program for facilities operating similarly to an REH in order to convert to an REH.

Allow REH facilities to maintain or create a unit for inpatient psychiatric care, obstetric care and allow for limited inpatient rehabilitation services.

Require the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services to provide additional funding for laboratory services.

Clarify that REH facilities are eligible for Small Rural Hospital Improvement grants.

Direct the Secretary of HHS to allow an REH to be eligible as a National Health Service Corp site.

Authorize REH facilities to transfer patients from acute care to a Skilled Nursing Facility without leaving the hospital, in accordance with the Social Security Act.

Allow an REH facility to revert back to a Critical Access Hospital (CAH) to regain necessary provider status, only if the facility was designated a necessary provider prior to converting to REH.

Clarify state Medicaid agencies can pay REH facilities as hospitals.

Full text of the legislation can be found HERE.

title: Sullivan, Scott, Tuberville Introduce Bill to Create Secretary of the Coast Guard Position
text:
WASHINGTON—U.S. Senators Dan Sullivan (R-Alaska), Rick Scott (R-Fla.), and Tommy Tuberville (R-Ala.) have introduced the Coast Guard Leadership Modernization Act, legislation that would create a Secretary of the U.S. Coast Guard, mirroring a position across all other branches of the U.S Armed Forces. Currently, the Coast Guard lacks a dedicated civilian leadership position, and it defaults to the U.S. Secretary of Homeland Security.

“I’m glad to join my colleagues in introducing legislation to provide even greater support and advocacy to our Coast Guard with a dedicated civilian Secretary who can represent the needs and perspective of the Coast Guard at the highest levels of our federal government,” said Sen. Sullivan. “We rely on our brave Coast Guardsmen to monitor and defend vast maritime borders, execute life-saving search-and-rescue operations, respond to international crises, and support Department of War missions. No state is more aware of the important service of the Coast Guard than Alaska—home to more coastline than the Lower 48 states combined—which is why I spearheaded the largest investment in the Coast Guard in history in last year’s Working Families Tax Cuts Act.”

“The Coast Guard has a unique and highly specialized mission to protect our country from threats posed by smugglers, drug traffickers, terrorists, and other lawbreakers, and it deserves a service secretary to oversee and coordinate its operations, just like every other branch of the military,” said Sen. Scott. “This bill creates a Secretary of the Coast Guard in federal law to ensure the Service has the leadership it needs to take on the challenges of the 21st century and beyond. This is a matter of readiness and national security; Congress should pass this immediately so President Trump can make his nomination, and the Senate can get to work on confirmation.”

“The men and women of the U.S. Coast Guard are critical to our national defense and security, which is why they deserve the same strategic organization as other branches of our military,” said Sen. Tuberville. “Having a permanent Coast Guard Secretary will make the organization even more effective and enhance our national security. I’m proud to join this legislation with Sen. Rick Scott to give President Trump full authority to nominate a Secretary of the Coast Guard and further his mission of Peace Through Strength.”

Currently, all branches of the U.S. Armed Forces have a dedicated Secretary overseeing operations and representing the branch. However, the Coast Guard lacks a civilian executive leader, in an organization responsible for protecting 95,000 miles of coastline and 3.4 million square nautical miles of the U.S. exclusive economic zone.

This legislation creates, in statute, a Secretary of the Coast Guard to run as the leader of the branch. Upon this bill becoming law, the President would have the authority to nominate a Secretary of the Coast Guard subject to Senate confirmation.

Full text of the bill can be found HERE.

BACKGROUND:

Sen. Sullivan has consistently championed support for and robust investments in the Coast Guard to include the homeporting of four icebreakers in Alaska – specifically, three Arctic Security Cutters and the Cutter Storis.

Sen. Sullivan worked to pass the budget reconciliation bill that was signed into law in 2025. Because of Sen. Sullivan’s strong advocacy in the negotiations, the Working Families Tax Cuts Act made the largest investment in the U.S. Coast Guard in history—$25 billion for Fiscal Year 2026, including:

16 new icebreakers—three Polar Security Cutters (heavy icebreakers), three Arctic Security Cutters (medium polar icebreakers), and 10 light and medium icebreaking cutters;

22 new cutters—nine Offshore Patrol Cutters, 10 Fast Response Cutters, and three Waterways Commerce Cutters;

More than 40 new helicopters, six new C-130J aircraft, three new river cutters, and new maritime surveillance equipment (Many of these new Coast Guard aviation and ship assets will be coming to Alaska);

$300 million for the homeporting of theJuneau icebreaker, the Storis; and

$4.379 billion to repair docks, hangars, and shore facilities and replace aging infrastructure, funds that will help address the Coast Guard’s nationwide infrastructure backlog, as found in communities like Sitka, Seward, Kodiak and St. Paul.

title: Tillis, Colleagues Introduce Bipartisan Provider Reimbursement Stability Act to Ensure Long-Term Access to Medical Care
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – This week, U.S. Senators Thom Tillis (R-NC), John Boozman (R-AR), Peter Welch (D-VT), Roger Marshall M.D. (R-KS), Angus King (I-ME), and Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) introduced the Provider Reimbursement Stability Act to modernize Medicare’s Physician Fee Schedule (MFPS). The bipartisan, comprehensive legislation would create greater predictability in Medicare physician payments, preserve patient access to care and better reflect the actual cost of delivering medical services.

According to the American Medical Association (AMA), when adjusted for inflation, Medicare reimbursement for physician services has declined 33 percent since 2001. This reduction, attributed to the Medicare budget neutrality threshold last updated in 1992 and other factors, has failed to keep pace with the rising cost of care. The legislation reforms key structural components of the MPFS, helping preserve physicians’ ability to care for Medicare patients.

“More than two million Medicare beneficiaries in North Carolina depend on timely access to quality care,” said Senator Tillis. “Year after year, Medicare reimbursement cuts have made it harder for physicians to care for patients. This bipartisan legislation makes long overdue reforms to outdated policies to ensure physicians are fairly reimbursed and seniors continue to have access to the care they deserve.”

“Providers should not face unpredictable payment cuts that make it more difficult to care for patients. Modernizing Medicare reimbursement is an important step toward ensuring long-term financial stability for our health care providers and preserving access to quality care. Our bill is a bipartisan solution that will more accurately reflect the costs of delivering quality care, which ultimately benefits patients in Arkansas and across our country,” said Senator Boozman.

“Outdated policies are creating instability for doctors and threatening access to care for Medicare patients in Vermont and across the country. Our commonsense, bipartisan bill will help ensure physicians can continue providing vital care to our communities,” said Senator Welch.

“For 25 years, I cared for patients in western Kansas. Like many, I didn’t go into medicine to worry about Washington’s payment formulas – I went into medicine to take care of people,” said Senator Marshall. “When doctors can’t make the numbers work, patients lose access to care. This legislation is a commonsense step toward stabilizing physician reimbursement so doctors can spend more time caring for patients and less time worrying about whether they can afford to stay in practice.”

“Accessible, reliable health care is essential for seniors across Maine, particularly in our rural communities where providers are already stretched thin,” said Senator King. “The Provider Reimbursement Stability Act would help ensure that Medicare providers are fairly reimbursed so they can continue delivering the full range of care that Maine seniors depend on for their healthcare needs. I’m proud to join my colleagues in supporting this commonsense bipartisan legislation to strengthen access to quality care for older Americans.”

“It’s critical we do all we can to ensure that Granite Staters who rely on Medicare for health insurance have access to the quality, affordable care they need,” said Senator Shaheen. “This bipartisan bill would make sure physicians are fairly compensated and guarantee adequate reimbursement for providers, which would help strengthen Medicare’s dependability for patients now and into the future.”

BACKGROUND

The Provider Reimbursement Stability Act would:

Increase the budget neutrality threshold from $20 million to $57.64 million and index it to the Medicare Economic Index (MEI) every five years, to address rising practice costs.

Revise spending estimates and budget neutrality adjustments based on utilization rates derived from claims data.

Provide updates to direct costs used to calculate practice expense relative value units (RVUs), including clinical wage rates, medical supplies and equipment, not less often than every five years.

Limit year-to-year positive or negative variances in the conversion factor to no greater than 2.5 percent.

###

title: Tuberville Discusses Plans to Protect Seniors from AI Scams
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Tommy Tuberville (R-AL) spoke with Matthew Ferraro, partner at Crowell & Moring, and Paul Benda, Executive Vice President for Risk, Fraud, and Cyber Security at the American Bankers Association, and Deborah Del Mastro, a victim of an Artificial Intelligence (AI) enabled scam, during a Senate Special Committee on Aging hearing. Sen. Tuberville emphasized the importance of AI education to prevent from potential online scams.

Excerpts from Sen. Tuberville’s remarks can be found below or viewed on YouTube or Rumble.

TUBERVILLE: “Thank you, Mr. Chairman. We got a mess. We know it. You know, technology—it brings us more and more every day. We’ve heard the problems. My solution is education.

At a young age, Baby Boomers are in trouble because we’re all gonna get scammed one way or another. And not just domestically, but internationally, I mean, it’s big time. I hear a lot of problems with that. So, Mr. Ferraro, how do we fix this? We got the problem. Give us a solution. I’m gonna ask everybody this. So, get your solution ready.”

FERRARO: “Senator, there is no silver bullet as Mr. Winters said, but I do think that education is very powerful. And if you’re looking for an example, I would point the committee to the example of Finland, which has been very aggressive in teaching both young and old. This is in my written testimony about both this information more broadly, but synthetic media, particularly. And they’ve found that it works that you can actually instruct people to be on the lookout for false media. As Mr. Benda said, pause before you send any money, double check, do all the things that we should do before we make any rash decisions.

And I do think education is quite important. As I said, I think from a government perspective, interagency cooperation is key here. This is an area where there isn’t now a quarterback to use a metaphor in the government on these issues. And I think that is something that the committee might want to consider, and I know that there are some bills pending for the committee on those issues.

And third, as I mentioned in my testimony, I think the technology piece is important as well. I mean, just draw the analysis or the analogy rather to email spam. You receive thousands of pieces of spam every day. You just don’t happen to see them because they’re filtered out by spam filters. One could imagine a situation where similar technology operates in the background on your browser or on your phone to either tag or remove AI generated media.

And that the technology largely exists now, it’s just a matter of integrating it. So, I’ll offer those.”

TUBERVILLE: “Well, if you do anything in life, you know, the big thing is when you get a manual, you get ethics with it first and the same thing with AI. We have to teach our kids ethics. Again, a lot of us are lost and gone. But our young kids can learn it. Mr. Benda, you have worked for DHS and DOW—give us your solution.”

BENDA: “I assume so. I think you’re right. Education is a key pillar. I think you start out young. I think having a national campaign on how to fight AI deep fakes, how to fight scams and fraud is important.

ABA runs financial literacy programs for children. Integrating the AI threat into that and scam threat into that is something that we’re looking at doing. I think the national campaign could address people of all ages. And I have hope for boomers, sir. I have some boomers that I love, my mother-in-law, in one particular.

And I think the focus needs to be on also a safe banking for seniors. So how do we get the message to them in channels that they respect and they use? Whether it’s directly from a banker or from people they trust. And the other piece I would point to is we have to enable and stop the tech companies from allowing the impersonation that happens out there. You should be able to trust what’s on your caller ID.

If you put a name and number on there, telecom should be held accountable if it’s not the right person calling. The social media platforms need to stop the impersonation scams that are out there. They shouldn’t be allowed to post the videos that the good doctor talked about. So those types of things I think need more controls and I think there’s some legislative solutions that are out there.”

TUBERVILLE: “Mrs. Del Mastro, I feel your pain. My mother-in-law got scammed. And this is internationally. She got a call from my granddaughter. She was in Europe.

Please send ten thousand dollars. I need it bad. I’m broke. I gotta get out of this situation.

She sent it. She sent it. She wasn’t in trouble other than the fact she just needed the money. It sounded just like her. What kind of legislation do you think we need to do for something like this?

Have you talked to anybody? Since your debacle?”

DEL MASTRO: “I have not spoken to any legislators until right now. I have spoken to a few experts in the field though, and I believe that, I mean, there are plenty of courses and education out there at how to use AI. And that is something you see on social media all the time, those ads, you know, how learn how take this class, learn how to use it. There’s nothing out there on how to protect yourself from AI. There’s nothing out there.

So that needs to happen. We need to know how to recognize it. And how to protect ourselves from it. Besides having a safe word, not answering the phone, you know, all the things that everybody immediately goes to. There’s got to be an awareness for senior citizens certainly.

You know, all of us don’t know how, you know, hand the remote to the kids to, you know, to change things. I mean, we need to be aware. If I had been aware that my daughter’s voice could possibly be an AI clone, I would have responded differently, but I did not know. So, I think education is key and awareness is key.”

TUBERVILLE: “Just think about we’re just now beginning AI. Just think how much more they’re gonna be able to fool people, and it’s gonna get worse and worse. Thank you very much. Thank you, Mr. Chairman.”

Senator Tommy Tuberville represents Alabama in the United States Senate and is a member of the Senate Armed Services, Agriculture, Veterans’ Affairs, HELP and Aging Committees.

title: Welch Joins 38 Colleagues in Demanding Trump Admin Restore Funding for Energy Projects That Were Illegally Canceled and Politically Targeted
text:
The letter follows an admission from the Trump Admin that the decision to cancel energy project grants in states that did not vote for Trump was “based solely” on politics

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Peter Welch (D-Vt.), Ranking Member of the Senate Agriculture Subcommittee on Rural Development, Energy, and Credit, joined U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, U.S. Senator Patty Murray (D-Wash.), Vice Chair of the U.S. Senate Appropriations Committee, and 36 Senate colleagues in sending a letter to U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Secretary Chris Wright and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Director Russell Vought demanding that the Trump Administration restore funding for the 223 energy projects canceled in October 2025. All Senators who cosigned this letter are from states with canceled grants and funding signed the letter.

The letter comes after the Trump Administration admitted to illegally canceling energy grants because those projects were in states that did not vote for President Trump in the 2024 election.

“Now that court documents have confirmed what we knew to be true, we write to demand that you restore previously awarded funding that the Trump administration has weaponized in an attempt to punish perceived political enemies,” the Senators wrote.

“Once an administration begins punishing Americans for how they vote, the threat extends far beyond these projects: no state, community, business, or worker can trust that the federal government will apply the law fairly,” the Senators continued. “This is not only an attack on jobs, affordable energy, and America’s economic competitiveness. It is an attack on the rule of law and the basic democratic principle that the federal government serves the entire country—not merely those who support the President.”

“At a time when energy prices are skyrocketing, the administration is hell-bent on political retribution instead of working to bring down costs for millions of Americans. The American people deserve to have a government that works for them—not one that is willing to push energy prices even higher and put the country’s energy security at grave risk,” the Senators concluded. “For the good of our country, the rule of law, and the American people, we demand that you change course and restore the previously awarded funding.”

Alongside Senators Welch, Heinrich, and Murray, the letter was signed by U.S. Senate Democratic Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) and U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Ben Ray Luján (D-N.M.), Tammy Duckworth (D-Ill.), Alex Padilla (D-Calif.), John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.), Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.), Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Ron Wyden (D-Ore.), Dick Durbin (D-Ill.), Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.), Brian Schatz (D-Hawaii), Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), Mazie Hirono (D- Hawaii), Lisa Blunt Rochester (D-Del.), Ed Markey (D-Mass.), Chris Coons (D-Del.), Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.), Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Jeanne Shaheen (D-N.H.), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.), Jeff Merkley (D-Ore.), Mark Kelly (D-Ariz.), Michael Bennet (D-Colo.), Tina Smith (D-Minn.), Amy Klobuchar (D-Minn.), Angela Alsobrooks (D-Md.), Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), Andy Kim (D-N.J.), Chris Murphy (D-Conn.), Maggie Hassan (D-N.H.), Cory Booker (D-N.J.), Jack Reed (D-R.I.), and Angus King (I-Maine).

Read and download the Senators’ full letter to DOE Secretary Wright and OMB Director Vought.

title: RI Delegation Joins Seniors on Anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid, Discuss their Fight to Lower Health Care Costs
text:
Coventry, R.I. – Today, U.S. Senators Sheldon Whitehouse (D-RI), Jack Reed (D-RI), along with U.S. Representative Seth Magaziner (RI-02), joined seniors and Neighborhood Health CEO Peter Marino at the Coventry Resource and Senior Center to mark the 61st anniversary of Medicare and Medicaid, provide an update on health care policy in Washington, and reaffirm their commitment to lowering health care costs for Rhode Islanders.

The event comes as Rhode Islanders continue to face rising health care costs following deep cuts enacted by President Trump and Congressional Republicans, including a nearly $1 trillion cut to Medicaid and the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits that helped make coverage more affordable.

View or download photos from the event here.

“For 61 years, Medicare and Medicaid have helped Rhode Islanders access affordable, lifesaving health care,” said Whitehouse. “Republican chaos and corruption are driving up Americans’ costs, and the party’s bizarre obsession with ripping away health care has destabilized our already-fragile health care system. It’s a disgrace, and I remain committed to protecting Medicare and Medicaid from Republican mischief.”

“Medicare and Medicaid are cost-effective and critical to the health and well-being of thousands of Rhode Islanders and millions of Americans. These programs have helped lift millions of Americans out of poverty, improved their health, and advanced health care innovations that benefit everyone. The historic success of Medicare is self-evident: Before Medicare was enacted, roughly half of all seniors had health insurance. Today, 99 percent of American seniors — adults aged 65 and older — have health insurance,” said Reed. “Working together, we can keep the promise of Medicare and Medicaid and ensure these programs are there for older Americans today, tomorrow, and for another sixty-one years. Supporting Medicare and Medicaid provides quality health care to more Americans, slows rising health care costs, and helps reduce federal budget deficit.”

“Medicare and Medicaid have helped provide health care to Rhode Islanders for 61 years,”said Magaziner. “But health care has become increasingly unaffordable and inaccessible because of direct attacks by the President and Congressional Republicans. We must do better. I, along with the entire delegation, will continue fighting for a health care system that is affordable for all Americans.”

“Medicare and Medicaid make a tremendous difference, especially because both programs help people manage chronic conditions like high blood pressure or diabetes, and continue living full lives,” said Peter Marino, President and CEO of Neighborhood Health Plan. “These programs make it more likely that someone will see a doctor when something feels wrong instead of waiting until a health issue becomes an emergency. For people without coverage, the choice too often becomes whether to seek care or pay for other basic needs. No one should have to make that choice. That’s why we need to continue investing in these vital programs – it is how we make sure we are taking care of each other.”

The event commemorated the signing of Medicare and Medicaid into law by President Lyndon B. Johnson 61 years ago while highlighting the challenges Rhode Islanders face today as health care becomes increasingly expensive and inaccessible.

During the event, the Delegation members outlined how recent federal health care cuts are affecting Rhode Islanders and the broader health care system. They also reaffirmed their commitment to protecting Medicare and Medicaid, reversing harmful cuts, and lowering health care costs for working people across the state.

For 61 years, Medicare and Medicaid have helped millions of Americans access quality, affordable health care. Today, more than 309,000 Rhode Islanders rely on Medicaid, including 64 percent of nursing home residents, more than half of adults with disabilities, 37 percent of children, and 43 percent of births in the state. An estimated 34,000 Rhode Islanders are expected to lose health insurance once Medicaid cuts passed by Republicans are in full effect. Another 244,570 Rhode Islanders, nearly one in five residents, depend on Medicare for their health coverage and have seen their health insurance rates skyrocket. Members of the Rhode Island delegation outline how recent Republican cuts to Medicaid and the expiration of enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits threaten to increase health care costs and put additional strain on the state’s health care system. They reiterated their commitment to protecting Medicare, restoring affordable health coverage, and ensuring every Rhode Islander can access the care they need.
